Favored on magnetic resonance imaging as the most probable benign retroperitoneal/pancreatic cystic lesion due to its thin-walled multiloculated appearance and absence of restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC, but definitively excluded during surgical visualization and pathology.

diagnostic_pivot: Laparotomy revealed a large multiloculated cyst in the pancreatic body and tail containing numerous daughter cysts, with pathological examination confirming Echinococcus granulosus.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman, employed as a company clerk and residing in Luzhou City, Sichuan Province, China, presented to the hospital with a 2-month history of intermittent abdominal pain lasting from several minutes to several hours per episode.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suggested by CT and ultrasound findings of an irregular right hepatic mass invading parenchyma with abscess-like characteristics, but argued against by the prolonged subacute 2-month course, normal leukocyte count, negative blood cultures, and absence of acute suppurative changes on aspiration.

Extensive nodular omental, mesenteric, and peritoneal thickening accompanied by ascites and a hepatic mass raised strong suspicion for metastatic malignant disease, but serum tumor markers (CEA, CA-19.9, CA-125, AFP) were strictly normal, and biopsy confirmed a benign chronic granulomatous etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous biopsy of the hepatic mass demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation, accompanied by a positive tuberculin skin test and positive real-time PCR detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA in aspirated pus, confirming hepatic tuberculosis with tuberculous peritonitis.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old male was transferred to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit in December 2024. He resided in a rural village in Liangshan Prefecture, Sichuan Province, China, and frequently played barefoot outdoors.

differentials.candidate: Primary bacterial pneumonia and bacterial septic shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis on presentation given bronchopneumonia, extreme leukocytosis, CRP of 93.53 mg/L, and procalcitonin of 45.936 ng/mL; however, the bacterial sepsis was actually a secondary complication of mucosal barrier breakdown caused by intestinal helminthic invasion.

differentials.candidate: Severe viral respiratory infection (Influenza A) with secondary superinfection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Viral nucleic acid detection was positive for influenza A and sputum grew Streptococcus pneumoniae, explaining initial respiratory decompensation, but this co-infection could not account for subsequent severe lower gastrointestinal bleeding and catastrophic drop in hemoglobin.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat stool testing on day 5 demonstrated parasitic ova, followed by bedside ultrasound identifying an active tubular structure in the jejunum with real-time peristalsis, and subsequent rectal expulsion of a 21 cm adult Ascaris lumbricoides following albendazole administration.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female, a permanent resident of Peshawar, presented to the Emergency Department in February 2025 with complaints of shortness of breath on moderate exertion, cough, and copious hemoptysis for the past 3–4 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect given the patient's previous treated pulmonary history, prominent hemoptysis, and focal lung mass, but ruled out by negative sputum acid-fast bacilli smears.
Considered when sputum KOH examination demonstrated fungal yeast cells, but this represented non-invasive airway colonization rather than a primary fungal cavity or mycetoma.

Considered in the differential of a well-defined solitary pulmonary mass presenting with hemoptysis and chest pain, but excluded based on distinctive cystic radiological characteristics on cross-sectional imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: Subsequent chest CT imaging established the definitive features of a pulmonary hydatid cyst, leading to targeted antiparasitic therapy with albendazole and resolution of respiratory symptoms.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old female presented for evaluation of repeated episodes of redness and discomfort in her left eye over the preceding 9 months. She had no other underlying health issues and reported no initial constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary explanation for recurrent ocular episodes and elevated ESR, prompting initiation of methotrexate and topical corticosteroid therapy, but contradicted by negative autoantibody screening and unmasking of cavitary pulmonary disease under immunosuppression.

Considered in the initial differential diagnosis of deep inflammatory eye disease, but ruled out clinically by rapid blanching with topical phenylephrine and lack of anterior chamber reaction or deep scleral pain.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergence of fever and cough prompting repeat imaging revealed cavitary lung lesions, with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying the episcleritis as an ocular manifestation of pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old female presented to the urology clinic with a 6-month history of recurrent painless gross hematuria without blood clots, accompanied by lower urinary tract storage symptoms including urinary frequency and occasional urgency.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suggested by hematuria, pyuria, frequency, and urgency, but repeatedly ruled out by the absence of bacterial growth on urine culture, confirming sterile pyuria.

Considered because persistent painless gross hematuria in children warrants evaluation for occult lower urinary tract masses, but cytology and histopathology showed preserved morphology with no dysplastic or neoplastic changes.

diagnostic_pivot: Early urine cytology revealed Schistosoma haematobium eggs in a hemorrhagic background, CT urography demonstrated submucosal calcifications, and cystoscopy revealed mucosal sandy patches with biopsy confirming ova surrounded by a giant-cell reaction.

clinical_summary: A patient was hospitalized and undergoing medical management for a large suspected hepatic abscess collection. The clinical course was managed with broad-spectrum antimicrobial coverage while diagnostic evaluations were initiated to identify the underlying etiology.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect for a large hepatic fluid collection, but excluded when bacterial blood cultures, aspirate cultures, and broad-range universal PCR for fungi and bacteria all returned negative.
Considered due to the large focal hepatic mass, but fluid cytology and tumor markers (CEA, BCG, and AFP) from the aspirate were completely negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Stool antigen testing returned positive for Entamoeba histolytica alongside sterile cultures, establishing amebic liver abscess and prompting transition to oral metronidazole as definitive standard-of-care therapy.

clinical_summary: A patient hospitalized with a large hepatic abscess was managed with broad-spectrum antibiotic monotherapy using eravacycline, demonstrating clinical improvement and remaining afebrile. Diagnostic investigations were concurrently underway to determine the definitive etiology of the abscess and assess whether targeted standard-of-care antimicrobial therapy was indicated.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially treated with broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage with clinical response, but eravacycline is not approved for definitive therapy of protozoan abscesses, and pathogen-specific testing identified a parasitic etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of Entamoeba histolytica via positive stool antigen testing prompted discontinuation of eravacycline and initiation of oral metronidazole as the definitive guideline-directed standard of care.

clinical_summary: A male patient with a large hepatic abscess managed with a percutaneous drainage catheter and targeted outpatient medical therapy presented for follow-up evaluation. During outpatient management, he reported new onset of paresthesias and a mild dermatologic rash, accompanied by newly documented peripheral eosinophilia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the large size of the collection, slow drainage reduction, and new eosinophilia and cutaneous findings, but outpatient fluoroscopic cavity examinations demonstrated consistent progressive decrease in cavity size.

differentials.candidate: Adverse drug reaction (metronidazole neurotoxicity and hypersensitivity)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Paresthesias, rash, and eosinophilia were recognized as drug-related adverse effects of ongoing therapy; after careful discussion, therapy was maintained under close observation to ensure complete resolution of the large collection.

diagnostic_pivot: Complete radiological resolution of the amebic hepatic abscess after 16 weeks of metronidazole and drainage, followed by a targeted course of paromomycin to eradicate intraluminal Entamoeba histolytica cysts.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old woman presents with progressive exertional dyspnea over the past several weeks. Her surgical history is notable for resection of a benign hepatic cyst one year prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the intramyocardial cystic collection, but ruled out by the chronic exertional presentation, normal leukocyte and eosinophil counts, absence of systemic inflammatory signs, and absence of bacterial growth upon culture.

differentials.candidate: Congenital pericardial cyst or cardiac cystic neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the solitary cystic appearance adjacent to the ventricular wall; however, the lesion demonstrated internal heterogeneity and echolucent compartments, and surgical histopathology identified characteristic parasitic cuticles and vesicles rather than mesothelial or neoplastic lining.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical median sternotomy revealed an apical left ventricular cyst containing turbid fluid, and microscopic histopathology demonstrated definitive laminated cuticles and vesicles of Echinococcus granulosus.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old male presents with persistent cough and white sputum of one month's duration, accompanied by three days of recurrent high fevers up to 39.6 °C and progressive altered mental status.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the patient was referred following an operation for presumptive lung cancer; however, immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated necrosis without neoplastic cells.

Considered due to nodular pulmonary infiltrates and a strongly positive Aspergillus galactomannan antigen index (6.98 GMI), but Talaromyces marneffei shares cell wall galactomannan epitopes leading to known serologic cross-reactivity, and microbiological cultures displayed dimorphic yeast rather than Aspergillus mold structures.

diagnostic_pivot: Day 2 blood, sputum, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cultures demonstrated thermal dimorphism (filamentous mold at 28 °C and yeast at 36 °C) with secretion of a characteristic soluble red wine pigment, confirmed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry as Talaromyces marneffei.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old woman presents with progressive left-sided proptosis, periocular swelling, and binocular diplopia developing five days after an upper respiratory prodrome. She notes vague left retrobulbar pain with eye movement but denies decreased vision.

differentials.candidate: Carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) or Cavernous sinus thrombosis (CST)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of unilateral proptosis, chemosis, and marked superior ophthalmic vein engorgement; ruled out by cerebral catheter angiography and dedicated magnetic resonance venography.

differentials.candidate: Sino-orbital mucormycosis or invasive fungal sinusitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered strongly in the setting of poorly controlled diabetes and subsequent endoscopically visualized septal necrosis, but fungal smears and mycologic cultures from nasal secretions and tissue biopsy yielded no fungal growth.

diagnostic_pivot: Nasal endoscopy identified necrotic tissue in the nasal septum; biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with 1+ acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain, positive growth on Lowenstein-Jensen medium, and positive PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA, supported by a 16-mm tuberculin skin test.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman (gravida 5, para 5), who reached menopause 3 years ago, presents with irregular vaginal bleeding with the passage of blood clots for the past month. She reports no pelvic or abdominal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, postcoital bleeding, fever, weight loss, or anorexia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary initial suspicion given postmenopausal vaginal bleeding, uterine enlargement, and an irregular, heterogeneous endometrial echo pattern on pelvic ultrasound; excluded by endometrial biopsy demonstrating granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant neoplastic tissue.

differentials.candidate: Active pulmonary tuberculosis with pelvic dissemination
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered once granulomatous inflammation was detected, but chest radiography showed no parenchymal pulmonary lesions or cavitation.

diagnostic_pivot: Endometrial curettage demonstrated epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) performed on endometrial tissue confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA, corroborated by an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (77 mm/h) and a strongly positive Mantoux skin test (32 mm).

clinical_summary: A two-month-old male infant born to healthy Bedouin parents is brought to the pediatric service for evaluation of multiple progressive facial ulcers. The lesions were first noted by the parents at one month of age as small skin papules that gradually enlarged into ulcers over the course of four weeks.

differentials.candidate: Visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) or systemic reticuloendothelial infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the desert living conditions and infant age, but ruled out by the absence of fever, absence of hepatosplenomegaly, absence of lymphadenopathy, and normal inflammatory markers.

Considered due to the crusted, erythematous facial ulcerative appearance in a young child; however, the ulcers demonstrated a chronic, progressive course over several weeks without acute suppurative drainage or response to routine topical hygiene, and biopsy showed intracellular parasites rather than bacterial colonies.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic evaluation of ulcer biopsy specimens revealed superficial reticular dermis packed with large pale histiocytes containing characteristic intracellular amastigotes, confirmed on Giemsa stain as cutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old male presents with a three-month history of intermittent passage of small, white, balloon-like, grape-sized structures in his urine during micturition. He reports no dysuria, gross hematuria, flank pain, or fever.

differentials.candidate: Cystic renal cell carcinoma or multilocular cystic nephroma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the extensive multiseptate cystic mass completely replacing the right renal parenchyma with loss of contrast excretion; however, gross and microscopic analysis of the passed urinary vesicles revealed parasitic laminated and germinal layers rather than neoplastic epithelium.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated or secondary echinococcosis with primary pulmonary or hepatic cysts
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the kidney is an uncommon site of primary hydatid disease; ruled out as primary extra-renal foci were excluded by normal chest radiography and normal liver ultrasonography.

diagnostic_pivot: Gross examination of the passed urinary structures revealed a 2-cm membranous cyst with histopathology showing outer acellular laminated and inner germinal layers, and right nephroureterectomy confirmed a kidney transformed into a bag of cysts containing multiple daughter cysts tracking down the ureter.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old woman who underwent surgical drainage of a retroperitoneal psoas abscess two months earlier presents with a relapse of symptoms. Over recent weeks, she has developed worsening abdominal pain and a newly noticeable palpable mass in the right lower quadrant, despite recent antimicrobial therapy.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic (bacterial) mycotic aneurysm of the aorta
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the saccular morphology of the aneurysm abutting a psoas abscess; however, the chronic indolent course with contiguous vertebral destruction (Pott's disease) and positive mycobacterial cultures from the psoas collection confirmed tuberculous aortitis rather than acute staphylococcal or salmonella infection.

differentials.candidate: Active pulmonary tuberculosis with hematogenous arterial seeding
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary source for arterial seeding; ruled out by normal chest radiography, indicating that aortic involvement occurred via direct contiguous erosion from adjacent tuberculous spondylitis and cold psoas abscess.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal CT revealed a saccular aneurysm arising from the suprarenal aorta directly enveloped by a retroperitoneal psoas abscess with destructive spondylitis, with microbiological cultures of the psoas collection confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old man presents to the hospital with a five-day history of persistent diffuse abdominal pain. He has had no antecedent trauma or recognized chronic medical illnesses.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial presumed clinical and radiological diagnosis based on acute abdominal pain and rim-enhancing fluid collection; however, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) performed on biopsy material confirmed mycobacterial DNA rather than pyogenic bacteria.

differentials.candidate: Primary atherosclerotic or inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the arterial outpouching, but the patient's young age (41 years) and intimate anatomical contact of the aneurysm with a rim-enhancing necrotizing retroperitoneal mass indicated infectious pseudoaneurysmal erosion rather than degenerative atherosclerosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Drainage and biopsy of the rim-enhancing para-aortic collection complicated by bleeding yielded tissue consisting mainly of clots, which tested positive for tuberculosis by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 25-year-old male farmer is admitted to a rural hospital in western Kenya with an acute febrile and gastrointestinal illness. Four days prior to admission, he developed sudden onset of high fever, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, severe diffuse muscle pains, and profuse diarrhea that rapidly became visibly bloody.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an admission differential diagnosis due to acute febrile onset, headache, and prominent neck stiffness; ruled out by normal cerebrospinal fluid cellularity and biochemistry.

differentials.candidate: Other endemic viral hemorrhagic fevers (Yellow fever, Rift Valley fever, Dengue)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when hemorrhagic manifestations escalated, but IgM-capture ELISA and RT-PCR screening for yellow fever, dengue, West Nile, Chikungunya, and Rift Valley fever were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Clinical progression to widespread mucosal hemorrhage followed by reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing and amplicon sequencing confirmed Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (C-CHFV).

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old diabetic male presents with a six-month history of low-grade fever and night sweats, accompanied by recurrent hemoptysis for the past three months. Thirteen years earlier, he was diagnosed with and treated for chronic cavitary granulomatous pulmonary infection.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the remote history of pulmonary tuberculosis, subacute fever, sweats, hemoptysis, and a thick-walled perihilar cavitary lesion; ruled out by negative sputum smears for acid-fast bacilli and absence of granulomatous mycobacterial disease on pathology.

Primary referral suspicion for fungus colonizing an inactive tuberculous cavity; however, surgical exploration revealed an underlying parasitic cyst wall with laminated membranes rather than an epithelialized fibrotic tuberculous cavity.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the resected cavitary wall demonstrated a definitive hydatid cyst containing Echinococcus hooklets, with secondary invasive Aspergillus hyphae infiltrating the cyst wall.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old female presents to the emergency department in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo, with an acute febrile illness of two days' duration. She reports high fever, severe frontal headache, prominent retro-ocular pain, diffuse arthralgias, and generalized myalgias.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the sudden onset of fever, frontal headache, arthralgias, and myalgias in South America, but ruled out because the clinical presentation was characteristic of dengue and viral real-time RT-PCR specifically amplified dengue viral RNA.

Considered in the regional differential of acute febrile illness with headache and severe myalgia, but excluded by the mild self-limited clinical course requiring only simple supportive therapy without hemorrhagic complications, renal impairment, or jaundice.

diagnostic_pivot: Quantitative real-time RT-PCR detected dengue viral RNA in serum, urine, and saliva samples obtained two days after symptom onset, viral isolation in C6/36 cells confirmed viable virus in serum, and serologic testing demonstrated specific IgM/IgG seroconversion.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old male who has worked in an aquarium shop in Saudi Arabia for more than 15 years presents with an 8-month history of breathlessness and vague abdominal discomfort, with worsening dyspnea and cough productive of scanty mucoid expectoration over the preceding month.

differentials.candidate: Bronchogenic Carcinoma / Pulmonary Malignancy with Necrotic Metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the long symptom duration, bilateral lung mass lesions, and secondary pneumothorax, but excluded by the patient's normal constitutional labs, benign clinical exam, and ultrasound demonstrating well-circumscribed fluid-filled lobulated cysts with detached internal membranes rather than solid invasive neoplasms.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Empyema or Amebic Lung/Liver Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the hydropneumothorax and concomitant thoracic and hepatic involvement, but ruled out by the absence of fever, completely normal leukocyte count, normal liver enzymes, and failure to aspirate purulent bacterial exudate.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracoscopic visualization of the visceral pleura revealed remnants of a partially ruptured cyst with an adherent glistening white parasitic membrane communicating with the pleural cavity, confirming pleuropulmonary hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old female presents with persistent pain and a pus-discharging sinus over the proximal portion of the third metacarpal bone of her left hand. Two months prior, she sustained minor superficial abrasions from a trivial injury to the hand.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the antecedent traumatic cutaneous abrasion and active pus drainage, but ruled out by normal total white blood cell count, failure to improve after a month of antibacterial therapy, sterile routine blood cultures, and positive slow-growing mycobacterial culture.

differentials.candidate: Primary Osseous Neoplasm (e.g., Enchondroma or Giant Cell Tumor)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to an isolated osteolytic lesion in a metacarpal bone in a young adult, but excluded by the infectious inflammatory picture of low-grade fever, marked ESR elevation (58 mm/hr), cutaneous retraction with active purulent sinus drainage, and complete radiological healing with antimycobacterial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis of tubercular dactylitis of the metacarpal bone was confirmed by a strongly reactive Mantoux tuberculin skin test (34 mm induration at 72 hours) and isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from the sinus pus culture using the Bactec method.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old man, a former smoker with known chronic silicosis resulting from 14 years of occupational work in the granite industry, is admitted to the hospital following an acute episode of severe hemoptysis with more than 200 mL of expectorated blood.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because Aspergillus saprophytic colonization within pre-existing fibrotic or silicotic cavities is a common cause of massive hemoptysis, but ruled out by negative serum immunodiffusion testing and negative fungal cultures from bronchoalveolar lavage.

Considered in a former smoker with silica exposure presenting with cachexia, hemoptysis, and cavitating conglomerate lung masses, but excluded by negative direct cytologic examination for malignancy on bronchoalveolar lavage.

diagnostic_pivot: Although direct sputum and BAL smears were negative, bronchoalveolar lavage culturing yielded viable Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing active reactivation silicotuberculosis complicated by hypertrophied bronchial arterial hemorrhage.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old Tunisian male in good general condition presents with moderate lower abdominal pain and symptoms of bowel subocclusion. His past surgical history is notable for an operation for a benign hepatic cystic lesion performed 16 years earlier (in 1994) in North Africa, though detailed operative records from that procedure are unavailable.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to advanced age, lower abdominal pain, signs of bowel subocclusion, and a mass intimately adherent to the sigmoid colon, but excluded by the purely cystic nature on cross-sectional imaging and absence of malignancy on en bloc surgical histopathology.

differentials.candidate: Benign Mesenteric or Peritoneal Inclusion Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the isolated pelvic cystic lesion in a patient with previous abdominal surgery, but ruled out by typical hydatid features originating from remote peritoneal seeding and definitive histological confirmation.

diagnostic_pivot: Histological examination of the resected pelvic mass and a secondary retrovesical cyst confirmed the diagnosis of peritoneal and pelvic hydatid disease secondary to remote peritoneal larval seeding.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male presents with a 3-month history of progressive lower urinary tract symptoms, including hesitancy, weak urinary stream, intermittency, nocturia, incomplete bladder emptying, terminal dribbling, dysuria, and lower abdominal pain, accompanied by painful penile lesions and a non-healing lesion on his lower lip.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of concurrent chronic urinary tract obstruction, sterile pyuria, mucocutaneous ulcerations, and nodular lung infiltrates, but ruled out by a negative PPD test, negative urine cultures, and negative sputum acid-fast bacilli smears.

differentials.candidate: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis and Lip
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a long-term smoker presenting with chronic ulcerated lesions of the lip and glans penis associated with unretractable foreskin, but excluded by histopathology showing granulomatous fungal inflammation rather than invasive squamous neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the penile biopsy demonstrated characteristic multi-budding yeast cells consistent with Paracoccidioides, confirming disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis causing genitourinary outflow obstruction.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old male residing in a rural area presents with a 3-year history of progressive obstructive and irritative lower urinary tract symptoms, culminating in acute urinary retention that required emergency suprapubic cystostomy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary granulomatous infectious cause of chronic lower urinary tract obstruction, sterile leukocyturia, and unilateral epididymo-orchitis, but ruled out by negative PPD skin testing, negative bacterial and mycobacterial urine cultures, and negative sputum acid-fast bacilli.

Considered due to the chronic severe bladder outlet obstruction and unilateral testicular enlargement in a 59-year-old male, but argued against by a normal PSA of 2.47 ng/mL and smooth elastic prostate on exam, and ruled out by histological demonstration of fungal granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy established the definitive diagnosis by demonstrating granulomatous chronic prostatitis containing typical fungal structures consistent with Paracoccidioides.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old female presents with a 1-year history of painless swelling on the left side of her neck, accompanied by progressive fatigue and headache. She reports no fever, chills, or night sweats.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) / Autoimmune Connective Tissue Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary autoimmune etiology for severe Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy in a teenage female, but ruled out by negative antinuclear antibody (ANA) testing.

Considered due to chronic painless matted cervical lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and secondary autoimmune hemolysis, but excluded by lymph node histopathology demonstrating caseating granulomatous inflammation without atypical lymphoid proliferations.

diagnostic_pivot: Excisional biopsy of the left cervical lymph node demonstrating caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis, corroborated by a strongly positive Mantoux test (18 mm induration), established tuberculous lymphadenitis as the underlying cause of the secondary immune hemolytic anemia.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male immigrant from Somalia presents with an 8-month history of persistent bilateral otitis media, progressive hearing loss, and tinnitus that have failed multiple courses of oral antibiotics. Over the past two weeks, he has developed malaise, fever, anorexia, weight loss, dizziness, and an unsteady gait, followed one week later by diplopia and a right-sided facial droop.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the invasive nasopharyngeal and skull base mass causing petrous bone erosion, parapharyngeal extension, and multiple cranial neuropathies (CN VI, VII, VIII), but excluded by histology demonstrating necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and absence of malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Refractory Bacterial Otitis Media / Malignant External Otitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe bilateral otorrhea and extensive temporal bone osteomyelitis, but the patient failed multiple antibacterial regimens and histological staining demonstrated acid-fast bacilli rather than typical pyogenic bacterial pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Auramine fluorescent staining identified an acid-fast rod in the nasopharyngeal biopsy specimen, corroborated by a strongly positive Quantiferon TB Gold assay (>10 IU/mL) and definitive recovery of susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis on culture.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old sedentary male presents with a 10-year history of chronic congestive heart failure symptoms. Over recent months, his functional status has deteriorated to New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class IV, experiencing marked dyspnea and fatigue even at rest or with minimal exertion.

differentials.candidate: Ischemic Cardiomyopathy / Severe Coronary Artery Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading cause of systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 40%) in a 65-year-old sedentary male, but ruled out by invasive cardiac catheterization and angiography demonstrating the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease.

Considered in a patient with chronic non-ischemic ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction, but excluded by the demonstration of two concordant positive specific serological assays establishing an infectious protozoan etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Dual concordant serological testing (indirect immunofluorescence and ELISA) confirmed chronic infection with Trypanosoma cruzi, in conjunction with coronary catheterization ruling out an ischemic etiology.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old man from the state of Chanchamayo, Junin, Peru, presents with a one-year history of daily mucoid bloody diarrhea, odynophagia, a painful upper palate ulcer, and an unintentional 12-kilogram weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's prior medical history of intermittent parasitic enteritis, HTLV-1 positive serostatus, and chronic wasting diarrhea, but serial stool parasitological evaluations were negative and helminthic infection fails to account for destructive mucosal and cutaneous ulcers.

Considered because of a 1-year history of bloody mucoid diarrhea, severe hypoalbuminemia, weight loss, and oral ulcerations, but idiopathic IBD does not explain the extrapulmonary nose and foot ulcers, and endoscopic microscopic examination demonstrated an infectious fungal etiology.
Considered due to profound wasting, cachexia, chronic diarrhea, and widespread mucosal ulcerations in a young adult, but blood ELISA for HIV was negative.

Direct microscopic examination of lesion scrapings and colonoscopy demonstrated fungal elements with diagnostic thick double walls and multiple peripheral gemmulation (mariner's wheel appearance), establishing paracoccidioidomycosis alongside Histoplasma coinfection.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old woman presents for medical evaluation. Her past medical history is notable for a partial gastrectomy performed 15 years earlier for a gastric ulcer.

differentials.candidate: HIV-Associated Opportunistic Pulmonary Infection / Wasting Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the profound low body weight (39 kg) and high risk of opportunistic intracellular infections, but definitively excluded by negative HIV serology.

differentials.candidate: Post-Gastrectomy Malnutrition Syndrome / Recurrent Peptic Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of her surgical history of partial gastrectomy 15 years prior and marked cachexia (weight 39 kg) without concurrent medications, but pulmonary diagnostic evaluation demonstrated an active infectious pulmonary process rather than an isolated nutritional or primary gastric disorder.

Gastrectomy-induced hypoacidity and chronic malnutrition predispose patients to secondary reactivation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which was confirmed on pulmonary workup leading to prompt initiation of quadruple antimycobacterial therapy.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old man of Chinese descent who recently immigrated to the United Kingdom represents to the hospital with a two-week history of fever and worsening left knee pain. Two weeks earlier, he had been evaluated for over-anticoagulation following warfarin therapy, which had been empirically initiated at another facility under the suspicion of deep vein thrombosis for three months of left...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute febrile joint worsening and marked systemic inflammatory markers, leading to an empiric trial of high-dose intravenous flucloxacillin; however, the patient failed to respond, fevers recurred, and routine bacterial cultures remained negative.

Considered due to the 5-year history of recurrent asymmetrical polyarthritis, dactylitis, and negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies, but pelvic MRI showed no sacroiliitis and synovial biopsy demonstrated granulomatous change rather than autoimmune synovitis.

Considered when synovial tissue histology demonstrated granulomatous changes alongside small-volume hilar lymphadenopathy on thoracic imaging, but excluded by the ultimate isolation of viable mycobacteria from synovial cultures.

The diagnostic turning point occurred after prolonged 8-week incubation of the initial synovial fluid aspirate, which yielded Mycobacterium tuberculosis, while an isotope bone scan demonstrated multi-focal inflammatory uptake across multiple joints and ribs.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman is evaluated after an incidental right lung base nodule is detected on a routine screening chest radiograph. She is entirely asymptomatic and specifically denies chest pain, cough, dyspnea, or hemoptysis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the foremost concern given the solitary 2.5 cm subpleural nodule with irregular spiculate borders, pleural tags, and peripheral ground-glass halo in a 48-year-old patient; however, surgical resection demonstrated a parasitic inflammatory organizing pneumonia and coexistent aspergilloma rather than neoplastic disease.

Considered due to subpleural consolidation and ground-glass attenuation, but peripheral blood counts and serum eosinophils were completely normal, and histology identified a distinct infectious etiology rather than idiopathic organizing pneumonia.

Histopathologic examination of the resected subpleural nodule demonstrated organizing pneumonia with bronchioles filled with necrotic debris and degenerated parasitic ova morphologically diagnostic of the lung fluke Paragonimus westermani, alongside a focal 2 mm aspergilloma.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old Nigerian undergraduate male presents with a 12-month history of insidious, progressive, colicky left loin pain. He reports no lower urinary tract symptoms, gross hematuria, loin swelling, weight loss, or cough, and has no history of retroperitoneal surgery.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial working diagnosis because of colicky flank pain, left hydroureteronephrosis, and radiographic calcification at the distal ureteric obstruction; however, intraoperative surgical exploration confirmed strictures but found no intraluminal calculus.
Considered given low-grade pyuria (4-5 WBC/HPF) and flank pain, but excluded by sterile urine cultures, absence of dysuria, and lack of systemic inflammatory signs.

Histopathological analysis of the resected strictured ureteric segment revealed a fibromuscular mass packed with numerous Schistosoma eggs within the ureteric wall, reflecting delayed chronic granulomatous stricturing and calcification despite prior treatment.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old woman presents with a swelling in the right paraumbilical region that has been progressively enlarging over the past year. She reports no associated abdominal pain, fever, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary provisional clinical diagnosis due to paraumbilical location and a positive cough impulse; however, cross-sectional CT and ultrasound demonstrated an intact peritoneum with a localized intramuscular cystic mass rather than a herniation defect or protruding bowel/omentum.

differentials.candidate: Soft Tissue Mesenchymal Neoplasm (Cystic Sarcoma / Lymphangioma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the large, chronic, expanding abdominal wall mass with dilated overlying collateral veins, but imaging showed thin-walled cystic fluid and characteristic internal undulating membranes rather than a solid or hypervascular soft-tissue tumor.

CT identification of internal undulating septations (water-lily sign) localized to the abdominal wall musculature and subsequent surgical exploration revealing a thick-walled fibrous capsule containing numerous daughter cysts confirmed echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old multiparous woman of low socioeconomic status is referred for urgent evaluation at 23 weeks of gestation due to rapidly progressive ascites. She reports a one-month history of progressive abdominal swelling accompanied by night sweats, anorexia, weight loss, and worsening diffuse abdominal pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary concern due to subacute progressive ascites, peritoneal thickening, and constitutional B-symptoms (anorexia, weight loss, night sweats), but pelvic ultrasound showed normal adnexa and diagnostic laparoscopy with biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Disseminated Serositis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given classic constitutional features and positive tuberculin reactivity, but ruled out as an active primary lung source by normal chest radiography and negative sputum acid-fast bacilli smears.

Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed 2.5 liters of straw-colored ascites with extensive necrotic peritoneal nodules and intestinal miliary deposits, with histological analysis establishing chronic caseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells diagnostic of peritoneal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a ten-day history of diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, and progressively worsening abdominal distension. He has no significant past medical history and reports no recent trauma.

differentials.candidate: Acute Secondary Bacterial Peritonitis / Perforated Viscus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the toxic clinical presentation with pyrexia (38.5°C), tachycardia (110 bpm), marked leukocytosis, CRP elevation (148 mg/L), and acute diffuse abdominal tenderness; however, plain abdominal radiography showed no free intraperitoneal air, bowel sounds were active, and imaging excluded hollow viscus disruption.

Considered in an elderly patient with high fever, systemic inflammatory reaction, and acute abdominal distension, but cross-sectional imaging revealed multiple sharply defined cysts with internal daughter vesicles typical of tapeworm hydatidosis rather than liquefactive pyogenic abscesses.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Abdominal and Splenic Echinococcosis (Hydatidosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Emergency abdominal CT demonstrated a massive 14.5 cm hepatic hydatid cyst with internal daughter cysts in the left liver lobe, multiple splenic hydatid cysts, and additional cysts in the gastrohepatic space, transverse mesocolon, and pelvis, confirmed during urgent exploratory laparotomy.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old man residing in urban Manaus is admitted to a secondary-care hospital in the Brazilian Amazon with acute abdominal pain after jumping from a tree; he denies sustaining any direct blunt trauma to the abdomen.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially due to the temporal onset of acute abdominal pain after jumping from a tree; however, the patient experienced no direct abdominal impact, and surgical pathology revealed a massive underlying 1,300 g spleen with prodromal constitutional symptoms, indicating pathological rather than mechanical rupture.

Considered when the patient spiked high fevers with rigors and myalgias following splenectomy, but acute profound thrombocytopenia (66,000/mm³) and antecedent rural forest exposure raised high suspicion for an endemic hemoparasitic infection.

Microscopic evaluation of a peripheral thick blood smear demonstrated high-grade intraerythrocytic parasitemia (10,000 to 100,000 parasites/mm³) confirmed as Plasmodium vivax monoinfection by real-time PCR, proving that acute malaria infection precipitated massive splenomegaly and subsequent capsular rupture.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male healthcare worker who emigrated from Vietnam 11 years ago presents with a two-month history of fevers, generalized myalgias, and a severe nonproductive cough. He has a history of extensive plaque psoriasis for which he has been treated with subcutaneous adalimumab for over two years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute onset of cough, fevers, and temporary improvement after empiric doxycycline and azithromycin; however, symptoms recurred with progression to polyserositis and extensive peritoneal and omental nodularity unresponsive to standard antibacterials.

Considered given the diffuse omental caking, peritoneal nodular studding, and exudative polyserositis in a patient receiving chronic immunosuppressive biologic therapy; however, histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Pulmonary and Peritoneal Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Diagnostic thoracentesis revealed an exudative lymphocytic effusion with markedly elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA 110.3 U/L), peritoneal biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli on Fite's stain, and tissue cultures definitively isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old previously healthy man residing in Porto Alegre, Brazil, presents with a progressive, intensely pruritic cutaneous eruption. Four days prior to presentation, he had been fishing barefoot in muddy ground adjacent to a freshwater pond.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially because the hemorrhagic blisters mimicked a purpuric vasculitic disorder, but excluded by the rapid linear-to-serpiginous propagation of urticarial tracks to the thigh and trunk and the presence of peripheral blood eosinophilia.

Zoonotic hookworm larva migrans produces slow-moving (millimeters per day) serpiginous burrows usually restricted to the feet or buttocks, whereas this patient experienced rapid migration of urticarial tracks extending up the leg and across the trunk over several days.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when the rapid advancement of serpiginous urticarial lesions from the foot to the trunk (larva currens) following freshwater mud exposure, combined with peripheral eosinophilia, prompted empirical ivermectin administration with rapid clinical regression, followed by definitive histopathologic confirmation of nematode larvae within the epidermis.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old girl weighing 20 kg presents with a history of recurrent hemoptysis. Plain chest radiography demonstrates a 4-cm homogenous opacity in the lower lobe of the left lung.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the abrupt bradycardia and severe desaturation following manipulation of the pulmonary lesion, but ruled out clinically because systemic blood pressure remained stable without cutaneous manifestations, angioedema, or generalized cardiovascular collapse.

Considered as a potential procedural catastrophe during the creation of artificial surgical pneumothorax, but excluded because breath sounds remained audible on the left side, right-sided breath sounds were decreased rather than absent with tension, and hemodynamics did not demonstrate obstructive shock.

Suspected due to decreased ventilation of the right dependent lung and elevated airway pressures, but repositioning and flexible fiberscopy revealed that obstruction was caused by endobronchial spillage of fluid and membranes rather than isolated mechanical displacement.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot and life-saving airway clearance occurred when rigid bronchoscopy retrieved 20-25 mL of cyst fluid with laminated membrane flakes from the tracheobronchial tree, confirming intraoperative endobronchial rupture of the pulmonary hydatid cyst, subsequently verified by histopathology.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old man presents with sudden-onset severe pain over the right side of his scrotum and fever of 2 days' duration. Earlier on the day of presentation, he noticed macroscopic cylindrical worms extruding through a cutaneous opening at the root of the scrotum.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute unilateral scrotal erythema, severe tenderness, high fever, and leukocytosis, but excluded by the macroscopic extrusion of live nematodes and intraoperative demonstration of a healthy, uninvolved testis and clear hydrocele fluid.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent Strangulated Inguinal Hernia with Enterocutaneous Fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to previous surgery for strangulated hernia and bowel resection, but ruled out because scrotal exploration showed no herniated visceral contents, peritoneal defect, or purulent enterocutaneous fistula.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal clinical and operative confirmation was established by emergency right scrotal exploration revealing adult cylindrical nematodes inhabiting the tunica vaginalis sac alongside clear hydrocele fluid, confirming ectopic scrotal ascariasis through a pre-existing patent surgical pathway.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man residing in Bengaluru, India, presents to the emergency department in July with a 4-day history of high-grade fever accompanied by headache, diffuse myalgia, and progressive abdominal pain with abdominal distension over the past 2 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute high fever, headache, severe myalgias, hepatosplenomegaly, and thrombocytopenia in an endemic region, but definitively excluded by a negative peripheral blood smear.

Considered in view of acute abdominal pain, distension, gross ascites, and fever in a diabetic patient, but excluded by sterile blood cultures and lack of intra-abdominal purulence or organ perforation on exploration.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of severe dengue complicated by spontaneous hemoperitoneum was established by positive serology with rising IgM-to-IgG antibody titers, coupled with paracentesis and laparoscopy revealing 1.5 L of hemorrhagic peritoneal fluid with blood clots and diffuse peritoneal hyperemia despite a normal coagulation profile.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 3-week history of continuous fever accompanied by chills and rigors, along with progressive blackish discoloration of the toes on both feet over the preceding week.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and symmetrical peripheral gangrene typically associated with bacterial septicemia and DIC, but excluded because three consecutive blood cultures showed no bacterial growth.

Considered because bilateral symmetrical distal gangrene can be triggered by ergot alkaloids or heavy tobacco vasoconstriction, but the patient had no drug exposures, no smoking history, and maintained palpable peripheral pulses.
Considered as a primary vascular cause of bilateral lower extremity digital necrosis, but excluded clinically by palpable pedal pulses and duplex imaging confirming normal large-vessel flow.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic discovery was the identification on peripheral blood smear of intraerythrocytic ring forms with occasional gametocytes characteristic of Plasmodium falciparum, establishing symmetrical peripheral gangrene secondary to microvascular parasitized red blood cell sequestration.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old previously healthy woman presents with a 1-month history of a painless lump in her right breast. Over the preceding 2 weeks, she has also experienced intermittent, low-grade fevers.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the patient's young age and the presence of a well-circumscribed, painless, freely mobile breast mass, but fails to account for the satellite inframammary nodule, intermittent low-grade fever, and markedly elevated ESR (60 mm/hr).

Must be considered in any discrete breast lesion with adjacent nodularity, but was clinically less likely given youth, lack of axillary lymphadenopathy, normal chest radiography, and subsequent cytology showing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant epithelial cells.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Breast Abscess / Idiopathic Granulomatous Mastitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic abscess presents with marked local erythema, warmth, and acute throbbing tenderness, which were conspicuously absent in this cold, painless, indolent lesion.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of primary breast tuberculosis was established when fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) from both the breast and inframammary lesions demonstrated epithelioid cell granulomas on a necrotic background, with positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining confirming acid-fast bacilli.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old previously healthy man presents to the clinic following two new-onset generalized seizure episodes occurring over the preceding 20 days. He also reports severe, intermittent headaches of 2 weeks' duration.

differentials.candidate: Colloid Cyst of the Third Ventricle
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because colloid cysts are the most common third ventricular cysts producing intermittent headaches and biventricular hydrocephalus, but colloid cysts are typically hyperdense on CT, situated anterosuperiorly at the foramen of Monro, and lack an internal punctate eccentric mural nodule.

Considered as potential intraventricular neoplasms obstructing CSF flow, but ruled out because the lesion was purely cystic and CSF-isodense without solid soft-tissue proliferation, tumor vascularity, or broad ependymal attachment.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnosis of intraventricular neurocysticercosis with obstructive hydrocephalus was confirmed when brain MRI identified a cystic third ventricular structure containing an eccentric mural nodule corresponding to the parasitic scolex, which subsequently exhibited intraventricular migration into the right lateral ventricular occipital horn following ventriculostomy.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old previously healthy Spanish man presents with a 1-week history of fever, diffuse myalgia, and a non-productive dry cough. Five weeks prior to symptom onset, he had traveled to Senegal, where his activities included swimming in freshwater pools near the Dindefelo falls.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because fever, myalgias, and mild thrombocytopenia in a traveler returning from Senegal strongly suggest acute malaria, but definitively excluded by a negative peripheral blood smear.

differentials.candidate: Common Acute Bacterial or Viral Respiratory Infections / Typhoid Fever
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute febrile illness with cough and systemic myalgia, but ruled out by sterile blood cultures, negative serologies, and prominent peripheral eosinophilia (9%), which is atypical for acute bacterial or viral infections.

Considered as an etiology for pulmonary symptoms with peripheral eosinophilia, but geohelminth larval migration typically manifests within 1-2 weeks of exposure, whereas Katayama syndrome characteristically arises 4-8 weeks after freshwater cercarial penetration.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever) with pulmonary involvement was established by freshwater exposure history in Senegal, positive specific indirect hemagglutination serology (1:80), and post-praziquantel worsening of eosinophilia and bilateral pseudonodular ground-glass halo lesions on chest CT.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old previously healthy woman presents with a 2-month history of persistent epigastric discomfort and intermittent dark-colored stools. She denies constitutional symptoms, including fever, chills, night sweats, anorexia, and weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis because CT and endoscopic ultrasound showed an ulcerated, hypervascular submucosal mass in the posterior duodenal wall, but surgical exploration revealed the lesion was not a mural tumor but an extrinsic perivascular lymph node invading the bowel wall.

Considered due to central ulceration and recent upper gastrointestinal bleeding, but endoscopic biopsy and surgical excision demonstrated absence of malignant epithelial or neuroendocrine cells, showing caseous granulomatous lymphadenitis instead.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnosis was reached through exploratory laparotomy and excision of the perivascular mass, which revealed chronic caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis positive for acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining and positive for mycobacterial DNA by PCR.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old male laboratory technician residing in north Karnataka presents with a 15-day history of left flank pain and the intermittent passage of small, pearly white, grape-sized balloon-like structures in his urine.

differentials.candidate: Multilocular Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma (Bosniak Class IV Cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because a large (11 x 13 cm) multilocular complex cystic renal mass with wall thickening in an adult raises high suspicion for malignancy, but cystic RCC typically manifests with microscopic or gross hematuria rather than spontaneous voiding of intact balloon-like daughter cysts, and lacks a benign spoke-wheel cyst configuration.

differentials.candidate: Multilocular Cystic Nephroma / Polycystic Kidney Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the chronic 18-year history of multicystic renal architecture, but cystic nephroma features non-communicating, fluid-filled locules that do not rupture into the collecting system or produce macroscopic hydatiduria.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of primary renal and ureteral echinococcosis was confirmed following left nephroureterectomy, which revealed thick-walled cysts with daughter cysts extending into the upper ureter, positive serum IgG antibodies, and parasitological demonstration of hooklets and protoscolices of Echinococcus spp. in the cyst fluid.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old woman originally from the Philippines and currently residing in Ireland is admitted for the evaluation and management of progressive acute renal failure. Over the preceding month, she had experienced generalized malaise and fatigue, alongside a painless swelling on the left side of her neck.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis due to rapidly worsening renal insufficiency, active urinary sediment, 1.2 g/24 h proteinuria, positive antinuclear factor, elevated anti-dsDNA titers, and C4 hypocomplementemia in a female patient. However, she lacked classic clinical ACR criteria (no malar rash, oral ulcers, or arthritis), and renal core biopsy refuted lupus nephritis by demonstrating caseating granulomatous nephritis rather than immune-complex glomerulonephritis.

Rapidly progressive renal impairment accompanied by active hematuria, proteinuria, and systemic inflammatory elevation raised concern for crescentic or necrotizing glomerulonephritis secondary to small-vessel vasculitis or anti-GBM disease; however, both ANCA and anti-GBM antibodies were negative, and biopsy lacked necrotizing vasculitic changes.

Considered given the patient's subacute fatigue, malaise, and solitary nontender cervical lymphadenopathy; however, fine-needle aspiration of the lymph node demonstrated non-neoplastic inflammatory changes with reactive lymphocytes and neutrophils without malignant lymphoma.

The diagnostic turning point was established when renal core biopsy showed extensive caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells. Despite negative light microscopy for acid-fast bacilli and negative serial urine AFB cultures, positive Mantoux testing (12 mm), patient provenance from an endemic region, and retroperitoneal/mediastinal lymphadenopathy confirmed extrapulmonary renal tuberculosis as the etiology of her renal failure.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male presents for evaluation of a 15-day history of persistent swelling of the lip that ulcerated two days prior to presentation. He reports no preceding facial trauma, fever, cough, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading provisional diagnosis due to diffuse lip tumefaction and eversion in a young adult; however, it typically features chronic, recurrent non-caseating granulomas without suppuration or caseous necrosis, whereas biopsy here revealed necrotizing granulomas with acid-fast bacilli.

An ulcerating, granular, bleeding exophytic lesion involving the lip, oral mucosa, and gingiva raised suspicion for aggressive mucosal neoplastic disease; excluded by incisional biopsy demonstrating granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells rather than malignant squamous or lymphoid proliferation.

differentials.candidate: Primary Syphilis / Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis / Deep Mycoses
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute ulceration with induration, crusting, and purulent discharge in the oral cavity mimicked syphilitic chancre or tropical granulomatous ulcerations; excluded by non-reactive targeted serological tests and absence of fungal or protozoal elements on tissue examination.

The diagnosis was conclusively established when incisional biopsy of the labial lesion demonstrated numerous necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining visualized acid-fast bacilli, subsequently confirmed by mycobacterial culture, despite a normal chest radiograph and non-reactive Mantoux test.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old woman of Bangladeshi origin presents with an insidious onset of swelling over her right knee. The swelling has been present for three months, initially developing after a mechanical fall.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected as the initial primary diagnosis due to acute-on-chronic fluctuant swelling, surrounding erythema, and purulent discharge following minor trauma, with initial pus aspirate yielding Staphylococcus aureus; however, simple pyogenic bursitis was refuted by failure of standard intravenous antibiotic therapy and emergence of a persistent discharging sinus tract originating from deep osseous pathology.

An infected, swollen anterior knee accompanied by difficulty walking and quadriceps atrophy raised consideration for intra-articular infection; ruled out by preserved arc of motion (0-110 degrees) and intraoperative confirmation that the lesion had no communication with the synovial knee joint cavity.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tuberculosis of the Patella (Patellar Tuberculous Osteomyelitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The persistent discharging sinus prompted repeat knee radiography and MRI, uncovering a central osteolytic nidus with necrotic bone sequestrum in the patella. Surgical sinus excision and sequestrectomy revealed perilesional granulomatous tissue, and sequestered bone microbiology grew acid-fast bacilli confirmed as Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old female migrant from Sierra Leone who has been residing in the United States for over ten years is admitted for evaluation of recurrent fevers and chills. She experienced multiple febrile episodes during childhood while living in West Africa, but had remained free of illness for many years after relocating to the United States.

differentials.candidate: Late Recrudescence or Relapse of Plasmodium falciparum
differentials.rule_out_reason: An episode of fever two years prior had been reported as Plasmodium falciparum trophozoites with very low parasite titer. However, P. falciparum lacks dormant liver hypnozoite stages and cannot cause true relapse years later; long-term recrudescence two years post-quinine without travel re-exposure was deemed biologically extraordinary and prompted formal slide re-examination which proved the initial speciation was erroneous.

Recurrent high-grade fevers and chills in an elderly immigrant without recent travel raised suspicion for occult bacterial infection, urinary sepsis, or endocarditis; ruled out by identification of intraerythrocytic trophozoites on blood smears and swift cure following targeted antimalarial therapy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Recrudescence of Plasmodium malariae
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when the hospital's chief pathologist conducted a side-by-side microscopic review of the 2010 and 2012 blood films, definitively identifying characteristic Plasmodium malariae trophozoites on both occasions, demonstrating persistent, low-grade subpatent erythrocytic recrudescence over a multi-year latency period that successfully resolved with chloroquine.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old female is transferred to our tertiary intensive care unit with progressive breathlessness, fever, and severe abdominal pain of five days' total duration. Prior to transfer, she presented to an outside hospital with acute, excruciating abdominal pain and high fever concerning for an acute surgical abdomen, where she underwent an urgent exploratory laparotomy and cholecystectomy.

differentials.candidate: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Complicated Cholecystitis / Visceral Perforation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe fever and abdominal pain initially raised strong suspicion for an intra-abdominal surgical emergency, prompting urgent laparotomy and cholecystectomy at the referring hospital; however, operative inspection revealed no acute surgical pathology or etiology for her abdominal pain.

differentials.candidate: Hospital-Acquired Pyogenic Sepsis and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The combination of marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC 21,500), multiorgan dysfunction, severe hypoxia requiring mechanical ventilation, and acute renal insufficiency raised concern for post-surgical pyogenic sepsis; however, standard bacterial sepsis failed to account for the focal cutaneous eschar, and she experienced rapid resolution without broad-spectrum gram-negative coverage.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Scrub Typhus Presenting as Acute Abdomen
differentials.rule_out_reason: The pivotal diagnostic breakthrough was the clinical recognition of a characteristic abdominal eschar, connecting her acute abdominal syndrome, capillary leak (albumin 1.7 g/dL), and multiorgan failure to systemic vasculitis caused by scrub typhus. Administration of doxycycline and azithromycin resulted in dramatic defervescence within 48 hours and extubation in 3 days, with definitive confirmation by positive IgM ELISA.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a four-day history of high-grade fever associated with chills, progressive jaundice, intractable vomiting, and severe abdominal pain. He reports no cough, dysuria, diarrhea, or confusion on initial presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute abdominal pain, elevated amylase and lipase, and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a febrile patient raised immediate suspicion for biliary pancreatitis or acute cholangitis; ruled out by normal hepatic transaminases and alkaline phosphatase, and imaging demonstrating pancreatic enlargement and peripancreatic fluid without cholelithiasis or common bile duct dilatation.
Systemic metabolic etiologies of acute pancreatitis were considered in the workup; ruled out by completely normal fasting serum lipid levels and normal serum calcium.

High fever with chills, leukocytosis (15,100/mm³), and ascites/ileus suggested acute bacterial intra-abdominal sepsis; ruled out by sterile blood and urine cultures and absence of gastrointestinal perforation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Severe Falciparum Malaria Complicated by Acute Pancreatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The definitive diagnosis was established by the detection of ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum on peripheral blood smear alongside a strongly positive histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP2) immunochromatographic rapid assay, identifying cytoadherence and microcirculatory pancreatic ischemia due to falciparum malaria as the primary trigger, which responded rapidly to intravenous artesunate.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old Iranian man with a history of end-stage diabetic nephropathy who underwent renal transplantation seven months prior presents to the dermatology clinic for evaluation of two rapidly growing, tumoral cutaneous lesions.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Post-Transplant Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Organ transplant recipients on prolonged calcineurin inhibitor and corticosteroid therapy have a massively elevated risk of aggressive cutaneous malignancies; the rapidly enlarging, cauliflower-like exophytic tumoral masses with epidermal pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia strongly suggested squamous cell carcinoma or Kaposi sarcoma. However, histopathology demonstrated reactive hyperplastic changes without malignant cytological atypia or invasive neoplastic cells.

Vegetating, chronic verrucous cutaneous tumors in an immunosuppressed renal allograft recipient raised high suspicion for opportunistic dimorphic or dematiaceous fungal infection (such as chromoblastomycosis, sporotrichosis) or atypical mycobacteriosis; ruled out by absence of fungal structures and specific detection of intracellular protozoan amastigotes.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Reactivation of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis Post-Transplantation
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic breakthrough was achieved when Giemsa-stained slit-skin smear and skin biopsy demonstrated dense dermal histiocytic infiltration containing numerous intracellular Leishman bodies (amastigotes), corroborated by a positive Montenegro skin test (5 mm induration), proving post-transplant reactivation of dormant leishmanial infection. The patient achieved complete lesion cure following parenteral sodium stibogluconate and local cryotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old Japanese male presents with a two-month history of sporadic nausea, a one-month history of abdominal discomfort, and progressive severe headaches. During infancy (at 11 months of age), he had cysto-peritoneal (CP) and ventriculo-peritoneal (VP) shunts implanted for hydrocephalus secondary to a suprasellar arachnoid cyst.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Bacterial Shunt Infection / Bacterial Peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute high fever, severe abdominal distension, markedly elevated CRP (31.8 mg/dL), and a huge abdominal fluid collection surrounding a VP shunt catheter initially raised strong suspicion for common pyogenic bacterial colonization (such as Staphylococcus epidermidis, S. aureus, or Enterobacteriaceae); however, repeated aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures of both CSF and cyst fluid remained sterile, and empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic regimens failed to resolve inflammation or prevent rapid fluid re-accumulation.

differentials.candidate: Peritoneal Malignancy / Carcinomatosis / True Intra-abdominal Cystic Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: A massive, non-resolving intra-abdominal fluid collection with marked systemic inflammatory markers raised concern for omental carcinomatosis, pseudomyxoma peritonei, or an uncharacterized intra-abdominal malignancy; ruled out by multiple negative cytological examinations and exploratory laparotomy demonstrating a fibrous, unlined pseudocyst without omental implants, true cyst wall, or ascites.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Peritoneal Tuberculosis Presenting as VP Shunt Malfunction
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of peritoneal tuberculosis remained elusive until two months after presentation, when the patient developed acute left knee monoarthritis yielding xanthochromatic synovial fluid identical in appearance to the abdominal pseudocyst fluid, which grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis on mycobacterial culture. Institution of antituberculous chemotherapy and conversion to a ventriculopleural shunt resulted in complete clinical recovery.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old male who emigrated from the Philippines six years prior and works as a nurse in a skilled nursing facility presents to the hospital with a one-month history of rapidly progressive fatigue, intractable vomiting, intense salt craving, loss of libido, and erectile dysfunction.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Classic clinical signs of primary adrenocortical failure (hypotension, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, salt craving) in a patient with pre-existing primary hypothyroidism initially suggested autoimmune polyglandular syndrome; however, autoimmune Addison's disease is characterized radiologically by idiopathic atrophy and small, shrunken adrenal glands, whereas contrast CT in this patient revealed prominent bilateral adrenal enlargement.

Fungal infections frequently target the adrenal cortex hematogenously, resulting in bilateral adrenal enlargement, caseous-type necrosis, and primary adrenal failure; ruled out by the patient's origin from an endemic tuberculosis zone (Philippines) rather than fungal endemic areas, and prior documentation of acid-fast bacilli in his peritoneal exudate.

Cachexia, unintentional weight loss, and large bilateral adrenal masses raised suspicion for bilateral malignant metastasis or primary adrenal lymphoma; ruled out by the clinical setting of microbiologically verified extra-adrenal granulomatous disease and prompt stabilization upon corticosteroid replacement without malignant progression.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tuberculosis of the Adrenal Gland
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of bilateral adrenal tuberculosis with primary adrenal insufficiency was established by hormonal confirmation (random cortisol 2.5 mcg/dL, ACTH 531.2 pg/mL, subnormal cosyntropin stimulation at 2.0 mcg/dL), bilateral adrenal enlargement on CT, and precipitation of crisis by rifampicin-mediated CYP3A4 enzymatic induction of cortisol degradation in a patient with culture-confirmed extra-adrenal peritoneal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old male is admitted to the hospital in Botucatu, São Paulo, Brazil, complaining of a progressively worsening, painful perianal suppurative ulcer of two months' duration. For the preceding six months, he had been receiving high-dose oral corticosteroid therapy (prednisone 40 mg daily) for a presumed adverse drug reaction.

differentials.candidate: Pyoderma Gangrenosum / Severe Cutaneous Adverse Drug Eruption
differentials.rule_out_reason: A massive, 10-cm phagedenic perianal ulcer with purulent discharge in a patient chronically treated with prednisone for an alleged drug eruption initially suggested a neutrophilic dermatosis such as pyoderma gangrenosum or persistent severe drug vasculitis; ruled out by histopathology showing dense histiocytic granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis and acid-fast bacilli rather than sterile neutrophilic infiltrate.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Lepromatous Leprosy with Severe Type 2 Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The emergence of papules and nodules containing foamy histiocytes with globi led clinicians to hypothesize that the perianal and inguinal ulcers were atypical severe necrotic manifestations of type 2 lepra reaction unmasked by steroid tapering; however, four weeks of antileprosy multidrug therapy and thalidomide resulted in worsening of the perianal ulcer, fever, and weight loss, disproving an isolated leprotic ulcer.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Coinfection of Lepromatous Leprosy and Cutaneous Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic resolution was confirmed by demonstrating two distinct mycobacterial diseases: polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from upper limb skin samples confirmed Mycobacterium leprae, while a strong tuberculin skin test (20 x 20 mm) and Lowenstein-Jensen mycobacterial culture of the perianal ulcer biopsy grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Addition of standard antituberculous therapy (isoniazid, ethambutol, rifampin) resulted in complete ulcer healing in two months, followed by curative antileprotic therapy.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male presented with pain and swelling involving the distal third of the left thigh. He initially noticed a small swelling that had progressively increased in size, accompanied by a low-grade fever without diurnal variation, weight loss, and loss of appetite.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered based on the initial plain radiograph of the left thigh demonstrating a bony overgrowth with well-defined margins; however, it was excluded by the presence of constitutional symptoms, elevated inflammatory markers, and CT findings of an irregular pseudo-tumor with calcifications.

Considered due to the progressive, painful, firm lower extremity mass and CT scan demonstrating an invasive-appearing 30 x 48 x 77 mm pseudo-tumor with irregular margins and calcifications; ruled out by elevated infectious markers and definitive microbiological and histopathological examination demonstrating granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when bacteriological examination demonstrated acid-fast bacilli positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and histological analysis identified epithelioid giant cell granulomas with pathognomonic caseous necrosis, leading to complete clinical improvement on antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented to the medical outpatient department with epilepsy diagnosed within the preceding 3 months. Her seizures had become progressively more frequent despite treatment with carbamazepine and phenobarbital administered at maximal tolerable dosages.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the new onset of seizures in an adolescent refractory to dual anticonvulsant therapy; ruled out by the absence of trauma history and the subsequent neuroimaging demonstration of structural parasitic cystic lesions within the cerebral parenchyma.
Considered as an associated intestinal source of parasitic transmission; ruled out by microscopic stool examination.

The diagnostic pivot occurred when brain CT neuroimaging demonstrated pathognomonic multiple calcified and vesicular cysts in the cerebral parenchyma, with marked clinical and radiological resolution following targeted antiparasitic therapy with albendazole.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old male was evaluated in the surgical outpatient department for follow-up of previously resected right lung adenocarcinoma with visceral pleural invasion, for which he had undergone video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy and four cycles of adjuvant cisplatin and gemcitabine chemotherapy, remaining disease-free for nearly three years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary concern given the patient's oncologic history and intense FDG avidity (SUVmax 6.1) of the enlarging subpleural nodule on PET-CT; ruled out when invasive tissue biopsy demonstrated infectious granulomatous pathology rather than tumor recurrence, consistent with stable serum tumor markers.

Considered during the 9-month period of observation when radiographs and serum tumor markers showed no progression; ruled out by subsequent CT demonstrating enlargement of the patchy opacities, emergence of the subpleural nodule, and marked hypermetabolism.
The diagnostic pivot was achieved via video-assisted thoracoscopic biopsy of the hypermetabolic nodule, which disproved malignancy and confirmed active tuberculosis infection.
