clinical_summary: In 2013, a 71-year-old male presented to a tropical medicine clinic in Germany with an acute febrile illness 3 days after returning from an extensive travel itinerary in West Africa.

differentials.candidate: Malaria and Other Endemic West African Febrile Illnesses
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary differential diagnosis in any traveler returning from West Africa with acute fever; excluded as clinicians must evaluate emerging arboviral etiologies in patients presenting with tropical febrile syndromes.

differentials.candidate: Exclusion of Non-Endemic Regional Transmission Assumption
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially considered less probable due to the historical view that Togo and Burkina Faso were non-endemic territories; refuted by the incubation window of under 14 days confirming local transmission.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue Virus Serotype 3 Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis was confirmed by positive NS1 antigen and IgM serology, followed by real-time RT-PCR and envelope gene sequencing identifying DENV-3 genotype III.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presented with a 2-day history of an acute eruptive rash consisting of multiple painful, erythematous skin lesions distributed over his face, abdomen, and extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the polymorphic papulonodular cutaneous eruption and history of multiple sexual exposures; ruled out by a non-reactive VDRL serological test.

Considered given the temporal onset of rash and fever four weeks after initiating nevirapine-based ART; ruled out by the characteristic earlobe infiltration, multiple thickened tender peripheral nerves, and peripheral sensory loss.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Lepromatous Leprosy with Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) as IRIS
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis was confirmed by slit skin smear demonstrating acid-fast bacilli with a bacteriological index of 4 and morphological index of 20%, alongside a skin biopsy showing Grenz zone, dermal edema, macrophage aggregates, and acute-on-chronic perivascular inflammation indicative of ENL unmasked during immune reconstitution.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old female presented with a chronic, progressive dermatological lesion on her right leg. The lesion had begun as an indurated, infiltrated erythematous-ferruginous plaque with central atrophic scars and subsequently progressed into a 6-cm ulcer displaying irregular borders and fibrino-necrotic areas.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential diagnosis of a chronic indurated, non-healing necrotic cutaneous ulcer on the lower extremity; ruled out by negative targeted serological testing and absence of characteristic Leishmania amastigotes.

Considered due to the chronic ulcerative and fibrino-necrotic progression of the plaque; ruled out by complete lack of response to antibacterial and antifungal regimens as well as negative bacterial and fungal cultures from biopsy material.

The definitive diagnosis was established despite the nonreactive PPD skin test by histopathologic demonstration of histiocytic and multinucleated giant cell granulomas, recovery of acid-fast bacilli on culture, and molecular confirmation via PCR targeting the IS6110 sequence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male was admitted with a 5-day history of high fever associated with chills and rigors. His family reported that his sensorium had become acutely altered starting the day prior to admission.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute onset of high fever, drowsiness, altered sensorium, and bilateral extensor plantar responses; ruled out by the absence of meningeal signs and the subsequent identification of blood-borne plasmodial parasites.

Considered given the combination of altered mental status, tachypnea, tachycardia, and significant azotemia (urea 85 mg/dL, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL); excluded as a primary non-parasitic septic syndrome upon demonstration of heavy malarial parasitemia.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Severe Falciparum Malaria with Cerebral and Renal Involvement
differentials.rule_out_reason: The definitive diagnosis was confirmed when peripheral thick and thin blood smears revealed intraerythrocytic ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum and a rapid immunochromatographic test for PfHRP-2 was strongly positive, with the patient's recovery later complicated by post-infectious Guillain-Barré syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male presented with a 6-day history of high fever accompanied by chills and rigors, severe headache, repeated vomiting, generalized convulsions, and progressive deterioration of sensorium. He had no history of recreational drug use, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, pre-existing renal disease, or systemic vasculitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the profound acute presentation with fever, severe headache, vomiting, seizures, coma, and mild nuchal rigidity; excluded as the primary entity by the confirmation of intraerythrocytic plasmodial infection on blood smear microscopy.

differentials.candidate: Primary Ruptured Intracranial Aneurysm / Arteriovenous Malformation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when persistent coma prompted neuroimaging that revealed subarachnoid hemorrhage; ruled out as the primary etiology by magnetic resonance angiography demonstrating normal intracranial vasculature, normal coagulation profile, and negative autoimmune and hemoglobinopathy workup.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Cerebral Malaria Complicated by Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of severe cerebral malaria was established by the demonstration of Plasmodium falciparum ring forms and gametocytes on peripheral blood smears alongside a strongly positive PfHRP-2 antigen assay, with non-contrast brain CT subsequently identifying secondary subarachnoid hemorrhage.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman presented with a 1-month history of persistent cough and a suspected episode of hemoptysis. She had no sputum production, chest pain, or dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on elevated D-dimer (600 ng/mL) and pulmonary artery filling defects leading to empirical low-molecular-weight heparin; ruled out because the filling defects were smooth, well-circumscribed, contiguous with a cystic nodule, and lacked lower extremity deep vein thrombosis or intracardiac thrombi.

Considered as a primary neoplastic etiology for intraluminal pulmonary arterial filling defects on CT; excluded when further imaging demonstrated an avascular fluid-filled cystic lesion rather than an invasive vascular malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Pulmonary Artery Hydatid Cyst (Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The definitive diagnosis was established by endobronchial Doppler ultrasound and thoracic MRI demonstrating protein-rich intraluminal cystic lesions, corroborated by positive indirect hemagglutination and specific IgE serological tests for hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old male agricultural laborer presented with a 5-month history of progressive headache, blurring of vision, and 3 to 4 episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures. He reported no history of fevers, chills, weight loss, or other constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary preoperative diagnosis given the young patient's contrast-enhancing, dural-based lesion producing mass effect associated with overlying bony hyperostosis; ruled out by histopathology demonstrating suppurative granulomas and fungal grains rather than meningothelial neoplasia.

differentials.candidate: Classic Scalp Mycetoma with Secondary Calvarial Erosion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of the patient's occupational exposure as a farm laborer and chronic calvarial involvement; differentiated by the complete absence of external scalp swelling, cutaneous nodules, or draining sinuses.

The definitive diagnosis was confirmed following surgical en bloc resection by histopathologic examination demonstrating suppurative granulomas containing 2–4 mm pale granules exhibiting the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon, with GMS and PAS staining revealing fungal vesicles and septate hyphae.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old female from a low socioeconomic background in New Delhi, India, presented with a 6-week history of dull, aching suprapubic pain that was persistent throughout the day and worsened significantly upon standing and walking.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially due to suprapubic pain and pubic symphysis erosion on plain radiograph, but ruled out by persistent refractory symptoms despite conservative anti-inflammatory management, marked constitutional weight loss, evening fevers, and systemic inflammatory elevation.
Considered in patients presenting with isolated pubic symphysis tenderness, but excluded by the absence of athletic training, mechanical injury, or prior pelvic intervention.

Considered given the constitutional fevers and weight loss in an endemic region, but ruled out as an active primary or secondary pulmonary focus by clear chest radiography and absence of respiratory signs.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine needle aspiration cytology of the eroded pubic symphysis revealed epithelioid cell clusters, histiocytes, and caseous necrosis, confirming tuberculous osteitis of the pubic symphysis, followed by complete clinical resolution upon receiving standard antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 5-month-old female infant presented with a 10-day history of persistent fever and multiple episodes of seizures. Physical examination revealed generalized petechial spots distributed over her trunk and both upper and lower extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the infant presentation with high fever, seizures, and petechial eruption, but ruled out as an acute pyogenic CNS infection in favor of an arboviral encephalitis/encephalopathy with thrombocytopenia responding to protocolized fluid management.
Considered because of fever and recurrent seizures in an infant, but classical neurotropic viruses do not typically cause primary thrombocytopenia and petechial rash without systemic coagulopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive dengue IgM serology in the context of thrombocytopenia, hemorrhagic petechiae, and prolonged febrile seizures confirmed dengue infection with acute neurological manifestations, which resolved fully with WHO-guided intravenous fluid resuscitation.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male with multiple myeloma presented with fever up to 38.5 °C and right cervical lymph node enlargement 70 days after undergoing an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation from an unrelated donor (9/10 HLA match).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the onset of fever and progressive lymphadenopathy during intensive post-allogeneic HSCT immunosuppression, alongside low-level peripheral EBV replication (820 copies/mL); excluded when EBV viremia cleared spontaneously without targeted therapy and histopathology demonstrated granulomatous rather than lymphoproliferative disease.

Considered given fever in an immunocompromised host, but ruled out after empirical oral antibacterial therapy failed to prevent disease recurrence, leading to wound breakdown and purulent discharge on day +90.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic evaluation of a repeat cervical node biopsy demonstrated classic caseating granulomas, with nodal PCR confirming specific mycobacterial sequences and cultures confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, leading to prompt clinical cure on targeted triple-drug therapy.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male immigrant from Mali presented with a 6-month history of progressive, inflammatory nodular swelling over his right arm extending proximally to the neck. His medical history was notable for prolonged forest living during conflicts in his home country.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the chronic fistulizing cervical and axillary lymphocutaneous lesions in an immigrant from West Africa, but histopathology revealed grain-centered microabscesses exhibiting the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon rather than typical caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis.
Considered due to the chronic discharging sinus tracts in the axilla and neck, but routine aerobic and anaerobic microbiological cultures were sterile.

Considered due to the characteristic tumefaction and sinus tract formation following forest exposure, but ruled out in favor of an actinomycotic etiology due to special stain positivity (Gram, Ziehl-Neelsen, Gomori Grocott) and clinical response to antibacterial regimens.

diagnostic_pivot: Deep surgical biopsy demonstrated nodular microabscesses organized around multilobated grains displaying the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon with positive Gram, acid-fast, and silver staining, confirming actinomycetoma, leading to treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and amoxicillin-clavulanate.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man presented with a 15-day history of persistent fever, loss of taste, anorexia, and weight loss. On examination, body temperature was 37.7 °C, heart rate 80 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and blood pressure 120/80 mmHg.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to large bilateral adrenal tumors, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and marked LDH/ferritin elevation; ruled out by histological analysis of both the adrenal gland, bone marrow, and lymph node showing necrosis without malignant cells.
Considered due to the combination of cytopenia, severe hyperferritinemia (>2000 ng/mL), elevated LDH, and hepatosplenomegaly; ruled out by negative viral serologies.
Considered given large bilateral adrenal masses with disproportionately elevated ACTH; excluded by CT-guided biopsy revealing epithelioid granulomas and caseous necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: CT-guided biopsy of the adrenal mass demonstrated epithelioid cell granulomas with caseous necrosis, and bone marrow biopsy confirmed active hemophagocytosis (4.6% hemophagocytic histiocytes) without neoplasia, establishing secondary hemophagocytic syndrome induced by bilateral adrenal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old male traveler from Guinea presented to an infectious diseases service in Dakar, Senegal, with a 6-day history of fever, persistent vomiting, and watery diarrhea without overt hemorrhage. He had arrived in the city one week earlier via an overnight bus journey, having been completely asymptomatic during travel.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the sudden onset of watery diarrhea, vomiting, and fever without initial bleeding, but refractory to routine clinic management and subsequently linked to fatal epidemic exposures.

Common endemic differentials for acute febrile illness with gastrointestinal symptoms in West African travelers, but superseded when epidemiological surveillance traced high-risk contacts with fatal index cases.

diagnostic_pivot: Cross-border surveillance notification from public health authorities in Guinea confirmed the patient was an untraced contact of fatal cases, prompting immediate strict isolation and confirmatory blood testing by the Pasteur Institute demonstrating Zaire ebolavirus.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old woman presented to an acute clinical reception unit in Freetown, Sierra Leone, on day 7 of an acute illness. She reported no known exposure to ill contacts.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary endemic diagnosis for acute fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, and severe myalgias; empirical artesunate was administered, but symptoms progressed independently of antimalarial therapy until viral etiology was identified.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial sepsis or gastroenteritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to profuse diarrhea, vomiting, and profound weakness; treated with intravenous broad-spectrum ceftriaxone, but the course was driven by filoviral infection rather than enteric bacterial pathogens.

Considered when the patient subsequently deteriorated into coma (GCS 9/15) on day 20; empiric fluconazole was given, and while CSF multiplex testing flagged MRSA and Klebsiella, these were judged contaminants given inadequate treatment dosing, spontaneous recovery, and positive CSF filoviral PCR.

diagnostic_pivot: Initial blood PCR on day 8 confirmed acute Ebola virus disease (Ct 23.5); following peripheral viral clearance, lumbar puncture performed during delayed neurological relapse demonstrated high opening pressure and confirmed central nervous system viral persistence by positive CSF RT-PCR (Ct 37.6).

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old male college student presented with a 4-day history of high-grade fever associated with chills, rigors, and generalized body aches. He had returned to Malaysia 5 days prior to symptom onset after spending 10 days in Nigeria.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute febrile illness with severe body aches, marked thrombocytopenia, and geographic presentation in Malaysia; ruled out by negative NS1 antigen and negative IgM/IgG serology.

Considered in the differential diagnosis of tropical acute febrile illness with elevated inflammatory markers and thrombocytopenia; excluded by negative serology and unrevealing diagnostic agglutination tests.

Considered the primary life-threatening possibility for high fever and thrombocytopenia returning from West Africa, but excluded by the absence of the falciparum-specific T1 band on rapid antigen testing and characteristic morphological features on microscopy.

diagnostic_pivot: BinaxNOW malaria testing yielded a pan-malarial T2 band, and thick and thin blood films demonstrated parasites at 0.27% parasitemia, while nested genus PCR and 18S rRNA gene sequencing definitively identified the non-falciparum variant Plasmodium ovale wallikeri, which responded promptly to artemether/lumefantrine and primaquine.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old male agricultural laborer from Ceará state in northeast Brazil presented with a 4-month history of extensive cutaneous eruptions. The lesions initially appeared on his face and lower legs before progressively spreading over much of his body, including the scalp, genitalia, and plantar surfaces of the feet.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the widespread polymorphic ulcerated, papular, and crusted lesions involving the trunk, genitalia, and plantar surfaces; excluded by non-reactive syphilis serological testing.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic disseminated fungal infection in HIV
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the hundreds of polymorphic cutaneous ulcers and nodules in a rural agricultural worker, which frequently reflects disseminated histoplasmosis or paracoccidioidomycosis in immunocompromised states; ruled out by negative HIV serology and normal organ function.
Considered due to the pustular and crusted appearance of numerous ulcers, but bacterial involvement represented secondary superinfection of a primary parasitic process.

diagnostic_pivot: Skin biopsy imprint directly identified amastigotes, skin culture on Novy-MacNeal-Nicolle (NNN) medium isolated promastigotes characterized by isoenzyme analysis as Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis, and the leishmanin skin test was positive, confirming disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis cured with oral fluconazole.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old female presented with a 5-day history of continuous high-grade fever, accompanied by headache and vomiting for 3 days. Over the preceding 24 hours, she developed progressive disorientation and acute facial asymmetry with facial deviation toward the left.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the acute high-grade fever, severe headache, neck rigidity with positive Kernig sign, and altered sensorium, but excluded by non-enhancing neuroimaging findings and full clinical resolution on supportive fluid therapy alone without antibacterial therapy.

differentials.candidate: Acute ischemic stroke with concurrent febrile illness
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute onset of disorientation and focal right-sided upper motor neuron facial palsy, but ruled out by prominent meningismus and neuroimaging demonstrating bilateral multifocal punctate lesions across the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale rather than a territorial vascular occlusion.

diagnostic_pivot: Brain MRI revealed bilateral non-enhancing T1-hypointense and T2/FLAIR-hyperintense lesions in the lentiform nuclei and centrum semiovale consistent with microvascular ischemic demyelination, which in conjunction with meningismus in an endemic setting confirmed dengue meningoencephalitis with complete neurological recovery following supportive care.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a 5-day history of high-grade continuous fever accompanied by chills and rigors. For the preceding 4 days, she experienced severe headache, anorexia, nausea, and multiple episodes of vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: HSV encephalitis was considered due to acute fever, disorientation, seizures, and temporal lobe involvement, but it typically exhibits asymmetric necrotizing lesions with contrast enhancement rather than nonenhancing thalamic alterations, and the patient made a complete recovery without antiviral therapy.

High-grade fever with rigors, severe headache, vomiting, and marked nuchal rigidity with Kernig sign raised strong concern for bacterial meningitis, but the absence of suppurative meningeal exudate and gradual resolution on supportive care alone excluded an acute bacterial etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Neuroimaging demonstrated nonenhancing bithalamic and medial temporal encephalitis consistent with arboviral central nervous system involvement, establishing the confirmed diagnosis of dengue meningoencephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old man presented with a 6-day history of high-grade continuous fever accompanied by chills and rigors, persistent severe headache, and multiple episodes of vomiting for 5 days. For the preceding 2 days, he had experienced progressive disorientation and recurrent episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Recurrent seizures, continuous high fever, vomiting, and meningismus prompted strong consideration of acute bacterial meningitis, but normal routine blood tests and resolution without antimicrobial therapy excluded pyogenic infection.

Repetitive generalized seizures and acute encephalopathy frequently suggest HSV encephalitis, but MRI revealed diffuse cerebral edema without temporal focal lesions, and the clinical course resolved with supportive care.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of diffuse cerebral edema on neuroimaging combined with IgM reactivity on MAC ELISA and compatible CSF findings confirmed dengue meningoencephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with a 5-day history of continuous high-grade fever without chills or rigors, accompanied by persistent severe headache and recurrent episodes of vomiting. Over the preceding 3 days, he experienced generalized tonic-clonic seizures followed by progressive drowsiness and declining consciousness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral symmetrical thalamic hyperintensities and altered sensorium in an endemic region strongly suggested Japanese encephalitis, but specific flaviviral assessment identified dengue as the causative pathogen, with resolution without classic extrapyramidal sequelae.

High-grade fever, vomiting, depressed sensorium, and positive Kernig sign raised suspicion of pyogenic bacterial CNS infection, but the patient recovered fully on conservative fluid and anticonvulsant therapy without antibiotics.

diagnostic_pivot: Neuroimaging demonstrating bilateral symmetrical T2 hyperintensities isolated to both thalami in the setting of acute febrile encephalopathy established the diagnosis of dengue meningoencephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old man presented with a 7-day history of continuous high-grade fever associated with chills and rigors, persistent severe headache for 6 days, multiple episodes of vomiting, and progressive disorientation for 5 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden combination of severe meningismus, profound coma, and lower extremity purpura raised strong clinical concern for Neisseria meningitidis infection, but the patient achieved gradual recovery without antibacterial therapy and neuroimaging showed parenchymal thalamic and splenial involvement.

Splenial and thalamic altered signal intensity on MRI raised ADEM as a consideration, but the presence of cutaneous purpuric manifestations and direct intrathecal antibody production confirmed acute primary arboviral neuro-invasion.

diagnostic_pivot: Detection of specific IgM antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid established definitive proof of direct viral neuro-invasion and confirmed dengue meningoencephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old boy presented with a 5-day history of continuous high-grade fever associated with chills and rigors, severe headache, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting for 3 days. Over the preceding 2 days, he developed neck stiffness, followed by drowsiness for 1 day.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Continuous high-grade fever, vomiting, and acute meningismus in a child strongly raised concern for pyogenic bacterial meningitis, but normal neuroimaging and gradual clinical resolution with supportive fluid and antipyretic care ruled out a bacterial infection.

Drowsiness, severe headache, and high fever raised suspicion of parenchymal viral encephalitis, but brain MRI showed no abnormal signal intensities and the patient lacked seizure activity or focal deficits.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation of aseptic meningitis based on positive MAC ELISA serology for dengue accompanied by a compatible CSF profile established the diagnosis of dengue meningitis.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old man presented with an 8-day history of continuous high-grade fever, headache, and vomiting, with worsening severe headache and persistent vomiting over the preceding 4 days. One day prior to admission, he developed acute altered sensorium.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multifocal brainstem lesions and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis strongly suggested an autoimmune demyelinating process such as ADEM or vasculitis, but systemic autoimmune serologies were negative and CSF showed absence of oligoclonal bands.

While metabolic encephalopathy secondary to hepatic dysfunction or electrolyte disturbance can cause altered sensorium in dengue, it is associated with normal brain MRI and unremarkable CSF, unlike the extensive neuro-axis structural inflammation seen here.

diagnostic_pivot: Neuroimaging identifying longitudinally extensive myelitis from C3 to conus combined with brainstem lesions and intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis led to the revised diagnosis of dengue meningoencephalomyelitis, treated successfully with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone.

clinical_summary: A 69-year-old Japanese woman with a past medical history of subarachnoid hemorrhage was referred to the dermatology department for evaluation of skin eruptions that had been present for 7 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to a 7-month duration of non-pruritic nodules, elevated serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor, and dense CD3+/CD4+ dermal lymphoid infiltration on initial biopsy, but ruled out by lack of Pautrier microabscesses, absence of systemic FDG avidity on PET/CT, and discovery of an epidermal mite.

Benign reactive lymphoid hyperplasia was considered given the dense polymorphic T-cell predominant infiltrate, but this nodular presentation was driven by an active ectoparasitic infestation that resolved completely following oral anti-parasitic therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Incidental detection of an epidermal mite within the stratum corneum on immunohistochemical thin sections followed by microscopic confirmation via potassium hydroxide (KOH) examination established the diagnosis of nodular scabies.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old female laboratory researcher presented to a community hospital with a 4-day history of systemic illness. Her symptoms began with generalized muscle pain, followed by vomiting, chills, and a febrile sensation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Natural mosquito-borne arboviral transmission was considered, but ruled out because the patient lived in an area without reported cases, presented during winter without mosquito exposure, and had no recent travel history.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bloodborne Viral Hepatitis / Retroviral Seroconversion
differentials.rule_out_reason: A needlestick injury in a healthcare/laboratory setting commonly prompts concern for HBV, HCV, or HIV seroconversion presenting with fever, rash, and transaminitis, but the incubation period, transient course, and rapid resolution without residual abnormalities excluded chronic bloodborne pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Documented occupational percutaneous inoculation during cell culture processing, rapid NS1 antigen detection, and confirmatory double-positive IgM capture ELISA established laboratory-acquired dengue virus infection.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 15-day history of fever, nausea, and vomiting, accompanied by progressive irritability and behavioral confusion for the preceding 5 days. On initial admission, the patient was vitally stable.

differentials.candidate: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Hyponatremia with concentrated urine and low serum osmolality in the setting of central nervous system infection initially suggested SIADH, but the patient failed a therapeutic trial of fluid restriction and exhibited massive natriuresis with polyuria up to 4 L/24 hours, characteristic of cerebral salt wasting syndrome.

Subacute febrile encephalopathy with lymphocytic pleocytosis raised suspicion for fungal or viral meningoencephalitis, but fungal smears were negative, viral markers were negative, and CSF culture showed no growth.

diagnostic_pivot: Marked lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis with profoundly elevated protein (314 mg/dL) and LDH (63 U/mL) in conjunction with severe cerebral salt wasting syndrome responded completely to 3% hypertonic saline, mineralocorticoids, and anti-tuberculous therapy, confirming tuberculous meningitis.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman presented to the surgical department complaining of chronic epigastric pain and persistent low-grade fever. In evaluation of these symptoms prior to admission, abdominal ultrasonography had revealed a multicystic lesion located in the left kidney.

differentials.candidate: Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma / Malignant Renal Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: A multicystic, thick-walled renal mass in an adult commonly represents cystic renal cell carcinoma or multilocular cystic nephroma, but serum tumor markers were entirely normal and surgical exploration confirmed an intact parasitic cyst rather than neoplastic tissue.

differentials.candidate: Complicated Benign Renal Cyst / Polycystic Kidney Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Benign simple or polycystic renal disease was considered, but the presence of thick calcified cyst walls on computed tomography and associated fever indicated an infectious parasitic process rather than simple cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal CT demonstrating a hypodense multicystic mass with calcified thick walls, corroborated by markedly elevated Echinococcus IgG antibody titers and surgical open cystectomy, established isolated renal hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 22-month-old girl presents with an 8-day history of high-grade fever up to 40°C and a mild non-productive cough. Her medical history is notable for failure to thrive, though neurological development has been age-appropriate.

differentials.candidate: Primary Familial Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (including Griscelli or Chédiak-Higashi syndromes)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe early-onset hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a stunted toddler, but argued against by normal hair and skin pigmentation without hypopigmentation, lack of parental consanguinity, normal perforin expression on flow cytometry, and sustained remission without full continuation of etoposide protocol.

Considered because the patient demonstrated serological reactivity to EBV with detectable low-level viral load (637 copies/mL), but EBV was an incidental co-infection or co-trigger that failed to explain the full presentation, as the child continued to deteriorate with progressive splenomegaly, petechiae, and deepening cytopenias until targeted antiparasitic therapy was instituted.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite initial negative immunochromatography and indirect immunofluorescence, nested polymerase chain reaction performed on peripheral blood and bone marrow aspirate definitively detected Leishmania DNA, confirming visceral leishmaniasis as the primary trigger of secondary HLH, followed by complete clinical recovery upon initiation of liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male with a history of childhood poliomyelitis presents to a tertiary care medical center with a 1-year history of a progressively enlarging, painless deep perianal mass accompanied by intermittent chronic constipation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial referral diagnosis for an extensive pelvic mass, but ruled out by the absence of solid enhancing mural nodules, absence of osseous invasion, and lack of abnormal FDG uptake on PET/CT imaging.

Tailgut cyst correctly accounted for the benign multilocular retrorectal retro-cystic mass, but failed to explain the separate contiguous cluster of smaller cysts infiltrating the left ischioanal fossa and subcutaneous perineum.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the separate resected left ischioanal and gluteal cystic lesions revealed an outer histiocytic inflammatory response surrounding a hydatid cyst, confirming primary perineal/ischioanal echinococcosis co-occurring with a benign developmental tailgut cyst.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old woman presents to a reproductive endocrinology and fertility clinic complaining of secondary amenorrhea persisting for 5 years, beginning at age 28. Menarche occurred at 14 years of age, followed by a regular menstrual cycle lasting 5 to 7 days requiring 2 to 3 pads daily without dysmenorrhea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given prolonged secondary amenorrhea and elevated prolactin level, but ruled out because neuroimaging demonstrated a completely normal pituitary gland without sellar or suprasellar mass lesions.

Considered as an ovarian cause of amenorrhea, but ruled out because the patient failed to bleed after a progesterone challenge and subsequently failed to experience withdrawal bleeding following a combined 21-day estrogen plus progesterone challenge, indicating an end-organ uterine outflow failure rather than hormonal deficiency.

diagnostic_pivot: Hysteroscopy revealed grade 4 dense intrauterine adhesions, and endometrial curettage pathology demonstrated granulomatous endometritis characterized by epithelioid histiocytes and Langhans multinucleated giant cells, establishing tuberculous endometritis in the setting of suspected pleural tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old Hispanic woman presents with a 4- to 5-month history of generalized pruritus and intermittent vague abdominal discomfort. She immigrated to the United States from Puerto Rico 32 years ago, with her last visit to the island 5 years prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of severe, intractable pruritus, but excluded by the complete absence of classical cutaneous excoriations, papules, web-space lesions, or diagnostic mite burrows.

Considered given pruritus with marked eosinophilia, but ruled out by lack of medication exposures, failure of response to antihistamines and skin product avoidance, and historical documentation of eosinophilia persisting across 7 years.

diagnostic_pivot: High-titer Strongyloides IgG serology confirmed chronic strongyloidiasis driven by decades of subclinical autoinfection, followed by complete clinical resolution and normalization of the eosinophil count after two days of oral ivermectin.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old boy residing in Dongfang county, Hainan province—a tropical region of southern China—presents with severe left parotid pain and facial swelling. He has never traveled outside the region.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a frequent cause of pediatric parotid enlargement, but ruled out by the unilateral, fluctuant, suppurative abscess formation with marked elevation of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (92 mm/1st hour).

Considered as the classical cause of acute bacterial parotid abscess, but argued against by the lack of antecedent dehydration, absence of intraoral ductal purulence or contiguous draining source, and lack of systemic fever.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical drainage yielded pus that grew non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli on blood agar, identified with >99% confidence by VITEK-2 and confirmed by 16S rRNA sequencing as Burkholderia pseudomallei, establishing pediatric parotid melioidosis linked to endemic freshwater exposure.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old male presents to the ophthalmology outpatient clinic with a 20-day history of progressive headache and diminution of vision. He denies fever, trauma, or altered sensorium.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a young patient presenting with headaches, papilledema, and absence of an obvious intracranial mass on routine MRI, but ruled out because neuroimaging demonstrated ventricular dilation and communicating hydrocephalus rather than slit-like ventricles.

Considered as an infectious cause of communicating hydrocephalus and elevated intracranial pressure, but excluded by the subacute afebrile course and complete lack of meningismus or systemic inflammatory signs.

diagnostic_pivot: High-resolution 3D constructive interference in steady state (CISS) MRI revealed an intraventricular non-enhancing ring lesion containing an eccentric hyperdense nodule representing the scolex in the fourth ventricle, establishing isolated intraventricular neurocysticercosis, which subsequently demonstrated intraventricular migration following shunt decompression.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old previously healthy Australian male presents with sudden onset of painless, patchy visual clouding (worse in the right eye) and floaters in the left eye. His ocular symptoms began on day 3 of an acute febrile illness contracted while traveling in Cambodia, characterized by high fever, severe headache, myalgias, and arthralgias.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected due to post-febrile visual loss, but excluded by the complete absence of a relative afferent pupillary defect, preserved color vision and brightness saturation, unswollen optic discs, and fundoscopic evidence of widespread perimacular intraretinal hemorrhages and microangiopathy.

Considered given anterior chamber reaction, vitritis, and retinal cotton wool spots, but excluded by the lack of antecedent autoimmune symptoms, noncontributory uveitis blood screens, and the acute temporal correlation with an imported viral thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Optical coherence tomography demonstrated hyperreflective lesions in the outer nuclear layer and photoreceptor segments encroaching on the retinal pigment epithelium (acute macular neuroretinopathy), confirming dengue fever-associated maculopathy and panuveitis which resolved concurrently with platelet count recovery.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old female presents with a palpable, long-standing mass in the periphery of her left breast that has been present for over 10 years and became painful over the past 8 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary concern for a growing, newly painful breast mass in a postmenopausal woman, but argued against by the lack of fixity to the chest wall, regular lobulated contour on mammography, absence of suspicious microcalcifications, and lack of regional axillary lymphadenopathy.

Considered as a benign cause of a longstanding well-circumscribed breast mass, but typical cysts or fibroadenomas lack internal detached floating parasitic membranes and circumferential daughter cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Breast ultrasound revealed pathognomonic features of hydatid disease including an internal detached membrane ('water lily' sign) and circumferential anechoic daughter cysts creating a wheel-spoke pattern, confirmed on MRI and surgical excision displaying characteristic daughter cysts.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 1-week history of persistent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Her past medical history is notable for an appendectomy and a previously known, untreated asymptomatic cystic lesion in the liver.

differentials.candidate: Hydatid Cyst Rupture into the Biliary Tract (Cystobiliary Fistula)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary suspected emergency diagnosis due to acute jaundice and RUQ pain in a patient with a known liver cyst, but definitively excluded when ERCP and abdominal MRI demonstrated normal bile ducts without ductal dilation, communicating fistulae, or intrabiliary hydatid debris.

Considered to account for the profound transaminase elevation exceeding 1,000 U/L, but ruled out by negative viral hepatitis serologies, negative tumor markers, and absence of any hepatotoxic medications or toxin exposures.

diagnostic_pivot: Spontaneous decline of bilirubin and transaminases supported a concurrent self-limited cryptogenic hepatitis, while subsequent exploratory surgery and histopathologic examination confirmed an intact, unruptured hepatic hydatid cyst without cystobiliary communication.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old female child from a low socioeconomic background is referred to an orthopedic clinic with a 1-week history of insidious-onset neck stiffness and minimal cervical pain. Her parents report a history of contact with an individual being treated for chronic pulmonary illness, but report no history of trauma, evening fevers, night sweats, anorexia, or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary diagnosis given a clear history of tuberculosis contact in a patient of low socioeconomic status, but argued against by the lack of fever, night sweats, or weight loss, a normal chest CT scan, and purely cystic imaging features rather than solid caseating granulomatous lesions.

Considered as the most common pediatric intramedullary mass lesions, but ruled out by the complete absence of progressive motor or sensory deficits and the presence of a well-circumscribed cystic lesion rather than an infiltrative or solid enhancing neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Cervical spine MRI demonstrated an eccentric intracystic T2-hypointense 'target'-like mural nodule representing the pathognomonic scolex, fulfilling absolute diagnostic criteria for solitary intramedullary neurocysticercosis, which was further corroborated by positive serum Ag-ELISA and symptom resolution on albendazole and steroids.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old male presented to the clinic with multiple papular lesions on his left cheek that had been present for three months and had gradually enlarged. Medical history was notable for a prior cutaneous lesion on the nose two years earlier, which had completely regressed following intralesional therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the multiple slightly elevated, rough papular lesions on the cheek in a pediatric patient, but excluded by the yellowish-brown granulomatous quality and parasitological demonstration of amastigotes.

Considered because chronic yellowish-brown facial papules and atrophic scarring strongly resemble cutaneous tuberculosis, but excluded by direct smear revealing protozoan amastigotes rather than acid-fast organisms.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when Giemsa staining of a parasitological smear of the cheek lesions demonstrated abundant intracellular amastigotes, confirming lupoid cutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old right-handed Hispanic male presented after experiencing a new-onset generalized seizure while driving. He had emigrated from Mexico 15 years prior to presentation and had not returned for 6 years; he had worked in several states across the United States before residing in Alabama for the past 11 years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the large intracranial mass causing mass effect and midline shift, but excluded by lack of peripheral contrast enhancement or restricted diffusion on MRI and unremarkable systemic staging CT.

Considered because cestode larval infections can cause large multiloculated intracranial cysts, but excluded by the absence of extracranial hepatic or pulmonary cysts on CT imaging and confirmation of cysticercosis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred with positive serum cysticercosis IgG antibody serology, followed by surgical resection and histopathologic demonstration of membranous racemose cyst walls containing microtriches and calcareous corpuscles without scolices.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old Hispanic male presented to the emergency department with frontal headache, fever, nausea, and vomiting that had been ongoing for two weeks. His medical history was notable for herpes zoster ophthalmicus two years prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to fever, headache, vomiting, and meningismus, but excluded by the 2-week subacute duration, normal peripheral white blood cell count, and CSF lymphocytic predominance (96% lymphocytes).

Considered given the lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein, but ruled out because viral meningitis typically features normal glucose, whereas this patient had marked hypoglycorrhachia (CSF glucose 37 mg/dL).
Both were documented and treated with penicillin and amphotericin/flucytosine, but neither accounted for persistent posterior fossa leptomeningeal enhancement and progressive cerebellar signs.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when CSF culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirmed by PCR restriction analysis (PRA-hsp65), establishing tuberculous meningitis as the coexisting etiology of chronic basilar meningitis.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old male from rural Guerrero, Mexico presented with a 10-year history of nodular lesions, progressive swelling, and draining sinuses involving the lower extremities, predominantly distributed on the left foot and right leg.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because aerobic actinomycetes are the most common cause of mycetoma in Mexico and cause identical sinus tracts with grains, but ruled out by direct microscopic examination and histopathology revealing thick fungal hyphae rather than fine bacterial filaments.

Considered given the decade-long history of draining sinuses and radiographic evidence of osteolysis and periostitis, but ruled out by the characteristic presence of discrete grains containing fungal colonies extruded through sinuses.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when direct mycological examination (KOH 10%) of the sinus discharge revealed black grains from the left foot and white grains from the opposite side, with culture and biopsy confirming eumycetomas caused by Madurella mycetomatis and Fusarium verticillioides.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old Syrian male immigrant presented with a two-month history of fever, shortness of breath, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. His medical history was unremarkable for chronic medical conditions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute shortness of breath, elevated inflammatory markers, and a right basal pulmonary consolidation on chest radiography, but ruled out when clinical deterioration continued despite intravenous antibiotic therapy and was traced to transdiaphragmatic rupture of a subcapsular hepatic cyst.

Considered due to the prolonged course of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, fever, and leukocytosis, but excluded by the presence of a well-defined cystic structure with laminar membrane detachment and daughter cysts rather than a liquefactive pyogenic abscess.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during surgical exploration, which revealed transdiaphragmatic rupture of a hepatic hydatid cyst with secondary cysts and laminar membrane detachment into the thoracic cavity, confirmed pathologically by necrotic cuticular membranes.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old kidney transplant recipient presented with progressive abdominal pain and significant involuntary weight loss of several weeks' duration. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the abdomen demonstrated multiple contrast-enhancing peritoneal nodules, large intraperitoneal soft-tissue masses, a hypodense lesion within the right adrenal gland, and prominent retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis because of an ulcerated colonic mass, peritoneal nodules, large intraperitoneal masses, and a suspected adrenal metastasis, but ruled out when serial endoscopic biopsies showed no dysplasia or malignant cells.

Considered given the immunosuppressed post-transplant status, bulky retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and ulcerated colonic lesion, but excluded by histopathology lacking lymphoid or neoplastic infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when Ziehl-Neelsen staining of targeted colonic biopsies revealed acid-fast bacteria, and Xpert MTB/RIF assay detected rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA, confirmed by rapid liquid culture.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male presented with a one-month history of low back pain, radiating pain to the right lower limb, and progressive weakness of the right lower limb for 20 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary alternative infectious etiology for a solitary intramedullary ring-enhancing spinal lesion with severe edema, but excluded based on positive CSF anti-cysticercal antibody testing and prompt lesion regression under albendazole and corticosteroid therapy.

Considered given the solitary ring-enhancing intramedullary mass causing progressive myelopathy without an identifiable scolex, but ruled out by lack of tumor progression and rapid clinical and radiologic resolution with conservative medical management alone.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when diagnostic cerebrospinal fluid analysis was positive for anti-cysticercal antibodies, establishing isolated intramedullary spinal neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old female presented to the emergency department in Puerto Rico with a 3-day history of fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anorexia. On physical examination, she appeared dehydrated with dry oral mucosa.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fever, acute abdominal pain, elevated amylase and lipase, and ultrasound evidence of cholelithiasis, but excluded as the primary cause because enzyme elevations were modest and could not explain the rapidly progressive multiorgan involvement, pulmonary hemorrhage, and marked thrombocytopenia.

differentials.candidate: Severe community-acquired pneumonia / Atypical respiratory tract infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient developed acute respiratory failure with bilateral confluent alveolar opacities on hospital day 3, but ruled out by negative blood and sputum cultures, negative mycoplasma IgM serology, and characteristic pulmonary hemorrhage.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when DNA specific to Leptospira interrogans was detected by PCR in early acute serum collected on illness day 2, subsequently corroborated by a convalescent microscopic agglutination test (MAT) titer of 3,200 against serogroup Australis.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old male farmer residing in southern Mauritania presented to the regional hospital with severe chronic arthralgia affecting the joints of the hands, associated with bilateral perforating plantar ulcers. His symptoms had evolved over seven years, initially presenting with hypopigmented maculopapular lesions and paresthesias at the interphalangeal extremities and on the plantar surfaces of the feet.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of long-standing hand arthralgias and severe joint deformities, but ruled out by the prominent cutaneous anesthesia, hypochromic macules, trophic perforating plantar ulcers, and hypertrophied nerve trunks.

differentials.candidate: Hereditary or diabetic peripheral sensory neuropathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic sensory loss, painless trophic plantar perforations, and distal phalangeal bone resorption, but excluded by the presence of hypopigmented cutaneous macules and bilateral palpable hypertrophy of major nerve trunks.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when clinical evaluation established two of the three cardinal World Health Organization criteria for leprosy: hypochromic anesthetic skin lesions and palpably hypertrophied peripheral nerve trunks.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male farmer residing in southern Mauritania presented with maculopapular and nodular skin lesions, accompanied by chest pain and a chronic productive cough. His cutaneous lesions had evolved over the past ten years, initially consisting of lichenoid lesions and multiple hypopigmented papules.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to facial lichenoid plaques mimicking lupus pernio in combination with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and pulmonary reticulonodular infiltrates, but ruled out by the pathognomonic finding of localized sensory loss within the cutaneous plaques.

differentials.candidate: Isolated cutaneous and pulmonary tuberculosis (lupus vulgaris)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because chronic productive cough, right bronchial rales, apical infiltrates, and chronic facial granulomatous lesions could represent single-organism disseminated tuberculosis, but excluded as the sole diagnosis because tuberculous lupus vulgaris does not produce localized cutaneous anesthesia.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when the patient was diagnosed with lepromatous leprosy based on the 10-year evolution of facial hypopigmented lesions with sensory loss, alongside concomitant active pulmonary tuberculosis manifested by productive cough, apical reticulonodular infiltrates, and hilar adenopathy.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old, well-nourished, well-developed female is brought to the medical examiner's facility for forensic evaluation following sudden, unexpected death. Past surgical history is notable for a remote right nephrectomy secondary to a motor vehicle accident.

differentials.candidate: Acute myocardial infarction / Coronary artery thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Gross examination of the heart demonstrated patent coronary arteries without atheroma or thrombus, intact valves, and no histological or gross signs of myocardial hyperemia, ischemia, fibrosis, or hypertrophy.

differentials.candidate: Acute poisoning / Toxic ingestion / Narcotic overdose
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multi-matrix postmortem toxicology screens for alcohol, narcotics, and other therapeutic or illicit substances across vitreous humor, gastric contents, urine, liver, and bile were entirely negative.

The obstructive intravascular masses causing saddle obstruction in the pulmonary arteries and right heart were not composed of fibrinous blood thrombi, but rather multiple intact, fluid-filled membranous cysts originating from the inferior vena cava.

Histopathological examination of the excised cystic emboli and hepatic cyst walls definitively identified the characteristic acellular laminated membrane containing viable protoscolices and hooklets, establishing hepatic hydatid disease with vascular rupture into the inferior vena cava and catastrophic pulmonary saddle embolization as the cause of sudden cardiac arrest.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old postmenopausal female of Filipino origin presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of progressive abdominal bloating, vomiting, and high fevers. She denies dysuria, hematuria, or altered bowel habits.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the combination of postmenopausal status, elevated serum CA-125, ascites, and a complex multiseptated 22 x 13 cm cystic ovarian mass was suspicious for ovarian malignancy, surgical resection confirmed a benign neoplasm without malignant epithelial proliferation.

Although initial CT suggested localized omental necrosis due to prominent focal fat stranding, laparotomy demonstrated diffuse pelvic inflammatory deposits and caseating granulomatous peritonitis rather than isolated vascular thrombosis or ischemic tissue necrosis.

Histopathologic evaluation of the resected pelvic and peritoneal tissues revealed extensive necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, and microbiological culture of the peritoneal fluid yielded Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming peritoneal tuberculosis in a patient with a coexisting benign cystadenoma.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of progressive dyspnea, generalized weakness, subjective fevers, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. His past medical history is significant for end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis, cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and benign prostatic hyperplasia.

differentials.candidate: Decompensated portal hypertension / Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient has pre-existing cirrhosis and hepatitis C, the ascitic fluid revealed a low serum-ascites albumin gradient (<1.1 g/dL), a normal polymorphonuclear neutrophil count (<250/mm³), and negative bacterial culture, ruling out uncomplicated portal hypertension transudate and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

Abdominal CT imaging demonstrated diffuse nodular peritoneal implants mimicking carcinomatosis, but multiple cytological examinations of pleural fluid and ascites revealed no malignant cells, and core tissue biopsy identified granulomatous inflammation rather than carcinoma.

Despite false-negative ascites fluid ADA (3.4 IU/L), smear, and PCR, ultrasound/CT-guided omental tissue biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli, and subsequent tissue culture confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old man presents to the clinic in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, with a recurrent non-healing wound infection on the plantar aspect of his right foot. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 22 years prior, managed on mixed insulin for the preceding three months, and has a history of hypertension and peripheral artery disease.

differentials.candidate: Common diabetic neuroischemic foot ulcer / Pseudomonas aeruginosa superinfection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although initial superficial wound swab yielded scanty growth of Pseudomonas sp., targeted antibiotic therapy with ciprofloxacin and cefixime resulted in zero clinical improvement, indicating colonization rather than the true primary pathogen.
Plain radiographs of the right foot showed no bony destruction or periosteal reaction, and the ulcer extended to muscle without bony involvement.

Repeat deep microbiological wound swab culture demonstrated bipolar-staining Gram-negative rods growing characteristically dry, wrinkled, purple colonies on Ashdown agar with a sweetish-putrid odor, and nested PCR targeting the 16S rRNA gene definitively identified Burkholderia pseudomallei.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old male of Indian origin presents with acute onset of left eyelid drooping and diplopia. He has a history of prior treatment default for chronic peritonitis, but no other known past medical conditions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's demographic origin in India and intracranial nodular/racemose-enhancing lesions, neurocysticercosis was a primary consideration, but specific cysticercosis immunoglobulin G antibody testing was non-reactive.
Highly destructive basal meningitis with cranial nerve palsy frequently occurs in immunocompromised hosts, but retroviral screening was negative.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Intracranial Tuberculomas and Tuberculous Meningitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Markedly elevated CSF adenosine deaminase (ADA 23.3 IU/L) together with positive CSF polymerase chain reaction confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex established intracranial tuberculomas complicated by tuberculous meningitis.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of rapid enlargement of a pre-existing goiter over recent weeks, without dysphagia, dysphonia, or dyspnea. She also reports a productive cough for the past two weeks.

differentials.candidate: Malignant thyroid neoplasm with pulmonary metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid expansion of a pre-existing goiter associated with multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules prompted a high suspicion for invasive thyroid cancer or anaplastic transformation, but histopathologic evaluation of the resected thyroid gland revealed benign hyperplasia with granulomas rather than malignant neoplasia.

Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis typically presents with acute anterior neck pain, tenderness, and transient thyrotoxicosis, whereas this patient presented with an indolent, painless plunging mass, normal thyroid hormone levels, and lung biopsies demonstrating true caseous necrosis.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Concomitant Tuberculosis of the Thyroid Gland and Lung
differentials.rule_out_reason: Surgical histopathology of both the excised thyroid tissue and minithoracotomy lung biopsies demonstrated epithelioid cell granulomas with giant cells and prominent caseous necrosis, confirming active mycobacterial tuberculosis involving both organs despite negative initial sputum smears.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old biparous woman presents two months postpartum following an uneventful full-term pregnancy and spontaneous vaginal delivery with severe, debilitating right-sided low back pain radiating down the posterior right lower extremity in a sciatic distribution.

differentials.candidate: Postpartum sciatic neuropathy / Lumbar disc herniation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although presenting with classic radiating low back pain that led to initial symptomatic treatment, CT imaging showed normal intervertebral discs and identified a massive 720-mL retroperitoneal fluid collection as the true compressive etiology.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial psoas abscess (Staphylococcus aureus / Enteric polymicrobial)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A typical acute pyogenic etiology was ruled out by the afebrile presentation, normal procalcitonin level, persistently sterile purulent aspirate on multiple standard bacterial and fungal cultures, and rapid recurrence of the abscess despite parenteral broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Primary Tuberculous Psoas Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Despite initial negative aspirate AFB stain, PCR, and cultures, open surgical drainage with full-thickness biopsy of the fibrotic abscess wall demonstrated characteristic epithelioid giant cells and caseous necrosis, establishing primary tuberculous psoas abscess without osseous spinal involvement.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old Saudi male residing in the Jizan province presents with a 3-week history of daily intermittent fevers accompanied by nocturnal shaking chills and rigors that fail to respond to antipyretics.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's direct contact with goats and sheep, consumption of unpasteurized goat milk, and presentation with undulating fevers and hepatosplenomegaly in Saudi Arabia, brucellosis was strongly suspected; however, specific Brucella serologic testing and bone marrow cultures were negative.
Endemic vector exposure, nocturnal fevers, chills, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly suggested plasmodial infection, but repeated peripheral blood smears and blood cultures were negative.

differentials.candidate: Systemic autoimmune flare / Lupus nephritis with secondary HLH
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pre-existing glomerulonephritis, cytopenias, and high ferritin raised concern for an autoimmune flare or systemic vasculitis, but comprehensive autoimmune serologies including ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, anti-SSA/SSB, and cryoglobulins were negative.

In an immunosuppressed patient from the Jizan endemic focus with progressive pancytopenia and splenomegaly, diagnostic bone marrow smear was falsely negative for amastigotes, but liver biopsy demonstrated granulomatous hepatitis with extramedullary hematopoiesis, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmed anti-Leishmania antibodies, and targeted liposomal amphotericin B resulted in complete clinical recovery.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old postpartum woman presents to a hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, with a 4-day history of acute febrile illness, diffuse rash, and eye redness. Ten months prior, she delivered a healthy infant via uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfeeding.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although co-circulating in Southeast Asia and causing acute fever, retro-orbital pain, and rash, classic dengue typically presents with high unremitting fever, severe myalgias ('breakbone fever'), and prominent thrombocytopenia or plasma leakage, whereas this patient exhibited low-grade fever, benign self-limited clinical course, and prominent non-purulent conjunctivitis.

While chikungunya causes acute febrile exanthems with polyarthralgia, it typically manifests with incapacitating, severe peripheral arthritis, whereas conjunctival hyperemia and mild arthralgia in the setting of spousal exposure favored an alternative flaviviral pathogen.

The diagnosis was definitively confirmed by molecular detection of viral RNA via real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) across multiple maternal body fluids including expressed breast milk, serum, and urine.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old man presents to the outpatient gastroenterology clinic with a two-year history of progressive abdominal distension. The abdominal bloating and distension worsen noticeably after meals, particularly following the ingestion of dairy products and milk.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the abrupt transition between a massively dilated sigmoid colon and a collapsed rectum suggested an obstructing colorectal mass, complete colonoscopy and cross-sectional CT confirmed a patent lumen and normal rectal vault without neoplastic masses.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic adult megacolon / Adult-onset Hirschsprung disease / Severe hypothyroid dysmotility
differentials.rule_out_reason: While severe chronic colonic dilation without mechanical blockage in a hypothyroid patient raised suspicion for enteric neuromuscular dysmotility or adult aganglionosis, histopathologic evaluation demonstrated chronic parasitic infection rather than absent ganglion cells or primary visceral myopathy.

Surgical histopathology of the resected sigmoid colon unexpectedly established chronic schistosomiasis with intramural egg deposition as the underlying cause of severe inflammatory neuroenteric injury and acquired megacolon, corroborated by a high Schistosoma antibody serologic titer of 1:1024.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old patient originally from the Republic of Congo presented to the emergency department with severe cramping abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea for 3 days, followed by cessation of bowel movements.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Adhesions account for the vast majority of small bowel obstructions but typically occur following previous abdominal surgery. Inspection of this patient revealed a virgin abdomen without prior surgical history.

differentials.candidate: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor or Mesenteric Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: An isolated 3-cm mesenteric mass causing bowel tethering and obstruction can represent neoplasia; however, the presence of concurrent chronic cough, prominent upper-lobe cavitary pulmonary disease, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers suggests a unified systemic infectious process rather than isolated intra-abdominal malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Exploratory laparotomy confirmed small bowel volvulus caused by tethering to a mesenteric mass resembling caseating necrosis. Biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis with Langhans giant cells, while sputum smear and culture confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old previously healthy female presented to an emergency department in Sergipe, Brazil in January 2016 reporting a 3-day history of high fever (>39°C), generalized joint pain, arthralgia, and an erythematous cutaneous rash.

differentials.candidate: Catheter-Associated Upper Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Upper extremity venous thrombosis is overwhelmingly provoked by mechanical vascular endothelial disruption from indwelling lines or recent cannulation. The patient had no instrumentation or infusions in the involved limb.

Chikungunya is a common co-circulating arbovirus presenting with high fevers, incapacitating arthralgia, and rash, and can incite inflammatory vascular responses. However, specific viral reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction excluded Chikungunya and demonstrated Zika infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Development of unprovoked right brachial vein thrombosis immediately following an acute febrile exanthematous illness prompted viral molecular diagnostic evaluation, which established the diagnosis by PCR.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male presented to an emergency department in Sergipe, Brazil with a 5-day history of fever, asthenia, headache, and polyarthralgia involving the elbows, knees, and shoulders. Over the course of 5 days, his arthralgias intensified and became accompanied by new-onset pain in the left calf and swelling of both lower extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute deep vein thrombosis is commonly provoked by orthopedic surgery, active malignancy, trauma, or prolonged stasis. This patient lacked any traditional predisposing mechanical or systemic risk factors, pointing toward an acute inflammatory-infectious trigger.

Chikungunya is a prevalent arbovirus in northeastern Brazil known to induce severe polyarthralgias and associated venous thromboembolism during acute infection, but specific viral testing confirmed an alternate etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The sudden development of popliteal vein thrombosis during an acute febrile polyarthralgia illness in an endemic region led to diagnostic confirmation via viral testing positive for Zika virus.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old male presented with a 9-month history of multifocal lower-extremity pain, localized swelling, and palpable masses in the bilateral thighs and calves. The swellings had gradually increased in size and number over several months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An outside MRI initially suggested rhabdomyolysis due to a history of strenuous exercise. However, serum creatine kinase, aldolase, and transaminases were completely normal, and an indolent 9-month progression of discrete muscular masses is inconsistent with acute rhabdomyolysis.

Diffuse abnormal muscular signals on MRI can represent inflammatory myopathy. However, muscle enzymes were normal, electromyography showed normal sensory and motor nerve conduction without irritable myopathic motor units, and the patient had localized pseudo-tumoral masses rather than symmetric proximal weakness.

diagnostic_pivot: Deep surgical biopsy of the gastrocnemius muscle demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells and epithelioid histiocytes. While acid-fast staining and tuberculin skin testing were negative, tissue PCR and culture of the calf muscle mass confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male from Sri Lanka with a 14-year history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented with progressive swelling of the left non-dominant hand and wrist of 7 months' duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In Sri Lanka, diabetic hosts are highly predisposed to subacute or chronic osteomyelitis and septic arthritis caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei. Specific serological testing was evaluated and proved negative.

Destructive lytic lesions confined to the carpal and metacarpal bones can mimic bone tumors or synovial sarcoma; however, the presence of multiple carpal involvement with focal fluid collections and high inflammatory markers points to an indolent infectious synovitis rather than a solitary neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Synovial exploration revealed gross intraoperative caseous material, histology demonstrated caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells, and rapid molecular testing (Xpert MTB/RIF) and culture confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 8-month-old male infant was evaluated for a 3-month history of a generalized, progressive cutaneous eruption. The infant had been born at 39 weeks gestation following an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, had reached normal developmental milestones, and had not received prior medications.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Infantile atopic dermatitis is a common cause of pruritic, excoriated eczematous plaques, but severe diffuse hyperkeratotic crusting with prominent palmoplantar and groin involvement is atypical. Furthermore, eczema does not transmit as an acute pruritic interdigital rash to adult household contacts.

Widespread hyperkeratotic plaques in an infant can suggest an inherited keratinization defect or infantile psoriasis; however, the delayed onset at 5 months of age and clustered presentation of pruritic papules in cohabiting parents and caregiver point directly to an infectious/contagious infestation.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of mineral oil skin scrapings and subsequent histopathological examination of a skin biopsy demonstrated abundant epidermal ectoparasites and ova, establishing the diagnosis of crusted scabies.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old male with a known history of sickle cell anemia maintained on daily folic acid presented to the emergency department in Jizan, Saudi Arabia, complaining of fever, nausea, headache, and yellowish discoloration of the sclera.

differentials.candidate: Acute Sickle Cell Hemolytic or Hepatic Crisis
differentials.rule_out_reason: While patients with sickle cell disease frequently experience hemolytic crises with jaundice and acute anemia, an uncomplicated sickle crisis does not explain the concurrent severe thrombocytopenia and sustained high fevers in a malaria-endemic locality.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis / Fulminant Hepatic Failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Profound jaundice with mixed hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 600 μmol/L) can indicate acute viral hepatitis; however, serum aminotransferases were only mildly elevated (AST 89 U/L, ALT 78 U/L), which is inconsistent with acute viral hepatic necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct peripheral blood film microscopy demonstrated abundant ring-form trophozoites with a 10% parasitemia index, establishing the diagnosis of severe falciparum malaria.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female was referred for evaluation after a routine follow-up chest computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a new pulmonary mass. Six months earlier, she had presented with right-sided chest pain of one year's duration, at which time chest CT demonstrated a 1.7 x 1.4 cm nodule in the right upper lobe, while the right lower lobe was clear.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A new, rapidly expanding 3.4-cm pulmonary mass in a 52-year-old raises major suspicion for primary lung cancer. However, the patient was a lifelong non-smoker, serum tumor markers were negative, and the lesion developed in the setting of successful radiographic regression of her primary nodule.

Immunocompromised or treated lung cavities can develop secondary fungal masses or mycomas. However, the patient remained afebrile without systemic inflammation, and specific fungal surveillance biomarkers were completely normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous CT-guided lung biopsy of the new lower lobe mass revealed necrotizing caseating granulomatous inflammation without malignancy, confirming a paradoxical upgrading reaction during anti-tuberculosis therapy, with subsequent spontaneous mass regression on continued treatment.

clinical_summary: A 77-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of worsening pain and swelling in the medial aspect of the left thigh, progressive lameness, and intermittent fever. Prior to presentation, he had undergone two needle aspirations at a community hospital with only temporary symptomatic relief followed by rapid relapse.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Septic Coxitis or Pyogenic Iliopsoas Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: A high CRP (>150 mg/L) with hip effusion and iliopsoas signal changes strongly suggests typical pyogenic infection (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus); however, the subacute 2-month course, lack of acute fulminant systemic toxicity, and negative aerobic/anaerobic blood cultures make common pyogenic bacteria unlikely.

Given the patient's age and history of degenerative lumbar spine disease, musculoskeletal or neurogenic pain was considered; however, this cannot account for the marked systemic inflammation (CRP > 150 mg/L, ESR 60 mm/hr) or MRI evidence of active acetabular synovitis and iliopsoas infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Joint exploration surgery revealed gross caseous material and granulomatous inflammation involving the femoral neck, femoral head, and capsule, while ultra-deep metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified specific Mycobacterium tuberculosis sequence reads in synovial fluid.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male originally from a rural area presented with a 12-month history of mild, intermittent abdominal pain accompanied by progressive abdominal distension and a sensation of generalized abdominal heaviness.

differentials.candidate: Primary Mesenteric Cyst or Retroperitoneal Cystadenoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: A massive 27-cm intra-abdominal cystic mass in an adult can mimic a mesenteric or retroperitoneal cystic neoplasm. However, simple or neoplastic mesenteric cysts lack internal undulating membranes and thick peripheral calcifications, and do not account for multifocal companion hepatic cysts.
