Abdominal distension with diffuse dullness on percussion and massive fluid accumulation can indicate mucinous peritoneal carcinomatosis; however, the well-circumscribed cystic capsule, internal membranes, parietal calcification, and absence of constitutional cachexia favor a chronic parasitic etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: CT characteristics showing an exophytic multi-stage calcified cyst with internal membranes combined with multiple hepatic cysts, positive parasitic serology, and surgical resection confirming an exophytic liver hydatid cyst extending into the inframesocolic compartment established the diagnosis of Echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old previously healthy male residing in Fortaleza, Ceará State, Brazil, presented to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, adynamia, myalgias, and progressive deterioration of his general condition.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute fever, hemodynamic instability with refractory shock, and multi-serosal effusions. Ruled out by sterile blood cultures and successful clinical recovery in the absence of antibiotics.

differentials.candidate: Common Viral or Parasitic Myocarditis (Coxsackievirus, Rubella, Chagas Disease, HIV, CMV, EBV, Toxoplasmosis, Hepatitis B and C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute viral prodrome leading to diffuse ST elevations, depressed left ventricular ejection fraction, and pericardial effusion. Ruled out by negative comprehensive viral and protozoan serologic investigations.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when serological testing of acute serum confirmed acute arboviral infection with positive anti-dengue IgM and IgG antibodies in a young patient presenting with acute myocarditis and cardiogenic shock.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old Thai female with locally advanced stage III-B breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide chemotherapy, along with lamivudine for chronic hepatitis B carrier status, presented to the hospital 10 days after her third chemotherapy cycle with acute fatigue, diarrhea, and fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the acute onset of diarrhea, high fever, and leukopenia in an oncology patient with recent hospital admissions and prior broad-spectrum beta-lactam exposure. Ruled out by a negative stool toxin assay.

differentials.candidate: Standard Enteric Gram-Negative Neutropenic Sepsis (e.g., Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacteriaceae)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary cause of septic shock and neutropenic enterocolitis with pyuria. Ruled out as the definitive causative pathogen by microbiological identification of a distinct endemic tropical agent.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when blood and urine cultures grew Burkholderia pseudomallei, followed by cross-sectional imaging demonstrating disseminated infection with multiple splenic and hepatic microabscesses.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male from a pastoral community in Seda County, Sichuan Province, China, presented to the hospital for a routine physical examination. He reported no abdominal pain, nausea, weight loss, fever, or other physical discomfort.

differentials.candidate: Primary or Secondary Hepatic Malignancy (Hepatocellular Carcinoma, Metastatic Carcinoma, Hepatic Sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of an infiltrative multicentric hepatic mass invading segments 4-5-6 associated with regional hepatogastric lymphadenopathy mimicking metastatic cancer. Ruled out by postoperative histopathologic examination which demonstrated parasitic larval alveolar structures without malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Benign Hepatic Lesions (Simple Cyst, Hemangioma, Lipoma, Pyogenic Liver Abscess)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential of space-occupying hepatic mass lesions in a young patient. Ruled out by the infiltrative solid-cystic behavior, presence of regional necrotic lymphadenopathy, and absence of purulent bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon surgical exploration revealing a 7.5 x 7.0 cm mass adhering to the gallbladder base and a cystic hepatogastric lymph node containing gray-yellow chylous fluid, with histological confirmation of alveolar echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man presented to the clinic with a continuous headache that had persisted for the preceding 15 days, complicated by the acute onset of fever, vomiting, and progressive alteration of consciousness over the last two days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute fever, altered mentation, positive meningeal signs, elevated CSF protein, and marked hypoglycorrhachia. Ruled out by a subacute two-week prodrome, failure of standard empiric antimicrobial therapy, presence of a parenchymal cerebellar lesion, and microbiological confirmation of mycobacterial infection.
Considered because of subacute headache, depressed consciousness, and focal intracranial pathology. Ruled out by marked CSF hypoglycorrhachia and definitive molecular detection of mycobacterial DNA.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when CSF PCR and Quantiferon tests yielded positive results for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, later confirmed by positive culture yielding drug-susceptible organisms.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old man with no previously diagnosed medical conditions presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of high fever, myalgias, nausea, and vomiting, accompanied by right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

differentials.candidate: Acute Calculous Cholecystitis or Ascending Cholangitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fever, right hypochondrial tenderness, marked hyperbilirubinemia, and procalcitonin >60 ng/L. Ruled out by abdominal ultrasound demonstrating the absence of gallstones, sludge, or biliary dilation, paired with laboratory evidence of Coombs-negative intravascular hemolysis.

Considered due to travel to South Asia, acute gastrointestinal symptoms, profound procalcitonin elevation, and high inflammatory markers. Ruled out by the identification of intraerythrocytic protozoal parasites on microscopic smear.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when peripheral blood smear microscopy directly identified Plasmodium vivax at 1.2% parasitemia (concomitant with positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR), with prompt clinical resolution following intravenous artesunate and artemether-lumefantrine.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male residing in Conakry, Guinea, who shared a single bedroom with a 33-year-old male friend, presented with a 5-day history of acute fever, intense headache, dyspnea, joint pain, and profound physical asthenia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect due to high regional endemicity, acute fever, headache, and severe arthralgias. Ruled out by lack of response to standard outpatient antimalarial chemotherapy.

Considered due to persistent high fever, prostration, and household cluster of gastrointestinal illness with diarrhea and abdominal pain. Ruled out by lack of improvement on empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and confirmatory molecular detection of a filovirus.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon performing RT-PCR testing at the specialized treatment center, which confirmed acute filoviral infection with Ebola Zaire virus in both individuals.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old gentleman with a medical history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of intermittent fevers with rigors, generalized headache, progressive disorientation, malaise, nausea, and vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, altered mentation, rigors, borderline hypotension, and thrombocytopenia in an elderly diabetic patient. Ruled out by normal chest imaging, absent bacteremia, and rapid identification of severe intraerythrocytic protozoal parasitemia.

Considered in light of his subsequent acute abdomen with subcapsular and intrasplenic hematoma. Ruled out as an external traumatic event by history, confirming spontaneous pathology secondary to severe infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear, which revealed heavy Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia (>1000 trophozoites/200 WBC), establishing the diagnosis of severe falciparum malaria with cerebral involvement.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old previously healthy adult presented for evaluation of progressive, inflammatory-type lumbar back pain persisting for the previous two months in the context of deterioration of general condition. The clinical interview revealed a potential close contact exposure to an individual with a chronic respiratory illness six months prior.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Spondylodiscitis and Psoas Abscess (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus, Enterobacteriaceae)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the most common etiology of destructive spondylodiscitis with psoas abscesses. Ruled out by pus aspirated from the psoas collections remaining sterile after 4 days of incubation on blood and chocolate agar under aerobic and anaerobic conditions.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Malignancy (Metastatic Carcinoma or Multiple Myeloma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute onset, deterioration of general condition, elevated sedimentation rate, and multilevel spinal destruction. Ruled out by classic contiguous intervertebral disc involvement with bilateral psoas fluid collections, followed by microbiological demonstration of an infectious mycobacterial etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when percutaneous CT-guided aspirate was subjected to GeneXpert MTB/RIF real-time PCR, which was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis without rifampicin resistance mutations, subsequently confirmed by culture on Lowenstein-Jensen and liquid VersaTREK media.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male residing in Tancredo Neves, State of Bahia, Brazil, presented for hospitalization with a widespread eruption of painless, ulcerated skin lesions. Two years prior, he had been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) on the basis of diffuse bullous skin lesions, polyarthritis involving the distal interphalangeal joints, and significant proteinuria (399 mg/day), for which he was receiving chronic...

differentials.candidate: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Cutaneous Flare (Bullous SLE / Cutaneous Vasculitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect given the patient's established history of SLE on maintenance mycophenolate mofetil. Ruled out because the current lesions were non-tender ulcerations rather than classic autoimmune blisters, failed to improve with immunosuppression, and tested positive on protozoal molecular assays.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pyogenic Bacterial Skin Infection (Ecthyma / Impetigo)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the crusted, exudative morphology of the facial and lip lesions and the presence of fever. While empiric cephalexin resolved the superimposed secondary pyogenic component, the deep underlying ulcerations remained unchanged.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred following tissue biopsies of the left nasal mucosa and right lower extremity ulcer on hospital day 3, which yielded positive PCR and a positive Montenegro intradermal test, confirming disseminated leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male residing in Mundo Novo, State of Bahia, Brazil, presented to the stomatology clinic of a university referral hospital with progressive localized facial pain, nasal obstruction, odynophagia, and dysphagia.

differentials.candidate: Head and Neck Malignancy (Squamous Cell Carcinoma or Mucosal Lymphoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the invasive, destructive, and friable presentation of the palate, uvula, and nasal mucosa in an older male. Ruled out by histopathologic examination of the palate, which demonstrated an inflammatory reaction without neoplastic or atypical cells.

differentials.candidate: Endemic Deep Mycosis (Paracoccidioidomycosis) or HIV-Associated Opportunistic Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the concurrent mucosal and cutaneous ulcerations with regional geographic distribution in Brazil. Ruled out by a negative HIV serological screen and a strongly positive leishmanin skin test.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when a palate biopsy confirmed a non-specific erosive chronic inflammatory process, and the patient tested positive for the Montenegro skin reaction, confirming mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old Caucasian woman, currently unemployed, from Salvador, State of Bahia, Brazil, is admitted to the hospital with painful oral and nasal mucosal ulcerations, recurrent back lesions, and neck swelling.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Deep endemic mycoses are common causes of chronic mucosal ulcerations of the upper aerodigestive tract and regional lymphadenopathy in South America, but fungal cultures and microbiological investigations were negative.

differentials.candidate: Oral mucosal malignancy / Squamous cell carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic non-healing orofacial ulcers with regional lymphadenopathy in an adult strongly suggest neoplastic disease, but histopathologic evaluation of oral lesions failed to demonstrate neoplastic features.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis with HIV co-infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: The persistent and refractory mucosal ulcerations were driven by severe immunosuppression from undiagnosed HIV co-infection in a patient with biopsy-confirmed Leishmania braziliensis, which responded to antiretroviral therapy and liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old Caucasian boy from Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, presents for medical evaluation of a persistent, pruritic lesion on his upper lip that has been present for six months. The lesion initially began as a small erythematous patch and has gradually enlarged.

differentials.candidate: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) cheilitis / Herpes labialis
differentials.rule_out_reason: HSV is the most frequent cause of localized recurrent lip lesions in children, but it was ruled out by complete lack of response to dedicated topical antiviral therapy and an atypically chronic 6-month duration.
Secondary bacterial pyoderma or chronic impetigo can cause crusted or hyperemic perioral lesions, but the lesion worsened despite first-line cephalosporin coverage.

The diagnosis was confirmed by a positive Montenegro skin test, demonstrating endemic cutaneous leishmaniasis of the upper lip that achieved clinical remission after liposomal amphotericin B following antimonial toxicity.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old Caucasian man, currently unemployed, presents to the clinic with widespread, eruptive skin lesions and painful mouth ulcers accompanied by systemic symptoms. Six years earlier, he was treated for an isolated skin nodule on his right leg with a 20-day course of targeted antimicrobial therapy, which resulted in complete lesion resolution.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated opportunistic fungal infection (e.g., Histoplasmosis, Cryptococcosis) or Kaposi Sarcoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread mucocutaneous ulcerations with fever and weight loss typically suggest severe immunodeficiency or disseminated fungal disease, but the patient was documented to be immunocompetent and free of other infections.

differentials.candidate: Secondary / Tertiary Syphilis or Systemic Granulomatous Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multifocal papular rash with mucosal mucous patches and constitutional symptoms mimics treponemal dissemination, but progression occurred in a patient with established reactivity to endemic protozoa without secondary co-infections.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis (Disseminated Leishmania braziliensis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Definitive diagnosis was established by PCR positivity for Leishmania braziliensis from the eyelid lesion, confirming mucosal and cutaneous dissemination that ultimately achieved complete remission after liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old Caucasian woman, unemployed, presents to the university hospital for admission due to non-healing, enlarging ulcerated lesions on her face and right leg. Her medical history is notable for diabetes mellitus, hypertension, congestive heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and spastic paraparesis secondary to human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) infection.

differentials.candidate: Primary bacterial ecthyma gangrenosum / Necrotizing staphylococcal-proteus soft tissue infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial pathogens were isolated from the lesions and blood, but these represented fatal secondary hospital-associated superinfections complicating the pre-existing chronic protozoal ulcerations.

differentials.candidate: HTLV-1 associated Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL) / Cutaneous T-cell malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given her HTLV-1 retroviral carrier status with paraparesis, chronic enlarging malar ulcers could represent neoplastic lymphoid infiltration, but the ulceration was confirmed to be infectious in origin.
The underlying diagnosis was established by a positive Montenegro intradermal skin test, confirming endemic mucocutaneous leishmaniasis complicated by renal toxicity and fatal secondary bacteremia.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old man of mixed ethnicity, currently unemployed and previously healthy, presents to the hospital with a two-month history of widespread, evolving skin and oral lesions. The illness began as an erythematous-crusted lesion over the mental protuberance of the chin that progressively spread over two months to involve the frontal and occipital scalp, nasal septum, ears, hands, and lower extremities.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic Melanoma / Primary Cutaneous Malignancy with distant metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient indeed possessed a primary cutaneous malignancy confirmed on biopsy of the plantar foot with regional lymph node involvement, but this did not account for the widespread infectious mucocutaneous ulcerations which resolved with antiparasitic therapy.

differentials.candidate: Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: An exophytic nodule in the labial mucosa with adjacent mucosal ulcers and hard lymphadenopathy strongly mimicked head-and-neck carcinoma, but the lesions represented inflammatory granulomatous changes rather than mucosal carcinoma.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis (coexisting with Cutaneous Melanoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of disseminated mucocutaneous leishmaniasis was confirmed by a positive Montenegro skin test and outside PCR analysis, leading to successful treatment with liposomal amphotericin B concurrently with surgical management of his independent melanoma.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old child presents to the hospital with painful neck stiffness and persistent fever for three weeks. There has been no alteration in general condition, anorexia, or weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Bacterial Spondylodiscitis / Deep Cervical Space Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked leukocytosis (16,000/mm³) and markedly elevated CRP (200 mg/L) with fever initially suggested acute pyogenic infection, but plain radiographs were normal, the clinical condition was preserved over three weeks, and non-invasive cultures were negative.

differentials.candidate: Primary Bone Neoplasm (e.g., Osteoid Osteoma, Osteoblastoma, Ewing Sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Posterior arch vertebral lesions with cortical erosion in children frequently represent bone neoplasms, but open exploration revealed an inflammatory collection rather than tumor.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Spinal Tuberculosis (Pott's Disease of the Posterior Arch)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Definitive diagnosis was established during surgical biopsy, which revealed an interspinous collection with histopathology confirming tuberculosis disease, successfully treated with 12 months of anti-tubercular chemotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old Newar housewife from Kathmandu, Nepal, with no known chronic comorbidities, presents to the emergency department with a 20-day history of cough with occasional sputum production and a 10-day history of low-grade fever.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV) / HIV-associated Hepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked elevation of AST (605 U/L) and ALT (308 U/L) initially suggested acute viral hepatitis co-infection, but comprehensive viral serologies were entirely non-reactive.

differentials.candidate: Toxin / Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI) or Alcoholic Hepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe transaminitis can result from xenobiotic exposure, but the patient had zero exposure to alcohol, acetaminophen, herbal compounds, or hepatotoxins.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Tuberculosis-Associated Transaminitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis was confirmed by sputum smear revealing 3+ acid-fast bacilli and GeneXpert detection of Rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis; remarkably, transaminases normalized following initiation of standard 4-drug anti-tubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old previously healthy woman presents to the department of critical care medicine with a five-day history of acute fever, productive cough, progressive shortness of breath, recurrent vomiting, abnormal involuntary body movements, and rapid loss of consciousness.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Bacterial / Meningococcal Meningitis and Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe septic shock with leukocytosis (25,000/mm³) and meningeal signs suggested fulminant bacterial meningitis, but CSF analysis showed a viral/lymphocytic-pattern meningoencephalitis rather than pyogenic bacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Thyrotoxic Crisis / Primary Thyroid Storm
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient met criteria for thyroid storm (Burch-Wartofsky score of 55), but hyperthyroidism alone does not account for alveolar pneumonia and meningoencephalitis, serving instead as a complication triggered by acute infection.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Scrub Typhus Meningoencephalitis with Secondary Thyroid Storm
differentials.rule_out_reason: The unifying diagnosis of scrub typhus was established by positive IgM serology, demonstrating Orientia tsutsugamushi infection presenting as meningoencephalitis, multiorgan dysfunction, bilateral pneumonia, and precipitating thyroid storm.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old previously healthy adult is referred to the head and neck clinic for evaluation of a right-sided cervical neck mass. The mass was noticed incidentally and has been slowly enlarging without pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Isolated, rubbery, painless jugular-carotid lymphadenopathy in a young adult with preserved constitutional health strongly mimics a lymphoproliferative disorder, but histologic architecture showed granulomatous mycobacterial infection rather than malignant lymphocytes.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic Head and Neck Carcinoma / Reactive Pyogenic Adenitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cervical node enlargement can herald occult mucosal head and neck cancer or bacterial adenitis, but detailed ENT evaluation was clear, and isolated nodal involvement was confirmed without other systemic sites.

The diagnosis was definitively established by an excisional cervical lymph node biopsy in the ENT unit, which histologically confirmed lymph node tuberculosis and prompted successful anti-tubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old man from Chhapra, Bihar, India, presents to the outpatient clinic with multiple non-pruritic nodular skin eruptions across his face, hands, and abdomen that have developed over several weeks.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Disseminated facial and acral nodular skin lesions in Bihar classically mimic lepromatous leprosy, but sensory perception over all cutaneous lesions was completely preserved, ruling out mycobacterial neural involvement.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Granulomatous / Autoimmune Diseases (Syphilis, Tuberculosis, Sarcoidosis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Granulomatous cutaneo-ocular diseases cause nodular eruptions and anterior uveitis, but routine serological and autoimmune screening (Mantoux test, VDRL, ANA, chest radiography) were non-reactive.
Definitive diagnosis was established by demonstration of Leishman-Donovan bodies on skin smear microscopy and high parasite load on qPCR, confirming PKDL following visceral leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old Caucasian man was referred to the outpatient endocrinology clinic following the incidental detection of an abdominal mass during an evaluation for abdominal pain. His past medical history was notable for gastroesophageal reflux disease, Barrett esophagus, hiatus hernia managed with omeprazole, a sleeve gastrectomy performed five years prior, a cholecystectomy three years prior, and tobacco use.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis based on CT imaging showing a para-aortic retroperitoneal lesion between the celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery; ruled out by normal 24-hour urine metanephrines, catecholamines, 5-HIAA, and absence of avidity on MIBG and octreotide SPECT/CT.
Considered given the solitary 4-cm enlarging retroperitoneal mass; ruled out by histopathology showing dense collagenous fibrosis without cytologic atypia.

Considered given tropical travel history and microorganism-like morphology in retroperitoneal tissue; ruled out by a negative Mantoux skin test and non-reactive serologies for Leishmania, Echinococcus, Taenia solium, Strongyloides, and Trypanosoma cruzi.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive serologic testing demonstrating acute and past infection, corroborated by resolution of abdominal pain and CT regression of the retroperitoneal lesion following praziquantel therapy.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old woman presented to the hospital with recurrent right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She resided in a pastoral agricultural region and reported regular contact with dogs and sheep.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma to the Liver
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the synchronous solid, contrast-enhancing renal mass; ruled out because the hepatic lesion demonstrated cystic architecture with mural calcification rather than solid vascular metastasis, and intraoperative opening revealed a classic hydatid cyst.

Considered due to the 6-cm hepatic mass with irregular margins and heterogeneous density; ruled out by normal serum AFP and CA 19-9 levels, normal liver biochemistry, and characteristic parasitic cyst morphology.

Considered due to pastoral residence, irregular margins, and heterogeneous density mimicking alveolar echinococcosis; ruled out by negative Em2 serology alongside positive EgCF, EgP, and EgB antibodies specific for cystic echinococcosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological confirmation via dot immunogold filtration assay demonstrating positivity for cystic echinococcal antigens (EgCF, EgP, EgB) with negative Em2, establishing cystic echinococcosis coexisting with renal carcinoma.

clinical_summary: An 8-month-old female infant presented to the hospital with intermittent high fever, paroxysmal cough, and progressive respiratory distress. The fevers began without an obvious antecedent trigger, recurring every 6 to 7 hours with peak temperatures of 40.7°C.

differentials.candidate: Fulminant Bacterial Pneumonia and Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high spiking fevers, rapid respiratory failure, marked elevation of CRP (124.8 mg/L) and procalcitonin (5.26 ng/mL), and cavitary lung nodules; ruled out by continuous clinical deterioration despite broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage with meropenem and linezolid.

Considered given cavitary pulmonary nodules, hepatosplenomegaly, profound systemic inflammation, and primary immunodeficiency; ruled out by rapid stabilization and long-term resolution achieved solely with targeted systemic antifungal therapy.

Considered given high fevers, massive hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, and hepatic dysfunction in an infant; ruled out as primary etiology in favor of an opportunistic systemic infectious disease that resolved upon antifungal eradication.

diagnostic_pivot: Failure of broad-spectrum carbapenem and oxazolidinone therapy in an infant with cavitary lung nodules, marked hepatosplenomegaly, and hypoplastic thymus, pivoting to opportunistic systemic fungal infection with prompt cure following systemic antifungal administration.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old man presented to the emergency department with severe swelling and pain involving his right eye and right side of his face that had been progressively worsening over the preceding eight days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary initial diagnosis given the 2-year history of severe toothache and an active mandibular fistulous tract releasing pus; ruled out as the solitary etiology because the patient failed standard broad-spectrum cephalosporin and nitroimidazole therapy and harbored chronic pulmonary symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Enteric / Opportunistic Bacterial Orbital Superinfection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to isolation of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus cohnii from the orbital drainage; ruled out as the primary systemic driver because it could not explain the 5-month bloody cough, which proved to be active pulmonary disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Re-evaluation of the chronic bloody cough leading to chest radiography and sputum Ziehl-Neelsen smear microscopy, which demonstrated acid-fast bacilli and prompt resolution upon antitubercular fixed-dose combination therapy.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 1) in her third trimester was referred to clinical genetics in Mérida, Mexico, following the detection of severe fetal malformations on prenatal ultrasound. A review of her prenatal history revealed that during her first trimester (before her pregnancy was recognized), she had experienced an acute illness characterized by unquantified fever, tender preauricular lymphadenopathy, generalized pruritus,...

differentials.candidate: Chromosomal Aneuploidy / Genetic Malformation Syndrome (e.g., Trisomy 18, Radial-Ray Syndromes)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of microcephaly, hypertelorism, retrognathia, radial aplasia, and multiple joint contractures; ruled out by a completely normal G-banded karyotype.

differentials.candidate: Classic TORCH Congenital Fetopathy (Toxoplasma, Rubella, CMV, HSV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given intracranial ventriculomegaly, microcephaly, and cerebral calcifications; ruled out by non-reactive maternal and infant serologies for all major TORCH pathogens.
Considered due to maternal febrile rash illness in an endemic region; excluded by specific cerebrospinal fluid multiplex molecular diagnostics confirming the specific flavivirus.

diagnostic_pivot: History of first-trimester febrile rash during a regional epidemic, distinctive fetal skull collapse, arthrogryposis, and neuroimaging showing subcortical calcifications with lissencephaly, confirmed definitively by detection of viral RNA in cerebrospinal fluid via RT-PCR.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old woman presented to the neurosurgery outpatient department reporting a 1-year history of progressively worsening headaches and bilateral diminished vision. Her medical history was notable only for essential hypertension treated with oral antihypertensive medication.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary preoperative radiological diagnosis given the 1.7 x 1.4 cm enhancing sellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, accompanied by hypopituitarism and stalk-effect hyperprolactinemia; ruled out when histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with preserved reticulin architecture surrounding viable pituitary nests rather than adenomatous reticulin breakdown.

Considered following the histological discovery of epithelioid cell granulomas and Langhans giant cells in the pituitary parenchyma; ruled out as non-infectious pathology by the demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological demonstration of Langhans giant cell granulomas with positive Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast staining of the sellar lesion, followed by complete clinical recovery and endocrine normalization under standard four-drug antitubercular chemotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old woman was transferred to the emergency department for further evaluation of extensive retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and omental fat stranding concerning for metastatic malignancy. Over the preceding month, she had developed progressive fatigue, anorexia, and involuntary weight loss that had worsened considerably over the past two weeks.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic Breast Carcinoma (Stage IV with Omental Carcinomatosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary clinical diagnosis due to a 2.5-cm left breast mass in conjunction with widespread retroperitoneal and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, pulmonary nodules, and omental caking; ruled out as the cause of lymphadenopathy when retroperitoneal node biopsy showed necrotizing giant-cell granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli rather than metastatic adenocarcinoma.

differentials.candidate: Primary Gastrointestinal Malignancy with Peritoneal Seedings
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of markedly elevated CA 19-9 (301.4 U/mL) and CEA (9.0 ng/mL) alongside omental fat nodularity and duodenal erosions; ruled out by histologically normal endoscopic biopsies of the colon and gastric mucosa.

diagnostic_pivot: Retroperitoneal lymph node biopsy demonstrating necrotizing giant-cell granulomas with positive acid-fast bacilli staining, confirming cryptic abdominal and miliary tuberculosis coexisting with newly diagnosed localized breast cancer.

clinical_summary: A 7-month-old male infant was admitted to the hospital with a two-month history of a recurring cough, persistent high fever for nine days, and an eruptive, progressive rash for two days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, extreme leukocytosis (33 x 10^9/L), and elevated CRP (272 mg/L) and procalcitonin (2.73 ng/mL); ruled out by complete lack of response to empirical potent broad-spectrum antibacterials.

Considered because of a history of persistent axillary lymphadenitis following neonatal BCG vaccination, pulmonary infiltrates, and hepatosplenomegaly in an infant with suspected inborn immunodeficiency; ruled out as the cause of acute sepsis by blood culture isolation and mNGS identification of a dimorphic fungus.

differentials.candidate: Kawasaki Disease / Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (sJIA)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever, polymorphic maculopapular rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, peripheral extremity edema, pericardial effusion, and high NT-proBNP; ruled out by normal coronary arteries and microbiological isolation of an opportunistic fungal pathogen.

diagnostic_pivot: Prompt defervescence, resolution of rash, and normalization of inflammatory parameters following targeted voriconazole antifungal therapy in a child with culturally confirmed dimorphic fungal sepsis.

clinical_summary: A 20-month-old HIV-exposed uninfected boy was brought to the emergency department with a 2-day history of acute shortness of breath, cough, and noisy breathing. Over the preceding week, he had experienced intermittent fever, vomiting, and night sweats.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Bronchiolitis / Reactive Airway Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initial clinical diagnosis based on acute tachypnea, chest wall indrawing, hyperinflation, and bilateral wheezing; ruled out by complete lack of response to nebulized hypertonic saline, oral corticosteroids, and amoxicillin, followed by the development of unilateral percussion dullness and a chylothorax.

Considered given the prior clinic diagnosis and 2-week history of first-line therapy; ruled out as adequate therapy because the patient clinically deteriorated with progressive lymph node enlargement obstructing the main bronchi, proven on BAL to harbor rifampicin resistance.

Considered when the patient developed dullness to percussion and absent breath sounds over the right hemithorax; ruled out by diagnostic thoracentesis yielding chyle rather than purulent bacterial exudate.

diagnostic_pivot: Development of a massive chylothorax caused by caseating mediastinal lymph nodes eroding the thoracic duct and main bronchi, with GeneXpert MTB/RIF on bronchoalveolar lavage identifying rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, leading to clinical cure on second-line MDR-TB treatment.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old woman with a two-year history of dermatomyositis managed with oral prednisone (25 mg daily) and cyclosporine (75 mg twice daily) was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to persistent high fever, sudden hypotension, and multi-organ failure.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Septic Arthritis with Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given acute purulent monoarthritis, extreme procalcitonin elevation, septic cardiomyopathy, and multi-organ failure; ruled out by repeatedly negative conventional blood and synovial fluid bacterial cultures and non-response to broad-spectrum vancomycin, imipenem/cilastatin, and linezolid.

Considered due to abrupt hypotension, elevated myocardial enzymes, and ST-segment elevations on ECG; ruled out by emergent coronary angiography demonstrating absence of coronary arterial occlusion, indicating sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy.

differentials.candidate: Severe Dermatomyositis Flare with Systemic Autoimmune Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 2-year dermatomyositis history, V-sign cutaneous rash, and monoarthritis; ruled out by purulent synovial effusion, marked procalcitonin elevation, and definitive microbiological demonstration of mycobacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of synovial pus and peripheral blood identifying Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirmed by direct microscopic identification of acid-fast bacilli in the joint fluid, revealing disseminated mycobacterial septic shock in an immunosuppressed patient.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female with a history of sickle beta-plus-thalassemia (genotype S/beta+-thalassemia, not on hydroxyurea; baseline outpatient laboratory values: hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 62 fL, leukocyte count 6.7 x 10^9/L, platelet count 123 x 10^9/L) is admitted during the summer with a 4-day history of diffuse myalgia, retro-orbital headache, abdominal pain, fever, and chills.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (A, B, and C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute viral infection of the liver was considered due to acute fever, jaundice, and hepatomegaly in a patient with a hemoglobinopathy, but specific viral serologic panels were non-reactive.

Biliary disease or choledocholithiasis was considered given the acute right upper quadrant pain and jaundice in a patient at risk for pigmented gallstones, but imaging confirmed normal ductal caliber and no lithiasis.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever / Severe Dengue
differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical picture of acute retro-orbital headache, severe myalgias, summer presentation in an endemic region, and evidence of systemic plasma leakage (ascites and pleural effusions) precipitating sickle cell intrahepatic cholestasis was confirmed by reactive IgM serology.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old woman with homozygous sickle cell anemia (genotype SS, with irregular outpatient follow-up and no history of hydroxyurea use; baseline outpatient values: hemoglobin 8 g/dL, leukocyte count 20.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count 612 x 10^9/L) is admitted with a 1-day history of diffuse myalgia, arthralgia, retro-orbital headache, vomiting, and fever.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (A, B, and C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute viral hepatitis was evaluated as a cause of acute jaundice and gastrointestinal upset, but serological testing for hepatitis A, B, and C was completely negative.

Symptomatic gallstone disease was considered given the high prevalence of cholelithiasis in sickle cell disease, but abdominal ultrasound confirmed the lack of inflammatory signs or biliary ductal dilatation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue Fever triggering Sickle Cell Crisis / Intrahepatic Cholestasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The acute presentation with retro-orbital headache, intense arthralgias and myalgias, vomiting, and high fever was definitively confirmed by early viral antigen detection.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a 1-day history of difficulty arousing from sleep, confusion, and incoherent speech. Two days prior to presentation, he experienced the acute onset of fever accompanied by coffee ground vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial CNS infection was considered due to acute febrile encephalopathy, but CSF evaluation demonstrated normal leukocyte count, normal protein, normal glucose, and negative Gram and acid-fast stains.

differentials.candidate: Japanese Encephalitis Virus (JEV) and Other Classical Neurotropic Pathogens
differentials.rule_out_reason: Common regional and classical encephalitic pathogens were systematically investigated but ruled out by specific molecular testing algorithms and serological assays.

The acute clinical picture of febrile encephalopathy, gastrointestinal bleeding, leukopenia, and acute transaminitis was definitively established by the detection of viral RNA directly within the cerebrospinal fluid and serum.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old girl presents to a tertiary pediatric orthopedic clinic with a multi-year history of dull pain and periodic purulent wound drainage on the lateral aspect of her right thigh.

differentials.candidate: Pyomyositis of the Vastus Lateralis / Recurrent Bacterial Subfascial Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected during initial presentations due to localized fluctuance and purulent collection, but recurred repeatedly over eight years despite two formal surgical evacuations and prolonged empiric oral antibacterial regimens.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Pyogenic Infection / Pseudomonas stutzeri Soft Tissue Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a potential primary pathogen after a superficial swab grew Pseudomonas stutzeri, but targeted antibacterial therapy produced no clinical or physical response.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tuberculous Trochanteric Bursitis (Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The constellation of an indolent draining sinus communicating with an expanded trochanteric bursa and an osteolytic trochanteric defect was definitively confirmed by positive mycobacterial culture and histopathologic verification of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old HIV-negative man presents to a clinic with a 3-month history of cough, severe fatigue, drenching night sweats, generalized body weakness, anorexia, marked weight loss, chest pain, and shortness of breath, alongside nausea, vomiting, and intermittent fevers over several months.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Lymphoproliferative Malignancy / Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
differentials.rule_out_reason: A primary hematologic malignancy was considered due to generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and marked peripheral lymphocytosis with smudge cells; however, the extensive bilateral tree-in-bud infiltrates and parenchymal destruction could not be attributed to leukemia alone.
Acute bacterial pneumonia was inconsistent with the indolent 3-month progression, severe cachexia, lack of acute neutrophilia, and prominent bilateral hilar adenopathy.

The constellation of chronic constitutional wasting, chronic productive cough, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, and pleural effusion was definitively established by automated molecular sputum testing identifying drug-sensitive mycobacterial infection.

clinical_summary: A 79-year-old woman with severe, refractory rheumatoid arthritis maintained on weekly tocilizumab (162 mg/week), methotrexate (12 mg/week), methylprednisolone (8 mg/day), and inhaled pentamidine prophylaxis presents with the sudden onset of high fever and a 2-week history of worsening cough and generalized fatigue.

differentials.candidate: Community-Acquired Bacterial or Viral Pneumonia (S. pneumoniae, Legionella, SARS-CoV-2, CMV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute bacterial and viral pathogens were considered due to fulminant septic shock and ARDS, but rapid urinary antigen tests and viral assays were negative.

differentials.candidate: Invasive Fungal Infection (Aspergillus, Candida, Cryptococcus neoformans)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Invasive fungal pneumonia was evaluated in this profoundly immunosuppressed host with diffuse ground-glass infiltrates, but fungal antigen assays were negative.

The severe presentation of necrotizing bilateral pneumonia and multiorgan failure was confirmed by positive sputum mycobacterial testing and post-mortem histopathology demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining with widespread extrapulmonary caseating granulomas.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old previously healthy female presents to an infectious disease department with a 7-day history of high fever, rigors, chills, anorexia, and generalized body pain, accompanied by dark urine, pale stools, and diarrhea.

differentials.candidate: Acute Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) or Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Mononucleosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute viral mononucleosis was considered due to high fever, prominent peripheral lymphadenopathy, and pancytopenia, but serologies confirmed prior past immunity rather than acute active infection.

Enteric pathogens and brucellosis were evaluated given travel to West Africa, diarrhea, pale stools, and fever of unknown origin, but history excluded unpasteurized dairy and animal contacts, and marked hemolysis pointed to intraerythrocytic parasitism.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mixed Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical presentation of febrile hemolytic anemia in a traveler returning from an endemic region was definitively confirmed by microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear identifying diagnostic morphological stages of both parasite species.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male smoker with no prior medical or family history presents with a 2-month history of progressive dyspnea and cough. He is a resident of the Middle East and reports no alcohol intake.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pulmonary embolism was evaluated during the patient's subacute course due to refractory dyspnea and an elevated D-dimer, but was excluded by contrast pulmonary angiography.

differentials.candidate: Constrictive Pericarditis / Pure Tuberculous Pericardial Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pericardial constriction was considered following the development of progressive pericardial effusion and dyspnea, but echocardiography and cardiac MRI confirmed normal hemodynamics and ultimately unveiled an intracardiac mass.

The subacute respiratory illness with lobar atelectasis and bronchiectasis in a patient from an endemic region was confirmed by positive acid-fast bacilli staining on bronchoalveolar lavage fluid despite initial negative sputum.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old male child is brought to the hospital with a 3-month history of holocranial headache, irritability, and occasional vomiting, followed by a 3-day history of acute mental status decline.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Intracranial Neuroepithelial or Arachnoid Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Non-parasitic congenital cysts were considered in the differential diagnosis of pediatric intraventricular fluid lesions, but such benign cysts lack the detached, free-floating undulating internal membrane characteristic of the Camalote sign.

differentials.candidate: Primary Visceral Echinococcosis (Hepatic or Pulmonary Hydatid Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extracranial visceral primary hydatid foci were evaluated to determine whether the intracranial lesion represented metastatic dissemination, but systemic imaging was entirely normal.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Cerebral Echinococcosis (Intraventricular Hydatid Cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The radiological demonstration of a collapsed intraventricular cyst with floating membrane causing foramen of Monro obstruction was confirmed by transcortical operative finding of a free-floating cyst wall in clear CSF and definitive histopathological examination.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old previously healthy female presents to a local hospital in Sri Lanka with a 2-day history of high fever, severe headache, diffuse myalgia, arthralgia, and abdominal pain. On physical examination, the patient appears acutely ill.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) or Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Microangiopathy and consumptive coagulopathy were considered when severe refractory thrombocytopenia failed to improve with platelet transfusions, but peripheral blood morphology revealed no characteristic features of DIC or TTP.

Occult internal bleeding was evaluated as a cause of profound circulatory shock, but was ruled out by hemoconcentration with rising hematocrit and ultrasound showing no free fluid in the chest or abdomen.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Severe Dengue Infection / Expanded Dengue Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: The acute tropical febrile presentation was confirmed on day 3 by positive viral nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) antigen testing, with subsequent critical-phase development of hemoconcentration (PCV 50), acute myocarditis with EF 30-35%, spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage, and biopsy-proven secondary HLH.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old previously healthy female presented with a 1-week history of right-sided painful neck swelling, fever, and odynophagia. She denied preceding pharyngitis, constitutional symptoms, night sweats, or known sick contacts.

differentials.candidate: Acute bacterial suppurative thyroiditis secondary to pyriform sinus fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: While Streptococcus anginosus and Eikenella corrodens were cultured from the purulent collection, flexible laryngoscopy ruled out the classic congenital predisposing tract (pyriform sinus fistula), and the extensive prevertebral extension and persistence pointed to an underlying tuberculous abscess.

Although subacute thyroiditis causes tender thyroid enlargement and transient thyrotoxicosis, it is a self-limiting nonsuppurative granulomatous inflammation and does not form large multiloculated necrotic abscesses or yield frank purulent aspirate.

differentials.candidate: Thyroid carcinoma with necrosis (e.g., anaplastic or aggressive papillary thyroid carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A rapidly expanding necrotic neck mass with cervical lymphadenopathy raises concern for thyroid malignancy, but histopathological examination of the resected lobe showed xanthogranulomatous inflammation and microabscesses without malignant cellular atypia.

diagnostic_pivot: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of the aspirated thyroid pus tested positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA despite negative acid-fast smears and negative mycobacterial cultures, identifying primary tuberculous suppurative thyroiditis with secondary bacterial superinfection.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old male residing in Guangxi, China, presented with recurrent cough, expectoration, and intermittent fever of more than 5 months' duration. Symptoms began subacutely with cough and sputum production and insidiously progressed to fever and exertional dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although solid organ transplant recipients on calcineurin inhibitors are susceptible to Aspergillus, the serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan was negative (<10 pg/mL), the galactomannan index was equivocal (0.598), and bronchoalveolar lavage metagenomic sequencing identified Talaromyces marneffei rather than Aspergillus species.

While bronchoalveolar lavage culture isolated Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the subacute 5-month duration, normal procalcitonin (0.079 ng/mL), and failure to resolve with antibacterial therapy indicated that bacterial colonization/infection was secondary to underlying opportunistic fungal infection.

PJP is a common cause of subacute fever and dyspnea in transplant recipients with depressed cellular immunity, but normal procalcitonin, negative plasma 1,3-beta-D-glucan, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing excluded Pneumocystis as the driver.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid next-generation sequencing detected Talaromyces marneffei sequence reads in a kidney transplant recipient from endemic Guangxi, establishing the definitive diagnosis of pulmonary talaromycosis complicated by Pseudomonas co-infection.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male residing in Guangxi, China, presented with recurrent fever and exertional dyspnea of 2 weeks' duration. His medical history was significant for renal hypertension, uremia, and chronic hepatitis B virus infection.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Profound CD4 depletion (<50 cells/µL) and severe acute respiratory distress syndrome raised high suspicion for PJP, prompting empirical trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, but direct fungal smear showing spores/hyphae, genital cutaneous lesions, and blood NGS identified disseminated Talaromyces marneffei.

Low-level CMV viremia (9.70 x 10^2 copies) was detected in this severely immunosuppressed host, but the presence of visible fungal structures on sputum fluorescent staining, cutaneous ulcerations, and high inflammatory markers indicated invasive fungal infection rather than isolated viral pneumonitis.

While Acinetobacter baumannii was subsequently cultured from sputum in the setting of elevated procalcitonin (1.86 ng/mL), antibacterial coverage failed to halt clinical deterioration as the primary systemic pathogen was disseminated dimorphic fungus.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) of peripheral blood demonstrated sequence reads of Talaromyces marneffei (TM) in a severely immunosuppressed transplant recipient from endemic Guangxi presenting with fever, pancytopenia, cutaneous lesions, and severe ARDS.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female from Portel, Pará State, northern Brazil, presented for evaluation of recurrent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, jaundice, pruritus, fever, and shivering. Her clinical illness began nearly two decades earlier (1983) and followed a chronic, relapsing course marked by recurrent episodes of obstructive cholangitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Extensive bilateral irresectable hepatic mass lesions causing obstructive jaundice and recurrent cholangitis mimic advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, but the extraordinarily prolonged 17-year timeline and absence of distant metastasis ruled against malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Primary sclerosing cholangitis / recurrent pyogenic cholangitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recurrent fever, shivering, pruritus, and biliary tract involvement resemble chronic bacterial or autoimmune cholangiopathy, but the aggressive invasive parenchymal mass lesions that required three prior liver resections pointed to an infiltrative parasitic etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive clinical and histopathologic confirmation of diffuse alveolar hepatic echinococcosis involving both hepatic lobes with irresectable biliary destruction and recurrent cholangitis, establishing the indication for orthotopic liver transplantation.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old female presented with dull left mid-back pain of 3 months' duration. The pain was moderate in intensity and radiated anteriorly toward the left breast and precordium.

differentials.candidate: Primary osseous neoplasm or thoracic metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cortical scalloping and erosion of the T7 vertebral body, pedicle, and adjacent rib head with an expansive paraspinal mass abutting the descending aorta raised strong clinical suspicion for a malignant or aggressive bone tumor, but percutaneous biopsy revealed caseating granulomas without neoplastic cells.

Acute pyogenic arthritis typically presents with rapid onset, high fever, marked leukocytosis, and acute suppuration, whereas this patient exhibited an indolent 3-month clinical course, mild inflammatory markers, and chronic granulomatous synovial proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of the left 7th costotransverse mass demonstrated caseous necrosis with epithelioid histiocytes and Langerhans giant cells, corroborated by GeneXpert detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis susceptible to isoniazid and rifampicin.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old female presented with high fever of 15 days' duration, upper abdominal pain and limb muscle soreness for 7 days, and rapidly progressive shortness of breath for 4 days.

differentials.candidate: Fulminant viral or acute pyogenic bacterial ARDS
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapidly progressive ARDS with high fever and leukopenia prompted empiric antiviral and carbapenem therapy, but procalcitonin was only mildly elevated (0.25 ng/mL) and respiratory failure persisted without response to standard antimicrobial coverage.

The constellation of high unremitting fever, polyserositis, transaminitis, and hepatosplenomegaly raised suspicion for a systemic rheumatic or autoimmune disorder, but extensive autoantibody screening was completely negative.

Whole-body PET-CT demonstrated multiple nodular hypermetabolic foci in the liver, lungs, and bone marrow, raising concern for lymphoma or secondary malignancy, but ultrasound-guided biopsy revealed infectious granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of contrast-enhanced ultrasound-guided liver biopsy revealed Langhans giant cells and confluent granulomas with caseous necrosis and positive acid-fast staining, with cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic sequencing confirming disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male residing in Nanning, Guangxi, China, presented for admission with advanced symptomatic immunodeficiency and esophageal symptoms. He reported a history of high-risk sexual exposures over a decade prior, had never received antiretroviral therapy, and denied any history of illicit substance use.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Tuberculosis was strongly suspected due to endemicity and atypical lung infiltrates in severe immunodeficiency, but sputum AFB smear, mycobacterial culture, and sputum TB-DNA PCR were all negative, and the lesions regressed with antifungal and antibacterial treatment.

differentials.candidate: Isolated bacterial pneumonia and esophageal candidiasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although bacterial pneumonia and mucosal candidiasis were present, the patient's profound immunodeficiency, geographic origin in Guangxi, severe marrow suppression, and systemic course were characteristic of disseminated endemic dimorphic fungal infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation of Marneffei talaromycosis in an ART-naive patient with advanced AIDS from endemic Guangxi presenting with profound CD4 lymphopenia, severe anemia, and pulmonary infiltrates.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old male was admitted with fever, severe cough, and yellow sputum production of 1 month's duration. Three months prior to admission, he had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma (cT4N2M0, stage IIIB) and had received 2 cycles of pemetrexed and cisplatin adjuvant chemotherapy.

differentials.candidate: Progression / metastatic recurrence of lung adenocarcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient with stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma recently treated with pemetrexed-cisplatin, new bilateral lesions and mediastinal lymphadenopathy raised concern for disease progression, but microbiological and molecular evaluation demonstrated active mycobacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Post-chemotherapy community-acquired or opportunistic bacterial pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 1-month history of fever and productive cough following cytotoxic chemotherapy could represent pyogenic bacterial lower respiratory infection, but repeated sputum microscopy and rapid molecular testing revealed acid-fast bacilli and mycobacterial DNA.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive sputum acid-fast bacilli smear and sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay confirming rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis retreatment.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old male was admitted with dry cough and shortness of breath. He had no history of tobacco use and reported good oral hygiene.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Massive bilateral pleural effusions accompanied by pericardial fluid and ascites in an elderly patient raised high clinical suspicion for disseminated malignancy, but pleural fluid interferon-gamma release assay was positive and surgical pathology demonstrated inflammatory caseous necrosis without malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Congestive heart failure or cirrhosis with transudative serositis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simultaneous pleural effusions, ascites, and pericardial effusion can occur in severe organ failure, but intraoperative findings revealed chronic thickened pericardial adhesions with calcification and cheese-like caseating lesions progressing to tamponade.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency pericardiectomy histopathology demonstrating fibrous tissue hyperplasia, collagenization with exudative inflammatory necrosis, and positive TB fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), confirming tuberculous constrictive pericarditis with polyserositis.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old male presented with a 1-month history of low-grade fever, persistent headache, and night sweats. He had no smoking history and maintained good oral hygiene.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial brain abscesses secondary to septic emboli
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple intracranial ring/abscess lesions can result from bacteremic seeding, but the indolent 1-month course with low-grade fevers and night sweats, along with concomitant pulmonary nodules, favored a chronic granulomatous infection.

Multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions with surrounding edema in a young patient strongly suggest parasitic cerebral disease, but sputum and CSF molecular testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum and cerebrospinal fluid GeneXpert MTB/RIF assays both testing positive, followed by confirmatory culture isolating Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing the diagnosis of disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and cerebral tuberculomas/abscesses.

clinical_summary: A 10-day-old male infant presents to the emergency department with a 6-day history of high-grade fever and jaundice, accompanied by new-onset seizures over the past 2 days. On physical examination, the infant is febrile, irritable, and icteric.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial clinical presentation and CSF pleocytosis prompted an admission diagnosis of neonatal bacterial meningitis; however, the CSF showed 95.1% mononuclear predominance and fever and CSF abnormalities persisted on empiric ampicillin and cefotaxime sodium.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Viral / Protozoal Infections (TORCH Complex: Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, CMV, HSV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Jaundice, hepatomegaly, and meningoencephalitis in the first 2 weeks of life strongly suggested congenital TORCH pathogens, but targeted diagnostic assays returned negative.

differentials.candidate: Endemic Tropical Infections (Malaria, Dengue, Leptospirosis, Japanese Encephalitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Vector-borne and zoonotic tropical pathogens causing acute febrile encephalopathy, jaundice, and hepatitis in endemic zones were ruled out by negative laboratory evaluations.

diagnostic_pivot: Lack of defervescence on beta-lactams prompted maternal re-evaluation, uncovering a history of peripartum fever of unknown origin and a 1.2 × 0.8 cm eschar in the mother's left groin; serologies (Weil-Felix OXK and IgM-ELISA) and mNGS confirmed Orientia tsutsugamushi in both mother and infant, establishing vertically transmitted congenital scrub typhus.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 2-month history of intermittent headaches, diplopia, and left lower limb weakness. Non-contrast cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed prior to presentation demonstrates a hypointense mass lesion in the right brainstem on T1-weighted images.

differentials.candidate: Low-Grade Brainstem Glioma / Primary Brainstem Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial MRI characteristics of an expansile brainstem mass with perilesional edema raised suspicion for a low-grade glioma; however, stereotactic biopsy was deferred, peripheral eosinophilia prompted parasitic testing, and the mass resolved completely following anthelmintic and corticosteroid therapy without surgical resection.

differentials.candidate: Alternative Parasitic Zoonoses (Cysticercosis, Sparganosis, Echinococcosis, Fascioliasis, Toxocariasis, Trichinellosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the peripheral eosinophilia and intracranial space-occupying lesion, major parasitic CNS and tissue infections were evaluated, but specific serum IgG antibody ELISA tests were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum and CSF IgG ELISA assays were positive for S. japonicum, and subsequent electronic colonoscopy with mucosal biopsy demonstrated S. japonicum eggs in the lamina propria of the rectum, confirming ectopic encephalic schistosomiasis with complete lesion resolution after praziquantel and prednisolone.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old woman presents to the Ear, Nose and Throat clinic with a 2-week history of a tender lump on the right side of her upper neck. She had an initial mild fever, but reports no loss of appetite, weight loss, night sweats, cough, chest pain, nasal obstruction, or otologic symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (NPC) with Regional Cervical Metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Location in the fossa of Rosenmüller, bilateral cervical adenopathy, and FNAC displaying atypical hyperchromatic cells strongly pointed to metastatic NPC; however, sequential biopsies demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli and no malignant cells.
Presumed initially by her general practitioner, but the mass persisted despite oral amoxicillin therapy and endoscopy revealed a primary nasopharyngeal granulomatous mass.

differentials.candidate: Deep Fungal Granuloma of the Nasopharynx
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of chronic necrotizing granulomatous inflammation in the upper airway; however, Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) staining was repeatedly negative for fungal hyphae.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat biopsy of the nasopharyngeal mass revealed caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain, and sputum smears confirmed acid-fast bacilli, establishing nasopharyngeal tuberculosis secondary to pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old male child presents to the general outpatient department of a district hospital after 8 days of persistent high-grade fever, generalized body aches, sore throat, and vomiting. Environmental assessment reveals that the child lives in an unpaved mud house in a wetland area situated near a community garbage dumping site.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial clinical triage in an endemic tropical region led to empiric treatment for malaria based on high fever, vomiting, and body aches; however, antimalarial therapy failed to stabilize the patient and acute hemorrhagic manifestations subsequently emerged.
Diagnosed alongside malaria at triage due to high fever, constitutional distress, and sore throat; however, empiric therapy was ineffective and the illness rapidly progressed to mucosal bleeding.

diagnostic_pivot: On the second hospital day, the emergence of spontaneous hemorrhage from mucosal orifices in a patient with household rodent infestation prompted suspicion of viral hemorrhagic fever, confirmed by positive blood RT-PCR for Lassa virus.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old postpartum Hispanic woman residing in Laredo, Texas, on the Mexican border, presents to the emergency room with recurrent fevers, chills, abdominal distension, bilateral lower extremity swelling, nausea, nonbloody emesis, and watery diarrhea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial radiological appearance of marked ascites, omental thickening, peritoneal thickening, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy initially suggested carcinomatosis, especially in the context of an elevated CA-125 level (199.5 U/mL); however, ascitic fluid cytology was negative for malignant cells and peritoneal biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation.

Suspected due to recent cesarean section, high fever, abdominal tenderness, and high procalcitonin (10.68 ng/mL); however, blood, urine, and vaginal cultures yielded no bacterial growth, and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy failed to control fevers.

differentials.candidate: Endemic Zoonoses and Tick-Borne Infections (Rickettsia typhi, RMSF, Q Fever, Syphilis, Viral Hepatitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's residence along the border and systemic febrile presentation, regional zoonoses and atypical infections were evaluated and excluded by negative serologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic paracentesis revealed lymphocytic ascites with elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA 34.9 U/L) and positive Mycobacteria PCR, followed by positive sputum AFB culture and laparoscopic peritoneal biopsy demonstrating caseating granulomas with positive AFB stain.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male technical worker presents to the emergency department for evaluation of recurrent fevers spanning 4 months, which have progressively worsened and been accompanied by severe diarrhea over the past month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's remote African travel history and periodic spiking fever pattern; however, oral artemisinin failed to abate the fevers, and multiple blood smear examinations and rapid Plasmodium antigen tests were negative.

Considered as primary causes of hepatosplenomegaly, cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and ascites in an endemic area; however, specific serological antibody panels against these trematode and cestode pathogens returned negative.
Considered in a patient presenting with cirrhosis and portal hypertension; however, serological markers for viral hepatitis A and B were negative, and serum tumor markers (AFP and CEA) were normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of peripheral blood detected Leishmania infantum and Leishmania donovani DNA, corroborated by a positive CDC rK39 antibody test, establishing visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar).

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old male middle-school student residing in Chongqing presents to an emergency fever clinic with a history of persistent fever and cough for more than 10 days. The illness began after an apparent upper respiratory infection, with body temperature initially fluctuating between 37 °C and 38 °C, accompanied by cough, fatigue, chills, and pharyngeal discomfort.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Extreme fever, marked splenomegaly, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia (>2,000 ng/mL), hypertriglyceridemia, and elevated LDH fulfilled clinical criteria for HLH; however, the syndrome was triggered secondarily by intracellular protozoal infection rather than primary genetic HLH.

differentials.candidate: Hematologic Malignancy / Lymphoma or Acute Leukemia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Entertained due to B-symptoms, cytopenias, splenomegaly, and high ferritin in an adolescent; ruled out by normal leukemia immunophenotyping and repeat bone marrow examinations showing reactive trilineage hyperplasia without malignant infiltration.

Considered due to the presence of multiple circulating autoantibodies (positive direct Coombs' test, ANA 1:100, anti-Jo-1, and rheumatoid factor); ruled out because these antibodies reflected non-specific polyclonal B-cell stimulation from chronic infection, and empirical dexamethasone failed to control the fever.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected DNA reads of Leishmania infantum, and rapid rK39 antibody testing performed by the CDC confirmed the clinical diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis, leading to complete fever defervescence and spleen regression on sodium stibogluconate.

clinical_summary: A 26-day-old neonate weighing 2,500 grams is referred from a public health center to the emergency department of a regional hospital with a 5-day history of fever, cough, tachypnea, and poor feeding since 21 days of life.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Neonatal Pneumonia and Septic Shock (e.g., GBS, Gram-Negative Bacilli)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial clinical presentation, leukocytosis, and hemodynamic collapse led to a working diagnosis of conventional pyogenic neonatal pneumonia and septic shock, treated with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics; however, after only transient temporary stabilization, the patient suffered severe clinical deterioration on day 16.

Suspected due to acute respiratory distress and diffuse interstitial B-line patterns on lung ultrasound; however, specific rapid antigen testing for SARS-CoV-2 was negative, and the illness progressed beyond self-limiting viral pneumonitis.

diagnostic_pivot: Worsening respiratory failure on day 16 necessitated endotracheal intubation, where aspirate analysis demonstrated positive acid-fast bacteria and a positive rifampicin-sensitive rapid molecular test, corroborated by positive tuberculosis screening in the mother, establishing perinatal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old male child is brought to the outpatient department by his parents for evaluation of persistent swelling of all fingers, associated with multiple blackish-colored ulcers on the digits and nails, and complete loss of the distal nail beds.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a young child with chronic loss of terminal digits and painless ulcerations; however, the patient exhibited peripheral nerve hypertrophy, lacked compulsive self-injurious biting behaviors or choreoathetosis, and had a positive household contact history.

Considered due to diffuse swelling of the fingers, digital ulcerations, and loss of nail beds; ruled out by profound sensory loss (cutaneous anesthesia) and palpable thickening of peripheral nerve trunks.

Entertained due to chronic disfiguring digital abnormalities presenting in early infancy; ruled out by classic neurotrophic anesthetic ulcers, peripheral nerve enlargement, and absence of asymmetric mosaic tissue overgrowth.

diagnostic_pivot: The cardinal clinical combination of painless cutaneous anesthesia in the fingers, palpable thickening of the peripheral nerve at the cuboidal site, recurrent trophic finger ulcers, and documented household contact history confirmed the diagnosis of childhood leprosy.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old woman with a history of cadaveric renal transplantation in 2006 for membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis presents with a 4-week history of diarrhea (averaging 4 loose stools daily, previously controlled with loperamide), which has become associated over the past week with nausea, crampy abdominal pain, and subjective fevers.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked involuntary weight loss (10 kg), refractory iron-deficiency anemia, long-term immunosuppression, and contrast CT showing a 4-cm segment of 80% colonic stenosis strongly raised suspicion for an invasive intestinal malignancy; however, endoscopic biopsies showed ulcerative inflammation without dysplasia, clonal proliferation, or malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Enteric Infections (Histoplasmosis, Syphilis, HSV Colitis, Bacterial Enteritis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteric opportunistic pathogens in an immunocompromised host were evaluated; stool bacterial cultures were negative, gastrointestinal film array was negative, urine Histoplasma antigen was negative, rapid plasma reagin was negative, and biopsy HSV I/II studies were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Colonic biopsy polymerase chain reaction (PCR) returned positive for both Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Cytomegalovirus, establishing intestinal tuberculosis with CMV coinfection in a renal transplant patient.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male presented to the emergency department with global aphasia and right-sided hemiplegia. Four months prior, he began experiencing intermittent headaches.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the indolent presentation, abdominal lymphadenopathy, and splenic granulomas; however, the patient deteriorated with rapidly expanding multi-compartment suppuration (epidural, subdural, and parenchymal abscesses) while receiving dedicated anti-tubercular therapy, and surgical cultures grew Burkholderia pseudomallei.

Considered because neuroimaging showed marked diffusion restriction and lipid-lactate peaks consistent with purulent bacterial infection; however, typical pyogenic brain abscesses arise acutely from contiguous sinus or otic sources or acute endocarditis, unlike this patient's subacute 4-month course with splenic granulomas and extensive three-compartment suppuration.

diagnostic_pivot: Decompressive craniectomy with surgical evacuation of purulent material across the epidural, subdural, and parenchymal compartments revealed viable Burkholderia pseudomallei on microbiological culture and histopathology, confirming cerebral melioidosis.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old male farmer presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of fever (reaching 38.3 °C), fatigue, chest tightness, and generalized myalgia. On initial presentation, he was alert and oriented with a regular pulse and normal systemic blood pressure.
