differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on fever, respiratory symptoms, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest CT; however, typical bacterial pneumonia does not explain severe gastrocnemius tenderness, elevated CPK, marked thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, or sudden circulatory collapse following antibiotic initiation.

Considered due to acute chest tightness accompanied by elevated CPK and CK-MB; however, the CPK elevation was secondary to infectious rhabdomyolysis and gastrocnemius muscle involvement rather than myocardial necrosis, and coronary ischemia cannot account for bilateral pulmonary alveolar opacities or thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Approximately 90 minutes after initiation of piperacillin-tazobactam, the patient experienced abrupt cardiovascular collapse, hypoxemic respiratory failure, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage indicative of a severe Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction; bronchoalveolar lavage metagenomic next-generation sequencing and exposure to raw river water confirmed Leptospira interrogans.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old male presented to an emergency department in rural Colombia with a 10-day history of high fever, holocranial headache, generalized myalgia, arthralgia, and retro-ocular pain, accompanied by sudden-onset epistaxis and dark urine (choluria).

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (Hepatitis B / Hepatitis C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of high fevers, choluria, and elevated serum transaminases; however, serological screening for hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody was completely non-reactive.

Initial presentation with retroocular pain, epistaxis, thrombocytopenia, and plasma leakage on ultrasound met criteria for dengue with warning signs; however, persistence of high fevers 72 hours into inpatient fluid therapy prompted blood smear analysis, revealing intraerythrocytic protozoa and disproving isolated viral disease.

Although Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia was confirmed, isolated malaria does not explain prominent third-space plasma leakage (ascites, pleural effusion, and gallbladder wall thickening), and acute MAC-ELISA and molecular PCR testing confirmed active viral co-infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Giemsa-stained thick and thin blood films revealed intraerythrocytic ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum (parasitemia index 2.3%, 215,000 parasites/μL) alongside positive MAC-ELISA and PCR for dengue virus type 2, confirming concurrent dual infection.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and end-stage kidney disease on twice-weekly compassionate hemodialysis presented to the emergency department for scheduled dialysis with subacute progressive abdominal distension and discomfort.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected due to end-stage kidney disease and a twice-weekly dialysis schedule; ruled out because ascitic fluid analysis revealed an exudative low serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG < 1.1 g/dL), elevated adenosine deaminase, and imaging demonstrated diffuse peritoneal thickening and omental caking inconsistent with hydrostatically mediated ascites.

Diffuse nodular omental thickening ('omental caking') with exudative effusions and hypercalcemia suggested metastatic malignancy; however, fluid cytology and flow cytometry of pleural and nodal specimens were negative for malignancy, and cervical lymph node biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with central necrosis.

Considered due to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D-mediated hypercalcemia, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and perilymphatic pulmonary nodules; however, cervical lymph node core biopsy revealed central caseous necrosis rather than non-necrotizing granulomas, and sputum tests confirmed active mycobacterial disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Ascitic fluid analysis demonstrated a low serum-ascites albumin gradient (<1.1 g/dL) with an elevated adenosine deaminase level of 32.6 U/L, cervical lymph node core biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, and sputum acid-fast smear and polymerase chain reaction confirmed pan-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male presented to the hospital with a 1-week history of irregular paroxysmal episodes of severe shaking chills, high fever, and profuse sweating, followed by transient defervescence. Two months prior to this presentation, he had completed six cycles of immunochemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone [R-CHOP]) for CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma originating in the right maxillary sinus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the leukocyte count of 2,000 cells/μL and recent cytotoxic therapy; however, the paroxysms began two full months after chemotherapy completion (well beyond the expected marrow nadir) and exhibited an irregular cyclical pattern of rigors, fevers, and drenching sweats unresponsive to broad-spectrum supportive care.

Considered because new fevers, night sweats, and severe pancytopenia in a lymphoma patient suggest marrow invasion or relapse; however, restaging computed tomography performed only four weeks earlier demonstrated complete radiographic remission, and the patient achieved rapid hematologic recovery upon antiparasitic treatment.

diagnostic_pivot: Immunochromatographic testing of malarial antigen confirmed Plasmodium falciparum, establishing an immunosuppression-provoked relapse/recrudescence years after remote occupational exposure in endemic regions.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male presented with a 2-week history of sudden-onset, progressively worsening shortness of breath and dry cough. His respiratory symptoms were constant throughout the day without diurnal variation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the sudden onset of progressive dyspnea and mild tachypnea in a patient with multiple cardiovascular risk factors; however, computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed patent pulmonary vasculature without filling defects.

Considered because chest imaging showed persistent ground-glass opacities with lymphadenopathy and subsequent bronchial and skin biopsies showed non-caseating granulomas; however, bronchial washing molecular testing was positive for mycobacteria, establishing true coexistence rather than isolated sarcoidosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoscopy with GeneXpert PCR of bronchial washings was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing active pulmonary tuberculosis triggered in the setting of long-term biological therapy.

clinical_summary: A female infant who previously presented at 9 months of age with severe failure to thrive, congenital heart disease, and bronchopneumonia underwent successful surgical ligation of a 0.4 cm patent ductus arteriosus at 15 months of age, with post-operative echocardiography confirming complete closure and zero residual shunt flow.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to recurrent fevers, cough, coarse crackles, and perihilar opacities; however, the infant failed three separate outpatient courses of broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy and chest physiotherapy, with progressive clinical decline and severe wasting over three months.

differentials.candidate: Residual Congestive Heart Failure / Surgical Complication
differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected given the S3 gallop rhythm, tachypnea, hepatomegaly, and cardiomegaly; however, post-operative echocardiography confirmed complete ligation of the ductus arteriosus without residual left-to-right shunt flow, indicating that cardiorespiratory distress was secondary to chronic severe pulmonary infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite a negative molecular GeneXpert assay (frequent in paucibacillary pediatric disease), the constellation of chronic unresolving pneumonia, failure to thrive with weight loss, and characteristic bilateral perihilar opacities led to empiric anti-tubercular therapy, producing rapid symptomatic resolution and robust weight gain.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male avid freshwater fisherman presented for evaluation of acute-onset blurred vision and an inferior visual field defect in the right eye of one day's duration. At initial onset, he reported no fevers, chills, headache, or constitutional symptoms, but recalled an insect bite-like skin induration on his lateral left leg two to three days prior to visual symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected due to acute unilateral optic disc edema and visual field defects, and managed with intravenous corticosteroids; however, vision paradoxically worsened during steroid therapy, the patient developed high fevers with an eschar and lymphadenopathy, and cell-based autoantibody assays for AQP-4, MOG, and GFAP were completely negative.

Considered given the acute optic neuritis accompanied by acute febrile illness and lymphadenopathy; however, comprehensive serological testing for Treponema pallidum, herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and cytomegalovirus was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Physical examination identifying a classic inoculation eschar on the lower extremity with regional lymphadenitis following wild outdoor exposure, coupled with positive serum metagenomic next-generation sequencing for Orientia tsutsugamushi, confirmed optic neuritis secondary to scrub typhus.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old male presented to the emergency department after waking up with an acute, severe generalized headache accompanied by profuse projectile vomiting. Over the preceding two weeks, he had noted progressively worsening holocranial headaches and episodes of blurred vision, which had provided only transient relief with over-the-counter analgesics.

differentials.candidate: Colloid Cyst of the Third Ventricle
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because colloid cysts are classic causes of acute episodic obstructive hydrocephalus and headache at the foramen of Monro; however, colloid cysts are located in the anterosuperior third ventricle, appear hyperdense on unenhanced CT, and lack an internal eccentric mural nodule (scolex).

Considered given the non-enhancing, thin-walled cystic appearance within the lateral ventricle; however, benign congenital cysts typically lack an eccentric mural nodule and do not produce inflammatory CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis or positive helminthic serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an intraventricular cyst containing a pathognomonic eccentric mural nodule (representing the larval scolex) obstructing the foramen of Monro, confirmed by CSF ELISA positivity for parasitic antibodies and intraoperative endoscopic extraction revealing a visible larval scolex.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old male presented to the hospital with a 1-week history of persistent nausea and vomiting, accompanied by progressive fatigue and pallor. He denied productive cough, fever, chills, chest pain, or hemoptysis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because high-count acute myeloid leukemia can infiltrate lung parenchyma; however, leukemic infiltration characteristically produces diffuse interstitial or alveolar opacities rather than localized apical cavitary lesions, and sputum smear confirmed high-density acid-fast bacilli.

Cavitary lung lesions in acute leukemia patients frequently indicate opportunistic mold infections; however, sputum examination revealed heavy acid-fast bacilli (AFB 3+) without fungal elements, and lesions progressively regressed upon antimycobacterial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Pre-chemotherapy chest computed tomography demonstrated a right upper lung cavitary lesion, and sputum smears showed acid-fast bacilli 3+, confirming active pulmonary tuberculosis reactivation complicating newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old female presents with a 4-year history of epigastric abdominal pain, loose stools, and significant weight loss despite a good appetite and adequate oral intake. The abdominal discomfort is non-radiating and unrelated to meals.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial terminal ileal aphthous ulcerations with intervening normal mucosa suggested Crohn's disease, but the patient failed to improve on corticosteroid therapy and repeat mucosal staining demonstrated acid-fast bacilli.
The patient had previously received triple therapy for dyspepsia, but lower gastrointestinal symptoms persisted and follow-up non-invasive antigen testing was negative.
Chronic watery diarrhea and significant weight loss raised suspicion for chronic parasitic or helminthic enteritis, but direct microscopic evaluation of stool specimens showed no ova or parasites.

diagnostic_pivot: Failure of empiric steroid therapy prompted repeat tuberculin testing (which converted to a 27 mm induration) and a second colonoscopy with mucosal biopsy, where acid-fast bacilli staining identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis, leading to complete symptom resolution and weight gain on antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male primary school director with a history of euthyroid goiter presents with a 1-week history of acute febrile illness accompanied by deep jaundice, abdominal pain, and loose stools.

differentials.candidate: Sepsis of acute intra-abdominal / biliary origin
differentials.rule_out_reason: Markedly elevated leukocytosis, fever, and right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness prompted consideration of acute cholangitis or severe intra-abdominal sepsis, but ultrasonography showed non-dilated bile ducts and blood cultures isolated no pathogenic organisms.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis / systemic viral infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with transaminitis raised suspicion for acute viral hepatotropic infection, but serologies for hepatitis A, B, C, HIV, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative.
Acute febrile jaundice accompanied by severe thrombocytopenia and acute renal failure strongly mimicked severe malaria, but the patient had no epidemiological travel history to an endemic area.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of acute febrile icterohemorrhagic hepatonephritis, marked thrombocytopenia, and sudden secondary necrotizing pancreatitis following domestic house renovation was confirmed by a positive microscopic agglutination test (MAT) with a 1:400 titer against Leptospira biflexa.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male with a history of inflammatory colonic disease diagnosed in 2017 presents to the emergency department with a 10-day history of cyclic high-grade fevers (101°F to 104°F) and right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis on initial CT imaging and treated empirically with broad-spectrum piperacillin/tazobactam, but ruled out when percutaneous aspirate Gram staining and bacterial cultures yielded no growth.

Considered given space-occupying cystic liver lesions in a patient with a remote history of travel to endemic Mediterranean and Middle Eastern regions, but excluded by specific serological evaluation.

diagnostic_pivot: Entamoeba histolytica enzyme immunoassay of serum returned positive on day 7, confirming an amebic liver abscess that was successfully eradicated with a two-week course of metronidazole followed by luminal paromomycin.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old male presents for clinical evaluation with a 1- to 2-month history of daily high-grade fevers, marked progressive weight loss, and severe abdominal distension. On physical examination, the child is chronically ill-appearing, febrile, and exhibits marked abdominal distension with fluid shifting dullness and hepatomegaly on palpation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute high fever, profound weight loss, multiple hypoechoic hepatic nodules, necrotic retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and gross ascites in a pediatric patient strongly raised concern for lymphoma, but mesenteric lymph node histopathology revealed non-malignant granulomatous disease.

differentials.candidate: Multifocal pyogenic hepatic abscesses with peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple hypoechoic liver lesions accompanied by high-grade fever suggested pyogenic bacterial abscesses, but necrotic lymphadenopathy and histological confirmation proved a mycobacterial etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Mesenteric lymph node biopsy definitively confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis, while ascitic fluid analysis revealed high triglyceride content and MR lymphangiography demonstrated retroperitoneal necrotic lymph nodes compressing the cisterna chyli to produce chylous ascites.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old HIV-negative female presents with a 3-month history of worsening exertional shortness of breath and a persistent dry, non-productive cough. She reports no fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected given the high-incidence setting, monocyte-predominant pleural effusion, and markedly elevated pleural adenosine deaminase (56.2 U/L), but excluded by negative mycobacterial cultures and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on both pleural and pericardial specimens.

Considered due to rapid fluid accumulation, persistent cardiac compression, and subsequent development of a mediastinal mass, but initial pericardial fluid cytology and tissue histology showed no malignant lymphomatous cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histological examination of the resected pericardial window revealed granulomatous inflammation centered around Schistosoma ova, confirmed by positive genus-specific PCR on pericardial tissue in a patient with extensive childhood freshwater exposure.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old male presents with a 2-month history of progressive blurring of vision accompanied by floaters in his left eye. He reports no ocular pain, redness, fever, weight loss, night sweats, or systemic symptoms, and has no prior chronic medical conditions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the initial primary diagnosis due to focal retinitis and vitritis, even showing initial clinical response to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, but ruled out when specific serologic testing showed completely negative Toxoplasma antibody titers.
Considered in the differential for posterior uveitis with retinal vasculitis and neuroretinitis with macular star, but ruled out by negative specific treponemal serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Systemic infectious workup demonstrated a positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assay (QuantiFERON) and a positive tuberculin purified protein derivative (PPD) skin test with 12 mm induration, with definitive cure achieved after a six-month course of anti-tuberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: A young adult male in his twenties presents to the hospital with a 2-month history of progressive painful ulcerations with necrotic slough, high-grade fevers, and generalized arthralgias, on a background of chronic bilateral inguinal lymph node swelling present for 5 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered clinically due to the rapid appearance of necrotizing papuloulcerative lesions with hemorrhagic crusts, but excluded by histopathology showing neurovascular foamy histiocytes laden with acid-fast bacilli.

Punched-out cutaneous ulcers with violaceous margins and necrotic slough strongly suggested an autoinflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis, but histopathology revealed prominent vascular invasion by acid-fast mycobacteria rather than a sterile neutrophilic infiltrate.

The initial 5-month history of bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy was treated empirically with anti-tubercular therapy, but failed to improve, and subsequent evaluations demonstrated lepromatous disease rather than tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Punch biopsy of the ulcer margin demonstrated neurovascular foamy histiocytic infiltrates with vasculitis and abundant fragmented acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining, with PCR and sequencing confirming dual infection with Mycobacterium leprae and Mycobacterium lepromatosis establishing diffuse lepromatous leprosy with Lucio's phenomenon.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old Melanesian female presents to the emergency department with a 7-month history of persistent back and bilateral flank pain accompanied by intermittent low-grade fever. Her past medical history includes a Bartholin abscess, a right ovarian cyst, and a self-resolved pleural effusion in the preceding year.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent complicated urinary tract infection / pyelonephritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected repeatedly over 7 months and managed empirically with multiple outpatient antibiotic courses (nitrofurantoin, metronidazole, trimethoprim, amoxicillin), but symptoms persisted and cross-sectional imaging revealed large retroperitoneal abscesses and vertebral destruction rather than primary renal pathology.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis / acute psoas abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Presumed following identification of large psoas collections and treated empirically with oral cloxacillin, but surgical fluid obtained during bilateral drainage remained sterile on routine bacterial culture media.

diagnostic_pivot: Failure of fluid from the psoas abscess to yield routine bacterial growth prompted targeted epidemiologic screening, uncovering a history of having been primary caretaker for her mother with pulmonary tuberculosis; subsequent mycobacterial laboratory testing of the aspirate confirmed tuberculous spondylitis (Pott's disease) with bilateral cold psoas abscesses.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old Ethiopian male farmer presents for evaluation of chronic severe exhaustion, exertional shortness of breath, marked anorexia, tinnitus, and lightheadedness persisting over the past year. Over the preceding 12 months, he experienced progressive weight loss and intermittent, non-bloody diarrhea occurring every 2 to 3 months, lasting approximately one week per episode and resolving spontaneously.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected as the source of occult gastrointestinal blood loss causing profound microcytic hypochromic anemia in an elderly male, but colonoscopic examination was entirely normal.

differentials.candidate: Chronic malabsorptive enteropathy / occult intra-abdominal pathology
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given significant involuntary weight loss, low BMI, and episodic diarrhea, but transabdominal ultrasound was unremarkable without lymphadenopathy or organic visceral lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy directly revealed multiple small translucent, blood-engorged hookworms anchored to the mucosa of the first portion of the duodenum, definitively identifying hookworm infection as the etiology of severe iron-deficiency anemia despite multiple false-negative direct stool examinations.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old Pakistani male presents to the emergency department of a tertiary care hospital in Karachi with acute altered consciousness of 1 day's duration, preceded by a 5-day history of high-grade fever, chills, rigors, vomiting, and severe abdominal pain.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis (Hepatitis A, B, or E)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading differential diagnosis given fulminant hepatic failure with encephalopathy and severe transaminitis, but serologic markers for Hepatitis A, B, and E were negative.

Considered given high-grade fevers with rigors, right upper quadrant discomfort, jaundice, and altered consciousness in an endemic tropical setting, but rapid immunochromatographic testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Although an initial rapid test on day 3 was negative, follow-up enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) on day 8 demonstrated positive dengue IgM antibodies, while ultrasound confirmed hallmark severe capillary leakage with gross ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, and marked gallbladder wall edema.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with a thick, scaly lesion on his left cheek that had been present for six months. He had been well until six months prior, when he noted small papules on the cheek that gradually enlarged and coalesced into a single lesion.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Discoid lupus erythematosus classically presents on sun-exposed facial areas with follicular plugging, adherent carpet-tack scale, telangiectasia, and cicatricial atrophy, none of which were observed in this patient's lesion.

Tuberculoid leprosy (Hansen's disease) typically manifests as hypopigmented or erythematous plaques associated with definite cutaneous sensory loss and thickened peripheral nerves, whereas sensation across this lesion was completely intact.
Chronic granulomatous or lupoid lesions of the face can mimic deep fungal infections or cutaneous leishmaniasis, but cultures for bacteria, fungi, and acid-fast bacilli were completely negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The demonstration of peripheral apple-jelly nodules on diascopy, a strongly positive tuberculin skin test (25 mm induration), and histopathologic confirmation of well-formed dermal epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells established the diagnosis of lupus vulgaris (cutaneous tuberculosis).

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old man was admitted to a tertiary care hospital serving a rural population in central India. He presented with persistent abdominal pain and progressive abdominal distension of one and a half months' duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Crohn's disease classically manifests with segmental transmural inflammation, skip lesions, and fibrostenosing strictures of the small bowel, but the presence of centrally necrotic retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes and caseating granulomas on histopathology favored an infectious mycobacterial etiology.

differentials.candidate: Gastrointestinal Malignancy / Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma or Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Small intestine obstruction associated with multifocal strictures and extensive retroperitoneal adenopathy in a middle-aged adult raises strong concern for gastrointestinal malignancy or lymphoma, but central nodal necrosis, multiple serosal tubercles, and lack of neoplastic cellular atypia ruled out carcinoma.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast CT demonstration of jejunoileal strictures with necrotic mesenteric and retroperitoneal adenopathy followed by resection revealing mucosal ulceration, transmural caseating granulomas extending to the serosa, and acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining established the diagnosis of intestinal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old male originally from Nigeria with a medical history of hypertension and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department in the United States. He complained of persistent right upper quadrant abdominal pain that radiated to his back, accompanied by darkening of his urine.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial abscess (e.g., Klebsiella pneumoniae or Enterobacteriaceae) was the leading consideration given the patient's uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, systemic signs of infection, lack of recent international travel (>2 years), and absence of preceding dysentery, which prompted initial broad-spectrum coverage with cefepime and vancomycin.

A massive complex cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe exceeding 14 cm can mimic a cystic hepatobiliary neoplasm or necrotic metastasis, but acute fever, jaundice, elevated liver enzymes, and suppurative liquefaction on CT favored an infectious abscess.

diagnostic_pivot: Interventional CT-guided percutaneous catheter drainage coupled with definitive positive serological testing for Entamoeba histolytica established the diagnosis of an amebic liver abscess, leading to targeted treatment with metronidazole and the luminal agent paromomycin with near-complete radiologic resolution.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old girl presented with complaints of suprapubic discomfort and persistent constipation for two months. She belonged to an endemic region but had no prior history of fever, weight loss, urinary symptoms, or menstrual abnormalities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In an adolescent female with a pelvic cystic mass, an ovarian cyst or adnexal neoplasm was the primary initial clinical and ultrasonographic suspicion, but CT accurately localized the mass to the rectouterine pouch and revealed internal folded daughter membranes.

Non-gynecologic pelvic cystic masses can include mesenteric or peritoneal cysts, but these unilocular thin-walled structures lack the internal enhancing membranes and daughter vesicles characteristic of hydatid cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Pelvic CT demonstration of internal membranes with a pathognomonic 'cyst within the cyst' pattern in the Pouch of Douglas, strongly positive Echinococcus IgG serology, and surgical excision identifying laminated membranes with hooklets and protoscolices confirmed a primary pelvic hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old male presented with dull, aching pain in the right hypochondriac region that radiated toward the left hypochondrium for four months. He also experienced breathlessness, cough, and intermittent fever associated with nausea, vomiting, and significant weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a 52-year-old man presenting with profound weight loss, fever, tachypnea, hepatosplenomegaly, and simultaneous pulmonary, hepatic, and splenic mass lesions, advanced metastatic carcinoma or lymphoma was a prime diagnostic consideration; however, imaging demonstrated well-circumscribed fluid-attenuating lesions with internal septations, peripheral calcifications, and daughter cysts without invasive solid soft-tissue components.

Concurrent hepatic and splenic fluid collections with fever, jaundice, and leukocytosis can represent multifocal pyogenic or amebic abscesses, but the indolent four- to five-month clinical course, well-encapsulated multilocular cysts, presence of splenic daughter vesicles, and lack of septic shock argued against acute bacterial or amebic suppuration.

diagnostic_pivot: The occupational history of shepherding with close dog contact, combined with characteristic multiorgan multiloculated cystic lesions demonstrating internal septations, peripheral calcifications, and pathognomonic daughter cysts in the lung, liver, and spleen, established the diagnosis of multiorgan hydatid disease, confirmed intraoperatively and on histopathology.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old man with no prior history of chronic medical illness was admitted to the intensive care unit following an open right hepatectomy for a large, multilocular cystic hepatic lesion.

differentials.candidate: Acute Ischemic Stroke / Transcortical Territorial Infarct
differentials.rule_out_reason: Sudden vision loss and neurological symptoms following major abdominal surgery with considerable intraoperative blood loss raised strong suspicion for perioperative hypotensive watershed ischemia or embolic stroke; however, emergency neuroimaging demonstrated patent cerebral arteries and no acute cortical territorial infarction.

differentials.candidate: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis / Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute excruciating postoperative headache accompanied by visual impairment could signify intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, but non-contrast CT confirmed the absence of extravascular intracranial blood or venous occlusion.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency brain CT demonstrating a hyperattenuating, homogeneous sellar and suprasellar mass causing sella expansion, suprasellar cistern effacement, and bony remodeling confirmed acute pituitary apoplexy complicating major hepatic resection of a hydatid cyst, successfully managed with intravenous steroids and urgent transsphenoidal surgical decompression.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old woman presented to the medical center with complaints of intermittent fever for two months and mild abdominal pain located in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant for one month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A liquefactive liver abscess in an endemic setting with weight loss and abdominal pain commonly suggests amebiasis; however, Entamoeba histolytica IgG serology was negative and widespread necrotic multi-station lymphadenopathy is inconsistent with uncomplicated amebic abscess.

Liquefied hepatic collections with leukocytosis typically represent pyogenic bacterial abscesses, but bacterial cultures from aspirated hepatic pus showed no growth, and extensive centrally necrotic retroperitoneal and pelvic lymphadenopathy favored a chronic granulomatous etiology.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated Lymphoma / Hepatic Malignancy with Necrotic Metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked cachexia, high-volume weight loss, multi-station centrally necrotic lymphadenopathy, and a focal hepatic mass strongly mimic lymphoma or necrotic carcinoma, but CBNAAT and lymph node biopsy demonstrated caseous necrosis and acid-fast bacilli nucleic acid rather than malignant neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: CECT identification of a liquefied right lobe hepatic abscess alongside extensive centrally necrotic intra-abdominal and inguinal lymphadenopathy, confirmed by positive cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification testing (CBNAAT) for Mycobacterium tuberculosis from hepatic pus and inguinal lymph node biopsy showing caseating epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, established the diagnosis of hepatic tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 79-year-old man had previously undergone three partial maxillectomies, a modified radical neck dissection, and concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cumulative cisplatin dose exceeding 200 mg/m2) for left-sided maxillary squamous cell carcinoma. He subsequently presented for consideration of another partial maxillectomy for recurrent maxillary squamous cell carcinoma.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a cancer patient treated with pembrolizumab presenting with new pulmonary nodular infiltrates and fever, immune checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis was a chief clinical suspect; however, irAE pneumonitis is an abacterial inflammatory reaction that cannot account for positive acid-fast bacilli on respiratory smears.
Acute respiratory decompensation with high fever during cytotoxic chemotherapy raised concern for viral community-acquired pneumonia, but targeted molecular viral assays were completely negative.

differentials.candidate: Pulmonary Metastases from Squamous Cell Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral nodular opacities on chest CT in a patient with recurrent aggressive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma could suggest hematogenous lung metastasis, but acute high fevers and the identification of acid-fast bacilli on bronchoscopy confirmed an infectious process.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic bronchoscopy with right apical sampling and sputum evaluation demonstrating positive acid-fast dry smear microscopy (Gaffky 1), positive mycobacterial cultures, and positive nucleic acid amplification testing confirmed immunotherapy-induced reactivation of pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old man presented to the dermatology clinic with progressive cutaneous lesions on his left lower limb that had erupted two years earlier and had been progressing continuously since then.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient presenting with classic chronic extremity tumefaction, sinus tracts, and grain extrusion, true fungal mycetoma was a primary clinical suspicion; however, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) special fungal stains were negative, and molecular sequencing detected no fungal DNA.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous Tuberculosis / Non-Tuberculous Mycobacterial Infection / Chronic Pyoderma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic indurated nodular plaques with draining sinuses mimic tuberculosis verrucosa cutis, deep fungal infections (sporotrichosis, chromoblastomycosis), or chronic bacterial pyoderma; an initial blind punch biopsy showed only scarring, obscuring the diagnosis until targeted dermoscopic examination isolated the pathognomonic grains.

diagnostic_pivot: Dermoscopy-directed puncture demonstrating white globules that yielded white grains composed of Gram-positive filamentous branching bacteria on Gram staining, with suppurative granulomatous dermatitis and 100% Sanger sequence identity with Streptomyces sp. without fungal DNA, confirmed bacterial actinomycetoma.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old man who was born in Jiayu County, Hubei Province, and resided in Guangzhou (Guangdong Province) presented to the hospital with a two-month history of persistent fevers and recent melena.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In an AIDS patient from southern China presenting with chronic wasting, high fevers, diffuse pulmonary nodules, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and multiorgan involvement, disseminated tuberculosis was a major diagnostic consideration, but interferon-gamma release assay (T-SPOT.TB) and mycobacterial gene amplification tests were negative.

Bilateral uniform ground-glass opacities on chest CT in an advanced HIV-infected patient with severe immunocompromise strongly raised suspicion for PJP; however, PJP does not explain overt gastrointestinal hemorrhage, progressive hepatic failure with biliary obstruction, or systemic fungal bacteremia.

High remittent fever, gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal tenderness, and hepatosplenomegaly in an endemic area could indicate severe Salmonella enteric fever, but Widal serology and standard bacterial cultures were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive serum fungal biomarkers (elevated 1,3-beta-D-glucan of 80.10 pg/mL and positive galactomannan) combined with the growth of fungal hyphae in blood culture (subsequently confirmed as Talaromyces marneffei by blood, sputum, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cultures) established the diagnosis of disseminated talaromycosis in an AIDS patient residing in endemic southern China.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old man from Fuzhou, Fujian Province, presented with a 5-day history of dry cough and progressive exertional dyspnea, accompanied by low-grade fever (up to 37.7°C) for 2 days. His past medical history was notable for hypertension, end-stage renal disease secondary to uremia managed with long-term peritoneal dialysis, and a deceased-donor renal transplantation performed 3 months earlier (January 2019), for...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although bronchoalveolar lavage PCR detected Pneumocystis jirovecii and the patient initially stabilized on caspofungin and steroids, fever and asthma relapsed on day 13 and progressed to refractory respiratory failure, demonstrating an unaddressed alternative opportunistic infection.

Candida parapsilosis was identified from BAL fluid PCR and high-titer urine culture in the setting of indwelling lines and immunosuppression, but escalating caspofungin and sulfamethoxazole failed to halt pulmonary exudates and clinical decompensation.

HCMV-DNA was detected on admission, but pulmonary infiltrates worsened despite early initiation of intravenous ganciclovir, indicating that CMV was not the primary driver of the relentless pulmonary disease.

diagnostic_pivot: In a renal transplant recipient from endemic Fujian presenting with progressive bilateral lung infection, cytopenias, and elevated (1,3)-beta-D-glucan, blood culture ultimately grew Talaromyces marneffei on day 29, establishing disseminated talaromycosis.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old man from Ica, a coastal city in Peru, presented with progressive skin detachment, fever, and respiratory difficulty. He had a 10-year history of epilepsy managed with valproic acid and lamotrigine.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Lamotrigine is a common cause of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, but drug-induced eruptions almost invariably develop within the first 8 weeks of therapy, whereas this patient had taken stable doses of lamotrigine and valproic acid for 10 years without adverse events.

Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome produces widespread superficial flaccid bullae with epidermal peeling and a positive Nikolsky sign, but characteristically spares mucous membranes, whereas this patient exhibited prominent bloody, desquamative mucosal involvement.

diagnostic_pivot: In an endemic coastal setting in Peru, the acute high fever and rash were confirmed as acute dengue virus infection by positive NS1 antigen testing and reference laboratory IgM serology, establishing dengue as the infectious trigger of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old man born and raised in Anhui, China, was admitted for evaluation and treatment of portal vein thrombosis discovered one year earlier. His past medical history was notable for chronic hepatitis B diagnosed in 2008 maintained continuously on nucleoside analogue therapy, and splenectomy performed in 2016 following gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to ruptured esophageal and gastric varices.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An asymptomatic mixed ground-glass nodule in the right upper lobe in an older adult without elevated inflammatory markers (CRP and PCT normal) raised strong suspicion for early-stage lung neoplasm; however, lung biopsy showed focal granulomatous inflammation and NGS proved fungal infection rather than malignancy.

Metagenomic next-generation sequencing detected human gammaherpesvirus 4 sequence reads alongside the fungal pathogen, but viral capsid antigen and early antigen IgM were negative, indicating latent viral persistence rather than active pulmonary infection.

diagnostic_pivot: In the setting of bamboo rat ingestion, metagenomic next-generation sequencing of the lung biopsy specimen confirmed Talaromyces marneffei infection with 51 specific sequence reads, with targeted voriconazole therapy producing complete radiographic resolution of the lesion.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old woman presented with a 3-week history of low-grade fever with evening rises, symmetrical polyarthralgia involving both wrists and ankles accompanied by morning stiffness, bilateral progressive pedal edema, and frothy urination.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Constitutional evening fever, inflammatory polyarthritis with morning stiffness, and nephrotic-range proteinuria with hematuria strongly simulated SLE with lupus nephritis; however, serum ANA and comprehensive ANA profiling were completely negative.

Symmetrical peripheral arthritis involving wrists and ankles with marked morning stiffness and high inflammatory markers raised concern for rheumatoid arthritis, but RF and anti-CCP antibodies were negative, pointing to a reactive rather than autoimmune synovitis.

Collapsing glomerulopathy is classically induced by viral pathogens such as HIV, hepatitis C, hepatitis B, or SARS-CoV-2; however, serological and molecular testing for all these viruses was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Kidney biopsy demonstrated collapsing glomerulopathy, FDG-PET identified generalized hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy, and cervical lymph node biopsy with GeneXpert confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis with necrotizing granulomas, establishing tuberculosis with reactive arthritis (Poncet's disease) and collapsing glomerulopathy.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old female presented to the emergency department after 3 days of progressive, stabbing epigastric pain (intensity 9/10) associated with vomiting. On physical examination, she had dry mucous membranes, and her skin and sclera showed moderate jaundice (++ / +++).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe 9/10 stabbing epigastric pain, abdominal distension, and upper abdominal tenderness raised immediate suspicion for acute pancreatitis or a surgical abdomen; however, amylase and lipase were not elevated and marked hepatocellular transaminitis dominated the laboratory picture.
Reactive hepatitis A antibodies accounted for acute jaundice and transaminase elevation, but failed to explain persistent high fever and marked leukopenia in an arbovirus-endemic setting.

diagnostic_pivot: Persistent fever and leukopenia prompted serologic testing on hospital day 5, yielding reactive dengue IgM and IgG antibodies, confirming an acute co-infection of dengue virus and hepatitis A virus.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman presented to the surgical outpatient clinic with a 45-day history of swelling on the left anterior chest wall below the medial end of the clavicle. Over the preceding 15 days, the swelling had increased in size, become painful, and caused difficulty in swallowing.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic sternoclavicular osteomyelitis / bacterial abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bony destruction and rim-enhancing abscess collection suggested acute bacterial osteomyelitis (e.g., S. aureus), but normal overlying skin temperature, absent systemic fever, and indolent 45-day course supported a cold abscess rather than acute bacterial infection.

Focal cortical bone erosion of the clavicle and sternum with regional axillary lymphadenopathy raised concern for primary or metastatic bone tumor, but aspirate showed inflammatory caseous necrosis and acid-fast bacilli without malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded caseous necrotic material containing acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain, confirmed by Cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification test (CBNAAT) and AFB culture as Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with myelodysplasia-related changes developed fever and abdominal pain starting on day +26 following allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation. He had received cytarabine and daunorubicin before undergoing transplantation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Post-engraftment fever accompanied by isolated peritoneal lymphadenopathy and pulmonary nodules in a heavily immunosuppressed allogeneic HSCT recipient strongly suggested PTLD, but diagnostic workup ruled it out.

differentials.candidate: Conventional pyogenic bacterial sepsis / Neutropenic typhlitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute fever and abdominal pain in a post-transplant patient suggested deep opportunistic bacterial infection, but broad-spectrum empirical anti-infection regimens produced no clinical response.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing during febrile episodes identified circulating Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA fragments, and targeted triple anti-TB therapy prompted rapid defervescence, pain relief, and documented nodal shrinkage on follow-up CT.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old man with classical Hodgkin lymphoma (stage IIA) developed fever and cough on day +30 following haploidentical allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. He had a history of extensive prior therapies, including multiple chemotherapy regimens, autologous stem cell transplantation followed by disease recurrence, PD-1 inhibitor therapy, decitabine, CD30 monoclonal antibody, and bendamustine.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a post-transplant patient with persistent thrombocytopenia and new focal upper lobe pulmonary consolidation, acute bacterial pneumonia was the primary suspect, but empirical antibiotics failed and standard bacterial cultures were negative.

Severely immunocompromised HSCT recipients with graft failure and multi-agent immunosuppression are at high risk for invasive pulmonary mold disease; however, systematic fungal screening was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood mNGS performed due to thrombocytopenia preventing BAL identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA on day +45, followed by microbiological isolation of MTB from sputum on day +50, establishing pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old patient with no significant prior medical history was admitted to the emergency department with acute diarrhea and abdominal distension. The illness began 10 days before admission with a progressive increase in abdominal volume associated with vomiting, diarrhea, asthenia, and unquantified fever.

differentials.candidate: Acute bacterial peritonitis / Secondary pyogenic peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse tenderness, neutrophilic leukocytosis, and high CRP strongly suggested acute bacterial peritonitis; however, routine aerobic cultures on sheep blood, chocolate agar, and BHI broth remained sterile, and the fluid showed lymphocytic predominance (73%).

Abundant partitioned loculated ascites, diffuse peritoneal thickening, mesenteric infiltration, anemia, and marked CRP elevation raised suspicion for peritoneal malignancy, but the patient was an 18-year-old with sterile lymphocytic fluid and confirmed mycobacterial etiology.

Gross ascites and reduced prothrombin ratio (48%) raised consideration of cirrhotic ascites; however, liver function tests were normal, and fluid analysis revealed a high-protein exudate (64 g/L) rather than a transudate.

diagnostic_pivot: Because of sterile bacterial cultures and high exudative protein, real-time PCR Xpert MTB/RIF was performed on the ascitic fluid, detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex without rifampicin resistance, subsequently confirmed by positive mycobacterial culture.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old man, a known hypertensive and 10 pack-year cigarette smoker, presented for evaluation of worsening epigastric pain and significant weight loss. He had a 3-year history of occasional mild epigastric pain unrelated to food intake, accompanied by intermittent episodes of jaundice.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A smoking history, chronic back pain, profound weight loss, marked ALP elevation, and a hypoenhancing pancreatic head mass with biliary and pancreatic ductal dilatation ('double duct sign') strongly suggested pancreatic cancer; however, CA 19-9 was normal (19.43 U/mL) and the lesion completely resolved on follow-up imaging following medical therapy for tuberculosis.

Longstanding epigastric discomfort, mild lipase elevation (191 U/L), main pancreatic duct dilatation, and parenchymal changes raised suspicion for chronic pancreatitis; however, the focal pancreatic head mass resolved completely without surgical intervention upon anti-TB therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic workup for systemic wasting identified bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis via positive sputum PCR; Category I anti-tuberculosis therapy led to complete symptom resolution, weight gain, and total disappearance of the pancreatic head mass on repeat endoscopic ultrasound.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old male with a 12.5 pack-year smoking history and no family history of malignancy presented with painless jaundice and unintentional weight loss. He was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus maintained on sitagliptin/metformin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis given age, smoking history, new-onset diabetes, obstructive jaundice, ill-defined pancreatic head mass, and markedly elevated CA 19-9 (>1000 U/mL). Ruled out when fine-needle biopsy showed fibrocollagenous stroma without neoplastic cells and the mass resolved completely with medical therapy.

Solid infiltrating tumors of the pancreatic head can present with obstructive jaundice and biliary duct ectasia. Ruled out by the absence of neoplastic cells on fine-needle biopsy and complete radiographic disappearance on surveillance imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: Presentation of an ill-defined pancreatic head mass causing severe biliary duct ectasia and extreme CA 19-9 elevation that resolved completely, along with resolution of peripancreatic and perihepatic lymphadenopathy, following completion of a 6-month course of anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old female with a history of a treated childhood pulmonary infection presented with a 1-year history of intermittent, non-radiating epigastric pain associated with recurrent fever episodes, progressive weight loss, clinical jaundice, tea-colored urine, and pruritus.

differentials.candidate: Locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma with vascular encasement
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to an invasive hypoenhancing pancreatic head/body mass encasing major mesenteric vasculature (hepatic artery and portal vein) and elevated CA 19-9. Ruled out by young patient age, concurrent ileocecal mucosal disease, demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on intestinal biopsy, and complete radiographic resolution on antimicrobial therapy alone.

Considered given the combination of terminal ileal and cecal thickening with ulcerations and mesenteric lymphadenopathy. Ruled out by detection of acid-fast bacilli on mucosal ulcer staining and complete endoscopic and clinical resolution after anti-tuberculosis therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Colonoscopic biopsy of irregular terminal ileum and cecal ulcers showing chronic active granulomatous inflammation positive for acid-fast bacilli on fluorescence microscopy, establishing disseminated tuberculosis, with complete resolution of the unresectable pancreatic mass on anti-tuberculosis treatment.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old Middle Eastern male presented to the emergency department with a 3-month history of watery diarrhea, vomiting, progressive abdominal distention, and generalized abdominal discomfort, associated with an unintentional 17-kilogram weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease / Ulcerative colitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic inflammatory diarrhea, severe weight loss, pancolitis, and an inflammatory colonic stricture. Ruled out by endoscopic mucosal biopsies showing only mild lamina propria eosinophilia without granulomas or architectural features of IBD.
Suspected due to previous hospital admissions, severe colitis with marked leukocytosis, and acute gastrointestinal symptoms. Ruled out by negative stool testing.
Considered as a secondary viral cause of intractable fulminant colitis and colonic ulceration. Ruled out by negative immunohistochemical staining on mucosal biopsies.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of motile rhabditiform larvae on stool agar plate culture microscopy and confirmation by polymerase chain reaction, establishing Strongyloides stercoralis infection causing chronic fulminant colitis complicated by enteric bacterial translocation.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old female who had completed a multi-drug antimicrobial regimen 2 years previously for a chronic dermatoneurologic condition presented to the outpatient department complaining of occasional pain and tingling sensations along the inner aspect of her right arm and forearm lasting for 6 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary differential for a well-circumscribed, T2-hyperintense, rim-enhancing mass arising from the ulnar nerve with paresthesias. Ruled out by cytopathological examination demonstrating epithelioid granulomatous inflammation and necrotic debris rather than neoplastic Schwann cells.

Considered given the necrotic granulomatous background on aspirate in a tuberculosis-endemic region. Ruled out by negative acid-fast staining, absence of systemic or pulmonary foci, and clinical cure following leprosy re-treatment with dapsone, rifampin, and corticosteroids.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of necrotizing granulomatous neuritis involving the ulnar nerve representing relapse of leprosy, confirmed by cytopathology showing epithelioid and lymphoid collections in a necrotic background and definitive clinical response with complete subsidence of the mass following multi-drug therapy and corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A patient presented for clinical evaluation of chronic pelvic discomfort and a localized pelvic mass. There was no history of fever, weight loss, night sweats, or other constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because pelvic tuberculous involvement can produce chronic pelvic pain, cold abscess formation, and local mass effect. Ruled out by the absence of constitutional symptoms, normal laboratory investigations, and lack of characteristic tuberculous imaging findings.
Considered as pelvic tumors presenting with indolent pelvic mass effect and chronic discomfort. Ruled out by MRI showing a purely cystic lesion rather than a solid neoplastic mass.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of an isolated cystic pelvic mass on MRI with absence of involvement in any other anatomical organ, establishing the diagnosis of primary pelvic hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 1, presented to the emergency department with complaints of severe abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and high fever. She had delivered a healthy infant via uncomplicated vaginal delivery 17 days prior.

differentials.candidate: Puerperal sepsis / Postpartum endometritis with secondary peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial primary suspicion for acute fever and peritonitis presenting 2 weeks after vaginal delivery. Ruled out by the absence of uterine tenderness or lochial foul odor, peripheral eosinophilia, and discovery of a ruptured left hepatic lobe cystic source.

differentials.candidate: Perforated acute appendicitis / Perforated hollow viscus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute surgical peritonitis with diffuse guarding and rebound tenderness in a previously healthy young adult. Ruled out by cross-sectional imaging and laparotomy confirming normal bowel and a collapsed cystic lesion in segment II of the liver.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast-enhanced CT scan demonstrating a collapsed peripheral cystic lesion in segment II of the liver with thick enhancing walls, a parietal defect, and serpentine structures spilling into the peritoneal cavity, confirmed at emergency laparotomy with hydatid cyst contents and serous fluid.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old male, married with three children, diagnosed with HIV infection 12 years earlier, presented complaining of right upper quadrant abdominal pain of 5 days' duration associated with vespero-nocturnal fevers, chills, and diaphoresis.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (FHCS) from sexually acquired perihepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Accounted for the right upper quadrant pain, recent purulent urethritis, and ultrasound findings of an anterior perihepatic fluid collection with pseudosepta. Ruled out as an isolated entity because it does not cause splenomegaly with diffuse parenchymal microabscesses or intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated opportunistic fungal microabscesses (Histoplasmosis / Candidiasis) or Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in an HIV-infected patient with treatment interruption and falling CD4 count presenting with multiple splenic lesions and lymphadenopathy. Ruled out in favor of splenic tuberculosis based on typical imaging and nocturnal constitutional symptoms.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasonic demonstration of diffuse millimeter-sized splenic parenchymal microabscesses and intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy in an immunocompromised patient with falling CD4 count alongside perihepatic pseudoseptated effusion, establishing the dual diagnosis of splenic tuberculosis associated with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old male from Hunan Province, China, was admitted to the hospital with a 5-day history of recurrent fevers and a 4-day history of an extensive cutaneous rash. Immediately preceding the onset of illness, he had been caught in heavy rain, subsequently developing high fevers reaching 40.6 C accompanied by headache and weakness.

differentials.candidate: Systemic vasculitis / Autoimmune connective tissue disease / Adult-onset Still's disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high spiking fevers, widespread cutaneous eruption with symmetric brown plaques, and profound elevations in ferritin and ESR. Ruled out by comprehensively negative autoimmune and rheumatologic screening panels.

differentials.candidate: Acute bacterial sepsis / Zoonotic infectious fever (Brucellosis, Typhoid, Rickettsiosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given sudden onset of high fever (40.6 C) after outdoor rain exposure with elevated procalcitonin and neutrophilia. Ruled out by negative blood cultures, negative Widal and Weil-Felix tests, and fever recrudescence despite empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of skin lesions demonstrating perivascular Virchow cell infiltration in the dermis packed with acid-fast bacilli (bacteriological index 5.7), establishing multibacillary leprosy presenting with an acute Type II lepra reaction.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old female agricultural worker with no history of diabetes, immunosuppressive therapy, or recent trauma was admitted to the oncology service with a 2-week history of headache, neck pain, numbness in both hands, and low-grade fevers (up to 37.6 C).

differentials.rule_out_reason: High initial suspicion due to mediastinal mass, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, rash, and an outside biopsy showing predominantly T-lymphocytic proliferation. Ruled out by repeat lymph node biopsy demonstrating non-clonal reactive hyperplasia and definitive microbiological identification of opportunistic fungal infection.

Considered due to cervical spine fracture, multi-site osteolytic bone lesions of the skull base and spine, and elevated CA 125. Ruled out by a normal immunoglobulin free light chain ratio (0.80) without monoclonal spike, and aspiration confirming a purulent infectious etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of Talaromyces marneffei by metagenomic next-generation sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, confirmed by positive fungal cultures from neck mass aspirate and blood, coupled with high-titer anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies confirming adult-onset immunodeficiency.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male from West Java, Indonesia, presented to the dermatology clinic on referral from a rheumatologist with erythematous plaques covered with thick scales on the face, neck, trunk, back, arms, and lower limbs that were neither itchy nor painful for the past month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial clinical impression due to widespread psoriasiform scaly plaques and inflammatory dactylitis with painful interphalangeal joints. Ruled out by marked cutaneous hypesthesia within the plaques, absence of nail dystrophy, negative Auspitz sign, and bilateral peripheral nerve enlargement.

Considered due to recurring episodes of eyelid and facial edema responsive to antiallergy medications. Ruled out by the chronic 2-year disease course, progressive cutaneous insensitivity leading to painless thermal burns, and peripheral nerve trunk thickening.

diagnostic_pivot: Slit-skin smear examination from anesthetic psoriasiform plaques demonstrating acid-fast bacilli with a bacterial index of 3+, combined with skin biopsy showing epithelioid and Langhans giant cell granulomas, establishing mid-borderline leprosy with a severe Type 1 reversal reaction.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old female presented for outpatient evaluation with a chronic history of progressive constipation and intermittent rectal bleeding. She was employed as a healthcare worker in a tertiary medical center, with routine exposure to communal toilet facilities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis due to chronic constipation, hematochezia, positive fecal occult blood, and cross-sectional imaging demonstrating a 10 mm distal rectal wall thickening with mesorectal fascia thickening and suspected lymphovascular invasion; however, multiple rectoscopic biopsies demonstrated no malignant cells or neoplastic dysplasia.

Considered in the differential diagnosis of inflammatory intestinal wall thickening and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in a young adult, but excluded on histopathology, which lacked the noncaseating granulomas and transmural lymphoid aggregates characteristic of Crohn's disease.

Considered as a known infectious cause of bowel wall thickening, ulceration, and inflammatory masses, but ruled out because intestinal tuberculosis displays caseating granulomas on histopathological examination.

diagnostic_pivot: Endoscopic biopsy served as the pivotal turning point, definitively ruling out adenocarcinoma and revealing protozoan trophozoites, with follow-up cross-sectional imaging demonstrating substantial regression of the rectal mass following luminal and tissue antiparasitic therapy.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy man in his 40s was admitted to the hospital with a 15-day history of persistent fever, headache, generalized fatigue, recurrent vomiting, and poor appetite. Ten days prior to admission, he had received an outpatient course of broad-spectrum antibiotics, but his clinical symptoms failed to improve.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the solitary pulmonary mass, hepatosplenomegaly with multiple discrete low-density lesions throughout the liver and spleen, jaundice, and systemic B-symptoms (fevers, anorexia, fatigue), but ruled out by fine-needle puncture biopsies that revealed characteristic yeast structures without malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune disease or adult-onset immunodeficiency with anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as potential etiologies for opportunistic intracellular fungal dissemination in an adult patient lacking overt immunosuppression, but comprehensive immunologic assays for autoimmune conditions and neutralizing autoantibodies were unrevealing.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous lung aspiration revealed distinctive sausage-shaped yeast forms with a transverse midline division (fission), with subsequent mycological cultures from blood, bone marrow, liver, and spleen confirming the diagnosis in the context of newly identified idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia (ICL).

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old man presented to the hospital with a 9-day history of fever and fatigue, accompanied by 8 days of progressively worsening shortness of breath. Symptoms of fever, chills, headache, and generalized weakness began acutely after he was caught in heavy rainfall while fishing in an outdoor wilderness area.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered prominently at initial presentation because of acute febrile multiorgan failure following outdoor wilderness exposure and a 2 × 2 cm calf scab wound mimicking an inoculation eschar, but ruled out when microbial metagenomic next-generation sequencing did not detect Orientia tsutsugamushi.

Considered because a local clinic rapid assay was positive for influenza A, which explained respiratory distress and lung infiltrates; however, primary viral influenza cannot account for profound direct hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 261 µmol/L), severe renal failure (creatinine 606 µmol/L), and massive pulmonary hemorrhage after freshwater immersion.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred with bronchoscopic visualization of diffuse active alveolar hemorrhage and identification of spirochetal reads via blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), prompting high-dose penicillin therapy.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 10-day history of continuous high-grade fever accompanied by chills and rigors, 5 days of progressive jaundice, and 3 days of worsening altered sensorium manifested by diminished responsiveness and incoherent speech.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered prominently because of prolonged continuous fevers, altered mental status, and outside imaging showing splenic hypodensities concerning for septic embolic infarcts; however, bedside echocardiography demonstrated normal valvular anatomy without vegetations.

differentials.candidate: Severe malaria and acute tropical viral/bacterial infections
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the combination of high-grade fever, chills, rigors, progressive jaundice, splenomegaly, and altered sensorium in a tropical setting; however, empiric antimalarials produced no clinical improvement, outside evaluations were negative, and cross-sectional imaging showed microabscesses.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast-enhanced cross-sectional imaging established the presence of multiple nonenhancing abscesses throughout the liver and spleen rather than bland infarcts, alongside pulmonary consolidation, with definitive identification of Burkholderia pseudomallei in blood cultures.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old child presented with a 3-month history of dull aching pain in the left hypochondrium, intermittent non-bilious vomiting, and persistent low-grade fevers. He had no history of chills or night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis because of prolonged fevers, prominent splenomegaly, multiple hypodense splenic nodules on cross-sectional CT, and associated peri-hilar lymphadenopathy; however, post-splenectomy histopathological analysis revealed chronic granulomatous inflammation without clonal lymphoid proliferation.

differentials.candidate: Primary hematologic malignancy or bone marrow failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a child presenting with fever, splenomegaly, and peripheral trilineage cytopenias (pancytopenia); however, bone marrow examination excluded leukemia, aplasia, or marrow infiltration, confirming reactive marrow hypercellularity secondary to peripheral sequestration (hypersplenism).

Initially considered less likely because the child lacked pulmonary symptoms, sputum smears and cultures were negative, the chest radiograph was completely normal, and the 6 mm tuberculin skin test was interpreted as a cross-reaction from previous neonatal BCG vaccination.

diagnostic_pivot: Laparoscopic splenectomy performed for persistent cytopenias provided the definitive turning point, revealing gross whitish foci of caseous necrosis, with histopathology demonstrating Langhans giant cell granulomas with central caseation and acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old woman (para 5) presented for hospital evaluation with a 1-year history of a progressively enlarging bulging mass protruding from the vagina. She reported accompanying severe loss of appetite, an unintentional 30% loss of body weight, and severe dyspareunia with discomfort during intercourse.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the initial referral diagnosis from the community clinic given her grand multiparity and protruding introital mass; however, detailed gynecologic examination and pelvic ultrasonography confirmed normal positioning of the uterus, cervix, and urinary bladder, identifying the lesion as an isolated mid-anterior vaginal wall mass.

differentials.candidate: Benign vaginal cyst or vaginal soft tissue neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the smooth, cystic appearance of the mass arising from the anterior vaginal wall in an emaciated patient; however, fine needle aspiration yielded purulent material positive for acid-fast bacilli rather than benign cystic fluid or malignant spindle cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine needle aspiration of the anterior vaginal wall mass served as the decisive turning point, demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining with confirmatory culture, resulting in complete disappearance of the lesion and weight restoration on standard anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old Venezuelan female presented to the emergency department in Kansas with a large, painful, ulcerated wound on her lower left shin that spanned the entire width of her ankle.

differentials.candidate: Deep fungal or subcutaneous mycotic infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered during initial physical examination because of the raised, crusted borders and indolent progression despite antibacterial therapy; however, specialized fungal serologies and biomarkers including galactomannan, Fungitell ((1,3)-beta-D-glucan), Histoplasma, Coccidioides, and Blastomyces were all negative.

differentials.candidate: Refractory bacterial pyoderma, osteomyelitis, or bartonellosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the localized inflammation, severe pain, and chronic drainage; however, lower extremity radiography showed no cortical involvement or periosteal reaction, and sequential courses of amoxicillin and doxycycline produced no clinical improvement.

diagnostic_pivot: A punch biopsy showing chronic lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with poorly formed granulomas, combined with travel history through Panama and CDC polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the excised ulcer, definitively established the diagnosis of complex cutaneous leishmaniasis due to Leishmania panamensis.

clinical_summary: An 82-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department following several episodes of transient dysarthria and left arm hypoesthesia, each lasting a few minutes, accompanied by new-onset behavioral changes characterized by aggressive behavior.

differentials.candidate: Primary psychiatric illness (Panic disorder / Severe anxiety disorder)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the working outpatient diagnosis given his long-standing psychiatric history and recent surge in panic attacks attributed to environmental anxiety; however, purely psychiatric disorders cannot account for focal neurological signs (transient dysarthria and left arm hypoesthesia), elevated systemic inflammatory markers, or focal perilesional vasogenic edema on neuroimaging.

differentials.candidate: Transient ischemic attack (TIA) or Acute cerebrovascular event
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in an 82-year-old presenting with episodic, stereotypic focal neurological deficits (dysarthria and arm numbness) lasting minutes; however, non-contrast head CT demonstrated a calcified left frontal parenchymal lesion with surrounding hypodense vasogenic edema rather than a vascular territory infarction.

diagnostic_pivot: Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed active-phase cystic lesions with perilesional inflammation alongside quiescent calcifications, and confirmatory Taenia solium serology established the diagnosis of active neurocysticercosis, leading to successful treatment with albendazole and corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 69-year-old male farmer with no prior medical history was transferred to the emergency intensive care unit (EICU) due to rapidly progressive respiratory failure. Five days prior, he had developed high fever following occupational exposure to poultry manure while working on his farm.

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial community-acquired pneumonia with secondary ARDS
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary working diagnosis at the referring facility; however, typical pyogenic pneumonia does not account for the rapid onset of massive, life-threatening diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with profound thrombocytopenia (43 × 10^9/L) and extreme rhabdomyolysis following agricultural exposure.

differentials.candidate: Non-leptospiral septic shock with multiorgan failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given extreme procalcitonin elevation (>100 ng/mL), vasopressor requirement, and hepatic and renal dysfunction; however, conventional blood and sputum bacterial cultures failed to identify common bacterial pathogens, and targeted sequencing revealed spirochetes.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred when metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of blood and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid confirmed Leptospira interrogans infection (coverage 1%, relative abundance 16.45%), establishing the diagnosis of severe pulmonary leptospirosis with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old male farmer with no prior medical history presented to the emergency room with a 3-day history of acute high fever and severe bilateral calf pain, followed by the onset of hemoptysis and breathlessness for 1 day.

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial community-acquired pneumonia with acute lung injury
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute fever, tachypnea, high procalcitonin, and bilateral pulmonary exudative changes; however, typical bacterial pneumonia does not explain the striking constellation of severe bilateral calf myalgia, profound thrombocytopenia (12 × 10^9/L), and massive pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune pulmonary-renal syndrome / Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute alveolar hemorrhage, hemoptysis, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, and concurrent renal impairment; however, high fever, marked procalcitonin elevation (74.68 ng/mL), occupational farming history, and prominent calf myalgia with rhabdomyolysis (myoglobin >2,000 ng/mL) strongly favored an infectious zoonotic etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was achieved on day 3 when metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) performed on blood and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid confirmed leptospirosis, explaining the triad of calf pain, severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and multiorgan failure.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old boy from a rural region of Tibet, China, where yak herding constitutes the predominant economic activity, was admitted to the hospital following the identification of a palpable abdominal mass one month prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered preoperatively in the differential diagnosis of the right renal cystic lesion, but the co-existence of extensive non-enhancing hepatic parenchymal masses and intraoperative visualization of encapsulated translucent membranes involving both organs excluded an isolated benign renal cyst.

Considered due to the anatomical distortion and partial occlusion of the right kidney, but excluded because the lesion was an encapsulated intra-parenchymal cystic mass without primary pelvicalyceal collecting system dilatation or urinary tract obstruction.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive serum IgG antibody testing, combined with surgical exploration revealing multiple firm translucent masses with intact cyst membranes and powdery skin-like cuticular contents communicating with the biliary tract, alongside a right renal cyst, and histopathological demonstration confirming Echinococcus granulosus infection.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old male manual laborer in India presented with worsening shortness of breath and an episode of syncope following two weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea and a brief febrile illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading emergency diagnosis given the hemorrhagic nature of the tamponade and the anatomical absence of an aortic rim predisposing to mechanical perforation; however, both transesophageal echocardiography and CT angiography demonstrated the device in situ without evidence of cardiac chamber or aortic disruption.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or fungal device endocarditis / infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when PET-CT demonstrated intense FDG uptake on the septal occluder device, but repeated bacterial and fungal blood cultures remained sterile, and the inflammatory process localized to regional lymph nodes and the pericardium.
