However, color Doppler demonstrated an absence of intralesional blood flow with only peripheral rim vascularization, and subsequent biopsy showed caseous necrotic debris and granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant epithelial cells or lymphoma.

differentials.candidate: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (de Quervain) or acute suppurative thyroiditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis and acute suppurative thyroiditis can cause rapid thyroid swelling with elevated inflammatory markers such as ESR. However, subacute thyroiditis classically produces prominent anterior neck pain, exquisitely tender palpation, and transient thyrotoxicosis, whereas acute suppurative thyroiditis presents with high fevers and localized erythema; this patient had a completely painless mass and normal euthyroid hormone levels.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration yielded thick caseous necrotic material and cutting needle biopsy revealed multifocal granulomatous nodules associated with caseous necrosis replacing thyroid follicles, accompanied by a strongly positive tuberculin test, establishing thyroid tuberculosis that subsequently resolved under antituberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male with high-risk acute lymphoblastic B-cell leukemia in first complete remission presents for scheduled post-transplantation outpatient surveillance 12 months after undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation (SCT). The transplant was performed with peripheral blood stem cells from an unrelated Portuguese matched 9/10 donor (mismatch at the HLA-A locus) following a myeloablative conditioning regimen of busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and antilymphocytic serum.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Because the patient had prior biopsy-confirmed upper digestive GVHD treated with corticosteroids, new or persistent cytopenias in an allogeneic graft recipient raised suspicion for immune-mediated graft dysfunction or marrow GVHD. However, comprehensive clinical, endoscopic, and laboratory examinations showed no evidence of active gastrointestinal, cutaneous, or hepatic GVHD.

differentials.candidate: Leukemic relapse or donor cell myelodysplastic syndrome (secondary graft failure)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Fluctuating thrombocytopenia one year after myeloablative allogeneic stem cell transplantation for high-risk B-ALL is concerning for disease recurrence or secondary myelodysplasia. However, repeat molecular testing verified stable 100% complete donor chimerism, and surveillance evaluations showed no evidence of blast infiltration or dysplastic features.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when a 12-month post-transplant surveillance bone marrow smear unexpectedly revealed massive intracellular infiltration of reticuloendothelial macrophages by amastigotes showing hemophagocytosis, confirmed by PCR analysis as Leishmania infantum, with prompt hematologic recovery following liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of continuous, dull aching pain localized to the right flank region. She reports no urinary symptoms, such as hematuria, dysuria, urgency, or frequency, and denies fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, or weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Multilocular cystic nephroma or cystic Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a 13-year-old child, a large, well-circumscribed, multiloculated cystic renal mass with internal septations arising from the upper pole of the kidney strongly suggests pediatric cystic neoplasms such as multilocular cystic nephroma or cystic nephroblastoma. However, cross-sectional imaging showed internal daughter vesicles giving a characteristic 'cysts within cyst' appearance, and subsequent serologic testing confirmed a parasitic etiology rather than a neoplastic process.

differentials.candidate: Polycystic kidney disease or complicated pyelogenic renal cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital polycystic renal disease or an infected pyelogenic cyst can present as a palpable lumbar mass. However, the cyst was strictly solitary and confined to the upper pole of the right kidney, the contralateral kidney and lower renal parenchyma were structurally intact, and the patient had no fever, pyuria, hematuria, hypertension, or renal functional impairment.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when the characteristic 'cysts within cyst' appearance on abdominal CT prompted serologic testing, which demonstrated positive echinococcal antibodies by ELISA, confirming an isolated hydatid cyst in the upper moiety of an incomplete duplex kidney.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus and chronic alcohol use presents with left-sided chest pain and a newly noticed swelling over the left chest wall that has progressed over the past 3 weeks.

differentials.candidate: Tuberculous empyema necessitans and rib cold abscess (Mycobacterium tuberculosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A lymphocyte-predominant exudative pleural effusion with necrotic mediastinal adenopathy and chronic chest wall fluid collection in an endemic region is typically attributed to tuberculosis. However, initial pleural fluid ADA was low, and the patient deteriorated clinically with new rib osteomyelitis and chest wall abscess despite two full months of supervised daily antitubercular therapy.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis and empyema necessitans (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic chest wall abscesses and bacterial rib osteomyelitis typically present with acute high fevers, rigors, and intense local inflammatory signs such as erythema and warmth. In contrast, this patient presented with an indolent course, normal overlying skin temperature, and multi-organ splenic microabscesses characteristic of disseminated tropical granulomatous infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when aspiration of the chest wall swelling yielded purulent fluid that grew Burkholderia pseudomallei demonstrating characteristic cornflower colony morphology and bipolar 'safety-pin' staining on microscopy, confirming pleuropulmonary melioidosis with rib osteomyelitis that cleared on intravenous imipenem followed by trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old male with a medical history of essential hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide presents to the emergency department with high-grade fever, profound fatigue, and progressive shortness of breath. One week prior, he developed high-grade fevers accompanied by generalized myalgias, frontal headache, and weakness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a middle-aged smoker with family history of premature CAD presenting in cardiogenic shock with an S3 gallop and severely reduced ejection fraction (10%), acute myocardial infarction was an immediate concern. However, ECG lacked ischemic ST deviations, echocardiography showed global dilation without regional wall motion abnormalities, cardiac enzymes were only mildly elevated without typical rise-and-fall kinetics, and cardiac catheterization revealed normal coronaries.

differentials.candidate: Fulminant viral myocarditis (e.g., enterovirus, adenovirus) or septic shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute biventricular decompensation and cardiovascular collapse after a febrile prodrome can represent fulminant myocarditis or severe bacterial sepsis. However, blood cultures were sterile, and acute fulminant necrosis was ruled out because cardiac biomarkers remained stable and low over the course of hospitalization despite marked ventricular dilatation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when acute serologic and molecular testing—heralded by baseline IgG positivity, Day 3 IgM seroconversion, and RT-PCR positive for dengue virus serotype 3 (DEN-3)—confirmed severe secondary dengue infection complicated by acute dilated cardiomyopathy.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old female presents to the emergency department for the evaluation and management of sudden-onset shortness of breath. She has no prior medical, surgical, or travel history and takes no medications.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital pericardial cysts are benign developmental anomalies that typically appear as unilocular, thin-walled, water-density lesions without internal architecture. However, CT and echocardiography in this patient showed an encapsulated, compartmentalized lesion containing distinct internal banded membrane structures (detached parasitic membranes) exerting severe mass effect upon the right ventricle.

differentials.candidate: Pericardial cystic teratoma or cystic thymoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary pericardial or mediastinal germ cell tumors and cystic thymomas can present acutely with mass effect compressing cardiac chambers. However, teratomas and thymic neoplasms characteristically contain heterogeneous soft-tissue nodules, fat, or calcifications, whereas this lesion was purely encapsulated fluid with internal membrane folds, lacking solid neoplastic elements.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when the distinctive imaging appearance of an encapsulated fluid lesion with internal undulating membrane bands compressing the right ventricle prompted serologic testing, which returned positive for hydatid antibodies, confirming a primary pericardial hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old woman residing in a rural village presents to the dermatology outpatient clinic with a 12-year history of progressive, multiple swellings and chronically discharging wounds involving the left shoulder region and chest wall.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic suppurative granulomatous nodules with multiple draining sinuses and fibrosis over the shoulder and chest wall commonly represent bacterial botryomycosis or actinomycetoma. Pus culture initially isolated Staphylococcus aureus in pure culture, prompting a presumptive diagnosis of botryomycosis; however, antibacterial therapy yielded no improvement, and tissue biopsy demonstrated dematiaceous fungal mycelia rather than bacterial granules.

In endemic regions, cutaneous tuberculosis frequently causes chronic cold subcutaneous nodules that break down to form draining sinuses with extensive scarring and hyperpigmentation. However, the patient had no regional lymphadenopathy, routine systemic and radiological investigations were normal, and multiple biopsies revealed fungal colonies rather than caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when multiple deep tissue biopsy fragments cultured on Sabouraud dextrose agar yielded black colonies identified microscopically by four-celled conidia with swollen subterminal cells as Curvularia species, corroborated by histopathology showing dark fungal mycelia within granulomas, establishing eumycotic mycetoma that resolved under itraconazole.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male from Nepal presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of high-grade fever, multiple joint pains, and joint swelling, preceded by a 4-week history of progressive, painful nodular skin lesions involving his face, scalp, bilateral ears, all four extremities, and upper chest.

differentials.candidate: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) or Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) / Systemic Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: High-grade fever, symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis, extreme leukocytosis (>35,000/uL), thrombocytosis, highly elevated acute-phase reactants (CRP 335 mg/L, ESR 87 mm/h), and active glomerulonephritis strongly mimic severe rheumatologic diseases such as AOSD or lupus nephritis. However, autoantibodies (ANA, RF, anti-CCP) were negative, complements were normal, and the patient exhibited bilaterally thickened ulnar nerve trunks alongside nodular lesions, pointing to a granulomatous mycobacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Reactive arthritis or Disseminated gonococcal infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile polyarthritis accompanied by prominent lower-extremity enthesitis (quadriceps insertion) and wrist tenosynovitis is characteristic of reactive arthritis. However, there were no preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary symptoms, plain radiographs of the hands and feet showed no periostitis or erosions, and reactive arthritis does not cause bilateral peripheral nerve enlargement.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when peripheral nerve enlargement in an endemic patient with tender nodules and polyarthritis led to a skin punch biopsy revealing non-necrotizing granulomas with foamy macrophages containing acid-fast bacilli, confirming borderline tuberculoid leprosy presenting with erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction).

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency department with acute diffuse abdominal pain and intermittent fever. His medical history is notable for a 2-year history of recurrent crampy abdominal pain and unintentional weight loss of 15 kg.

differentials.candidate: Refractory Crohn's disease with free ileal perforation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Transmural inflammation with small-bowel skip lesions, post-inflammatory ileal strictures, and enteroenteric fistulization closely mimics aggressive Crohn's disease. However, the patient failed to respond to combined corticosteroid and azathioprine therapy and suffered fatal progression to free bowel perforation, with surgical histology from the perforation site demonstrating granulomatous inflammation containing acid-fast bacilli.

differentials.candidate: Primary intestinal lymphoma or gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma with perforation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe 2-year constitutional weight loss (15 kg), chronic abdominal pain, polypoid mucosal lesions in the terminal ileum, and acute intestinal perforation can indicate gastrointestinal lymphoma or malignant stricturing neoplasm. However, initial colonoscopic biopsies showed only chronic inflammation without malignant cells, and histological evaluation of the resected perforated segment revealed caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli rather than neoplastic infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during emergency laparotomy for bowel perforation following failed immunosuppression, when histopathological evaluation of the resected terminal ileum revealed caseating granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli, confirmed as miliary and intestinal tuberculosis by positive PCR and mycobacterial culture from sputum, stool, and ascites.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old woman with no prior medical history presents to the emergency department with mental confusion and fever that developed over the preceding ten days. She is a resident of Tunisia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute bacterial brain abscesses typically produce marked peripheral leukocytosis and a neutrophilic CSF profile if meningeal inflammation is present, and would be expected to respond to standard broad-spectrum cephalosporins (empiric cefotaxime), whereas this patient demonstrated marked lymphocytic pleocytosis (76% of 340 WBC/mm³) and subsequent multifocal infratentorial and supratentorial lesions.

HSV encephalitis frequently presents with fever, acute confusion, neck stiffness, temporal lobe localization, and lymphocytic pleocytosis, prompting immediate empiric acyclovir therapy; however, the presence of discrete ring-enhancing abscesses on CT and MRI and development of hydrocephalus and vermian lesions exclude uncomplicated viral encephalitis.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical presentation of subacute meningoencephalitis in an endemic region (Tunisia) accompanied by lymphocytic pleocytosis (76%), markedly elevated proteinorrachia (172 mg/dL), and neuroimaging showing hydrocephalus along with multilocular vermian and temporal brain abscesses established the clinical and radiological diagnosis of tuberculous encephalitis.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a 20-day history of progressively worsening headaches, vomiting, and intermittent fever. On physical examination, he appears well, and both general physical and detailed neurological examinations are completely normal.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial brain abscess was considered given the subacute presentation with headaches, vomiting, and intermittent fever; however, routine inflammatory markers and eosinophil counts were normal, and operative cultures failed to isolate any infectious bacterial pathogen.

Intracranial cystic lesions in pediatric patients typically raise suspicion for neurocysticercosis, cystic astrocytoma, or arachnoid cysts; however, the absence of perilesional edema, scolex identification, or solid mural neoplastic nodules, along with the operative finding of multiple spherical unruptured daughter cysts, excluded primary neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Frontoparietal craniotomy using Dowling's technique allowed delivery of a huge intracranial cyst and 19 intact daughter cysts without rupture, with definitive histopathological examination confirming the diagnosis of cerebral hydatid cysts.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old nursing mother presents for evaluation of generalized skin lesions that have been present for several years. The lesions initially began as painful subcutaneous nodules that intermittently discharged mucoid fluid, with a marked worsening during her last pregnancy (delivered six months prior).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Deep systemic and cutaneous fungal infections (such as paracoccidioidomycosis, blastomycosis, or histoplasmosis) were strongly suspected given the chronic noduloulcerative lesions with mucoid discharge, oral mucosal papules, and laryngeal edema; however, special staining of tissue sections failed to identify fungal elements.

Psoriasis and secondary/tertiary syphilis were initial diagnostic considerations for the generalized chronic cutaneous eruptions; however, the presence of painful subcutaneous nodules discharging mucoid fluid, partial eyebrow loss (madarosis), nasal mucosal crusting, and laryngeal infiltration are incompatible with psoriasis and ruled out by negative serological and histological criteria.

diagnostic_pivot: Skin wedge biopsy demonstrated dermal granulomatous inflammation with abundant bacilli identified on Wade-Fite staining, corroborated by Ziehl-Neelsen slit skin smear microscopy demonstrating numerous acid-fast bacilli, confirming multibacillary lepromatous disease.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old woman from rural Morocco presents with a two-year history of worsening pain and progressive swelling along the medial aspect of her right leg. She reports having undergone surgical excision of a subcutaneous cystic mass in the same anatomical region at another hospital three years prior, without receiving adjuvant medical therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A recurrent, enlarging deep muscular mass adjacent to major neurovascular structures in an adult patient strongly raises suspicion for a malignant soft-tissue neoplasm (such as synovial sarcoma or malignant fibrous histiocytoma); however, the multi-cystic fluid nature with well-defined scalloped walls and lack of invasive solid tissue proliferation on MRI, combined with positive parasite serology and surgical cyst walls, excluded a malignant tumor.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Pyogenic / Tuberculous Intramuscular Cold Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic intramuscular fluid collections can represent pyogenic abscesses or tuberculous cold abscesses; however, the patient lacked systemic symptoms, fevers, or erythema, exhibited normal inflammatory and hematological labs, and showed clear fluid-filled encapsulated architecture rather than caseous suppurative tracking.

diagnostic_pivot: The patient's epidemiological origin in rural Morocco, previous surgical resection of a subcutaneous cyst without adjuvant chemotherapy, typical MRI characteristics of multi-compartmental thick scalloped cystic collections, positive specific ELISA serology, and subsequent surgical pathology confirming hydatid membranes established the diagnosis of recurrent subcutaneous and muscular hydatidosis.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old multiparous woman from Ghana, at 38 weeks of gestation, presents to labor and delivery with suprapubic pain, pressure, vomiting, and suspected leakage of amniotic fluid. She also reports a three-to-four-month history of a frequent productive cough and progressive visual deterioration in both eyes that commenced early in pregnancy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Active uveitis, papillitis, and choroiditis in a young adult initially suggested an autoimmune ocular inflammatory etiology or sarcoidosis, leading to the prescription of topical corticosteroids and cycloplegics; however, this non-infectious mechanism failed to account for her chronic constitutional symptoms, subacute productive cough, and subsequent apical lung lesion.

The patient's persistent productive cough was initially considered as routine pregnancy-associated respiratory tract infection or common bacterial bronchitis, which contributed to delay in diagnostic radiographic evaluation.

diagnostic_pivot: Following delivery, maternal chest radiography revealed a 1.6 × 1.0 cm right apical nodular opacity, and sputum microbiological analysis confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis by positive acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear and culture, unifying her chronic cough and ocular dissemination.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension presents for evaluation of a large, painless mass on the right side of her forehead that has expanded gradually over two years from an initial marble-sized nodule.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An extra-axial calvarial lesion displaying bony destruction and inner dural enhancement was strongly suspected to represent a primary intraosseous meningioma, prompting preoperative surgical planning and neck dissection for proximal vascular control; however, histological evaluation lacked meningothelial proliferation and instead demonstrated caseous granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Primary or Metastatic Calvarial Bone Tumor
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's age and extensive osteolytic punched-out defect with dural and pericranial erosion, a calvarial metastatic tumor or malignant bony neoplasm was considered; however, microscopic examination revealed no malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological analysis of the en bloc resected cranial lesion revealed extensive caseous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes, lymphocytes, and Langhans giant cells forming granulomas infiltrating bone, confirming caseating granulomatous inflammation characteristic of calvarial tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old male renal transplant recipient residing in Miracema, Rio de Janeiro, presents with a three-month history of cough, a 6-kg weight loss over the preceding month, and recurrent febrile episodes for the past ten days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Tuberculosis was a primary diagnostic consideration given the subacute pulmonary syndrome of chronic cough, fevers, weight loss, and bilateral nodular infiltrates in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, prompting immediate empiric therapy; however, acid-fast bacilli staining of bronchoalveolar lavage was negative.

Acute-on-chronic bacterial pneumonia was empirically covered due to high risk of opportunistic pulmonary infections under tacrolimus and steroid immunosuppression; however, the indolent three-month tempo, failure to respond to antibacterials, and prominent mucocutaneous lesions pointed toward a systemic mycosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct mycological examination of bronchial lavage fluid revealed characteristic fungal elements, and biopsies of the oral and cutaneous lesions corroborated the fungal morphology, with definitive identification secured by culture growth of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old girl presents with a two-day history of continuous fever, severe retro-orbital headache, vomiting, and generalized myalgias. On initial examination on illness day three, she is febrile and uncomfortable but alert.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The subsequent acute emergence of altered consciousness, cogwheel rigidity, and bilateral thalamic and basal ganglia hypodensities in an endemic pediatric setting raised strong suspicion for Japanese encephalitis or other neurotropic viral encephalitides; however, lumbar puncture revealed completely acellular cerebrospinal fluid with normal protein, which is uncharacteristic of typical primary viral encephalitis.

Acute extrapyramidal signs and declining Glasgow Coma Scale (10/15) could suggest acute demyelinating encephalomyelitis or systemic toxic-metabolic injury; however, these disorders do not account for progressive systemic cytopenias (leukopenia nadir 1.9 × 10³/mm³ and thrombocytopenia nadir 50,000/mm³) and marked acute hepatocellular injury.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when serologic testing revealed positive IgM antibodies and negative IgG antibodies specific to dengue virus in the presence of acute transaminitis, hepatomegaly, and bilateral basal ganglia/thalamic CT hypodensities, confirming primary dengue infection with atypical neurologic involvement.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 3-year-old girl is admitted with a three-day history of continuous high fever, intermittent abdominal pain, vomiting, and retro-orbital headache. Her parents report an isolated episode of spontaneous gum bleeding on the first day of illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute onset of high fever followed on day 5 by tremors, cogwheel rigidity, masked facies, and bilateral thalamic/basal ganglia lesions in a young child strongly suggested acute viral encephalitis (such as Japanese encephalitis); however, CSF evaluation showed an absence of significant pleocytosis (only 2 lymphocytes) with normal protein, which argues against classical direct viral neuroinvasion.

differentials.candidate: Primary Coagulation Disorder / Severe Sepsis with DIC
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recurrent spontaneous mucosal bleeding (gum bleeding) in the setting of acute infection raised concern for an acute primary coagulopathy or disseminated intravascular coagulation; however, clotting parameters remained completely normal despite worsening thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by serological testing showing positive IgM and negative IgG antibodies specific for dengue virus, together with the evolution of leukopenia (2.27 × 10³/mm³), thrombocytopenia (67,000/mm³), hepatic tenderness with transaminitis, and brain CT demonstrating diffuse bilateral basal ganglia and thalamic hypodensity.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old Sinhalese man presents to the hospital on the fourth day of an acute illness characterized by high fever, severe headache, generalized myalgias, arthralgias, nausea, and anorexia. One week prior to the onset of fever, he had been digging a well and working in waterlogged rice paddy fields in an area endemic for freshwater-borne zoonoses during a concurrent municipal...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Leptospirosis was an equally suspected co-differential given the patient's high-risk exposure of digging a well and working in flooded rice paddies in an endemic region, leading to empiric antibiotic coverage with penicillin and subsequently doxycycline; however, the lack of renal dysfunction, absence of jaundice, and subsequent serological confirmation of acute viral infection led to antibiotic discontinuation.

Other flaviviral infections such as Japanese encephalitis (JE) can cross-react on serological assays; however, JE is extremely rare in the central hill country where the patient resided, he had no travel history or JE vaccination, and he demonstrated no encephalitic signs.

diagnostic_pivot: During a localized community epidemic, the patient developed classic biphasic hematologic changes and characteristic cutaneous flushing, with serologic testing on illness day seven demonstrating positive IgM and IgG antibodies specific to dengue virus.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old woman presented to the eye emergency department with a 10-day history of decreased vision and pain in her right eye. She had no significant past medical history and denied fever, weight loss, night sweats, cough, or other systemic complaints.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the elevated choroidal mass and serous retinal detachment; less likely given the patient's young age and the presence of ocular pain, but could not be ruled out until an infectious etiology was proven.
Considered among non-infectious inflammatory granulomatous causes of choroidal masses; ruled out by a negative angiotensin-converting enzyme titer and normal systemic assessment.

differentials.candidate: Ocular toxoplasmosis or HIV-associated ocular disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered among infectious etiologies for posterior segment granulomatous masses; excluded by negative serologic titers.

Epidemiologic assessment prompted targeted mycobacterial testing, revealing a positive QuantiFERON-TB assay and a 13 mm induration on tuberculin skin testing with a normal chest radiograph and no systemic involvement, confirming isolated choroidal tuberculoma that responded to antituberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old man presented with a 3-year history of recurrent upper abdominal pain. The pain was moderate in intensity, occurred primarily on an empty stomach, and was characteristically relieved by food intake.

differentials.candidate: Uncomplicated Helicobacter pylori-associated acid peptic disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed based on typical meal-relieved dyspepsia and endoscopic visualization of a duodenal bulb ulcer; ruled out when symptoms failed to improve after complete triple eradication therapy, prompting imaging that revealed pneumobilia and peripancreatic adenopathy.

differentials.candidate: Chronic peptic ulcer with gallstone-associated choledochoduodenal fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected preoperatively based on chronic ulceration, gallbladder sludge, and fistulous communication; ruled out as primary etiology during surgical exploration which uncovered nodular peritoneal seeding rather than simple benign peptic perforation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tuberculous duodenal ulceration with choledochoduodenal fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: Intraoperative identification of a duodenal nodule with fistulous opening and multiple peritoneal deposits, followed by histopathology showing caseation with epithelioid granulomas, confirmed gastrointestinal tuberculosis as the cause of the fistula.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old female who recently moved to the United States from Bangladesh presented to primary care with a tender right breast lump that had been present for 4 to 5 days.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic breast abscess / bacterial mastitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading acute presentation for a painful breast mass with systemic feverishness, prompting empiric oral antibiotics; ruled out when the lesion failed to resolve, Gram stain was negative, and histology showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation.

Considered in a 64-year-old postmenopausal woman presenting with a distinct palpable breast lump; ruled out by needle biopsy showing inflammatory abscess formation and necrotizing granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis of the breast
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although initial smears were negative, specialized mycobacterial cultures from the needle aspirate grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing primary mammary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old previously healthy girl was admitted to the emergency department following an epileptic attack, described as four episodes of partial seizures with secondary generalization. Her parents reported no preceding headache or vomiting, fever, or prior neurological symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary differential for a solitary large cerebral cystic mass causing seizures and focal deficits in a child; ruled out by the complete lack of contrast enhancement, absence of mural nodularity, and absence of perilesional vasogenic edema.
Considered given the mass effect and focal deficits; ruled out by the lack of fever, headache, or systemic signs, and the absence of typical ring contrast enhancement or surrounding vasogenic edema.

Considered as a parasitic cause of pediatric seizures; ruled out by the absence of calcifications, absence of scolex or inflammatory ring enhancement, and presence of internal peripheral daughter cysts.

Preoperative neuroimaging showed pathognomonic features of cerebral hydatid disease (spherical cyst with daughter cysts, hypointense rim, and no edema or enhancement), confirmed histopathologically following unruptured surgical extirpation via the Dowling technique.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old Tunisian male with a past medical history of appendectomy and ileocecal Crohn's disease presented to the gastroenterology department with persistent abdominal pain and vomiting. On physical examination, the patient was skinny and pale.

differentials.candidate: Isolated severe exacerbation of Crohn's disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Presumed initially given the known past history of ileocecal Crohn's disease, terminal ileal stricture, enterocutaneous fistula, and bilateral sacro-iliitis; however, mucosal biopsy of rectosigmoid lesions demonstrated parasitic ova rather than simple idiopathic IBD flare.

Considered as a major infectious mimic of Crohn's disease causing terminal ileal strictures, fistulae, and mesenteric adenopathy in North Africa; excluded histologically by the absence of caseating granulomas and the presence of trematode eggs.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Colonic schistosomiasis coexisting with Crohn's disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Histopathological examination of mucosal biopsy specimens from the upper rectum and sigmoid demonstrated submucosal schistosoma eggs with characteristic thick shells and terminal spines, confirming active colonic schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old female presented with a hyperkeratotic plaque on the left side of her forehead. The lesion started as a small papule 3 months after a roadside fall sustained 2 years earlier, gradually increased in size, and spread in an annular fashion to form a plaque with a warty surface, which had started showing ulceration over the preceding 3 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a chronic granulomatous cutaneous disease endemic to the region; ruled out clinically by the lack of sensory loss, absence of hypopigmented anesthetic macules, normal peripheral nerves, and negative epidemiologic history.

Considered as another clinical variant of cutaneous tuberculosis occurring on the face; ruled out on histopathology which revealed marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis characteristic of tuberculosis verrucosa cutis rather than typical lupus vulgaris architecture.

A strongly positive tuberculin skin test (20 mm induration) combined with punch biopsy demonstrating pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and dermal granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain established tuberculosis verrucosa cutis.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old Asian woman who had received a two-antigen mismatched deceased donor renal transplant 3 months prior presented with acute fever. Her post-transplant induction had included alemtuzumab and methylprednisolone, followed by maintenance immunosuppression with delayed-release mycophenolic acid (720 mg twice daily) and tacrolimus (target trough 9–12 ng/mL).

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic viral infection (CMV, EBV, Parvovirus B-19)
differentials.rule_out_reason: High clinical suspicion in an alemtuzumab-depleted renal transplant recipient presenting with fever and hepatitis 3 months post-transplant; ruled out by negative quantitative PCR assays.
Considered given intense lymphocyte-depleting induction and retroperitoneal adenopathy; excluded by histopathology which demonstrated granulomas without neoplastic lymphoproliferation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis complicated by IRIS
differentials.rule_out_reason: Para-aortic lymph node biopsy demonstrated acid-fast bacilli confirmed as Mycobacterium tuberculosis by NAAT and culture; following treatment initiation and reduction of immunosuppression, she experienced sterile abscesses consistent with immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal distention, bilateral lower extremity edema, and severe dyspnea. On physical examination, he was in respiratory distress.

differentials.candidate: Primary Budd-Chiari syndrome (thrombophilia / primary endoluminal thrombosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary cause of acute hepatic venous outflow tract obstruction and tension ascites; ruled out by imaging demonstrating that obstruction was secondary to extrinsic compression by an 8-cm hepatic cystic mass at the hepatic dome.

Considered due to cloudy ascitic fluid and prominent tension ascites; excluded by sterile paracentesis fluid, absence of polymorphonuclear predominance (90% lympho-monocytes), and negative Gram stain and culture.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Secondary Budd-Chiari syndrome and right atrial thrombosis induced by hepatic hydatid cyst (Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Emergency ultrasound and Doppler identified an 8-cm hepatic hydatid cyst compressing the IVC and left hepatic vein, with extension of a mobile thrombus into the right atrium, establishing secondary Budd-Chiari syndrome due to Echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old Indian male who arrived in Singapore from Mumbai, India, 7 months earlier for employment presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of high-grade fever associated with chills and rigors.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading viral differential in Singapore for acute fever, rigors, and severe thrombocytopenia with lymphopenia; ruled out by negative NS1 antigen and negative IgM/IgG serologies.

Considered in a young migrant from India presenting with acute fever, chills, and cytopenias; ruled out by positive blood microscopy demonstrating intraerythrocytic protozoan parasites and rapid response to antimalarial therapy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Plasmodium vivax malaria (with co-incidental Wuchereria bancrofti microfilaremia)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Malaria microscopy was positive, confirming Plasmodium vivax with 0.4% parasitemia; subsequent blood surveillance revealed concurrent asymptomatic Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old Zimbabwean-born male was referred with a 12-month history of cough. He was a lifelong non-smoker with no significant prior medical history, and specifically no history of pancreatitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on chronic cough, patchy sub-pleural consolidation on CT, and marked serum IgG4 elevation (4.61 g/L); ruled out when surgical biopsy revealed intravascular trematode worms and egg granulomas rather than IgG4-related storiform fibrosis and phlebitis.

differentials.candidate: Systemic vasculitis / connective tissue disease (e.g. EGPA)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the pulmonary infiltrates and relative eosinophilia (8%); excluded by negative autoimmune and vasculitic serologies and normal CRP.
Surgical lung biopsy demonstrated adult schistosome worms within pulmonary vessels and interstitial egg granulomas, confirmed by identification of Schistosoma mansoni ova in stool microscopy.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male military service member stationed on Guam presented to the clinic with 3 days of subjective fever, severe headache, intense myalgias particularly focused in the lower back, profound fatigue, and insomnia that progressively worsened throughout the day.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient had documented prior immunization against typhoid, lacked gastrointestinal manifestations such as diarrhea or abdominal pain, and microbiologic blood cultures yielded no growth.
Patients lacked insect bite exposures, had no characteristic skin rashes or conjunctival injection, and showed no hepatosplenomegaly on physical examination.

diagnostic_pivot: Epidemic clustering 2 weeks after freshwater and mud immersion in the jungle with skin abrasions, followed by seroconversion on convalescent serologic testing and rapid clinical recovery on doxycycline therapy.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old male Austrian resident presented with a three-week history of fever of unknown origin, severe fatigue, and an unintentional weight loss of 6 kg. His medical history was notable for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism, both managed on medical therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography identified no structural valvular focus of infection, serial blood cultures showed no growth, and prolonged broad-spectrum intravenous antibacterial regimens failed to improve symptoms.
Specific infectious disease diagnostics—including blood smear, serology, interferon-gamma release assay, and molecular viral assays—were repeatedly negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Progression of mild bicytopenia to severe pancytopenia in the setting of persistent high fevers, massive splenomegaly, and Mediterranean travel, leading to bone marrow examination demonstrating intracellular amastigotes inside macrophages and confirmatory molecular testing.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old woman presented with an 11-month history of occipital, neck, and upper back pain that was worse on the left side. Over the preceding month, her pain had progressively intensified despite conservative outpatient management at a local hospital.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although myelopathic signs and neck pain were prominent, purely degenerative spondylosis cannot explain the prominent constitutional symptoms including recurrent night sweats, fevers, profound weight loss, and marked inflammatory marker elevation.

While marked cachexia, anemia, and multilevel destructive vertebral lesions raised suspicion for a malignant tumor, cross-sectional imaging and surgical exposure demonstrated contiguous multilevel spondylodiscitis with a large retropharyngeal/paravertebral cold abscess draining 25 mL of purulent material.

diagnostic_pivot: Advanced cross-sectional CT and MRI imaging identified characteristic osteolytic destruction of the C5, C6, and C7 vertebral bodies with paravertebral cold abscess, which responded to surgical debridement, reconstruction, and quadruple antitubercular pharmacotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old man presented with a 6-month history of insidious, intermittent low back pain that had severely worsened over the preceding 20 days, resulting in substantial difficulty with ambulation and sleep.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to diffuse osteolytic skeletal destruction and elevated inflammatory markers, but excluded by normal serum protein electrophoresis and a negative bone marrow examination.

Widespread multi-level worm-eaten osteolytic lesions sparing the intervertebral disks raised high suspicion for metastatic malignancy or lymphoma; however, open surgical biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Open biopsy of the T11 transverse process lesion demonstrated necrotic cheese-like material and histology confirmed chronic granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, leading to complete clinical and radiological remission with antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male presented to the outpatient pulmonology clinic with a persistent cough that had lasted for two months. Over the preceding four months, he had experienced profound progressive fatigue, exertional dyspnea, diaphoresis, and an unintentional weight loss of 10 kg.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic pulmonary malignancy / Disseminated fungal infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread bilateral diffuse pulmonary nodules accompanied by prominent constitutional wasting and dyspnea raised high concern for metastatic malignancy or fungal disease, but sputum evaluation confirmed mycobacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss / Vestibular schwannoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute unilateral deafness and tinnitus were shown not to be an isolated idiopathic cochlear event or retrocochlear schwannoma, but rather direct hematogenous labyrinthine and brainstem involvement.

diagnostic_pivot: Miliary distribution on chest imaging with positive sputum testing for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, followed by brain MRI demonstrating multiple small parenchymal nodules and vestibulocochlear labyrinthine enhancement.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male presented to the clinic with a 2-year history of a slowly and progressively enlarging mass located on the hard palate. The mass initially appeared the size of a peanut and had steadily increased to its current size.

differentials.candidate: Salivary gland neoplasm (Pleomorphic adenoma / Adenoid cystic carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: While minor salivary gland tumors represent the most frequent cause of firm palatal masses, they do not explain the patient's subtle systemic facial cutaneous infiltration ('suffused face') and are excluded by biopsy.

differentials.candidate: Malignant bone / mucosal tumor (Squamous cell carcinoma / Maxillary sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The lesion demonstrated very indolent two-year growth without mucosal ulceration, contact hemorrhage, sensory nerve deficit, or regional lymph node involvement.

diagnostic_pivot: The slowly progressive lobulated palatal mass occurring in conjunction with subtle facial infiltration led to an incisional biopsy, which established the diagnosis by revealing characteristic histopathology with abundant foamy macrophages and mycobacteria.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old woman who emigrated from Ecuador 14 years prior presented to the emergency department with a 1-year history of progressive, intermittent abdominal pain, persistent diarrhea, and profound weight loss totaling 70 pounds.

differentials.candidate: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease) / Systemic vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: While transmural intestinal inflammation, diarrhea, strictures, and profound weight loss strongly suggested severe Crohn's disease or autoimmune vasculitis, autoimmune serologies were negative and the pulmonary involvement reflected active mycobacterial disease.

Considered because of severe cachexia, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and circumferential friable colonic ulceration; however, endoscopic biopsies showed necrosis without malignancy, and surgical pathology demonstrated granulomatous inflammation.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction from induced sputum and acid-fast bacilli in stool culture, followed by colonic resection histology confirming confluent necrotizing granulomas.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 5-day history of progressive generalized weakness, lightheadedness, frontal headaches, and fevers up to 102°F (38.9°C). Four days prior to arrival, he developed an episode of nonbilious, nonbloody vomiting followed by right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While fever, right upper quadrant pain, vomiting, diarrhea, and dark urine suggested an acute hepatobiliary process, the clinical pattern represented episodic paroxysms tied to remote jungle exposure.

differentials.candidate: Patient non-adherence / True drug-resistant parasitic strain
differentials.rule_out_reason: Repeated recrudescence after multiple regimens was thought to be compliance failure or parasite resistance, but compliance had been verified under directly observed therapy and without re-exposure.

diagnostic_pivot: Smear confirmation of recurrent intraerythrocytic parasites and host CYP2D6 pharmacogenomic testing revealing a *4/*5 null-allele variation (poor metabolizer genotype) preventing metabolic bioactivation of primaquine, resolving with extended chloroquine prophylaxis.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old pregnant Canadian woman (gravida 4, para 3) presented for infectious disease and obstetric evaluation at 13 weeks and 6 days of gestation. Five weeks earlier (at 9 weeks gestation), while visiting family and friends in Trinidad, she developed an acute low-grade fever and a generalized maculopapular rash 6 weeks after arriving on the island.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Dengue was a prominent co-circulating arboviral possibility given fever, rash, and retro-orbital headaches, but acute reverse transcription PCR was negative and serologic cross-reactivity reflected prior remote flavivirus exposure without active acute infection.
Chikungunya frequently co-circulates in the Caribbean causing febrile rash syndromes, but it was ruled out by negative acute molecular PCR testing and non-reactive IgM and IgG serologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive viral RT-PCR in maternal serum at 30 days post-onset coupled with second-trimester fetal ultrasonography demonstrating early neurotropism (asymmetrical lateral cerebral ventriculomegaly and dilated jugular lymph sacs), confirmed by viral RNA detection in fetal neural tissue and placenta.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old African-American female (para 2) presented to her primary care provider and was subsequently transferred to the emergency department complaining of progressive abdominal pain and distention for two weeks, accompanied by shortness of breath and an unintentional 10-pound weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Advanced-stage epithelial ovarian cancer / Peritoneal carcinomatosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although markedly elevated CA-125 with pelvic/ovarian masses, ascites, and dense omental cake was initially presumed to be ovarian cancer, ascitic fluid cytology and surgical biopsies showed noncaseating granulomas without any malignant neoplastic cells.

Pancreatic head and parenchymal hypoechoic lesions were noted on initial ultrasound, but normal serum CA 19-9 and CEA alongside tissue biopsies negative for malignant adenocarcinoma excluded primary pancreatic malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Operative diagnostic laparoscopy revealed diffuse peritoneal nodularity whose biopsies demonstrated granulomatous inflammation without malignancy, with definitive confirmation provided by positive mycobacterial tissue culture growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male farmer with a history of well-controlled diabetes mellitus presents with intermittent episodes of high-grade fever lasting for more than one year, accompanied by occasional dull aching pain in the left subcostal region.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient completed a prior 6-month course of antitubercular therapy without symptomatic relief, and subsequent fine-needle aspiration of the splenic lesion tested negative on GeneXpert PCR.
Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels and chest radiography were completely normal, and lymph node biopsy showed no evidence of noncaseating granulomas.
Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations or regurgitation, and serial blood cultures showed no microbial growth.

differentials.candidate: Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma / Hematological Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bone marrow examination was normal, and neither splenic fine-needle aspiration cytology nor axillary lymph node biopsy revealed atypical lymphoid or malignant cells.

The definitive turning point occurred when bacterial culture of the splenic aspirate grew Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming splenic melioidosis in a diabetic farmer with chronic splenic granulomas.

clinical_summary: An 86-year-old woman residing in a rural area presents with a subacute history of productive cough yielding yellowish-green sputum, mild shortness of breath, and loss of appetite. She has a documented medical history of a hepatic cystic lesion identified four years earlier, for which she received long-term medical therapy with unspecified agents.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial Pneumonia / Lower Respiratory Tract Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient remained afebrile without leukocytosis, sputum cultures demonstrated only scanty normal respiratory flora, and advanced thoracic imaging showed circumscribed cystic lesions rather than infectious parenchymal consolidation.

Airspace opacification was initially suspected to represent atelectasis, but thoracic imaging revealed this was secondary volume loss adjacent to a large parenchymal cystic lesion and pleural effusion.

Intraluminal filling defects in the pulmonary arterial tree were evaluated, but MRI demonstrated fluid-signal intensity with characteristic internal septations diagnostic of intraluminal hydatid cysts rather than vascular thrombi.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Echinococcosis (Pulmonary Artery and Parenchymal Hydatid Cysts)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Thoracic CT and MRI established the diagnosis by revealing multiple intraluminal cystic filling defects within the right main pulmonary artery and lobar branches, bilateral parenchymal lung cysts, and a known hepatic cyst.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old man presents with a six-week history of persistent low-grade fever, anorexia, and significant unintentional weight loss. On physical examination, he appears mildly pale.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Smears prepared from the enlarged cervical and epitrochlear lymph nodes were stained with Ziehl-Neelsen stain and demonstrated no acid-fast bacilli.

Cytologic evaluation showed a polymorphous cell population with reactive lymphoid cells, histiocytes, and tingible body macrophages containing intracellular amastigotes rather than a clonal malignant lymphoproliferative process.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Visceral Leishmaniasis with Leishmanial Lymphadenitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Identification of Leishmania amastigotes inside macrophages on lymph node FNAC, coupled with bone marrow smears demonstrating a heavy parasite load (5+), confirmed visceral leishmaniasis complicating HIV infection.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old female child presents with a 10-day history of worsening headache, multiple episodes of nonbilious projectile vomiting, and altered sensorium on the day of presentation. Her parents report no history of contact with household pets or farm animals.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient was completely afebrile without neck stiffness or other meningeal signs, and urgent brain neuroimaging demonstrated a large discrete intraventricular cystic mass with herniation rather than diffuse parenchymal or meningeal inflammation.
Brain MRI showed non-enhancing multicystic lesions without solid tumor components, and surgical craniotomy demonstrated thin-walled cysts containing crystal-clear fluid devoid of neoplastic tissue.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Cerebral Echinococcosis (Intraventricular Hydatid Cysts)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Emergency craniotomy and cyst removal yielded 30 thin-walled cysts; histopathological examination confirmed hydatid cyst architecture, and wet mount of cyst fluid showed abundant brood capsules and protoscolices, confirming Echinococcosis despite negative serum IgG antibodies.

clinical_summary: A 78-year-old man from a rural area in western Iran presents to an outpatient dermatology clinic for evaluation of multiple chronic ulcerative and exudative cutaneous lesions involving his mid-face, the dorsal aspects of both hands, and the posterior aspects of both heels.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic progressive destructive ulcerations of the extremities and face, but the patient had failed prior therapies for this condition, and initial histopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation rather than a neutrophilic dermatosis.

Considered for the chronic facial and acral granulomatous lesions, but skin biopsy revealed necrotizing rather than typical noncaseating granulomas, and repeat sampling identified intracellular parasites.

Strongly suspected when initial smears were negative and a tuberculin skin test showed 27 mm of induration, prompting a full course of quadruple antitubercular therapy; however, the lesions did not respond, and repeat tissue analysis revealed parasitic organisms.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis (Leishmania major)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Repeat dermal biopsy revealed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, mixed inflammatory infiltrate, and intracellular Leishman bodies; PCR-RFLP confirmed Leishmania major as the etiologic pathogen.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old man presents with a three-month history of worsening upper abdominal pain accompanied by intermittent vomiting, melena, and an unintentional 7 kg weight loss. On physical examination, he appears pale.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A palpable epigastric mass, profound weight loss, upper GI bleeding (melena), and deep excavated ulceration strongly suggested advanced malignancy, but biopsies demonstrated inflammatory caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells rather than malignant neoplastic tissue.

Multifocal gastrointestinal involvement with ulceration in the esophagus, stomach, and transverse colon and fistulous formation raised suspicion for Crohn's disease; however, abdominal CT revealed necrotic perigastric and periportal lymphadenopathy, and culture isolated mycobacteria.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Gastroduodenal and Colonic Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Histopathologic examination of esophageal, antral, and colonic ulcer biopsies demonstrated caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells, and mycobacterial culture via Mycobacteria Growth Indicator Tube (MGIT) was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old woman presents with a one-month history of recurrent nonbilious, nonprojectile vomiting occurring 1 to 2 hours after meals, accompanied by persistent low-grade fever. She reports marked loss of appetite and significant unintentional weight loss over this duration.

differentials.candidate: Peptic Ulcer Disease with Gastric Outlet Obstruction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Postprandial vomiting and microcytic anemia suggested peptic ulcer disease with pyloric/duodenal stenosis, but imaging revealed extensive necrotic retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and complex entero-colonic fistulization inconsistent with uncomplicated peptic ulceration.

The presence of ulceronodular lesions in both the duodenum and colon, colo-jejunal fistula, bowel clumping, and noncaseating granulomas on initial biopsy mimicked Crohn's disease; however, necrotic lymphadenopathy on CT and positive mycobacterial culture confirmed tuberculosis.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Gastroduodenal and Colonic Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Automated mycobacterial liquid culture (TB MGIT) of the duodenal biopsy specimen grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing the diagnosis of gastroduodenal tuberculosis complicated by duodenal ulceration and fistulae.

clinical_summary: A 75-year-old woman presents to an orthopedic clinic with a two-year history of left upper leg pain and the recent emergence of a discharging sinus over her proximal left leg.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial Periprosthetic Joint Infection / Chronic Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the discharging sinus and isolation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from the purulent discharge; however, surgical exploration and histopathology demonstrated parasitic membranes within a preexisting bone cyst, confirming that the bacterial infection was secondary colonization of a ruptured hydatid cyst.
A well-demarcated osteolytic lesion near a prosthetic joint in an elderly patient raised concern for bone tumors, but incisional biopsy showed no malignant or atypical cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Osseous Echinococcosis (Tibial Hydatid Cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pathology of the tibial lesion and surgical exploration revealed a diaphyseal cyst containing whitish aggregated membranes; microscopic examination confirmed osseous tissue with characteristic hyaline and germinative membranes diagnostic of hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 13-year-old male adolescent presents to the emergency department complaining of severe, continuous lower back pain and marked fatigability lasting for three days. He recently traveled to the southern region of Saudi Arabia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Spinal MRI demonstrated cord edema and abnormal signal intensity consistent with acute transverse myelitis, but the presence of prominent peripheral eosinophilia and travel to an endemic area strongly favored an infectious parasitic etiology, confirmed by elevated specific serology without requirement for immunosuppressive pulse steroids.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial / Viral Meningomyelitis or Epidural Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential of acute spinal cord compression and myelopathy, but cerebrospinal fluid Gram stain and bacterial cultures were completely negative, and brain MRI was unremarkable.

differentials.candidate: Intestinal or Urogenital Helminthic Infection (Ova-positive Schistosomiasis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Direct parasitological examination was pursued given eosinophilia and travel, but microscopy revealed no parasite eggs in urine or stool specimens.

The diagnostic breakthrough was achieved with a markedly elevated Schistosoma serology titer in the setting of acute cord edema on MRI, leading to complete clinical recovery upon administration of specific antiparasitic therapy.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old woman with a history of metastatic cutaneous malignant melanoma—previously treated with high-dose interleukin-2 and subsequently receiving maintenance therapy with the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor pembrolizumab—presents with a one-week history of new-onset hemoptysis, expectorating approximately 10 mL of bloody sputum daily.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient with metastatic melanoma, an enlarging pulmonary nodule associated with hemoptysis strongly suggested progressive metastatic disease; however, transbronchial lung biopsy demonstrated extensive caseous necrosis without malignant melanocytic cells.

differentials.candidate: Immune-Related Adverse Event / Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient had well-documented immune-related adverse events from pembrolizumab (sicca syndrome, vitiligo, positive anti-RO52 antibodies), raising consideration for autoimmune pneumonitis; however, chest CT revealed a localized expanding upper lobe lesion rather than diffuse interstitial/ground-glass opacities, and microbiologic testing confirmed mycobacteria.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis activated during PD-1 inhibition
differentials.rule_out_reason: Unconcentrated bronchoalveolar lavage fluid tested positive on GeneXpert MTB/RIF without rifampin resistance mutations, liquid culture isolated drug-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and transbronchial biopsy demonstrated abundant caseous necrosis with acid-fast bacilli.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old Japanese man who had returned from Nigeria was admitted to the hospital with a persistent high fever of 2 days' duration. Upon presentation, he exhibited dysarthria, expressive aphasia, urinary incontinence, and truncal ataxia, with clinical signs suggestive of cerebellar ataxia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's acute febrile encephalopathy, travel to an endemic region in West Africa, thrombocytopenia, and hepatorenal impairment. However, classical cerebral malaria is defined by unarousable coma (Glasgow Coma Scale score <= 11) with severe multiorgan failure, whereas this patient retained a GCS of 13, exhibited low parasitemia (0.05%), and lacked classical hallmarks of severe cerebral sequestration.

Considered because of acute fever, confusion, aphasia, ataxia, and elevated inflammatory markers. However, emergent head CT was unremarkable, cerebrospinal fluid evaluation revealed only a slightly elevated cell count with normal protein and glucose, and blood testing demonstrated parasitemia.

differentials.candidate: Acute ischemic stroke / focal intracranial vascular lesion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the abrupt onset of focal neurological deficits including expressive aphasia, dysarthria, and truncal ataxia in a middle-aged male. However, initial head CT showed no acute infarction or hemorrhage, and subsequent brain MRI revealed a restricted lesion isolated to the splenium of the corpus callosum rather than a vascular territorial infarction, which fully regressed on follow-up imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point was peripheral blood smear examination demonstrating intraerythrocytic ring forms with 0.05% parasitemia, confirmed by PCR as Plasmodium falciparum, in conjunction with brain MRI revealing diffusion restriction in the splenium of the corpus callosum that completely resolved on follow-up, confirming mild encephalitis/encephalopathy with a reversible splenial lesion (MERS) due to malaria.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man presented with complaints of suprapubic swelling and difficulty in micturition for the preceding 4 months. He reported straining to void with a noticeably diminished urinary stream.

differentials.candidate: Pelvic malignancy / Invasive pelvic neoplasm (e.g., bladder, rectal, or prostatic carcinoma, pelvic sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 4-month history of progressive lower urinary tract obstruction, constipation, and a large palpable suprapubic and pelvic retrovesical mass in a 50-year-old male. However, digital rectal examination demonstrated an extrinsic mass with normal mucosa, there was no hematuria or weight loss, and cross-sectional imaging demonstrated a well-defined encapsulated cystic mass rather than an invasive, infiltrative malignant lesion.

differentials.candidate: Pelvic abscess / Complicated bacterial urinary tract collection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the presence of pyuria (5-6 pus cells/hpf) and local tenderness in a patient with an obstructive pelvic mass. However, the patient was completely afebrile, lacked systemic leukocytosis (TLC 8,900/mm³), and urine cultures were repeatedly sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal turning point occurred during exploratory laparotomy, which revealed a large pelvic cystic lesion adherent to the urinary bladder and rectosigmoid, containing numerous daughter cysts and laminated membranes, with final confirmation of Echinococcosis on histopathological examination.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old man presented with pain in his lower limbs and a non-itchy, erythematous rash distributed over both lower extremities. He reported a low-grade, intermittent fever of 3 months' duration.

differentials.candidate: Connective tissue disorder with systemic vasculitis (e.g., SLE, Henoch-Schönlein purpura, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the combination of prolonged fever, lower extremity palpable purpura, and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia. However, anti-nuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, and serum cryoglobulins were negative, serum complement levels (C3 and C4) were normal, and urinalysis showed no active sediment.

Considered because of prolonged fever, wasting/malnutrition, massive splenomegaly, and severe pancytopenia in a young adult. However, CT scans showed no discrete malignant lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow examination demonstrated no clonal lymphoproliferation or blasts, identifying intracellular parasites instead.

differentials.candidate: Tropical rickettsial or chronic viral infection (HIV, scrub typhus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute febrile illness with rash and endemic environmental exposures. However, serologic evaluation for rickettsia, scrub typhus, HIV, and viral hepatitis (HBsAg, anti-HCV) was completely negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmatory turning point was the detection of peripheral blood antibodies against the rK39 antigen and the identification of typical Leishman-Donovan bodies (amastigotes) within bone marrow histiocytes, accompanied by skin biopsy confirming leukocytoclastic vasculitis secondary to visceral leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old male retired teacher presented with a 2-month history of a gradually developing, painless swelling over the anterior aspect of his left knee, associated with a small cutaneous sinus that was extruding straw-colored fluid.

differentials.candidate: Acute or chronic pyogenic bacterial bursitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because prepatellar bursal collections with draining cutaneous sinuses are most commonly pyogenic in origin. However, the patient's presentation was indolent, completely painless, and afebrile, and aspirated bursal fluid revealed normal cell counts, no organisms on Gram stain, and sterile bacterial cultures.

differentials.candidate: Deep periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) / prosthetic hardware loosening
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of a draining sinus tract in close proximity to an in situ total knee arthroplasty. However, the patient maintained a full range of motion without intra-articular effusion, plain radiographs demonstrated no bone-prosthesis interface loosening or osteolysis, and a three-phase bone scan showed normal uptake.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal clinical and microbiological turning point was Ziehl-Neelsen staining of the aspirated bursal fluid demonstrating acid-fast bacilli, subsequently confirmed on culture as Mycobacterium tuberculosis sensitive to first-line agents, establishing isolated tuberculous prepatellar bursitis sparing the prosthetic knee.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented to the orthopedic department with chief complaints of neck pain, difficulty in walking, and difficulty in deglutition of 2 months' duration. On physical examination, general physical findings were within normal limits with the exception of palpable posterior cervical lymphadenopathy.

differentials.candidate: Primary spinal / skull base neoplasm (e.g., chordoma, Ewing sarcoma, lymphoma, osteoblastoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of a progressive destructive osteolytic lesion of the upper cervical spine causing compressive myelopathy and dysphagia in an adolescent. However, the presence of posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, elevated ESR, lymphocytosis, and characteristic prevertebral cold abscess shadow strongly favored an infectious granulomatous etiology rather than a primary bone malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic cervical spondylodiscitis / acute retropharyngeal abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the neck pain, dysphagia, and prominent prevertebral shadow. However, the patient followed an indolent 2-month clinical course without acute toxic fever or neutrophilic leukocytosis, exhibiting relative lymphocytosis and normal constitutional parameters.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal clinical and radiological turning point was the demonstration of destructive C1-C2 vertebral osteolysis with prevertebral cold abscess and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy in an adolescent with compressive myelopathy, establishing the clinicoradiological diagnosis of craniovertebral junction tuberculosis (Pott's spine).

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male presented with a 4-day history of intermittent high-grade fever and acute diffuse chest pain of 3 hours' duration. The pain was moderate in intensity and radiated to the nape of the neck.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered emergently due to acute chest pain radiating to the neck accompanied by ST-segment elevation in leads I, II, aVL, V5, and V6 on admission ECG. However, emergency coronary angiography demonstrated completely normal coronary vessels without stenosis or thrombosis, and cardiac troponin was not significantly elevated.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic or primary viral acute pericarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered after post-catheterization evaluation demonstrated positional chest pain relieved by leaning forward, a pericardial friction rub, PR segment depression, and mild pericardial effusion. However, isolated viral pericarditis would not account for systemic multiorgan involvement including profound thrombocytopenia (60,000/mm³), splenomegaly, transaminitis, and acute renal impairment.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was the examination of the peripheral blood smear, which was positive for Plasmodium falciparum, establishing the diagnosis of falciparum malaria presenting with acute pericarditis mimicking myocardial infarction.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old man presented with a history of progressive abdominal distension, intermittent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, accompanied by increasing fatigue, emaciation, and a 10-kg weight loss over recent months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to progressive abdominal distension, marked weight loss, elevated serum CA-125, omental smudging, and sheetlike peritoneal nodularity on CT. However, gastroscopy was negative for primary malignancy, multiple paracentesis fluid cytologies revealed no malignant cells, and surgical biopsy confirmed granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli rather than neoplastic implants.

Considered because of extensive sheetlike thickening of the parietal peritoneum, encasement of small bowel loops, and recurrent hemorrhagic exudative ascites. However, histopathology of the encapsulating membrane and peritoneal nodules demonstrated caseating granulomas rather than malignant mesothelial proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmatory turning point was diagnostic laparoscopy demonstrating the small bowel encapsulated within a dense fibrous cocoon-like membrane with miliary peritoneal tubercles, with biopsy showing caseous granulomatous inflammation positive for acid-fast bacilli and positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old non-obese Ethiopian woman (para 0) presented for medical evaluation after experiencing prolonged secondary amenorrhea and infertility of 5 to 6 years' duration. She had no other significant past medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of prolonged secondary amenorrhea and low anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH 0.61). However, normal serum gonadotropins (FSH, LH), estradiol, and progesterone confirmed intact cyclic hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian function with recent ovulation, pointing toward uterine end-organ pathology.

Considered due to the onset of secondary amenorrhea following an open abdominal myomectomy. However, diagnostic workup and subsequent hysteroscopic inspection revealed no typical dense fibrous intrauterine synechiae, identifying instead a mottled, inflamed endometrium.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmatory turning point was diagnostic hysteroscopy demonstrating mottled fundal endometrium, with endometrial curettings showing necrotizing granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli and positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming pelvic tuberculosis causing secondary amenorrhea and infertility.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy was referred to an academic hospital due to an 8-month history of worsening backache, severe upper back pain, and a progressive gibbus deformity. He had no history of chronic cough, fever, loss of weight, or anorexia, and no known history of exposure to individuals with chronic infections.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis / acute spinal osteomyelitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to destructive vertebral changes, paravertebral abscess formation, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 18 mg/L). However, the patient exhibited an indolent 8-month progression without acute septic symptoms or leukocytosis, and superficial pus swabs were negative for bacterial pathogens.

differentials.candidate: Pediatric spinal neoplasm (e.g., Ewing sarcoma, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, lymphoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a solitary destructive thoracolumbar spinal lesion leading to pathologic kyphosis in a 9-year-old child. However, the lesion involved contiguous vertebral endplates across the disc space with preserved posterior elements and extensive cold abscess formation, and biopsy revealed chronic necrotizing granulomas rather than malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmatory turning point was vertebral biopsy demonstrating chronic necrotizing granulomas with Langhans-type giant cells, followed by surgical drainage of deep gibbus pus isolating Mycobacterium tuberculosis confirmed as rifampin-resistant by line-probe assay (MTBDRplus) and phenotypic MGIT drug susceptibility testing, establishing multidrug-resistant spinal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old previously healthy male presented with a 5-day history of high-grade fever accompanied by constitutional symptoms. Two days prior to admission, he developed right hypochondrial pain, dark tea-colored urine, and yellowish discoloration of the eyes.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to deep jaundice, tender hepatomegaly, marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and extreme transaminase elevation (>3,000-5,000 U/L). However, acute hepatitis A monoinfection does not typically cause simultaneous marked leukopenia (3,000/μL) and thrombocytopenia (116,000/μL), which indicated concurrent arboviral disease confirmed on serology.

differentials.candidate: Severe dengue with acute liver failure / Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute febrile illness with subsequent defervescence, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and extreme transaminitis. However, the patient preserved hepatic synthetic function throughout admission with normal PT/INR, had no encephalopathy, and did not develop plasma leakage, hemoconcentration, or hemorrhagic manifestations.
