diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmatory turning point was serological evaluation demonstrating positive dengue IgM antibodies via chromatographic immunoassay co-existing with positive hepatitis A IgM antibodies via ELISA, confirming a rare acute coinfection of dengue virus and hepatitis A virus.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male with diabetes mellitus and negative human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) serology presented with progressive headache, nausea, and staggering gait. Two months earlier, he had been evaluated for lower back pain associated with spondylitis and an iliopsoas abscess, for which he had been maintained on a targeted antimicrobial regimen with resolution of his back pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because an adult presenting with an aggressive solitary nodular enhancing posterior fossa mass and noncommunicating hydrocephalus raises high suspicion for primary neuroepithelial neoplasm; however, the lesion demonstrated hypointensity on DWI without typical high-grade infiltrative features, and surgical pathology showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cells.

Considered due to the patient's prior spinal and psoas abscess infections, but excluded by the absence of fever, lack of meningismus, normal inflammatory markers, and the lack of characteristic central diffusion restriction on diffusion-weighted MRI.

diagnostic_pivot: The emergence of a de novo enhancing cerebellar mass with obstructive hydrocephalus during successful antimicrobial therapy for musculoskeletal disease represented a central nervous system paradoxical reaction (PR), confirmed on surgical lesionectomy by histopathology showing caseous granulomatosis with lymphocytic and macrophage infiltration.

clinical_summary: A 2-month-old male infant in Nigeria presented for outpatient evaluation accompanied by his mother with a one-week history of fevers occurring rhythmically every 2 to 3 days. His mother noted that the infant appeared distinctly unwell while febrile, but acted active and well when afebrile.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and pallor in a 2-month-old infant strongly suggest systemic bacterial infection; however, the infant was interactive and well when afebrile, lacked leukocytosis or neutrophilia, and experienced fever recurrence despite intravenous and oral cephalosporin therapy.

Considered due to maternal and paternal HIV status; however, the mother had sustained adherence to antiretroviral therapy, the infant received postnatal antiretroviral prophylaxis, and infant virologic testing returned negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The rhythmic paroxysm of fevers every 2 to 3 days accompanied by pallor, worsening anemia, and massive splenomegaly in an endemic area established clinical suspicion, confirmed by microscopic examination of the peripheral blood film demonstrating intraerythrocytic trophozoites.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old female who had undergone haploidentical allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for acute myeloid leukemia secondary to myelodysplastic syndrome presented on day +320 post-transplant with nausea, vomiting, nystagmus, diplopia, and severe cutaneous purpura.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to heavy post-transplant immunosuppression and pre-HSCT IgG seropositivity in both patient and donor; however, high-dose intravenous trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole failed to halt disease progression, with follow-up neuroimaging demonstrating expansion of the multicystic lesions and impending herniation.
Considered in the differential diagnosis of multilocular cystic posterior fossa lesions; however, the lesion was entirely absent on pre-transplant neuroimaging and developed de novo.

differentials.candidate: Central nervous system tuberculosis (Tuberculoma / tuberculous cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a potential cause of multicystic central nervous system infection in an immunocompromised host; however, both the tuberculin skin test and interferon-gamma release assay were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The presence of multicystic cerebellar lesions with fourth ventricular compression in a patient with rural exposure and prior household contact, coupled with prompt clinical and radiological resolution following cysticidal treatment with albendazole, fulfilled revised consensus criteria for neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old Tanzanian man presented to the outpatient surgery clinic with a two-year history of a right groin swelling that became progressively more prominent with standing and physical exertion. He described episodic dull discomfort in the right groin without severe pain, and denied any fevers, altered bowel habits, weight loss, or urological complaints.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered clinically given the chronic reducible groin bulge with cough impulse in a young healthy male; however, surgical exploration revealed an atypical sliding Amyand hernia containing the cecum and appendix with an unexpected indurated apical mass.

Considered intraoperatively upon discovering an indurated, firm mass at the distal tip of the vermiform appendix; however, histopathological evaluation revealed granulomatous inflammatory tissue surrounding calcified ova without evidence of cellular atypia or malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Travel/origin from an endemic area (Tanzania) and surgical resection of the incarcerated appendix revealed periappendiceal necrotizing granulomatous inflammation enclosing calcified parasitic ova, confirming appendiceal schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old pregnant woman at 20 weeks of gestation, who had traveled from Nigeria to the United States nine days prior, presented to the emergency department with a five-day history of fever, diffuse arthralgias, drenching night sweats, vomiting, and severe malaise.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial cystitis and streptococcal pharyngitis with septic shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially due to presumed localized urinary and throat symptoms; however, standard antibacterial therapy with cephalexin produced no improvement, and the patient progressed to multi-organ failure and hemodynamic instability.
Considered due to pregnancy status, acute dyspnea, and markedly elevated D-dimer (10.04 µg/mL); however, chest computed tomographic angiography (CTA) was completely negative for thromboembolism.

diagnostic_pivot: Recent travel from West Africa in a pregnant host who stopped chemoprophylaxis, presenting with shock, acute Coombs-negative hemolysis, and profound thrombocytopenia, confirmed by blood smear demonstrating intraerythrocytic ring forms with 9.8% parasitemia and positive rapid antigen testing for Plasmodium falciparum.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection on antiretroviral therapy (elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide) presented for follow-up of dysphagia and an incidental abnormal chest radiograph. His last CD4+ T-cell count was 1,271 cells/µL with an undetectable viral load.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic / endemic fungal infection (Aspergillosis, Blastomycosis, Histoplasmosis, Cryptococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the presence of esophageal candidiasis indicating immunosuppression, travel history, and a thick-walled cavitary nodule; however, specific fungal serologies and bronchoalveolar lavage cultures were negative.
Considered due to evidence of systemic corticosteroid excess and opportunistic candidiasis; however, targeted serum polymerase chain reaction was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The detection of a solitary thick-walled apical cavitary nodule in a patient with iatrogenic Cushingoid immunosuppression and travel to endemic regions, with initial bronchoalveolar lavage negative, was definitively resolved by CT-guided percutaneous core needle biopsy culture yielding Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male born in the Philippines who immigrated to the United States two years prior presented to the emergency department in shock. Over the preceding seven months, he had suffered from chronic abdominal pain, an unintentional 60-pound weight loss, severe fatigue, and non-bloody diarrhea.

differentials.candidate: Crohn's disease with secondary septic complications
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because segmental inflammatory ulcerations, skip lesions, and non-granulomatous inflammation on initial colonoscopy mimic inflammatory bowel disease; however, anti-TNF therapy with infliximab triggered catastrophic clinical deterioration, multiorgan dissemination, and intestinal perforation containing necrotizing granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli.

Considered given severe constitutional cachexia (60-pound weight loss), multiple hypodense liver lesions, and an obstructing mass at the biliary confluence; however, diagnostic paracentesis, thoracentesis, and liver core biopsy were negative for neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The fulminant reactivation and dissemination following anti-TNF inhibition in an immigrant from an endemic region, with diagnostic thoracentesis, paracentesis, and exploratory laparotomy revealing extensive caseating granulomatous disease teeming with acid-fast bacilli in the ileocecal region.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old Caucasian female presented to the hospital with a one-year history of vague discomfort in the right upper quadrant and left flank, complicated by acute fatigue and fever over the past ten days.

differentials.candidate: Polycystic kidney and liver disease (Autosomal dominant polycystic disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because simultaneous hepatic and renal cystic lesions can represent adult polycystic disease; however, congenital polycystic disease involves innumerable diffuse bilateral renal parenchymal cysts rather than an isolated unilateral renal cyst, and does not cause coexisting discrete pulmonary cysts.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial abscesses of the liver and kidney
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute fever, left flank tenderness, and AST elevation; however, the multi-organ cystic architecture was longstanding (one-year history), well-circumscribed, and systemic blood counts remained normal outside of localized cyst superinfection.

diagnostic_pivot: The multi-organ distribution across pulmonary, hepatic, and renal parenchyma, corroborated by an extremely high indirect hemagglutination titer (1:16,384) and confirmed intraoperatively during laparoscopic decompression by the presence of a purulent superinfected cyst and excision of the characteristic germinal membranes.

clinical_summary: A pediatric patient presented to the hospital with acute-onset severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain. One week prior, the patient had been evaluated for hepatobiliary symptoms, where an abdominal ultrasound had shown a distended gallbladder with very dense intraluminal content, but no hydrops and no intra- or extrahepatic bile duct dilatation, and targeted medical therapy had been initiated.

differentials.candidate: Acute calculous / acalculous cholecystitis requiring emergency surgery
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because intense right upper quadrant pain, a positive Murphy's sign, and ultrasonographic gallbladder hydrops typically signify acute cholecystitis; however, the biliary obstruction was transient and secondary to fluke sludging/lysis, resolving completely within days under conservative intravenous hydration without operative cholecystectomy.

differentials.candidate: Pediatric Loeffler's syndrome / systemic allergic eosinophilic pneumonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in pediatric trematodiasis presentations presenting with systemic inflammatory symptoms (such as multi-joint arthralgias, severe peripheral eosinophilia, and bilateral perihilar ground-glass infiltrates); however, this patient presented primarily with localized obstructive biliary symptoms rather than migratory pulmonary-rheumatologic disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Known biliary trematode infestation where post-treatment worm expulsion or lysis caused transient common bile duct and cystic duct obstruction with gallbladder hydrops, which resolved completely following conservative intravenous fluid support as documented by follow-up ultrasound.

clinical_summary: A pediatric patient was referred to the hospital for comprehensive evaluation of an abdominal mass identified on preliminary outpatient assessment. Abdominal examination revealed a palpable right upper quadrant fullness without severe peritoneal signs.

differentials.candidate: Pediatric hepatic malignancy (e.g. hepatoblastoma or solid abdominal tumor)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary referral diagnosis due to the detection of a solitary solid-appearing hepatic lesion in a child; however, high-resolution ultrasonography showed features more consistent with parasitic infection, and histopathology lacked cellular atypia, demonstrating an inflammatory and necrotic pseudotumor.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial liver abscess / systemic bacterial phlegmon
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in children presenting with acute, sleep-disrupting abdominal pain, anorexia, and fever (as observed in acute hepatic cohort presentations such as Patient 6); however, this patient presented with an indolent mass-like lesion, and biopsy revealed eosinophil-predominant granulomatous necrosis rather than purulent polymorphonuclear suppuration.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasonographic identification of parasitic liver parenchyma changes corroborated by percutaneous liver biopsy revealing intense mixed infiltrates of eosinophils and lymphocytes with histiocyte-rimmed necrotic tracts, culminating in complete radiological resolution following flukicidal treatment with triclabendazole.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old man with no past medical or family history presented to the clinic with dyspnea during strenuous activities. He denied cough, hemoptysis, chest pain, fever, weight loss, or constitutional symptoms, and reported no history of drug, alcohol, or substance abuse.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bronchogenic cysts are congenital foregut malformations that present as solitary fluid-filled cysts; however, an intact cyst attaining massive proportions (>15-20 cm) in an otherwise healthy young adult is rare, and thoracotomy in this patient revealed parasitic laminated membranes rather than respiratory epithelium.

Giant bullae are thin-walled intra-parenchymal airspaces usually associated with smoking, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or barotrauma; this patient was a non-smoker whose lesion was completely fluid-filled rather than gas-containing.

Loculated parapneumonic effusions or pleural empyemas cause unilateral decreased breath sounds and space-occupying fluid collections, but typically present with febrile illness, toxic systemic features, leukocytosis, and pleural inflammation, none of which were present in this patient.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during right posterolateral thoracotomy, which entered a large cystic cavity in the right lower lobe and evacuated 2500 cc of crystal-clear hydatid fluid along with the classic laminated membrane of Echinococcus, followed by oral albendazole therapy resulting in resolution of the residual cavity.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old man presented to an orthopedic outpatient clinic with chronic progressive redness, warmth, and swelling of the right knee that had persisted and worsened over the preceding five years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute bacterial joint infections typically run a fulminant course with high fevers, systemic toxicity, and elevated inflammatory markers; this patient had an indolent 5-year course with normal blood counts and lack of response to prior cephalosporin therapy.

A chronic soft-tissue mass associated with progressive osteolytic bone destruction in the proximal tibia and fibula raised concern for synovial sarcoma or primary bone malignancy; however, subsequent biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

While symptoms initiated following a vehicular accident, simple post-traumatic arthropathy cannot account for progressive multi-bone osteolytic destruction, soft-tissue abscess formation, or bilateral upper lobe pulmonary infiltrations.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during right knee arthrotomy and total synovectomy, which revealed an unattached synovial mass, with histopathology demonstrating epithelioid cell proliferation, caseating necrotizing granulomas, lymphocytic infiltration, and localized fibrosis consistent with Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, accompanied by the bilateral upper lobe pulmonary lesions.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old man presented for surgical evaluation complaining of a lump in the right groin region accompanied by lower back pain (visual analogue scale score 5) that had been present for four months.

differentials.candidate: Inguinal hernia or primary gastrointestinal defect
differentials.rule_out_reason: A groin mass in a young man commonly prompts evaluation for an inguinal hernia or gastrointestinal wall defect, but clinical examination revealed no abdominal abnormality or reducible visceral defect, prompting orthopedic referral.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic spondylodiscitis / pyogenic psoas abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute pyogenic spine infections typically present with high spiking fevers, acute systemic toxicity, and rapid progression; here the patient exhibited an indolent 4-month history without radicular deficits or acute inflammatory collapse.

differentials.candidate: Mechanical lumbar disc herniation / degenerative spine disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Mechanical back pain relieved by recumbency is typical of lumbar disc pathology, but degenerative disease alone cannot account for a concomitant palpable mass in the right groin.

diagnostic_pivot: Specialist referral to the pulmonary and orthopedic divisions established that the groin mass represented a descending cold abscess arising from lumbosacral tuberculous spondylitis (Pott's disease), prompting anti-tuberculous chemotherapy and arthroscopic abscess decompression.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old Lao-speaking man presented to the emergency department with generalized weakness, postprandial dull epigastric pain, early satiety, and bloating of two months' duration. He denied fevers, night sweats, melena, hematochezia, hematemesis, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's age, smoking history, severe occult gastrointestinal bleeding, and an ulcerated friable antral mass, gastric carcinoma was the foremost suspicion; however, multiple endoscopic biopsies and definitive subtotal gastrectomy specimens were completely negative for malignant cells.
Chronic peptic ulceration can cause blood loss anemia and epigastric discomfort, but tissue evaluation was negative for H. pylori, and the mass failed to heal despite proton-pump inhibitor treatment.

NSAID gastropathy produces erosive mucosal injury and blood loss, but the patient had no history of NSAID use and only received low-dose aspirin, which does not account for a tumefactive ulcerated mass.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon histopathological evaluation of the resected gastric specimen following subtotal gastrectomy, revealing chronic inflammation and scattered microscopic nematode morphology favoring Strongyloides, followed by concentrated stool wet mount demonstrating Strongyloides stercoralis rhabditiform larvae and positive serum IgG serology.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old boy with Down's syndrome, intellectual disability, and hyperexcitability was brought to a pediatric cardiology clinic by his parents due to progressive dyspnea and decreased exercise tolerance. The family lived in a rural farming community in close contact with domestic animals.

differentials.candidate: Congenital cardiac cyst or ventricular diverticulum
differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital heart anomalies and cardiac cysts can occur in Down's syndrome; however, congenital cystic malformations do not explain subsequent synchronous large intracerebral cystic development or strongly positive parasitic serology.

differentials.candidate: Primary cardiac neoplasm (cardiac fibroma or rhabdomyoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Intramyocardial tumors such as fibromas or rhabdomyomas frequently involve the interventricular septum and induce ventricular dysfunction, but typically present as solid or heterogeneous intramural masses rather than well-defined, unilocular fluid-filled cysts.

Cysticercosis causes parasitic cyst formation in humans with domestic animal exposures, but primarily targets the brain and skeletal muscle, whereas primary interventricular septal cyst involvement with subsequent cerebral hydatid disease is characteristic of Echinococcus.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred with strongly positive hydatid serological assays (hemagglutination titer >1:5,000 and positive ELISA OD 1.034), followed by emergent left fronto-temporo-parietal craniotomy with intact Dowling-Orlando enucleation of a synchronous giant cerebral cyst, whose histopathological evaluation definitively confirmed hydatid echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: An 86-year-old man presented to a surgical clinic with a two-month history of a progressively enlarging mass in the anterior aspect of his right thigh. He reported no local pain, trauma, fevers, chills, or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In an elderly patient receiving antiplatelet therapy (aspirin), spontaneous deep intramuscular hemorrhage is a primary consideration; however, ultrasonography revealed a structured, encapsulated multicystic lesion with wall calcifications rather than an organizing hematoma.

Deep muscle abscesses typically present with localized pain, tenderness, overlying warmth, erythema, and leukocytosis, none of which were observed in this non-tender, mobile mass with normal blood counts.

differentials.candidate: Soft-tissue neoplasm (myxoma, cystic lymphangioma, epidermoid cyst, sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary musculoskeletal benign or malignant neoplasms are common etiologies of extremity masses in the elderly; however, histological evaluation confirmed non-neoplastic parasitic cystic membranes rather than cellular stromal proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon complete en bloc surgical excision of the intact thigh cyst, with histopathological review of the cyst wall revealing an acellular laminated layer surrounded by a fibrous capsule and containing characteristic protoscoleces admixed with necrotic debris, confirming isolated intramuscular Echinococcus granulosus infection.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old male farmer residing in central Thailand was transferred to a tertiary medical center with a three-month history of prolonged fever, non-productive cough, left-sided chest tightness, and an unintentional 4 kg weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Typical community- or hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonias were ruled out by the subacute 3-month duration and the complete lack of clinical or febrile response to a 14-day course of intravenous meropenem.

In a post-transplant patient on chronic mycophenolate and cyclosporine, fungal opportunistic pneumonia is a major consideration, but serum cryptococcal antigen was negative and biopsy stains lacked fungal elements.

differentials.candidate: Isolated non-small cell lung carcinoma with tumor necrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: While core needle biopsy confirmed non-small cell lung adenocarcinoma, neoplastic tumor fever alone could not account for the marked neutrophilia and persistent septic profile, which harbored concomitant active necrotizing bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon evaluation of the transthoracic core-needle biopsy of the left upper lobe mass, where Brown-Hopp tissue staining revealed clusters of gram-negative bipolar rods with characteristic safety-pin morphology that yielded Burkholderia pseudomallei in tissue culture, confirmed by a serum antibody titer of 1:1280 and defervescence with ceftazidime.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old female homemaker presented for evaluation of persistent, worsening pain and swelling in her left wrist that had progressed over four months. Two months earlier, she had sought medical care for left wrist swelling while undergoing treatment for presumed seronegative rheumatoid arthritis with methotrexate, low-dose prednisolone, and rituximab (four total cycles, the last administered five months prior).

differentials.candidate: Refractory flare of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Monoarticular exacerbation in a patient treated for seronegative rheumatoid arthritis was initially treated as an autoimmune flare; however, increasing doses of methotrexate and corticosteroids resulted in worsening inflammation and the formation of a cutaneous draining fistula, an atypical feature for pure RA.

Acute pyogenic joint infections classically produce severe localized pain, high fevers, marked toxic systemic features, and positive bacterial blood cultures, whereas this patient experienced an indolent multi-month course with negative routine blood and urine cultures.
Reactive and viral arthritides are usually migratory or oligoarticular and resolve spontaneously over weeks to months without chronic granulomatous destruction or draining sinus tract development.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon surgical debridement of the left wrist fistula, which revealed acid-fast bacilli on histopathology and positive polymerase chain reaction and culture confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis, leading to complete clinical cure with quadruple antituberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old individual presented for evaluation of bilateral cervicobrachial pain persisting for nine months. The symptoms had developed insidiously alongside unquantified unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic spinal malignancy or multiple myeloma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Vertebral osteolytic collapse accompanied by constitutional weight loss in a 42-year-old strongly suggests primary or metastatic osseous neoplasia; however, MRI features of epiduritis and paravertebral phlegmon indicated an infectious process, and subsequent biopsy excluded malignancy.

Pyogenic bacterial spinal infections typically run an aggressive, febrile, destructive course with rapid development of severe neurological deficits, distinct from this patient's 9-month indolent history without sensorimotor dysfunction.

Degenerative cervical disc herniation frequently causes cervicobrachialgia, but cannot explain frank osteolytic bone destruction of the C4 vertebral body, epidural abscess formation, or constitutional weight loss.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon histological biopsy of the C4 lesion, which confirmed active tuberculosis, prompting definitive surgical management with anterior cervical arthrodesis and a 12-month course of quadruple antituberculous chemotherapy leading to full neurological recovery.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old male plaster worker living in northwestern Iran presented with persistent skin lesions involving his face and upper lip that had been present for three months. The lesions were pruritic, and several had become prominent, nodular, and hemorrhagic.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Infectious impetigo or ecthyma causes crusted and erythematous perioral lesions, but is rapidly responsive to antibacterial agents, whereas this patient's lesions showed no response to multiple systemic oral antibiotics and topical treatments.

Pruritic facial plaques that partially improve with topical corticosteroids can mimic allergic or contact eczema; however, the discrete hyperkeratotic nodular morphology and subepithelial tuberculoid granulomas with multinucleated giant cells rule out a primary eczematous dermatosis.

Cutaneous leishmaniasis is highly endemic in Iran and characteristically manifests as chronic facial nodules or crusted plaques; however, histopathology revealed epithelioid granulomas containing acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain rather than Leishmania amastigotes.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred with histopathological analysis of the skin biopsy, which demonstrated multiple subepithelial granulomas composed of epithelioid cells, multinucleated giant cells, and lymphocytes, confirmed as Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection by positive Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast staining and a strongly reactive purified protein derivative (PPD) skin test.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old male with a history of pre-fibrotic primary myelofibrosis (intermediate-1 risk by DIPSS, JAK2 V617F-positive, managed with ruxolitinib 20 mg twice daily for four months) presented to the hospital with a one-week history of fever and productive cough.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute-to-subacute presentation of fever, productive cough, elevated procalcitonin, and pulmonary consolidation in an immunocompromised host. However, empiric antibacterial therapy failed to resolve the infection, and routine workup did not yield a conventional bacterial pathogen.

differentials.candidate: Pulmonary infarction secondary to acute pulmonary thromboembolism
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the patient developed acute syncope, confirmed lower extremity deep venous thrombosis, and bilateral pulmonary emboli with pleural effusions and consolidative changes. However, thromboembolism alone could not explain the progressive mediastinal lymphadenopathy and soft tissue masses encasing the left main bronchus.

differentials.candidate: Extramedullary hematopoiesis or secondary hematologic malignancy / lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because patients with primary myelofibrosis and JAK2 mutations can develop extramedullary myeloid tumors, chloromas, or secondary lymphomas manifesting as mediastinal masses and lymphadenopathy. However, histopathologic and molecular evaluation of the lymph node demonstrated mycobacterial infection rather than malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite initial sputum smears being negative and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing negative for culture, AFB smears, and rapid molecular assays, a tracheobronchial lymph node biopsy ultimately confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis via polymerase chain reaction, establishing tracheobronchial tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old female presented to the hospital with a more than 1-month history of mild, persistent abdominal pain localized to the epigastrium and right upper quadrant. She also reported anorexia, a low-grade fever, and an intentional weight loss of 4 kg over the preceding month.

differentials.candidate: Primary hepatocellular carcinoma or metastatic liver disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis because the patient presented with weight loss, hepatomegaly, transaminitis, and multiple contrast-enhancing liver masses on cross-sectional imaging. However, liver biopsy and subsequent histopathological examination showed no evidence of neoplastic cells.

differentials.candidate: Parasitic hepatic infection or inflammatory pseudotumor
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered after initial needle biopsy demonstrated prominent eosinophilic infiltration, lymphocytes, and epithelioid necrosis, which raised suspicion for a parasitic liver process or inflammatory pseudotumor. However, definite parasite elements were absent, and definitive resection revealed classic caseating necrotizing granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Partial hepatectomy of segment VI of the right hepatic lobe demonstrated multiple necrotizing granulomas with central caseating necrosis pathognomonic for tuberculous infection, further corroborated by a positive QuantiFERON-TB assay.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old girl presented to a pediatric hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, with a 20-day history of intermittent fevers, non-bloody diarrhea, night sweats, progressive weight loss, and dry cough. She had received routine neonatal BCG vaccination and had no known prior medical conditions or known sick contacts with chronic cough or respiratory illness.

differentials.candidate: Enteric fever (Salmonella enterica) or severe pyogenic sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 3-week course of remittent fever, gastrointestinal symptoms (diarrhea), wasting, and marked neutrophilic leukocytosis. However, typical bacterial sepsis does not cause a diffuse miliary micronodular pattern on chest radiography and failed to improve on empiric ceftriaxone monotherapy.

Considered because malnourished pediatric patients with cell-mediated vulnerability can present with prolonged fever, weight loss, diarrhea, and diffuse miliary pulmonary nodules. However, diagnostic evaluation isolated acid-fast mycobacterial organisms rather than fungal yeast forms.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when gastric washing aspirate testing identified rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis via rapid molecular assay, subsequently reaffirmed by duodenal biopsy demonstrating acid-fast bacilli within mucosal granulomatous inflammation.

clinical_summary: An 8-month-old previously healthy boy, born in Germany to healthy parents originating from the Balkan peninsula, presented with a multi-week history of persistent high fever and progressive cough refractory to broad-spectrum outpatient antibacterial regimens including beta-lactams and glycopeptides.

differentials.candidate: Primary / familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHLH) or genetic immune deficiency
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the infant met diagnostic criteria for HLH (fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, elevated sIL-2R, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis) during the first year of life. However, flow cytometric NK-cell degranulation was preserved (14.7%) and expression of perforin, CD27, SAP, and XIAP was normal, excluding classical primary genetic HLH syndromes.

differentials.candidate: Viral-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis or pyogenic sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the rapid progression to septic shock and acute respiratory distress syndrome, with viral triggers like EBV, CMV, adenovirus, and herpesviruses being common precipitants of secondary HLH in infants. However, exhaustive viral serology and PCR panels as well as standard bacterial cultures were repeatedly negative.

diagnostic_pivot: After initial negative BAL smears and PCR on Day 6, a positive interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) on Day 12 prompted empiric antituberculous therapy, which led to subsequent clinical recovery; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture and repeat PCR ultimately grew fully susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and neuroimaging confirmed miliary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male born in Tamil Nadu, India, who had emigrated to Singapore six years earlier, presented to the emergency department following a first-onset generalized seizure witnessed by his wife.

differentials.candidate: Intracranial tuberculoma / Central nervous system tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading differential given the patient's demographic origin, leukocytosis, solitary ring-enhancing temporal lesion, and intraoperative finding of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, which initially prompted empiric antituberculous therapy. However, acid-fast stains and GeneXpert MTB/RIF testing on brain tissue were repeatedly negative.

differentials.candidate: High-grade glial neoplasm or brain metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because a new-onset adult seizure accompanied by a solitary ring-enhancing parenchymal mass with surrounding vasogenic edema frequently represents a primary high-grade glioma or metastatic lesion. However, surgical excision revealed inflammatory exudate and chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cellular proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Although imaging and initial histology lacked a visible larva or scolex, molecular analysis of the excised brain lesion by species-specific PCR and sequencing confirmed Taenia solium mitochondrial DNA (99.6% identity), supported by positive send-out serum cysticercosis ELISA, definitively establishing neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old female laboratory physician presented to the hospital with a 7-day history of hoarseness. She denied fever, cough, expectoration, weight loss, night sweats, sore throat, fatigue, or myalgias.

differentials.candidate: Laryngeal carcinoma / Vocal cord squamous neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because persistent hoarseness accompanied by irregular milky hyperplastic lesions of the vocal cords strongly mimics primary laryngeal carcinoma or papillomatosis. However, serum tumor markers were normal and histopathologic examination of the vocal cord biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation without cellular atypia or malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Fungal laryngitis / Mycotic vocal cord granuloma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because fungal infections such as candidiasis or deep fungal granulomas can present with white hyperplastic vocal cord plaques and hoarseness. However, special fungal staining of the vocal cord biopsy tissue with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Although sputum smears, throat swab PCR, and tissue acid-fast stains were negative, direct homogenate processing of the vocal cord biopsy utilizing a mycobacterial identification gene chip array successfully amplified Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA, confirming primary laryngeal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male with a medical history of cerebral palsy was referred to the neurosurgery department from the ophthalmology clinic with a four-month history of progressive right supraorbital swelling involving the right upper eyelid.

differentials.candidate: Primary calvarial neoplasm or metastatic bone disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because a chronic progressive skull mass causing osteolytic destruction of the orbital roof and frontal bone with an associated epidural mass in a cachectic patient strongly mimics osteosarcoma, myeloma, or skull metastasis. However, surgical exploration revealed purulent fluid collection, and bone histology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis and subperiosteal abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because bacterial infection (such as staphylococcal or streptococcal osteomyelitis) can destroy the frontal bone and extend into the epidural space. However, pyogenic abscesses produce acute inflammatory warmth, erythema, and severe local pain, whereas this lesion followed a four-month indolent course manifesting as a non-inflammatory, painless 'cold abscess'.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration through a right eyebrow incision evacuated thick cold purulent collection beneath the eyelid, and histological analysis of the osteolytic frontal/orbital bone biopsy demonstrated characteristic caseo-follicular tuberculosis, establishing tuberculous osteitis and orbital cold abscess.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old autistic boy residing in São Paulo, Brazil, presented to the emergency department with a one-month history of progressive lower extremity weakness, loss of bowel control (fecal incontinence), and acute-on-chronic urinary retention.

differentials.candidate: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor / High-grade glioma or ependymoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary preoperative concern because an expansile, heterogeneously enhancing conus medullaris mass with extensive syrinx formation in a preschool child typically indicates an aggressive intrinsic neuroepithelial neoplasm. However, surgical inspection and biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous tissue without neoplastic glial proliferation.

Considered because chronic granulomatous infectious myelopathy in an endemic South American setting often suggests tuberculous involvement of the spinal cord or conus medullaris. However, histopathology identified parasite eggs rather than acid-fast organisms or caseating tubercular granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive histopathologic analysis of the resected conus medullaris tissue identified granulomatous inflammation centered around Schistosoma mansoni ova, establishing spinal cord schistosomiasis and prompting curative therapy with praziquantel.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male presented to the outpatient thoracic clinic complaining of progressive left-sided thoracic and back pain of increasing intensity over the preceding two months, accompanied by an involuntary weight loss of 5 kg.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading infectious differential because an immigrant from an endemic region with hemoptysis, constitutional weight loss, and a large cavitary/cystic pulmonary mass strongly suggests cavitary mycobacterial disease. However, bronchoscopy was unremarkable, and mycobacterial PCR performed on both serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid was negative.

differentials.candidate: Primary cystic lung neoplasm or necrotic pulmonary malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because a giant 9-cm expanding intrathoracic pseudotumor causing hemoptysis, localized thoracic pain, and weight loss can represent a congenital bronchogenic cyst, cystic sarcoma, or cavitating lung carcinoma. However, histological examination of the resected specimen revealed parasitic laminar architecture without neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative pre-operative Echinococcus serology, definitive diagnostic lobectomy of the left lower lobe demonstrated a thick acellular laminated cuticular membrane, an inner nucleated germinal layer, and intraoperative smears teeming with protoscolices and hooklets, pathognomonic for hydatid cyst echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department with a 5-day history of high-grade fever, shaking chills, rigors, profuse drenching diaphoresis, lethargy, and a dry cough.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral respiratory tract infection (COVID-19) alone
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the patient presented during an endemic wave with cough, pharyngeal erythema, and confirmed positive nasopharyngeal RT-PCR. However, despite resolution of pharyngitis and cough after three days of supportive care, the patient experienced abrupt recrudescent fever spikes (39.1°C) with classic shaking rigors and diaphoresis.

Considered because an acute high-grade fever spike to 39.1°C with neutrophilic leukocytosis and rigors in a diabetic patient raised immediate concern for hospital-acquired or secondary pyogenic bacteremia. However, comprehensive blood cultures remained completely sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Persistent paroxysmal rigors and sweats prompted microscopic evaluation of thick and thin peripheral blood films, which revealed ring forms and developing trophozoites of Plasmodium vivax at 0.1% parasitemia, establishing a hypnozoite reactivation relapse triggered by intercurrent viral infection.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old woman presented to the gastroenterology service with a two-month history of progressive odynophagia and high dysphagia, accompanied by a 5-kg weight loss. Her symptoms had advanced from difficulty swallowing solids to total dysphagia for both solid and liquid foods, complicated by sialorrhea, marked physical asthenia, and night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe dysphagia, profound weight loss, asymmetric-appearing tonsillar congestion, and firm immobile cervical lymphadenopathy in an immunosuppressed patient strongly suggested tonsillar carcinoma or lymphoma, but histopathological evaluation of tonsillar biopsy specimens demonstrated no evidence of malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial pharyngotonsillitis / Peritonsillar abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked odynophagia, tonsillar hypertrophy, and elevated systemic inflammatory markers raised suspicion for acute pyogenic pharyngitis, but symptoms relentlessly progressed despite sequential broad-spectrum antibacterial courses (amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and ceftriaxone), and microbiological culture of pharyngeal exudate showed no pathogenic streptococci or staphylococci.

The direct visualization of diffuse whitish-gray mucosal granulations throughout the pharynx and larynx in a patient with pharmacologic immunosuppression raised concern for invasive oropharyngeal candidiasis, but pharyngeal exudate was negative for Candida species.

Chronic mucosal lesions accompanied by cervical lymphadenopathy and systemic asthenia required consideration of secondary syphilis and HIV-associated acute pharyngotonsillitis, but specific serologic screens were non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when microscopic examination of the patient's sputum revealed Koch bacilli, corroborated by thoracic computed tomography showing massive apical cavitation and diffuse micronodular condensations consistent with hematogenous dissemination following anti-TNF-alpha biological therapy.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old man from Guangxi, China, presented to the hospital with a seven-month history of cough, fever, and progressive emaciation, and a one-month history of an enlarging mass on the left side of his neck.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial lymphadenitis / Burkholderia cepacia abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid enlargement of tender, fluctuant cervical masses with neutrophilic leukocytosis suggested bacterial lymphadenitis, and initial pus cultures did recover Burkholderia cepacia; however, despite susceptibility-guided antibacterial therapy, the patient developed worsening pulmonary consolidations and endobronchial lesions driven by an underlying dimorphic fungus.
Subacute febrile pulmonary consolidation and pulmonary nodules in a debilitated patient raised concern for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, but the serum galactomannan index was normal.

A solitary 8-cm cervical mass associated with profound weight loss and submental lesions in an adult male suggested lymphoma or metastatic carcinoma, but bronchofibroscopic biopsy revealed inflammatory endobronchial nodules without malignant cytopathology.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis was reached when bronchofibroscopy identified obstructive bronchial nodules and hilar lymphadenopathy, and fungal cultures along with next-generation sequencing confirmed Talaromyces marneffei from bronchial tissue, hilar lymph nodes, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in a patient subsequently found to harbor neutralizing anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old otherwise healthy Sri Lankan male presented to an outpatient clinic with a six-month history of swelling in his left ankle joint. He noted progressive swelling associated with stiffness, restricted range of movement, and discomfort during weight-bearing.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic insidious joint swelling with restricted mobility and elevated inflammatory markers suggested an inflammatory arthropathy, but comprehensive serological testing including rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and antinuclear antibody was entirely negative.

Progressive joint destruction and disability could suggest a indolent pyogenic joint infection, but the classical signs of bacterial sepsis—including local erythema, warmth, severe joint tenderness, systemic pyrexia, and peripheral leukocytosis—were distinctly absent.

Chronic weight-bearing pain and limited range of motion in an ankle joint could represent post-traumatic or degenerative osteoarthrosis, but there was no preceding history of mechanical injury or surgery, and advanced imaging demonstrated subarticular osteitis and inflammatory marrow edema.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough was achieved when an open synovial biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation, and definitive automated culture of the synovial tissue grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming primary tuberculous arthritis of the ankle.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 35-year-old female bank employee presented to the emergency department complaining of a five-day history of high-grade fever of a waxing-and-waning nature, associated with vomiting, generalized body aches, and progressive somnolence.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High-grade fever, somnolence, and systemic myalgias arising in mandatory travel quarantine strongly warranted exclusion of acute pandemic viral infection, but nasopharyngeal swab PCR was negative.

Severe undulating fevers, lethargy, gastrointestinal upset, and transaminitis following international travel suggested acute bacterial septicemia or enteric fever, but serial blood cultures and urine cultures remained negative throughout hospitalization.

differentials.candidate: Primary systemic autoimmune disease / Systemic lupus erythematosus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subsequent development of persistent fevers, pleural effusions, splenic infarcts, positive antinuclear antibody (ANA), and Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia suggested an underlying autoimmune connective tissue disorder; however, these findings represented an acute inflammatory post-infectious and drug-induced response (post-artesunate delayed hemolysis) that resolved without immunosuppressive therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic discovery on emergency admission was the examination of peripheral blood smears, which identified heavy intraerythrocytic trophozoite infection confirming hyperparasitemic Plasmodium falciparum infection.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old male immigrant from Mexico presented to the emergency department complaining of progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness of one month's duration, resulting in worsening difficulty ambulating. Over the preceding two weeks, he noted a loss of sensation below the nipple level, and during the past week, he developed urinary and stool retention.

differentials.candidate: Isolated pyogenic spondylodiscitis (Streptococcus anginosus epidural abscess)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid neurological decline and the intraoperative isolation of Streptococcus anginosus from epidural purulence initially pointed toward acute pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis; however, the operative findings of a chronic fibrotic mass and histologic discovery of caseating granulomas indicated that the bacterial infection was an opportunistic co-infection complicating a chronic granulomatous nidus.

differentials.candidate: Spinal neoplasm / Metastatic epidural cord compression
differentials.rule_out_reason: Vertebral osteolysis involving contiguous thoracic vertebrae with severe spinal cord compression and constitutional night sweats in a middle-aged adult raised serious concern for metastatic malignancy or primary lymphoma, but surgical biopsy demonstrated inflammatory granulomas rather than malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Infective endocarditis with hematogenous septic seeding
differentials.rule_out_reason: Spinal infection caused by Streptococcus anginosus group organisms frequently originates from hematogenous seeding associated with occult infective endocarditis, but echocardiographic imaging showed no evidence of valvular vegetations.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when intraoperative biopsy specimens revealed caseating granulomas and, after six weeks of incubation, surgical mycobacterial cultures definitively isolated pan-susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott's disease) complicated by bacterial superinfection.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male from Kerala, South India, presented to a tertiary hospital with a three-week history of watery, non-bloody loose stools occurring three to four times per day. He reported intermittent vague abdominal pain, decreased appetite, and a 3- to 4-kg weight loss over the preceding month.

differentials.candidate: Acute bacterial enteritis / Aeromonas sobria infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and leukocytosis led to the isolation of Aeromonas sobria on stool bacteriological culture; however, antibacterial therapy failed to arrest the underlying illness because the bacteria were opportunistic secondary invaders crossing an intestinal mucosa disrupted by nematode hyperinfection.

In a diabetic patient with recent chronic antimicrobial exposure presenting with copious watery diarrhea and leukocytosis, pseudomembranous colitis was a prominent diagnostic consideration, but stool testing for Clostridium difficile toxins was negative.

Weight loss, anorexia, chronic diarrhea, and hypodense hepatic lesions on abdominal CT raised high concern for occult gastrointestinal malignancy with metastatic dissemination, but upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal, and the liver lesions reflected fatty/inflammatory changes in the setting of chronic alcohol use and systemic illness.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was stool wet preparation microscopy, which revealed abundant motile rhabditiform larvae, corroborated by the classic agar culture plate 'positive trail sign' demonstrating bacterial tracks created by crawling larvae, confirming hyperinfection by the soil-transmitted nematode Strongyloides stercoralis.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old male was urgently transferred to a tertiary hospital with acute febrile illness. In late July, he noticed profound fatigue, followed by progressively severe lower leg pain, intense headache, diarrhea, and vomiting.

differentials.candidate: Rickettsial infection / Scrub typhus / Spotted fever
differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, excruciating calf myalgias, headache, thrombocytopenia, and outdoor forestry work strongly raised suspicion for rickettsial disease, prompting empirical minocycline; however, the clinical picture was definitively proven to be spirochetal rather than rickettsial by molecular diagnostic assays.

differentials.candidate: Severe community-acquired pneumonia / Sepsis with ARDS
differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, hemoptysis, ground-glass pulmonary opacities, and acute organ dysfunction suggested severe bacterial pneumonia with respiratory distress, but plain chest radiography lacked focal airspace consolidations and computed tomography showed diffuse centrilobular ground-glass changes indicative of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune pulmonary-renal syndrome (ANCA-associated vasculitis / Anti-GBM disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The constellation of pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage with nephritic acute renal failure (granular casts, azotemia) and thrombocytopenia raised clinical concern for an autoimmune vasculitis, but an environmental history of rodent cohabitation and positive infectious testing confirmed a zoonosis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was the confirmation of leptospiral DNA by real-time PCR in urine samples performed by the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, corroborated by paired microscopic agglutination testing showing significant antibody titer rises against Leptospira interrogans serovars Autumnalis and Rachmati.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female with established Crohn's disease presented for evaluation of new-onset fever, cough, and sputum production. Her past medical history was notable for diagnosis of Crohn's disease with perianal fistulas one year earlier, along with completion of neonatal BCG vaccination and a history of parental treated pulmonary infection three years prior.

differentials.candidate: Crohn's disease flare / Loss of response to infliximab
differentials.rule_out_reason: Worsening systemic symptoms, diarrhea, and rising inflammatory markers shortly after biologic therapy were initially interpreted as Crohn's disease exacerbation caused by pharmacokinetic failure, but the subsequent development of miliary pulmonary nodules signaled systemic infection rather than active inflammatory bowel disease.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic fungal or pyogenic bacterial pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral diffuse micronodular infiltrates in an immunosuppressed adolescent on anti-TNF and methotrexate raised strong concern for invasive fungal infection or pyogenic bacterial pneumonitis, but bacterial and fungal cultures from respiratory and tissue specimens showed no growth.

Patients on long-term methotrexate can develop subacute pulmonary toxicity with diffuse nodular or interstitial opacities, but the imaging appearance was classic for miliary dissemination and was microbiologically proven to be infectious.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when bronchoscopy with tracheal biopsy and bronchial washing fluid yielded a positive tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction test confirming miliary disease, followed later by incidental detection and positive mycobacterial culture from an asymptomatic psoas abscess and spinal spondylitis.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old woman in her fifth pregnancy (gravida 5, para 3+1) was urgently transferred to a tertiary hospital from a provincial district hospital at an estimated gestational age of 42 completed weeks and four days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Isolated thrombocytopenia discovered near term is commonly benign gestational thrombocytopenia or immune thrombocytopenia; however, platelet counts below 50,000/µL are atypical for gestational thrombocytopenia, and neither condition explains the concurrent leukopenia, anemia, and prolonged clotting time.

Severe acute consumptive thrombocytopenia in an advanced post-term pregnancy raised immediate suspicion for HELLP syndrome, but the patient was normotensive, lacked proteinuria on urinalysis, and demonstrated entirely normal liver transaminases and bilirubin.

differentials.candidate: Primary bone marrow failure / Aplastic anemia
differentials.rule_out_reason: New-onset trilineage pancytopenia (leukopenia, anemia, and severe thrombocytopenia) without prominent fever suggested primary marrow aplasia or hypoplasia, but the abnormalities resolved rapidly following targeted antiparasitic chemotherapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred upon microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear, which revealed abundant ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum, establishing asymptomatic severe malaria presenting with profound consumptive coagulopathy and pancytopenia in late pregnancy.

clinical_summary: A 1-year-7-month-old male infant was admitted to the hospital with a one-week history of worsening shortness of breath. His illness began with intermittent fevers over the preceding six months and a chronic cough for the past month.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated pediatric malignancy / Lymphoma / Metastatic neuroblastoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Concomitant multi-focal mass lesions involving the brain, lung, and cervical lymphatic system in an infant strongly raised concern for lymphoma or metastatic neuroblastoma; however, excisional cervical lymph node biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cells.

differentials.candidate: Acute necrotizing bacterial pneumonia with septic intracranial embolization
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute respiratory distress, high leukocytosis (22,300/µL), and fever could indicate severe pyogenic bacterial pneumonia with metastatic cerebral abscesses, but the chronic multi-month calcified lymphadenopathy and isolation of acid-fast bacilli pointed toward chronic granulomatous infection.

differentials.candidate: Primary central nervous system neoplasm (multicentric glioma / embryonal tumor)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive focal neurological deficits with multiple intra-axial parenchymal brain masses, severe vasogenic edema, and suture diastasis suggested primary brain tumors, but the concurrent leptomeningeal enhancement and systemic pulmonary mass favored disseminated granulomatous disease.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when microscopic examination of gastric aspirate demonstrated acid-fast bacilli (AFB) on smear, corroborating multi-organ tuberculomas (giant pulmonary tuberculoma, intracranial tuberculomas, and tuberculous lymphadenitis) in an infant.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old man presents to the hospital with a 3-day history of fever and 1 day of acute dyspnea. His past medical history is notable for pemphigus vulgaris, for which he has received prednisolone, methylprednisolone, and other immunosuppressive agents over the preceding 9 years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary etiology given severe T-cell immunosuppression from 9 years of corticosteroid therapy, hypoxia, elevated LDH, and diffuse interstitial opacities; although sputum cysts subsequently documented PCP coinfection, it failed to explain the subsequent development of an enlarging focal consolidation in the left upper lobe.

Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis was considered in the differential diagnosis given high susceptibility in chronic corticosteroid-dependent patients with respiratory failure, but was excluded after diagnostic workup failed to isolate fungal hyphae.
Considered as a potential cause of acute hypoxemic pneumonia in an immunocompromised host, but broad-spectrum coverage failed to prevent the progression of upper lobe consolidation.

Follow-up chest CT unexpectedly demonstrated an enlarged consolidation in the left upper lobe despite initial clinical recovery; subsequent repeated bronchoscopy with lung tissue biopsy, smear, culture, and histopathology confirmed the definitive diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male builder is admitted to the hospital with a 1-year history of diffuse abdominal pain, an unintentional weight loss of 14 kg, and daily fevers over the preceding 4 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Heavily favored based on profound B-symptoms, generalized adenopathy, and intense multi-station nodal and reticuloendothelial FDG avidity on PET imaging; although excisional lymph node biopsy confirmed concurrent nodular sclerosing Hodgkin's lymphoma, this did not account for the intracellular protozoa seen in the bone marrow aspirate.

differentials.candidate: Systemic infectious diseases (HIV, syphilis, viral hepatitis, EBV, CMV, toxoplasmosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Evaluated as infectious causes of persistent fever of unknown origin, hepatosplenic involvement, and lymphadenopathy, but excluded by universally negative serologic panels.

differentials.candidate: Classical Visceral Leishmaniasis (L. donovani / L. infantum)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, splenomegaly, and cytopenia in a patient from Brazil, but routinely employed rapid and indirect serological assays were completely negative due to antigenic variation in this rare visceral strain.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Visceral leishmaniasis (Leishmania amazonensis) in Hodgkin's lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bone marrow aspiration definitively visualized Leishmania amastigotes on direct microscopy, subsequently confirmed by PCR and culture with species identification as L. amazonensis, accompanied by lymph node biopsy demonstrating concurrent nodular sclerosing Hodgkin's lymphoma with positive Leishmania immunohistochemistry.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old patient presents with persistent neck pain for three months, accompanied by tingling sensations and heaviness in both upper extremities. The past medical history includes hypertension and a remote pulmonary infection treated in 1997 that was declared cured.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic spinal neoplasm / primary osseous malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: An isolated destructive osteolytic lesion centered on a cervical vertebral body with posterior cortical recession and epidural mass effect in a 66-year-old strongly raised clinical concern for metastatic cancer or primary tumor, but was ruled out by histological examination of the corpectomy specimen.

Bacterial spinal infections typically manifest with acute axial pain, systemic febrile toxicity, and marked leukocytosis; the indolent 3-month chronology with preservation of normal neurological status favored a chronic granulomatous process over pyogenic discitis.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Cervical Pott's disease (Tuberculous spondylitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient underwent surgical decompression via C3-C4 corpectomy with iliac bone grafting and anterior cervical plate fixation; histopathological examination of the resected cervical vertebral tissue confirmed Pott's disease, prompting a curative 12-month course of anti-tuberculosis chemotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old woman presents with a 20-day history of progressive weakness and loss of appetite. Her past medical history includes cholecystitis treated by cholecystectomy several years prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the patient developed intermittent fevers up to 38.3 °C with coarse pulmonary rales and inflammatory nodules on chest CT, but excluded when blood cultures showed no bacterial growth and symptoms recurred after broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy.

Evaluated as a primary cause of massive hemorrhagic/exudative pericardial effusion and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, but excluded by negative exfoliated cytology, normal serum tumor markers, and lack of neoplastic uptake on PET/CT.
Considered as potential etiologies of unexplained pericardial fluid accumulation, but ruled out by negative rheumatologic antibodies and minimally altered free T3.

Following recurrent effusion and chest pain 2 months later, thoracic surgical biopsy of the pericardial mass and mediastinal lymph nodes revealed classic granulomatous lesions and fibrous hyperplasia, establishing tuberculous pericarditis in conjunction with lymphocyte-predominant exudate and elevated ADA.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy presents with a 5-day history of intermittent fevers reaching up to 38.0 °C and nocturnal diaphoresis. His medical history is significant for alpha-thalassemia (-SEA/αα), for which he received five packed red blood cell transfusions prior to 2018.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered a likely etiology for prolonged fevers, night sweats, bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and cytopenias in a school-aged child, but ruled out by negative EBV molecular testing.

Initially suspected after IGRA and PPD were reactive while chest CT revealed only calcified hilar and mediastinal nodes without parenchymal consolidation; ruled out as the patient experienced progressive active fever and systemic cytopenias.

Suspected as the primary source of mycobacterial infection explaining cervical adenopathy, but ruled out when excisional biopsy of the cervical lymph node showed no granulomatous necrosis or acid-fast organisms.
Considered when the patient developed high fever, severe hyperferritinemia, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis, but excluded by whole-genome sequencing demonstrating no pathogenic exon variants.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Isoniazid-resistant bone marrow tuberculosis with secondary hemophagocytic syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: A second bone marrow aspirate revealed acid-fast bacilli on direct smear; subsequent real-time PCR confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis with gene sequencing identifying an InhA promoter mutation (-15C > T) conferring isoniazid resistance, alongside bone marrow hemophagocytosis.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital with a 3-week history of persistent fever and an enlarging neck mass. He was born prematurely at approximately 33 weeks of gestation and has a history of poor immune function and recurrent illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial chest radiograph suggested acute miliary tuberculosis in a child with prolonged fever and adenopathy; however, the etiology remained unresolved on further testing and failed to respond to antimicrobial regimens until fungal etiology was revealed.

Considered given fever, generalized lymphadenopathy, pancytopenia, marked hyperferritinemia, and splenomegaly meeting HLH criteria, but excluded by negative autoantibodies, bone marrow and lymph node biopsy, and flow cytometry.

Considered due to fulfilling HLH-2004 criteria in an immunocompromised child, but excluded as primary perforin deficiency because cytolytic and regulatory protein levels were intact, confirming secondary HLH driven by severe fungal sepsis.

Peripheral blood and bone marrow cytology identified mature granulocytes engulfing fungal spores, subsequently confirmed by mNGS of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and blood cultures identifying Talaromyces marneffei.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated in a surgical outpatient clinic for persistent left upper quadrant abdominal pain that has been present for six years without other associated symptoms. She emigrated from Iraq, where she had frequent, direct contact with sheep and domestic dogs.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because preliminary community laboratory screening identified positive Strongyloides IgG, but this parasite cannot account for a massive isolated unilocular splenic fluid-filled cyst.

differentials.candidate: Post-traumatic splenic pseudocyst / Congenital non-parasitic splenic cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential diagnosis of a large solitary splenic fluid collection in a young patient, but ruled out given the absence of any preceding blunt abdominal trauma, surgical history, or non-parasitic etiology in a patient with high-risk pastoral exposures.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic splenic abscess / Cystic splenic neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the massive size of the splenic mass, but the indolent 6-year history without fever, chills, leukocytosis, or solid neoplastic components made an abscess or cystic malignancy unlikely.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Isolated Splenic Hydatid Disease (Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Positive hydatid serology, combined with characteristic cross-sectional CT findings and pastoral livestock exposure, definitively established isolated splenic echinococcosis, leading to medical sterilization with albendazole and successful laparoscopic-assisted splenectomy.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old woman presents with progressive weakness and numbness in all four extremities, leaving her unable to walk, stand, or sit unsupported. Over the preceding two weeks, she experienced sharp, burning mid-back pain radiating into both legs (numerical rating scale score 7/10).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial discitis and vertebral osteomyelitis commonly produce vertebral body collapse and epidural inflammation, but characteristically present with acute high fevers, leukocytosis, and rapid destruction rather than subacute progression with large cold abscesses.

Severe cachexia, chronic radicular pain, and destructive cervical vertebral collapse causing spinal cord injury in an elderly patient raised high clinical suspicion for spinal metastases; however, contiguous multi-level involvement with extensive longus colli muscle abscess formation strongly pointed to a chronic granulomatous infection.

New-onset scleral icterus, nausea, vomiting, and epigastric discomfort in an elderly patient raised suspicion for hepatobiliary pathology or acute hepatitis, but physical exam confirmed absence of hepatosplenomegaly, indicating medication-related liver injury in the setting of severe sarcopenia and malnutrition.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Cervical spinal tuberculosis (Pott's disease) with spinal cord injury
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cervical spine MRI confirmed C5-C6 spondylodiscitis with large paravertebral and longus colli cold abscesses causing spinal cord injury (ASIA C C5), leading to emergent surgical anterior cervical corpectomy decompression and fusion (ACDF) confirming tuberculous spondylitis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old morbidly obese woman with a history of hypertension is brought to the emergency department following an acute loss of consciousness and left-sided weakness for two days, accompanied by high-grade fever and vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected as the sole diagnosis given chronic hypertension, morbid obesity, acute left hemiparesis, and basal ganglia hematoma; however, persistent extreme hyperthermia, massive rhabdomyolysis, coagulopathy, and antecedent flu-like illness indicated that the hemorrhage was a complication of systemic arboviral infection.
Considered because the patient spiked extreme fevers with acute renal failure, multiorgan involvement, and shock, but repeated microbiological blood and body fluid cultures remained sterile.

Evaluated in the differential diagnosis of extreme hyperthermia (core temperature 106-107 °F) and profound rhabdomyolysis (creatine kinase 10,000 IU/L), but eliminated after thorough medication and toxin reconciliation.

differentials.candidate: Other tropical pathogens (Malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, chikungunya, scrub typhus, COVID-19)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Systematically screened in the setting of acute febrile multi-organ failure with myalgia and chills in an endemic setting, but ruled out by non-reactive tests.

Tropical serology returned positive for dengue IgM antibodies, establishing the definitive diagnosis of Expanded Dengue Syndrome characterized by atypical spontaneous basal ganglia hemorrhage, extreme hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, coagulopathy, and acute kidney injury.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old male farmer is brought to the regional public hospital in Sikka Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, with acute loss of consciousness, generalized seizures, and profound jaundice. Fourteen days prior to presentation, he developed persistent fever, headache, and abdominal pain.

differentials.candidate: Complicated dyspepsia / Peptic ulcer disease with upper GI bleeding
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed and treated as dyspepsia at primary care facilities due to prominent abdominal pain; however, the subsequent emergence of acute renal failure, hemolysis (blackwater fever), seizures, and coma ruled out uncomplicated gastrointestinal disease.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis / Acute fulminant liver failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Evaluated because of deep jaundice, hepatomegaly, transaminase elevation, and altered sensorium, but excluded by negative serological markers for viral hepatitides and HIV.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria with multiorgan dysfunction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Examination of the peripheral blood smear demonstrated intraerythrocytic ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum with high-density parasitemia of 176,000 parasites/µL (3.52%), establishing severe malaria with cerebral involvement, blackwater fever, acute kidney injury, and hematemesis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old previously healthy male presented to a dermatology clinic with a persistent cutaneous lesion over his right mandible that had been gradually enlarging over five months. The lesion was characterized by localized swelling, erythema, and draining fistulous tracts exuding slightly seropurulent discharge, measuring approximately 3 cm by 4 cm.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the characteristic mandibular localization, chronic course, induration, and draining fistulous tracts discharging seropurulent secretion. Ruled out by the absence of characteristic sulfur granules or filamentous Gram-positive branching bacteria on tissue Gram stain and lack of bacterial growth on specific media.

Considered because chronic, non-healing ulceronodular and fistulizing cervicofacial lesions (such as scrofuloderma) can develop in endemic areas and fail empiric antibiotics. Ruled out by negative Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli on tissue sections and absence of mycobacterial growth.

Considered given the chronic granulomatous and fistulizing cutaneous lesion following travel to a subtropical region (Veracruz). Ruled out by absence of fungal elements on PAS and Giemsa stains and lack of fungal growth on Sabouraud dextrose, potato dextrose, and brain heart infusion agar over 5 weeks.

Considered as a leading protozoan differential for chronic ulcerative and nodular skin lesions in travelers returning from endemic areas of Mexico. Ruled out by negative Leishmania species-specific PCR testing performed on tissue biopsy and peripheral blood DNA.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when histopathological examination of the mandibular biopsy revealed amastigotes and trypomastigotes within the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, and satellite DNA PCR confirmed Trypanosoma cruzi (99% identity with clone ClBE07, DTU II). Delayed serological seroconversion (positive ELISA and Western blot at 4 months) further corroborated the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old previously healthy male presented in respiratory failure and multiorgan decompensation after an acute febrile illness. Ten days prior to admission, he sustained a rat bite to his left big toe, for which he received a tetanus vaccination and wound assessment at an outpatient facility.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the direct history of a rat bite to the left foot 10 days earlier. However, rat-bite fever characteristically manifests with migratory polyarthralgias, asymmetrical joint effusions, and an acral pustular or maculopapular exanthem, rather than the severe icterohemorrhagic triad of severe conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, acute renal failure, and diffuse pulmonary capillaritis with alveolar hemorrhage.

Considered due to rodent exposure leading to acute renal failure, thrombocytopenia, and diffuse pulmonary infiltrates/hemorrhage. Ruled out because hantavirus infections typically cause massive proteinuria and hemoconcentration without the profound cholestatic conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal transaminases observed in this patient.

differentials.candidate: Fulminant Sepsis with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in any patient presenting with high fever, ecchymoses, thrombocytopenia, pulmonary infiltrates, and multi-organ dysfunction. Ruled out as the primary etiology by the disproportionate cholestasis with preserved transaminases, specific rodent bite history, and prominent pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage indicative of infectious capillaritis rather than pure consumable coagulopathy.
