Myopericarditis was considered due to diffuse ST-segment changes and troponin release in a patient with acute systemic infection, but echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular systolic function (EF 61%) without regional wall motion abnormalities or pericardial effusion.

Cardioembolic origin of the anterior cerebral artery occlusion was ruled out by contrast-enhanced echocardiography demonstrating absence of intracardiac thrombus, while Doppler ultrasound showed resolution of common carotid thrombus without intrinsic hemodynamically significant stenosis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred on hospital day 3 when stool cultures confirmed Vibrio cholerae, establishing an overarching unifying diagnosis of cholera complicated by extreme hypovolemia, hemoconcentration, and dual arterial thromboembolic vascular occlusions.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male with a history of orthotopic cardiac transplantation performed 2 months prior presented to the emergency department with progressive dyspnea and severe hypoxia. He was in septic shock requiring hemodynamic resuscitation.

differentials.candidate: Primary opportunistic bacterial pneumonia and sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient presented in septic shock with Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia and bacteriuria; however, alveolar hemorrhage and characteristic purpura persisted despite empiric antimicrobial therapy, indicating that bacteremia was a secondary complication of mucosal disruption driven by larval penetration.

differentials.candidate: Drug-induced vasculitis or mechanical adhesive purpura
differentials.rule_out_reason: While the purpuric patches on the chest adhered to the margins of adhesive monitoring pads, the simultaneous appearance of periumbilical and proximal thigh lesions in a transplant recipient represented the characteristic 'thumbprint purpura' of subcutaneous parasite migration rather than an allergic drug reaction or adhesive trauma.

diagnostic_pivot: Plasma microbial cell-free DNA (Karius) testing detected Strongyloides, followed by punch biopsy of the thigh lesion confirming helminth larvae and egg-like forms within the dermis, with subsequent rereview of bronchoalveolar lavage and repeat stool microscopy confirming disseminated Strongyloides infection.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old woman who lived alone was admitted to the hospital with left lower back pain, fatigue, and difficulty walking. She had previously been hospitalized at another institution for approximately one month and treated with bed rest, analgesics, and empiric systemic anti-infectives without symptomatic improvement.

differentials.candidate: Isolated retroperitoneal and hip tophaceous gout
differentials.rule_out_reason: While the patient had marked hyperuricemia, deforming peripheral tophi, and sandy calcifications on CT, isolated tophaceous gout could not explain the persistent cyclical nocturnal fever (peaking at 39.3°C) that began on day 2 and failed to respond to febuxostat and NSAIDs.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial or fungal psoas abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic bacterial abscess and fungal collections were ruled out because 8 days of IV ceftriaxone failed to alleviate symptoms, and multiple aspirated fluid and surgical tissue cultures were negative for Gram-positive, Gram-negative, anaerobic bacteria, and fungi.

diagnostic_pivot: T-cell interferon detection returned positive, and subsequent open debridement of the iliopsoas collection combined with high-throughput metagenomic gene sequencing confirmed divergent Mycobacterium tuberculosis co-infecting the gouty tophus.

clinical_summary: An 80-year-old female presented to the emergency department with acute headache and confusion that began the previous evening. Family members documented an oxygen saturation of 70% on ambient air at home; she had not previously utilized supplemental oxygen.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although a sputum multiplex pneumonia panel identified high-copy Staphylococcus aureus, acute staphylococcal pneumonia was clinically inconsistent with the patient's indolent 6-month constitutional decline, negative procalcitonin, absence of dense lobar consolidation, and unresponsiveness to outpatient antibacterial agents, indicating incidental upper airway colonization.

Indolent weight loss and reticulonodular infiltrates raised suspicion for neoplastic dissemination; however, HRCT showed discrete, diffuse micronodules rather than primary masses or lymphadenopathy, and bronchoalveolar lavage cytology revealed only mild reactive inflammatory changes without malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: High-resolution CT confirmed multiple diffusely distributed micronodules characteristic of miliary disease, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis by positive QuantiFERON-TB Plus and positive MTB polymerase chain reaction.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male daily wage laborer was admitted to the general medicine ward with a 3-day history of acute high-grade fever accompanied by chills, rigors, severe anorexia, and complete insomnia.

differentials.candidate: Primary bipolar affective disorder / idiopathic mania
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient exhibited pressured speech, motor hyperactivity, and ideas of grandiosity, he had no prior personal or family history of psychiatric illness, and the behavioral changes appeared in direct temporal relationship with acute febrile thrombocytopenia.

In the setting of severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count 32,000/µL) and acute neuropsychiatric decompensation, acute intracranial bleeding or focal structural encephalitis was a major concern, but magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrated no abnormalities.

diagnostic_pivot: Specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) testing confirmed positive dengue IgM antibodies in the setting of acute fever, myalgias, and severe thrombocytopenia, establishing dengue fever with secondary neuropsychiatric manifestation.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female presented to the dermatology outpatient clinic with an 8-month history of an enlarging patch below her right knee. The lesion had begun as a small, pea-sized spot that progressively expanded in size, accompanied by noticeable loss of temperature and light touch sensations over the area.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although presenting as a discrete hypopigmented macule, vitiligo and post-inflammatory pigmentary alterations demonstrate fully preserved thermal, tactile, and pinprick sensations and are never associated with peripheral nerve enlargement.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous tuberculosis (lupus vulgaris) or cutaneous sarcoidosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: While both disorders may produce dermal epithelioid granulomas, neither causes localized thermal anesthesia with prominent regional peripheral nerve trunk hypertrophy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was established by the triad of an anesthetic hypopigmented plaque, palpable common peroneal nerve thickening confirmed by high-resolution ultrasonography showing an increased cross-sectional area, and full-thickness punch skin biopsy revealing epithelioid cells and Langhans' giant cells, confirming borderline tuberculoid leprosy despite a negative slit-skin smear.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old female was admitted with a 2-year history of recurrent thoracolumbar back pain and fevers. Two years earlier, she had been diagnosed with a thoracic vertebral infection and achieved temporary symptom resolution following intravenous antibiotic therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although prior BAL fluid metagenomic sequencing reported a high sequence abundance of Pneumocystis jirovecii following corticosteroid therapy, the patient was HIV-negative and serum (1,3)-beta-D-glucan was completely negative (<37.5 pg/mL), confirming that Pneumocystis represented asymptomatic respiratory colonization rather than invasive pneumonia.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: While her symptoms had shown transient temporary improvement with vancomycin months earlier, the 2-year indolent clinical course, cold abscess formation, and lack of persistent bacterial isolation on targeted debridement ruled out an uncomplicated pyogenic bacterial infection.
Invasive pulmonary fungal disease was suspected due to steroid therapy, lymphopenia, and bilateral pulmonary lesions, but was excluded by a negative serum galactomannan antigen level.

diagnostic_pivot: C-arm-guided biopsy of the thoracic vertebral abscess yielded purulent fluid confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA/RNA, and lung tissue metagenomic sequencing demonstrated overwhelming MTBC dominance (72,040 sequences, 85.68% abundance).

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus infection and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS, CD4+ T-cell count 115 cells/µL) presented with a two-week history of worsening pain and swelling of the left fifth digit.

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis / septic arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute pyogenic dactylitis (such as Staphylococcus aureus) typically presents with intense acute inflammation, leukocytosis, and fever; in contrast, this patient had a normal leukocyte count of 5,000/mm³, an indolent 2-week course without fever, and soft mottled yellow bone rather than acute purulent phlegmon.

In a patient with severe CD4 lymphopenia and disseminated pulmonary nodules, opportunistic fungal osteomyelitis was a leading differential, but specific mycobacterial molecular assays and fungal smears were negative for fungal pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Incision, drainage, and biopsy of the left fifth phalanx revealed acid-fast bacilli on direct microscopy, qualitative Gen-PROBE testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex ribosomal RNA, and both bone tissue and induced sputum cultures confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old male presented with a 4-month history of continuous, dull aching upper abdominal pain and a progressively enlarging visible lump in the upper abdomen over the preceding two months.

differentials.candidate: Biliary cystadenoma or cystic hepatic neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although cystic neoplasms of the biliary tree can present as large multilocular intrahepatic masses, they typically lack multiple independent internal daughter cysts, are not associated with marked peripheral eosinophilia (900/µL), and do not demonstrate positive echinococcal serology.

Bacterial or amebic abscesses typically cause high fever, right upper quadrant tenderness, leukocytosis, and deranged liver function tests; this patient was afebrile, non-icteric, had a normal leukocyte count of 7,500/µL, normal liver function tests, and sterile evacuated cyst contents.

diagnostic_pivot: Specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) serology was positive for echinococcus, and surgical exploration with evacuation of three liters of cyst fluid demonstrated diagnostic daughter cysts, hooklets, laminated membranes, and protoscolices.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old man presented to the hospital with right upper quadrant and epigastric pain that began 20 days prior following weightlifting, accompanied by nausea and anorexia. One day prior to admission, he developed an acute fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected preoperatively due to the solid-cystic pseudotumoral appearance on ultrasound and extensive peritoneal fluid, but excluded intraoperatively when the lesion was shown to be an exophytic cyst filled with daughter cysts and nonpurulent gelatinous matrix without neoplastic tissue.
Considered due to the abrupt onset of fever, right flank tenderness, leukocytosis, and peritoneal fluid collection, but intraoperative aspirate cultures were negative for bacterial growth.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration revealed a huge exophytic hepatic cyst packed with daughter vesiculae and gelatinous matrix, and microscopic fluid examination confirmed characteristic parasitic hooklets.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old physician presented with the acute onset of high fever, profound asthenia, and severe systemic illness. Several days prior, he had performed endotracheal intubation on a critically ill patient admitted to the hospital in Kosovo.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to petechiae, mucosal bleeding signs, high fever, and marked thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by coagulation testing showing no evidence of consumptive coagulopathy.

differentials.candidate: Severe Community-Acquired / Atypical Bacterial Pneumonia with Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, asthenia, and respiratory manifestations, but the presence of soft palate enanthem, petechiae, and direct occupational exposure during airway instrumentation pointed to a nosocomial viral hemorrhagic syndrome.

diagnostic_pivot: Viral RNA extraction from serum and whole blood followed by nested RT-PCR targeting the small (S) RNA segment yielded a specific 260-bp band identical to the index patient, confirming Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus infection.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old man presented with a chronic draining cutaneous fistula on the left chest wall. He was a moderate tobacco smoker with no history of substance abuse.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the fistula developed five years earlier following a traumatic rib fracture and emergency incision/drainage, but baseline inflammatory markers and routine hematology were entirely normal, and surgical exploration demonstrated parasitic vesicles rather than bacterial osteomyelitis.

Considered due to the palpable mass and cortical bone destruction on the 6th rib, but excluded by CT showing absence of invasive soft-tissue extension and confirmed non-neoplastic on surgical pathology.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracotomy and resection of the lateral arch of the 6th rib revealed parasitic vesicles and bone sequesters, with pathological examination confirming hydatid cyst of the rib.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old man living in Haiti, with a history of heavy alcohol consumption and two previous episodes of tropical febrile illness treated with chloroquine, presented with acute fever, headache, nausea, and diarrhea of six days duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the rapid deterioration from fever and headache into altered sensorium and generalized seizures, but an infectious encephalitis panel was completely negative.

differentials.candidate: Primary Sepsis / Severe Bacterial Enteric Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, diarrhea, hematemesis, bloody stools, DIC, and acute multiorgan failure, but peripheral blood smears confirmed intraerythrocytic parasites, indicating complicated parasitic infection with secondary polymicrobial coinfections.

diagnostic_pivot: Initial presentation in Haiti demonstrated Plasmodium falciparum ring forms on peripheral blood smear, and despite antiparasitic therapy, he suffered fulminant complicated disease with multiorgan failure and secondary Clostridium perfringens bacteremia and Candida tropicalis fungemia.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of left-sided chest pain and low-grade fever. She had no significant past medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a large lymphocytic exudative effusion with markedly elevated ESR (110 mm/h), but argued against by an extremely high adenosine deaminase level (120 U/L), positive tuberculin skin test, and absence of malignant cells on pleural biopsy.

Considered in a patient with fever and pleural effusion, but ruled out by the subacute one-month course, straw-colored appearance of the aspirate, and marked lymphocytic predominance (90% lymphocytes) rather than a neutrophilic exudate.

diagnostic_pivot: Pleural biopsy revealed tubercular granulomas, and pleural fluid culture by the Bactec method confirmed drug-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old man presented with a three-week history of headaches that had previously provided partial relief with ibuprofen and acetaminophen. On the day prior to admission, he developed a severe headache accompanied by nausea and multiple bouts of emesis.

differentials.candidate: Colloid Cyst of the Third Ventricle / Intraventricular Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a classic cause of paroxysmal headache, emesis, and acute obstructive hydrocephalus in young adults, but typically occurs at the anterior foramen of Monro rather than the posterior third ventricle, and surgical histopathology demonstrated a parasitic larval wall rather than a mucinous cyst.

Considered given initial partial analgesic responsiveness, but excluded by progressive cognitive decline (forgetfulness), lack of personal or family headache history, and neuroimaging revealing obstructive ventriculomegaly.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergent external ventricular drainage and subsequent stereotactic transcortical excision of the third ventricular cyst revealed characteristic cestode larval morphology with a three-layered cuticle, suckers, and rostellum containing hooklets.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old male with no known chronic comorbidities was referred to the hospital with persistent moderate- to high-grade fever, cough with scant expectoration, worsening bilateral pleural effusions, and new-onset epistaxis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the abrupt onset of high fever, petechial rash, hepatosplenomegaly, and severe thrombocytopenia with mucosal bleeding, but excluded by negative peripheral blood smears and nonreactive dengue serologies.

differentials.candidate: Enteric Fever (Typhoid) / Bacterial Sepsis / Infective Endocarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given prolonged fever, cachexia, hepatosplenomegaly, and multiorgan involvement, but disproven by negative blood and urine cultures, negative Widal titers, negative ASO titers, and a normal echocardiogram.

diagnostic_pivot: CECT revealed classic diffuse miliary pulmonary nodules with necrotic lymphadenopathy and systemic visceral granulomatous lesions, while bone marrow biopsy confirmed necrotizing epithelioid cell granulomas and megakaryocytic hyperplasia consistent with secondary immune thrombocytopenia.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old boy who was born and lived in rural Cameroon for four years before immigrating to Italy two years prior was brought to the Emergency Department in status epilepticus lasting over 30 minutes, which had failed to terminate following rectal diazepam (0.5 mg/kg).

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Status Epilepticus / Recurrent Febrile Seizure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the prior history of an isolated febrile seizure at age 1, but excluded by focal semiology (right head and gaze deviation, right hemiclonic jerks), focal EEG slowing over left leads, and distinct structural parenchymal cysts on brain MRI.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Encephalitis / Accidental Toxic Ingestion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a child with sudden onset of prolonged seizure, coma, and respiratory compromise, but the child was afebrile without preceding systemic infection, trauma, or toxic exposure.

diagnostic_pivot: Brain MRI demonstrated two distinct round cystic lesions in the right lentiform nucleus and left frontoparietal lobe, and serological evaluation confirmed specific anticysticercal antibodies by Western blot assay.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man presented with a severe febrile illness accompanied by profound malaise, headache, diaphoresis, and worsening jaundice of five days duration. Two weeks prior to illness onset, he had returned from a business trip to Cameroon; he had not taken travel chemoprophylaxis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Heavily considered in a returning traveler with high fevers, severe jaundice, acute renal impairment, and marked thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by negative slide macro-agglutination testing.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral / Atypical Myocarditis or Zoonotic Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fever, tachycardia, and low-voltage QRS complexes on ECG, but extensive serologic screening for cardiotropic viruses, Coxiella burnetii, Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, and enteric pathogens was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Peripheral blood film examination demonstrated a heavy 20% parasitemia of Plasmodium falciparum, and post-mortem evaluation identified severe acute lymphocytic myocarditis with myocardiolysis and parasitized erythrocytes within the myocardial microvasculature.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old HIV-negative male was admitted to the hospital with community-acquired pneumonia that progressively worsened despite initial therapy. He had a significant smoking history.

differentials.candidate: Peptic Ulcer Disease / Perforated Gastric Ulcer (H. pylori or NSAID-induced)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the most common cause of acute gastric perforation and free air, but excluded by negative gastric biopsies for Helicobacter pylori, absence of NSAID exposure, and ongoing PPI therapy.

Considered due to an extensive 3 cm ulcerative and necrotic process in an older smoker near the gastroesophageal junction, but multiple gastric ulcer biopsies showed only reactive epithelial changes without malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergent laparotomy revealed a posterior gastric wall perforation and contiguous necrotic mass; cultures of both peritoneal fluid and gastric tissue grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and resected colonic tissue demonstrated classic caseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old male presented with a holocranial headache of four months' duration, primarily located in the frontal region, accompanied by gradual diminution of vision in the left eye over the preceding two months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pituitary adenoma is the most common sellar/suprasellar mass in this age group but typically presents with endocrine dysfunction or solid contrast enhancement, whereas this patient had completely preserved pituitary hormone profiles and a cystic/ring-enhancing lesion with central hypointensity.
Central nervous system fungal infection can produce thick-walled ring-enhancing sellar lesions, but fungal culture and staining of the curetted material isolated no fungal organisms.
Bacterial abscess typically presents with acute febrile illness, elevated systemic inflammatory markers, and leukocytosis, none of which were present in this afebrile patient with normal hematology.

diagnostic_pivot: Right subfrontal craniotomy revealed a thick-walled avascular suprasellar lesion containing caseous material; histopathology revealed lymphocytic infiltration with destruction of pituitary tissue, epithelioid cells, and Langhans giant cells, and PCR was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old female patient presented with a 3-month history of progressive weakness in both lower limbs, numbness extending from the lower thorax to the feet, and new-onset bowel and bladder incontinence.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary intramedullary spinal cord tumors typically display expansile, infiltrating heterogeneous solid tissue enhancement and syrinx formation, whereas MRI in this child demonstrated a discrete, well-circumscribed cystic lesion with an eccentric mural nodule and ring enhancement.

Tuberculous granulomas of the spinal cord are an important consideration in endemic settings, but spinal and chest radiographs showed no evidence of bony or pulmonary tuberculosis, and the tuberculin skin test was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Spinal MRI revealed pathognomonic cysticercosis features consisting of a well-defined intramedullary cyst with an isointense mural nodule (scolex) and ring enhancement, and CSF analysis demonstrated lymphocytic-eosinophilic pleocytosis with positive ELISA for anti-Taenia solium IgG antibodies, followed by rapid neurological recovery on antiparasitic and steroid therapy.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old woman presented to the hospital with fever and productive cough. Her surgical history was notable for having undergone an open total cyst pericystectomy 9 months earlier for a massive multivesicular cystic lesion (measuring 16 x 17 x 18 cm) that had replaced the right hepatic lobe, accompanied by diaphragmatic fixation of the left lateral segment.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While the patient presented with fever, cough, and right lower lobe consolidation on chest radiography, typical bacterial pneumonia cannot account for the gross expectoration of bile-stained sputum (bilioptysis).

Although the patient had a prior episode of cholangitis, her current presentation was dominated by pulmonary complaints and bile expectoration in the absence of hyperbilirubinemia or clinical jaundice.

diagnostic_pivot: The direct observation of persistent bilioptysis prompted a 99mTc-mebrofenin cholescintigraphy scan, which confirmed a biliobronchial fistula (BBF) with radioisotope passage from the liver into the right lower lobe and sputum; percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography revealed stenosis of the biliojejunal anastomosis with biliothoracic fistulization, which resolved completely following stricture dilation and stenting.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old female with severe aplastic anemia underwent allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation from an HLA-matched sibling donor following a conditioning regimen of fludarabine and cyclophosphamide. Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis consisted of equine anti-thymocyte globulin, methotrexate, and intravenous cyclosporine.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Invasive aspergillosis is the most common mold infection following stem cell transplantation and was initially treated with empiric voriconazole, but bronchoalveolar lavage demonstrated acid-fast bacilli and lung biopsy revealed broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching diagnostic of mucormycosis rather than Aspergillus.

Bacterial etiology was considered given the acute onset in a post-transplant patient, but blood and urine cultures remained sterile, early neutropenic coverage had been completed, and the focal upper lobe consolidation failed to respond to antibacterial coverage.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoalveolar lavage analysis established the diagnosis of active pulmonary tuberculosis by identifying acid-fast bacilli, prompting initiation of quadruple anti-tubercular therapy, while subsequent lung tissue biopsy confirmed concurrent mucormycosis with characteristic broad aseptate hyphae, leading to dual therapy with liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old Caucasian male presented to the Infectious Diseases Unit two days after returning from a one-month business trip in the Democratic Republic of Congo. He reported high fevers, severe frontal headache, nausea, and epigastric abdominal pain that had begun 48 hours prior to admission.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteric fever is a leading cause of febrile illness and gastrointestinal discomfort in travelers returning from endemic zones, but blood cultures for bacterial pathogens using continuous automated monitoring were sterile.
Systemic bacterial infection was excluded by negative aerobic and anaerobic blood cultures and prompt therapeutic response to antiparasitic agents rather than broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear confirmed Plasmodium falciparum with 0.2% parasitemia on initial admission; after a full course of artemether-lumefantrine, readmission 14 days later revealed recrudescent Plasmodium falciparum with 2% parasitemia (late clinical failure), which successfully cleared with oral quinine and doxycycline.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old Caucasian woman presented for evaluation of a chronic discharging sinus and suspected prosthetic infection following a total left hip arthroplasty performed two years earlier. Sixteen months after her initial joint replacement, she had developed insidious left hip pain and motion limitation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Conventional bacterial prosthetic joint infection was excluded by repeatedly sterile blood and aspirate cultures on aerobic and anaerobic media, failure to improve on multiple broad-spectrum antibiotics (linezolid, teicoplanin, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones), and the presence of non-acute granulomatous histology.

While prominent mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation and elevated ACTH with low-normal cortisol confirmed primary adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune adrenalitis was ruled out by negative anti-adrenal cortex antibodies and CT findings of enlarged calcified adrenal glands rather than idiopathic atrophy.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of active mycobacterial infection by positive tuberculin skin test, positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold (3.08 IU/mL), positive RD1 interferon-gamma response, CT findings of a periprosthetic abscess extending to the psoas muscle and calcified adrenal enlargement, and positive PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex from the fistulous exudate established the diagnosis of periprosthetic tuberculosis with secondary adrenal destruction.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old Asian man with diabetes mellitus, employed as an office clerk, presented with a one-month history of daily fevers and a five-day history of painful swelling below the left submandibular region.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Thoracic CT scan suggested an anterior mediastinal malignant mass, but submandibular lymph node excision biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation composed of lymphocytes and plasma cells without neoplastic lymphoid proliferation, and blood/marrow cultures subsequently isolated an infectious pathogen.

Although histopathology from the submandibular node biopsy showed non-caseating granulomas suggestive of tuberculosis, the tuberculin skin test was negative, bone marrow showed no acid-fast bacilli or granulomas, and blood and bone marrow cultures isolated a non-mycobacterial pathogen.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood and bone marrow cultures grew Burkholderia pseudomallei susceptible to ceftazidime and co-trimoxazole, establishing the diagnosis of disseminated melioidosis presenting as mediastinal and cervical lymphadenitis, with clinical resolution achieved on targeted antibiotic therapy.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old female registered nurse presented to the emergency room in Paris, France, with fever, nausea, and general malaise. Her past medical history was notable only for spontaneously regressive Henoch-Schönlein purpura during infancy.

differentials.candidate: Acute Occupational Viral Hepatitis (HBV / HCV / HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although percutaneous needle exposure frequently prompts concern for bloodborne viral hepatitis or acute retroviral syndrome, documented HBV immunization, negative baseline HCV/HIV serologies, and rapid development of acute severe thrombocytopenia with hemolysis point away from classical viral hepatitis.
Concomitant jaundice, abdominal tenderness, and transaminitis can indicate acute biliary obstruction or cholangitis, but emergency abdominal imaging was completely normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Peripheral blood smear examination identified intraerythrocytic ring stages, confirming Plasmodium falciparum with a parasitemia of 0.038 per 100 erythrocytes contracted nosocomially via needlestick injury, which resolved with quinine therapy.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old woman, 28 weeks pregnant, of Kenyan origin residing in France, presented to the gynecology-obstetrics emergency room at a Parisian area hospital with acute fever and systemic malaise. She reported having traveled to Kenya and returning to France 20 days prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile presentation during the late second / early third trimester raises concern for chorioamnionitis or obstetric sepsis, but localized pelvic or uterine signs were absent, and examination of blood smears revealed a specific bloodborne protozoal etiology.

differentials.candidate: Acute Retroviral Syndrome or Bloodborne Viral Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Maternal systemic viral infections were considered given international travel and fever, but specific serological screening was negative for acute HIV and HCV infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of thin and thick blood smears revealed intraerythrocytic protozoa, confirming Plasmodium falciparum malaria with a parasitemia of 0.05 per 100 erythrocytes, which resolved with oral and intravenous quinine.

clinical_summary: A female physician residing in Hungary presented with an acute illness characterized by fever, headache, diffuse maculopapular rash, myalgia, cervical lymphadenopathy, and general malaise. She had never traveled to any tropical or vector-borne disease-endemic region.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Mononucleosis / Exanthem (EBV, Parvovirus B19, Rubella)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute non-tropical viral exanthems frequently present with fever, rash, and tender lymphadenopathy, but the strict 7-day incubation following accidental percutaneous inoculation with viremic blood from a tropical traveler strongly pointed toward a bloodborne arboviral transmission rather than respiratory viral infection.

Initial presentation of an acute arboviral illness raised vigilance for complicated hemorrhagic progression, but the patient exhibited completely normal platelet counts, stable hematocrit without hemoconcentration, and uneventful clinical recovery.

diagnostic_pivot: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) using universal flavivirus primers identified viral RNA demonstrating 98% nucleotide sequence identity with dengue virus type 2 (strain ThNH76/93), and sequential serological ELISA demonstrated appearance of anti-dengue IgM antibodies on day 12 followed by IgG seroconversion at 3 weeks, confirming nosocomial transmission of dengue virus via needlestick injury.

clinical_summary: An adult patient with confirmed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presents for clinical evaluation of persistent mucocutaneous ulcerations. Baseline hematologic investigations reveal moderate anemia with a hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dL and systemic inflammation with an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 30 mm in the first hour.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While common in HIV patients with CD4 counts below 200 cells/μL, early cultures yielded inconclusive results rather than typical rapid yeast or bacterial growth.
Although Histoplasma capsulatum causes mucosal ulcers in advanced HIV infection, it does not produce folded greenish-black colonies with red pigment diffusion on Sabouraud's dextrose agar.
The characteristic macroscopic colonial appearance with red pigment secretion combined with microscopic penicillate brush border morphology confirmed the diagnosis of Talaromyces marneffei infection.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a one-day history of coughing up approximately five cups filled with blood. For the preceding 3 months, she had been experiencing a persistent cough, significant weight loss, and drenching night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bronchial arterial hypertrophy represents the primary source of massive hemoptysis in cavitary lung disease, but selective bronchial angiography demonstrated normal vessels without active contrast extravasation.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Lung Abscess / Cavitary Bacterial Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: While pyogenic cavitary lung abscess can produce chronic constitutional symptoms and cavitation, the etiology was verified as mycobacterial by positive acid-fast bacilli staining.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Pulmonary Artery (Rasmussen) Aneurysm secondary to Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Contrast CT demonstrated focal parenchymal enhancement, and selective pulmonary angiography definitively identified a 5-cm pulmonary artery aneurysm originating from the left lower lobe, which was successfully treated with coil embolization.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old woman is admitted with a 7-day history of fever, general malaise, and progressive dyspnea. Five years prior to presentation, she underwent bilateral silicone breast augmentation, with a right-sided revision procedure performed 7 months ago following implant rupture.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial infection was initially suspected given respiratory distress and multiorgan involvement, but empiric antimicrobial therapy had no clinical impact and peripheral blood cultures were negative.

Sarcoidosis was supported by elevated serum ACE and lysozyme levels, BALF CD4/CD8 ratio elevation, and noncaseating granulomas on liver biopsy, but corticosteroid treatment triggered miliary progression rather than disease control.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Miliary Tuberculosis secondary to Corticosteroid Immunosuppression
differentials.rule_out_reason: Follow-up chest CT revealed classic bilateral miliary nodules, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis was definitively identified by acid-fast staining of gastric fluid, sputum, and liver specimens alongside positive PCR testing.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male factory worker is evaluated in the emergency department for acute behavioral changes. Over the preceding 5 days, he developed pressured speech, euphoric mood, marked motor agitation, increased self-confidence, decreased need for sleep and food, severe irritability, and outbursts of aggression with grandiose claims.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While DSM criteria for mania were met with severe grandiosity and hyperactivity, primary psychiatric illness was inconsistent with the acute febrile prodrome, profound thrombocytopenia, and absence of psychiatric history.
Given endemic exposure, high-grade fever, transient encephalopathy, and marked thrombocytopenia, severe malaria was considered but excluded by microscopic examination.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial/Viral Encephalitis or Intracranial Hemorrhage
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute central nervous system infection or hemorrhage was considered in light of altered consciousness and severe thrombocytopenia, but signs of meningeal irritation were absent and neuroimaging was completely normal.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue Infection with Acute Mania (Neuro-dengue)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Serological confirmation was established by a positive IgM ELISA in conjunction with marked thrombocytopenia and systemic transaminitis.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old male farmer presents with multiple shiny, non-pruritic cutaneous nodules, papules, and plaques distributed over the trunk, lower back, buttocks, arms, legs, face, chest wall, elbows, and knees, numbering approximately 42 lesions in total.

differentials.candidate: Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL) / Granulomatous Infectious Dermatosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the widespread papulonodular eruption in an agricultural worker, but excluded by the absence of Leishmania amastigotes and the discovery of acid-fast bacilli on specialized staining.

Histopathological examination initially showed a storiform and whorled proliferation of spindle-shaped histiocytic cells resembling fibroblasts, raising suspicion for a fibrohistiocytic neoplasm before special stains were applied.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: De Novo Histoid Leprosy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining with 5% sulfuric acid demonstrated abundant, elongated, solid acid-fast bacilli intracellularly and extracellularly, corroborated by a high bacteriological index (4+ to 5+) on slit skin smear.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old nondiabetic, immunocompetent man presents with a 6-year history of slowly progressive swelling of the left foot. Over several years, he had received multiple empirical courses of oral and intravenous antibacterial agents at primary care facilities without clinical improvement, and had undergone two unsuccessful incision and drainage procedures at a regional hospital.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to long-standing tarsal/metatarsal osteolysis and soft tissue ulceration, but was completely unresponsive to multiple oral and parenteral antibiotic courses and repeated surgical drainage attempts.
While clinically similar, actinomycetes were excluded when tissue cultures demonstrated true dematiaceous fungal mycelia rather than filamentous bacteria.

Despite the atypical absence of discharging sinuses, MRI demonstrated the classic 'dot in circle' sign, and surgical biopsy verified granulomatous inflammation with microbiological culture isolating Curvularia lunata.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old man presents with a 3-month history of mild intermittent peri-umbilical pain, low-grade fevers, decreased appetite, and an intentional weight loss of 4 kg. His bowel and bladder habits are entirely normal, and he has no past medical or surgical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Infected urachal remnants typically manifest as acute pyogenic abscesses caused by Staphylococcus or gram-negative bacteria, but urine culture was sterile and surgical exploration revealed cold caseous necrosis rather than acute purulent drainage.

Primary neoplasms of the urachus present as supravesical cystic or solid masses in young adults, but histological analysis confirmed benign urothelium alongside granulomatous inflammation without malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Primary Urachal Cyst Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: En bloc resection revealed thick pultaceous material, and histopathology demonstrated classic caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells, definitively confirmed by culture isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis on Lowenstein-Jensen media.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old man presents with a 4-month history of progressive perianal ulceration and purulent discharge. One year previously, he underwent surgical drainage of a perianal abscess that recurred two months after initial healing.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Crohn's disease was a leading initial consideration for recurrent perianal ulcerations and systemic wasting, but endoscopic visualization revealed completely normal rectal and sigmoid mucosa, and subsequent histology demonstrated caseating necrosis rather than non-caseating granulomas.

Simple bacterial perianal disease was suspected based on prior abscess drainage, but cannot account for the accompanying abdominal tenderness, massive cachexia, and upper lobe pulmonary cavitary lesions.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Perianal Tuberculosis with Pulmonary and Peritoneal Involvement
differentials.rule_out_reason: Histological examination of peritoneal and perianal biopsies demonstrated epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells and caseous necrosis, and perianal culture confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old previously healthy boy residing in a crowded urban area in Sri Lanka presents with a 5-day history of high-grade intermittent fever, epigastric discomfort, and backache. He has had no severe myalgias, overt bleeding manifestations, or respiratory symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Severe Dengue Infection / Dengue Shock Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Prevalent in urban Sri Lanka and recognized to trigger shock, myocarditis, and severe thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by negative viral antigen and antibody testing.
Rapid onset of pulmonary hemorrhage and progressive acute renal failure strongly mimicked ANCA-associated vasculitis or anti-GBM disease, but autoimmune serologies and complement levels were normal.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Severe Leptospirosis (Weil Disease with Pancreatitis and Pulmonary Hemorrhage)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic dilemma of multisystem collapse was resolved by microscopic agglutination testing confirming a markedly elevated Leptospira titer alongside positive IgM antibodies.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man presents to a tertiary hospital in Jamaica with red-colored urine and severe muscle aches. Eight days prior to presentation, he developed sudden fever and back pain that resolved within 48 hours following acetaminophen use.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In tropical settings, fever and intense myalgia followed by thrombocytopenia, transaminitis, and pigmented red urine strongly suggest leptospirosis, but the patient had no rodent exposure and specific leptospiral serologies were negative.

Severe transaminase elevation suggested acute viral hepatitis, and red urine with a positive blood dipstick raised concern for acute glomerulonephritis; however, hepatitis serologies were negative, and urine microscopy lacked erythrocytes or casts, confirming isolated myoglobinuria.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Acute Dengue Fever Complicated by Massive Rhabdomyolysis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute dengue infection was definitively proven by detection of the dengue virus non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen on day 4 of illness, followed by documented IgM seroconversion on days 8 and 14.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old Caucasian female with known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (CDC stage A3) and hepatitis C virus (HCV, genotype 1b) co-infection (Child-Pugh score 5) presented to the hospital with a one-week history of fever and a productive cough of two days' duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient with advanced HIV infection (CD4 144/mm³) presenting with subacute infection and subsequent CNS involvement, Cryptococcus is a primary consideration, but latex agglutination testing in blood and CSF as well as fungal cultures were negative.
Pyogenic bacterial and fungal central nervous system infections were excluded by negative CSF Gram stains, smears, and sterile routine cultures.

differentials.candidate: Viral and Parasitic Encephalitis (Toxoplasma, CMV, HSV, VZV, JC Virus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Common opportunistic CNS infections in immunocompromised individuals were ruled out by negative multiplex CSF real-time PCR panels and negative CMV pp65 antigenemia.

differentials.candidate: Primary Autoimmune Vasculitis or Hypercoagulable Stroke
differentials.rule_out_reason: Following the development of hemiplegia and aphasia, non-infectious causes of ischemic stroke such as thrombophilia, cardioembolism, and systemic vasculitis were excluded by normal vascular imaging, echocardiography, and negative autoimmune serologies.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic confirmation was established by bronchoalveolar lavage culture isolating multi-susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis, in conjunction with CSF showing marked lymphocytic pleocytosis with hypoglycorrhachia, and neuroimaging demonstrating middle cerebral artery occlusion with Sylvian fissure leptomeningeal enhancement indicative of tuberculous vasculitis.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male from the Guntur District of Andhra Pradesh presented with a four-month history of productive cough, chest pain, hemoptysis, and progressive dyspnea. He noted occasional low-grade fever but reported no significant weight loss or night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial thoracic CT scan suggested a pyogenic lung abscess because of the thick-walled hypodense lesion with adjacent loculated fluid; however, the indolent four-month progression, lack of septic symptoms, and peripheral eosinophilia argued strongly against a typical pyogenic bacterial abscess.

Considered as a primary suspect given chronic productive cough, hemoptysis, and referral to a pulmonary tuberculosis clinic, but excluded by absence of weight loss and repeatedly negative sputum acid-fast smears.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic confirmation was achieved when ultrasound-guided aspiration of the pulmonary cyst revealed viable scoleces, followed by definitive right thoracotomy and resection of a unilocular hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old man with known chronic kidney disease presented with a 20-day history of a painless, slowly enlarging swelling over the lower part of his sternum. He reported no preceding history of chest trauma, sternal puncture, or thoracic surgery.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Sternal Osteomyelitis / Acute Bacterial Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute pyogenic sternal osteomyelitis typically results from median sternotomy or direct trauma and presents with acute severe pain, erythema, warmth, and leukocytosis, which were completely absent in this indolent fluctuant cold abscess.
The negative tuberculin skin test initially argued against active mycobacterial infection, but this was recognized as cutaneous anergy secondary to uremia and malnutrition in chronic kidney disease.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis was confirmed by fine-needle aspiration cytology of the sternal mass demonstrating necrotic material with epithelioid giant cells and positive PCR for tuberculous bacillus, alongside excisional biopsy of the matted cervical nodes revealing caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis with Langhans giant cells.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy from Nepal presented with a five-month history of mild, dull right upper quadrant abdominal pain and recurrent low-grade fevers. Over the preceding four months, his family also noted mild intermittent facial puffiness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial sonographic evaluation suggested cylindrical roundworms in the common bile duct, a frequent cause of biliary colic in endemic areas, but endoscopic extraction recovered flat leaf-like trematodes rather than nematodes.

Considered due to chronic fevers, right upper quadrant tenderness, hepatomegaly, and liver microabscesses, but patient had completely normal liver biochemistries without icterus, marked peripheral eosinophilia, and intraluminal parasitic flukes on cholangiography.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis was confirmed by endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), which revealed irregular intraluminal filling defects in the common bile duct, from which multiple adult Fasciola hepatica flukes were successfully extracted following sphincterotomy.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old woman presented with an eight-month history of persistent headache, general slowness in activities of daily living, and progressive memory disturbances. Over the preceding six months, her symptoms worsened with gait instability, pronounced psychomotor slowing, and new-onset urinary incontinence.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient presented with the classic triad of gait impairment, urinary incontinence, and dementia, but neuroimaging revealed non-communicating obstructive hydrocephalus due to an obstructing intraventricular cystic lesion rather than communicating ventriculomegaly.

differentials.candidate: Primary Neurodegenerative Parkinsonian Dementia / Lewy Body Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Parkinsonian features including cogwheel rigidity and shuffling gait suggested a neurodegenerative parkinsonian dementia, but this was excluded by the structural obstructive hydrocephalus and dramatic cognitive recovery (MMSE improving to 22/30) immediately following ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis was confirmed by brain MRI demonstrating multilocular, racemose conglomerate cystic lesions in the Sylvian fissure, basal cisterns, and third ventricle, corroborated by strongly positive serum and CSF IgG ELISA titers for neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old male native to Bolivia was admitted to the hospital 64 days after undergoing an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from an HLA-identical sibling for underlying refractory anemia with multilineage dysplasia.

differentials.candidate: Acute Hepatic and Gastrointestinal Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute GVHD was the primary clinical suspicion given the presentation of bloody diarrhea, jaundice, and severe liver injury around day +60 post-allogeneic HSCT; however, liver biopsy showed no evidence of GVHD, and steroid intensification subsequently accelerated the underlying parasitic dissemination.
Mechanical biliary tract obstruction was considered given marked elevations in alkaline phosphatase, GGT, and conjugated bilirubin, but was definitively ruled out by cross-sectional imaging.

Although blood and urine cultures subsequently grew Escherichia coli, this was a secondary complication of gut barrier breakdown caused by massive larval migration rather than an isolated primary bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis was established by stool parasitological examination demonstrating numerous migrating filariform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis, confirming fatal hyperinfection syndrome with secondary bacterial translocation triggered by corticosteroid therapy in an immunosuppressed patient from an endemic region.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old girl presented with a six-month history of intermittent colicky pain in the right lumbar region and dysuria, accompanied by the visible passage of small, pale, ruptured grape-skin-like membranous structures in her urine.

differentials.candidate: Simple Renal Cyst (Gharbi Type I / Bosniak Type I)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple cysts present as thin-walled, non-septated fluid collections lacking internal architecture or communication with the pelvicalyceal system, whereas this patient presented with multiseptated architecture containing daughter cysts and active rupture into the collecting system.

differentials.candidate: Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma / Multilocular Cystic Nephroma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Complex multiseptated cystic renal masses can simulate malignant cystic tumors, but the passage of collapsed daughter cyst membranes (hydatiduria) is pathognomonic for communicating parasitic cyst rupture into the calyces.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis was confirmed by positive serum ELISA for echinococcal antibodies, abdominal CT demonstrating an 11.5 × 11.0 cm multilocular lesion with a 'cyst within the cyst' appearance involving the kidney and upper ureter, and histopathologic confirmation of hydatid disease following nephroureterectomy.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old male from China presented with a two-year history of worsening generalized skin lesions and an 18-year history of progressive numbness involving both upper and lower extremities. Twenty years earlier, he had received dapsone monotherapy (50 mg daily) for a widespread dermatologic condition; he discontinued the medication after six months once his skin lesions cleared and subsequently relied on...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic disseminated noduloulcerative cutaneous eruptions can simulate leishmaniasis or systemic fungal infections, but the hallmark eighteen-year progression of extensive peripheral limb numbness points definitively to a neurotropic mycobacterial infection.

Although clinical relapse was suspected following years of untreated disease, the failure of subsequent therapy and development of new lesions while taking rifampicin suggested acquired drug resistance selected by prior irregular monotherapy rather than simple drug-sensitive relapse.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of relapsed lepromatous disease was confirmed by slit-skin smears demonstrating a high bacillary index (5.0) and skin biopsy isolating acid-fast bacilli, with 16S rDNA and repetitive element gene sequencing identifying the pathogen and rpoB codon 441 mutation confirming secondary rifampicin resistance.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old previously healthy man presented with a two-day history of acute, severe headache, unsteady gait, and new-onset urinary incontinence. He denied any previous history of dietary consumption of raw or undercooked pork meat.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute ventriculomegaly presenting with headache, disorientation, and gait disturbance initially suggested an intracranial mass obstructing ventricular outflow; however, cranial CT definitively excluded parenchymal or intraventricular lesions.

The combination of lower-extremity hypotonic paresis, urinary incontinence, and failed lumbar puncture ('dry tap') suggested a diffuse intradural compressive tumor or meningeal carcinomatosis, but surgical biopsy revealed parasitic cyst membranes rather than neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal turning point occurred when thoracolumbar spine MRI revealed extensive intradural contrast-enhancing cystic lesions extending from C7 through S1, and subsequent microsurgical laminectomy with biopsy confirmed chronic inflammation, calcification, and fibrosis pathognomonic of cysticercosis cyst walls.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old previously healthy male presented with a three-day history of persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, and marked decrease in urine output. Two weeks prior, he had been hospitalized at a local facility for a one-week febrile illness accompanied by jaundice, anemia (hemoglobin 8.8 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelet count 55,000/μL), and mild renal dysfunction (serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL), which was managed with...

differentials.rule_out_reason: TTP was considered in the setting of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated LDH, but was argued against by the absence of fever or fluctuating neurological abnormalities, the predominance of acute oliguric renal failure, and prompt stabilization with plasma exchange.
Drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy, particularly from quinine used in febrile illnesses, is a well-known cause of acute HUS, but the patient had no exposure to this medication.

Connective tissue disease and viral hepatitides/retroviral glomerulopathies were excluded by negative autoimmune and viral serologies, as well as absence of immune deposits on renal immunofluorescence.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis was post-infectious hemolytic uremic syndrome triggered by Plasmodium vivax infection (documented by schizonts on prior blood smear and negative P. falciparum testing), with persistent renal thrombotic microangiopathy confirmed on kidney biopsy showing glomerular capillary double contours and arteriolar onion-skin changes.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male presents with recurrent crops of crusted papular lesions on the extensor surfaces of his upper limbs and back for one month, along with painful boils over his buttocks for 20 days.

differentials.candidate: Primary cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis / Pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta (PLEVA)
differentials.rule_out_reason: While skin histopathology demonstrated a focus of leukocytoclastic vasculitis in the mid-dermis, the presence of bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, hemoptysis, and marked hypersensitivity to mycobacterial antigens pointed away from an isolated idiopathic vasculitis or PLEVA.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial furunculosis and ecthyma gangrenosum / Pyoderma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient presented with boils and a 4x4 cm ulcer with a necrotic base on the buttock, the symmetric distribution of centrally necrotic papules on extensor surfaces and concomitant respiratory symptoms indicated a systemic hypersensitivity process rather than simple pyogenic infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when sputum testing confirmed acid-fast bacilli and the tuberculin skin test showed high-grade reactivity, linking the necrotic papules to papulonecrotic tuberculid (PNT) secondary to pulmonary tuberculosis, with rapid resolution upon initiating multidrug antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: An 87-year-old woman with a medical history of senile dementia, diabetes mellitus, hypertensive diastolic heart failure, and chronic kidney disease presents to the Emergency Department with progressive jaundice and features of acute obstructing cholangitis.

differentials.candidate: Choledocholithiasis / Retained common bile duct stone
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a post-cholecystectomy elderly patient presenting with acute obstructing cholangitis, common bile duct stones represent the most frequent etiology. However, endoscopic evaluation did not identify biliary calculi; instead, soft cystic contents were visualized and retrieved.

Profound obstructive jaundice with high direct bilirubin and severe ductal dilatation in an 87-year-old patient strongly suggests malignant obstruction such as cholangiocarcinoma or ampullary carcinoma. However, ductal clearance revealed parasitic membranes communicating with a peripheral liver cyst rather than an infiltrative tumor.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during ERCP when sphincterotomy and bile duct debridement yielded multiple round laminated membranes and cyst remnants, confirming intrabiliary rupture of the right hepatic hydatid cyst, complemented by subsequent CT evidence of concomitant free intraperitoneal cyst rupture.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old Portuguese woman presents to the emergency department with severe, refractory upper abdominal pain radiating to the back. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the epigastrium without peritoneal signs or abdominal guarding.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back is classical for acute pancreatitis; however, the serum laboratory investigations and abdominal CT scan were entirely normal, and subsequent advanced imaging excluded pancreatic parenchymal or ductal inflammation.

Biliary duct dilatation and severe biliary colic typically raise suspicion for common bile duct stones; however, endoscopic imaging demonstrated a long, non-shadowing, triple-layered tubular structure rather than an acoustic shadowing calculus.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was achieved when biliopancreatic endoscopic ultrasonography revealed the pathognomonic longitudinal triple-layered structure of Ascaris lumbricoides in the common bile duct, confirmed by endoscopic retrograde cholangiography and definitive extraction of a 15-cm adult worm using a Dormia basket.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old female homemaker residing in a rural area presents with intermittent high fever, severe abdominal pain, recurrent vomiting, and markedly reduced urine output. On physical examination, her pulse rate is 110 beats/min and blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg; she is afebrile at the time of evaluation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High intermittent fever, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, jaundice, and acute kidney injury in a rural patient strongly suggest severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria; however, peripheral parasite testing was negative.

The constellation of fever, conjunctival findings, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, severe acute renal failure, and microscopic hematuria closely mimics leptospirosis, but specific serology was non-reactive.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial sepsis / Gallstone pancreatitis with sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe abdominal pain with dramatic pancreatic enzyme elevation (amylase 2662 U/L, lipase 3822 U/L) and multiorgan failure suggested acute necrotizing pancreatitis with systemic bacterial sepsis, but prolonged blood cultures yielded no bacterial growth.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was achieved with specific serological testing demonstrating high Weil-Felix agglutination titers against OX-K (1:320) and positive IgM antibodies to Orientia tsutsugamushi, establishing scrub typhus presenting with the rare complication of acute pancreatitis and subsequent pseudocyst.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever, recurrent vomiting episodes, and severe dehydration, developing 17 days after returning from a 6-week trip to Cote d'Ivoire, during which she stayed in both rural and urban areas without taking chemoprophylaxis.

differentials.candidate: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) / Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS) with bacterial pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extreme hyperglycemia (glucose 794 mg/dL), dehydration, lactic acidosis, and right middle lobe pneumonia strongly suggested a hyperosmolar diabetic crisis triggered by community-acquired bacterial pneumonia; however, the profound thrombocytopenia (6 x 10^9/L) and acute drop in hemoglobin pointed toward a severe hemolytic parasitic infection rather than an isolated metabolic event.

differentials.candidate: Enteric fever (Typhoid fever) / Severe bacterial sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recent travel to West Africa presenting with fever, vomiting, abdominal symptoms, multiorgan involvement, and lobar pneumonia raised high clinical suspicion for Salmonella bacteremia or invasive bacterial sepsis, but blood testing specifically demonstrated hemoparasites.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when peripheral blood smear microscopy revealed high-grade Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitemia with 40% parasitized red blood cells, confirming life-threatening falciparum malaria presenting with the unusual complication of extreme hyperglycemia.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old female presents with right-sided partial motor seizures, progressive bilateral decrease in vision, headache, vomiting, and fever for 15 days, followed by the development of right-sided hemiparesis over the last 2 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A two-week history of fever, headache, vomiting, seizures, and focal neurological deficit associated with a large mass lesion raises high suspicion for an intracranial infectious abscess; however, the lesion was a giant, thin-walled solitary cyst without surrounding purulent necrosis, and systemic inflammatory signs were minimal.

differentials.candidate: Cystic intracranial neoplasm (Pilocytic astrocytoma / Arachnoid cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Massive solitary cystic mass causing long-standing elevated intracranial pressure (bilateral optic atrophy) and hemiparesis in a 9-year-old is frequently a low-grade cystic astrocytoma or congenital cyst; however, non-parasitic congenital cysts do not typically present with acute seizures and fever, and neoplasms usually feature enhancing mural nodules.

Neurocysticercosis is the most common parasitic brain lesion causing pediatric seizures in endemic zones, but it characteristically produces small (1–2 cm) multiple parenchymal cysts rather than an isolated giant 9-cm cyst, and specific serological testing confirmed echinococcal etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was established by strongly reactive serum Echinococcus ELISA (0.96 D) and definitive histopathological identification of dead scolices of Echinococcus granulosus within the surgically excised unilocular cyst wall.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 55-year-old man with no prior known cardiovascular disease presents to the emergency department with high fever and generalized arthralgias of five days' duration. On physical examination, his temperature is 39.0°C, blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his pulse is distinctly irregular with a heart rate of 78 beats/min.

differentials.candidate: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) / Ischemic ventricular arrhythmia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Ventricular trigeminy and elevated total creatine kinase in a 55-year-old male raised concern for acute myocardial ischemia or infarction; however, cardiac troponin was negative (<0.5 ng/mL), CPK-MB was normal (20 U/L), and the patient presented with fever, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia rather than ischemic chest discomfort.

differentials.candidate: Primary viral myocarditis (Enterovirus / Parvovirus B19 / Influenza)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute viral myocarditis frequently manifests with ventricular arrhythmias, apical hypokinesia, and reduced ejection fraction; however, the prominent hematocrit elevation (48.1%), leukopenia (3,100/mm³), and precipitous drop in platelets (to 55,000/mm³) pointed specifically toward an acute arboviral capillary leak syndrome.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred with positive serum IgM for dengue, coupled with echocardiographic confirmation of apical hypokinesia (ejection fraction 50%) that fully normalized alongside spontaneous resolution of ventricular trigeminy within 24–48 hours as the platelet count recovered.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man, formerly employed as a forest ranger in Albania prior to migrating to Italy five years earlier, is admitted to an orthopedic surgery unit for planned lower extremity amputation of his right foot.

differentials.candidate: Chronic pyogenic osteomyelitis / Bacterial soft-tissue fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: A multi-year history of foot swelling with discharging sinuses following outdoor labor is frequently misdiagnosed as chronic bacterial osteomyelitis; however, repeated surgical debridements and broad-spectrum antibiotics failed to halt disease progression, and the presence of organized macroscopic granules is not seen in typical pyogenic osteomyelitis.

The clinical presentation with chronic tumefaction and draining sinuses strongly suggested mycetoma; differentiating eumycotic infection (fungal) from actinomycotic infection (bacterial) was essential because fungal mycetoma typically produces dark/black granules and usually mandates surgical excision rather than medical cure.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon microbiological analysis of the extruded white grains, which yielded Actinomadura madurae, confirming actinomycetoma and enabling successful medical treatment with the Welsh antibiotic regimen, completely sparing the limb from amputation.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old male woodcutter from Albania presents for evaluation of progressive swelling and non-healing lesions on his right lower extremity amputation stump. His clinical history began nearly two decades earlier with chronic inflammatory swelling of the right foot.

differentials.candidate: Chronic bacterial stump osteomyelitis / Post-surgical sinus tract
differentials.rule_out_reason: Persistent draining sinuses in an amputation stump are frequently attributed to deep bacterial osteomyelitis or retained foreign material; however, long-standing lack of response to penicillin and aminoglycosides and the production of organized white granules pointed away from standard pyogenic pathogens.

Chronic grain-producing fistulous tumefaction refractory to standard antibiotics is characteristic of mycetoma; distinguishing eumycetoma from actinomycetoma was essential, as fungal etiologies (such as Madurella mycetomatis) often produce dark/black grains and mandate aggressive surgical re-amputation, whereas bacterial forms respond to medical therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when needle aspiration of the stump nodules and white granules isolated Actinomadura madurae, definitively establishing recurrent actinomycetoma of the stump and guiding successful curative medical antibiotic therapy without requiring above-knee amputation.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old Bulgarian woman presents to the emergency department with a 2-hour history of acute, severe epigastric pain that migrated rapidly to the lower abdomen. She notes a history of mild, intermittent, dull epigastric discomfort over the preceding year, but has no other past medical history and no history of trauma.

differentials.candidate: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy / Ruptured hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute peritonitis with pain radiating to the suprapubic area and sudden vascular collapse in a healthy 24-year-old female raised immediate suspicion for ruptured ectopic pregnancy or pelvic hemorrhage; however, urine beta-hCG was negative, and imaging localized the ruptured pathology to the liver with concurrent anaphylactic urticaria.

differentials.candidate: Perforated peptic ulcer / Pancreatitis with septic shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute epigastric pain followed by peritonitis, lactic acidosis, and rapid onset of shock could suggest gastrointestinal perforation or severe pancreatitis; however, the sudden development of extensive urticaria, periorbital edema, and hypothermia responding to antihistamines and steroids indicated anaphylaxis rather than septic or hypovolemic shock from a hollow viscus perforation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when emergency abdominal CT revealed a large cystic left hepatic lobe mass with detached internal membranes (serpiginous strands) and diffuse peritoneal fluid, which upon laparotomy and histology confirmed an intraperitoneally ruptured hydatid cyst lined by a PAS-positive laminated capsule with scolices and positive hydatid ELISA.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department and requires admission to the intensive care unit due to prolonged fever lasting several weeks associated with generalized symptoms of systemic inflammatory response syndrome and severe sepsis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, and severe cytopenias, but excluded by negative microbiological and serological evaluation.
Considered in the differential diagnosis of acute febrile illness with cytopenias, hepatitis, and coagulopathy, but excluded by negative serology.
Considered given the constellation of prolonged fever, jaundice, acute kidney injury, and pulmonary involvement, but ruled out by negative serological tests.
Considered due to persistent fever, constitutional symptoms, and hepatosplenomegaly, but ruled out by negative serology and sterile cultures.
Considered as a classic viral driver of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a patient fulfilling HLH diagnostic criteria, but ruled out by negative serology.
Initial working diagnosis given SIRS, ARDS, multiorgan dysfunction, and coagulopathy, but excluded by sterile microbial cultures across multiple anatomical sites.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of severe multiorgan failure, secondary HLH, and a classic cutaneous eschar prompted confirmatory serologic testing, which definitively established the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old previously healthy man presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of high fever and severe headaches. He had returned 10 days earlier from a 10-day work trip to South Sudan, during which he slept under an insecticide-treated bed net but did not take chemoprophylaxis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential diagnosis of acute febrile illness with thrombocytopenia, transaminitis, and acute renal dysfunction in a returned traveler, but excluded by sterile blood cultures.
Evaluated during the clinical course as a potential predisposing cause of severe intravascular hemolysis following oxidant or antimalarial exposure, but excluded by normal enzyme activity.
Considered when the patient developed severe secondary delayed intravascular hemolysis and dark urine following blood transfusions, but ruled out by absence of red blood cell alloantibodies.
Serological screens showed positive antibody titers to these organisms, but these represented past remote exposures rather than the etiology of the acute febrile and hemolytic crisis.

diagnostic_pivot: Review of peripheral blood smears during initial assessment revealed massive intraerythrocytic parasitemia, confirming severe falciparum disease.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male, born in a rural area of Trujillo state, Venezuela, and residing in La Guaira city, presents to the emergency department with high fever, new-onset generalized seizures, and progressive neurological impairment that developed one week prior to admission.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary presumptive diagnosis given the presence of ring-enhancing mass lesions in the basal ganglia in a severely immunosuppressed HIV patient, but excluded by failure to demonstrate clinical improvement following empirical therapy with pyrimethamine and sulfadiazine.

diagnostic_pivot: Cytological evaluation of cerebrospinal fluid obtained via lumbar puncture revealed parasitic flagellates morphologically compatible with trypomastigotes, which along with the patient's geographic origin in an endemic state confirmed central nervous system trypanosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old man with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease presents to the emergency department with a 3-month history of intermittent fever, chills, night sweats, poor appetite, abdominal fullness, and profound involuntary weight loss of 11 kg over the past month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis given severe cachexia, constitutional decline, and a solitary 7-cm solid liver lesion, but excluded by negative serum oncologic biomarkers (CEA, CA 19-9, AFP, PSA) and absence of neoplastic cells on histopathology.
Considered due to the large focal hepatic mass in an adult male, but excluded by negative hydatid serological evaluation.
Considered in a patient with chronic fevers, right upper quadrant knocking pain, and solitary liver mass, but ruled out by negative amoebic hemagglutination serology.

Considered given fever, chills, right hypochondrial tenderness, and hepatic space-occupying lesion, but ruled out by sterile blood/sputum cultures and absence of bacteria on direct examination of aspirate exudates.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological evaluation of the liver biopsy revealed chronic granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells consistent with tuberculoma, resulting in complete resolution upon administration of antituberculosis chemotherapy.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old woman originally from Guinea-Bissau, West Africa, is admitted with an 18-month history of progressive dorsal back pain, asthenia, and marked weight loss, complicated over the preceding 8 months by complete loss of the ability to walk.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to multifocal, disseminated musculoskeletal and dermatologic disease in a young patient from an endemic region of West Africa, but excluded by negative HIV serology and normal immunodeficiency screening.

Considered in the differential diagnosis of large destructive paravertebral and epidural abscesses with osteolytic vertebral collapse, but excluded by negative routine bacterial blood and urine cultures.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Primary Neoplasm or Metastatic Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an etiology of multi-level osteolytic vertebral destruction, pathologic kyphotic collapse, and complete paraplegia, but ruled out by histopathology demonstrating granulomatous inflammation and absence of neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of bone biopsy material demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation containing acid-fast bacilli, and tissue cultures conclusively isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman of low socioeconomic background from Veracruz, Mexico, presents to the emergency department with a one-week history of progressive headache, phonophobia, high-grade fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea.
