She has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) diagnosed in 2003 with joint, cutaneous, and renal involvement.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) Flare / Lupus Pneumonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis given her underlying autoimmune disease history and subsequent development of acute pulmonary hemorrhage, but ruled out by absence of active lupus stigmata at presentation and failure to respond to high-dose intravenous corticosteroid boluses.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) / Microangiopathic Hemolysis / DIC
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given her recent history of TTP and the subsequent emergence of a purpuric cutaneous rash, but excluded by normal haptoglobin levels and absence of laboratory evidence of intravascular hemolysis or consumptive coagulopathy.
Considered when pulmonary infiltrates and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure developed during hospitalization, but excluded due to lack of diagnostic clinical criteria.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the purpuric skin lesions and postmortem autopsy revealed filariform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis migrating throughout the skin, lungs, thyroid, liver, and gastrointestinal tract, confirming fatal disseminated strongyloidiasis.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male of Caribbean descent presents to an ophthalmology clinic with complaints of progressive visual blurring, pain, and photosensitivity in the right eye of several weeks' duration. Concurrently, he reports acute constitutional symptoms consisting of high fever, severe generalized arthralgia, malaise, severe headache, and dehydration.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Autoimmune Panuveitis / Sarcoidosis / Syphilitic or Tubercular Uveitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the initial presumptive differential diagnosis for bilateral panuveitis with secondary ocular hypertension, but ruled out following a negative comprehensive systemic workup and a normal plain chest radiograph.

Considered given the severe acute febrile and algic syndrome in an endemic tropical Caribbean setting, but classical hemorrhagic plasma leakage was excluded by the complete absence of thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis of acute arboviral panuveitis and secondary uveitic glaucoma was established by demonstration of significantly elevated specific serum IgM antibody titers on two independent serial measurements.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old Tarahumara male is transferred to an intensive care facility with a 4-month history of persistent cough, hemoptysis, progressive dyspnea, intermittent fever, and severe involuntary weight loss. On physical examination, he appears severely cachectic and in acute respiratory failure.

differentials.candidate: HIV-Associated Opportunistic Pulmonary Infection (e.g., Pneumocystis / Fungal)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe cachexia, profound peripheral lymphopenia (0.2 × 10^3/µL), and diffuse bilateral alveolar pulmonary opacities, but ruled out by negative HIV serologic testing.

differentials.candidate: Viral Hepatitis (Hepatitis B / Hepatitis C) Co-Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Evaluated in the setting of severe wasting, chronic infection, and hypoalbuminemia prior to initiation of complex systemic antimicrobials, but excluded by negative serologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Microbiological examination of sputum smears revealed positive acid-fast bacilli, and real-time polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of specific mycobacterial DNA, establishing acute respiratory failure secondary to cavitary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old Indian male presents with a 1-month history of progressive weakness, loss of appetite, dizziness, involuntary weight loss, and low-grade fever, accompanied by a noticeable pulsatile mass in the abdomen.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Mycotic Aneurysm (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Salmonella, Gram-Negative Bacilli)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnostic possibility for an infected saccular aortic aneurysm in a young adult, but ruled out by repeatedly sterile microbial blood cultures.
Considered as an opportunistic fungal cause of infective aortitis and aneurysmal degeneration, but excluded by negative fungal blood cultures.

Considered in the differential diagnosis of extensive conglomerate necrotic retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and marked constitutional decline, but ruled out by lack of primary neoplastic mass lesions or bowel involvement on CT angiography and absence of neoplastic cells on histology.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the enlarged peri-aneurysmal retroperitoneal lymph node revealed classic central caseous necrosis with epithelioid cells and macrophages, confirming a tuberculous etiology.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old man presents to an outpatient otolaryngology clinic with a 1-month history of progressive hoarseness, decreased appetite, and low-grade fever. He denies cough, sputum production, or hemoptysis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary clinical diagnosis in an elderly patient presenting with hoarseness and an exophytic laryngeal mass, but ruled out by histopathological examination demonstrating chronic granulomatous inflammation rather than invasive malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Laryngeal Involvement from Active Pulmonary Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because laryngeal involvement is classically secondary to bronchogenic seeding from active cavitary pulmonary disease, but ruled out by normal respiratory examination and normal chest radiography.

diagnostic_pivot: A positive tuberculin skin test combined with histopathological evaluation of the epiglottic biopsy demonstrating Langhans giant cells, epithelioid granulomas, and caseous necrosis confirmed primary laryngeal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old woman is referred to the dermatology clinic for evaluation of a severe, diffuse, and recurrent cutaneomucosal dermatosis that has been intermittent over the preceding 3 years. The patient has failed multiple empiric topical therapies.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had a history of recurrent fungal infections and dystrophic nail changes, physical inspection showed no active fungal lesions at presentation, and prior topical antifungals failed to control the disease.

Thick white hyperkeratotic plaques on the hands, feet, and nail beds resemble severe palmoplantar psoriasis or hereditary keratoderma, but the widespread excoriations and generalized crusted papules suggest a severely pruritic, non-keratinization process.

differentials.candidate: Systemic lupus erythematosus / Autoimmune connective tissue disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Systemic autoimmune disease was considered given multisystem pathology and early-onset nephrotic syndrome with renal failure, but autoimmune and monoclonal workups were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of mineral oil skin scrapings prepared from the hyperkeratotic plaques revealed numerous live mites, establishing crusted (Norwegian) scabies occurring in a host with suspected cutaneous immunodeficiency.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old girl is brought to the hospital with a history of recurrent seizures over the past 18 months. The seizure semiology initially presented as multifocal events with secondary generalization, which gradually evolved into tonic seizures.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The large size, butterfly distribution crossing the corpus callosum, mass effect, and extensive vasogenic edema raised strong concern for high-grade glial neoplasm; however, neurosurgical biopsy was deferred due to classic multifocal inflammatory imaging, and the lesion regressed on medical therapy.

Ring-enhancing cerebral lesions can represent pyogenic abscesses, but the afebrile 18-month chronic course, normal hemogram, normal CSF indices, and lack of acute inflammatory markers argued against bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated a distinct lactate double peak with diffuse suppression of all normal metabolite peaks, characteristic of caseating granulomatous lesions, leading to deferred biopsy and subsequent clinical and radiological resolution on antitubercular treatment.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old woman presents to the hospital with a history of persistent cough, expectoration, and worsening shortness of breath over several months. Her respiratory symptoms have become progressively more severe despite previous symptomatic medical therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral wheezing, cough, and severe obstructive ventilatory defect (FEV1 35.2% predicted) suggested severe asthma; however, failure of symptom resolution and chest CT demonstrated fixed structural tracheal narrowing rather than reversible bronchospasm.

Focal stenosis of the upper trachea at the thoracic inlet raised concern for primary endotracheal neoplasm or idiopathic subglottic stenosis; however, histopathology showed chronic inflammatory mucosal changes with fibrous proliferation rather than malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of positive acid-fast bacilli in sputum combined with bronchoscopic visualization of mucosal granulomatous lesions with caseous necrosis confirmed endobronchial tuberculosis complicated by cicatricial tracheal stenosis.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with a 3-year history of cough and expectoration, and approximately 1 month of worsening chest tightness and shortness of breath. Three years prior, she had been admitted to a local facility with cough and expectoration of white phlegm without fever, night sweats, fatigue, or chest pain, where she had been treated with...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic productive cough and diffuse wheezing initially led to a diagnosis of bronchial asthma, but the failure of anti-inflammatory therapies and presence of structural central airway narrowing on CT refuted this diagnosis.

differentials.candidate: Bronchogenic carcinoma / Malignant central airway obstruction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute severe right main bronchus stenosis with lobar consolidation raised suspicion for primary endobronchial malignancy, but bronchoscopic examination demonstrated caseous necrotizing material rather than a neoplastic mass.

diagnostic_pivot: Microbiological examination of sputum demonstrating positive acid-fast bacilli, alongside bronchoscopic findings of lower tracheal stenosis and right main bronchial occlusion with adherent caseous necrotic material, confirmed active tracheobronchial and pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old male farmer presents with a 10-month history of progressive neck, chest wall, and back pain, along with 1 month of a subcutaneous swelling below his right nipple and new-onset numbness in both lower extremities.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic bone disease / Skeletal malignancy of unknown primary
differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread osteolytic lesions in the vertebrae and ribs with dural compression strongly pointed to metastatic bone disease; however, extensive oncologic screening, normal tumor markers, and fine needle aspiration of the rib lesion failing to demonstrate neoplastic cells ruled this out.
Multiple osteolytic lesions in the axial skeleton presenting with normocytic anemia and elevated inflammatory markers suggested multiple myeloma, but monoclonal gammopathy screening was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Spontaneous ulceration and purulent discharge from the sub-nipple chest wall mass yielded positive acid-fast bacilli staining and positive TB-DNA PCR, definitively establishing multifocal musculoskeletal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old previously healthy woman presents to an ophthalmology clinic complaining of a several-month history of a symptomatic lesion in her right eye, associated with a persistent foreign body sensation and local ocular discomfort.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The nasal interpalpebral conjunctival location and fibrovascular appearance initially suggested a common pterygium, but surgical excision revealed intense granulomatous inflammation rather than solar elastotic degeneration, followed by rapid postoperative recurrence.

differentials.candidate: Ocular surface squamous neoplasia / Pyogenic granuloma
differentials.rule_out_reason: A vascularized, recurrent ocular surface lesion raised suspicion for conjunctival dysplasia or reactive vascular granuloma; however, histologic analysis demonstrated a specific protozoan granulomatous etiology without dysplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the excised conjunctival mass revealed prominent stromal granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid and multinucleated giant cells packed with intracellular protozoan parasites.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male is referred to a tertiary cancer center for evaluation of a painful, non-healing ulcer on his left cheek that has persisted for one month. He has a significant history of habitual cigarette smoking.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient's chronic smoking history and a painful, solitary, indurated oral ulcer strongly suggested oral cancer, but histopathological examination of the buccal mucosal biopsy definitively ruled out malignancy, demonstrating granulomatous inflammation instead.

differentials.candidate: Deep fungal infection / Oral Crohn's disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Granulomatous mucosal ulceration with giant cells can occur in deep mycoses or inflammatory bowel disease, but special histochemical staining and sputum smears demonstrated mycobacterial organisms.

diagnostic_pivot: Application of the Ziehl-Neelsen stain to repeat mucosal biopsy tissue demonstrated acid-fast bacilli, corroborated by sputum smear positivity (grading 1+) and fibrocalcific changes on chest radiography.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old woman presents to the ophthalmology emergency service with acute, severe right eye pain and sudden diminution of vision, occurring three days after sustaining ocular trauma from a wooden stick.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Traumatic corneal perforation accompanied by rapid hypopyon and severe vitritis pointed strongly to fulminant bacterial endophthalmitis; however, corneal scrapings, conjunctival swabs, and diagnostic vitreous tap were negative for bacteria, and the eye deteriorated despite intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime.

Vegetative ocular injury from a wooden stick commonly introduces filamentous fungi, but fungal smears from corneal scrapings and vitreous tap were negative, and hourly fortified topical natamycin failed to arrest progression to panophthalmitis.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic evaluation of eviscerated ocular tissue demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, confirmed by positive acid-fast bacilli staining and PCR detection of mycobacterial antigen in corneal tissue.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old Brazilian male presents to the emergency department with a five-day history of abdominal pain, dark stools, and syncope. His past medical history includes an episode of esophageal variceal bleeding that was presumed to be secondary to cirrhosis; however, an extensive workup for chronic liver disease at that time was negative, and a prior liver tissue core evaluation demonstrated...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Esophageal varices, splenomegaly, and nodular hepatic appearance on ultrasound suggested decompensated cirrhosis; however, hepatic synthetic function was entirely normal, peripheral stigmata were absent, and liver histology demonstrated portal fibrosis without the architectural distortion or regenerative nodules characteristic of cirrhosis.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic non-cirrhotic portal hypertension / Portal vein thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Presinusoidal portal hypertension with preserved hepatic synthetic function can occur in idiopathic non-cirrhotic portal hypertension, but this was ruled out by the discovery of an active parasitic cause within the gastrointestinal tract.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the descending colonic polyp revealed numerous large parasitic eggs featuring a prominent lateral spine surrounded by an eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate, diagnostic of Schistosoma mansoni infection causing presinusoidal periportal fibrosis (Symmers' pipe-stem fibrosis) and chronic blood loss.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old male who has worked as an industrial sandblaster for the past 13 years presents with a 2-month history of fever, cough, breathlessness, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain that acutely worsened over the preceding 2 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive lobar consolidation in a patient with chronic industrial dust exposure, emaciation, and nonresolving infiltrates raised strong suspicion for malignancy; however, CT-guided lung biopsy confirmed the absence of neoplastic cells, revealing interstitial pneumonia with fibrosis.

Bilateral ground-glass opacities and basal consolidations with high ESR, leukocytosis, and negative sputum acid-fast smears suggested nonresolving bacterial pneumonia or organizing pneumonia; however, repeat imaging showed progressive disease and bronchoalveolar lavage subsequently identified an infectious mycobacterial etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchial lavage fluid was positive for acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, while polarized microscopy demonstrated numerous birefringent silica crystals, clinching the diagnosis of active pulmonary tuberculosis complicating underlying occupational silicosis (silicotuberculosis).

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old male with a significant past medical history of diffuse bilateral infiltrative pulmonary disease at the stage of fibrosis presented after experiencing two generalized tonic-clonic seizures accompanied by persistent occipital headaches.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Preoperative brain MRI demonstrated a peripheral frontal mass with intralesional hemorrhage and mass effect, radiologically mimicking a meningioma, but surgical excision and histopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis rather than meningothelial neoplasia.
Initial cranial CT suggested a calcified frontal tumor with surrounding edema, but histopathology following surgical resection excluded malignancy, identifying an infectious pseudo-tumor.

diagnostic_pivot: Neurosurgical resection and pathological anatomical analysis demonstrated a cerebromeningeal granuloma with caseous necrosis presenting as a pseudo-tumor (tuberculoma), establishing the definitive diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old male priest presented with a 2-year history of progressive, generalized raised cutaneous nodular lesions. The illness began insidiously two years prior as small, reddish raised papules over the right knee that gradually enlarged and eventually ruptured, discharging blood-stained purulent material.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the chronic nodular presentation over extremities and an external biopsy suggesting fungal etiology, but ruled out because fungal microscopy and fungal cultures of multiple lesion specimens were completely negative, and prior itraconazole therapy was ineffective.

Considered because the nodules had previously ruptured with purulent discharge, but bacterial cultures from multiple lesions were negative and prior treatment with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid yielded no clinical response.

diagnostic_pivot: Slit skin smears stained by modified Ziehl-Neelsen (5% sulfuric acid) revealed characteristic acid-fast bacilli with a bacterial index of 4+, skin biopsy demonstrated foamy histiocytes positive on Fite-Faraco staining, and nerve conduction studies demonstrated thickened peripheral nerves with sensory neuropathy, confirming multibacillary lepromatous disease.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male shepherd residing in the Hodh El Gharbi region of Mauritania with no prior history of renal disease presented with acute high-grade fever, chills, severe myalgias, vomiting, and sudden loss of consciousness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of extreme hyperpyrexia (40.5 C), acute coma with a GCS of 8, and septic shock, but cerebrospinal fluid analysis was entirely normal.

Considered due to abdominal pain, jaundice, direct hyperbilirubinemia, and transaminitis in the setting of shock, but ruled out by lack of biliary signs and rapid confirmation of intraerythrocytic parasitemia.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid diagnostic antigen testing and microscopic examination of blood smears confirmed heavy Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia, explaining the severe cerebral involvement, intravascular hemolysis, and secondary acute renal failure with pulmonary edema.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old man presented for clinical evaluation of recurrent right flank pain of two years duration. Two years earlier, an abdominal ultrasound and subsequent computed tomography (CT) scan had detected an incidental right suprarenal mass.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the large suprarenal mass, but excluded by entirely normal serum cortisol, ACTH, aldosterone/renin ratio, and fractionated metanephrine and normetanephrine levels.

Considered given the large size (>8 cm) and mass effect on the kidney and liver, but excluded radiologically by lack of contrast enhancement and pathologically by a three-layered acellular laminated cyst wall devoid of neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal MRI revealed pathognomonic undulating internal membranes (water lily sign) in a non-enhancing calcified cyst, and histopathologic examination of the resected adrenal mass confirmed a three-layered fibrous capsule with a characteristic middle laminated cuticular layer diagnostic of echinococcal cyst.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old previously healthy, right-handed boy presented with a 1-month history of progressive headache of mild-to-moderate intensity. The headache was initially localized to the right side of the head before becoming holocranial and bilateral, and was associated with nausea, blurred vision, and photophobia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a large solitary intra-axial mass causing focal neurological deficits and midline shift, but definitively excluded by diffusion-weighted MRI which showed completely unrestricted diffusion within the cyst cavity, ruling out purulent material.

Considered due to progressive intracranial mass effect and papilledema in a child, but microscopic examination of the completely excised intact cyst specimen revealed no morphologic features of malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical en bloc delivery using the Dowling-Orlando technique yielded an intact unruptured 5x5 cm cyst containing clear fluid, and histopathology demonstrated a laminated acellular outer layer and inner germinal layer with attached brood capsules containing scolices, establishing primary cerebral echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old woman with a past medical history of essential hypertension and dyslipidemia was referred to the gastroenterology clinic for evaluation of chronic, non-specific abdominal pain and mild intermittent watery diarrhea of 9 months duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of chronic abdominal symptoms, immigrant status from West Africa, and granuloma formation in the colonic mucosa, but ruled out by negative acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stains.
Considered as an infectious cause of chronic diarrhea, marked peripheral eosinophilia, and colonic mucosal granulomatous inflammation, but Grocott-Gomori's methenamine silver stain was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Colonoscopy identified a sessile sigmoid polyp whose histological examination revealed submucosal granulomas containing trematode eggs with a characteristic prominent lateral spine, corroborated by positive microsomal antigen serology.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a progressively growing subcutaneous mass located in the left periumbilical region of the abdominal wall, present for approximately six months. Over recent weeks, the mass had become increasingly painful.

differentials.candidate: Subcutaneous Pyogenic Abscess / Infected Epidermal Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a painful, fluctuant, mobile subcutaneous mass with hyperemic overlying skin, but ultrasound showed a well-defined lesion with a smooth contour and avascular wall, and operative exploration confirmed an intact parasitic cyst rather than purulent suppuration.
Considered given the indolent 6-month progression of a mobile subcutaneous mass, but imaging showed a strictly fluid-filled avascular cyst and surgery demonstrated an intact cystic membrane.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration of the subcutaneous tissue demonstrated an intact cystic lesion possessing a characteristic germinative membrane, and histopathology confirmed a primary subcutaneous hydatid cyst without concurrent hepatic or pulmonary involvement.

clinical_summary: A 75-year-old male farmer from Aran va Bidgol in Isfahan province, central Iran, presented to a regional health center with multiple widespread, progressive skin lesions on his face, hands, legs, and right upper eyelid.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of ulcerative and crusted lesions in an agricultural worker with animal and soil exposure, but excluded by the indolent chronic course, absence of pain, complete lack of fever or systemic signs, and absence of bacterial pathogens.

Considered because of multiple nodular and crusted lesions on exposed extremities following farm work, but direct smears stained with Giemsa demonstrated protozoan amastigotes rather than fungal yeasts or hyphae.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of vaccinostyle smears prepared from the active borders of the skin lesions and stained with Giemsa revealed characteristic intracellular amastigote forms, and molecular PCR testing confirmed Leishmania major.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old woman residing in Haryana, North India, with a past medical history of diet-controlled diabetes mellitus for 5 years and cryptogenic chronic liver disease for 3 years, presented with a 1-month history of insidious dry cough, generalized weakness, and significant unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Intestinal or Tissue Helminthic Infection (Strongyloidiasis / Filariasis / Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the most likely etiology for severe peripheral hypereosinophilia (32%, absolute eosinophils 4,000/uL) and pulmonary symptoms, but ruled out by repeated negative stool examinations, negative antifilarial and Echinococcus serologies, and failure to respond to empiric albendazole and diethylcarbamazine.

differentials.candidate: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) / Autoimmune Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute dry cough, systemic constitutional symptoms, elevated ESR, and marked peripheral eosinophilia, but excluded by negative ANA and ANCA serologies, normal echocardiogram, and bone marrow biopsy devoid of vasculitis.

Considered because of weight loss, persistent leukocytosis with marked eosinophilia, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, but bone marrow aspiration and biopsy showed only reactive eosinophilic precursors with no neoplastic or abnormal cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli on smear, and BACTEC liquid culture subsequently grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, followed by rapid normalization of eosinophilia upon antitubercular treatment.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old Vietnamese male kidney transplant recipient presented to his outpatient nephrologist for the acute evaluation of gross hematuria. Over the preceding several weeks, he had also experienced an insidious cough productive of yellow sputum, exertional dyspnea, intermittent chills, generalized fatigue, and unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of gross hematuria, pyuria, and systemic chills in a renal transplant recipient, but urine culture failed to isolate any bacterial organism.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Bacterial or Fungal Pneumonia (Pneumocystis / Nocardia)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to productive cough, dyspnea, bilateral lung crackles, and chest CT opacities in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, but blood cultures remained negative and all symptoms resolved completely on antiparasitic therapy alone.

diagnostic_pivot: Stool wet mount microscopy directly demonstrated numerous nematode larvae characterized by a large genital primordium and short buccal capsule, confirmed by a positive Strongyloides stercoralis IgG titer (1.96 IU), diagnosing severe hyperinfection syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old right-handed female was brought to the emergency department after a sudden onset of unconsciousness lasting for 6 hours. Her family reported a 3-month history of persistent headache and intermittent vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary presumptive diagnosis based on age and an intraventricular lesion obstructing the Foramen of Monro; ruled out when total surgical excision and histopathology revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than neoplastic glial proliferation.

Considered due to the characteristic anatomical location obstructing the Foramen of Monro; excluded intraoperatively and pathologically by a firm, solid, moderately vascular mass with Langhans giant cells rather than a mucinous fluid collection with simple epithelial lining.
Considered due to homogenous contrast enhancement and T2 hypointensity; excluded by negative HIV serology and absence of malignant lymphoid infiltrates on tissue histopathology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred unexpectedly after right frontal craniotomy and transcallosal transventricular total excision of the third ventricular mass, when histopathological examination revealed epithelioid and Langhans giant cells confirming tuberculoma, leading to full recovery on antituberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male who emigrated from Mali 25 years ago presented with subcutaneous skin nodules in the periumbilical area and left lower quadrant that had been present for 5 years.

differentials.candidate: Irritable Bowel Syndrome / Functional Bowel Disorder
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of 14 years of fluctuating abdominal pain, nausea, and alternating diarrhea and constipation without systemic signs on routine CBC; ruled out because functional disorders cannot explain subcutaneous nodules or migratory linear cutaneous lesions.

Considered due to recurrent maculopapular eruptions and lack of peripheral blood eosinophilia; ruled out because the transient longitudinal morphology on the back reflected larval cutaneous migration (larva currens) and symptoms cleared completely following anthelmintic therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was identifying the combination of decades-long geographic residency risk, chronic gastrointestinal disturbance, and transient migratory linear trunk rash, confirmed by positive anti-strongyloidiasis IgG serology despite normal eosinophil counts.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old male presented to the medical emergency department with complaints of weakness and significant weight loss over 1 year. He had experienced recurrent episodes of low-grade fever over the preceding year, for which he had been treated for chronic cavitary granulomatous pulmonary infection 2 years previously.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High initial suspicion given previous pulmonary tuberculosis, chronic low-grade fever, weight loss, generalized and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and failure to improve on empiric antitubercular therapy; definitively excluded by negative Ziehl-Neelsen staining, negative PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and negative mycobacterial culture.

differentials.candidate: Hematologic Malignancy / Lymphoma or Plasma Cell Dyscrasia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to generalized and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and severe hypergammaglobulinemia with peripheral smear rouleaux; ruled out by lymph node cytology and bone marrow examination showing reactive plasmacytosis without clonal neoplastic proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was fine-needle aspiration cytology of the enlarged lymph nodes revealing epithelioid granulomas and numerous intracellular and extracellular amastigote forms, corroborated by positive rK39 antigen and bone marrow aspirate confirming visceral leishmaniasis complicated by underlying advanced HIV infection.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old male presented with a 3-day history of fever associated with chills, continuous holocranial headache, and 3 to 4 episodes of vomiting. On the third day of illness, he noted acute giddiness, difficulty sitting and standing independently requiring family support, and swaying while walking.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the explosive onset of rapid horizontal saccadic oscillations and severe truncal ataxia; ruled out as an isolated post-infectious autoimmune syndrome by the acute concurrent presence of viremic hallmarks (thrombocytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, transaminitis), lack of limb myoclonus, and normal CSF analysis.
Considered because of acute fever, headache, vomiting, and ataxia; ruled out by preserved orientation, normal brain MRI without parenchymal abnormalities, and entirely normal CSF analysis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was identifying acute parainfectious ocular flutter and ataxia occurring alongside hallmark systemic thrombocytopenia (76,000/mcL) and transaminitis, confirmed by positive serum NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by rapid steroid-responsive recovery.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old military airman deployed on an overseas mission presented to an on-site primary care field clinic with a 2-day history of nausea and vomiting. He had been stationed in temporary shelters during base construction, had engaged in outdoor operational duties with exposure to mosquito bites, and had discontinued prescribed chemoprophylaxis due to gastrointestinal side effects.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Common presumptive diagnosis for acute nausea and vomiting in military deployment camps; ruled out by the rapid clinical deterioration over the subsequent 24 to 48 hours, development of severe anemia, and positive parasite antigen testing.

Considered endemic tropical febrile illnesses with prominent gastrointestinal symptoms in deployed personnel; ruled out by rapid onset of profound acute hemolytic anemia requiring emergency blood transfusion and rapid diagnostic confirmation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was immediate point-of-care rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) identifying Plasmodium falciparum in an unprophylaxed serviceman exposed to outdoor mosquito bites, which progressed within 24 to 48 hours to severe disease requiring transfusion and antiarrhythmic management.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old male recipient of a bilateral lung transplant (performed for end-stage cystic fibrosis) presented to the hospital at week 67 post-transplantation with fever, fatigue, progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and lower extremity peripheral edema.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's acute kidney injury, fluctuating immunosuppressant drug levels, and ongoing transaminitis; ruled out as the primary cause of heart failure because calcineurin toxicity does not account for acute dilated cardiomyopathy with marked global ventricular hypokinesia following donor parasite exposure.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Myocarditis (e.g., Cytomegalovirus) / Infiltrative Cardiomyopathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's high CMV transmission risk profile (donor positive, recipient negative) and immunosuppressed status; ruled out by normal cardiac MRI without scarring or infiltration and positive surveillance serial PCR and hemoculture confirming protozoal parasitemia.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was identifying new-onset dilated cardiomyopathy in a lung transplant recipient receiving organs from an El Salvadorian donor with known cardiac disease, confirmed by recurrent positive peripheral blood PCR assays that prompted anti-trypanosomal therapy.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old right-handed male from the State of Mexico, with a history of poor hygiene and dietary habits and hypertension controlled on losartan, presented with severe headache. Two days prior to admission, he experienced an intermittent holocranial headache rated 7/10 on the visual analogue scale that was refractory to analgesics, followed by sudden worsening to 10/10 accompanied by persistent nausea...

differentials.candidate: Posterior Fossa Neoplasm (e.g., Fourth Ventricle Ependymoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis for adult-onset solitary fourth ventricular mass causing tetraventricular hydrocephalus and gait ataxia; ruled out during neuro-endoscopic exploration, which revealed a mobile, non-adherent translucent cystic vesicle rather than a solid or vascular neoplastic tumor.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Fourth Ventricular Outlet Stenosis / Ependymitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to isolated fourth ventricular dilation and symmetric hydrocephalus; ruled out when endoscopic inspection revealed completely normal ependymal lining without ependymitis and confirmed patent fourth ventricular exits (foramina of Luschka, aqueduct, and obex) once the cyst was extracted.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was urgent transcerebellar rigid neuro-endoscopy entering the fourth ventricle, which visualized and completely excised an intact, non-adherent cystic lesion (cysticercus vesicle) that immediately restored normal CSF dynamics, followed by postoperative albendazole therapy.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old male with a medical history of chronic renal failure, chronic heart failure, and alcohol-related cirrhosis was admitted to the hospital with fever, abdominal pain, and an actively draining cutaneous fistula in the right flank discharging copious purulent secretion.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pyogenic Soft-Tissue Abscess / Cutaneous Fistula
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initial clinical diagnosis based on the right-flank purulent drainage and ultrasound finding of a subcutaneous collection; ruled out by cross-sectional MRI and fistulography showing the fluid tract extending deep through the right iliac muscle into an intrahepatic cavity.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pyogenic Liver Abscess with Spontaneous Rupture
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a cirrhotic patient presenting with bacterial superinfection (Pseudomonas and Klebsiella) draining purulent fluid; ruled out because the origin was not a de novo pyogenic abscess but an ancient, heavily calcified parasitic cystic cavity that had become secondarily colonized.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was CT-fistulography performed by catheterizing the cutaneous flank opening with water-soluble contrast, which demonstrated continuous opacification of the tract ascending through the iliac muscle directly into the pre-existing calcified hepatic cyst, proving bacterial superinfection of a dead hydatid lesion.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old male presented with a 1-year history of mild, gradually worsening abdominal distention and pain localized predominantly to the right upper abdomen. The symptoms were unrelated to food intake, and he reported no history of fever, weight loss, previous surgeries, or significant medical conditions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of multifocal masses involving both the liver and the pelvic ileal mesentery; ruled out by entirely normal inflammatory markers, lack of constitutional symptoms or primary mucosal tumor, and absence of malignant cells on histopathology.

Considered due to the well-circumscribed, cystic lesion compressing the urinary bladder in a young adult; ruled out by concurrent presence of a large calcified hepatic lesion with daughter cysts and positive zoonotic serology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was combining the patient's rural canine contact with CT findings of a calcified multi-vesicular hepatic cyst and mesenteric lesions, confirmed by positive anti-Echinococcus ELISA IgG serology and intraoperative extraction of characteristic lamellated ectocysts and daughter cysts.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old female clothing stall vendor presented to a pulmonary clinic with progressive cough, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and low-grade fever. She was being concurrently evaluated for a suspected thyroid adenoma.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary clinical suspicion given progressive cough, hemoptysis, subacute fever, and diffuse miliary opacities on chest radiography in Southeast Asia; ruled out by negative Ziehl-Neelsen microscopic examinations and absence of mycobacterial growth on Lowenstein-Jensen culture media.

Considered because the patient had an enlarging thyroid neck lump subsequently confirmed as papillary thyroid carcinoma, which can metastasize hematogenously to pulmonary parenchyma as miliary nodules; ruled out as the cause of acute pulmonary decline by sputum isolation of a dimorphic fungus and clinical improvement following antifungal therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was routine sputum culture on Sabouraud's dextrose agar at 25°C demonstrating a mold with green mycelia that secreted a characteristic soluble red-brown pigment into the agar, exhibiting thermal dimorphism at 37°C, with definitive species identification confirmed by 18S rRNA gene sequencing.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female presented to the hospital with a 1-week history of progressively worsening shortness of breath. For over two months prior, she experienced a persistent nonproductive cough, nocturnal fevers, significant involuntary weight loss, generalized joint pains, and fatigue.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute cough, diffuse interstitial opacities, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, but the patient had no history of immunodeficiency and repeat rapid testing was negative.

Considered among atypical causes of diffuse miliary lung infiltrates and acute deterioration, prompting empirical antiviral and antifungal coverage, but definitive molecular testing proved another pathogen.

Considered given the diffuse micronodular pattern on imaging and profound constitutional weight loss in a young patient, but the acute febrile deterioration, leukocytosis, and microbiological findings refuted neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Endotracheal sputum molecular nucleic acid amplification confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis without rifampin resistance, confirming acute fulminant miliary dissemination.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a 3-month history of progressive dyspnea, cough, low-grade fever, and chills. On physical examination, she was hemodynamically stable.

differentials.candidate: Massive pleural effusion or chronic empyema
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given 3 months of fever, chills, cough, percussion dullness, and a completely opacified hemithorax on plain radiography, but cross-sectional CT revealed well-encapsulated multi-cystic structures rather than diffuse loculated pleural fluid.

differentials.candidate: Pleural neoplasm (e.g., malignant mesothelioma or pleural sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a patient with chronic respiratory symptoms and hemithoracic opacification, but the CT appearance showed non-invasive cystic collections and surgical exploration confirmed benign cystic architecture without malignant soft-tissue infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: Right posterolateral thoracotomy directly demonstrated a large primary pleural hydatid cyst containing numerous daughter cysts, which were excised and irrigated with scolicidal hypertonic saline.

clinical_summary: In August 2016, a 78-year-old man residing in the San Juan metropolitan area presented to a hospital emergency department with a 4-day history of progressive bilateral paresthesia and weakness affecting both the upper and lower extremities.

differentials.candidate: Acute ischemic stroke or intracranial lesion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered upon initial presentation of progressive limb weakness, but non-contrast cranial CT demonstrated no acute pathology, and subsequent examination revealed symmetric quadriparesis with generalized areflexia rather than upper motor neuron signs.

differentials.candidate: Classic bacterial or viral antecedents of Guillain-Barré syndrome (e.g., Campylobacter jejuni, Mycoplasma, CMV, EBV, HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as conventional triggers of post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy, but exhaustive diagnostic screening for all classical enteric, respiratory, and viral pathogens returned negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Urine reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) detected Zika virus RNA, and serum testing confirmed Zika virus IgM antibodies in a patient with Brighton Level 2 criteria for Guillain-Barré syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old girl presented to a pediatric nephrology and hypertension clinic with a 3-month history of painless, waxing and waning gross hematuria. The urine varied between reddish and tea-colored, with blood present throughout the entire urinary stream.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute painless tea-colored hematuria, but the patient had normal blood pressure, no edema, no preceding skin or pharyngeal infection, and kidney biopsy confirmed normal parenchyma with negative immunofluorescence.
Empirically treated by a general practitioner, but excluded based on persistent waxing and waning gross hematuria lacking dysuria, urgency, foul odor, or fevers.
Considered as a mechanical cause of gross hematuria, but the child lacked flank colic or stone passage, and ultrasound revealed only bladder debris without calculi.

diagnostic_pivot: Centrifuged manual urine sediment microscopy directly identified characteristic parasite eggs of S. haematobium after eliciting a history of travel to an endemic area.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old man presented to the hospital with a 2-day history of right lower quadrant abdominal pain, progressive abdominal distension, and obstipation. He also reported moderate-to-high-grade fevers associated with chills and rigors.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected based on the prominent 12-13 cm circumferential mural thickening with fat stranding and luminal obstruction on CT, but histopathologic examination of the resected specimen and 13 isolated regional lymph nodes demonstrated absence of malignancy.

Considered due to acute fever, leukocytosis, and a tender right lower quadrant mass, but CT revealed extensive colonic involvement up to the hepatic flexure rather than an isolated periappendiceal collection.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency right hemicolectomy specimen histopathology revealed transmural flask-shaped ulcerations in the cecal mucosa packed with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old woman presented to the gynecology clinic for evaluation of postmenopausal vaginal bleeding. She had no documented history of contact with individuals diagnosed with chronic pulmonary infections or unexplained chronic cough, and reported no constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The cardinal initial clinical suspicion in an elderly woman presenting with postmenopausal uterine bleeding and endometrial thickening, but histopathological evaluation of the endometrial biopsy specimen revealed no evidence of malignant neoplasia.

differentials.candidate: Benign endometrial polyps or hyperplasia alone
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although benign endometrial polyps were identified histologically, the coexisting granulomatous endometritis indicated an infectious granulomatous process rather than simple benign proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Liquid mycobacterial culture of the endometrial biopsy specimen using MGIT medium was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, confirmed by conventional biochemical tests and PCR-RFLP.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old woman residing in São Paulo, Brazil, presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of acute fever, headache, generalized cutaneous rash, arthralgia, and marked prostration. Her past medical history was notable for an absence of prior vaccination against measles or rubella.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to acute fever, maculopapular rash, arthralgia, and unvaccinated status, but specific serum IgM and IgG were negative and urine RT-qPCR was negative.
Considered due to the acute rash, fever, and lack of immunization, but excluded by negative serum antibodies and negative RT-qPCR.
Investigated as causes of acute febrile illness with rash and arthropathy, but molecular testing by RT-qPCR was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Urine RT-qPCR was positive for Zika virus RNA, and viral isolation from urine in SIRC and Vero cell cultures demonstrated cytopathic effect and viable, replicating Zika virus.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old man from Southwest Iran presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of continuous, generalized throbbing headaches, persistent fever, chills, progressive weakness, anorexia, and involuntary weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, headache, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and endemic geographic exposure in Iran, but Wright agglutination and 2-mercaptoethanol (2ME) tests were negative.

differentials.candidate: Viral hepatitis or HIV-associated portal hypertension
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to hepatosplenomegaly, dilated splanchnic/portal veins, and cytopenias, but specific viral serologies were entirely non-reactive.

Considered due to profound pancytopenia, marked hyperferritinemia, transaminitis, and splenomegaly, but bone marrow evaluation demonstrated infectious amastigotes rather than malignant neoplastic infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy definitively identified numerous intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within macrophages, confirming visceral leishmaniasis with atypical central nervous system parenchymal (pontine) involvement seen on subsequent FLAIR MRI.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old previously healthy man presented to the emergency department and was admitted to the intensive care unit with acute high fever (39.5°C / 103.1°F), persistent generalized muscular pain, and ascending paresthesias originating in his feet and progressing proximally.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of high-grade fever, severe persistent muscular pain, and weakness leading to a fall, but excluded by a completely normal serum creatine kinase level.

differentials.candidate: Acute central nervous system infection (e.g., Herpes, Varicella, Toxoplasmosis, HIV) or bacterial sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, speech difficulty, rapid neurologic deterioration, and pulmonary infiltrates, but comprehensive serologic panels and blood cultures were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Specific serology was positive for Zika virus IgG antibodies, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrated classic albuminocytological dissociation (protein 191 mg/dL with normal leukocyte count) establishing Zika-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old Eritrean woman with a known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presented to the emergency department with progressive generalized weakness, generalized lymphadenopathy, and a rapidly expanding mass involving the right breast.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected on initial admission due to constitutional weakness and extensive cervical, axillary, retropectoral, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, but cervical lymph node biopsy was negative for neoplastic lymphoid proliferation.

Considered given her family history of fatal young-onset breast cancer and a massive breast lesion with axillary adenopathy, but mammography and ultrasonography excluded a solid tumor, and fluid cytology showed no malignant cells.
Initially managed as a bacterial infection, but lacked heat, erythema, and acute pain ("cold abscess"), failed empiric antibiotics, and aspirate cultures were negative for bacteria and fungi.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of a colliquated cervical lymph node core biopsy revealed caseating granulomas with central necrosis, and molecular testing by nucleic acid amplification and PCR confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old male presented for evaluation after an abnormal screening chest radiograph. He was completely asymptomatic, without dyspnea, chest discomfort, palpitations, or systemic symptoms, and had a noncontributory past medical history.

differentials.candidate: Primary Cardiac Neoplasm (e.g., Myxoma, Fibroma, or Sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary cardiac neoplasms typically present with solid tissue architecture and enhancement on contrast-enhanced imaging; the purely cystic, non-enhancing nature of this mass localized within myocardial fibers rules them out.
Congenital pericardial or bronchogenic cysts are typically located in the mediastinum or cardiophrenic angles rather than deeply embedded within the ventricular myocardium.

Pseudoaneurysms demonstrate internal contrast opacification communicating with the left ventricular cavity and usually follow myocardial infarction or trauma; this lesion was completely non-enhancing and smooth-surfaced.

diagnostic_pivot: Left anterolateral thoracotomy and pericardial reflection directly exposed the intramyocardial mass containing classic pale yellow daughter cysts and scolices, which were inactivated with povidone-iodine and evacuated, definitively proving an intramyocardial hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old Asian Indian female presented with sudden blurring of vision in the left eye of 1 week duration. Her medical history was notable for chronic cervical lymphadenopathy under ongoing medical therapy for the past 3 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Choroidal melanoma typically presents as a mushroom-shaped or dome-shaped mass displaying high internal optical reflectivity and lacks vitreous cellular inflammation; the homogeneous hyporeflectivity on SS-OCT and vitritis rule it out.
Choroidal hemangiomas are vascular reddish-orange lesions that demonstrate high optical and acoustic reflectivity without associated vitreous cells or inflammatory exudates.
Choroidal metastases usually present as multifocal, placoid, diffuse lesions in patients with known primary carcinoma, rather than an isolated solitary lobulated subretinal granulomatous mass.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic analysis of her cervical lymph node demonstrating necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli, combined with characteristic SS-OCT hyporeflective choroidal thickening and regression under anti-tubercular therapy and corticosteroids, established choroidal tuberculoma.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old Chinese woman from Wuhan was admitted with a 6-month history of left quadrant abdominal pain and weight loss. The pain worsened after meals and was accompanied by abdominal distension, belching, and decreased flatus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Crohn's disease can cause small-bowel ulceration, stricture, and mesenteric inflammation, but it does not account for the characteristic pattern of hepatic periportal fibrosis and lobar remodeling, and was excluded by histopathologic identification of parasite ova.

differentials.candidate: Primary Jejunal Adenocarcinoma or Intestinal Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: An obstructive jejunal mass with weight loss in an elderly patient raises strong suspicion for malignant neoplasm; ruled out by enteroscopy and biopsy showing chronic granulomatous inflammation without atypical malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of jejunal mucosal biopsies demonstrated chronic ulcerative inflammation with deposition of classic Schistosoma japonicum eggs, confirming intestinal and hepatic schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old woman residing in a rural village in Beja, northwestern Tunisia, presented with recurrent episodes of right upper quadrant biliary colic over a 2-month period. She had a history of dyslipidemia with no prior surgical interventions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical presentation, benign exam, and ultrasound showing a single 10 mm stone are identical to typical cholesterol/pigment cholelithiasis; however, routine cholelithiasis does not explain the chronic intramural granulomatous parasitic infestation detected on resection.

differentials.candidate: Gallbladder Malignancy or Chronic Acalculous Cholecystitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Ruled out by normal inflammatory markers, normal hepatic biochemistry, completely thin gallbladder wall on ultrasound, and absence of neoplastic proliferation on pathology.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the resected gallbladder revealed chronic mucosal inflammation, fibrosis, lymphocytic infiltration of the chorion, and calcified schistosomal ova staining positively with periodic acid-Schiff, establishing gallbladder schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male with no significant prior medical comorbidities presented for evaluation of chronic, progressive, and severe cutaneous lesions affecting both hands. For nearly three years, the patient had been managed under a presumptive diagnosis of severe psoriasis and had received ongoing topical and systemic corticosteroid treatments.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Psoriasis was the initial working diagnosis for nearly three years; however, prolonged corticosteroid administration failed to control the condition and instead permitted catastrophic progression, indicating a non-autoimmune etiology.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous Verrucous Carcinoma or Squamous Cell Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: The massive, debilitating hyperkeratotic growth causing complete loss of hand function raised suspicion for malignant proliferative neoplasia; ruled out by parasitologic confirmation of mite infestation rather than invasive malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Extensive surgical debulking and microscopic examination revealed teeming Sarcoptes scabiei mites, identifying Norwegian (crusted) scabies that had been severely exacerbated by corticosteroid misuse and was successfully eradicated with debulking and antiparasitic therapy.

clinical_summary: A male patient was admitted to the inpatient ward for systemic bacteremia, and a plastic surgery consultation was requested to evaluate severe, progressive hand lesions. The cutaneous condition had worsened over a three-year interval following an initial evaluation, during which he had been lost to specialty follow-up.

differentials.candidate: Giant Verrucous Carcinoma / Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: The massive, progressive 12 × 15 cm tissue proliferation causing structural destruction and loss of hand function closely mimicked a malignant verrucous neoplasm; ruled out by histopathology showing mite infestation without malignant cytology.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Deep Mycobacterial or Fungal Soft-Tissue Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the concurrent bacteremia and severe vegetative plaques, deep fungal or atypical mycobacterial infectious dermatoses were considered; ruled out by pathology confirming ectoparasitic infestation.

diagnostic_pivot: The patient underwent tangential excisional debridement of a 12 × 15 cm area on the right hand, with histopathological analysis demonstrating overwhelming Sarcoptes scabiei mite burden consistent with Norwegian scabies, subsequently treated with oral ivermectin and permethrin cream.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old female presented with a 6-month history of progressive weakness in both lower extremities, sensory disturbance, and sphincter dysfunction. Her symptoms had rapidly worsened over preceding weeks, resulting in complete inability to walk.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Spinal arachnoid cysts typically occur as solitary, isolated fluid collections without severe secondary arachnoiditis, rather than numerous distinct clustered cystic vesicles at multiple discontinuous spinal levels.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Schwannoma or Meningioma with Cystic Degeneration
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary intradural extramedullary neoplasms are typically solitary contrast-enhancing solid tumors with occasional cystic degeneration; multicentric purely cystic lesions at T4-6 and T9-11 are inconsistent with typical nerve sheath tumors.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical laminectomy revealed 12 cystic lesions protruding through the arachnoid gap at T4-T6 and severe arachnoiditis at T9-T11, with histopathological examination definitively confirming spinal neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old Caucasian female with an active 25 pack-year smoking history was followed in the pulmonary clinic for chronic intermittent rhinitis and surveillance of a stable 6 mm nodule in the right upper lobe.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Organizing pneumonia is the classical and most frequent etiology of the reversed halo sign, and empiric corticosteroids were initially planned; however, invasive sampling identified active mycobacterial infection, excluding COP.

A new, rapidly expanding 36 mm pulmonary mass in an active heavy smoker was highly concerning for malignancy; ruled out by normal tumor markers, cytology, and biopsy revealing necrotic tissue without neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchial secretions collected during bronchofibroscopy demonstrated Mycobacterium tuberculosis susceptible to all first-line drugs, confirming active pulmonary tuberculosis as the etiology of the mass presenting with the reversed halo sign.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old woman was hospitalized with progressive dyspnea and cough. She had emigrated from Venezuela to Germany one year prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed based on non-necrotizing interstitial granulomas and elevated serum IL-2 receptor; ruled out when high-dose corticosteroid therapy failed to improve imaging and instead precipitated acute respiratory failure, with re-biopsy revealing fungal yeast structures.

Initial histopathologic stains showed small intracellular yeasts suggestive of Histoplasma; however, complement fixation was negative, Histoplasma-specific qPCR was negative, and deeper histological sections revealed multi-budded yeasts.

A black exophytic mass invading the left main bronchus raised concern for malignant or neuroendocrine airway neoplasm; ruled out by histology demonstrating granulomatous inflammatory changes with fungal elements and complete resolution on antifungal therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Broad-range fungal PCR amplicons sequenced from formalin-fixed lung tissue demonstrated 99.7% pairwise identity with Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, confirmed by specific immunodiffusion antibodies and identification of multi-budded yeasts.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old female child was referred for specialized consultation due to acute, progressive swelling of the face, cheeks, and ears. Her medical history was significant for a chronic dermatologic condition characterized by multiple cutaneous patches on her face and suprascapular region, for which a standardized multidrug therapeutic regimen had been initiated three months earlier at a primary healthcare facility.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Facial and malar erythema in an adolescent female with anemia, leukocytosis, and high ESR can mimic lupus erythematosus; ruled out by involvement of earlobes, lack of systemic constitutional signs, and acute reactivation occurring directly within preexisting chronic patches.

Type-2 reactions typically present with crops of painful, tender subcutaneous nodules accompanied by high spiking fever and systemic toxicity; this patient had no fever and exhibited acute edema and erythema exclusively within preexisting chronic lesions.

Facial and ear swelling can suggest allergic angioedema or soft tissue bacterial infection; ruled out by lack of acute pruritus, lack of fever/warmth, and confinement of inflammation to preexisting chronic plaques.

diagnostic_pivot: The acute onset of inflammatory erythema and swelling localized specifically within preexisting facial and suprascapular lesions following three months of multidrug antimycobacterial therapy established a Type-1 (reversal) leprosy reaction, confirmed by rapid response to prednisolone.

clinical_summary: A 14-month-old boy with a history of Down syndrome, surgically corrected tetralogy of Fallot, generalized epilepsy, and failure to thrive presents for medical evaluation due to unsuccessful treatment of pneumonia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although initial screening showed cross-reactive IgG antibodies against both larval cestode species, repeat serologic testing demonstrated negative E. granulosus antibodies, excluding hydatid disease.

Given the patient's congenital heart disease and unresponsive pneumonia, a septic splenic focus was considered, but the lesion was an incidental, small stable cyst with normal hepatic enzymes rather than an acute infectious collection.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmatory Western blot specifically demonstrated positive IgG antibodies against Echinococcus multilocularis, establishing the definitive diagnosis of primary alveolar echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old girl (height 120 cm, weight 21 kg) presents to the emergency room with acute abdominal pain, vomiting, and a fever of 38°C. On initial emergency assessment, an abdominal ultrasound is performed, which demonstrates two well-defined cystic lesions measuring 2.3 cm and 1.8 cm containing transparent fluid in hepatic segments 7/8, and a single 1.0 cm cyst in segment...

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or Amoebic Liver Abscess with Mesenteric Lymphadenitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy strongly raised concern for acute bacterial or amoebic suppuration, but ultrasound demonstrated well-circumscribed cysts containing clear, transparent fluid rather than thick inflammatory pus, and hepatic enzymes remained normal.

Borderline seropositivity for E. multilocularis initially impeded definitive categorization, but the cyst morphology lacked infiltrative necrotic features and repeat serology was non-confirmatory for alveolar disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Hepatic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple distinct cystic lesions with typical septa across liver segments, and repeat serology confirmed high-titer Echinococcus granulosus IgG antibodies, establishing the diagnosis of cystic echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male residing in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, with a history of alcohol and cocaine abuse presents with progressive ulcerated lesions of the upper respiratory tract and genitalia. The condition began one year prior as erythematous, painful papules that progressively enlarged.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Endemic dimorphic fungal infection is a leading cause of chronic destructive mucosal granulomas in South America, but fungal serological panels, direct mycological examination, and histopathology were negative for fungal yeast forms.

Severe necrotizing palatal and septal destruction, especially in a cocaine user, closely mimics vasculitic necrosis or neoplastic infiltration; however, systemic autoimmune and malignant workup was negative, and chest tomography was normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of laryngeal and nasal mucosa demonstrated a chronic inflammatory infiltrate with macrophages containing cytoplasmic amastigote-like forms, accompanied by positive specific serology and confirmatory PCR.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male presents to the emergency department with high-grade fever and chills of 3 months' duration, accompanied by cough productive of occasional brownish-red sputum for the past month, and worsening headache with progressive drowsiness over the last 2 days.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Abscess (Hepatic and Metastatic Intracranial)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial sepsis with metastatic cerebritis was the primary initial consideration given severe leukocytosis and ruptured liver abscess; however, blood and urine cultures were sterile, and drained purulent fluid was negative on Gram stain and bacterial cultures.
Prolonged 3-month constitutional symptoms, pulmonary consolidation, and organ space collections raised strong suspicion for tuberculosis, but molecular testing of abscess fluid was negative.

differentials.candidate: Primary Brain Tumor or Metastatic Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapidly deteriorating sensorium and ring-enhancing brain lesions raised concern for malignancy, but cytologic examination of liver aspirate showed no malignant cells and neurosurgical exploration revealed organized purulent collections.

diagnostic_pivot: Aspiration yielded classic anchovy sauce-like purulent fluid, and serum ELISA testing for Entamoeba histolytica IgG returned strongly positive, confirming invasive extraintestinal amebiasis with metastatic cerebral lesions.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old male who underwent rectal stump excision and ileal pouch-anal anastomosis 6 days previously presents with acute deterioration on postoperative day 7. His immediate postoperative course was complicated on day 2 by transient fever, tachycardia, and hypoxemia, which resolved with supportive care after CT pulmonary angiography was negative for pulmonary embolism (showing bilateral basal atelectasis/consolidation).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Postoperative respiratory distress, tachycardia, and hypoxia raised high suspicion for pulmonary thromboembolism; however, CT pulmonary angiography excluded vascular occlusion.

differentials.candidate: Postoperative Intra-abdominal Sepsis or Anastomotic Leak
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute drain-site hemorrhage, respiratory failure, and free peritoneal fluid mimicked an anastomotic dehiscence or surgical hematoma; however, the abdomen was soft and non-tender, the ileostomy functioned normally, and extreme hemoconcentration (hematocrit 67.8%) indicated systemic vascular hyperpermeability rather than localized surgical sepsis.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of profound plasma leakage (massive pleural effusions and ascites with hematocrit 67.8%), critical defervescence, severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 9 x 10^9/L), and positive dengue IgM and IgG serology confirmed dengue hemorrhagic fever.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old female, mother of three from eastern Bhutan, presents to the dermatology clinic for evaluation of chronic, progressive facial lesions and ocular impairment. Fifteen years prior, during pregnancy, she experienced a prolonged severe febrile illness accompanied by hepatomegaly and severe anemia that required blood transfusions and an antimonial regimen.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus (CLE) or Chronic Dermatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Symmetrical erythematous centrofacial plaques and scarring in a woman of childbearing age led to a prolonged clinical suspicion of cutaneous lupus or chronic dermatitis, but the lesions were refractory to topical, intralesional, and systemic corticosteroids.

Chronic infiltrative facial plaques with destruction of eyebrows/eyelids, lagophthalmos, and mucosal extension can mimic lepromatous leprosy or tertiary syphilis; however, syphilis serology was negative and microscopic slit-skin smears demonstrated protozoan LD bodies rather than acid-fast bacilli.

diagnostic_pivot: Slit-skin smear stained with Giemsa identified abundant Leishman-Donovan (LD) bodies, confirmed by positive rK-39 rapid dipstick testing and histopathology revealing lymphohistiocytic granulomas with intracellular amastigotes, proving post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A three-month-old infant boy with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency department with acute onset of ischemia and discoloration of the left foot evolving over 12 hours.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute acral ischemia and digital gangrene in an infant immediately suggested acute arterial thrombosis or embolus; however, peripheral pulses were intact across all four limbs and Doppler ultrasound showed no intraluminal thrombus.

differentials.candidate: Primary Autoimmune Vasculitis (e.g., Henoch-Schönlein Purpura or Polyarteritis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cutaneous vasculitic features with digit necrosis suggested a primary immune-complex-mediated vasculitis; however, immunofluorescence demonstrated an absence of perivascular IgG, IgM, IgA, or C3 deposits, confirming a reactive cell-mediated lymphocytic vasculitis.

differentials.candidate: Primary Staphylococcal Pyoderma or Ecthyma Gangrenosum
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pustular lesions prompted skin swabbing which isolated methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, but secondary bacterial colonization did not account for the extensive non-thrombotic lymphocytic microvascular necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical finding of an intensely pruritic, diffuse papular eruption coupled with household epidemiological clustering (both parents suffering from severe generalized scratching) confirmed primary scabies infestation complicated by reactive lymphocytic microvasculopathy.

clinical_summary: An infant is evaluated for acute acral ischemia and evolving cyanosis involving the lower extremity digits in the setting of concurrent skin lesions. Contrast CT-angiography of the abdomen and lower extremities is performed and demonstrates normal patent vasculature without evidence of arterial thrombosis or occlusion.

differentials.candidate: Inherited or Acquired Thrombophilia / Deep Vein Thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe acute digital ischemia and thrombocytosis raised high suspicion for hypercoagulability or venous/arterial thromboembolism; however, CT-angiography was normal and functional coagulation inhibitor levels were completely within normal limits.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Autoimmune Vasculitis or Antiphospholipid Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: High inflammatory markers with digital necrosis and weakly positive speckled ANA raised concern for systemic lupus, ANCA-associated vasculitis, or antiphospholipid syndrome; however, specific antibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-Ro/La, anti-RNP, p-ANCA, c-ANCA, anti-cardiolipin, anti-beta-2-glycoprotein 1, lupus anticoagulant) and cryoglobulins were negative.
Acral purpura, gangrene, and cold-sensitive cyanosis are classic for mixed or monoclonal cryoglobulinemia; however, serum testing for cryoglobulins was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Following targeted antiscabetic therapy, the cutaneous lesions completely healed within two weeks with concurrent resolution of inflammatory biomarkers (CRP dropping to 17.1 mg/L), confirming that the reactive microvascular ischemia was secondary to scabies.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old previously healthy woman presents with progressive paraplegia and lower extremity numbness evolving over the past 2 months without antecedent trauma. Neurological examination reveals bilateral lower extremity motor weakness (American Spinal Injury Impairment Scale grade C) and severe hypalgesia and paresthesias at the T6-T7 dermatomal level.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive osteolytic vertebral collapse without systemic inflammatory signs in an elderly patient strongly suggested spinal metastasis; PET-CT and aspiration cytology demonstrated papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid, initially prompting a misdiagnosis of spinal metastasis, but spinal surgical pathology showed inflammatory infiltrates without malignant cells.

Acute pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis/discitis typically presents with fever, leukocytosis, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers, whereas this patient was afebrile with normal leukocytes and normal CRP.

diagnostic_pivot: Upon recurrence 9 months later with progressive osteolysis and a right pulmonary coin lesion, CT-guided needle biopsy and tissue culture definitively isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming spinal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old female presents to an outpatient clinic in Kathmandu, Nepal, with a 2-day history of loose, watery diarrhea occurring 4 to 5 times per day. The diarrhea is associated with abdominal bloating, prominent abdominal gurgling sounds, one transient episode of self-resolving fever the day prior to presentation, and a single episode of vomiting on the day of arrival.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile watery diarrhea in a traveler with poor hand hygiene strongly suggested acute bacterial gastroenteritis; however, macroscopic and microscopic stool examinations revealed no fecal leukocytes or erythrocytes, and systemic C-reactive protein was negative.

Watery diarrhea with abdominal bloating and borborygmi is classic for Giardia or Entamoeba infection, but wet mount and concentration microscopy did not reveal flagellates, amoebic trophozoites, or protozoal cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct wet mount and formol-ether concentration stool microscopy identified abundant clear, pale-yellow eggs measuring 60-65 μm by 50-55 μm with a characteristic lateral knob, confirmed by the national reference laboratory as Schistosoma japonicum.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old man native to Gabon and residing in the Noya region presented to the hospital with a severe and violent headache associated with a high fever of 39 °C.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe cerebral malaria was a prime consideration given the acute febrile encephalopathy, high fever, severe anemia, and residency in an endemic region of Gabon, but rapid and microscopic diagnostic testing was non-reactive.

differentials.candidate: Neurosyphilis / HIV-associated Central Nervous System Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic subacute meningoencephalitis with cachexia, motor deficits, and inflammatory markers raised concern for neurosyphilis or opportunistic infections secondary to retroviral disease, but serological evaluations were negative.
