High fever, meningeal syndrome, leukocytosis, and profound CRP elevation mimicked acute bacterial meningoencephalitis, but the presence of prominent abdominal scratching lesions, severe cachexia, and basal ganglia CT hypodensities prompted parasitic investigation rather than revealing pyogenic CSF changes.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic analysis of fluid aspirated from an enlarged lymph node ganglion demonstrated extracellular trypanosomes, followed by lumbar puncture confirming stage 2 central nervous system disease with clear CSF, pleocytosis (27/mm³), and trypanosomes.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old female non-smoker with a history of chronic sinusitis since age 12, purulent sputum production since age 20, and a prior thoracotomy drainage for empyema presented with progressive cough, expectoration, chest tightness, and wheezing.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Sputum and initial bronchoalveolar lavage cultures yielded Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a well-recognized secondary colonizer in damaged airways, but this failed to explain the new focal apical pulmonary nodule appearing after prolonged steroid therapy.

Prolonged corticosteroid use placed the patient at high risk for opportunistic fungal infections, and lavage culture yielded low-level Fusarium growth; however, this was insufficient to explain the primary pathology without specific histological or molecular confirmation.
Connective tissue diseases and ANCA-associated vasculitis can present with recurrent sinobronchial disease and pulmonary nodules, but rheumatological and immunologic serologic testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat bronchoalveolar lavage fluid smear revealed acid-fast bacilli (1 root/300 visual fields) and confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex group DNA, establishing secondary pulmonary tuberculosis following long-term immunosuppressive steroid therapy.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male with no previous medical comorbidities presented to an emergency hospital in Goiás State, Brazil, with high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, and diffuse myalgias. He received intravenous hydration and was discharged home for supportive care.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Autoimmune Vasculitis / Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden emergence of lower extremity purpuric lesions, severe serositis with pericardial tamponade, and transaminitis strongly suggested acute systemic autoimmune vasculitis or SLE, but autoantibody and complement panels were entirely normal.

Exudative pericardial effusion, high neutrophil predominance in pericardial fluid, and pulmonary infiltrates prompted empiric therapy with ceftriaxone and oxacillin, but microbiological testing showed no bacterial growth.

differentials.candidate: Viral Carditis (Cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr Virus, HIV, Hepatitis B/C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cardiotropic and systemic viruses known to cause myopericarditis and reactive rashes were evaluated serologically, but active infection was excluded.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat immunochromatographic testing on day 10 demonstrated clear seroconversion with positive IgM and IgG antibodies following an acute illness characterized by retro-orbital pain, severe thrombocytopenia, capillary leakage/pericardial effusion, and biopsy-proven leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old male farmer and active smoker residing in a village in Fars Province, Southern Iran, presented to the pulmonary clinic for further evaluation of abnormal thoracic imaging. He had a history of regular contact with domestic animals in his village.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Bronchogenic Cyst / Foregut Duplication Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral discrete, thin-walled pulmonary cysts in an otherwise asymptomatic adult without eosinophilia frequently mimic congenital bronchogenic cysts, but surgical resection demonstrated a multilayered parasitic wall rather than respiratory ciliated epithelium.

Although histopathologic staining identified Aspergillus hyphae, the primary architecture of the cavitary lesion was a true parasitic ectocyst, confirming secondary fungal colonization of a preexisting hydatid cyst rather than an isolated fungal mass in a preexisting non-parasitic cavity.

differentials.candidate: Hepatic Hydatid Disease with Transdiaphragmatic Extension
differentials.rule_out_reason: Hydatid disease most commonly affects the liver, with secondary pulmonary involvement occurring via the bloodstream or transdiaphragmatic rupture; however, abdominal ultrasonography showed no cysts in the liver or other organs.

diagnostic_pivot: Gross examination and histopathological staining of the excised surgical specimen revealed a well-defined, multilayered creamy-white cyst wall characteristic of an echinococcal ectocyst with surrounding granulomatous giant-cell reaction, confirming pulmonary hydatid cyst coinfected with Aspergillus.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old green-grocer, native to Assam, India, presented with a 10-month history of intractable hiccups associated with low-grade fever, abdominal bloating, and progressive weight loss. He had a medical history of chronic diabetes mellitus, active tobacco smoking, and chronic alcohol consumption.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In South Asia, chronic indolent fever, weight loss, and multifocal splenic hypoechoic lesions in an immunocompromised host most often suggest splenic tuberculosis, but aspirate smear and culture demonstrated characteristic Gram-negative bacilli rather than acid-fast bacilli.

Indolent constitutional symptoms including weight loss accompanied by splenomegaly and multiple focal splenic lesions raised clinical suspicion for a lymphoproliferative malignancy, but restricted diffusion on MRI and fine-needle aspiration of purulent material established an infectious abscess.

Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus predisposes to common pyogenic splenic abscesses, but the specific morphological clustered appearance ('necklace sign') and microbiological identification excluded enteric and staphylococcal pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration yielded frank pus that grew Gram-negative bacilli with a safety-pin appearance on Gram stain and metallic sheen on MacConkey agar, identified by automated system as Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming splenic melioidosis as the cause of diaphragmatic irritation and hiccups.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male from Tamil Nadu, India, presented with a 2-week history of fever and acute onset of abdominal pain for 4 days. He had a medical history of chronic diabetes mellitus and hypertension, for which he was noncompliant with medications.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with peripancreatic fat stranding mimicked typical acute pancreatitis, but serum amylase and lipase levels were completely normal, directing suspicion toward an infectious inflammatory phlegmon.

Focal enlargement of the pancreatic body and tail with contiguous splenic vein occlusion and collaterals in an older diabetic patient strongly suggested pancreatic malignancy, but the absence of a distinct mass or ductal dilation and the presence of high fevers favored an acute infectious process.

differentials.candidate: Primary Splanchnic Vein Thrombosis / Hypercoagulable State
differentials.rule_out_reason: Isolated splenic vein thrombosis can occur spontaneously in thrombophilic states, but the localized peripancreatic phlegmon and systemic fever demonstrated that the thrombosis was secondary to septic thrombophlebitis.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood cultures drawn on admission revealed Gram-negative bacilli exhibiting characteristic bipolar 'safety-pin' Gram staining and metallic sheen colonies on MacConkey agar, identified by the VITEK2 automated system as Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming pancreatic melioidosis complicated by acute septic splenic vein thrombosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old previously healthy male presented to the hospital complaining of progressive left-sided pleuritic chest pain lasting several weeks. He noted two large swellings on the front of his chest that had been slowly increasing in size over four months at the exact site of his pain.

differentials.candidate: Primary Chest Wall / Rib Malignancy (Chondrosarcoma, Osteosarcoma, Ewing Sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The combination of painless, slowly enlarging anterior chest wall masses with cortical rib osteolysis and significant weight loss in a young male strongly mimicked an osseous or soft tissue chest wall malignancy, but imaging demonstrated cystic collections rather than solid tumor matrix, and aspirate confirmed mycobacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Bacterial Chest Wall Abscess / Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic bacterial infections of the ribs and soft tissues typically manifest with acute inflammatory signs including erythema, marked tenderness, calor, and systemic fever, whereas this presentation was indolent over four months with completely cold, painless masses.
Parenchymal pulmonary tuberculosis was investigated as the primary source of the perihilar opacity, but the patient was completely asymptomatic pulmonarily and failed to produce sputum for analysis.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine-needle aspiration of the anterior chest wall collection yielded fluid that, despite a negative direct acid-fast smear, was positive by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and grew pan-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex on culture, confirming primary chest wall tuberculosis with rib destruction.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male forest guard residing in a sub-Himalayan hill station, with a 15-year history of schizophrenia treated with aripiprazole and trihexyphenidyl, presented to the emergency department with high-grade intermittent fever for 7 days accompanied by myalgias and severe headache.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A forest guard in the sub-Himalayan region presenting with acute febrile illness, thrombocytopenia, cutaneous vasculitic lesions, acute kidney injury, and acute respiratory distress was highly suspicious for scrub typhus, but specific serological testing was negative.

High fever, jaundice, acute renal failure, respiratory distress, and profound thrombocytopenia raised immediate concern for complicated malaria, but peripheral smear and rapid testing were repeatedly negative.
Severe arboviral infection presenting during seasonal outbreaks with severe arthralgias, myalgias, and reactive cutaneous purpura was considered, but serology was non-reactive.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial Sepsis with DIC / Purpura Fulminans
differentials.rule_out_reason: Impending peripheral acral gangrene with purpura, shock, thrombocytopenia, and elevated fibrin degradation products suggested meningococcemia or severe pyogenic sepsis-induced DIC, but blood cultures remained sterile and D-dimer levels were normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay confirmed positive dengue IgM serology, and punch skin biopsy of the purpuric lesions revealed upper dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltration with leukocytoclasia, establishing Expanded Dengue Syndrome with leukocytoclastic vasculitis and myocarditis.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old male residing in a rural area of Colombia presented with a six-month history of progressive neurological decline. Three months prior, he had developed headaches accompanied by lower extremity weakness, gait instability requiring support to climb stairs, memory loss, and behavioral changes.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic lymphocytic pleocytosis with hypoglycorrhachia in an endemic region led to empiric anti-tuberculosis therapy, but the patient suffered clinical progression and specific mycobacterial cultures and PCR were negative.
Subacute basilar meningitis causing obstructive hydrocephalus and papilledema frequently stems from fungal pathogens, but latex agglutination, fungal cultures, and fungal serologies were negative.

A focal cerebellar cystic mass producing progressive ataxia, obstructive hydrocephalus, and raised intracranial pressure raised suspicion for a primary posterior fossa tumor, but histological examination revealed parasitic tissue.

diagnostic_pivot: Open biopsy of the cerebellar cyst demonstrated the definitive histopathological architecture of a cysticercus cyst, confirming subarachnoid racemose neurocysticercosis with cerebellar involvement and secondary obstructive hydrocephalus.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old previously healthy woman presented to the otolaryngology clinic with a four-month history of reduced hearing and persistent tinnitus in her left ear. She reported no otalgia, otorrhea, fever, nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, chronic cough, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Refractory Bacterial Otitis Media with Effusion
differentials.rule_out_reason: A dull tympanic membrane and type B tympanogram commonly indicate chronic bacterial otitis media with effusion, but the condition was completely refractory to multiple courses of oral antibiotics.

differentials.candidate: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma / Fossa of Rosenmüller Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Unilateral Eustachian tube obstruction causing serous otitis media and mixed hearing loss in an adult is a classic presentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, but biopsy of the obstructing lesion demonstrated non-specific inflammatory tissue without malignant neoplasia.

differentials.candidate: Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Secondary Upper Airway Involvement
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extrapulmonary nasopharyngeal mycobacterial involvement usually represents secondary seeding from active cavitary pulmonary disease, but the chest radiograph was clear and serial sputum examinations were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Biopsy of the yellowish slough occluding the left Eustachian tube opening demonstrated positive acid-fast bacilli staining with nonspecific inflammatory changes on histopathology, establishing primary Eustachian tube tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 83-year-old man presented to an outpatient dermatology clinic with generalized skin pruritus lasting for approximately six months. He had a history of extensive lifetime ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure, having worked outdoors for decades as a marine radio navigator, frequently sunbathing without photoprotection.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's long-term unprotected UV radiation exposure and the asymmetric, ulcerated, pigmented scapular lesion showing a grey-blue veil with brown globules and streaks, but complete surgical excision and histopathology confirmed basal cell carcinoma rather than melanoma.
Confirmed histologically as the etiology of the isolated left scapular nodule, but could not account for the generalized six-month pruritus, disseminated papules, and excoriations across the trunk.

Present as co-existing benign background lesions on the trunk exhibiting classic fingerprint-like structures and milia-like cysts, but benign and incapable of explaining the diffuse excoriated pruritic eruption.

Clinical and dermoscopic evaluation of the pruritic trunk papules revealed the pathognomonic triangle sign representing the burrowing mite, with rapid symptomatic resolution following topical 5% permethrin treatment.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old boy presented with severe swelling and aching pain involving the metacarpals, metatarsals, and phalanges of both hands and feet. Swelling had begun when he was one year of age, at which time he was diagnosed with polyarthritis and treated for one month without improvement.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed at age one and considered as a provisional admission diagnosis, but ruled out due to lack of response to anti-inflammatory therapies, marked osseous destructive changes and subluxation on radiography, and co-existing polyserositis (pleural effusion and ascites).

Diagnosed during earlier hospitalization at another facility, but ruled out because genetic skeletal dysplasias cannot account for systemic inflammatory elevations (ESR, CRP), progressive tender dactylitis, hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, or pleural effusions.

Included on the admission differential due to profound cachexia, extensive periarticular erosions, and subluxation on radiography, but ruled out by diffuse symmetric multi-digit involvement and lack of malignant histology on biopsy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tuberculosis (Spina Ventosa / Tuberculous Dactylitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Established by a positive QuantiFERON-TB assay, exudative high-protein pleural effusion, skin lesions with gummatous changes, and histopathological demonstration of epithelioid granulomas, resulting in complete clinical resolution and resolution of organomegaly/effusions after quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 17-month-old female infant from Berkane, Morocco, presented with a 3-month history of erratic, irregular fever associated with profound pallor, epistaxis, and growth/stature retardation. She was born to consanguineous parents; a female sibling had died at age 6 of an unknown etiology.

differentials.candidate: Primary / Familial Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS / HLH)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Evoked as the primary clinical diagnosis because the patient fulfilled diagnostic criteria for MAS (fever, splenomegaly, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia) alongside a family history of parental consanguinity and unexplained sibling death; however, it was determined to be secondary to an intracellular infection rather than a primary genetic immune defect.

Considered due to severe pallor, profound anemia (3 g/dL), and a positive direct Coombs test, but ruled out because the Coombs positivity was an epiphenomenon of marked reticuloendothelial hyperactivity, and the aregenerative pancytopenia reflected central bone marrow suppression.

Considered given the prolonged fevers, failure to thrive, hepatosplenomegaly, bleeding diathesis, and severe trilineage cytopenia, but ruled out by a normal peripheral blood smear without circulating blasts and absence of leukemia on marrow analysis.

Cytological examination of the bone marrow aspirate (myelogram) demonstrated characteristic intracellular Leishmania amastigote bodies alongside prominent hemophagocytic figures, establishing visceral leishmaniasis complicated by secondary macrophage activation syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 3-week history of cough and fever. She had a 3-year history of primary myelofibrosis with massive symptomatic splenomegaly, for which she had been receiving ruxolitinib therapy for the past 10 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed based on left lower lobe consolidation and acute-on-chronic respiratory symptoms, but ruled out due to complete lack of clinical and radiographic response to a 7-day course of levofloxacin.

Considered as an opportunistic fungal pathogen in the setting of ruxolitinib-mediated immunosuppression (and subsequently identified as a co-infection when the patient later deteriorated with pleural effusion), but was not the primary initial infection driving the lobar consolidation that responded to four-drug antimycobacterial therapy.

Despite initial negative sputum AFB smear microscopy and cultures, molecular nucleic acid amplification of sputum detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, prompting initiation of quadruple anti-tuberculous therapy with prompt resolution of initial symptoms.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of HIV infection eight days prior (not yet receiving antiretroviral therapy or cotrimoxazole prophylaxis) presented with a 3-day history of worsening cough and dyspnea.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Severe COVID-19 Pneumonia with Ischemic Stroke
differentials.rule_out_reason: Supported by positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR, rapid antigen testing, anosmia, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, and acute thromboembolic MCA infarction; however, isolated acute viral infection could not account for the preceding two months of evening fevers, weight loss, productive cough, or prominent meningismus.

Confirmed by positive serum and CSF cryptococcal antigen tests, explaining the acute meningeal signs, headaches, and depressed mentation, but isolated fungal meningitis could not account for the extensive diffuse miliary micronodular pattern seen on chest radiography.

Considered on initial evaluation in an endemic setting given acute febrile encephalopathy, tachycardia, and microcytic anemia, but excluded by a negative peripheral blood smear for Plasmodium and other hemoparasites.

Demonstrated at bedside triage by a positive urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM Grade II) assay and classic miliary pattern on chest radiograph, and definitively confirmed by detection of rifampicin-susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA via sputum GeneXpert.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female farmer was admitted to the intensive care unit with acute respiratory distress and fever. She had undergone in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer (IVF-ET) for fallopian tube obstruction, achieving pregnancy three months earlier.

differentials.candidate: Severe Bacterial Pneumonia and Post-Abortal Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed and treated as severe bacterial pneumonia and sepsis based on sudden onset fever, high procalcitonin (peaking at 18.24 ng/mL), elevated CRP (142.4 mg/L), and septic shock; however, the patient failed sequential empiric regimens (cefpodoxime, cefoperazone/sulbactam, moxifloxacin, meropenem, linezolid), with persistent afternoon fevers and failure of weaning from mechanical ventilation.

Considered after standard microbiological panels for routine bacteria, viruses, and fungi returned repeatedly negative while inflammatory markers remained elevated, leading clinicians to suspect a non-infectious etiology; however, molecular testing identified a fastidious pathogen.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Hematogenous Disseminated Pulmonary Tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid detected sequences of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, corroborated by positive GeneXpert MTB testing (rifampicin susceptible) and eventual positive mycobacterial culture.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male carpenter from Wales was transferred to a liver transplant center with neutropenic sepsis and acute kidney injury four months after undergoing orthotopic liver transplantation. His transplant had been performed for alcohol-related liver disease and portal hypertension following two years of documented abstinence.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected when cytopenias coincided with normal liver graft function at 4 months, prompting a 50% reduction in MMF dosing; however, neutropenia worsened and culminated in severe febrile neutropenic sepsis rather than recovering.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Bacterial or Fungal Neutropenic Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered on emergency admission due to acute kidney injury, fevers, and profound neutropenia in an immunosuppressed allograft recipient, but empirical broad-spectrum therapy with meropenem, vancomycin, and fluconazole yielded no clinical improvement or pathogen isolation on standard cultures.
A frequent cause of post-transplant fever and bone marrow suppression, but considered highly improbable because pre-transplant donor and recipient IgG serologies were both negative.

Diagnostic bone marrow biopsy revealed intracellular Leishmania amastigotes and secondary hemophagocytosis; molecular PCR detected Leishmania donovani complex DNA, and serology was strongly positive (titre >= 1:102,400). Subsequent investigation confirmed the organ donor had traveled to India in the year preceding death and harbored positive anti-Leishmania serology.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old male agricultural worker presented with a persistent, disfiguring cutaneous lesion on his nose. The patient had no prior significant medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially managed empirically with systemic antibacterial therapy in primary care, but excluded after the extensive nasal plaque failed to improve and continued to progress over several months.

Strongly considered given the characteristic anatomical location (nasal plaque) and an initial private biopsy showing epithelioid and mononuclear cells with a vaguely granulomatous arrangement, but ruled out because histopathology lacked well-formed sarcoidal non-caseating granulomas and failed to meet diagnostic criteria.

differentials.candidate: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis with Deep Structural Invasion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected on clinical examination due to the extensive infiltrating mid-facial lesion, but excluded by radiographic studies showing completely preserved nasal bones without osseous lysis and intact underlying mucosal surfaces.

Diagnostic microscopic examination of skin scrapings from the ulcerated margin demonstrated intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within macrophages, definitively identified as Leishmania tropica by ITS1 PCR-RFLP and MN1-I restriction analysis, leading to complete clinical resolution after intramuscular meglumine antimonate therapy.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old single male insurance company employee presented with a 3-day history of acute, severe right-sided abdominal pain, intractable nausea and vomiting unresponsive to antiemetics, generalized weakness, and decreased urine output.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered on initial emergency presentation given acute severe right flank pain, oliguria, nausea/vomiting, CVA tenderness, and neutrophilic leukocytosis (12,000/uL, 88% PMNs); however, urinalysis was unremarkable and CT showed no nephrolithiasis, revealing instead extrinsic ureteral compression from large pelvic cysts.

differentials.candidate: Non-Parasitic Pelvic Cystic Neoplasm / Mesenteric Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the atypical, isolated pelvic localization of the two large cysts in the absence of typical hepatic, splenic, or pulmonary cystic involvement; however, serological and histopathological analysis confirmed a parasitic etiology.

Serological testing demonstrated a markedly elevated hydatid antibody index of 29 on ELISA (normal < 11), prompting albendazole therapy and exploratory laparotomy with cyst resection; histopathological examination confirmed an Echinococcus hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old woman was transferred to an intensive care unit with acute circulatory shock, progressive jaundice, and acute respiratory failure. She had a history of untreated hydronephrosis for four years and had been positive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) for several decades.

differentials.candidate: Severe Bacterial Pneumonia with Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Formulated as the initial working diagnosis due to extreme leukocytosis (57.0 x 10^9/L), procalcitonin elevation (10.73 ng/mL), refractory hypotension requiring noradrenaline, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates; however, broad-spectrum coverage with meropenem and continuous renal replacement therapy failed to halt progression to diffuse pulmonary hemorrhage and multiorgan failure.

differentials.candidate: Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Hepatitis B with Hepatorenal Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's long-standing HBsAg positivity, documented cirrhotic morphology with ascites, profound hyperbilirubinemia, and hyperammonemia, prompting administration of entecavir and ornithine aspartate; however, acute HBV flare could not account for acute severe thrombocytopenia, bilateral pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage, or severe multiorgan failure following mountain field exposure.

differentials.candidate: Viral Hemorrhagic Fever (Epidemic Hemorrhagic Fever / Hantavirus or Dengue)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the exposure history of unprotected mountain farming, acute myalgias, profound thrombocytopenia (10 x 10^9/L), coagulopathy, and acute oliguric renal failure; however, serum antibodies against dengue and epidemic hemorrhagic fever returned negative.

Although standard serum and body fluid IgM/IgG antibodies were initially negative due to testing early in the acute bacteremic phase, next-generation sequencing (NGS) of blood definitively detected four unique DNA sequences of Leptospira interrogans, confirming Weil's syndrome presenting with severe pulmonary hemorrhage and multiorgan failure.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old woman with a background from Sierra Leone presented to the hospital complaining of pleuritic chest pain, fever, and cough. Her medical history was notable for human immunodeficiency virus infection successfully managed with antiretroviral therapy and a recent subclinical viral respiratory illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's West African origin and history of treated retroviral infection, but the imaging lacked typical apical cavitary lesions or calcified nodes.

differentials.candidate: Atypical and Zoonotic Pulmonary Infections (Q-fever, Syphilis, Viral/Bacterial pneumonias)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in the differential for febrile nodular pulmonary consolidations, but invasive lavage and comprehensive serologic assays were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Serial imaging showed migratory nodular pulmonary lesions in the setting of marked eosinophilia in an immigrant from an endemic region, leading to serological confirmation of schistosomiasis and clinical resolution with praziquantel.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old female with a medical history of peripheral arterial disease status post left common iliac stenting and spinal stenosis presented to the hospital with a 3-week history of generalized weakness, fatigue, and headache.

differentials.candidate: Intracranial Space-Occupying Lesion, Hydrocephalus, or Basilar Meningitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute progressive headache, photophobia, altered mental status, and profound SIADH, but neuroimaging revealed no intracranial lesions or meningeal enhancement.

differentials.candidate: Structural Spinal Cord or Thecal Sac Compression
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given persistent post-surgical back pain and bilateral lower extremity weakness, but imaging demonstrated no thecal sac effacement or cord compromise requiring surgical decompression.

diagnostic_pivot: The public health notification that the surgical bone graft was contaminated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis prompted systemic evaluation, revealing miliary pulmonary nodules and L4-L5 osteomyelitis.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old previously healthy woman from Guilan Province in northern Iran presented with a two-month history of progressively worsening epigastric and right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain. The pain was constant, non-radiating, and unrelated to food intake or position.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the most likely initial diagnosis, but the patient failed to respond to empiric broad-spectrum coverage with intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole.

differentials.candidate: Amebic Liver Abscess and Hydatid Cyst (Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Prevalent regional parasitic causes of large cystic or abscess-like hepatic lesions, but excluded by non-reactive serological testing.
Considered given the multiloculated hepatic mass, regional lymphadenopathy, and significant constitutional weight loss, but excluded by endoscopic evaluation and biopsy.

diagnostic_pivot: Marked peripheral eosinophilia (32%) prompted targeted trematode serology, which yielded a positive FAST-ELISA for Fasciola hepatica, confirmed by biopsy showing acute necrotic inflammation.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old Brazilian man was admitted to the hospital with a severe wasting syndrome, fever of unknown origin, anorexia, asthenia, and night sweats, progressing over the preceding month to the point of becoming bedridden.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever of unknown origin, night sweats, 25-kg weight loss, and hepatosplenomegaly, but excluded by negative interferon-gamma testing and normal thoracic imaging.

differentials.candidate: Syphilis, HIV, and Chronic Viral Hepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as potential etiologies for subacute wasting, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and peripheral neuropathy, but all serological screenings were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Recognition of thickened peripheral nerve trunks and cutaneous infiltration prompted bone marrow and skin examinations, which revealed characteristic acid-fast bacilli forming globi, positive anti-PGL-I serology, and positive qPCR.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old Caucasian male with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with persistent resting dyspnea, chest pain, and a cough that had started dry and became productive fifteen days prior to admission.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute febrile productive cough and consolidations, but the patient had failed outpatient aminopenicillin/clavulanate therapy and had a normal procalcitonin level.

While acute respiratory failure and ground-glass opacities were consistent with viral pneumonitis, isolated viral infection could not explain the preceding weeks of night sweats, 10-kg weight loss, or extensive bilateral micronodular tree-in-bud lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: The presence of bilateral micronodules and consolidations superimposed on ground-glass opacities prompted molecular sputum testing, which detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis by PCR, confirming dual coinfection complicated by deep venous thrombosis.

clinical_summary: A 3-year-old Ethiopian boy presented to the hospital with a four-month history of progressive dry cough, worsening shortness of breath, and low-grade intermittent fever. He had no history of weight loss, jaundice, abdominal pain, or abdominal distention, and had no known contact with chronically ill or coughing individuals.

differentials.candidate: Hyperreactive Airway Disease (Pediatric Asthma) and Bacterial Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to diffuse wheezing, cough, and tachypnea, but multiple courses of oral antibiotics and inhaled salbutamol failed to relieve symptoms, and chest radiography demonstrated massive bilateral space-occupying lesions rather than bronchospasm or focal consolidation.

Considered in an endemic region presenting with chronic cough, but ruled out by absence of sick contact exposure, absence of weight loss, and cross-sectional imaging demonstrating large fluid-filled cysts rather than caseous consolidations or hilar adenopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Close domestic canine contact combined with thoracic ultrasound and CT demonstrating giant, bilateral thick-walled cystic lesions without septations pointed to pulmonary hydatid disease, confirmed by successful intact surgical enucleation.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old man undergoing treatment for centrally located squamous cell lung carcinoma (T3N0M0) invading the left pulmonary artery and comorbid chronic pulmonary granulomatous infection on established four-drug oral therapy presented with an acute, fulminant skin eruption and high fevers.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to generalized erythema and extensive desquamation, but ruled out by extensive sheet-like epidermal necrolysis, severe oral mucosal sloughing, and a positive Nikolsky sign.

differentials.candidate: Anti-Tuberculosis Drug-Induced Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reaction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy is a well-recognized cause of severe drug rashes, but the patient had taken the four-drug regimen for months without adverse events and successfully continued anti-TB therapy throughout follow-up without recurrence.

diagnostic_pivot: The rapid onset of widespread epidermal detachment covering >50% body surface area with mucosal involvement and positive Nikolsky sign occurring 10 days after sintilimab therapy confirmed immune-checkpoint-inhibitor-induced toxic epidermal necrolysis, managed successfully with systemic corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old Asian woman presented to the hospital with acute-onset headache, nausea, and vomiting that had started one day prior to admission. She had no fever, dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis, or cough.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary cause of concurrent cerebral sinus thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in a young female without exogenous risk factors, but coagulation factor assays and autoantibodies were completely normal.
Considered given the unprovoked multifocal venous thromboses in distinct vascular territories, but excluded by systemic contrast imaging showing no neoplastic lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracic CT revealed left upper lobe cavitary lesions and hilar lymphadenopathy, with positive interferon-gamma release assay implicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis as the chronic inflammatory trigger of hypercoagulability, subsequently confirmed by culture.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old female from San Luis Potosí, Mexico, with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and a 2-year history of known cholelithiasis presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of moderate-to-severe colicky right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary clinical diagnosis given postprandial RUQ colic, profound neutrophilic leukocytosis, and septic shock, but excluded when all preoperative blood cultures and intraoperative bile and purulent fluid cultures remained sterile.

Suspected intraoperatively and on gross pathological inspection due to an enlarged gallbladder with a firm mass, extensive wall thickening (4–10 mm), and dense duodenal-omental adhesions, but excluded by histopathology showing necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological analysis of the resected gallbladder revealed caseous necrosis with acid-fast bacilli, confirmed definitively as Mycobacterium tuberculosis by polymerase chain reaction.

clinical_summary: A 75-year-old man from rural Zhejiang Province, China, presented to the hospital with a six-day history of fever and productive cough with yellow tenacious sputum, and a five-day history of watery diarrhea occurring four to five times daily.

differentials.candidate: Cryptococcal Meningitis or Central Nervous System Mycobacterial Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient developed acute agitation, restlessness, and delirium while undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy, but lumbar puncture analysis demonstrated normal CSF opening pressure, normal protein/glucose, and absence of cryptococcal or mycobacterial organisms.

Although active pulmonary mycobacterial infection was verified in sputum, isolated pulmonary tuberculosis failed to account for acute watery diarrhea, severe bilateral thigh and calf myalgias, thrombocytopenia, fulminant oliguric renal failure, and acute encephalopathy following broad-spectrum antibiotic administration.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum molecular testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, whereas plasma, urine, and CSF metagenomic next-generation sequencing along with CDC ELISA IgG confirmed Leptospira interrogans, establishing concurrent coinfection.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man presents with a 5-day history of high-grade fever, chills, and one episode of vomiting. On admission, he suffers a single seizure episode, followed by altered sensorium and rapidly deteriorating neurological status.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute febrile illness accompanied by seizures, rapid altered sensorium, and symmetric bilateral thalamic lesions on neuroimaging; however, the presence of a generalized erythematous macular rash and acute thrombocytopenia (60,000/μL) are characteristic of an arboviral hemorrhagic syndrome.

Considered given the symmetric bilateral hypodensities in the thalami, cerebellum, and deep white matter with petechial microhemorrhages; however, the presentation occurs in the setting of acute primary flaviviral infection with marked thrombocytopenia rather than a secondary post-infectious demyelinating or metabolic necrotizing syndrome.

Considered in a patient from an endemic region presenting with acute high-grade fever, seizures, severe anemia (7 gm/dL), and thrombocytopenia; however, the prominent cutaneous rash and rapid development of symmetric thalamic hemorrhagic necrosis prompted evaluation for viral hemorrhagic fever pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by positive non-structural NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies indicating acute primary infection, confirming dengue-associated haemorrhagic encephalitis complicated by obstructive hydrocephalus.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old boy presents with a 12-day history of high-grade fever and chills, accompanied by severe headaches, retro-orbital pain, and occasional episodes of vomiting. Five days after the onset of fever, he developed acute weakness of the right upper and lower extremities, followed by progressive weakness of the left upper extremity and a decreased level of consciousness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the prolonged febrile illness with chills, headaches, vomiting, neurological impairment, and thrombocytopenia; ruled out by negative dual antigen diagnostic testing.

differentials.candidate: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1) Encephalitis / Japanese Encephalitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to pediatric febrile encephalopathy presenting with focal neurological deficits and impaired consciousness; ruled out by negative serological markers for both HSV-1 and Japanese encephalitis.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological detection of specific IgM antibodies in conjunction with acute thrombocytopenia and typical MRI findings of multifocal non-enhancing demyelinating lesions confirmed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis secondary to dengue infection.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old male presents with a 1-day history of acute high fever, chills, and severe vomiting, accompanied by generalized myalgia, frontal headache, and arthralgia. Within 12 hours after hospital admission, his neurological condition deteriorates, progressing to a significantly decreased level of consciousness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the hyperacute presentation of fever, severe headache, vomiting, and rapid deterioration of consciousness within 12 hours; however, brain MRI demonstrated an isolated non-enhancing lesion confined to the splenium of the corpus callosum and the patient recovered completely with supportive therapy alone.

Considered because the splenial lesion demonstrated restricted diffusion with low ADC values; however, true ischemic infarction is rare in young patients without cardiovascular risk factors, and follow-up MRI demonstrated complete resolution consistent with transient cytotoxic edema (RESLES) rather than permanent infarction.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by positive non-structural NS1 antigen and IgM serology confirming acute dengue infection, correlating with characteristic reversible splenial lesion syndrome (RESLES).

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male presents with a 1-day history of acute neurological symptoms including left hand and right leg weakness, slurred speech, occipital headache, and giddiness, accompanied by a single convulsive episode.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute onset of unilateral hand and leg weakness, dysarthria, and headache in a middle-aged patient; however, neuroimaging demonstrated an extra-axial collection with blood-breakdown products rather than acute arterial territorial ischemia.

Considered given the classic crescent-shaped extra-axial collection overlying the cerebral convexity; ruled out by clinical history confirming normotension and complete absence of trauma or external bleeding diathesis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by confirming acute febrile infection complicated by significant thrombocytopenia and spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage on GRE MRI sequence.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department in a drowsy state following a 4-day history of intermittent moderate-grade fever without chills or rigors. On admission, her blood pressure is 96/66 mm Hg.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute febrile illness with altered sensorium and bilateral cerebral lesions; ruled out by neuroimaging demonstrating vasogenic edema without diffusion restriction, hemorrhage, or post-contrast enhancement, along with prompt and complete clinical and radiological resolution.

Considered given the typical posterior reversible leukoencephalopathy pattern; however, classic hypertensive encephalopathy was excluded by the persistent absence of elevated blood pressure, with the patient instead presenting normotensive to hypotensive requiring dopamine for vascular tone.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by positive non-structural NS1 antigen testing in the setting of severe thrombocytopenia and characteristic vasogenic edema on neuroimaging that completely resolved on follow-up, confirming PRES secondary to dengue fever.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old woman residing in southern Ethiopia presents with a 1-day history of acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The pain is described as intermittent, colicky, and nonradiating, without aggravating or relieving factors, and is accompanied by anorexia and nausea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute colicky right upper quadrant pain, scleral icterus, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and elevated alanine transaminase; ruled out by abdominal ultrasonography demonstrating tubular mobile worms obstructing the common bile duct rather than acoustic-shadowing biliary calculi.

Considered due to neutrophilic leukocytosis and extrahepatic cholestasis; however, the classic triad of cholangitis was incomplete as the patient remained strictly afebrile with normal vital signs and without evidence of sepsis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by microscopic visualization of characteristic ova on stool examination combined with abdominal ultrasound revealing live worms in the distal common bile duct causing biliary ductal dilation.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old female farmer with a history of occupational exposure to field sewage presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of generalized body pain, fatigue, and anorexia, followed by progressive dyspnea and fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's sudden loss of consciousness, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and initial head CT findings; however, head CT revealed only chronic lacunar infarctions that could not explain the rapidly developing hemodynamic shock, severe hypoxemia, or elevated inflammatory markers.

differentials.candidate: Severe Bacterial Pneumonia with Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the profound dyspnea, marked elevation of procalcitonin (3.8 ng/mL) and interleukin-6, leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance, and refractory hypotension; however, standard bacterial pathogens were absent, and advanced molecular testing revealed a zoonotic spirochetal etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by metagenomic next-generation sequencing of both CSF and blood identifying Leptospira borgpetersenii reads along with positive IgG serology, followed by MRI demonstration of acute demyelinating lesions.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old man from a mountainous region in Hebei Province, China, presents with persistent high-grade fevers (>39°C), profuse chills, drenching sweats, progressive fatigue, and an unintentional weight loss of approximately 10 kg over the preceding 6 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given admission to the rheumatology service for fever of unknown origin, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, elevated ESR/CRP, and serositis (pericardial effusion); ruled out by the complete absence of arthralgias, synovitis, cutaneous rashes, or mucosal ulcers, and failure of empirical anti-inflammatory response.

Considered due to the subacute wasting syndrome with 10-kg weight loss, massive splenomegaly, and progressive trilineage cytopenias; initial bone marrow evaluation showed dysplastic changes without malignant clonality, and subsequent staining revealed an infective etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by metagenomic next-generation sequencing demonstrating 5,946 reads of Leishmania donovani in peripheral blood combined with bone marrow aspirate cytology revealing hemophagocytes containing intracellular amastigotes.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old female homemaker residing in the urban metropolitan area of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, presents with a 5-month history of progressive jaundice, dull abdominal pain, ascites, unintentional weight loss, and an eruptive skin rash.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 5-month presentation of progressive obstructive jaundice, extreme alkaline phosphatase elevation, intrahepatic ductal ectasia, heterogeneous pancreatic enlargement, intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy, and cachexia; ruled out by tissue histopathology demonstrating granulomatous infection rather than epithelial malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Primary Biliary Cholangitis with Lichen Planus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the violaceous, slightly desquamative papules had a distinctive lichenoid clinical appearance and the patient presented with chronic cholestatic liver disease; ruled out when skin biopsy revealed suppurative granulomatous dermatitis with fungal structures rather than lichenoid interface dermatitis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by histopathological examination of skin, liver, and lymph node biopsies with Grocott silver staining demonstrating pathognomonic spherical budding yeast cells resembling a 'marine pilot's wheel' and 'Mickey Mouse ears'.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a 3-week history of progressive dyspnea, substernal chest pain, and daily hemoptysis productive of 1 to 2 teaspoons of fresh blood.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially on multiple presentations given fever, productive cough, hemoptysis, and bilateral infiltrates; ruled out by lack of response to outpatient and inpatient broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy (azithromycin and ceftriaxone), acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, negative bacterial cultures, and progressive alveolar hemorrhage.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's age, female sex, nephritic urinary sediment, positive autoimmune serologies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), and response of alveolar hemorrhage to immunosuppression; however, the subacute constitutional wasting syndrome (30-pound weight loss, night sweats), high-risk incarceration history, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy signaled an underlying chronic mycobacterial infection that provoked immune dysregulation.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic turning point was established when bronchoalveolar lavage cultures yielded slow-growing acid-fast bacilli, confirming active Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection presenting as diffuse alveolar hemorrhage in the setting of lupus.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old retired man presents with persistent, worsening neck pain two months following cervical spine surgery. His past surgical history is notable for an anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) performed at the C3–C4 level for cervical spondylotic myelopathy, which had manifested as a one-year history of neck stiffness, lower extremity weakness described as 'walking on cotton,' bilateral hyperreflexia, and...

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis / Postoperative surgical site infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic spinal infection typically responds to potent broad-spectrum coverage or presents with acute toxic features, but the patient experienced no symptomatic relief after sequential empiric courses of ceftriaxone and vancomycin.

differentials.candidate: Cervical spine neoplasm / Primary or metastatic spinal tumor
differentials.rule_out_reason: Destructive endplate erosion with soft-tissue phlegmon raised suspicion for an underlying neoplasm, but this possibility had been formally evaluated and ruled out on preoperative contrast-enhanced imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: The emergence of nocturnal diaphoresis and low-grade pyrexia, historical apical pulmonary scarring, nonresponse to antibacterial therapy, and positive tuberculosis-specific T-cell culture with interferon-gamma release confirmed secondary adjacent-segment tuberculous spondylodiscitis.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old previously healthy man, a non-smoker with no known medical co-morbidities, presents with an insidious onset of cough and constitutional symptoms lasting one month. The cough is productive of mucoid sputum, accompanied by poor appetite, generalized malaise, and an involuntary 5-kilogram weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia / Pyogenic lung infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial pneumonia was considered given dense acinar consolidation, crackles, and elevated inflammatory reactants; however, the indolent one-month duration, severe constitutional wasting, upper-lobe predilection, and lack of acute pyogenic response pointed away from typical acute bacterial pathogens.

First-line anti-tubercular therapy was initially initiated following positive smear microscopy, but the patient experienced treatment failure with clinical deterioration, inability to gain weight, and worsening radiographic consolidation.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrated 2+ acid-fast bacilli, CBNAAT showed high Mycobacterium burden with rifampicin resistance, LJ culture confirmed resistance to first-line agents and levofloxacin, and line probe assays confirmed rpoB, katG, and fluoroquinolone resistance, establishing pre-extensively drug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old man with no prior known medical co-morbidities presents to the hospital with a one-month history of progressive cough with mucoid expectoration, worsening dyspnea, and profound weight loss of 14 kilograms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Extensive cavitary consolidation in the right upper and middle lobes accompanied by subacute cough and sputum suggested a lung abscess or necrotizing bacterial infection, but typical pyogenic features and aspiration risk factors were absent.

differentials.candidate: Cavitary bronchogenic carcinoma / Primary pulmonary malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extreme cachexia with a 14-kg weight loss, pallor, anemia, and large unilateral cavitary opacities raised high suspicion for cavitary lung cancer, but the patient's young age and subsequent high-titer microbiological positivity refuted neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrated 2+ acid-fast bacilli, CBNAAT identified high-level rifampicin resistance, and line probe assays confirmed resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and fluoroquinolones with aminoglycoside sensitivity, confirming pre-extensively drug-resistant cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old male presents for clinical evaluation following the incidental discovery of abnormal pulmonary findings on a screening examination three weeks prior. He is entirely asymptomatic, denying cough, sputum production, dyspnea, fever, chest pain, hemoptysis, anorexia, or weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Welder's Siderosis / Welding-associated pulmonary fibrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Occupational welding exposure for three decades supported pneumoconiosis; however, pure welder's siderosis is generally non-destructive and cannot explain the development of thick-walled cavitary lesions and granulomatous necrosis.

differentials.candidate: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage / Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Intra-alveolar macrophage iron accumulation raised the possibility of alveolar hemorrhage; however, the ingested iron particles exhibited intense metallic luster and refraction typical of exogenous welding fumes rather than non-refractive hemosiderin.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoscopic evaluation yielded acid-fast bacilli on brush smears and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, electron microscopy confirmed mycobacterial bacilli, and histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation alongside iron deposits, establishing concurrent siderosis and active pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old female who recently immigrated from Micronesia presents with a one-week history of painful nodules on both lower legs, accompanied by intermittent fevers and night sweats. She also reports progressive areas of diminished cutaneous sensation across her upper and lower extremities.

differentials.candidate: Acute bacterial cellulitis / Pyogenic soft tissue infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral erythema, edema, and tender nodules with fevers initially prompted treatment for bacterial cellulitis; however, cephalexin failed to provide relief, and pyogenic cellulitis does not account for peripheral sensory deficits or widespread hypopigmented macules.

Tender pretibial subcutaneous nodules accompanied by constitutional symptoms (fevers, night sweats) and anemia raised high suspicion for erythema nodosum secondary to tuberculosis, but this was excluded by a negative interferon-gamma release assay.

diagnostic_pivot: Full-thickness punch biopsy of the lateral lower leg revealed noncaseating granulomatous inflammation with numerous acid-fast bacilli demonstrated on Fite staining, establishing lepromatous leprosy complicated by a type 2 erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) reaction.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old boy from an agricultural family of low socioeconomic status is brought to the emergency department with a two-day history of severe colicky abdominal pain, recurrent vomiting, and obstipation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes accompanied by ileocolic intussusception initially suggested reactive lymphoid hyperplasia; however, intussusception in a 13-year-old child strongly implies a pathological lead point, and the presence of pica with 10% peripheral eosinophilia pointed toward an enteric helminthic etiology.

A palpable right lower quadrant mass, fever, guarding, and leukocytosis mimicked appendiceal phlegmon; however, erect abdominal radiography demonstrated acute mechanical obstruction and ultrasonography revealed the classic concentric target sign of telescoping bowel.

diagnostic_pivot: Sonographic demonstration of tubular hypoechoic structures with parallel echogenic margins within dilated proximal bowel, followed by urgent exploratory laparotomy revealing gangrenous ileocolic intussusception with an obstructing bolus of Ascaris lumbricoides as the mechanical lead point, confirmed soil-transmitted helminthiasis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a three-day history of high-grade fevers, shaking chills, generalized myalgias, and nausea with three episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting. He reports absolute constipation and absence of flatus since the onset of symptoms, accompanied by poor oral intake.

differentials.candidate: Undifferentiated bacterial sepsis / Septic paralytic ileus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Systemic inflammatory response criteria (fever, tachycardia, leukopenia with 33% bandemia, elevated lactate and procalcitonin) and adynamic ileus suggested bacterial sepsis, prompting broad-spectrum intravenous coverage; however, no focal bacterial infectious nidus was detected.

Acute persistent vomiting, obstipation, and multiple intestinal air-fluid levels on radiography raised concern for acute mechanical bowel obstruction; however, cross-sectional abdominal CT demonstrated non-obstructive adynamic ileus without a transition point.

diagnostic_pivot: Examination of the peripheral blood smear revealed characteristic intraerythrocytic ring forms, and confirmatory parasite testing identified Plasmodium falciparum infection, establishing falciparum malaria presenting with microvascular sequestration and paralytic ileus.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old Asian male presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of severe abdominal cramps, nausea, recurrent vomiting, and continuous, copious watery diarrhea. He denies hematochezia, melena, recent medications, or prior antibiotic therapy.

differentials.candidate: Invasive bacterial dysentery (e.g., Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extreme inflammatory markers (procalcitonin 20.5 µg/L, CRP 174.5 mg/L, 40,000 neutrophils/µL) suggested invasive bacterial enteritis, but the diarrhea was voluminous, non-bloody, and purely watery without mucosal ulceration or tenesmus.

Acute diarrheal illness progressing to severe anuric acute kidney injury with proteinuria and hematuria mimicked HUS; however, the patient exhibited marked hemoconcentration (hemoglobin 18.8 g/dL, hematocrit 54.3%) and preserved platelets rather than microangiopathic Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Stool culture confirmed the isolation of Vibrio cholerae, establishing acute cholera with catastrophic enterotoxin-mediated secretory purging leading to hypovolemic shock, rhabdomyolysis, and dialysis-requiring acute tubular necrosis in a traveler returning from an endemic region.

clinical_summary: A 3.2-year-old boy born to consanguineous parents presents with a chronic, progressive, intensely pruritic erythematous papular and crusted cutaneous eruption involving his scalp, face, trunk, palms, and soles. His medical history is significant for primary immunodeficiency (mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1 [MALT1] deficiency) characterized by failure to thrive, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, chronic colitis, and autoimmune vitiligo, managed with...

differentials.candidate: Psoriasiform dermatitis / Severe primary immunodeficiency-associated eczema
differentials.rule_out_reason: Refractory dermatitis since infancy and initial histopathologic findings of psoriasiform dermatitis suggested an endogenous inflammatory dermatosis; however, transmission of pruritus to close caregivers and rapid progression to thick hyperkeratotic crusted plaques pointed to an infectious ectoparasitic cause.

differentials.candidate: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis / Cutaneous Langerhans cell histiocytosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Infantile crusted scalp and facial eruptions in a child with failure to thrive suggested severe seborrheic dermatitis or histiocytosis; however, severe pruritus, involvement of the palms and soles, and contagion to household contacts ruled out this possibility.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of skin scrapings from the hyperkeratotic crusted plaques revealed abundant Sarcoptes scabiei mites, confirming Norwegian (crusted) scabies facilitated by underlying cellular immunodeficiency and prolonged topical corticosteroid therapy.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old male born in Guyana and currently residing in Canada presents with an unusual facial rash. His medical history is notable for ulcerative colitis diagnosed on colonic biopsies, well-controlled on maintenance mesalamine (5-ASA) and the immunosuppressive agent azathioprine, with remote courses of oral prednisone.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A creeping serpiginous cutaneous tract appearing shortly after tropical Caribbean beach exposure suggested zoonotic hookworm larvae; however, typical cutaneous larva migrans is intensely pruritic, predominantly affects the lower extremities, and migrates steadily daily rather than exhibiting episodic multi-week migratory jumps across the face.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous extra-intestinal manifestation of ulcerative colitis / Reactive inflammatory dermatosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Underlying inflammatory bowel disease on azathioprine prompted consideration of an atypical reactive cutaneous manifestation; however, a discrete wandering serpiginous line is characteristic of helminthic larval migration and responded rapidly to targeted anti-parasitic treatment.

diagnostic_pivot: High epidemiologic suspicion based on endemic country of origin (Guyana) and immunosuppressive therapy prompted reference enzyme immunoassay testing at the CDC, which detected elevated antibodies at an optical density of 2.08 (reactive > 1.70), confirming autoinfective Strongyloides stercoralis infection presenting with larva currens.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old woman is evaluated in clinic for ongoing management of chronic gastrointestinal symptoms. She was born in Nigeria and has a history of extensive travel throughout the Caribbean over the preceding decades, including trips to Antigua, Barbados, Curaçao, the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Haiti, and Puerto Rico.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although diagnosed 10 years earlier, idiopathic UC typically causes continuous colonic mucosal inflammation with crypt architectural distortion and rectal involvement, and does not account for peripheral eosinophilia or complete symptom resolution after antiparasitic therapy; re-examination of the histopathology showed rectosigmoid sparing and preserved crypts.

differentials.candidate: Human T-Cell Lymphotropic Virus Type 1/2 (HTLV-1/2) Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's origin in Nigeria and Caribbean travel, HTLV-1/2 coinfection was evaluated as a potential driver of severe or refractory helminthic disease, but screening returned negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of rhabditiform larvae on stool microscopy, highly elevated specific serology (OD 2.39), and biopsy re-examination revealing eosinophilic lamina propria infiltrates with preserved crypt architecture established chronic strongyloidiasis mimicking IBD.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old man presents with a 3-year history of chronic left-sided pleuritic chest pain without other associated symptoms. He reports no dyspnea, cough, hemoptysis, fever, chills, night sweats, or unintended weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary initial diagnosis given the posterior paravertebral location, rib remodeling, and neural foraminal extension; however, MRI revealed multilocular daughter cysts within a mother cyst matrix and no solid enhancing nodules or malignant features.
Aggressive osseous erosion could indicate malignancy, but the absence of metabolic activity on PET/CT and cystic morphology argued against high-grade neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast MRI demonstrated characteristic multivesicular architecture with low-T1 and high-T2 daughter cysts inside a mother cyst matrix, and surgical histopathology confirmed acellular laminated membranes characteristic of echinococcal hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: In June 2021, a 7-year-old boy with no significant past medical history from a peri-urban community in southern Bahia, northeastern Brazil, presents with acute fever, chills, severe fatigue, headache, myalgias, dyspnea, marked pallor, apathy, and hyporexia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had a positive SARS-CoV-2 IgM rapid test in June 2021, confirmatory nasal RT-qPCR was negative, and severe normocytic anemia with hepatosplenomegaly was inconsistent with isolated coronavirus disease.

Arboviral infections like dengue cause fever and thrombocytopenia, but the marked splenomegaly, profound anemia, and transmission clustering near an active transmission focus pointed specifically toward protozoal parasitemia.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid antigen testing and Giemsa-stained thin blood-smear examination demonstrated Plasmodium vivax trophozoites with a parasitemia of 378.3 parasites/microL, confirmed by slide qPCR.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman with a history of mild hypertension presents to the emergency department with a 10-day history of persistent fever, rigors, headache, diffuse myalgias, asthenia, and weight loss. Her child was recently hospitalized with severe acute febrile illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had a positive nasopharyngeal SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR, chest imaging showed minimal pulmonary involvement (<5%), which was insufficient to explain the profound thrombocytopenia, jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, and hyperferritinemic cytokine storm profile.

While hypotension, thrombocytopenia, and renal impairment were present, the patient maintained a normal INR of 1.0 without overt bleeding, pointing to acute hemolysis and splenic sequestration rather than consumptive coagulopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid diagnostic testing and quantitative blood smear microscopy demonstrated heavy intraerythrocytic Plasmodium vivax parasitemia (2,078.15 parasites/microL, two crosses), confirming acute co-infection.

clinical_summary: A 77-year-old man who underwent surgical resection of an intracranial mass is transferred to the intensive care unit due to acute clinical deterioration. He was born and resided in Cape Verde until 1965, subsequently living in urban Portugal and the Netherlands while working in maritime commerce without other tropical travel.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Postoperative Nosocomial Sepsis / Healthcare-Associated Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Conventional hospital-acquired pneumonia and primary bacteremia do not account for recurrent transmural translocation of enteric microorganisms in a patient on long-term corticosteroid therapy without an obvious primary gastrointestinal source.
Evaluated as potential causes of accelerated immunosuppression and opportunistic infection in an individual originating from Cape Verde, but serologies were unreactive.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of sputum, stool, and urine revealed massive numbers of filariform and rhabditiform Strongyloides stercoralis larvae, and CSF PCR was positive, confirming corticosteroid-induced hyperinfection and larval dissemination carrying enteric bacteria.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old South Asian male farmer with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency department with acute chest pain, generalized myalgias, and progressive fatigue. One week prior to admission, he had direct occupational exposure to floodwaters.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A viral prodrome leading to acute myocarditis was considered, but rapid coronavirus testing was negative and the marked icterus after floodwater exposure pointed away from typical respiratory viral infections.

Chest pain, hypotension, and an S3 gallop raised concern for acute myocardial infarction, but the admission ECG showed normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes, and systemic icterus indicated multiorgan disease rather than primary coronary occlusion.

diagnostic_pivot: History of immersion in floodwaters followed by severe icterohemorrhagic illness, acute myocarditis with biventricular failure (ejection fraction 30-35%), and confirmatory reactive spirochetal serology established the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old man living in Hubei Province presents to the hematology unit with a 1-month history of intermittent high fevers with daily temperature spikes up to 40°C. One month prior to the onset of fever, he had worked on an agricultural farm in Xinjiang Province.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial contrast-enhanced CT suggested splenic angioma due to sustained nodular enhancement, but persistent high fevers, progressive pancytopenia, and diffuse reticuloendothelial FDG avidity on PET/CT ruled out a benign vascular lesion.

Splenic lymphoma and secondary HLH were strongly suspected based on marked splenomegaly, diffuse FDG uptake, and hemophagocytosis on two consecutive marrow aspirates; however, chemotherapy provided only temporary remission before fever and pancytopenia relapsed.

diagnostic_pivot: Post-splenectomy histopathology and a third bone marrow biopsy demonstrated diffuse intracellular and extracellular amastigotes within reticuloendothelial macrophages, with rapid cure following liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old man presents to the outpatient clinic with a 1-year history of non-productive cough, a 2-month history of worsening mid-thoracic back pain, and left-sided chest heaviness. He has received multiple courses of oral antibiotics and antitussives without symptomatic relief.

differentials.candidate: Malignant Posterior Mediastinal Neoplasm / Neurogenic Sarcoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked osseous destruction of multiple vertebrae and ribs with foraminal widening was initially concerning for an aggressive invasive malignancy; however, CT showed a predominantly fluid-density cystic mass with minimal wall enhancement and no solid invasive tumor components.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Tuberculosis (Pott's Disease with Cold Abscess)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Thoracic back pain, vertebral bone destruction, elevated ESR, and a paraspinal/chest wall fluctuant mass strongly mimic a tuberculous cold abscess; however, the lung parenchyma was entirely clear, and histopathology lacked caseating granulomas or acid-fast bacilli.

diagnostic_pivot: CT-guided biopsy revealed characteristic acellular laminated cuticular membranes accompanied by foreign body giant cell granulomatous reaction and necrotic debris diagnostic of hydatid cyst disease.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old Ethiopian woman presents to the emergency surgical service with severe abdominal pain of 2 days' duration. The pain originated in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant before becoming diffusely generalized over the preceding 24 hours.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary working diagnosis given the chronic history of food-relieved epigastric pain followed by generalized peritonitis; however, erect radiographs showed no pneumoperitoneum, and surgical exploration demonstrated that the stomach perforation was actually part of a fistulous tract secondary to biliary parasite migration.

Although gallbladder perforation with 600 mL of purulent bile peritonitis was found, cholelithiasis was absent; rather, mechanical disruption and fistulization to the distal gastric antrum arose from migrating helminths.

diagnostic_pivot: Exploratory laparotomy demonstrated a choledochogastric fistula connecting the common bile duct to the gastric antrum, within which a large, live adult Ascaris was extracted from the common bile duct, followed by postoperative emesis of multiple worms.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old man is referred to a dermatology clinic for evaluation of chronic, severely pruritic nodules that have persisted for 3 months. Three months prior, he developed intensely pruritic erythematous papules, papulovesicles, and small nodules involving the finger web spaces, abdomen, thighs, and external genitalia, characterized by pronounced nocturnal exacerbation of itching.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While presenting with intensely pruritic hyperkeratotic or smooth nodules resistant to topical steroids, prurigo nodularis typically spares male genitalia and does not follow a household cluster of nocturnal finger-web papulovesicles.

Active mite infection was initially present and treated, but persistent lesions represented post-infectious immunogenic granulomatous hypersensitivity rather than ongoing replication, evidenced by clearance of burrows and response of the initial rash to sulfur ointment.

diagnostic_pivot: The pathognomonic distribution of treatment-resistant pruritic nodules on the penis and scrotum following resolved scabies, coupled with rapid remission upon targeting JAK-STAT inflammatory pathways with tofacitinib, confirmed recalcitrant nodular scabies.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old man is referred for evaluation of persistent, severely pruritic nodules on his buttocks. Four months prior, he had developed an acute eruption of intensely itchy papules and nodules over his lower abdomen, genitalia, and buttocks, with marked nocturnal exacerbation of the pruritus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Prurigo nodularis presents with chronic intensely itchy nodules on extensor surfaces driven by repetitive scratching, but does not explain an acute preceding eruption involving the lower abdomen and genitalia with nocturnal exacerbation that largely resolved after topical sulfur ointment.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia / Arthropod bite reaction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Persistent bite reactions or cutaneous pseudolymphoma can cause refractory pruritic nodules, but would not present with widespread synchronous involvement of the lower abdomen and genitalia that cleared with sulfur therapy while sparing only buttock nodules.

The pivotal clinical features establishing the diagnosis are the pathognomonic distribution involving the genitalia, lower abdomen, and buttocks with nocturnal itching, complete clearance of peripheral lesions following topical sulfur, and persistent isolated buttock nodules refractory to conventional anti-inflammatory and antihistamine therapies.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old man is admitted for evaluation of severe, persistent itchy nodules on the foreskin of his penis. Six months prior, he had developed an acute eruption of pruritic papules and nodules distributed across his lower abdomen, thighs, groins, and genitalia, characterized by pronounced nocturnal exacerbation of itching.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Genital HPV lesions present with asymptomatic or mildly irritating exophytic papules on the penis, but do not explain an acute multi-focal eruption across the lower abdomen, thighs, and groins with nocturnal exacerbation that cleared with sulfur therapy.

differentials.candidate: Lichen simplex chronicus / Genital prurigo nodularis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Neurodermatitis or localized prurigo causes chronic pruritic plaques or nodules, but cannot account for preceding widespread involvement of the lower abdomen and thighs that cleared completely after topical sulfur cream.

The diagnostic turning point is the classic history of widespread pruritic papules in characteristic predilection sites with nocturnal exacerbation, resolution of peripheral lesions following topical sulfur, and persistent isolated genital nodules resistant to intralesional and topical steroids and antihistamines.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old boy is referred for evaluation of persistent, itchy nodules on his scrotum and hips of two months' duration.
