Two months prior, he had developed an acute, pruritic eruption consisting of papules and nodules localized to the interdigital web spaces of his fingers, abdomen, genital regions, and hips; multiple close classmates at his school had developed similar itchy skin...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Molluscum contagiosum can spread among school-aged peers and cause genital papules, but classically features smooth dome-shaped lesions with central umbilication, lacks characteristic interdigital web involvement, and does not clear with sulfur ointment.

Benign proliferations such as mastocytomas or xanthogranulomas are non-communicable, do not present synchronously among school classmates, and do not follow an acute generalized eruption involving web spaces and trunk that clears with sulfur ointment.

The diagnostic turning point is the classic epidemiological exposure among classmates, pathognomonic initial distribution (finger webs, abdomen, genitals), clearance of peripheral lesions after topical sulfur, and persistent scrotal nodules refractory to repeated intralesional triamcinolone acetonide and topical corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man is admitted for evaluation of severe, persistent itching nodules on his scrotum and the foreskin of his penis. Six weeks earlier, he had presented with an acute eruption of pruritic papules and nodules involving the web spaces of his fingers, abdomen, and genital regions (scrotum and foreskin).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Genital lesions of secondary syphilis are classically painless, non-pruritic, often associated with systemic features and lymphadenopathy, and do not explain an initial intensely itchy interdigital and abdominal eruption that responded rapidly to sulfur ointment.

Lymphomatoid papulosis and lymphoid hyperplasia present with recurrent, chronic papulonodular lesions, but do not present synchronously with characteristic interdigital web papules that clear rapidly following sulfur treatment.

The diagnostic turning point is the classic predilection for finger web spaces, abdomen, and genitalia, prompt clearance of peripheral lesions with sulfur ointment, and persistent residual genital nodules refractory to four weeks of systemic antihistamines and topical corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A female patient born and raised in Bijie, Guizhou Province, presents for evaluation of progressive left upper extremity skin changes and weakness. Her past medical history is notable for cholecystectomy for hepatolithiasis five years prior.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous tuberculosis (Lupus vulgaris / Tuberculosis verrucosa cutis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cutaneous tuberculosis can cause chronic erythematous plaques and granulomatous infiltration, but does not cause prominent peripheral nerve enlargement, intra-lesional sensory loss, or focal thenar atrophy.

differentials.candidate: Cubital tunnel syndrome / Compressive ulnar neuropathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Mechanical nerve entrapment explains ulnar distribution motor weakness and nerve swelling, but fails to account for overlying edematous dark erythema, cutaneous hypopigmentation, and complete intra-lesional loss of pain and touch sensation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Borderline tuberculoid leprosy with Type 1 leprosy reaction
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point is the classic combination of hypopigmented anesthetic skin lesions, palpable ulnar nerve enlargement, thenar muscle atrophy, lymphohistiocytic infiltration with nerve injury on biopsy despite paucibacillary negative acid-fast staining, and neuroimaging confirmation of peripheral nerve thickening, accompanied by acute inflammatory edema indicative of a Type 1 reversal reaction.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old female (gravida 2, para 1, aborta 1) presents to the emergency department on postpartum day 43 with intermittent high-grade fevers and progressive deterioration. She had undergone an emergency lower-segment cesarean delivery at 35 weeks of gestation due to severe oligohydramnios and intrauterine growth restriction, following an otherwise uneventful antenatal course.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pelvic tuberculosis was considered due to the subacute presentation of a multiseptated pelvic mass with systemic inflammatory signs in an endemic region, but molecular testing for mycobacterial DNA on pus was negative.

differentials.candidate: Polymicrobial puerperal pelvic inflammatory disease / Tubo-ovarian abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Common puerperal pelvic pathogens (enteric Gram-negatives, anaerobes, Streptococci) cause postpartum abscesses, but do not explain the rapid relapse after initial ceftazidime therapy or the specific microbiological features of non-lactose fermenting colonies with a metallic sheen.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Tubo-ovarian abscess due to Burkholderia pseudomallei (Melioidosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was the microbiological isolation and automated identification of Burkholderia pseudomallei from intraoperative pus, peripheral blood cultures, and high vaginal swab, confirming disseminated melioidosis presenting as puerperal pelvic sepsis.

clinical_summary: A 69-year-old woman (height 165 cm, weight 43 kg) presents with a one-month history of persistent fever and progressive neurological decline. Her illness began without an apparent precipitating event with high fevers peaking at 39.7°C, accompanied by slurred speech and left eyelid ptosis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Viral meningoencephalitis can present with subacute fever, focal cranial neuropathies, and lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis, but characteristically maintains normal CSF glucose levels, whereas this patient showed marked hypoglycorrhachia and elevated CSF protein.

Fungal basilar meningitis causes subacute cranial nerve palsies, altered consciousness, and low CSF glucose, but was excluded when molecular metagenomic sequencing and PCR specifically identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis while conventional smears and cultures were negative.

The diagnostic turning point was the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the cerebrospinal fluid by next-generation sequencing (NGS) and confirmation by real-time fluorescence PCR melting curve analysis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old man with a two-year history of myelodysplasia presents with a one-week history of worsening productive cough, aggravated sputum production, shortness of breath, and high fever reaching 38.5°C. One year prior, he had developed a chronic cough for which he received a three-month course of multi-drug antimicrobial therapy; however, treatment was prematurely discontinued because of progressive leukocyte decline.

differentials.candidate: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis / Invasive fungal pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a pancytopenic host with myelodysplasia presenting with cavitary lung lesions and fever, invasive pulmonary aspergillosis is a critical consideration, but serum galactomannan (GM) and 1,3-beta-D-glucan (G) assays were negative.

differentials.candidate: Systemic autoimmune disease with pulmonary cavitation (e.g., Granulomatosis with polyangiitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Granulomatous vasculitis can produce cavitary pulmonary lesions, constitutional symptoms, and secondary cytopenias, but comprehensive autoimmune testing was completely normal.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Relapsed pulmonary tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was the microbiological demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear, confirmed by positive Xpert MTB/RIF PCR for M. tuberculosis DNA without rpoB mutation, and growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex on sputum culture.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old woman with a three-year history of alcoholic cirrhosis presents to the hospital with a one-week history of worsening cough productive of sputum, accompanied by acute hemoptysis. One year prior, she had presented with chronic cough, white sputum, night sweats, fatigue, and low-grade afternoon fevers, for which she received six months of multi-drug antimicrobial therapy before discontinuing treatment on...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Cavitary lung disease complicated by severe hemoptysis in a patient with underlying cirrhosis strongly raises suspicion for chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis or mycetoma, but microbiological investigations confirmed mycobacterial rather than fungal etiology.

NTM infections can produce chronic fibrocavitary disease in hosts with liver disease and prior structural lung changes, but species-specific culture and molecular testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Relapsed drug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was the demonstration of heavily positive acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear (4+), positive Xpert detection of M. tuberculosis DNA, and sputum culture confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex with phenotypic resistance to isoniazid and fluoroquinolones.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old man who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation nine years prior for end-stage liver disease secondary to hepatitis C and alcoholic cirrhosis presents with recurrent productive cough, purulent sputum, and dyspnea.

differentials.candidate: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis / Opportunistic fungal infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: In an immunosuppressed solid organ transplant recipient with cavitary lung disease, invasive fungal pneumonia is a primary differential consideration, but serum GM and G tests were completely negative, and sputum microbiological studies confirmed mycobacterial infection.

Nocardia commonly causes subacute cavitary pulmonary infiltrates in solid organ transplant recipients, but sputum culture and molecular assays specifically confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex rather than branched filamentous bacteria.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Relapsed multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was the microbiological detection of acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear (2+), positive Xpert assay demonstrating TB bacterial DNA with rpoB gene resistance mutations, and positive sputum culture for M. tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old woman presents with persistent headache, nausea, and daily fevers. She has a 10-year history of severe hidradenitis suppurativa with extensive fistulous tracts involving the medial thighs, inguinal region, pubic mound, and axillae, for which she has been treated with adalimumab for the past two and a half years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although initially diagnosed as post-herpetic neuritis given her previous trigeminal zoster episode, the presence of daily fevers, elevated inflammatory markers, a cerebellar vermis lesion on MRI, and clinical deterioration despite intravenous acyclovir ruled out an uncomplicated post-viral neuralgia.

Opportunistic fungal meningoencephalitis was a critical diagnostic possibility in this patient on TNF-alpha antagonist therapy presenting with subacute headache and mononuclear CSF pleocytosis, but was ruled out by negative fungal smears and negative cryptococcal antigen testing.

While leukocytosis, elevated CRP (81.4 mg/L), and high ESR reflected marked systemic inflammation, the CSF demonstrated mononuclear predominance rather than polymorphonuclear pleocytosis, normal glucose levels, and a negative Gram stain.

diagnostic_pivot: Clinical progression on acyclovir, repeat neuroimaging demonstrating progressive pachymeningeal granulomatous infiltration involving the venous sinuses, and a positive interferon-gamma release assay prompted empiric antituberculous therapy, resulting in rapid symptom improvement and complete radiological regression.

clinical_summary: A 77-year-old male is referred to the hospital for evaluation of progressive dyspnea and bilateral lower extremity edema persisting for over six months. His medical history is notable for hypertension managed with oral antihypertensive therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Infiltrative nodular masses coating the pericardium with heterogeneous enhancement and restricted diffusion on MRI were highly suspicious for malignant mesothelioma preoperatively, but excisional biopsy demonstrated caseous necrosis and granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant mesothelial proliferation.

Mass-like pericardial thickening accompanied by prominent mediastinal and cardiophrenic lymphadenopathy suggested pericardial involvement by lymphoma, but metabolic PET/CT imaging showed no extracardiac disease and histopathological evaluation revealed necrotizing granulomas rather than atypical lymphocytes.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic pericardial neoplasm of unknown origin
differentials.rule_out_reason: Nodular pericardial infiltration in an elderly patient is most commonly secondary to metastatic carcinoma, but systemic PET/CT staging identified no occult primary tumor and histopathology revealed epithelioid granulomatous inflammation.

diagnostic_pivot: Excisional biopsy of the pericardial nodules revealed abundant gross caseous material, intraoperative frozen section and permanent H&E staining demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes, and PCR was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old woman with no prior medical history presents for evaluation of chronic left flank discomfort. She reports a 10-year history of dull left lumbar pain.

differentials.candidate: Cystic renal cell carcinoma / Malignant renal neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: A massive exophytic cortical mass in an adult with lumbar pain raised concern for cystic renal malignancy (Bosniak IV), but this was ruled out by the total absence of solid nodular components and lack of post-contrast enhancement on cross-sectional imaging.

differentials.candidate: Benign complex renal cyst / Multilocular cystic nephroma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple or complicated non-parasitic renal cysts lack daughter vesicle proliferation producing a honeycomb appearance and do not exhibit thick, calcified outer fibrous walls.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative hydatid serological tests, cross-sectional imaging showing a calcified multivesicular exophytic cyst and intraoperative macroscopic confirmation of a grape-cluster-shaped multivesicular tumor upon left total nephrectomy established the definitive diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old individual residing in Nova Mutum, Mato Grosso, Brazil, presents with progressive swelling, pain, paresthesias, and diminished thermal and tactile sensation in the right lower extremity. Epidemiological history is notable for prolonged household cohabitation with a sibling who completed a multidrug treatment regimen for a chronic mycobacterial infection ten years ago.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous / Borderline Leprosy with secondary neuritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Typical forms of Hansen's disease are characterized by hypopigmented or erythematous anesthetic skin macules and plaques, but this patient had completely normal skin and negative slit-skin smear bacilloscopy from both auricular lobes and elbows.

Isolated entrapment (e.g., fibular head compression or tarsal tunnel syndrome) cannot account for concurrent enlargement and tenderness of multiple non-contiguous nerve trunks with sensorimotor mononeuropathy multiplex in an endemic contact.

diagnostic_pivot: Concurrence of thickened, tender nerve trunks without cutaneous lesions, motor and sensory mononeuropathy multiplex confirmed on electroneuromyography, and a positive Bioclin fast ML Flow rapid test confirmed pure neural leprosy.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old non-smoking woman presents with a right infra-auricular swelling that has been slowly and progressively enlarging over the past three years. She has a prior surgical history of surgically treated normal pressure hydrocephalus.

differentials.candidate: Isolated pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 3-year history of a painless, mobile parotid tumor with characteristic biphasic MRI and ultrasound signals strongly suggested an isolated benign mixed tumor, but permanent surgical pathology demonstrated active necrotizing granulomatous lesions coexisting within the adenoma.

differentials.candidate: Malignant parotid neoplasm (e.g., mucoepidermoid or adenoid cystic carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Involvement of both superficial and deep parotid lobes with intraoperative compression and lamination of the cervical branch of the facial nerve raised concern for malignancy, but histopathologic examination showed no cellular atypia or malignant invasion.

diagnostic_pivot: Because parotid tuberculosis was clinically unsuspected in the absence of constitutional or pulmonary symptoms, the diagnosis was definitively established by permanent histopathology following conservative total parotidectomy demonstrating the coexistence of active tuberculosis lesions.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female presents to the emergency department of a rural community hospital in New Hampshire complaining of severe, progressive fatigue. Three weeks prior to presentation, she self-diagnosed COVID-19 using a home antigen test; she received no prescription treatment, and while her mild respiratory symptoms resolved, her fatigue progressively worsened.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In rural New England, endemic tick-borne Babesia microti was the initial working diagnosis for acute hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia with intraerythrocytic rings, leading to empiric atovaquone and azithromycin; however, travel to West Africa and pathologist smear review revealed falciparum trophozoites and schizonts rather than maltese crosses.

Recent COVID-19 infection, severe fatigue, tachycardia, borderline hypotension, and elevated lactate prompted resuscitation for presumed septic shock, but blood smear review demonstrated intraerythrocytic parasitic forms driving intravascular hemolysis.

diagnostic_pivot: Pathologist examination of the peripheral blood smear identifying numerous ring trophozoites and cluster schizonts with 39.3% parasitemia, positive Plasmodium falciparum rapid antigen testing, and dilated funduscopic confirmation of malarial retinopathy established severe falciparum malaria.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old female agricultural worker from a rural area in Espírito Santo State, Brazil, presents with progressive cutaneous facial lesions, oral ulcerations, marked weight loss, and altered mental status. Two years earlier, she developed erythematous lesions on her face; a previous skin histological sampling showed a histological granulomatous pattern without identifiable microorganisms, leading to an empirical diagnosis of granulomatous rosacea...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Facial erythematous plaques with telangiectasias and an initial biopsy showing granulomas without microorganisms led to prolonged unsuccessful therapy for rosacea; however, rosacea does not cause mucosal ulceration, generalized lymphadenopathy, or systemic constitutional wasting.

Sarcoid-like infiltrative plaques, generalized lymphadenopathy, and granulomatous histology raised suspicion for sarcoidosis, but clear chest radiography, moriform hemorrhagic gingival ulceration, and identification of fungal structures on special stains excluded sarcoidosis.
Disseminated mucocutaneous ulcerations, generalized lymphadenopathy, and neurological impairment were consistent with treponemal disease, but nontreponemal serological testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: A repeat skin biopsy demonstrating suppurative granulomatous dermatitis with Grocott-Gomori silver-positive thick-walled fungi surrounded by Langhans giant cells, together with a reactive double immunodiffusion titer of 1:16 and widespread systemic organ involvement on CT/MRI, established chronic multifocal paracoccidioidomycosis.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old man presents to an emergency department in California complaining of progressive abdominal distension and worsening abdominal pain over a 3-week period, accompanied by nonbloody diarrhea and two days of progressive shortness of breath.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A bloody, exudative eosinophilic effusion in a cirrhotic patient with loculated ascites raised high concern for serosal malignancy, but repeated cytological examination of pleural fluid and cell blocks demonstrated reactive mesothelial cells without malignant neoplasia.

Severe peripheral eosinophilia (32%) and serosal infiltration prompted bone marrow biopsy and flow cytometry, which demonstrated reactive eosinophilia with no clonal, myeloid, or lymphoid immunophenotypic aberrancy.
Eosinophilic polyserositis can occur in systemic connective tissue diseases or eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, but ANA, RF, ANCA, and anti-CCP autoantibodies were all negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Severe total serum IgE elevation (2549 kU/L) in an immigrant from Guatemala with eosinophilic polyserositis culminated in a positive Strongyloides IgG serology, with rapid normalization of eosinophil count and complete resolution of ascites and effusions following ivermectin therapy.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of abdominal pain and progressive constipation of three weeks' duration. The pain has been gradual and progressive, rated 6 out of 10 in severity.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute bowel obstruction in a young adult most commonly results from postoperative adhesions or bands, but this patient had a virgin abdomen with no prior surgical history, abdominal trauma, or surgical scars.
Three weeks of progressive obstipation with crampy discomfort could suggest functional colonic constipation or fecal impaction, but digital rectal examination revealed an empty rectal vault.

diagnostic_pivot: Eliciting a detailed history that the patient passed worms in his stool, followed by microscopic stool examination demonstrating fertilized eggs of Ascaris lumbricoides and oral contrast CT revealing pathognomonic worm-like longitudinal filling defects in the ileum, confirmed partial bowel obstruction due to ascariasis.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old woman is referred to the surgical clinic by the otorhinolaryngology department for evaluation of a large, painless swelling in the left neck region suspected of extending into the upper mediastinum.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A soft, slowly growing supraclavicular cystic lesion was initially suspected to represent a vascular or lymphatic malformation, but superficial ultrasonography demonstrated complete lack of flow and no relationship to cervical vascular structures.

differentials.candidate: Congenital cervical cyst (branchial cleft cyst / cystic hygroma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Indolent growth, benign cystic architecture, and lack of MRI contrast enhancement were consistent with a benign developmental cyst, but intraoperative exploration revealed clear yellow hydatid fluid and characteristic laminated parasitic membranes.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical incision of the 8 cm mass yielding clear yellow cyst fluid and characteristic laminated cyst membranes, combined with complete resection and histopathological examination of both neck lesions, confirmed hydatid cyst disease.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old child presents with a 4-month history of burning chest pain radiating towards the shoulders, accompanied by asthenia, night sweats, and a 3-kg weight loss. One month after the onset of pain, a palpable mass appeared at the level of the upper sternum.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial osteomyelitis typically follows an acute, febrile course with local calor, rubor, and rapid purulent collection. In this patient, the lesion evolved indolently over four months in an apyretic state with multifocal pulmonary and splenic involvement. Direct smears of biopsy and respiratory samples were negative for pyogenic organisms, while molecular testing identified mycobacterial DNA.

differentials.candidate: Malignant Bone Tumor / Sternal Lymphoma (e.g., Ewing Sarcoma, Osteosarcoma, Hodgkin Lymphoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The combination of sternal body osteolysis, associated soft-tissue infiltration, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, intrasplenic lesions, and constitutional B-symptoms (weight loss, night sweats) in an adolescent strongly mimics primary bone sarcoma or lymphoma. However, histopathological and microbiological examination confirmed an infectious etiology rather than neoplastic malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when GeneXpert real-time PCR of the surgical sternal biopsy detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex at a low level without rifampin resistance, subsequently confirmed by positive cultures on liquid MGIT (6 days) and solid Lowenstein-Jensen media (19 days), establishing multifocal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old female presents with an 8-month history of chronic cough and hemoptysis. Her medical history is notable for systemic lupus erythematosus, for which she received treatment with corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab 5 years ago.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given her prior immunosuppression with rituximab and glucocorticoids, opportunistic fungal cavitary disease with hemoptysis was a critical diagnostic consideration. However, the presence of well-demarcated cystic lesions in both the lungs and liver, coupled with the water lily sign and histopathological confirmation of parasitic protoscolices rather than fungal hyphae, excluded aspergillosis.

Bilateral pulmonary nodules associated with a concomitant focal hepatic lesion in a young adult can suggest metastatic malignancy. However, the lesions had well-defined cystic borders rather than solid, invasive neoplastic architecture, and surgical resection confirmed a benign parasitic cyst without malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was established by the CT finding of round cystic lesions in the lower pulmonary lobes and liver featuring 'the water lily sign' in the right lung, followed by definitive surgical histopathology demonstrating cystic echinococcosis with protoscolices and refractile hooks.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old female with no prior medical history presents with a 2-month history of persistent back pain and fever. On initial clinical evaluation, physical examination findings are ambiguous and non-focal.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pulmonary aspergillosis was initially suspected based on the appearance of a cavitary/cystic pulmonary lesion with internal contents, but the patient failed empirical antifungal therapy completely, and subsequent serological and histopathological examinations identified parasitic cestode structures rather than fungal organisms.

A pulmonary mass or cavitary lesion displaying an air-fluid level in the lower lobe accompanied by fever and back pain strongly mimics a pyogenic lung abscess. However, the indolent two-month progression without response to antimicrobial management and subsequent positive immunological testing ruled out simple bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when the CT revealed the characteristic round cystic lesion with air-fluid level, leading to positive echinococcal immunological testing and definitive surgical thoracotomy pathology demonstrating echinococcal scolex and hooks.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old male presents with recurrent cough and sputum production for 1 year, accompanied by joint pain involving all extremities for 10 months. One year prior, he was hospitalized elsewhere for cough, sputum, and fever, where thick brown pericardial and pleural fluid was aspirated; empirical therapy for chronic granulomatous infection was administered without symptom relief.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic cough, polyserositis, multifocal osteolysis, lymphadenopathy, and cold abscesses led to an initial clinical misdiagnosis of tuberculosis; however, interferon-gamma testing was negative, empirical antitubercular therapy failed, BALF Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA/Xpert assays were negative, and lymph node biopsy showed no granulomas or acid-fast bacilli.

Extremity polyarthralgia, sacroiliac and spinal abnormalities, and a positive HLA-B27 test prompted a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis; however, marked bone destruction, extensive soft-tissue abscesses, negative autoimmune antibodies, and purulent draining sinuses indicated an aggressive infectious process rather than an autoimmune inflammatory spondylopathy.

Marked leukocytosis (41.23 × 10^9/L) with neutrophil predominance and purulent draining abscesses suggested acute pyogenic bacterial infection; however, broad-spectrum meropenem therapy was ineffective, and aspirate cultures were sterile for bacteria.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was informed by the patient's exposure history (extended residence in Myanmar and bamboo rat consumption), positive Aspergillus galactomannan cross-reactivity, bone marrow aspirate demonstrating fungal hyphae, and definitive identification of Talaromyces marneffei via metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of pus aspirated from the subcutaneous mass.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male from Zanhuang County, Hebei Province presents with a 5-month history of intermittent fever, poor appetite, nausea, and vomiting. Five days prior to admission, his fever recurred with peak temperature of 39.5°C, accompanied by chills, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, without cough, expectoration, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked elevation of serum (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (814 pg/mL) combined with persistent fever and pancytopenia raised high suspicion for invasive fungal infection; however, empirical antifungal therapy with amphotericin B and fluconazole failed to produce improvement, and subsequent bone marrow and metagenomic testing confirmed parasitic infection rather than fungal pathogens.

Profound pancytopenia and splenomegaly in an elderly patient, with marrow imaging showing megakaryocyte dysplasia and reduced cellular proliferation, strongly simulated primary marrow failure or myelodysplastic syndrome; however, marrow examination showed no increase in juvenile blast cells and instead revealed intracellular protozoal organisms.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Autoimmune Disease (e.g., Systemic Lupus Erythematosus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Prolonged intermittent fever, polyserositis symptoms, pancytopenia, splenomegaly, and an elevated ESR (101 mm/h) suggested a systemic autoimmune disorder, but autoantibody serologies were unrevealing.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when bone marrow aspiration identified intracellular Leishmania amastigotes, further confirmed by blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) yielding tens of thousands of sequence reads for Leishmania infantum, Leishmania donovani, and Leishmania chagasi.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old male recipient of a matched-sibling donor hematopoietic stem cell transplant for myelodysplastic syndrome, maintained on an immunosuppressive agent, presents on day +317 post-transplant with acute onset of fever and body ache.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile illness accompanied by body ache and harsh breath sounds in an immunosuppressed stem cell transplant recipient necessitates ruling out bacterial bacteremia; however, blood cultures were negative and the patient recovered completely with supportive hydration and antipyretics alone.

differentials.candidate: Transplant Graft Rejection or Disease Relapse
differentials.rule_out_reason: The development of acute thrombocytopenia post-transplant raises concern for marrow graft failure or relapse of myelodysplastic syndrome; however, the patient maintained >90% donor chimerism, and the thrombocytopenia resolved spontaneously following a transient nadir.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was established by the rapid detection of viral NS1 antigen in the setting of acute fever, body ache, hemoconcentration (hematocrit 48%), and acute thrombocytopenia in an endemic setting.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old boy with a history of severe aplastic anemia presents to the transplant emergency department on day +88 post-transplant with a 2-day history of high-grade fever associated with shivering, pain in the right hypochondrium, and loose watery stools.

differentials.candidate: Acute Gastrointestinal and Hepatic Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Watery diarrhea, right upper quadrant pain, and transaminitis on day +88 post-transplant strongly suggest acute gut and liver GVHD; however, the hyperacute onset of high fever with rigors, rapid hematocrit increase, and capillary plasma leakage (ascites, pleural effusion) indicated an infectious vascular leak syndrome rather than GVHD.

High-grade fever with rigors, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and hepatitis in an allogeneic transplant recipient frequently points to enteropathogenic or typhoidal bacteremia; however, comprehensive microbiological workup and pan-cultures remained sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was achieved by the positive detection of Dengue NS1 antigen in conjunction with the classical signs of plasma leakage (hemoconcentration, ascites, pleural effusion, and rapid platelet decline).

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old boy with transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia and a history of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (confirmed on previous bone marrow tissue examination) who underwent a matched-related donor transplant presents to the emergency department on day +130 post-transplant with a 1-day history of continuous high-grade fever and myalgias.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given his documented history of bone marrow biopsy-proven secondary HLH and persistent cytopenias, sudden high-grade fever and severe thrombocytopenia strongly suggested disease recurrence; however, the hyperacute presentation was triggered by viral infection with confirmed antigenemia, leading rapidly to plasma leakage and refractory circulatory failure.

Acute high fever and severe thrombocytopenia in a patient on triple immunosuppressive agents raised immediate concern for life-threatening bacterial sepsis; however, the clinical course was dominated by capillary leak syndrome (periorbital puffiness, ascites, oliguria, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension) confirmed by positive viral antigen testing.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the detection of Dengue NS1 antigen in an immunosuppressed child presenting with continuous high-grade fever, profound thrombocytopenia (platelet 16 × 10^9/L), and subsequent development of severe dengue shock syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 3.5-year-old boy presents with high-grade fever and body ache of 1 to 2 days' duration, 8 months following an allogeneic stem cell transplant for transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia major. His current medications include cyclosporine for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis and active antimycobacterial therapy for a pulmonary granulomatous infection that developed 4 months post-transplant.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Sudden high fever, body aches, acute leukopenia, and coagulopathy in an immunosuppressed toddler on cyclosporine strongly suggested acute bacterial sepsis; however, the illness followed a self-limiting course without septic shock or localized bacterial infection, entering a spontaneous recovery phase after defervescence.

Concomitant multi-drug antimycobacterial regimens and cyclosporine can induce profound myelosuppression and coagulopathy; however, the abrupt onset of high fever and transient nature of the cytopenias with prompt rebound following the febrile phase ruled out static drug toxicity.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the clinical confirmation of acute dengue fever characterized by the classical biphasic evolution of rapid leukopenia, coagulopathy, a platelet nadir of 15 × 10^9/L at day 5, and subsequent uneventful recovery without plasma leakage.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old male with a history of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia presents on day +103 following a matched-sibling donor hematopoietic stem cell transplant with acute onset of fever, throat pain, and flu-like symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Acute Respiratory Viral Pharyngitis (e.g., Influenza, Adenovirus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Fever, sore throat, and flu-like symptoms in an adolescent frequently indicate acute upper respiratory tract viral infection; however, the presence of concurrent thrombocytopenia in an endemic region prompted arboviral testing, which confirmed acute arboviral infection.

differentials.candidate: Leukemic Relapse / Post-Transplant Bone Marrow Dysfunction
differentials.rule_out_reason: New fever and thrombocytopenia in a leukemia recipient shortly after transplant raises immediate suspicion of early leukemic relapse or marrow failure; however, surveillance on day +100 confirmed complete remission with negative MRD and full donor chimerism, and the mild cytopenia did not progress.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the rapid detection of positive Dengue NS1 antigen, identifying dengue virus infection as the cause of the acute febrile flu-like illness and mild thrombocytopenia, allowing successful outpatient supportive management.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old man who had previously undergone autologous stem cell transplantation for multiple myeloma presented to the emergency department with persistent fever and cough. On initial evaluation, a plain chest radiograph was normal, showing no pulmonary infiltrates or consolidation.

differentials.candidate: Lower Respiratory Tract Infection / Bacterial Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, cough, and post-transplant immunosuppression, but ruled out by unremarkable pulmonary imaging.

differentials.candidate: Transplant-Associated Thrombotic Microangiopathy or Severe Bacterial Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given acute renal dysfunction, gross hematuria, and severe thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by spontaneous stabilization and recovery with hydration and supportive care alone.

diagnostic_pivot: The characteristic trajectory of acute thrombocytopenia falling from baseline, bleeding manifestation (gross hematuria), and self-limiting course in a dengue-endemic region confirmed the clinical diagnosis despite negative initial viral antigen and serology.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia, who had undergone a matched-sibling donor hematopoietic stem cell transplant 18 months earlier and was off all immunosuppressive therapy, presented with a 24- to 48-hour history of intermittent fever.

differentials.candidate: Acute Myeloid Leukemia Relapse / Secondary Graft Failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to post-allogeneic transplant status and new-onset cytopenia, but ruled out by isolated, transient thrombocytopenia without systemic progression or peripheral blasts.
Considered in any post-transplant febrile episode, but ruled out by a benign clinical course resolving with simple supportive measures without broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid detection of viral antigen in a patient presenting with acute fever and isolated thrombocytopenia in an endemic region established the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old child admitted to the transplant unit for a haploidentical stem cell transplant for beta-thalassemia major developed a sudden fever spike on day +26 post-transplant. Baseline triage laboratory investigations revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers, including high C-reactive protein and procalcitonin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although Escherichia coli was cultured from urine and targeted antibiotics were administered, the patient suffered a subsequent fever spike and vascular leakage inconsistent with treated bacterial infection alone.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Viral (CMV, BKV) or Fungal (Aspergillosis) Infection / Malaria
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to post-transplant immunosuppression, but extensive microbiological testing for opportunistic pathogens returned negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergence of positive serology at a recurrent fever spike accompanied by objective third-space fluid accumulation (plasma leak syndrome) on thoracic and abdominal imaging confirmed severe dengue.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old boy with transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia major admitted for a second hematopoietic stem cell transplant developed an acute fever spike on day +1 post-transplantation, prompting initiation of the institutional febrile neutropenia protocol.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered immediately given early post-transplant neutropenia, but exhaustive microbiological cultures across multiple sets were consistently sterile.
Although ring forms were identified on peripheral smear, the biphasic fever pattern and prominent plasma leakage were characteristic of arboviral co-infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Appearance of a new fever spike after a 72-hour afebrile window with positive viral antigen detection and multiorgan third-spacing (ascites, pleural effusion, gallbladder edema) confirmed dengue.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old man originally from the Eastern Cape province and residing in the Western Cape of South Africa presented to the emergency center with new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures. His medical history included hypertension, obesity, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

differentials.candidate: Primary Hematologic Malignancy / Autoimmune or Nutritional Cytopenia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered to explain severe bicytopenia, but extensive evaluation showed no nutritional deficits, hemolysis, thyroid/hepatic dysfunction, or autoantibody markers.
Considered on differential for a solitary pulmonary mass, but ruled out by typical, sharply defined cystic architecture with peripheral calcification on advanced computed tomography.

diagnostic_pivot: Cross-sectional thoracic CT demonstrating a massive, calcified cystic lesion in the lung, followed by hematologic recovery upon antihelminthic therapy, established the diagnosis despite negative serum ELISA.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer in remission and a 50 pack-year smoking history presented for her annual low-dose chest CT lung cancer screening. She reported a 3-month history of progressively worsening mid-thoracic back pain, while denying fevers, chills, cough, dyspnea, weight loss, or neurological symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given cancer history, hypercalcemia, and destructive bone lesions, but spine MRI demonstrated characteristic inflammatory bone marrow edema and phlegmon involving endplates rather than neoplastic infiltration.
Considered as primary infectious etiologies, but blood cultures, Karius microbial cell-free DNA, Brucella serologies, and bone biopsy cultures/stains were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Strongly positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus assay, disclosure of occupational exposure in correctional settings, disc-sparing vertebral endplate MRI findings, and prompt clinical/biochemical response to empiric antitubercular therapy confirmed the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old male child from Metema, Gondar, Ethiopia, residing in an endemic tropical region, presented with a 4-day history of high-grade intermittent fever accompanied by chills and rigors. He also experienced loss of appetite, three episodes of non-projectile vomiting of ingested matter, and profound prostration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, prostration, and subsequent bowel perforation, but initial labs showed normal WBC differential, and stool examination and urinalysis showed no signs of enteric infection.
Considered after emergent laparotomy identified a 2 x 2 cm anterior duodenal perforation, but postoperative testing for H. pylori was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of the peripheral blood film demonstrating intra-erythrocytic ring forms established severe Plasmodium falciparum infection responsible for microvascular sequestration and ischemic ulcer perforation.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman from a rural area in Tunisia with unfavorable socioeconomic conditions and no prior medical history presented to the emergency service with a 1-year history of progressive pain, swelling, and functional limitation of the right elbow.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to local erythema, heat, and purulent fistulization, but ruled out by the chronic 1-year progression, normal white blood cell count, and characteristic marginal periarticular osteolysis on plain films.
Considered intraoperatively when hypertrophic synovial tissue mimicked a neoplastic lesion, but histopathology demonstrated granulomatous caseation rather than malignant mesenchymal neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Microbiological isolation of acid-fast bacilli from draining sinus pus and histopathological confirmation of necrotizing granulomas with Langhans giant cells established the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old man presented to the emergency department with cough, anorexia, and oliguria with a 24-hour urine output of less than 400 mL. Two months earlier, he had experienced recurrent cough, intermittent nocturnal fevers, and bilateral palpable cervical lumps, for which he had been initiated on a multidrug antimicrobial regimen at an outside hospital.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to profound hyperglobulinemia, acute renal failure, anemia, and hypergammaglobulinemia, but excluded by negative immunofixation electrophoresis for monoclonal paraproteins.

differentials.candidate: Drug-Induced Acute Interstitial Nephritis / Acute Tubular Necrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a medication-related etiology following antimicrobial therapy, but renal biopsy revealed severe IgG4-rich plasma cell interstitial infiltration (>40% IgG4/IgG ratio) diagnostic of IgG4-related kidney disease concurrent with systemic infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine-needle aspiration of the enlarged cervical lymph nodes revealing necrotizing granulomas with acid-fast bacilli and positive Xpert MTB testing confirmed acute hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old woman presented for evaluation after routine health screening chest radiography revealed incidental bilateral pulmonary lesions. She was entirely asymptomatic, reporting no fever, dry cough, wheezing, dyspnea, or weight loss, and had no prior history of respiratory disease.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered on the differential for bilateral pulmonary nodules and tree-in-bud opacities accompanied by marked eosinophilia, but systemic vasculitis and malignancy were systematically ruled out.

Although the patient met ISHAM criteria for ABPA based on mucus impaction, severe hyper-IgE, and peripheral eosinophilia, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing demonstrated active mycobacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic sequencing and positive molecular Xpert MTB/RIF testing confirmed active pulmonary tuberculosis despite negative sputum smears and cultures.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old female with a medical history of hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and recently diagnosed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma presented to the emergency department with gradually progressive shortness of breath and swelling of her face and bilateral upper extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to progressive erythema and worsening pain at the indwelling pleural catheter insertion site in an immunocompromised cancer patient, but excluded due to the absence of purulent discharge, fluctuance, or fluid collection, and by the absence of bacterial suppuration.

Considered because of localized pruritus and erythema underneath an old catheter dressing without systemic symptoms, but ruled out when symptoms failed to resolve after cleansing and applying a fresh dressing, instead evolving into severe pain.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct visual inspection of the opened connection tubing demonstrated a viable, motile 17-cm grayish-white helminth migrating out of the chest wall tract, morphologically identified as female Ascaris lumbricoides, confirming aberrant thoracic soil-transmitted helminthiasis.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old East African man presented to the hospital with hemoptysis, dyspnea, night sweats, and generalized fatigue lasting for two months. Four months prior to this presentation, he had been evaluated for similar but more severe symptoms of hemoptysis, dyspnea, night sweats, and fatigue, and was started on a multi-drug antimycobacterial regimen consisting of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the acute-on-chronic presentation with high fever (38.9 C), profound hypoxemia, bilateral crackles, and wheezing, but ruled out when empiric antibacterial therapy failed to provide clinical improvement and was subsequently discontinued.

Considered given his 7-year occupational history of silica dust exposure in gemstone mines and bilateral auscultatory abnormalities, prompting adjunctive corticosteroid therapy, but ruled out as an isolated non-infectious pathology because active mycobacterial infection was concurrently present.

diagnostic_pivot: Molecular cartridge-based testing of sputum was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming active silicotuberculosis in a patient with severe occupational silica exposure who suffered recurrent or persistent disease despite maintenance dual-agent antimycobacterial therapy.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department with a 5-day history of persistent high-grade fever exceeding 39 C, chills, rigors, generalized fatigue, and severe muscle aches localized predominantly in his lower back and legs that significantly limited his mobility.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the rapid post-febrile onset of paraparesis progressing to quadriparesis and sensory paresthesias, but ruled out by generalized flaccid areflexia in all four extremities, absence of a discrete spinal sensory level, absence of bowel/bladder dysfunction, and neurophysiologic confirmation of peripheral demyelinating polyneuropathy.

Considered given the profound antecedent back and leg myalgias following acute arboviral illness, but ruled out because the profound motor deficit was driven by peripheral nerve demyelination with prolonged latencies and loss of deep tendon reflexes, rather than primary muscle fiber pathology.

diagnostic_pivot: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrated albuminocytologic dissociation with elevated protein (110 mg/dL) and normal leukocytes, nerve conduction studies confirmed AIDP, and serological testing confirmed acute dengue infection with positive IgM and IgG antibodies, confirming Guillain-Barré syndrome secondary to dengue fever.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old male with no significant past medical history presented with a 20-day history of persistent fever and cough without an obvious precipitating cause. His body temperature fluctuated around 37.8 C.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute presentation of fever and cough, but ruled out because the patient showed no clinical improvement despite prolonged empiric anti-infective treatment, with paradoxically progressive lymphadenopathy.

Considered given the subacute progression of isolated unilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and interlobular septal thickening in a young male, but ruled out by negative serum tumor markers and lymph node histology demonstrating necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

Considered when EBUS-TBNA demonstrated necrotizing granulomas while standard smear, culture, and Xpert MTB/RIF all returned negative, initially leading clinicians to discount tuberculosis, but subsequently refuted by advanced molecular capture testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Hybrid capture-based targeted next-generation sequencing (hc-tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and subsequent acid-fast staining of the lymph node biopsy confirmed the definitive diagnosis of pulmonary and mediastinal lymph node tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old female weighing 35 kg was evaluated for management of drug-resistant chronic pulmonary cavitary disease. She had previously completed a nine-month standard antimycobacterial regimen (three months of four-drug intensive therapy followed by six months of dual maintenance therapy), but subsequently developed a recurrent early-morning cough productive of mucoid sputum that worsened in the left lateral decubitus position.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the florid presentation of delusions, visual hallucinations, irrational speech, and aggression, but ruled out by the lack of prior psychiatric history, absence of psychiatric family history, acute temporal onset 10 days post-drug initiation, and rapid reversibility upon drug cessation.

Considered given the patient's severe wasting (body weight 35 kg), anemia, and chronic debilitating lung disease, but ruled out by entirely normal serum electrolytes, renal function parameters, urinalysis, and thyroid function tests.

diagnostic_pivot: Adverse drug reaction evaluation demonstrated a Naranjo probability score of 7 and a BPRS score of 50, pointing to cycloserine-induced neurotoxicity; withdrawal of cycloserine while continuing the remaining anti-TB drugs resulted in prompt clinical recovery, with BPRS falling from 50 to 20 within 72 hours.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old nulliparous Black woman presented to the emergency department complaining of persistent pelvic pain, abdominal distension, dysuria, and an unintentional 4-kg weight loss over the preceding eight months. She denied fever, dysmenorrhea, or abnormal vaginal discharge, but reported sporadic dyspareunia.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Pelvic Inflammatory Disease / Tubo-Ovarian Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic pelvic pain, adnexal cystic lesions, and cervical motion tenderness, but ruled out by lack of response to multiple empiric antimicrobial regimens, negative STD screening, normal leukocyte count, and laparoscopic confirmation of non-pyogenic granulomatous disease.

Strongly suspected based on cachexia, ascites, peritoneal thickening, bilateral complex adnexal masses, elevated CA125, and laparoscopic visualization of diffuse peritoneal nodules, but ruled out by negative ascitic fluid cytology and histopathology demonstrating granulomatous peritonitis without malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic laparoscopy and peritoneal biopsy demonstrated granulomatous peritonitis, accompanied by an elevated ascitic fluid adenosine deaminase of 45.5 U/L and positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), confirming peritoneal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset reduced vision and photophobia in both eyes lasting for one week. She had no preceding history of ocular trauma, systemic fever, constitutional symptoms, or prior medical conditions, and her family history was unremarkable.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute bilateral vision loss, vitreous haze, and extensive retinal hemorrhages and perivascular exudation in a young adult, but ruled out by normal serological tests, absence of full-thickness necrotizing retinal lesions, and absence of systemic viral illness.

Considered due to the classic appearance of opaque perivenous sheathing resembling frosted tree branches with vitreous haze and hemorrhages, but reclassified as secondary Type 2 FBA due to positive immunological evidence of mycobacterial sensitization and sustained cure on antitubercular therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Immunologic testing demonstrated a strongly reactive Mantoux test and borderline elevated ESR without systemic pulmonary involvement on chest radiography, confirming ocular hypersensitivity to tuberculosis (Type 2 FBA), which responded with dramatic regression of perivascular sheathing and restoration of 20/20 visual acuity following antitubercular therapy and corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old male farmer with no known medical comorbidities presented to the hospital with a 10-day history of high-grade, intermittent fever without chills or rigors, and progressive generalized fatigue for five days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's farming occupation, prolonged high fever, systemic fatigue, and developing thrombocytopenia, but ruled out by negative leptospiral IgM antibodies and negative peripheral blood smears for malarial parasites.

Considered because of acute bilateral hearing impairment without ear discharge or ototoxic medication exposure, but excluded as an isolated primary otologic entity when audiometry and response to doxycycline/corticosteroids confirmed secondary auditory neuropathy due to systemic vasculitis.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical finding of a pathognomonic 1.5 x 1 cm eschar in the left lumbar region combined with a positive scrub typhus IgM ELISA established the diagnosis of scrub typhus complicated by sudden sensorineural hearing loss and acute bronchitis, which resolved following oral doxycycline and steroids.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male farmer with a medical history of well-controlled diabetes mellitus presented to the hospital with a 10-day history of high-grade, intermittent fever accompanied by chills, rigors, and generalized body aches.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial Sepsis / Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia with Secondary Arrhythmia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to fever, leukocytosis (13.1 x 109/L), tachypnea, bilateral infrascapular crackles, and bilateral airspace opacities on chest radiograph, but ruled out by negative blood and urine cultures and prompt clinical resolution with doxycycline monotherapy.

Considered when the patient developed acute chest tightness and an irregularly irregular pulse, but ruled out by normal admission ECG, normal echocardiography, normal 24-hour Holter monitoring, and absence of arrhythmia recurrence following resolution of the acute infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The detection of a 2 x 1.5 cm necrotic eschar on the nape of the left neck alongside a positive scrub typhus IgM ELISA established the diagnosis of scrub typhus complicated by bilateral pneumonitis and transient atrial fibrillation, which completely resolved with oral doxycycline.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old Asian male with no significant past medical history presented with progressive, painless swelling in the left cervical region that had been increasing in size over the preceding three months.

differentials.candidate: Extramedullary Blast Phase / Granulocytic Sarcoma of CML
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected as the cause of isolated lymphadenopathy in a patient newly diagnosed with Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML, but ruled out when the lymphadenopathy showed no regression after four months of imatinib therapy, prompting a biopsy that demonstrated caseating granulomas rather than leukemic blasts.

Considered due to the chronic, painless, solitary firm cervical lymphadenopathy in a young adult, but ruled out by histopathology showing classic caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis without neoplastic lymphoid architecture.

diagnostic_pivot: Excisional lymph node biopsy demonstrated caseating granulomas, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis was confirmed through acid-fast bacilli smear, polymerase chain reaction, and mycobacterial culture, establishing tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis concomitant with CML.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old male from Mali was referred for medical evaluation complaining of gross hematuria over the preceding two months, without fever, chills, vomiting, diarrhea, or other systemic symptoms. His medical and family history was limited due to language barriers and lack of cooperation; he was currently residing in a family home under the care of a guardian.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of gross painless hematuria and multiple large nodular, vegetating papillomatous bladder lesions up to 31 mm on imaging and cystoscopy in an adolescent. Ruled out by histological sampling revealing granulomatous eosinophilic inflammation without neoplastic cellular atypia, and persistent negative urine cytologies for malignancy.

Considered given the patient's origin from an endemic region, sterile pyuria, hematuria, and granulomatous bladder wall pathology mimicking chronic granulomatous infection. Ruled out by consistently negative tuberculin skin testing, negative interferon-gamma release assay, and negative urine Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR.

Considered after bladder wall histopathology demonstrated dense eosinophilic infiltration and granulomatous changes. However, this inflammatory pattern was secondary to a parasitic helminthic infection rather than an idiopathic allergic or autoimmune eosinophilic cystitis.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Bacterial Cystitis / Enteric Pathogen Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a common infectious cause of hematuria, pyuria, and diffuse bladder wall thickening. Ruled out by absence of nitrites on urinalysis, lack of systemic inflammatory signs, repeatedly sterile urine cultures, and negative extended stool cultures for enteropathogens.
Considered as a possible helminthic etiology given the patient's geographic origin in Mali and marked peripheral eosinophilia. Ruled out by negative serum anti-Strongyloides stercoralis ELISA.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred upon microscopic parasitological examination of the urine sediment, which revealed large embryonated eggs with a characteristic terminal spine, definitively establishing urinary schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old Indonesian man presented with progressive fatigue and intermittent shortness of breath of two months' duration that was unrelated to physical exertion. He also reported intermittent nocturnal fevers over the preceding three months and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg over the past month, which was attributed to poor appetite and inadequate nutritional intake.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic fatigue, profound asthenia, recurrent borderline hypotension, marked hypocortisolemia (cortisol 28.46 nmol/L), and constitutional symptoms. Ruled out as primary adrenal failure because ACTH was low rather than markedly elevated, and renal ultrasound demonstrated normal, unenlarged adrenal glands, establishing secondary adrenal insufficiency.

differentials.candidate: Acute Retroviral Sero-conversion / Window Period Failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an underlying driver of opportunistic infection and secondary adrenal insufficiency given his high-risk sexual history. However, initial multi-platform screening was negative, reflecting a temporary false-negative state that delayed immediate immunodeficiency confirmation.

Considered when the patient acutely developed severe headaches, vomiting, and generalized tonic-clonic seizures following discharge. Ruled out as the primary etiology of the initial pulmonary presentation, but confirmed as a concurrent opportunistic intracranial infection once repeat HIV testing demonstrated profound CD4 depletion.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point for the pulmonary disease and underlying systemic infection was the identification of Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA by sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF in conjunction with suspicious infiltrates on chest radiography.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old woman with no notable past medical history and no known infectious sick contacts was admitted for evaluation of a hard, painful swelling on her left lower leg that had been progressively increasing over a year, with no history of trauma.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's age and a one-year history of a solitary, progressive, hard pretibial mass with mixed lytic and sclerotic features on plain radiography. Ruled out by the absence of typical malignant radiographic features such as periosteal elevation, cortical bone destruction, or soft tissue invasion.

Considered as a primary infectious etiology for chronic localized tibial pain and bony swelling. Ruled out by the indolent one-year clinical course, complete absence of local signs of acute inflammation (no erythema or warmth), lack of systemic fevers or leukocytosis, and absence of pyogenic bacterial growth.

Considered initially given the periarticular location near the ankle, nocturnal exacerbation of tingling pain, and referral to rheumatology. Ruled out by non-response to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory therapy, negative rheumatoid factor, and negative antinuclear antibodies.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic pivot was achieved via tibial bone biopsy, which detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis through molecular techniques (GeneXpert MTB/RIF), culture, and histopathology.

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old woman presented to the obstetric unit 22 days after delivering her first child via spontaneous vaginal delivery at 36 weeks of gestation. Her antenatal care had been booked at 20 weeks of gestation; she had never received a growth ultrasound during her pregnancy.

differentials.candidate: Retained Products of Conception (RPOC) / Puerperal Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading diagnosis 3 weeks postpartum in a patient with a firm, tender 22 cm pelvic mass and ultrasound showing multiple intrauterine cystic lesions and solid areas. Ruled out by normal septic markers, sterile blood cultures, and intraoperative evacuation of purulent fluid with cystic membranes and daughter cysts rather than retained placental tissue.

Considered given the acute respiratory presentation with pleuritic chest pain, cough, night sweats, hypoxia, and a large pleural effusion. Ruled out by negative sputum GeneXpert testing, negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR, normal septic markers, and postoperative imaging demonstrating a characteristic cystic pulmonary lesion rather than parenchymal consolidation.

Considered due to the rapidly enlarging postpartum uterine mass with mixed cystic and solid components. Ruled out by histopathological examination demonstrating an acellular laminated cyst wall with no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred during exploratory laparotomy for suspected uterine rupture, revealing a distended ruptured uterus containing a large cystic mass with multiple daughter cysts, histopathologically confirmed as a hydatid cyst, with postoperative CT revealing pulmonary and hepatic hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old previously healthy man presented with fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, and dyspnea for three days after working in paddy fields. On admission, he was conscious, with low blood pressure (94/63 mmHg) and tachycardia (pulse rate 145 beats/min).

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial Gastroenteritis with Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered initially given the prominent onset of nausea, vomiting, profuse watery diarrhea, and rapid progression to distributive shock. Ruled out as the primary etiology because enteric gastroenteritis fails to account for concurrent severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome, bibasilar crepitations, profound thrombocytopenia, and anuria following agricultural mud immersion.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Necrotizing Vasculitis (ANCA-Associated Vasculitis / Polyarteritis Nodosa)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered during the patient's catastrophic course due to simultaneous alveolar hemorrhage, rapidly progressive renal failure, severe thrombocytopenia, and subsequent transmural bowel ischemia. Ruled out by histopathological evaluation of the resected bowel and peritoneal viscera, which demonstrated ischemic necrosis without evidence of underlying systemic vasculitis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established on hospital Day 8 when the Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) turned strongly positive at a high titer, confirming severe leptospirosis as the underlying driver of multiorgan capillary vasculopathy, pulmonary hemorrhage, and ischemic bowel necrosis.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old man with Type 2 diabetes presented with fever, arthralgia, and myalgia for three days after working in paddy fields. On admission, he was febrile, icteric, dyspneic, and hypotensive (blood pressure 93/60 mmHg), with bibasal lung crepitations.

differentials.candidate: Acute Ascending Cholangitis with Septic Shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the presentation of acute fever, marked jaundice (icterus), metabolic acidosis with high lactate (7.1 mmol/L), elevated liver enzymes, and septic shock in a diabetic patient. Ruled out because ascending cholangitis does not explain the concurrent diffuse pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome, bibasal lung crepitations, and severe thrombocytopenia following agricultural mud exposure.

Considered due to acute fever, severe myalgias, arthralgias, marked thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic pulmonary involvement in a tropical agricultural setting. Ruled out by the presence of marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (rather than leukopenia), deep scleral icterus, and early acute renal shutdown requiring urgent dialytic support.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by positive confirmatory serology on the Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) with a diagnostic titer of 1:640, identifying severe Weil's disease presenting with pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome and subsequent mesenteric/bowel complications.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old female patient presented with a 7-month history of T-prolymphocytic leukaemia, diagnosed through histopathological examination of bone marrow and cervical lymph node with molecular confirmation via next-generation sequencing, and was admitted due to thrombocytopenia with nasal bleeding for one day.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given profound Grade IV neutropenia (0.40 x 10^9/L), high fever (39 C), marked abdominal distension, and localized right lower quadrant peritoneal tenderness at McBurney's point. Ruled out as the primary etiology because fevers persisted despite empirical imipenem-cilastatin, and aerobic blood cultures subsequently yielded fungal pathogens rather than enteric bacteria.

Considered due to documented high-level CMV viremia on quantitative PCR increasing to 2.42 x 10^5 copies/mL during valacyclovir therapy in a profoundly immunosuppressed patient. Ruled out as the primary cause of fevers, as CMV was recognized as a co-existing immunomodulating viral reactivation facilitating opportunistic invasive mycosis.

Considered due to persistent breakthrough fevers in a neutropenic host on fluconazole prophylaxis and early blood culture smears demonstrating septate hyphae with antler-shaped mold morphology. Ruled out by Wright's staining of peripheral blood smears showing intracellular elongated yeast cells dividing by fission (central septation) rather than budding, and temperature-dependent thermal dimorphism on culture.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by dual-phase cultivation demonstrating thermal dimorphism—filamentous colonies producing a characteristic diffusible red pigment at 25 C and slow-growing yeast colonies at 37 C—confirmed as Talaromyces marneffei by internal transcribed spacer (ITS) rRNA gene sequencing.

clinical_summary: A 47-day-old full-term male infant, delivered vaginally, who had received routine neonatal vaccination at birth according to the national immunization schedule, was admitted with a ten-day history of coughing and a three-day history of fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading presumptive diagnosis on admission due to acute respiratory failure, marked leukocytosis (WBC 30.53 x 10^9/L), high CRP (131.39 mg/L), and dense bilateral consolidations on chest CT. Ruled out as the sole etiology because empiric therapy with meropenem and ampicillin produced no clinical improvement, prompting specialized molecular pathogen testing.

Considered given the infant's age, acute hypoxic respiratory distress, and bilateral pulmonary involvement. Ruled out by a comprehensive multiplex respiratory pathogen screen which was completely negative for respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

Considered and initially diagnosed when nasopharyngeal PCR on hospital day 2 returned positive for Bordetella pertussis, explaining the paroxysmal coughing and hyperleukocytosis. Ruled out as the sole pathogen when the infant failed to improve on macrolide (erythromycin) therapy, leading to invasive sampling that uncovered a concurrent opportunistic mycobacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred on hospital day 3 when bronchoalveolar lavage fluid PCR and GeneXpert returned positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA, which coincided with epidemiological investigation uncovering active maternal pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old man, born and raised in rural Ireland, presented with a 1-week history of progressively worsening penile pain, swelling, and erythema, prompting admission under the urology team. His past medical history was significant for cadaveric renal transplant 15 years prior for end-stage renal disease secondary to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, on maintenance immunosuppression comprising tacrolimus 2 mg twice daily, mycophenolate...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial working diagnosis on admission given acute-onset erythema, swelling, tenderness, and induration of the penile foreskin in an immunosuppressed patient with fever and elevated CRP. Ruled out when the lesion failed to improve and instead progressed despite broad-spectrum intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam and vancomycin.

Considered given the localization of an indurated genital lesion with ulceration in an adult male. Ruled out based on an asymptomatic monogamous partner and completely negative serologic and nucleic acid testing for Treponema pallidum, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Chlamydia trachomatis.

differentials.candidate: Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Genital Neoplasia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's long-term immunosuppressed transplant state, progressive penile induration with tissue breakdown, and non-responsiveness to antibiotics. Ruled out by penile MRI demonstrating non-specific foreskin thickening without a discrete mass and punch biopsy histology confirming granulomatous inflammation without malignancy.

Considered due to the patient's rural agricultural background, work as a butcher handling cattle and deer, and outdoor game-dressing activities. Ruled out by negative targeted serologies for Coxiella and Rickettsia and negative standard blood and tissue cultures.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when systemic computed tomography revealed diffuse pulmonary miliary nodules, prompting penile punch biopsy which demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli and positive Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male presented to the outpatient department with chief complaints of recurrent pain in the right upper abdomen for the past 4 months, along with dyspepsia, weight loss, and loss of appetite.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Calculous Cholecystitis with Concealed Gallbladder Perforation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary working diagnosis based on recurrent right upper quadrant pain, prior conservatively managed perforation, ultrasound showing a 7.5 mm thickened wall with acoustic shadowing indicating cholelithiasis, and MRCP showing a contracted gallbladder with pericholecystic adhesions. Ruled out when surgical pathology demonstrated chalky intramural white areas and caseating granulomatous inflammation rather than simple chronic calculous inflammation.

Considered due to the patient's age, constitutional symptoms (weight loss and anorexia), diffuse asymmetric wall thickening up to 10 mm on MRCP, and dense adhesions infiltrating the adjacent liver bed, duodenum, and colon. Ruled out by histopathological evaluation of the resected gallbladder, which confirmed benign granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells or dysplastic changes.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic pivot was established upon histopathological examination of the resected gallbladder specimen, which demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, multinucleated giant cells, and Langhans giant cells, confirming isolated gallbladder tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 86-year-old bedridden woman with diabetes mellitus and bullous pemphigoid was evaluated for recurrent fever. Four months earlier, she had initiated immunosuppressive therapy comprising prednisolone, cyclosporine, and intravenous immunoglobulin.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Bacterial Pyometra / Bacterial Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although uterine fluid initially yielded general enteric flora, recurrence of fever despite antimicrobial therapy and the subsequent emergence of diffuse granular pulmonary opacities indicated that standard bacterial pelvic sepsis did not account for the systemic clinical picture.

In an elderly postmenopausal woman with persistent pyometra and bilateral lung lesions, uterine malignancy with metastatic dissemination was an important consideration, but cytological examination of the uterine aspirate was negative for neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The progressive enlargement of pyometra in an immunosuppressed host combined with the new development of diffuse granular bilateral lung opacities represented genital mycobacterial disease with hematogenous miliary dissemination, confirmed by positive acid-fast bacilli smears, NAAT, and mycobacterial culture from uterine contents and sputum.

clinical_summary: A woman in her mid-40s was brought to the emergency department during the peak monsoon season with a 3-day history of high-grade fever (maximum temperature 104 °F) accompanied by chills and rigor, headache, progressive limb stiffness (upper extremities greater than lower extremities), and rapidly declining mental status.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral thalamic involvement during peak monsoon season strongly pointed to Japanese encephalitis as the leading diagnosis, but it was excluded by negative specific IgM serology.
