Considered in the setting of raised intracranial pressure, altered sensorium, and thalamic hyperintensities, but ruled out by the absence of dural sinus occlusion or parenchymal hemorrhagic transformation on neuroimaging.

Although bilateral thalamic diffusion restriction can occur in acute Artery of Percheron infarction, the presence of a high-grade febrile prodrome and progressive meningoencephalitic illness made a primary ischemic vascular event unlikely.

diagnostic_pivot: The patient's meningoencephalitis with an atypical neuroimaging pattern of bilateral thalamic lesions was confirmed as scrub typhus by positive serological testing.

clinical_summary: A cohort of pediatric male patients (mean age 9.7 ± 4.8 years) with previously confirmed sickle cell disease (documented by hematological evaluation and hemoglobin electrophoresis) presented to a pediatric emergency department in Cartagena, Colombia, with acute febrile illness.

differentials.candidate: Sickle Cell Vaso-occlusive / Acute Abdominal Crisis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Children with sickle cell anemia frequently experience acute abdominal pain and jaundice during vaso-occlusive or hepatic crises; however, the presence of an acute febrile prodrome, retro-ocular pain, myalgia, rash, and mucosal bleeding indicated an acute systemic infectious trigger rather than an isolated vaso-occlusive event.

Functional asplenia in sickle cell disease predisposes to rapid fulminant bacteremia by encapsulated bacteria presenting with fever, tachycardia, and tachypnea, but the combination of rash, epistaxis, retro-ocular pain, and characteristic virological markers pointed to an epidemic arboviral infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical progression of fever with warning signs to severe disease in pediatric patients with sickle cell disease was definitively confirmed as dengue through positive antigen detection, serology, and RT-PCR.

clinical_summary: Pediatric patients with documented sickle cell disease presented for urgent hospital evaluation after an acute illness. Several patients had remained at home for approximately 4 to 5 days following the onset of symptoms before seeking emergency medical care.

differentials.candidate: Aplastic Crisis / Splenic or Hepatic Sequestration Crisis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute hematologic crises in sickle cell disease present with worsening anemia and organomegaly; however, the concurrent presentation of leukopenia, marked thrombocytopenia, and transaminitis points to systemic viral hematotoxicity and endothelial injury rather than pure erythroid aplasia or isolated sequestration.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial Sepsis with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Invasive bacterial sepsis in asplenic sickle cell patients typically causes marked leukocytosis with left shift, whereas the triad of leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and transaminitis is characteristic of severe arboviral infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of severe cytopenias, transaminitis, and critical clinical progression in children with sickle cell disease was confirmed as dengue virus infection (serotype 2) by positive NS1 antigen, serology, and RT-PCR.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old man was admitted to the pulmonology service with a several-month history of progressive asthenia, fever, night sweats, and exertional dyspnea. His social history was significant for a 50-pack-year tobacco smoking history and prior periods of incarceration in 1998 and 2005.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A 50-pack-year smoking history and multiple pulmonary nodules strongly raised suspicion for lung cancer, but thoracic imaging demonstrating centrilobular tree-in-bud micronodules and subsequent microbiological confirmation proved an infectious mycobacterial etiology.
Considered when pulmonary infiltrates presented with systemic inflammation, but autoimmune serological screening was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical picture of chronic constitutional symptoms, incarceration exposure history, and bilateral nodular infiltrates was confirmed as pulmonary tuberculosis by sputum testing.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old male truck driver was hospitalized in Marseilles, France, with acute fever and disorientation. He resided in Portugal and had been driving across Spain for two weeks before arriving in France three days prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, altered sensorium, and overt meningeal signs (cervical rigidity, Brudzinski's sign, photophobia) strongly suggested acute bacterial meningitis; however, initial CSF evaluation on day 1 revealed only 4 leukocytes/mm³ without purulent pleocytosis.
Considered in a traveler presenting with hyperpyrexia, encephalopathy, thrombocytopenia, hepatalgia, and coagulopathy, but excluded by negative peripheral blood smears.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of high fever, prominent leg myalgias, conjunctivitis, hepatic dysfunction, and coagulopathy culminated in the microscopic observation of spirochetes on dark-field microscopy of cerebrospinal fluid.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old Nepalese man presented with a 3-month history of gradually progressive jaundice, intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort, and a 5-kg weight loss over the preceding two months. He had no cough, fever, hemoptysis, or dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive painless obstructive jaundice, palpable gallbladder, weight loss, and a discrete heterogeneous mass in the pancreatic head causing diffuse biliary dilation is the classic presentation of pancreatic carcinoma; this led to intraoperative resection, but histopathology subsequently demonstrated necrotizing granulomas rather than neoplasia.

Obstructive jaundice with right upper quadrant discomfort can arise from common bile duct stones, but imaging clearly demonstrated a discrete parenchymal mass in the pancreatic head and uncinate process rather than intraductal calculi.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the resected pancreatic head mass demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with positive staining for acid-fast bacilli, confirming isolated pancreatic tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old woman of African descent with chronic alcohol and nicotine abuse was admitted to the hospital with a two-day history of left-sided lower abdominal pain and high fever. Her past medical history included human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection diagnosed six years prior, for which antiretroviral therapy had been discontinued one year earlier due to medication intolerance.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Pelvic Inflammatory Disease / Bacterial Tubo-ovarian Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute severe left lower quadrant pain, high fever, and a purulent adnexal fluid collection in an immunosuppressed patient typically represent acute polymicrobial or sexually transmitted bacterial pelvic infection, but extensive aerobic, anaerobic, and chlamydial cultures were negative.

A history of prior laparotomy for an ovarian cyst and ultrasound demonstration of a 5 × 6 cm cystic adnexal lesion suggested recurrence of a cystic neoplasm or complicated ovarian cyst, but histological evaluation confirmed an infectious granulomatous inflammatory process.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the excised fallopian tube revealed necrotizing granulomatous salpingitis, and molecular testing identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex-specific DNA.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented with a 1-month history of fever, headache, and vomiting. She had no significant past medical history other than occasional mild headaches relieved by analgesics.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Extra-Adrenal Paraganglioma with Hypertensive Encephalopathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe hypertension, tachycardia, and sulcal effacement supported a catecholamine-secreting tumor causing hypertensive crisis; however, elevated catecholamines alone failed to explain the protracted 1-month fever, meningeal signs, and CSF pleocytosis.

Meningismus, headache, vomiting, and fever suggested acute bacterial meningitis, but the protracted 1-month timeline and subsequent lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis ruled out typical acute pyogenic infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical presence of subacute meningeal signs with cerebral sulcal effacement and lymphocytic pleocytosis with high protein in the cerebrospinal fluid established tuberculous meningitis coexisting with an extra-adrenal paraganglioma.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old immigrant child, native of Azerbaijan living in Turkey for 10 years, presented to the emergency clinic with a 10-day history of fever, persistent headache, and vomiting. On physical examination, the patient exhibited mild confusion, nuchal rigidity, and positive signs of meningeal irritation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute loss of consciousness, seizures, and lymphocytic pleocytosis prompted urgent empiric acyclovir therapy; however, specific viral diagnostic testing returned negative.

Rapid hemodynamic collapse and profound hypoglycorrhachia led to broad-spectrum cephalosporin therapy, but the 10-day prodrome and lymphocytic predominance were incompatible with typical acute pyogenic bacterial meningitis.
Subacute headache, fever, vomiting, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and pronounced hypoglycorrhachia suggested fungal meningoencephalitis, but microscopic evaluation was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Severe CSF hypoglycorrhachia, lymphocytic pleocytosis, markedly elevated protein, suspected miliary chest pattern, and maternal history culminated in positive molecular testing and isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from the CSF.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old woman, without any history of farming or raising livestock, presented with an enlarging neck mass that had been noticed 18 months before presentation. On physical examination, a well-circumscribed 3.0 x 3.0 cm mass was palpated in the right lobe of the thyroid, which was nontender on palpation.

differentials.candidate: Colloid cyst / multinodular goiter with cystic degeneration
differentials.rule_out_reason: Benign cystic nodules are the most common etiology of thyroid cystic lesions; however, high-resolution ultrasound demonstrated an atypical multilocular architecture featuring a large lobulated cyst with multiple adjacent isthmic daughter cysts, and gross operative inspection confirmed a thick fibrous wall delineating the cyst rather than simple colloid degenerating parenchyma.

A solitary cold thyroid nodule on technetium-99m scintigraphy in a young woman requires ruling out thyroid carcinoma; however, fine-needle aspiration was deliberately withheld due to clinical suspicion of an intact parasitic cyst to avoid fatal anaphylaxis and scolicidal spillage, and histopathologic examination showed no cellular atypia or malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Primary Thyroid Hydatid Cyst / Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sonographic appearance of multiple grouped cystic nodules without extrathyroidal lesions led clinicians to suspect echinococcosis and perform a subtotal thyroidectomy without needle biopsy, avoiding anaphylaxis; gross pathology and histopathology definitively confirmed hydatid cyst architecture with laminated membranes and fibrous encapsulation.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old Zimbabwean-born Caucasian patient who had resided in the United Kingdom for four years presented for medical evaluation following a three-week trip to Mozambique (Maputo/Tete). The patient had not taken any antimalarial chemoprophylaxis or preventative medications during the travel.

differentials.candidate: Typhoid fever (Enteric fever / Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteric fever is a leading cause of systemic febrile illness in travelers returning from sub-Saharan Africa without prophylaxis; however, the acute clinical syndrome was rapidly explained by the identification of high circulating intraerythrocytic protozoa rather than enteric bacteremia.

Arboviral infections are prominent differentials for travelers presenting acutely after travel to Mozambique; however, microscopic examination of the peripheral blood demonstrated diagnostic intraerythrocytic stages rather than viral etiology.

Examination of a pre-treatment peripheral blood smear directly revealed circulating intraerythrocytic asexual trophozoites and mature schizonts at a parasitaemia of 1.3%, confirming acute Plasmodium falciparum infection acquired during unprotected travel to Mozambique.

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old Ghanaian-born individual who had resided in the United Kingdom for 22 years presented to the emergency service with an acute, severe systemic febrile illness following a visit to family in Ghana.

differentials.candidate: Gram-negative bacterial sepsis / Severe enteric fever
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe acute prostration after travel to Ghana frequently mimics severe bacterial septicemia; however, blood examination established high-grade intraerythrocytic parasite burden rather than primary bacterial bloodstream infection.

differentials.candidate: Viral hemorrhagic fever / Acute arboviral illness
differentials.rule_out_reason: Travel to West Africa with severe systemic symptoms necessitates consideration of viral hemorrhagic fever or severe arbovirus; this was superseded by the diagnostic detection of asexual erythrocytic parasites on blood smear.

Peripheral blood smear analysis demonstrated asexual Plasmodium falciparum forms with 3.0% parasitaemia in an individual with lost childhood immunity, establishing severe malaria and mandating prompt intravenous quinine treatment.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old European individual, residing in the United Kingdom with no previous history of tropical febrile illnesses, presented acutely with a severe, critical systemic illness after returning from a 10-day trip to Kenya.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A hyperacute critical presentation in a non-immune traveler returning from sub-Saharan Africa raises immediate concern for fulminant bacterial septicemia; urgent peripheral blood smear identified overwhelming intraerythrocytic protozoal invasion rather than bacterial infection.

differentials.candidate: Viral hemorrhagic fever (e.g., Rift Valley fever, Yellow fever)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute travel to Kenya presenting with critical prostration requires triage for viral hemorrhagic fever; however, examination of the peripheral blood demonstrated diagnostic intraerythrocytic parasite forms.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Severe Plasmodium falciparum Malaria with Hyperparasitaemia)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Urgent peripheral blood film microscopy demonstrated extreme Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia of 39% in a non-immune traveler, confirming life-threatening severe malaria that required immediate intravenous artesunate therapy.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male presented with massive hemoptysis of two days duration. For the previous five months, he had been experiencing low-grade fever and recurrent episodes of streaky hemoptysis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute fever, constitutional decline, hemoptysis, and an ill-defined nodular opacity with apical cavities in a 56-year-old male raise strong suspicion for lung cancer; however, MDCT angiography showed inflammatory necrosis with ground glass opacities, tree-in-bud nodules, and vascular hypertrophy without a malignant tumor mass.

Rasmussen aneurysm is the classic cause of life-threatening hemoptysis in patients with history of cavitary lung disease, typically arising from a branch of the pulmonary artery bordering a cavity; however, contrast MDCT angiography traced the aneurysm directly to the systemic bronchial artery circulation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Reactivated Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Bronchial Artery Aneurysm)
differentials.rule_out_reason: MDCT angiography and selective catheterization identified active tuberculous inflammation (necrotic nodule with surrounding ground-glass nodules) feeding a 3 x 5 mm right bronchial artery aneurysm, which was successfully treated with transcatheter polyvinyl alcohol particle embolization alongside antimycobacterial therapy.

clinical_summary: A right-handed adolescent female originally from India who migrated to Malaysia presented with medically refractory focal seizures. At age 9 in India, she experienced an initial simple partial seizure characterized by clonic shaking of her right hand lasting one minute.

differentials.candidate: Low-grade cerebral neoplasm / Ganglioglioma / Cavernous malformation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Focal cortical calcification presenting with medically refractory motor seizures in a young person raises suspicion for a low-grade tumor or vascular malformation; however, long-term neuroimaging showed a stationary calcified core with fluctuating perilesional inflammatory edema rather than a progressive expansile neoplasm, and surgical pathology showed no neoplastic cells.

Tuberculomas are the leading cause of solitary ring-enhancing granulomas in the Indian subcontinent; however, the lesion demonstrated a dense punctate calcified core with cyclical episodic perilesional edema rather than expanding caseation, and histology confirmed a necrotic cystic cavity surrounded by gliosis.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Calcified Neurocysticercosis Granuloma with Perilesional Edema)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Stereotactic craniotomy and resection of the epileptogenic calcified lesion revealed an encapsulated cystic structure surrounded by gliotic parenchyma containing necrotic parasitic remnants, confirming an involuted calcified Taenia solium metacestode causing recurrent perilesional inflammatory edema and intractable seizures.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old man presented with sudden onset of headache, nausea, and giddiness of two days duration. He did not have any significant past medical history.

differentials.candidate: Pontine ischemic stroke (Infarction of the medial longitudinal fasciculus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute sudden onset of internuclear ophthalmoplegia with skew deviation in an adult most commonly represents brainstem ischemia; however, neuroimaging demonstrated a discrete cystic lesion rather than microvascular or thromboembolic ischemic infarction.

Isolated internuclear ophthalmoplegia in a young adult is a classic hallmark of demyelinating plaques in the dorsal pons; however, neuroimaging showed an isolated cystic lesion with an intracavitary scolex rather than multiple sclerosis plaques.

Brain MRI demonstrated a characteristic well-defined cystic lesion containing an intracavitary scolex on the right side of the mid-pons, fulfilling absolute diagnostic criteria for neurocysticercosis; the patient experienced complete recovery following albendazole and corticosteroid therapy.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old Ugandan male presented to a tertiary referral hospital in Kenya with progressive, symmetrical darkening and severe ischemic pain of all four extremities. Five days earlier, he had presented with severe headache and joint pain to a local health facility in Uganda, where an acute systemic febrile infection was identified and parenteral antimicrobial therapy initiated.

differentials.candidate: Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger's disease) / Atherosclerotic peripheral vascular disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute distal extremity gangrene suggests severe obliterative vasculopathy or thromboembolism; however, the patient was a non-smoker without history of diabetes or cardiovascular risk factors, presenting with an acute febrile onset following infection.

differentials.candidate: Purpura fulminans / Bacterial sepsis-induced Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Symmetrical peripheral gangrene is classically caused by severe bacterial septic shock (e.g., Neisseria meningitidis or Streptococcus pneumoniae); however, the patient had no primary bacterial septic focus and tests for viral and systemic pathogens were negative.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Symmetrical Peripheral Gangrene complicating Severe Plasmodium falciparum Malaria)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient's acute syndrome was triggered by severe Plasmodium falciparum infection, where intense microvascular sequestration, parasitized red blood cell rigidity, and hypercoagulability obstructed digital microcirculation, resulting in bilateral symmetrical peripheral gangrene requiring eventual transmetatarsal and ray amputations.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old man with no relevant medical history was evaluated in the internal medicine clinic reporting a 6-day history of poorly defined malaise, night sweats, sleeplessness, tinnitus, and episodic diarrhea without blood or pathologic products.

differentials.candidate: Intestinal parasitic infection / Amebiasis (Entamoeba histolytica and helminths)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Stool microscopy identified multiple intestinal parasites that could intuitively account for the patient's episodic diarrhea; however, intestinal parasitosis alone could not account for systemic symptoms including night sweats, malaise, and tinnitus.

Constitutional symptoms following a trip to the Caribbean raise concern for arboviral illness; however, the absence of fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia made acute arbovirus improbable.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Imported Mixed Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium malariae Malaria)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Despite an afebrile presentation and Caribbean travel history, routine peripheral blood film evaluation revealed diagnostic intraerythrocytic trophozoites of both P. vivax and P. malariae, which cleared following treatment with chloroquine and primaquine.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with an acute increase in bilateral neck swellings over the past 5 to 6 days, associated with neck pain, fever, and weight loss. Two months earlier, he had been admitted with altered sensorium; he tested positive for HIV with a CD4 count of 48 cells/mm³ and brain MRI was normal.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Paradoxical worsening and massive enlargement of lymph nodes during first-line anti-tubercular therapy raises immediate concern for drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis; however, mycobacterial sensitivity testing demonstrated complete susceptibility to first-line agents.

Rapid emergence of massive conglomerate cervical lymphadenopathy (up to 12 cm) in a patient with severe HIV-related immunosuppression strongly raises suspicion for an aggressive lymphoid malignancy; however, therapeutic aspiration yielded purulent fluid rather than neoplastic tissue.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Tuberculosis Immune Reconstitution Disease with MAC Lymphadenitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The temporal surge in CD4 count following antiretroviral therapy accompanied by inflammatory flare of preexisting mycobacterial infection established Immune Reconstitution Disease (IRD), with nodal aspirate culture yielding Mycobacterium avium complex sensitive to first-line agents, responding favorably to adjunctive corticosteroids and targeted antimicrobials.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old male farmer from a suburban area presents to the otorhinolaryngology outpatient clinic complaining of a painless ulcer in his oral cavity for the past 10 days, accompanied by pain in both ears and throat for 3 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical presentation of an irregular, friable, bleeding alveolar ulcer in an elderly man strongly simulated oral carcinoma; however, serial histopathologic sections showed necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant cells.
Primary chancre or tertiary gummatous ulcer of the oral mucosa was ruled out by non-reactive serology and absence of spirochetes on silver staining.
Granulomatous oral ulcers caused by endemic or opportunistic mycoses were excluded by negative silver stain of the tissue section.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological evaluation of the ulcer margin revealing necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells and positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrating acid-fast bacilli confirmed primary oral tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 1-month history of right flank pain and a heavy sensation. He denies any history of trauma.

differentials.candidate: Simple hepatic cyst / Polycystic liver disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple and polycystic liver lesions are thin-walled without internal septations or multivesiculation, whereas ultrasound and CT in this patient demonstrated complex internal septations and honeycomb multivesicular cysts.

Biliary cystic neoplasms present as multiloculated cystic masses with internal septa, but the classic honeycomb multivesiculated architecture extensively replacing hepatic parenchyma corresponds to hydatid cyst formation.

Hepatic abscesses typically cause acute febrile illness, severe right upper quadrant tenderness, and central liquefaction rather than an indolent 1-month heaviness with well-organized multivesiculated honeycomb cysts without fever.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal ultrasonography showing well-rounded hypoechoic cystic areas with internal septa, corroborated by abdominal CT showing multivesiculated honeycomb cysts (WHO type CE2) extensively occupying the right liver, established cystic echinococcosis, followed by percutaneous fluid aspiration for microscopic analysis.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male who underwent allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation for very severe aplastic anemia 7 months earlier presents with a progressive right foot lesion. His post-transplant immunosuppressive regimen includes oral cyclosporine (therapeutic trough levels maintained between 150–300 ng/mL).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial actinomycetoma presents identically with tumefaction and draining sinuses, but discharged granules in this patient contained fungal septate hyphae rather than bacterial filaments, and culture yielded a mold.
Botryomycosis is a chronic bacterial pseudo-mycosis producing grain-filled sinus tracts, but microscopic examination demonstrated fungal septate hyphae and Sabouraud's agar grew a pathogenic fungus.

Cutaneous mycobacterial or nocardial infections cause chronic nodular and sinus-draining lesions in transplant recipients, but the macroscopic presence of black grains containing thick septate fungal hyphae ruled out bacterial and mycobacterial etiologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of discharged black granules on KOH mount demonstrating septate hyphae, accompanied by Sabouraud's dextrose agar culture growing Madurella mycetomatis and biopsy confirmation of pigmented fungal colonies, established eumycetoma.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old man of East African origin presents to the emergency department with acute constrictive chest pain. His past medical history is notable for acute methanol intoxication resulting in bilateral permanent blindness due to necrosis in the bilateral putamen.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute coronary syndrome was considered due to constrictive chest pain and elevated initial troponin, but excluded by diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression, normal echocardiography, and a rapid decrease in troponin levels.

The patient carried an established diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis based on chronic inflammatory back pain, bilateral sacroiliitis, and knee synovitis; however, marked systemic inflammation, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and pulmonary condensation indicated an infectious granulomatous mimic rather than pure spondyloarthropathy.

Whole-body PET/CT displaying diffuse hypermetabolic mediastinal, hilar, supraclavicular, and cervical lymphadenopathy with skeletal and pulmonary lesions strongly raised suspicion for lymphoma, but pulmonary biopsy demonstrated necrotic granulomas and mycobacteria.

diagnostic_pivot: Whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT showing diffuse hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy, pulmonary condensation, and axial lesions, combined with a strongly positive tuberculin skin test (22 x 27 mm) and bronchoscopic biopsy showing necrotizing granulomas with microbiological isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirmed disseminated tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old man presents to the urology outpatient clinic with a 3-month history of urinary frequency, dysuria, and hematuria. He reports no history of diabetes mellitus, sexually transmitted infections, or trauma.

differentials.candidate: Primary transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder (non-parasitic)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Gross hematuria and a solitary polypoid bladder tumor strongly suggested primary bladder urothelial carcinoma; however, histopathology revealed characteristic parasitic eggs embedded in the bladder mass alongside synchronous squamous and transitional cell carcinomas.

Lower urinary tract symptoms and palpable prostatic enlargement suggested a primary prostatic etiology, but the prostate was smooth, serum PSA was normal for age (2.2 ng/mL), and ultrasonography localized the pathology to a polypoid bladder mass.

differentials.candidate: Sexually transmitted infection / Non-parasitic bacterial cystitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Infectious dysuria and hematuria can result from sexually transmitted or bacterial cystitis, but the patient had no STI history and ultrasound revealed a discrete proliferative polypoid bladder tumor.

diagnostic_pivot: Cystoscopic biopsy of the polypoid bladder tumor demonstrating the presence of Schistosoma haematobium ova embedded in the bladder wall alongside simultaneous squamous cell and superficial transitional cell carcinomas established urinary schistosomiasis with malignant transformation.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of nonbloody diarrhea associated with persistent fever, abdominal fullness, upper gastrointestinal discomfort including mild dysphagia and vomiting, and profound weakness. On physical examination, he is febrile and cachectic with marked pallor and splenomegaly.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Trypanosoma cruzi is endemic in Brazil and displays marked gastrointestinal tropism with motility disturbance and diarrhea, but serologic testing for anti-T. cruzi antibodies was negative.

The combination of chronic diarrhea, pancytopenia, and wasting in an endemic area strongly suggested advanced HIV disease with opportunistic enteropathy; however, anti-HIV testing was negative and CD4 T-lymphocyte counts were preserved.

Identification of Schistosoma mansoni eggs in stool microscopy explained intestinal symptoms, but targeted anti-schistosomal treatment with praziquantel failed to resolve the diarrhea and wasting, demonstrating that schistosomiasis was not the sole cause.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of Leishmania amastigotes in bone marrow aspirates and duodenal biopsies (confirmed by immunohistochemistry and qPCR), combined with the detection of Schistosoma mansoni eggs on stool microscopy, established dual co-infection with visceral leishmaniasis and schistosomiasis causing persistent diarrheal syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man undergoes surveillance thoracic imaging during clinical follow-up for previously treated hepatic disease. He reports feeling in relatively good health without acute cardiopulmonary symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Primary bronchogenic carcinoma / Solitary pulmonary metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 45 mm solid-appearing apical pulmonary lesion in a middle-aged adult raised serious concern for primary lung malignancy, but the lesion demonstrated dramatic regression under antiparasitic therapy and correlated with specific parasitic serologies.

differentials.candidate: Inflammatory degenerative arthropathy / Non-parasitic bone pathology
differentials.rule_out_reason: Abnormal bone structure discovered during elective hip arthroplasty raised concern for metastatic osseous parasitic involvement, but histological analysis did not confirm parasitic disease and favored inflammatory arthritis.

Cystic echinococcosis was distinguished from alveolar echinococcosis by Western blot serology displaying specific 7 kDa and 26–28 kDa diagnostic bands and positive Em2/EmC ELISA specific for Echinococcus multilocularis.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracic CT identification of a 45 mm apical mass, corroborated by serial Western blot serology demonstrating 7 kDa and 26–28 kDa Echinococcus multilocularis antigen binding and complete metabolic and radiologic resolution on PET-CT under albendazole therapy, confirmed recurrent alveolar echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of fever, breathlessness, and continuous dull-aching pain accompanied by a dragging sensation in the left side of her abdomen. She also reports progressive loss of appetite and weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Fever, leukocytosis, and air-fluid levels on CT scan strongly suggested a pyogenic splenic abscess; however, the presence of peripheral eosinophilia and subsequent histology demonstrating daughter cysts without bacterial suppuration ruled out a simple bacterial abscess.
Non-parasitic congenital or post-traumatic splenic cysts are typically unilocular, devoid of peripheral eosinophilia, and lack daughter cyst formations and laminated membranes.

A massive splenic mass associated with weight loss and abdominal distension raised concern for splenic malignancy, but imaging and gross examination revealed multivesicular cystic architecture rather than malignant solid neoplastic tissue.

diagnostic_pivot: Gross and histopathological examination of the resected spleen revealing a three-layered cyst wall containing multiple daughter cysts in a flower-shaped pattern, laminated membranes, hydatid sand, and scolices of Echinococcus granulosus established isolated splenic echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old previously healthy male manual laborer presents to the emergency department with a 6-day history of intermittent fever associated with chills and rigors, and a 5-day history of sudden-onset weakness in both lower limbs, complete loss of sensation below the nipples, and acute urinary retention.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral or para-infectious transverse myelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Sudden-onset flaccid paraplegia with sensory level and bladder paralysis following a brief febrile illness initially suggested acute transverse myelitis; however, CSF examination demonstrated heavy neutrophilic pleocytosis with hypoglycorrhachia and MRI revealed an expanding intramedullary purulent mass.

Neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis and identification of yellowish purulent material loosely attached to the conus medullaris suggested a bacterial pyogenic abscess, but bacterial smears and aerobic/anaerobic cultures were negative and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics failed to halt disease progression.
Fungal infections can produce indolent or progressive intramedullary masses, but potassium hydroxide mounts, fungal stains, and fungal cultures were repeatedly negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Isolation and growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis colonies in 12 B medium of the BACTEC 460 TB system after 6 weeks of incubation from surgical neural tissue, accompanied by a strongly reactive Mantoux test (24 mm), confirmed primary intramedullary holocord tubercular abscess.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old man presents to the hospital with a generalized erythematous maculopapular rash distributed across his trunk and extremities. His past medical history includes long-standing hypertension and diabetes mellitus treated with amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 500 mg, and glipizide 5 mg daily.

differentials.candidate: Systemic autoimmune vasculitis (ANCA-associated vasculitis or SLE)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Palpable purpura, anemia, and leukocytosis mimicked systemic autoimmune small vessel vasculitis, but ANA and ANCA serologic tests were negative, and urinalysis showed no evidence of renal glomerulonephritis.

Severe cholestatic jaundice and purpuric eruptions raised suspicion for hepatitis B or C virus-induced immune complex vasculitis, but viral serologies were negative and abdominal ultrasound was unremarkable.

Although the initial generalized exanthem resolved upon drug withdrawal, the subsequent emergence of fixed, non-blanchable annular purpuric lesions indicated true necrotizing leukocytoclastic vasculitis rather than a simple benign exanthematous eruption.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of a purpuric annular skin biopsy showing perivascular and interstitial neutrophil infiltration with erythrocyte extravasation and fibrin deposition, coupled with direct immunofluorescence demonstrating IgA, IgM, and C3 deposition along superficial dermal blood vessels, confirmed drug-induced leukocytoclastic vasculitis and cholestasis.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old malnourished boy is referred with a 1-month history of fever and a 14-day history of right upper abdominal pain, loose motions, and vomiting. His prior medical history is unremarkable.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever, hepatomegaly, and liver abscess with secondary septic thrombophlebitis. However, pus aspirate from the surgically deroofed cavity showed no pyogenic bacteria on culture or microscopy.

differentials.candidate: Primary Budd-Chiari syndrome / Inferior vena cava thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary hepatic vein or inferior vena cava thrombosis causes hepatomegaly and ascites, but imaging revealed that the cavoatrial thrombus originated from contiguous inflammatory and mechanical extension of a solitary hepatic abscess rather than a primary prothrombotic state.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of a solitary left-lobe hepatic abscess with contiguous caval extension, positive serum amebic ELISA antibody testing, and evacuation of classic sterile anchovy sauce pus confirmed amebic liver abscess complicated by cavoatrial thrombosis.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old male, originally a resident of Bihar, presents to an outpatient department in New Delhi with a history of longstanding fever, progressive abdominal distention, significant weight loss, and generalized weakness over the preceding ten to twelve months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given chronic fever, constitutional wasting, hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia in an endemic area. Excluded by negative tuberculin skin testing and absence of caseating granulomas or mycobacteria.

differentials.candidate: Chronic viral infection (HIV / Hepatitis B / Hepatitis C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as causes of chronic hepatosplenomegaly, wasting, and cytopenias. Excluded by nonreactive serological assays.

differentials.candidate: Hematologic malignancy / Primary bone marrow disorder
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever, massive splenomegaly, and pancytopenia. Bone marrow examination showed reactive plasmacytosis without leukemic blasts, lymphoma infiltration, or aplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative initial bone marrow microscopy, strong endemic suspicion and marked hypergammaglobulinemia demonstrated by a strongly positive aldehyde test led to diagnostic splenic aspiration, which demonstrated hallmark amastigotes.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old female patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presents with a palpable mass in the left breast associated with pain of long duration. She reports no nipple discharge and no fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's age and a large, dense, rapidly expanding or long-standing lobulated, circumscribed breast mass. Excluded as the lesion lacked internal vascularity on Doppler interrogation and histology showed acellular parasitic membranes rather than fibroepithelial neoplasia.

Considered given the large dense mass coded as BI-RADS 4A in an older female. Excluded by absent Doppler flow, lack of internal enhancement on cross-sectional imaging, and absence of malignant epithelial or stromal proliferation on core biopsy.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasonographic demonstration of peripheral anechoic daughter cysts with absent internal vascularity, followed by core needle biopsy revealing fragmented acellular laminated eosinophilic membranes, definitively established primary breast hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male presents with fever, cough, and breathlessness of 2 months' duration, accompanied by swelling, redness, and pain affecting both ankles for the preceding 7 days. Two months earlier, he had received unsuccessful treatment for suspected enteric fever, at which time he was also newly diagnosed with diabetes mellitus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of prolonged fever, toxic appearance, and splenomegaly. Excluded by lack of clinical response to prior empiric therapy and negative Widal serology and urine cultures.
Considered given the 2-month history of fever, cough, dyspnea, and homogenous lobar consolidation in an uncontrolled diabetic host. Excluded by negative serial acid-fast sputum examinations.

diagnostic_pivot: Severe multifocal sepsis presenting with consolidation, jaundice, and septic arthritis in a poorly controlled diabetic patient prompted blood, endotracheal, and joint aspirate cultures, which yielded nonfermenting, oxidase-positive, wrinkled colonies identified as Burkholderia pseudomallei.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus presents with intermittent fever occurring on and off over the preceding 1 to 1.5 years, along with cough, pain, and swelling of the left knee for the past 2 weeks.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary explanation for protracted undulating fever over 1–1.5 years accompanied by cough, bilateral fluffy nodular lung opacities, and monoarthritis in a diabetic patient. Excluded by negative sputum acid-fast stain and mycobacterial culture.
Considered as alternative causes of persistent or recurrent febrile illness in an endemic region. Excluded by nonreactive malaria antigen and Widal serological testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Recurrent fevers with sudden respiratory failure and septic arthritis in a diabetic host culminated in microbiological confirmation when peripheral blood cultures drawn at admission and during fever spikes isolated Burkholderia pseudomallei.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old Chinese girl presents with a 3-week history of low-grade fever and cough. Her previous medical history is unremarkable.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary concern given multiple hypoechoic macronodules throughout the liver and spleen, thoracic and abdominal lymphadenopathy, and anemia. Excluded by liver and intestinal biopsies demonstrating necrotizing caseating granulomas without neoplastic cells.

Considered as a cause of hepatosplenic granulomatous nodules and lymphadenopathy, particularly in immunosuppressed patients. Ruled out as the patient was HIV-negative and cultures specifically isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Strong tuberculin reactivity (20 mm) and positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold led to colonoscopic and liver biopsies showing caseating granulomas, with definitive confirmation provided by sputum and gastric lavage cultures growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old male is referred to a gastroenterology department with a 6-month history of recurrent epigastric pain, nausea, and occasional vomiting, accompanied by significant weight loss over the preceding 2 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis given the patient's substantial weight loss, obstructive symptoms, and an irregular infiltrative antral mass on endoscopy and CT. Excluded by histopathological evaluation of multiple biopsies showing caseating granulomas without dysplastic or malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Peptic ulcer disease with cicatricial stenosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chronic gnawing epigastric pain and gastric outlet obstruction. Excluded because endoscopic and cross-sectional imaging revealed a prominent hypertrophic, irregular mass lesion rather than benign chronic peptic ulcer scarring.

diagnostic_pivot: Targeted endoscopic mucosal biopsies revealed multiple epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans-type giant cells and caseation necrosis, with definitive confirmation provided by positive tissue PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old pregnant woman with an 11-year history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection is admitted at 32 weeks of gestation with clinical manifestations of intracranial hypertension and meningoencephalitis, including temporospatial disorientation, slurred speech, nausea, vomiting, and hemiparesis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect for a focal central nervous system mass lesion with edema in a severely immunocompromised patient with AIDS and a CD4 count under 100 cells/uL. Excluded by negative Toxoplasma gondii serological assays.
Considered as a potential etiology of meningoencephalitis and focal mass lesions in advanced HIV infection. Excluded by nonreactive Treponema pallidum serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Endemic exposure history in Argentina combined with severe immunosuppression raised suspicion for reactivated Chagas disease, which was confirmed by positive anti-T. cruzi serology, direct detection of circulating parasites by microhematocrit, and high-level parasitic DNA on quantitative PCR.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old male with no previous medical history presents to a surgical unit with a 3-day history of abdominal pain that began in the epigastrium and subsequent localization to the right iliac fossa, associated with multiple bouts of vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the presumptive working diagnosis due to migratory right lower quadrant pain, vomiting, fever, localized guarding, and pericecal fluid collection. Excluded intraoperatively by the finding of a normal appendix and histopathology demonstrating no gross or microscopic appendiceal inflammation.

Considered given the intraoperative finding of multiple enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes in a pediatric patient with lower abdominal pain. Excluded as a primary bacterial etiology given progressive bicytopenia, absence of leukocytosis, and self-limited viral course.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of severe right lower quadrant pain with marked leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in an endemic Caribbean setting, followed by negative appendiceal histology, prompted viral testing that confirmed acute infection via positive dengue IgM and IgG ELISA.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old female presents with a 4-month history of intense frontal headaches, progressive loss of vision, and tonic seizures of the lower extremities. On physical examination, the patient is afebrile with normal vital signs.

differentials.candidate: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary preoperative presumptive diagnosis given the patient's age and an anterior third-ventricular mass causing acute-on-chronic obstructive hydrocephalus. Excluded on surgical pathology, which revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than a mucin-filled cyst.

Considered due to the solid, nodular, contrast-enhancing appearance in the third ventricle with obstructive ventricular dilation in a child. Excluded by histopathological demonstration of central caseous necrosis surrounded by granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Total microsurgical resection via a subchoroidal approach demonstrated central necrosis surrounded by granulomatous inflammation, definitively confirmed as mycobacterial disease by positive Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of left flank pain and progressive severe obstructive urinary symptoms. His past medical history is notable for multiple laparotomies following abdominal gunshot injuries in 1984, including splenectomy, appendectomy, and cholecystectomy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The large size, ureteral encasement, irregular wall, and 2-cm soft tissue component raised concern for a pelvic sarcoma or cystic neoplasm; however, exploratory laparotomy and surgical histopathology demonstrated characteristic benign hydatid cyst architecture rather than neoplastic tissue.

A massive retrovesical cystic collection causing persistent suprapubic mass and urinary outlet obstruction could represent a giant bladder diverticulum, but endoscopic visualization of the bladder lumen demonstrated normal mucosa without any diverticular opening.

diagnostic_pivot: Although indirect hemagglutination serology was negative (< 1:32), exploratory laparotomy with pericystectomy and histopathologic examination of the surgical specimen established hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 76-year-old Hispanic male presents with a 2-month history of progressive fatigue, nausea, intractable vomiting, and an unintentional 30-pound weight loss. His past medical history is significant for idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura diagnosed 4 months ago, for which he received a 3-week course of systemic corticosteroids.

differentials.candidate: Hypovolemic hyponatremia secondary to gastrointestinal losses
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe hyponatremia in the context of intractable vomiting initially suggested volume depletion; however, volume expansion with isotonic saline failed to correct sodium levels, while high urine osmolality with plasma hypo-osmolality confirmed SIADH.

differentials.candidate: Central nervous system lesion / intracranial mass causing SIADH
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given his age and 40 pack-year smoking history, an occult central nervous system neoplasm or intracranial pathology causing SIADH was considered, but structural neuroimaging was entirely normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Upper endoscopy performed to evaluate intractable vomiting revealed gastroduodenal inflammation, and histopathology of duodenal mucosal biopsies combined with stool microscopy demonstrated characteristic parasitic larvae confirming hyperinfection.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 23-year-old man presents with a 4-day history of fever, occasional headache, and vomiting. Two days prior to hospital admission, he suffered a generalized tonic-clonic seizure followed by altered sensorium and left-sided weakness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple intracranial ring-enhancing lesions with marked vasogenic edema raised strong clinical consideration for cerebral toxoplasmosis; however, postmortem serological assays and CSF antibodies were negative for Toxoplasma gondii, and basal exudate smears demonstrated acid-fast bacilli.

differentials.candidate: Systemic prothrombotic vasculopathy / autoimmune venous thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe deep cerebral venous thrombosis in a healthy young man warranted investigation for systemic thrombophilic or autoimmune vasculitic conditions, but extensive autoimmune and biochemical serologies were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microbiological smear of the thick basal brain exudates revealed acid-fast bacilli by Ziehl-Neelsen stain, establishing tuberculous thrombophlebitis as the underlying etiology of the deep venous infarction.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male agricultural laborer presents with a 7-day history of fever and headache, preceded by a 1-year history of three generalized tonic-clonic seizures, progressive irritability, explosive angry outbursts, and inability to recognize family members.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple ring- and disc-enhancing parenchymal lesions in an endemic region raised strong suspicion for cerebral toxoplasmosis; however, postmortem CSF and serologic testing were negative for Toxoplasma gondii, and basal exudate smears demonstrated acid-fast bacilli.

A 1-year history of seizures and multiple enhancing brain lesions in a rural agricultural worker strongly suggested neurocysticercosis; however, CSF and serum testing for cysticercosis were negative, while mycobacterial immune complexes and antibodies were confirmed.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of the thick basal subarachnoid exudate revealed numerous acid-fast organisms on Ziehl-Neelsen stain, establishing mycobacterial infection as the cause of extensive dural venous and cortical vein thrombophlebitis.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old adolescent presents with a history of recurrent abdominal pain and fever. The illness began 1 year earlier with acute abdominal pain originating in the right hypochondrium that resolved with non-specific symptomatic treatment without initial diagnostic imaging.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The presence of numerous palpable masses spread throughout the peritoneal cavity in an adolescent raised concern for malignant peritoneal dissemination; however, imaging showed purely cystic architecture with internal vesicles, and surgical exploration revealed encapsulated benign cysts without malignant infiltration.

Recurrent fevers, severe abdominal pain, high CRP, and multi-organ fluid collections could represent tuberculous peritonitis or pyogenic abscesses; however, cross-sectional imaging identified non-inflammatory cyst walls with a type 5 calcified cyst and multivesicular daughter cyst architecture.

diagnostic_pivot: Median laparotomy enabled direct surgical removal of all 39 intraperitoneal and visceral cysts, with successful extraction and identification of diagnostic germinal membranes from the hepatic and splenic lesions.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old man presents with progressive lower extremity weakness and sensory loss. Two months prior to admission, he underwent an open cholecystectomy for cholecystolithiasis under epidural anesthesia at a community hospital.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Post-anesthetic acute transverse myelitis was initially diagnosed and treated aggressively with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins; however, complete absence of clinical response after 2 months and subsequent focal mass enlargement argued against uncomplicated idiopathic demyelinating myelitis.

Transient radicular shooting pain during catheterization and use of epinephrine raised suspicion for anterior spinal artery ischemia; however, the absence of intraoperative hypotension, prominent loss of posterior column proprioception, and well-circumscribed ring enhancement on MRI were incompatible with SCI.

diagnostic_pivot: Due to progressive neurological deterioration and an ambiguous ring-enhancing intramedullary mass, surgical laminectomy and complete microsurgical excision were performed; histopathological analysis established a tuberculous granulomatous lesion.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old male presents with a 5-cm wide non-healing ulcerative lesion in the anterior floor of the mouth that has persisted for 7 months. On physical examination, the lesion demonstrates aggressive local invasion into the ventral aspect of the tongue and the mandibular alveolar ridge.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic regional lymphadenopathy from oral squamous cell carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: In the setting of a biopsy-proven invasive T4a oral floor carcinoma, the prominent 3-cm submandibular lymph node was clinically presumed to represent regional metastasis; unexpectedly, exhaustive pathologic evaluation of 97 resected cervical nodes demonstrated complete absence of metastatic carcinoma.

differentials.candidate: Reactive or secondary bacterial submandibular lymphadenitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Non-neoplastic cervical adenopathy secondary to an infected oral ulceration typically reflects non-specific reactive follicular hyperplasia or acute bacterial lymphadenitis; however, histopathology revealed chronic granulomatous infection caused by an endemic dimorphic fungus.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of the bilateral neck dissection specimen unexpectedly demonstrated paracoccidioidomycosis within a solitary submandibular lymph node, revealing a synchronous granulomatous mycosis mimicking nodal metastasis.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male garment factory worker presents with a 3-month history of an abnormal band-like sensation across his upper abdomen, unaccompanied by local abdominal or spinal pain. Concurrently, he noted urinary hesitancy, a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying, and a feeling of inadequate bowel evacuation.

differentials.candidate: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor (e.g., astrocytoma, ependymoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A well-circumscribed, brilliantly ring-enhancing solitary intramedullary cord mass with perilesional edema in a patient with a normal chest X-ray and negative Mantoux test was radiologically diagnosed as an intramedullary neoplasm; however, surgical excision and histopathology revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than neoplastic proliferation.

Subacute descending sensory loss and bilateral spastic paraparesis can signify inflammatory myelitis, but neuroimaging revealed a discrete 16 x 10 mm expansile mass with central flow void and intense ring enhancement rather than non-expansile plaque-like signal alteration.

diagnostic_pivot: Microsurgical resection via D3-D4 laminectomy enabled total excision of the fleshy mass, and histopathologic examination revealed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells and microscopic demonstration of acid-fast bacilli typical of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old woman with a rural background presents to the outpatient clinic with a 3-year history of headache and a 6-month history of difficulty walking. On physical examination, general physical findings are unremarkable.

differentials.candidate: Intraventricular neuroepithelial cyst (colloid cyst / ependymal cyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A non-enhancing cystic mass near the foramen of Monro causing unilateral ventricular obstruction commonly represents a colloid or ependymal cyst; however, these benign cysts are unilocular and do not display internal daughter cysts or an acetate peak on spectroscopy.

differentials.candidate: Intraventricular cystic neoplasm (e.g., central neurocytoma, choroid plexus papilloma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cystic intraventricular neoplasms typically exhibit solid contrast-enhancing mural components and elevated choline peaks on MRS; in contrast, this lesion demonstrated complete lack of contrast enhancement and a prominent acetate resonance.

diagnostic_pivot: Microsurgical left frontal craniotomy with saline hydrodissection of the cleavage plane allowed intact removal of the cystic mass, with histopathologic examination establishing the definitive diagnosis of a hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old man presents with an 18-month history of intermittent high-grade fevers and non-radiating right lower quadrant abdominal pain, for which he had sought care at five different healthcare facilities without symptomatic improvement.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Prominent systemic constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, 10% weight loss) combined with widespread generalized painless lymphadenopathy and parahilar nodes strongly mimicked a lymphoproliferative disorder; however, lymph node biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant lymphoid architecture.

differentials.candidate: Persistent mesenteric adenitis / post-appendectomy abdominal pathology
differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic right lower quadrant pain that had led to prior appendectomy suggested localized mesenteric adenitis; however, abdominal ultrasonography was normal, and widespread superficial and mediastinal lymphadenopathy demonstrated systemic granulomatous dissemination.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of an excised cervical lymph node demonstrated classic necrotizing granulomas containing Langhans giant cells and central caseation necrosis, confirming tuberculous lymphadenitis in the setting of parahilar adenopathy.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old woman presents for oncologic evaluation and staging. She had sought medical attention complaining of vaginal itching and pain, and gynecological examination revealed a vulvar mass with vaginal invasion.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (pulmonary metastasis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis given the known invasive vulvar carcinoma with spiculated pulmonary nodules on staging CT (initially staged as T3 N0 M1, stage IV). However, isolated hematogenous pulmonary metastasis without regional pelvic or inguinal lymph node involvement is highly atypical for vulvar squamous cell carcinoma, and lung biopsy showed no evidence of neoplasia.

Considered due to the patient's age and the spiculated, irregular morphology of the pulmonary nodules on thoracic CT. Ruled out by histopathological examination of the lung nodules, which showed no malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous biopsy of the pulmonary nodules demonstrated chronic inflammatory reaction with granulomas, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining confirmed the presence of acid-fast bacilli without evidence of malignancy, establishing pulmonary tuberculosis and allowing curative-intent resection of the localized vulvar carcinoma.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old woman with a medical history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension presents with jaundice and abdominal pain. An abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan reveals a 4.7 cm periampullary mass at its longest axis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis given the presence of bilateral 1.5 cm pulmonary nodules on staging imaging in a patient with biopsy-proven duodenal adenocarcinoma, raising suspicion of stage IV metastatic disease. However, lung nodule biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

Considered as a potential synchronous secondary neoplasm given bilateral discrete pulmonary nodules in an elderly patient. Excluded by histopathology of the lung lesions showing inflammatory granulomatous tissue without neoplastic features.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous biopsies of the pulmonary nodules demonstrated chronic inflammatory granulomatous reaction with caseous necrosis, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrated acid-fast bacilli, confirming pulmonary tuberculosis and enabling curative surgical resection of the localized T4 N0 M0 duodenal adenocarcinoma.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old female presents to the hospital with fever and headache. Two months prior, she had undergone an elective splenectomy following the incidental discovery of an asymptomatic multilocular splenic mass with splenomegaly on routine physical examination; surgical exploration had revealed tense adhesions and caseous curdled suppuration, and postoperative histology reported intrasplenic granulation tissue with necrosis, but she had received no...

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic brain abscess with septic pulmonary emboli
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute fever, headache, leukocytosis, elevated CRP, and solitary intracranial abscess with midline shift. However, pyogenic bacterial infections typically present with fulminant acute sepsis, neutrophilic meningitis, and absence of extensive multiorgan caseating granulomatous disease.

differentials.candidate: Primary central nervous system neoplasm (e.g., high-grade glioma or metastatic disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the large 4.0 x 3.3 cm mass in the right frontal lobe causing mass effect and midline shift. However, the concurrent presence of fever, multiple cavitary lung nodules, and elevated CSF protein indicated a multi-system infectious etiology rather than isolated primary neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Delayed intraoperative splenic pus cultures confirmed bacillary growth, revealing that surgical manipulation of the splenic lesion without postoperative coverage led to hematogenous dissemination, resulting in tuberculous brain abscess and cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old male presents to the emergency room with worsening headaches and visual decline. He had emigrated from Mexico 13 months prior to presentation and reports no other significant medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's immigration from an endemic region, basilar cistern involvement, elevated opening pressure, and lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated CSF protein. However, tuberculous meningitis typically presents with constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss), profound CSF hypoglycorrhachia, and thick basilar pachymeningeal/leptomeningeal enhancement rather than numerous grape-like non-enhancing cysts.

Considered because cryptococcal infection can cause communicating hydrocephalus, gelatinous pseudocysts (soap-bubble lesions) in basal cisterns and Virchow-Robin spaces, and elevated intracranial pressure. However, the patient was immunocompetent with a normal peripheral white count and was subsequently confirmed to have parasitic cysticercal antibodies.

Considered due to the presence of non-enhancing CSF-isointense cystic lesions in the subarachnoid space and sylvian fissures. However, arachnoid cysts are congenital, typically solitary and non-progressive, and do not cause progressive hydrocephalus, papilledema, CSF pleocytosis, elevated protein, or spinal dissemination.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis of racemose neurocysticercosis was established by positive CSF cysticercus antibody ELISA testing in conjunction with the characteristic cisternal multi-cystic architecture on neuroimaging and recent immigration from Mexico.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old primigravida presents for medical and obstetric management. She had a history of pulmonary disease at age 14 for which she received a 6-month antimicrobial regimen.

differentials.candidate: Drug-susceptible pulmonary infection with treatment non-adherence or malabsorption
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because treatment failure is most commonly caused by poor compliance or pharmacokinetic subtherapeutic dosing during first-line therapy. However, formal phenotypic drug susceptibility testing documented confirmed in vitro resistance to primary agents.

Considered given the persistent acid-fast bacillary smear positivity and failure to respond to standard first-line antimicrobial therapy. Ruled out by specific microbiological isolation and drug resistance profiling demonstrating resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum drug susceptibility testing confirmed dual resistance to both isoniazid and rifampicin, establishing the diagnosis of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) requiring an individualized second-line antimicrobial regimen throughout pregnancy.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old man presents with chief complaints of recurrent right hypochondrial pain, loss of appetite, and dyspepsia for the past 1 month. He reports no fever, chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary preoperative provisional diagnosis given the combination of an intraluminal gallbladder mass, cholelithiasis, thickened gallbladder wall, and apparent infiltration across the liver-gallbladder interface on contrast-enhanced CT. However, frozen-section examination and definitive histopathology revealed no evidence of malignant neoplasia.

Considered as an inflammatory mimic of gallbladder carcinoma that produces severe mural thickening, cholelithiasis, and local fibrous adherence/invasion into hepatic parenchyma. Ruled out by characteristic histopathological findings of tuberculous granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological evaluation of the resected gallbladder demonstrated chronic epithelioid granulomas with typical Langhans giant cells in the absence of malignancy, supported by a positive Mantoux tuberculin skin test, establishing gallbladder tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old previously healthy male farmer from rural South India presents to the emergency department with high-grade, intermittent fever for 4 days, accompanied by chills, rigors, headache with retro-orbital pain, severe myalgia, and right upper abdominal pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's rural agricultural occupation, acute febrile illness, diffuse rash, hepatomegaly, and multiorgan dysfunction. Ruled out clinically by the absence of a pathognomonic necrotic eschar and by confirmatory dengue serology.

Considered because of the patient's occupational farming exposure, severe myalgia, hepatic transaminitis, renal dysfunction, and thrombocytopenia. However, leptospirosis rarely causes acute capillary permeability with severe plasma leakage (bilateral effusions and ascites) and hemoconcentration, and serology confirmed dengue infection.

Considered given the presentation of acute high-grade intermittent fever with chills and rigors in an endemic area. Excluded by peripheral blood smear evaluation and positive dengue serological testing.

differentials.candidate: Primary acute viral, toxic, or ischemic hepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prominent right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness and significant hepatic transaminase elevation. Ruled out as the primary etiology by the multisystem manifestations, hemoconcentration, and positive dengue serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological testing demonstrated positive IgM and IgG antibodies to dengue virus in the presence of thrombocytopenia, hemoconcentration, and third-space plasma leakage, establishing dengue hemorrhagic fever; subsequent persistent fever with bicytopenia, extreme hyperferritinemia, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis confirmed reactive secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old boy from a rural area is brought to the emergency department with fever, headache, and weight loss of 4 months duration, which acutely worsened over the past week.

differentials.candidate: Isolated central nervous system tuberculomas / tuberculous meningitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the initial presumptive diagnosis given chronic fever, recurrent chest infections, brother's fatal disseminated disease, and ring-enhancing intracranial lesions, prompting empiric therapy. However, craniotomy and histopathological examination of the excised brain abscesses revealed fungal hyphae rather than tuberculous abscesses.

Considered due to the marked leukocytosis (17,900/µL), elevated ESR, purulent brain collection, and acute neurological decline with focal weakness. Ruled out by histopathology and microbiological cultures of the excised abscess wall, which identified fungal hyphae and grew Aspergillus without pyogenic bacteria.

diagnostic_pivot: Neurosurgical excision of the brain abscesses confirmed Aspergillus hyphae, while tracheal aspirate testing proved positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis by PCR assay; subsequent negative nitroblue-tetrazolium (NBT) testing diagnosed underlying chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) facilitating dual opportunistic fungal and mycobacterial infection.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old woman with no prior medical history is admitted to the medical ward presenting with a 3-day history of high fever, headache, progressively reducing platelet count, and increasing hematocrit.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary etiology for central retinal vein occlusion occurring in a young patient under 50 years of age without vascular risk factors. Ruled out by normal coagulopathy and thrombophilia workup, including normal protein C activity, protein S activity, antithrombin activity, anti-cardiolipin antibodies, and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein 1 antibodies.

differentials.candidate: Atherosclerotic, hypertensive, or diabetic microvascular disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as standard conventional risk factors for central retinal vein occlusion. Ruled out by absence of chronic medical illness, normal blood pressure, and completely normal fasting blood sugar and lipid panels.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis of acute dengue virus infection was established by a reactive Dengue NS-1 antigen test in the setting of hemoconcentration and thrombocytopenia; subsequent ophthalmologic evaluation confirmed right central retinal vein occlusion with extensive intraretinal hemorrhages and macular edema directly triggered by dengue-associated endothelial inflammation and hemoconcentration.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old Nigerian woman with a history of sickle cell disease presents to the hospital with a chief complaint of a progressively enlarging mass on her left flank over the past 2 years.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis and retroperitoneal abscess (e.g., Salmonella or Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered high on the differential because patients with sickle cell disease are predisposed to bone infarcts and pyogenic osteomyelitis/bacteremia from Salmonella and Staphylococcus aureus. However, pyogenic spondylodiscitis typically presents acutely with high fevers, severe spinal tenderness, leukocytosis, and bacteremia, whereas this patient had an indolent 2-year afebrile course, normal WBC, negative routine blood cultures, and sterile initial Gram stains.

differentials.candidate: Soft tissue neoplasm or chronic organized hematoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's hemoglobinopathy and a slowly growing, painless, non-erythematous fluctuant flank mass over several years without systemic B symptoms. Ruled out by MRI showing destructive L4-L5 diskitis and osteomyelitis with contiguous retroperitoneal fluid tracking, and thick viscous purulent fluid on aspiration.

diagnostic_pivot: Aspiration of the viscous flank mass yielded purulent fluid with 82% neutrophils, and subsequent mycobacterial cultures confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis from the drained abscess, confirming spinal tuberculosis with an extensive gravitating cold abscess.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male residing in India with no prior medical history presents with a 1-month history of low-grade fever, inflammatory pain and morning stiffness in the small joints of both hands, generalized weakness, and anorexia with a 3-kg weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given auricular chondritis sparing the lobules, inflammatory polyarthralgia, and high inflammatory markers; ruled out by negative autoimmune workup and cutaneous biopsy proving mycobacterial etiology.

Considered due to the combination of chondritis, systemic inflammatory symptoms, and glomerulonephritis/proteinuria; ruled out by the absence of pulmonary/sinus involvement and negative ANCA serology.
Considered for external ear inflammation, but ruled out by subacute 1-month duration and lack of response to two courses of broad-spectrum antibiotics.
Rare structural causes of auricular chondritis, excluded by detailed exposure history.

diagnostic_pivot: Skin punch biopsy of the extensor elbow lesions revealed perivascular/periadnexal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with ill-formed granulomas, and positive Ziehl-Neelsen and Fite-Faraco staining confirmed acid-fast bacilli.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old previously healthy and immunocompetent male presents for medical evaluation of the prostate. Physical examination, routine biological investigations, and diagnostic imaging reveal prostatic abnormalities that raise a strong clinical suspicion of prostate cancer.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Highly suspected based on clinical findings, biological investigations, and prostatic imaging; ruled out when histopathologic evaluation of needle core biopsy tissue revealed granulomatous inflammatory lesions rather than adenocarcinoma.
Considered in patients presenting with chronic prostatic lesions, but differentiated by histological identification of specific tuberculous lesions rather than ordinary chronic inflammatory changes.

diagnostic_pivot: Transrectal needle biopsy of the prostate was performed to evaluate the suspected malignancy, and histological examination definitively identified tuberculous lesions.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old man from a lower socioeconomic background presents with a 6-month history of progressive lower urinary tract obstructive symptoms, specifically marked urinary frequency and dysuria. These symptoms have been accompanied by evening low-grade fevers, asthenia, anorexia, and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg over six months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected based on the hard, nodular prostate on digital rectal examination, elevated serum PSA of 8 ng/mL, and heterogeneous gland architecture on ultrasound; disproved when histopathologic examination of core biopsies showed no neoplastic tissue.
Considered given obstructive urinary symptoms and dysuria, but routine urine microbiological culture was sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Transrectal needle core biopsy of the prostate disproved malignancy and demonstrated follicles with multinucleated giant cells and caseous necrosis characteristic of prostatic mycobacterial infection.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old boy of Nigerian descent living in Italy presents to the emergency room with a 3-day history of fever, accompanied by vomiting and generalized abdominal pain that began two days after returning from a 1-month visit to Nigeria.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected upon arrival in the emergency department because of acute fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain in a pediatric patient; ruled out as symptoms were driven by tropical parasitic infection with splenomegaly.
Considered when the patient exhibited persistent right upper quadrant pain and ultrasound revealed thickened gallbladder walls; managed non-operatively as reactive acalculous cholecystitis.

Considered on repeat ultrasound showing multiple focal splenic lesions in the context of persistent fever; disproved by abdominal MRI showing classic subcapsular pyramidal wedge-shaped infarctions and negative infectious serologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency evaluation identified blood parasitemia confirming acute infection, with subsequent hemoglobin electrophoresis revealing HbS 40.6% confirming sickle cell trait as the mechanism for microvascular splenic infarction.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male presents with a 4-month history of a gradually enlarging swelling on the plantar aspect of his left foot. He reports no local pain, fever, or cutaneous drainage.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Formulated as the primary working diagnosis due to a progressively expanding, firm, non-tender deep plantar mass appearing of muscular or fibrous origin on MRI; disproved when histopathology of the excised specimen revealed infectious grain architecture without malignant neoplasia.
Considered based on MRI demonstration of a well-defined lesion of fibrous or muscular origin without inflammatory changes, but refuted by microscopic confirmation of specific grain pathology.
