Considered atypical and initially overlooked because the patient lacked characteristic external nodules, ulcerations, and draining sinuses, as well as classic inoculation risk factors such as barefoot walking or trauma.

diagnostic_pivot: Excisional biopsy and subsequent histopathological examination surprisingly revealed characteristic grain structures confirming mycetoma of the left foot.

clinical_summary: A 78-year-old underweight Hispanic woman with a history of hypertension and mitral stenosis presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of cramping abdominal pain, nausea, dehydration, and watery diarrhea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given recurrent episodic diarrhea, severe cachexia, and later CT findings showing circumferential sigmoid and rectal wall enhancement; excluded following detailed clinical history and identification of nematode larvae.

Considered because the initial chest radiograph showed possible pneumonia in the setting of high fever; ruled out by the complete absence of cough, dyspnea, tachypnea, or physical respiratory abnormalities.
Considered due to the co-occurrence of pulmonary radiographic abnormalities, fever, and intestinal disease; excluded because the patient was not immunosuppressed and lacked multisystem dysfunction.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct stool microscopy identified larvae/ova of Strongyloides stercoralis, establishing the diagnosis of intestinal soil-transmitted helminthiasis, which was confirmed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man of Middle Eastern origin with a history of occupational exposure to livestock presents with a 3-year history of a slowly enlarging swelling on the right elbow. The mass recently became tender and painful, accompanied by localized pruritus, but without preceding rigors.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to the chronic 3-year progressive expansion of a deep intramuscular mass in a young man; disproved when ultrasound and subsequent MRI demonstrated a cystic multivesicular rosette architecture rather than a solid neoplastic lesion.

Considered when the patient developed acute fever to 38.8°C and localized elbow tenderness; excluded by normal total white blood cell count (5.0 × 10⁹ cells/L), normal ESR (15 mm/h), and absence of purulent fluid or cellulitis.

differentials.candidate: Primary hepatic or pulmonary hydatid disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because hydatid disease predominantly affects the liver and lungs, but ruled out as the primary site by normal liver function tests and clear chest radiography.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative pre-operative hydatid serology, en bloc pericystectomy revealed a multivesicular cyst filled with viable daughter cysts and characteristic hydatid sand, confirming primary musculoskeletal echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old Sub-Saharan African woman with known HIV infection diagnosed 3 years ago, compliant with combination antiretroviral therapy and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis, presents to the emergency unit with a 2-month history of slowly progressive abdominal distention, drenching night sweats, and generalized fatigue.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to scleral icterus, elevated transaminases (AST 97 IU/L, ALT 83 IU/L), and right upper quadrant tenderness; ruled out by negative hepatitis B and C serologies and sonographically normal liver architecture.

Considered upon acute readmission with fever, rebound tenderness, and septic shock; refuted at emergency laparotomy which revealed multiple necrotic jejunal perforations and caseous nodal inflammation rather than primary spontaneous bacterial infection.
Evaluated during initial diagnostic screening for constitutional symptoms; ruled out by clear lung fields on chest radiography and negative sputum smears.

diagnostic_pivot: Ascitic fluid showed lymphocytic exudate with a 14 mm PPD induration, and subsequent emergency laparotomy demonstrated caseous necrosis of the omentum, multiple jejunal perforations, and abundant acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining of peritoneal exudate.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old previously healthy young man presents with a 2-week history of vague postprandial epigastric pain and nausea, accompanied by marked anorexia. Over this 2-week period, he has experienced an unintentional weight loss of 6 pounds.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected on cross-sectional imaging due to an irregular low-density mass in the pancreatic head/neck with vascular encasement of the hepatic artery and portal vein and bile duct dilation; ruled out when resected specimens demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than adenocarcinoma.

Considered when endoscopy demonstrated a mucosal protrusion with a central fur-coated ulcer in the duodenal bulb with disrupted glandular architecture; ruled out when endoscopic biopsy revealed chronic mucosal inflammation with low-grade atypical hyperplasia without malignancy.
Evaluated as the customary primary site of mycobacterial disease; ruled out by an entirely normal chest radiograph without parenchymal consolidation or hilar adenopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Exploratory laparotomy and pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) revealed hard peripancreatic and mesenteric lymph nodes, with histopathology definitively demonstrating multiple caseating granulomas containing epithelioid cells and multinucleated polykaryocytes diagnostic of pancreatic tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male office worker presents to the outpatient orthopedic clinic with persistent pain, swelling, and an inability to bear weight on his right lower extremity 6 months following surgical fracture fixation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Formulated as the primary clinical suspicion due to persistent pain, implant loosening, peri-implant osteolysis, and failure of callus formation; disproved during surgical exploration which revealed indurated soft tissues and pearly white structures rather than purulent exudate, confirmed as parasitic membranes on histology.

Considered at the initial low-energy fracture presentation in a young adult, but ruled out because initial radiographs showed normal bone architecture without pre-existing lytic or blastic tumor lesions.

Considered as potential primary source since skeletal involvement typically represents secondary haematogenous spread from liver or lung lesions, but excluded by negative post-operative abdominal and chest imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical debridement revealed pearly white flattened structures, and histopathological microscopy demonstrated thick eosinophilic acellular lamellated exocyst membranes and characteristic refractile dagger-shaped hooklets diagnostic of femoral hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old Indian male presented to the emergency department after the sudden onset of near-syncope, nausea, diaphoresis, light-headedness, and a wide-staring gaze with upward and lateral deviation of both eyes.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the hyperacute onset of diaphoresis, light-headedness, nausea, and near-syncope within 30 minutes of ingesting a newly prescribed medication regimen. However, there were no manifestations of hemodynamic collapse, bronchospasm, urticaria, or angioedema, and further evaluation revealed preserved awareness with isolated dystonic motor blockage.
Considered because sudden conjugate gaze deviation or oculogyric dystonia may occur secondary to acute brainstem or cranial injury, but excluded by history and physical examination.

diagnostic_pivot: The dramatic and complete resolution of symptoms following intravenous diphenhydramine, alongside the characteristic conjugate eye deviation and temporal link to antimycobacterial ingestion, confirmed an acute oculogyric crisis induced by standard quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old Hispanic female born in Mexico presented to the emergency department with lethargy, high fevers, and worsening abdominal distress. Her medical history was notable for insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus and rheumatoid arthritis managed with methotrexate, abatacept, and chronic prednisone; her prednisone dosage had been increased two days prior to presentation following a corneal transplant.

differentials.candidate: Diabetic ketoacidosis secondary to bacterial colitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to hyperglycemia, ketonuria, severe metabolic acidosis, and CT evidence of colonic thickening, but failed to explain the protracted multi-week gastrointestinal symptoms refractory to empirical ciprofloxacin/metronidazole and the impending translocational enteric bacteremia following steroid escalation.

differentials.candidate: Primary bacterial gastroenteritis or intra-abdominal sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and abdominal signs, but broad-spectrum antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, metronidazole) failed to eradicate the condition, which rapidly culminated in systemic bacteremia and respiratory exhaustion.

diagnostic_pivot: In an immunosuppressed patient born in an endemic region who experienced accelerated gastrointestinal symptoms after corticosteroid escalation, the growth of Gram-negative enteric bacilli in blood and subsequent microscopic visualization of filariform larvae in stool and sputum established soil-transmitted helminthic hyperinfection syndrome (Strongyloides stercoralis).

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with localized pain, tenderness, and progressive swelling in the left inguinal region. His medical history was notable for completion of a course of multidrug therapy 10 years earlier for a chronic dermatologic and peripheral nerve disorder; he had remained symptom-free in the interim.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the localized tenderness, warmth, and acute nodal swelling, but Gram stain and bacterial cultures showed no bacterial organisms, and cytology demonstrated a chronic histiocytic and granulomatous background rather than simple suppurative pyogenic infection.

differentials.candidate: Incarcerated inguinal hernia or soft tissue neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an anatomical or neoplastic groin mass, but excluded by cytological demonstration of active inflammatory infiltrate containing neutrophils, foamy macrophages, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine-needle aspiration demonstrating negative images of bacilli on Wright-Giemsa smears and numerous intracellular and extracellular acid-fast lepra bacilli on modified Fite staining confirmed erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) presenting as an isolated inguinal mass.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with localized swellings on his right forearm. On clinical inquiry, he noted a previous history of focal motor weakness involving the right forearm four years earlier, which had not been definitively evaluated.

differentials.candidate: Subacute pyogenic soft-tissue infection or bacterial furunculosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of multiple inflammatory subcutaneous nodules, but both Gram stain and bacterial cultures were negative for pyogenic pathogens.

differentials.candidate: Benign mesenchymal neoplasms or rheumatoid nodules
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the indolent presentation and localized nodular morphology in an elderly male, but cytological evaluation demonstrated a dense polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate with foamy macrophages, eosinophils, and epithelioid granuloma formation rather than bland adipocytic/fibrous tissue or necrobiotic granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: In a patient with antecedent focal upper extremity neuropathy, fine-needle aspiration yielding granulomatous and neutrophilic inflammation with positive Fite staining for lepra bacilli definitively established erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction).

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old female presented for evaluation of a prolonged, unremitting fever of two months' duration. The fever was characterized by evening rises of temperature, accompanied by chills, rigors, and a productive cough with expectoration.

differentials.candidate: Systemic lupus erythematosus or primary autoimmune large-vessel vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's young female demographic, positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), polyserositis (pleural effusion and ascites), and extreme inflammatory markers, but ruled out as the primary etiology by advanced PET imaging demonstrating contiguous large-vessel aortitis driven by hypermetabolic mediastinal and abdominal lymphadenopathy that resolved with antimycobacterial therapy.

differentials.candidate: Occult deep bacterial infection or pyogenic sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of the severe systemic symptoms, chills, rigors, and extreme elevation of C-reactive protein (>320 mg/L), but ruled out by the complete lack of response to empirical higher-generation antibiotics and the absence of peripheral leukocytosis.

diagnostic_pivot: 18F-FDG PET-CT revealed intense linear FDG uptake along the ascending aorta and aortic arch associated with extensive hypermetabolic mediastinal and abdominal lymphadenopathy, establishing disseminated extrapulmonary tuberculosis with secondary aorto-arteritis, which achieved complete clinical resolution on antitubercular therapy and steroids.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old Filipino female domestic worker presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of persistent high-grade fevers and painful bilateral groin swellings that caused significant difficulty ambulating. She had been evaluated twice in primary care and prescribed sequential courses of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (one week) and moxifloxacin (five days) without clinical improvement.

differentials.candidate: Tumid lupus erythematosus or systemic connective tissue disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to indurated erythematous facial plaques, peripheral edema, and constitutional symptoms, but excluded by negative antinuclear antibodies, negative double-stranded DNA antibodies, and normal serum complement (C3, C4) concentrations.

Considered given high fevers, dramatic leukemoid leukocytosis (36.18 x 10^9/L), extensive necrotic lymphadenopathy on CT, and an acute inflammatory dermatosis, but ruled out when biopsy demonstrated foamy histiocytic infiltration with perineural inflammation rather than malignant lymphoma or aseptic neutrophilic dermatosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Physical palpation demonstrating bilaterally thickened greater auricular and lateral peroneal nerves, followed by a punch skin biopsy revealing a diffuse dermal and subcutaneous infiltrate containing foamy macrophages with neurovascular tropism and abundant acid-fast bacilli on Fite and Ziehl-Neelsen stains, confirmed lepromatous leprosy with erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male presented to the emergency department in July with a 4-day history of acute fevers, generalized myalgias, bone pain, headache, malaise, chills, and nausea. Two days prior to arrival, he had been evaluated at a local health center for dehydration and received intravenous fluid resuscitation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis due to acute onset of fever, bone pain, headache, nausea, and marked thrombocytopenia in an endemic region, leading clinicians to discharge the patient under this clinical impression; however, confirmatory spirochetal serology established an alternative diagnosis.

Considered due to the absence of fever at ED arrival, dry cough, and constitutional complaints, but ruled out given the marked hematologic and hepatic involvement that progressed to leukocytosis and dynamic thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological analysis demonstrated an acute microscopic agglutination test (MAT) reciprocal titer of 100 on day 5 that rose 32-fold to a convalescent reciprocal titer of 3,200 against serogroup Icterohaemorrhagiae (serovar Mankarso) on day 8, confirming acute leptospirosis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male presented to the emergency department in March with a 5-day history of acute fevers, chills, severe back pain, diffuse arthralgias, headache, and eye pain. On physical examination, he was febrile and appeared ill.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis (Hepatitis A, B, or C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary etiology given the acute onset of fever, scleral icterus, jaundice, elevated bilirubin, and bilirubinuria, but ruled out by completely non-reactive viral serologies.

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial sepsis with secondary multiorgan dysfunction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute prostration, chills, thrombocytopenia, and marked rhabdomyolysis, but blood cultures drawn on admission remained sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Real-time PCR detected Leptospira interrogans DNA in serum collected on illness day 3, and convalescent serology upon discharge demonstrated seroconversion with a reciprocal MAT titer of 1,600 against serogroup Bataviae (serovar Bataviae), establishing severe leptospirosis complicated by rhabdomyolysis despite an initial negative commercial IgM.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male presented to the emergency department on March 24 with a 3-day history of acute fevers, malaise, generalized myalgias, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and persistent headache. On physical examination, he was febrile and visibly fatigued.

differentials.candidate: Uncomplicated acute viral syndrome or upper respiratory infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis at ED triage due to prominent rhinorrhea, sore throat, fever, and myalgia, leading to initial discharge on supportive therapy; however, convalescent serology revealed life-threatening tropical pathogens.

Considered given endemicity and confirmed by positive convalescent anti-dengue IgM antibodies, but this represented a true co-infection rather than an isolated viral etiology, as concurrent high-titer spirochetal seroconversion was demonstrated.

diagnostic_pivot: Although day 2 molecular PCR and MAT were negative, convalescent serum obtained 18 days post-onset demonstrated a reciprocal MAT titer of 800 against serogroups Bataviae (serovar Bataviae) and Canicola (serovar Canicola) along with positive anti-dengue IgM, establishing acute leptospirosis co-infection in an endemic environment.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male rural worker presented with painful non-healing oral ulcerations and a persistent cough of six months' duration. He reported a chronic history of tobacco smoking and had no known prior medical comorbidities.

differentials.candidate: Oral squamous cell carcinoma with regional metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given the patient's substantial tobacco exposure, chronic indurated oral ulcer with loosening teeth, and necrotic cervical lymphadenopathy; however, mucosal biopsy showed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with chronic granulomatous inflammation and microabscesses rather than malignant epithelial dysplasia or invasive carcinoma.

Considered due to the 6-month history of productive cough, butterfly-wing infiltrates on chest radiography, and draining cervical lymphadenopathy with cutaneous fistula; however, molecular testing specifically ruled out mycobacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct mycological examination of cervical lymph node aspirate, sputum, and oral scraping demonstrated characteristic large yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds surrounding mother cells ('mariner's wheel' appearance), confirmed by fungal culture yielding Paracoccidioides species and tissue biopsy showing birefringent yeasts within granulomas.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old male with melanoderma, who is a chronic smoker and resident of a rural region, is referred to the surgery outpatient clinic with a chief complaint of a "mouth sore." On physical examination, there is an ulcerated oral mucosal lesion studded with fine hemorrhagic dots.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In an elderly chronic tobacco smoker presenting with a chronic non-healing oral ulcer, squamous cell carcinoma is the foremost diagnostic consideration; however, biopsy demonstrated characteristic granulomatous fungal infection rather than neoplastic tissue.

A benign aphthous ulcer was suspected based on the initial chief complaint of a mouth sore, but physical examination revealed an ulcerated lesion displaying characteristic hemorrhagic dots rather than a typical self-limited aphthous ulcer.

diagnostic_pivot: Identification of the pathognomonic mulberry-like ulceration with hemorrhagic puncta in a rural resident prompted an incisional biopsy under local anesthesia, which definitively confirmed the diagnosis and initiated targeted antifungal therapy with itraconazole.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male rural worker and smoker with systemic arterial hypertension attends the outpatient clinic complaining of "sore and pain in the lips and mouth." Clinical examination reveals erythematous ulcers involving the lips and oral mucosa, with a slight limitation of mouth opening due to the inflammatory process installed in the lips.

differentials.candidate: Oral / Labial Malignant Neoplasia (Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient's age, smoking history, and painful, destructive ulcerative lesions involving the lips and oral cavity raised strong suspicion for malignancy; however, anatomopathological examination of biopsied fragments excluded neoplasia and confirmed mycotic disease.

Significant labial tumefaction causing limitation of mouth opening raised consideration for chronic inflammatory or granulomatous cheilitis, but histopathologic evaluation confirmed a definitive infectious fungal process.

diagnostic_pivot: Collection and anatomopathological examination of multiple tissue fragments obtained under local anesthesia established the definitive diagnosis, leading to targeted antifungal therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old male rural worker with no history of tobacco use, substance use, or chronic medical comorbidities presents to the clinic with a chief complaint of a "bleeding wound in the mouth." Physical examination of the oral cavity reveals an ulcerated lesion measuring approximately 4 cm associated with hemorrhagic dots.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A solitary, large (4 cm) bleeding oral ulcer in an adult male warrants high clinical suspicion for oral malignancy; however, anatomopathological evaluation showed infectious fungal features rather than malignancy.

differentials.candidate: Traumatic / Vascular Ulcerative Lesion (e.g., Pyogenic Granuloma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden complaint of a bleeding wound in a healthy manual worker suggested an acute traumatic or reactive vascular mucosal process, but examination showed a classic 4 cm ulcer with fine hemorrhagic dots characteristic of a deep mycotic infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Anatomopathological examination of the 4 cm bleeding ulcer established the definitive diagnosis, leading to prompt therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male rural worker and smoker with no known comorbidities presents to the clinic complaining of gingival bleeding when brushing his teeth. A persistent gingival lesion is observed, which fails to resolve following basic periodontal treatment.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bleeding upon toothbrushing in a smoker initially suggested standard plaque-induced periodontal disease; however, the gingival lesion failed to resolve after basic periodontal therapy.

differentials.candidate: Gingival Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Hematologic Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Refractory bleeding gingival ulceration in a tobacco smoker raises concern for primary gingival malignancy, but pathologic examination established a fungal infectious etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Lack of response to conservative periodontal treatment necessitated an incisional biopsy, which revealed characteristic fungal pathology and prompted targeted therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old female presents with an 8-month history of progressively worsening pain in the left ankle and inability to stand or walk, particularly over uneven surfaces. She has no history of trauma, joint pain elsewhere, or constitutional symptoms such as fever or weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Seronegative Subtalar Joint Arthritis / Primary Osteoarthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis at presentation given the chronic 8-month history of localized subtalar joint destruction, complete absence of constitutional symptoms, and normal hematological and arthritic panels; however, subsequent surgical non-union, persistent erosions, and histopathology established an infectious tuberculous etiology.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Septic Arthritis / Low-Grade Hardware Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient exhibited persistent postoperative pain, non-union, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 16 mm/L, ESR 36 mm/h, leukocytosis 12,000); however, an intensive four-week course of broad-spectrum intravenous and oral antibiotics produced no clinical improvement, and revision surgery found no purulence.

diagnostic_pivot: Revision surgery and debridement revealed dirty granulation tissue without pus, and histopathological analysis demonstrated epithelioid granulomas with abundant Langhans giant cells, establishing the diagnosis of skeletal tuberculosis and resulting in complete bony fusion upon initiation of antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male teacher presents to the outpatient clinic with a 2-year history of slowly progressive swelling of the right index finger, accompanied by dull pain and difficulty flexing the digit.

differentials.candidate: Giant Cell Tumour (GCT) of the Tendon Sheath
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading provisional diagnosis due to the chronic, painless, lobulated soft-tissue mass along the flexor tendon sheath; however, surgical exploration revealed a synovial sac distended by rice bodies and histopathology showed chronic granulomatous inflammation rather than a true neoplasm.

differentials.candidate: Compound Palmar Ganglion and Tendinous Xanthoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Maintained on the differential diagnosis for chronic swelling of the flexor tendon sheath and palm; excluded when surgical exploration uncovered a thickened sheath packed with shiny rice bodies and confluent Langhans giant-cell granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exposure revealed a synovial sheath distended with copious rice bodies, and histopathology confirmed confluent epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells; subsequent sputum testing yielded acid-fast bacilli, confirming tuberculous tenosynovitis and leading to complete cure with anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male tourist from South Korea presents with acute fever, rash, and severe malaise 2 days after arriving in Chile. He reports flu-like symptoms with chills, intense headache, and myalgias that began 5 days earlier.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Exanthem (EBV, CMV, Parvovirus B19, or Respiratory Viral Infection)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute onset of high fever, rash, transaminitis, thrombocytopenia, and atypical reactive lymphocytes in an acutely ill traveler strongly resembled an acute viral illness; however, comprehensive viral PCR and IgM serologies were negative, and viral infections do not cause a necrotic eschar.

differentials.candidate: Indigenous Chilean Rickettsiosis (Orientia sp. Chiloé Island isolate)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Because the patient presented in Chile with a rickettsial presentation, locally acquired Chilean rickettsiosis was considered; however, phylogenetic sequencing revealed that the isolate was 100% homologous to East Asian strains (Kawasaki type) contracted on a farm in Korea, unrelated to Chilean isolates.

diagnostic_pivot: Recognition of a classic painless eschar with a red halo in an acutely ill traveler returning from rural South Korea prompted empiric doxycycline therapy, resulting in defervescence within 36 hours and subsequent confirmatory ELISA, immunofluorescence, and PCR testing.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old female from a rural region of northern India presents with vague abdominal pain, burning micturition, and urge incontinence. She describes a 6-month history of intermittent passage of small, white, balloon-like, grape-sized structures in her urine.

differentials.candidate: Peritoneal Carcinomatosis / Ovarian Cystadenocarcinoma / Pseudomyxoma Peritonei
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple disseminated multicystic intraperitoneal masses involving the adnexa, iliac fossa, and retrovesical space in an elderly female strongly suggested metastatic cystic malignancy; however, cross-sectional imaging showed internal daughter cysts and non-invasive fistulization rather than malignant ascites or peritoneal implants.

differentials.candidate: Complicated Primary Pelvic Abscess / Bladder Diverticulum
differentials.rule_out_reason: Urinary frequency, dysuria, and a fistulous tract to the posterior bladder wall raised suspicion of a chronic pelvic abscess or complicated diverticular fistula; furthermore, negative serology could have distracted from an infectious parasitosis, but microscopic analysis of the passed membranes established the etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Gross examination of the voided urine revealed an intact balloon-like membrane, and histopathology demonstrated the pathognomonic outer acellular laminated layer and inner nucleated germinal layer, confirming disseminated hydatid cyst disease complicated by a cystovesical fistula.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old female with HIV infection (on antiretroviral therapy for 5 months with a CD4 count of 417 cells/μL) presents with a 3-month history of right upper quadrant colicky pain radiating to the infrascapular area, accompanied by low-grade fever, anorexia, and weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Needle Track Abscess / Foreign Body Reaction
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden development of an erythematous, tender subcutaneous nodule at a recent percutaneous needle puncture site suggested a superficial bacterial infection or localized foreign body response; however, excision revealed caseating granulomatous inflammation rather than acute suppurative abscess formation.

differentials.candidate: Iatrogenic Neoplastic Needle Track Seeding (Cholangiocarcinoma / Lymphoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: In the setting of biliary ductal dilatation with abrupt cut-off and periportal adenopathy, malignant tract seeding was an important differential concern; however, high clinical suspicion for tuberculous inoculation prompted an excision biopsy that ruled out malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Excision biopsy of the puncture site skin nodule demonstrated epithelioid cell granulomas, Langhans giant cells, and positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli, definitively establishing implantation cutaneous tuberculosis and enabling curative four-drug antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old male manual laborer presents to the emergency department with acute pain, paresthesias, and coldness of the right lower extremity. He has no prior history of cardiac disease or trauma and was previously in good health.

differentials.candidate: Intracardiac Tumor (Left Ventricular Myxoma / Fibroma) with Embolization
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a young patient without cardiovascular disease presenting with acute peripheral arterial embolism and an intracardiac mass, a primary cardiac tumor such as myxoma was a leading consideration; however, echocardiography showed a distinctly anechoic cystic lesion rather than a solid or gelatinous parenchymal mass.

Acute major arterial occlusion from an embolic source in a young adult can occur secondary to endocarditis; however, there were no valvular vegetations or systemic septic features, and regional endemicity raised high suspicion for an echinococcal cyst.

diagnostic_pivot: Urgent surgical embolectomy with a Fogarty catheter retrieved an occluding cruor thrombus containing a pathognomonic white parasitic membrane, which was confirmed as hydatid tissue on histopathology, identifying embolization from a ruptured left ventricular hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male farmer presented with a 3-year history of atypical chest pain that had markedly worsened over the preceding month. He reported no weight loss, diaphoresis, fever, rash, gastrointestinal complaints, or respiratory symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Acute Coronary Syndrome / Ischemic Heart Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had a prior history of coronary ectasia and presented with worsening chest pain, pathologic Q waves in III and aVF, and negative T waves in II, III, aVF, and V6, troponin was negative and echocardiography revealed that wall hypokinesia was due to mechanical compression from an intramyocardial mass.

differentials.candidate: Primary Cardiac Neoplasm (e.g., Myxoma, Fibroma, or Angiosarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary cardiac tumors typically present as solid intracavitary or infiltrating mural masses rather than encapsulated multicystic fluid collections containing internal daughter vesicles in an agricultural worker.

diagnostic_pivot: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a massive encapsulated intramyocardial cystic left ventricular mass with daughter cysts and pericystic myocardial fibrosis, corroborated by positive echinococcal ELISA serology and surgical extraction of daughter cysts with scolicidal irrigation.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented to the outpatient surgical clinic complaining of a painless swelling over the right upper chest, situated 3 cm inferior to the clavicle, which had been present for two and a half years.

differentials.candidate: Intramuscular Soft Tissue Neoplasm / Lipoma / Lymphangioma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Soft tissue mesenchymal tumors of the chest wall present as painless chronic swellings, but chest CT demonstrated a hypodense multiseptated cystic mass rather than adipose tissue or a solid mesenchymal tumor.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or Tuberculous Cold Abscess / Chronic Hematoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: An infectious collection or chronic organizing hematoma would typically feature local pain, inflammatory changes, systemic signs, or an antecedent trauma history, all of which were absent.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration of the pectoralis major mass revealed a thick-walled cystic cavity containing numerous pathognomonic daughter cysts, establishing the definitive diagnosis of primary intramuscular echinococcal hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old male presented with acute abdominal discomfort and postprandial abdominal distention accompanied by watery diarrhea of two months' duration. He reported no involuntary weight loss, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, melena, or hematochezia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although an 8 x 8 cm obstructing right-sided mass with palpable fullness and luminal narrowing strongly suggested colonic adenocarcinoma, serum tumor markers were normal and CT imaging revealed central low-density attenuation suggestive of an inflammatory process rather than neoplasm.

While terminal ileum and cecal concentric wall thickening could indicate Crohn's ileocolitis, there were no skip lesions in the distal colon, and mucosal biopsy revealed only inflammatory cell infiltration without granulomatous ulceration.

diagnostic_pivot: Given the inflammatory features of the pseudotumor, initiation of oral metronidazole therapy resulted in rapid symptom resolution within three days, normal repeat colonoscopy up to the terminal ileum, and complete radiographic disappearance of the 8 x 8 cm mass after two weeks, confirming an amebic pseudotumor (ameboma).

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old woman presented to the outpatient surgical clinic complaining of a painless mass in her right calf that had been present for two years. The mass was discovered incidentally two years earlier and had been diagnosed clinically at that time as a lipoma, for which no treatment was initiated.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected clinically because of the chronic, soft, painless, and mobile nature of the calf mass, but excluded when soft tissue ultrasound demonstrated a complex multicystic fluid lesion containing internal small vesicles rather than uniform adipose tissue.

differentials.candidate: Baker Cyst / Intramuscular Hematoma or Seroma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Synovial cysts and organizing hematomas can form cystic collections in the calf, but the absence of antecedent knee joint effusion or trauma, combined with the presence of multiple well-formed internal daughter cysts, excluded a simple fluid collection.

diagnostic_pivot: Ultrasound identification of a multilocular cystic architecture with internal vesicles in the gastrocnemius muscle, confirmed intraoperatively by surgical cystotomy revealing innumerable classic daughter cysts, definitively established isolated intramuscular echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male laborer presented with pain, swelling, and localized tenderness in his left lower leg. Twelve years earlier, he had sustained blunt trauma to the left leg without breach of skin integrity.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis because of the chronic draining sinus tract, intramedullary fluid collection surrounded by a sclerotic halo on CT, and typical T1 serpiginous / T2 hyperintense cavitary appearance on MRI, but empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy produced no clinical improvement, routine aspirate cultures were sterile, and open biopsy demonstrated caseating granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Bone Neoplasm (e.g., Osteoid Osteoma or Osteosarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cortical thickening, periosteal reaction, and radiolucent nidus-like areas in the tibial metaphysis can mimic bony neoplasms, but the presence of an active draining sinus orifice, systemic inflammatory markers, and sequestra inside caseating granulation tissue ruled out primary bone tumor.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical biopsy and curettage revealed caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells and bony sequestra, and real-time PCR on tissue blocks detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex-specific DNA, later confirmed by culture growth on Lowenstein-Jensen medium.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old girl was brought by her parents to the emergency unit of a regional hospital in northern Benin with a 48-hour history of acute abdominal pain, diffuse abdominal tenderness, high fever, recurrent vomiting, and anorexia, which had been treated at home with local herbal infusions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although enteric fever readily explains acute small bowel perforation and severe leukopenia, isolated typhoid infection could not account for the extensive miliary caseous nodules studding the visceral and parietal peritoneum, massive retroperitoneal lymphadenomegaly, and dense acid-fast bacilli on nodule microscopy.

differentials.candidate: Acute Ruptured Appendicitis / Pyogenic Bacterial Peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Classic pyogenic intra-abdominal sepsis typically presents with brisk neutrophilic leukocytosis rather than severe leukopenia (WBC 1,300/mm³), and would produce fibrinopurulent exudate without widespread caseating granulomatous miliary tubercles.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency explorative laparotomy revealed diffuse caseous tubercles across the bowel and peritoneum with retroperitoneal lymphomegaly alongside jejunal perforations, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining of peritoneal nodules demonstrated a heavy burden of acid-fast bacilli, confirming miliary peritoneal tuberculosis occurring simultaneously with typhoid intestinal perforation.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old man was transferred to a regional hospital in the Zinder Republic of Niger with acute fever, vomiting, and abrupt impairment of consciousness. Ten days earlier, he had developed high fever and vomiting for which he received an initial 3-day course of intramuscular quinine injections at 25 mg/kg/day.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Massive acute intravascular hemolysis with hemoglobin drop to 4 g/dL and jaundice can occur in AIHA, but direct antiglobulin testing was negative, pointing instead to drug-mediated oxidative or immune hemolysis.

Dark 'Coca-Cola' colored urine accompanied by acute renal failure (creatinine 559.6 µmol/L) can mimic acute glomerulonephritis, but dipstick and microscopic examination revealed free hemoglobinuria without intact red blood cells or erythrocyte casts.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of intermittent quinine exposure, massive intravascular hemolysis with Coca-Cola colored hemoglobinuria, and severe acute uremic syndrome alongside a positive rapid diagnostic test confirming Plasmodium falciparum antigenemia established blackwater fever.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old woman with no prior medical history was admitted to the hospital with acute headache, high fever, scleral jaundice, and progressive alteration of consciousness. Two days prior to admission, she had developed a febrile illness and received intramuscular quinine injections administered at her home.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden occurrence of port wine-colored urine in the setting of acute renal failure (creatinemia 450 µmol/L) can mimic acute nephritic syndrome, but dipstick testing revealed hemoglobinuria with a total absence of red blood cells or cellular casts.

differentials.candidate: Severe Bacterial Sepsis with Multi-Organ Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS)
differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, tachypnea, encephalopathy, and acute kidney injury can suggest severe bacterial sepsis, but the sudden collapse in hemoglobin to 5 g/dL and massive hemoglobinuria immediately following quinine injections pointed specifically to massive intravascular hemolysis.

diagnostic_pivot: Urinary catheterization demonstrating port wine-colored urine from severe hemoglobinuria and acute uremic syndrome after quinine administration, confirmed by a positive rapid diagnostic test for Plasmodium falciparum despite a negative thick peripheral smear, established blackwater fever.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old man with no significant medical history was admitted to the hospital with acute drowsiness, fever, and marked palpitations. On initial examination, he weighed 55 kg.

differentials.candidate: Septic Shock with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial high fever, extreme tachycardia (140 bpm), and rapid circulatory collapse suggested overwhelming bacterial septic shock, but the acute precipitous plunge in hemoglobin from 10.3 g/dL to 5.5 g/dL within 12 hours accompanied by port wine-colored urine indicated massive intravascular hemolysis rather than consumptive coagulopathy.

differentials.candidate: Acute Fulminant Hepatic Failure / Hepatorenal Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Worsening obnubilation and prominent conjunctival jaundice can mimic acute hepatic encephalopathy, but the development of port wine-colored urine and massive anemia reflect pigment-induced hemoglobinuric acute tubular necrosis rather than primary end-stage hepatic necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation of severe malaria with 17,400 Plasmodium falciparum trophozoites/mm³ on thick blood smear, coupled with sudden catastrophic post-quinine intravascular hemolysis, port wine-colored hemoglobinuria, and anuric uremic syndrome, confirmed fatal blackwater fever.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old man with no significant past medical history was hospitalized with acute fever, jaundice, and altered mental status. On the preceding day, he had received an initial dose of quinine at 25 mg/kg/24 hours for a febrile illness.

differentials.candidate: Acute Hepatorenal Syndrome / Fulminant Hepatic Failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Concomitant jaundice, encephalopathy (GCS 11), and extreme renal impairment (creatinine 1500 µmol/L) suggested fulminant hepatorenal failure, but the acute onset following quinine and port wine-colored urine pointed to massive intravascular hemolysis and pigment-induced acute tubular necrosis rather than primary end-stage liver disease.

differentials.candidate: Severe Sepsis with Ischemic Acute Tubular Necrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe bacterial sepsis can present with fever, tachypnea, altered mental status, and oligoanuric acute kidney injury, but it does not account for the characteristic port wine urine caused by acute intravascular hemoglobinuria following quinine ingestion.

diagnostic_pivot: Severe oligoanuric acute renal failure and port wine-colored urine developing after quinine exposure, confirmed by a positive rapid diagnostic test for Plasmodium falciparum despite a negative thick peripheral blood smear, established blackwater fever.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old male residing in Darchula District, Nepal, presents to a specialized tropical and infectious disease referral hospital with a 1-week history of intermittent fever and vague abdominal pain, accompanied by epistaxis for 4 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Intermittent fever and massive splenomegaly in an endemic area strongly suggest chronic malaria or hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly, but repeated peripheral blood parasite examinations were negative.
Tuberculosis was considered given cachexia, prolonged fevers, and hepatosplenomegaly, but chest imaging was normal and microbiological testing of sputum was negative.

Profound pancytopenia with massive splenomegaly in an adult raised high concern for leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, or lymphoma, but peripheral blood smear cytology demonstrated normal cell morphology without blasts or abnormal cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of characteristic intracellular and extracellular Leishman-Donovan (LD) amastigotes on bone marrow cytology along with positive rK39 immunochromatographic testing confirmed relapsed visceral leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old female farmer residing in a rural community in Nepal presents with a 12-month history of intermittent abdominal pain localized to the right upper quadrant and the left iliac fossa, associated with progressive abdominal distension.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A complex multiseptated mass in the left iliac fossa in a young female could represent an ovarian cystadenoma or cystic teratoma, but her menstrual cycles were regular, pelvic architecture was non-tender, and the synchronous presence of an identical multilocular hepatic lesion with peripheral eosinophilia pointed toward a disseminated parasitic process.

Hepatic abscesses typically manifest with acute or subacute fever, leukocytosis, and right upper quadrant tenderness, which is inconsistent with this patient's 12-month indolent afebrile course, normal leukocyte count, and distinct internal daughter septations on cross-sectional imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: Markedly elevated Echinococcus-specific IgG antibody titers (19.5 U/mL) and laparotomy confirming multi-organ loculated hydatid cysts with daughter cysts in the liver and left iliac fossa established the definitive diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old woman residing in Tunis, Tunisia, is admitted for evaluation of fevers evolving over several weeks, accompanied by profuse sweating and chills. Documented oral temperatures have ranged from 38°C to 39°C.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Brucellosis is endemic in the Mediterranean basin and commonly causes persistent fever, chills, night sweats, splenomegaly, and cytopenias, but multiple blood cultures and specific Brucella serologic testing were completely negative.

Typhoid fever presents with prolonged fever, constitutional symptoms, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, and leukopenia, but bacteriological cultures of blood, stool, and urine and Salmonella antibody assays showed no growth or reactivity.

Pancytopenia, splenomegaly, and a monoclonal spike on serum protein electrophoresis raised strong suspicion for a plasma cell dyscrasia or lymphoproliferative neoplasm, but bone marrow examination revealed intracellular protozoal amastigotes rather than malignant lymphoid or plasma cell clones.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive rK39 immunochromatographic assay, positive immunofluorescence antibody titers (1:400), and identification of Leishmania amastigotes on bone marrow aspiration established visceral leishmaniasis, with identical parasite DNA demonstrated in both the bloodstream and the co-occurring cutaneous basal cell carcinoma.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old man presents to the surgical outpatient department of a tertiary public hospital in Greece with a 1-month history of mild right upper quadrant abdominal pain and a sensation of abdominal fullness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple hepatic cysts are unilocular, homogenous fluid collections with thin, imperceptible walls that lack internal daughter vesicles or complex septations, contrasting sharply with the multivesicular architecture seen in this patient.

Biliary cystic neoplasms (mucinous cystadenoma/cystadenocarcinoma) typically demonstrate irregular thick septations, papillary projections, and solid mural nodules, whereas this lesion demonstrated well-marginated internal daughter cysts without solid neoplastic nodularity.

Hepatic abscesses present acutely with high fever, chills, leukocytosis, and right upper quadrant peritoneal signs, whereas this patient had an indolent 1-month history without fever or systemic symptoms.

diagnostic_pivot: The classic imaging features of a giant multivesicular cyst containing internal daughter cysts together with positive Echinococcus-specific IgG and IgM antibodies confirmed Echinococcosis (hydatid cyst).

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old man with no antecedent comorbidities presents to the emergency department of a tertiary hospital in South Western Nigeria with an acute-onset high-grade intermittent fever accompanied by chills, rigors, headache, severe myalgias, diffuse abdominal pain, and intractable vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe malaria is hyperendemic in Nigeria and causes acute fever, myalgia, severe thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and acute kidney injury, but the patient failed pre-admission antimalarial therapy and had repeatedly negative blood films for malaria parasites.

Neutrophilic leukocytosis, high-grade fevers, and abdominal pain prompted broad-spectrum coverage, but the patient experienced persistent fevers and clinical deterioration despite aggressive antibiotic therapy.

The subsequent development of hypoxemia, crackles, and perihilar opacities prompted treatment for atypical pneumonia, but these findings reflected progressive systemic microvascular plasma leakage and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema characteristic of severe viral hemorrhagic fever rather than primary bacterial pneumonia.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of positive dengue virus RNA on a real-time polymerase chain reaction panel in the setting of severe thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and plasma leakage confirmed dengue hemorrhagic fever.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old girl from Hooghly district in West Bengal, India, presents with a 15-day history of high-grade fever, difficulty walking for 4 days, and sudden visual disturbance with diplopia for 1 day.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Encephalitis (Japanese Encephalitis / HSV / Dengue)
differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, headache, meningismus, raised intracranial tension, and acute cerebellar signs in an endemic region suggested an arboviral or herpesvirus central nervous system infection, but specific testing for Japanese encephalitis, Herpes simplex, and dengue was negative.
Marked leukocytosis, neck stiffness, and high fevers raised concern for bacterial meningitis or complicated typhoid fever, but blood, urine, and CSF cultures yielded no bacterial growth.

differentials.candidate: Acute Post-Infectious Cerebellitis / Posterior Fossa Mass
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid-onset ataxia and sixth cranial nerve palsy suggested isolated cerebellar inflammation or a posterior fossa space-occupying lesion, but magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was completely normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Detection of positive scrub typhus IgM in peripheral blood together with positive scrub typhus IgM and IgG in the cerebrospinal fluid established the diagnosis of neuro-scrub typhus with acute cerebellar ataxia and intracranial hypertension.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old Sri Lankan male presents to a tertiary care hospital in the Northern Province of Sri Lanka with a 3-day history of high-grade fever associated with severe diffuse myalgia, arthralgia, retro-orbital pain, anorexia, and recurrent vomiting.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (Hepatitis A, B, or C)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extreme transaminase elevations into the thousands with coagulopathy strongly mimic hyperacute hepatotropic viral infection, but serologic screening for hepatitis A, B, and C was negative.

Recent binge drinking on a background of chronic alcohol consumption raised concern for acute alcoholic hepatitis, but transaminases in alcoholic liver disease rarely exceed 300 to 500 U/L and cannot account for transaminases approaching 10,000 to nearly 30,000 U/L.

Hyperacute centrilobular hepatic necrosis with transaminases in the thousands is classically triggered by toxic paracetamol ingestion or herbal toxins, but rigorous drug history confirmed zero exposure to supra-therapeutic analgesics or hepatotoxic remedies.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid serum positivity for dengue non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen on admission followed by convalescent IgM and IgG seropositivity confirmed expanded dengue syndrome with acute hepatic necrosis and liver failure.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old Chinese woman presents to a hospital in Guizhou Province, China, in February 2017 with persistent cough, expectoration of sputum, and progressive shortness of breath. She reports a five-year antecedent history of chronic pulmonary illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Sputum smear acid-fast bacillus positivity and an initial automated molecular assay indicated rifampicin susceptibility, but the patient experienced treatment failure with radiological progression on standard first-line anti-tuberculous therapy.

Cavitary lung disease with positive acid-fast bacillus smear microscopy can be caused by environmental mycobacteria like Mycobacterium avium complex or M. kansasii, but automated molecular testing specifically identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

diagnostic_pivot: Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing confirmed resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol, establishing multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), with rpoB gene sequencing demonstrating an uncommon non-RRDR missense mutation at codon 491 (Ile491Phe) that avoided standard molecular detection.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old Chinese man presents in 2016 with a 2-month history of cough, expectoration, increasing dyspnea, and headache, accompanied by hoarseness for 1 week. He is a farmer who grew up in a small town in Zhejiang Province and resided in Guangzhou for 2 years approximately 20 years earlier.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The synchronous combination of an enhancing pulmonary mass with necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy and an osteolytic calvarial lesion strongly mimicked advanced lung carcinoma with skull metastases, but endobronchial ultrasound-guided and percutaneous needle aspiration biopsies demonstrated inflammatory changes without malignant cells.

Chronic cough, necrotic mediastinal lymphadenitis, and osteolytic bone destruction in an endemic country raised high clinical suspicion for systemic tuberculosis, but sputum acid-fast bacillus smear and purified protein derivative skin testing were negative.
Invasive fungal infection was considered given angioinvasive necrotic lesions, but serum fungal biomarker assays were non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: Fungal cultures of aspirated pus from the forehead mass, bone marrow, sputum, and blood yielding Talaromyces marneffei exhibiting classic thermal dimorphism (filamentous mold producing soluble red pigment at 25°C and yeast phase at 37°C) confirmed disseminated talaromycosis.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old previously healthy Sri Lankan male pharmacist presents to a tertiary care hospital with an 8-day history of intermittent high spiking fevers. Concurrent with the onset of fever, he developed frequent, small-volume, watery loose stools without visible blood, mucus, or tenesmus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute diarrheal onset with high fevers, leukocytosis, and right lower quadrant tenderness initially suggested acute gastrointestinal sepsis or typhlitis, but blood and urine cultures were sterile, and the patient had persistent fever spikes and elevated inflammatory markers despite multi-agent intravenous antibiotics (meropenem, ofloxacin, and metronidazole).

High serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG 1.5 g/dL) typically reflects sinusoidal portal hypertension, but the patient had normal serum bilirubin, intact cardiac function without pericardial effusion, and absence of hepatic stigmata.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical excision of the appendix and histopathologic examination of the serosa and mesoappendix revealing multiple granulomas composed of epithelioid cells and Langhans giant cells with spotty central caseous necrosis established the diagnosis of appendicular tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man residing in an urban informal settlement on the outskirts of New Delhi presented to the emergency surgical service with diffuse abdominal pain of 5 days duration, obstipation for 2 days, and progressive abdominal distension for 1 day.

differentials.candidate: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia / Mesenteric Vessel Thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary cause of diffuse bowel gangrene, necrosis, and peritonitis in an elderly patient with vascular risk factors; excluded during surgical exploration which showed patent mesenteric vasculature without thrombosis.

Considered given transmural colitis with segmental mucosal ulcerations and toxic colonic perforation; excluded on histopathological examination which lacked crypt architectural distortion, crypt-destructive colitis, or non-caseating granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency subtotal colectomy and histopathologic examination of the resected bowel identified characteristic flask-shaped mucosal ulcers with erythrophagocytic trophozoites positive for periodic acid-Schiff staining, corroborated by markedly positive amoebic IgM serology.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old man, a chronic cigarette smoker, was admitted to the hospital with acute inflammatory lumbar pain that had developed 3 months after starting an empiric four-drug antimicrobial regimen (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) for an exudative left pleural effusion associated with unexplained weight loss, night sweats, and dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an acute bacterial superinfection causing progressive vertebral destruction and psoas abscess formation; ruled out by negative Gram stain, negative Ziehl-Neelsen stain, and absence of bacterial growth on abscess fluid cultures.

differentials.candidate: Drug-Susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis Infection (Standard Pott's Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Standard first-line regimen was initially maintained on presumptive clinical grounds, but the patient experienced treatment failure with symptom worsening and extensive cold abscess progression into the gluteal and trochanteric soft tissues due to high-level multi-drug resistance.

diagnostic_pivot: CT-guided vertebral biopsy aspiration subjected to GeneXpert MTB/RIF and line probe assay confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis with multi-drug resistance (rifampicin and high-level isoniazid) and second-line fluoroquinolone (ofloxacin) resistance, establishing pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculous spondylodiscitis.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old Hispanic man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented to the outpatient infectious disease clinic for evaluation of progressive left testicular swelling and tenderness of 6 months duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary concern that prompted previous right radical inguinal orchiectomy; definitively excluded by histopathologic examination of the surgical specimen which demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with no neoplastic elements.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial, Sexually Transmitted, or Zoonotic Epididymo-orchitis and Granulomatous Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to scrotal erythema, mass, and concurrent lingular pneumonia; excluded by failure of antibiotic therapy (doxycycline) and negative serologies for brucellosis, syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia, as well as negative ANCA autoantibodies.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic verification of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation in tissue blocks, together with lingular infiltrate, prior positive tuberculin reactivity, and rapid clinical resolution following initiation of standard 4-drug antitubercular therapy, established tuberculous epididymo-orchitis.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female agricultural worker residing in a rural community presented to an oral medicine service for evaluation of an extensive palatal lesion and progressive hoarseness that had persisted for 3 months following an acute upper respiratory illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a leading differential diagnosis given rural agricultural sugarcane exposure, chronic destructive naso-oropharyngeal mucosal lesions, and pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia; excluded by negative direct mycological examination.

Considered due to continuous denture wear and removable white plaques overlying erythematous mucosa; excluded when an empiric course of nystatin oral suspension produced no clinical improvement or change in the granulomatous lesions.

differentials.candidate: Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Head and Neck Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given smoking history, destructive mucosal ulceration, and pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia on referral biopsy; excluded by absence of cytological malignancy on deep incisional biopsy.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis of mucosal leishmaniasis was confirmed by an intensely reactive Montenegro intradermal test demonstrating an exacerbated bullous reaction, along with biopsy findings compatible with chronic granulomatous infiltration, followed by complete clinical mucosal healing upon treatment with meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime).

clinical_summary: A 19-year-old male presented to the hospital with progressive mid-back pain and weakness of both lower extremities of 3 months duration. Neurological weakness had started in the left lower extremity and progressively involved the right lower extremity.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary differential diagnosis for a well-circumscribed intramedullary cord mass causing progressive myelopathy; excluded on excisional biopsy which revealed chronic granulomatous inflammation rather than an ependymal neoplasm.

Considered given the intramedullary location and signal characteristics on MRI; ruled out by histopathology demonstrating epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans giant cells, and central caseous necrosis without neoplastic glial proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Posterior T6-T8 laminectomy and durotomy revealed a brown-greyish, multilobulated intramedullary mass whose excisional biopsy demonstrated classic chronic granulomatous inflammation with Langhans multinucleated giant cells, peripheral lymphocytic cuffing, and central caseating necrosis diagnostic of spinal cord tuberculoma.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old non-diabetic male businessman presented to the outpatient department with a 2-week history of cough productive of sputum, pleuritic anterior chest pain, reduced appetite, intermittent fevers with chills, and drenching night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading acute diagnosis given recent air travel, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, lymphopenia, and elevated LDH/CRP; ruled out as the sole etiology by the subacute 2-week course, recurrent hemoptysis, and microbiological detection of acid-fast bacilli in sputum.

Considered given fever, productive cough, tachypnea, and bilateral consolidation; inconsistent with significant lymphopenia, prolonged night sweats, and refuted by the detection of specific mycobacterial and viral pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum fluorescent microscopy and cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification testing (CBNAAT) detected rifampicin-susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis (later confirmed by BACTEC MGIT liquid culture), while qualitative oropharyngeal RT-PCR confirmed concurrent SARS-CoV-2 RNA.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old man with a 20-year history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and surgical resection of a hepatic cyst 4 years prior presented to the emergency department of a referral hospital in Tehran, Iran, with recurrent postprandial upper abdominal pain, progressive jaundice, abdominal distension, and bilateral lower extremity edema.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given marked obstructive jaundice, biliary ductal dilation with intraluminal filling defects, and new ascites; excluded by normal serum CA 19-9 levels, negative ascites fluid cytology, and absence of an infiltrative malignant mass on cross-sectional imaging.

Considered as the primary cause of biliary obstruction and jaundice; although biliary stones and sludge were present, endoscopic intervention revealed they were secondary to parasitic cyst rupture and membrane passage rather than primary biliary lithiasis alone.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) extracted more than 30 pigmented calculi along with classic hydatid cyst laminar membranes from the common bile duct, confirming a communicating cystobiliary fistula from the calcified hepatic hydatid cyst resulting in secondary biliary cirrhosis and portal hypertension.

clinical_summary: A male infant was born precipitously in an ambulance at 38.6 weeks of gestation to a 28-year-old previously healthy Colombian woman traveling from a remote rural area. The mother had received late and irregular prenatal care.

differentials.candidate: Classical Congenital TORCH Infections (Cytomegalovirus, Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, Syphilis, HSV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading cause of congenital microcephaly, intracranial calcifications, and ventriculomegaly following maternal gestational fever; excluded by comprehensive serological testing.

differentials.candidate: Primary Monogenic Microcephaly / Genetic Malformation Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe craniofacial dysmorphism, overlapping sutures, arthrogryposis, and structural cortical malformations; prompted formal genetic evaluation, but the clinical spectrum was fully explained by vertical viral infection.

diagnostic_pivot: First-trimester maternal febrile illness in an endemic region followed by detection of viral RNA by RT-PCR in amniotic fluid, together with pathognomonic neuroimaging findings of fetal disruption syndrome (severe microcephaly, pachygyria, schizencephaly, calcifications, and arthrogryposis), confirmed congenital Zika virus syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 79-year-old man presented to the infectious disease department of a hospital in Ningbo, China, with a 1-month history of cough and fever. Over the preceding month, he had visited two other local hospitals multiple times where investigations were undertaken.

differentials.candidate: Bronchogenic Carcinoma / Pulmonary Malignancy with Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary initial suspicion due to elderly smoking history, ground-glass nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy; ruled out by negative bronchoscopic needle biopsy of mediastinal nodes and normal serum tumor markers (CEA, CA 19-9, AFP, CA 125).

Initial working diagnosis upon hospital admission given leukocytosis and elevated CRP; ruled out by clinical and radiographic deterioration with progressive infiltrates and pleural effusion despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy including piperacillin-tazobactam, moxifloxacin, meropenem, and tigecycline.

Considered given the subacute 1-month duration of fever, cough, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy in an endemic country; ruled out by negative T-SPOT.TB interferon-gamma release assay and lack of response to empiric antitubercular therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive serum galactomannan antigen prompted fiberoptic bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage, where metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified Penicillium marneffei (Talaromyces marneffei), subsequently confirmed by extended fungal culture, with rapid clinical cure following voriconazole.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old previously healthy male farmer from the Kurunegala district of Sri Lanka presented to the hospital with a 10-day history of fever with chills and rigors, and a painful right leg wound with associated painful swelling.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary differential diagnosis considered due to occupational exposure to wet paddy field soil and water with subsequent febrile illness progressing to acute kidney injury and thrombocytopenia; excluded by negative leptospirosis IgM and IgG serological titers.

differentials.candidate: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Wound Sepsis and Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a typical cause of penetrating traumatic wound infection with purulent discharge, refractory cellulitis, and regional lymphadenitis; ruled out by normal radiographs of the right tibia and fibula and lack of MRSA isolation on blood and wound cultures.
Considered given high endemicity in Sri Lanka, acute febrile onset, and subsequent rapid decline in platelet count; ruled out by negative dengue antibody testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Wound swab and repeat blood cultures isolated Burkholderia pseudomallei demonstrating characteristic resistance to first-line cephalosporins, penicillins, and aminoglycosides with sensitivity to meropenem and co-trimoxazole, establishing acute severe melioidosis septicemia.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male farmer presents to the orthopedic outpatient department with a 12-year history of a painful left gluteal mass associated with progressively restricted left hip movement. Over the past decade, he had undergone incision and drainage of the gluteal swelling on two separate occasions at a local health center; in both instances, painful swelling recurred after brief initial symptomatic...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the chronic destructive bone lesion and cold-abscess-like presentation, but the patient had already undergone a full course of antitubercular therapy without clinical response, making tuberculosis highly unlikely.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent pyogenic abscess / Chronic bacterial soft-tissue infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Repeated incision and drainage provided only transient symptomatic relief followed by swift recurrence, and pelvic radiography showed destructive osseous involvement rather than a simple soft-tissue collection.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum IgG ELISA for Echinococcus exceeded the diagnostic cutoff, and complementary pelvic CT and MRI demonstrated a multiloculated cyst with destruction of the ischial tuberosity, acetabulum, and femoral head alongside calcified foci, subsequently confirmed by en bloc excision showing lamellated membranes and daughter cysts.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old female child is brought to the pediatric emergency department with a 7-day history of high-grade fever without chills or rigors, progressive pallor over the past 5 days, and diffuse bluish spots (petechiae) over her body for the past 2 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially considered the primary diagnosis given the combination of acute pallor, petechiae, hepatosplenomegaly, cervical lymphadenopathy, and altered sensorium, but excluded when bone marrow aspiration and biopsy demonstrated hemophagocytosis without malignant cells.
Included in the differential for persistent high-grade fever accompanied by rash, organomegaly, and systemic collapse, but ruled out as targeted blood testing confirmed a parasitic etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Peripheral blood smear demonstrated trophozoites of Plasmodium falciparum, identifying malaria-induced secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) as the unified driver of cytopenias, shock, and organomegaly, with complete defervescence on targeted therapy.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old male child is admitted to the pediatric emergency department with a 15-day history of persistent fever. Over the preceding 3 days, he developed acute bleeding manifestations, including spontaneous nasal bleeding, red-colored urine, and black tarry stools.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical picture of prolonged fever and severe hematological parameters was consistent with HLH; however, the disorder was reactive (secondary HLH) rather than primary, resolving rapidly with antiparasitic treatment alone without cytotoxic therapy.

differentials.candidate: Primary coagulopathy / Acute gastrointestinal hemorrhage of surgical etiology
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multisite bleeding involving the nasopharynx, urinary tract, and gastrointestinal tract was driven by secondary bone marrow suppression and severe thrombocytopenia rather than an isolated anatomical bleeding source or congenital coagulopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: A peripheral blood smear returned positive for Plasmodium falciparum, establishing falciparum malaria complicated by reactive secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis as the cause of pancytopenia and bleeding.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old woman residing in Pirabad, a village in the central part of Lorestan Province in western Iran, presents for clinical evaluation with a 1-month history of abdominal and back pain.

differentials.candidate: Pulmonary tuberculosis / Lower respiratory tract infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cough, hemoptysis (bloody sputum), and intermittent fevers raised suspicion for tuberculosis, but the lack of significant weight loss and the co-occurrence of abdominal pain, rash, and raw aquatic plant consumption pointed to a systemic parasitic fluke infection.
Abdominal and back pain with fevers suggested an acute or chronic hepatobiliary condition, but could not account for the concurrent respiratory and dermatologic manifestations.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum ELISA testing was positive, and microscopic stool examination revealed characteristic operculated Fasciola hepatica eggs, corroborated by a 700 bp PCR product sequencing with 99%-100% homology to F. hepatica.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old pregnant woman from Darbid Village in Delfan County, Lorestan Province, western Iran, presents with a 1-month history of abdominal and back pain accompanied by a sore throat. She has not experienced significant weight loss and has no cutaneous manifestations.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Abdominal and back pain are common obstetric complaints, but the concurrent sore throat and known dietary ingestion of raw watercress prompted investigation for a foodborne parasitic infection.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral pharyngitis / Peptic disease of pregnancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Sore throat and mild epigastric/abdominal discomfort could mimic a viral illness or gestational dyspepsia, but the lack of systemic viral features and chronic 1-month duration pointed toward fluke infestation.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic evaluation demonstrated positive ELISA and stool microscopy identifying Fasciola eggs, confirmed by PCR amplification and sequencing matching Fasciola spp. (GenBank accession MF187502).

clinical_summary: An 80-year-old male farmer living in Venaei Village in Borujerd County, Lorestan Province, western Iran, presents with a history of recurrent fever and chills. He reports no other localizing clinical symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Common causes of fever and chills in elderly farmers, but excluded by positive trematode serology and identification of liver fluke eggs in stool.
Considered in rural farmers presenting with fevers and chills, but ruled out in favor of trematode infection following specific serological and stool microscopic testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum ELISA testing was positive and microscopic stool examination revealed operculated Fasciola hepatica eggs, with PCR confirmation sequencing to F. hepatica (GenBank accession MF991068).

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male farmer from Venaei Village in Borujerd County, Lorestan Province, western Iran, presents with a 1-month history of abdominal and back pain, sore throat, and significant weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient had been managed and treated for H. pylori for over a year without clinical improvement, establishing that his symptoms were not explained by simple peptic ulceration.
Significant weight loss and chronic abdominal/back pain in a young patient raised concern for malignancy, but the dietary exposure and parasitological workup established an infectious fluke etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood ELISA and microscopic examination of the stool were positive for Fasciola hepatica eggs, confirmed by diagnostic PCR and sequencing matching F. hepatica (GenBank accession MF991069).

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old woman living in Venaei Village in Borujerd County, Lorestan Province, western Iran, presents with persistent coughing and a sore throat. She has no fever, abdominal pain, back pain, or weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Viral pharyngitis / Upper respiratory tract infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient presented exclusively with cough and sore throat without gastrointestinal symptoms, closely mimicking common respiratory infections, but diagnostic testing demonstrated a parasitic trematode infection.

Classical biliary stage fascioliasis presents with abdominal symptoms and shedding of eggs in feces, whereas this patient had negative stool examination, indicating early pre-patent hepatic migration or ectopic pharyngeal involvement.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum ELISA returned positive for Fasciola antibodies, and molecular PCR amplified a 700 bp band whose sequence confirmed 99%-100% homology to Fasciola hepatica (GenBank accession MF991070), leading to complete resolution of symptoms after antiparasitic therapy.
