clinical_summary: A 16-year-old boy with no prior medical history presents to the emergency department complaining of a severe, progressive headache of 1-month duration. Over recent days, the headache has been accompanied by episodes of vomiting and blurred vision.

differentials.candidate: Pineal gland germinoma / Germ cell tumor
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect given the patient's age, sex, midline pineal lesion, and obstructive hydrocephalus, but excluded by normal serum AFP and beta-hCG levels, and biopsy demonstrating granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

Considered because histopathology revealed small non-necrotizing granulomas and Ziehl-Neelsen staining was negative, but ruled out by a normal chest CT, normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) levels, and clinical regression on antitubercular therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Excision biopsy with frozen section and final histopathology demonstrated small non-necrotizing granulomas, perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates, and reactive microglia consistent with tuberculous encephalitis without malignancy, followed by significant radiological tumor regression on anti-TB therapy.

clinical_summary: A 2-day-old neonate is admitted to a regional referral hospital with high-grade fever, irritability, poor breastfeeding, and jaundice that developed approximately 36 hours after delivery. The infant was born to a 29-year-old G2P1 mother who attended antenatal care six times starting in the first trimester.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High-grade fever, irritability, poor feeding, and jaundice within 36 hours of birth prompted empiric coverage for presumed neonatal sepsis; however, C-reactive protein at 48 hours was nonreactive and antibiotics were stopped as parasitemia cleared on antimalarials.

differentials.candidate: Rh or ABO isoimmunization / Hemolytic disease of the newborn
differentials.rule_out_reason: Early-onset neonatal jaundice in an infant born to an Rh-negative mother raised suspicion of isoimmune hemolysis; however, both the mother and infant were blood group A Rh-negative, hemoglobin was normal (15.2 g/dL), and platelet count was preserved.

diagnostic_pivot: A malaria rapid diagnostic test (MRDT) was positive for P. falciparum, and a thin blood smear demonstrated intraerythrocytic P. falciparum trophozoites (1.846 × 10^3 infected red blood cells), confirming congenital malaria.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old male farmer with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department with a one-week history of persistent, high-grade fever associated with retro-orbital headache, generalized arthralgia, and intense myalgia.

differentials.candidate: Acute cerebrovascular accident or intracranial hypertension
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient developed acute drowsiness and agitation, but cranial computed tomography ruled out acute vascular insults or edema.
Considered due to persistent fevers and rapid multiorgan decompensation, but transthoracic echocardiography revealed normal valvular anatomy without vegetations.
Considered in light of profound septic shock, pulmonary-renal failure, and subsequent hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, but standard microbiological blood cultures remained sterile.
The constellation of muddy water exposure, pulmonary hemorrhage, acute renal failure, and secondary HLH culminated in posthumous definitive serological confirmation.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old female residing in a rural community in the Macanao municipality on Margarita Island, Venezuela, presented to the health center with a 6-month history of intermittent nocturnal fevers, progressive malaise, a 6-kg weight loss, arthralgias, anorexia, dizziness, and secondary amenorrhea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prominent B symptoms, generalized lymphadenopathy, marked hepatosplenomegaly, and peripheral pancytopenia, but bone marrow flow cytometry showed non-neoplastic maturation arrest with only 1% blasts.
Considered as a leading infectious etiology for prolonged fever of unknown origin with hepatosplenomegaly and generalized adenopathy, but tuberculin skin testing was negative.
Considered because endemic fungal infections can cause prolonged fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and cytopenias, but fungal cultures remained negative.
Direct microscopic examination of bone marrow trephine biopsy demonstrated high-density intracellular parasitism within marrow macrophages along with positive rK39 serology.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old woman with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection diagnosed one year prior presented to the hospital with a 6-month history of progressively spreading skin lesions. The eruption initially manifested on her face and subsequently extended to involve her chest, abdomen, and extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because disseminated vascular papules and nodules are classic opportunistic manifestations in advanced HIV, but histopathological evaluation showed dense inflammatory histiocytic infiltration rather than vascular or spindle cell proliferation.

While standard cutaneous infection presents with solitary or localized self-limiting ulcerated lesions, the widespread anatomic dissemination across the face, trunk, and extremities indicated diffuse disease favored by cellular immunodeficiency.
High-power microscopic examination of the skin biopsy revealed macrophages laden with classic intracellular amastigotes, definitively confirming the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse, anxiety, and insomnia presented to an outpatient primary care clinic for his annual physical examination. He reported a 25-year history of smoking half a pack of cigarettes daily.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered on initial chest radiograph given the medial upper lobe opacity, but symptoms were indolent without fever or leukocytosis, and repeat imaging demonstrated branching nodularity in an accessory lobe.

differentials.candidate: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or smoker's chronic bronchitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 25-pack-year smoking history, productive morning cough, and exertional dyspnea with obstructive spirometry, but this failed to account for focal apical peribronchovascular nodules on computed tomography.

differentials.candidate: Bronchogenic carcinoma / Malignant solitary pulmonary nodule
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to smoking history and an apical mass-like nodule measuring up to 2 cm, but transbronchial biopsy revealed infectious necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant neoplasia.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Tuberculosis of the azygos lobe)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Transbronchial biopsy and bronchoalveolar lavage targeted to the right lung apex and azygos lobe isolated the acid-fast pathogen on microbiological evaluation.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old boy (weight 19 kg, height 113 cm, BMI 14.9 kg/m²) with no significant past medical history presented to the hospital following transfer from a primary care facility with a 5-day history of persistent fever, marked asthenia, generalized myalgias, arthralgias, multiple episodes of emesis, severe abdominal pain, and headache.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to persistent fevers, third spacing, oligoanuria, and multiorgan dysfunction, but multiple serial bacteriological cultures remained entirely sterile.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis / Mononucleosis syndromes (EBV, CMV, Toxoplasmosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and marked transaminitis, but comprehensive acute infectious serologies were negative.

Considered because of persistent bicytopenia with hepatosplenomegaly extending beyond the usual acute infection course, but bone marrow evaluation revealed reactive nonnecrotizing granulomas without neoplastic cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Severe dengue with post-infectious Evans syndrome)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute arboviral infection with capillary leak and warning signs was confirmed by IgM serology, followed by autoimmune Coombs-positive bicytopenia consistent with Evans syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old previously healthy man presented with a one-month history of progressive gait unsteadiness, urinary incontinence, and recurrent symptoms of increased intracranial pressure, including intense headaches, projectile vomiting, and brief episodes of loss of consciousness.

differentials.candidate: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given location at the foramina of Monro with paroxysmal hydrocephalus, but operative intervention revealed a vascularized wall containing purulent fluid rather than mucinous substance.
Considered due to the cystic, calcified appearance extending into the third ventricle, but aspiration of the lesion yielded thick frank purulent exudate.
Considered upon aspirating thick purulent fluid from the ventricle, but standard bacterial staining revealed acid-fast organisms rather than typical pyogenic cocci or bacilli.
Molecular analysis of the intraventricular purulent fluid unequivocally identified the mycobacterial pathogen.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old Caribbean man was admitted to the intensive care unit with acute deterioration of consciousness, severe neck stiffness, and high fever of 102.2 °F (39.0 °C). He had no significant prior past medical history aside from an ongoing 3-month history of severe chronic watery diarrhea accompanied by an unintentional 33-pound weight loss that was undergoing outpatient evaluation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered on initial emergency presentation given high fever, meningism, and neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis, prompting standard empiric antimicrobial coverage, but microbiological isolation of enteric bacilli pointed to intestinal breach rather than nasopharyngeal pathogens.
Considered based on bilateral basal ganglia hyperintensities and diffuse cerebral edema on MRI, but clinical features were secondary to severe enteric bacterial sepsis and parasitic translocation.
The combination of enteric rod meningitis with purpura and alveolar hemorrhage was confirmed by identifying invasive filariform larvae on dermal punch biopsy and in respiratory secretions.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old female school student living in a rural community in Cameroon presented to a local clinic with insidious-onset right hypochondriac abdominal pain and intermittent fevers progressing over one month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fever, tachypnea, right basilar stony dullness, crackles, and chest radiograph revealing pleural effusion, but these pulmonary signs reflected reactive transdiaphragmatic inflammation secondary to underlying subdiaphragmatic hepatic pathology.

Considered given the large cystic liver mass in an endemic rural region, but the acute septic toxicity, high-grade fevers, extreme leukocytosis, thick irregular walls, and internal gas bubbles indicated an invasive infectious abscess.
Direct parasitological stool microscopy identifying characteristic cysts along with Charcot-Leyden crystals confirmed invasive intestinal protozoan infection explaining the giant hepatic abscess.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old male student presented to the medical unit with a two-week history of progressively worsening shortness of breath, increasing abdominal distension, a dry non-productive cough, anorexia, and unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute constitutional decline, anorexia, weight loss, and large pericardial effusion, but systemic examination revealed no peripheral or visceral lymphadenopathy or neoplastic masses.
Considered given the patient's youth, but idiopathic viral pericarditis typically presents acutely with chest pain and rarely causes massive hemorrhagic exudative tamponade with systemic wasting.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Tuberculous pericarditis with hemorrhagic tamponade)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute presentation with polyserositis, exudative hemorrhagic pericardial effusion, and residence in a high-burden endemic setting justified the definitive diagnosis and full resolution on targeted therapy.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male residing in Dilla presented to the medical clinic with a one-year history of right-sided pleuritic chest pain and a cough productive of whitish sputum. Over the preceding three months, his symptoms had accelerated significantly, accompanied by drenching night sweats, intermittent fevers, anorexia, and progressive involuntary weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Pleural malignancy (Malignant mesothelioma, bronchogenic carcinoma, or lymphoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 1-year chronic course, profound weight loss, and massive unilateral pleural opacity causing compressive mass effect on chest radiograph, but microbiological molecular testing demonstrated an infectious mycobacterial etiology.

differentials.candidate: Chronic bacterial empyema or lung abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of chronic productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and dense opacification, but rapid diagnostic assays ruled out typical pyogenic bacteria.
Direct automated molecular sputum testing identified the mycobacterial pathogen while simultaneously demonstrating resistance to first-line rifampicin.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female with a medical history of type 1 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department complaining of backache and progressive lower limb weakness. On admission, contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbosacral region demonstrates loss of intervertebral disc space with a paraspinal collection at the L3-L4 level extending into the bilateral iliopsoas muscles with associated neural compression.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute pyogenic spondylodiscitis classically produces bacteremic fever and acute neutrophilia; in this patient, initial standard treatment failed, and repeated percutaneous aspirates sent for standard aerobic microbiology yielded no bacterial growth, while liquid culture demonstrated acid-fast mycobacteria.

differentials.candidate: Spinal epidural neoplasm / Metastatic spinal malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Vertebral metastases typically involve the vertebral bodies or posterior elements with sparing of the intervertebral disc; in contrast, imaging demonstrated prominent disc-space collapse and contiguous bilateral psoas fluid collections typical of an infectious discitis.

diagnostic_pivot: Needle aspiration of the paraspinal collection with rapid molecular testing (Xpert MTB/RIF) and automated liquid culture (MGIT) that confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis with rifampicin resistance, followed by secondary anaerobic culture isolation of Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus via MALDI-TOF MS upon acute relapse.

clinical_summary: An 85-year-old previously healthy man presents to the surgical clinic with acute, generalized, constant dull abdominal pain that began two days prior to evaluation, rated 4 out of 10 in severity with no radiation and no correlation to meals or exertion.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or amebic liver abscess with intraperitoneal rupture
differentials.rule_out_reason: Hepatic abscess rupture typically manifests with high fevers, leukocytosis, and acute peritonitic signs; this patient had a normal white blood cell count, mild afebrile tenderness without peritonism, and CT imaging demonstrated well-demarcated encapsulated fluid collections with floating endocyst membranes rather than purulent thick-walled abscess cavities.

differentials.candidate: Benign mesenteric or simple peritoneal inclusion cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple intra-abdominal epithelial cysts typically lack internal membranes, do not elevate inflammatory markers (CRP 187 mg/L), and are not associated with concurrent multi-organ liver lesions or intra-abdominal bloody fluid originating from hepatic perforation.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrating pathognomonic detached undulating laminar membranes (water lily sign) within hepatic cysts and a pelvic cystic mass, confirmed on laparotomy and histopathological examination of the excised cyst capsule as echinococcal hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old female presents with a one-month history of intermittent upper abdominal pain and discomfort that worsens following ingestion of fatty foods. She has a history of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection since childhood without prior antiviral therapy or HBV DNA monitoring, as well as a family history of HBV carriage in her mother and siblings.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although chronic active hepatitis B, cirrhosis, and extreme serum alpha-fetoprotein elevation (1,210 ng/mL) confirmed underlying HCC, the presence of dense peripheral arc-like calcifications in an endemic pastoral resident suggested an independent second pathology, which was verified by intradermal Casoni positivity and dual pathology on surgical resection.

An infectious bacterial or amebic abscess typically produces high fevers, acute right upper quadrant peritonism, and leukocytosis; in contrast, this patient had a normal-to-low leukocyte count (3.7 × 10^9/L) and thick circumferential calcifications inconsistent with acute purulent liquefaction.

diagnostic_pivot: Epidemiologic history of pastoral residence, positive Casoni intradermal test, and abdominal CT demonstrating conspicuous calcification within a discrete hepatic space-occupying lesion, definitively confirmed on surgical specimen pathology as hydatid infection coexisting with moderately differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old female presents to the university hospital with a one-month history of recurrent fevers, involuntary weight loss, and intermittent lumbar back pain. She also reports persistent headache, chills, and drenching night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread FDG-avid skeletal lesions, constitutional B-symptoms (fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss), and lack of pulmonary disease initially suggested advanced skeletal metastasis or lymphoma; however, surgical bone biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomatous sequestrum without malignant tumor cells.

Pyogenic bone infections typically cause acute local suppurative inflammation and neutrophilic infiltration; here, the indolent multifocal skeletal presentation and absence of an acute bacterial source prompted an open vertebral biopsy that demonstrated characteristic granulomatous changes.

diagnostic_pivot: Open surgical biopsy of the L2 lamina and vertebral bodies showing local sequestrum formation, multinucleated Langhans giant cells, and necrotic bone, establishing the definitive diagnosis of multifocal skeletal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old Nepalese woman living in Western Europe presents to the emergency department with worsening unilateral headaches of 10 days' duration, accompanied by nausea and vomiting, refractory to simple analgesics.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary intraventricular neoplasms usually exhibit solid tissue architecture, vascularity, and prominent gadolinium enhancement on MRI; this lesion was completely non-enhancing, isointense to CSF, and contained an eccentric non-vascular nodule.

differentials.candidate: Colloid cyst or non-parasitic ependymal cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Colloid cysts characteristically obstruct the foramen of Monro in the anterior third ventricle rather than the occipital horn of the lateral ventricle, and simple ependymal cysts do not contain diffusion-restricting internal scoleces or coexist with remote cerebral calcifications.

diagnostic_pivot: Neuroimaging identification of a non-enhancing intraventricular cystic mass with an eccentric diffusion-restricting scolex that proved free-floating following endoscopic ventriculostomy, corroborated by positive ELISA detection of Taenia solium antigen and antibodies in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male presents for clinical evaluation with multiple persistent cutaneous lesions following international travel. Physical examination reveals a total of 10 discrete skin lesions distributed across the bilateral upper extremities, lower extremities, and the flank.

differentials.candidate: Falciparum malaria with cutaneous manifestations / coinfection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although a rapid diagnostic antigen test for Plasmodium falciparum returned positive during the fever workup, the patient had primary indolent skin ulcers rather than acute febrile hemolysis, and confirmatory blood testing including repeated thick-and-thin blood smears and qualitative RT-PCR were completely negative, demonstrating an antigen cross-reaction.

Deep fungal infections can present with widespread noduloulcerative lesions in travelers, but special fungal stains and microbiological evaluation failed to identify fungal yeast or hyphal elements, directing reference referral for dedicated parasite evaluation.

diagnostic_pivot: Reference laboratory examination of skin biopsy tissue confirming Leishmania amastigotes on histopathology and positive immunohistochemical staining, proving cutaneous leishmaniasis as the true etiology of the lesions and unmasking the false-positive malaria rapid test.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old female presents with recurrent rectal bleeding mixed with stools and crampy lower abdominal pain of 5 days' duration. On focused review of systems, she reports a 3-month history of productive cough, drenching night sweats, and an unintentional 10-kg weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Endoscopic features of segmental ileocecal ulceration, inflammatory polyps, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy closely mimicked Crohn's disease; however, endoscopic biopsy histopathology demonstrated necrotizing (caseating) granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli rather than non-caseating granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Anticoagulation-induced coagulopathic gastrointestinal bleeding / Vascular ectasia
differentials.rule_out_reason: While therapeutic warfarin with an INR of 2.78 contributed to the severity of acute blood loss (hemoglobin 5.30 g/dL), anticoagulation alone does not account for deep segmental colonic ulcerations, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, or chronic pulmonary consolidations.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on direct sputum smear and colonoscopic biopsy specimens revealing necrotizing granulomas with acid-fast bacilli positivity, later confirmed by growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex on Lowenstein-Jensen medium.

clinical_summary: A 78-year-old man with a medical history of hypertension and remote cerebral infarction presents with recurrent fevers, fatigue, and a 5-kg weight loss over the preceding year. Two weeks prior to admission, his fatigue abruptly intensified, and fever spiked up to 39.5°C.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial infective endocarditis / Pyogenic mycotic aortitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic arterial infection typically exhibits frank bacteremia, high procalcitonin levels, and valvular vegetation; in this patient, echocardiography showed normal valves without vegetation, procalcitonin was only mildly elevated (0.213 ng/mL), and mycobacterial testing subsequently confirmed tuberculosis.

differentials.candidate: Penetrating atherosclerotic aortic ulcer / Non-infectious intramural hematoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although age and hypertension predisposed to aortic atheroma, isolated atherosclerotic disease cannot account for recurrent high-grade fevers, progressive weight loss, or interval rapid expansion of diffuse pulmonary lesions into miliary nodules with pleural effusion.

diagnostic_pivot: Interval imaging demonstrating rapid expansion of diffuse pulmonary micronodules into florid miliary tuberculosis with pleural effusion, accompanied by positive interferon-gamma T-SPOT, positive sputum culture, and positive sputum GeneXpert assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old woman presents with intermittent low back pain that persisted for one month, worsening acutely over the preceding week until becoming unbearable. Three months previously, she was evaluated at a local hospital for a productive cough, where chest computed tomography showed suspicious pulmonary lesions and an interferon-gamma release assay was positive; an empirical multi-agent regimen was initiated, but she...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Uncomplicated degenerative aneurysms occur without surrounding periaortic inflammatory mantles, regional lymphadenopathy, or synchronous diffuse miliary pulmonary nodularity; here, imaging and past exposure strongly implicated an infectious lymph-node erosive process.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial mycotic aneurysm (e.g., Salmonella or Staphylococcus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic aortitis typically presents with severe acute bacteremia, marked leukocytosis, and high procalcitonin levels; in contrast, this patient demonstrated a normal white blood cell count (7.22 × 10^9/L) and low procalcitonin (0.213 ng/mL), with GeneXpert testing confirming mycobacterial disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum GeneXpert assay positive for rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing active miliary tuberculosis as the etiology of the contiguous retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and eroding abdominal aortic pseudoaneurysm.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old woman without significant past medical history presents with a 3-month history of progressive dysphagia, initially for solid foods and subsequently for both liquids and solids. She reports an intentional or unintentional 10-kg weight loss, loss of appetite, and intermittent fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive dysphagia, a 10-kg weight loss, and a large 3-cm esophageal ulcer in a 55-year-old strongly raised suspicion for esophageal cancer; however, endoscopic biopsies showed granulomatous inflammation without cellular atypia or malignancy, and chest CT revealed diffuse pulmonary micronodules rather than primary esophageal tumor mass.

differentials.candidate: Esophageal Crohn's disease / Idiopathic fistulizing esophagitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although mucosal ulceration with a fistula tract and epithelioid cell granulomas without caseation can mimic esophageal Crohn's disease, Crohn's disease does not typically manifest with widespread necrotic mediastinal adenopathy or diffuse bilateral pulmonary micronodules, and sputum testing demonstrated acid-fast bacilli.

diagnostic_pivot: Chest CT imaging demonstrating necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy eroding into the esophagus and diffuse miliary pulmonary micronodules, corroborated by a positive sputum smear for acid-fast bacilli.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old immunocompetent man presents with an 11-year history of a huge, expanding erythematous erosive plaque on his neck. The lesion initially began as a pigeon's egg-sized nodule 11 years prior and gradually progressed.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected and treated with prednisone acetate and azathioprine over a 10-year span, but the cutaneous plaque relentlessly expanded despite prolonged systemic immunosuppression.

Considered due to the chronic verrucous and nodular plaque, but ruled out by a normal neurological examination, negative microscopic examination for acid-fast bacilli, and negative specific serological tests (IgM/IgG against NDO-LID and MMP-II) and ELISPOT.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite an initial negative single PCR and negative T-SPOT.TB, histopathology revealed dermal necrotizing epithelioid-cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells. Nested PCR targeting rpoB and hsp65 genes was positive, and tissue cultures on Lowenstein-Jensen medium yielded yellow caseous colonies 100% homologous to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with near-complete clearance following a standard 6-month 2HRZE/4HR regimen.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old man presents with progressive headache, fever, unresponsiveness, irritability, and neck pain. Over the preceding two years, he experienced an unintentional weight loss of 35 kg.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial working diagnosis given acute-subacute encephalopathy and CSF pleocytosis; however, the patient deteriorated clinically despite intravenous acyclovir, developing high fever, worsening delirium, and cranial nerve palsies.

Anti-NMDAR IgG antibodies were identified in serum and CSF, explaining the neuropsychiatric presentation; however, isolated primary autoimmune encephalitis could not explain apical fibrocavitary lung lesions, encapsulated pleural effusion, and positive mycobacterial testing, establishing that the autoimmune process was secondary to underlying central nervous system infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was achieved when tuberculin PPD skin test (++), T-SPOT.TB assay, and CSF MTB complex DNA PCR all returned positive, alongside repeat brain MRI demonstrating leptomeningeal enhancement, ring-enhancing nodules, and parenchymal signal abnormalities, with substantial clinical and radiographic recovery upon targeted anti-tuberculosis therapy and high-dose glucocorticoid pulse therapy.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old girl is admitted with a 13-month history of worsening intermittent chest pain, cough, and fever. Her illness began 13 months prior with acute chest pain, fever, and cough.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial lung abscess and purulent pericarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected given suppurative lung cavitation, high CRP, and pericarditis; however, the patient failed multiple prolonged courses of broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy, and marked peripheral eosinophilia persisted.

Empirically treated with dual-agent anti-tuberculosis drugs for several months without symptomatic remission, and extensive mycobacterial workups across hospitalizations remained consistently negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of persistent high-grade peripheral eosinophilia (17%) and geographic exposure in Yunnan province established suspicion for a foodborne trematode; serum ELISA for Paragonimus was positive, and oral praziquantel resulted in rapid resolution of pleural effusion and complete cessation of chest pain and fevers.

clinical_summary: A 20-month-old female infant presents to the clinic accompanied by her mother with a chief complaint of traumatic self-injury to both hands caused by a 'pointed tooth.' The child has a complex congenital medical background significant for microcephaly, arthrogryposis, ocular and auditory abnormalities, and neuromuscular spasticity with a seizure disorder managed on chronic anticonvulsant and muscle antispasmodic medications.

differentials.candidate: Other Congenital TORCH Infections (e.g., Cytomegalovirus, Congenital Syphilis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although classic TORCH agents cause microcephaly, intracranial calcifications, and neurosensory deficits, congenital syphilis characteristically induces permanent incisor notches (Hutchinson teeth) rather than primary incisor claw cusps, and CMV/toxoplasmosis do not classically cause the severe fetal arthrogryposis sequence seen here.

differentials.candidate: Neurogenetic / Metabolic Self-Mutilation Syndromes (e.g., Lesch-Nyhan syndrome)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to involuntary biting and finger trauma in an infant with motor delay and spasticity; however, the self-injury was purely mechanical due to perioral hypotonia resting against a malformed, pointed claw cusp rather than compulsive behavioral automutilation.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of congenital microcephaly, arthrogryposis, ocular and auditory abnormalities, and characteristic primary tooth dysmorphology with claw-cusp malformation confirmed congenital Zika virus syndrome, managed with two-stage digital restorative coronoplasty and indirect composite crowning.

clinical_summary: An 8-month-old Chinese boy is admitted with a 6-day history of persistent fever and cough. Prior to referral, he received a 5-day course of empiric antibacterial therapy at an outside hospital without clinical response; laboratory evaluation there showed a white blood cell count of 24.62 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 44.1%) and C-reactive protein of 32.4 mg/L.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given marked leukocytosis, elevated CRP, and dense lobar consolidation; however, the infant developed escalating fevers above 39°C and rising inflammatory markers despite broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage with cefoperazone-sulbactam and imipenem-cilastatin.

Considered due to the presence of calcified axillary nodules, prominent supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and pulmonary consolidation; however, purified protein derivative (PPD) and T-SPOT assays were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when blood mNGS identified Talaromyces marneffei within 14 hours, subsequently confirmed by microbiological blood culture growth on day 9; combined with the detection of a hemizygous CD40LG mutation underlying hyper-IgM syndrome, targeted antifungal therapy with amphotericin B and itraconazole led to complete defervescence and recovery.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male renal transplant recipient presents with high fever, night sweats, diarrhea, and progressive dyspnea. Two years prior, he received a kidney transplant maintained on immunosuppressive therapy with tacrolimus and prednisone; mycophenolate had been suspended three months earlier during a mild viral illness from which he had recovered.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given his recent history of viral infection and bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT; however, triage repeat nasopharyngeal RT-PCR was negative and chest radiography revealed an extensive nodular/miliary pattern atypical for isolated viral pneumonia.

Considered as an opportunistic fungal cause of febrile nodular lung disease in a renal allograft recipient; while fungal cultures later revealed concurrent Histoplasma capsulatum growth, the primary immediate pathogen identified on initial bronchoalveolar lavage was Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage yielded positive PCR testing for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (alongside CMV and RSV), establishing pulmonary tuberculosis as the leading cause of the extensive nodular infiltrates and prompting immediate quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male technical worker presents for emergency evaluation with a 4-month history of recurrent high fevers, which escalated over the preceding month with severe watery diarrhea. Four months prior, he developed abrupt fevers peaking at 39.9°C, typically spiking each afternoon and remitting spontaneously after several hours, accompanied by headache, diffuse myalgias, and nausea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's remote African travel history, previous treated malaria, and severe splenomegaly with pancytopenia; however, multiple peripheral blood smears and rapid Plasmodium antigen tests were repeatedly negative, and fever was unresponsive to artemisinin.

differentials.candidate: Decompensated Cirrhosis with Bacterial Sepsis / Hypersplenism
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because imaging demonstrated cirrhosis, ascites, portal hypertension, and splenomegaly alongside elevated procalcitonin; however, empirical targeted antimicrobial therapy (moxifloxacin) failed to halt the recurrent fever spikes, indicating an unaddressed systemic protozoal etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of peripheral blood on day 4 identified Leishmania infantum and Leishmania donovani sequences, and CDC rK39 antibody testing confirmed visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar); prompt initiation of sodium stibogluconate resulted in rapid defervescence within 72 hours, although the illness was later complicated by multiorgan failure.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old male student residing in Chongqing presents to the emergency fever clinic with a persistent febrile illness and cough of several weeks' duration. His illness began with low-grade fever fluctuating between 37°C and 38°C, fatigue, chills, dry cough, and pharyngeal discomfort following a presumed viral upper respiratory illness.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) / Macrophage Activation Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of prolonged high fevers, splenomegaly, cytopenias, marked hyperferritinemia (>2000 ng/mL), hypertriglyceridemia, and elevated LDH; however, rather than idiopathic or malignant HLH, the hyperinflammatory state was triggered by an occult intracellular protozoan infection.

Considered given positive direct Coombs test, ANA (1:100), anti-Jo-1 antibody, and elevated rheumatoid factor; however, these represented nonspecific polyclonal B-cell activation secondary to reticuloendothelial infection, and empiric dexamethasone failed to control the fever.

diagnostic_pivot: Plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified Leishmania infantum on day 4, and CDC rK39 antibody testing confirmed visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar); intravenous sodium stibogluconate (SSG) led to prompt defervescence within 72 hours, spleen retraction to 4.5 cm, and normalization of liver function and hematology.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old male student presents with a 3-day history of recurrent, colicky, migratory right iliac fossa pain. Prior to presentation, medical interventions at a peripheral medical center had failed to alleviate his symptoms.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Appendicitis with Appendiceal Phlegmon
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis based on migratory right iliac fossa pain, peritoneal irritation signs, and a large inflammatory mass on ultrasound; although the acute inflammatory phlegmon regressed with intravenous antibiotics, the underlying driver was an ectopic parasitic granulomatous process.

Considered in a young adult presenting with a large 8 x 10 cm right lower quadrant mass; however, the mass regressed with conservative medical therapy, interval appendectomy showed a grossly normal cecum and ileum without neoplastic invasion, and histology revealed non-neoplastic granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the resected appendix following interval appendectomy revealed transmural chronic fibrotic granulomatous inflammation encasing both viable and non-viable ova of Schistosoma mansoni and Schistosoma hematobium, and the patient was successfully cured with oral praziquantel therapy.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old nulliparous woman is referred to the gynecologic oncology clinic for evaluation of progressive abdominal distension and constitutional symptoms concerning for ovarian malignancy. She reports a 6-month history of abdominal discomfort, progressive abdominal swelling, drenching night sweats, intermittent fevers, and unintentional weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis given the combination of massive CA-125 elevation (1,289 U/mL), omental nodularity ('omental caking'), ascites, and an adnexal mass; however, paracentesis fluid cytology showed only benign mesothelial cells, endometrial and omental biopsies showed no neoplasm, and diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed normal ovaries without malignant lesions.

differentials.candidate: Non-Infectious Granulomatous Peritonitis (e.g., Sarcoidosis, Ruptured Cyst Reaction)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered upon discovery of omental granulomas without malignant cells; however, the presence of necrotizing (caseating) granulomas, chest CT showing biapical pleural scarring and a parenchymal nodule, a 10-mm tuberculin skin test, and a positive interferon-gamma release assay identified an infectious etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when laparoscopic biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomas, alongside positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus and remote apical lung scarring; empirical quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy led to rapid clinical recovery, CA-125 reduction to 74 U/mL at 4 weeks, and complete radiological resolution of omental caking, ascites, and lymphadenopathy at 8 weeks.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old Asian woman presented at 33 to 34 weeks of gestation with premature rupture of membranes and underwent an emergency cesarean section, delivering a preterm infant. Three months prior to presentation, following interpersonal stress, she became socially withdrawn, remained secluded in her room for two months, ate poorly, and had unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Depressive disorder with peripartum onset / postpartum psychosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected given her prominent withdrawal, depressed mood, tearfulness, weight loss, irritability, and auditory hallucinations following childbirth; however, psychiatric illness alone could not account for three weeks of intermittent fevers and headaches, subsequent focal cranial nerve deficits, positive meningeal signs, and hydrocephalus on neuroimaging.
Considered when the patient suffered an acute deterioration in consciousness two days post-admission; excluded by entirely normal electrolyte and metabolic evaluations.

differentials.candidate: Cerebral infarction from embolization / Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Raised after non-enhanced brain CT demonstrated hypodense subcortical lesions in the occipital lobe, parietooccipital lobe, and cerebellum with hydrocephalus; ruled out when contrast administration revealed intense basilar and leptomeningeal enhancement rather than ischemic or vasogenic edematous patterns.

diagnostic_pivot: Neurological examination revealing meningeal signs, facial paresthesia, and tetraparesthesia with pathological reflexes, combined with contrast-enhanced CT showing prominent enhancement of basal cisterns and sulci with communicating hydrocephalus, alongside chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound confirming disseminated pulmonary and lymph node involvement, established tuberculous meningitis with intracranial tuberculoma.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old woman residing in the western region of Madagascar presented to the thoracic surgery outpatient clinic for evaluation of chronic dry cough. She was an office worker and had no significant prior medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered high on the differential diagnosis given the high endemicity in Madagascar, chronic cough, and nodular parenchymal lesion; excluded by preserved general condition, lack of constitutional symptoms, and negative molecular testing for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

differentials.candidate: Primary bronchogenic carcinoma / solitary pulmonary metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Prompted initial referral to the thoracic surgery department due to the solid subpleural nodule; ruled out by young non-smoking status, lack of internal contrast enhancement, surrounding ground-glass halo, peripheral eosinophilia, and subsequent complete radiologic disappearance with anti-helminthic therapy.

Considered because of concurrent pulmonary and hepatic nodular findings with peripheral eosinophilia in an endemic area; excluded by normal liver biochemistries and negative amoebic serological testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of positive Schistosoma serology in the context of prominent peripheral eosinophilia and solitary subpleural nodule, followed by rapid symptom resolution and radiologic disappearance (>75% reduction at 3 months, complete resolution at 6 months) after a single dose of praziquantel, confirmed pulmonary nodular schistosomiasis.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old woman with a history of bilateral lung transplantation for severe emphysema presented with painful occipital subcutaneous nodules and painful swelling of her right index finger approximately 74 days post-transplantation.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial cellulitis and acute flexor tenosynovitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected and treated outpatient; ruled out by failure of a 14-day course of linezolid and ceftriaxone, progression to systemic symptoms, and emergence of multifocal hepatic abscesses.

Strongly considered when acid-fast bacilli were identified on synovial fluid and liver histology in an immunosuppressed host with skin and soft tissue involvement; excluded when MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry identified the organism as Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex rather than an atypical mycobacterial species.

differentials.candidate: Invasive fungal infection (e.g., endemic mycosis, Aspergillus, Candida)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A high-probability consideration in a lung transplant recipient receiving augmented immunosuppression with glucocorticoids and rituximab; ruled out by negative fungal stains (GMS) and absence of fungal growth.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic evaluation of core needle liver biopsy and surgical drainage of the flexor tendon sheath demonstrating necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli, coupled with culture identification via MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry as Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, established donor-transmitted disseminated tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old girl from Ethiopia presented to the hospital with a 4-month history of progressive global headaches. Over the preceding month, her symptoms had escalated, accompanied by daily projectile non-bilious vomiting occurring two to three times per day and blurred vision.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of fluid characteristics that strictly follow CSF signal intensity (T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense, complete FLAIR suppression) with total absence of wall enhancement or edema; however, arachnoid cysts are typically extra-axial developmental anomalies, whereas this lesion represented an expansive, intraparenchymal spherical mass producing progressive intracranial hypertension and marked midline shift in an endemic setting.

differentials.candidate: Cystic intracranial neoplasm (e.g., pilocytic astrocytoma or glioblastoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: High suspicion in a pediatric patient presenting with subacute intracranial hypertension and a massive cerebral lesion; excluded by the complete absence of any mural nodular enhancement, lack of cyst wall gadolinium enhancement, and lack of surrounding vasogenic edema.

Considered given the infectious risk in the region; ruled out by the lack of peripheral rim enhancement, lack of capsular thickening, complete absence of perilesional vasogenic edema, and absence of an eccentric scolex.

diagnostic_pivot: The distinctive MRI phenotype of a huge, unilocular intraparenchymal cyst matching CSF signal with complete FLAIR suppression, no peripheral contrast enhancement, and no vasogenic edema, combined with successful intact surgical excision of a 15x13x12 cm cyst whose histopathology confirmed an acellular laminated cuticular layer and nucleated germinal layer, established giant intracranial hydatid cyst (Echinococcosis).

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old previously healthy male surgeon presented with a painful lesion on his right thumb, ipsilateral axillary swelling, low-grade fever, and chest tightness. Fifty days prior to presentation, he had sustained a deep accidental needlestick puncture injury to the palmar aspect of his right thumb while performing an emergency thoracentesis and pleural drainage on an acutely ill patient who presented...

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial cellulitis and flexor tenosynovitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Common after penetrating needlestick injuries to the hand; ruled out by the prolonged 3-week incubation period, failure of acute suppurative evolution within the first 48 hours, and indolent development of an indurated granulomatous plaque with regional lymphadenopathy.

differentials.candidate: Atypical environmental mycobacterial infection (e.g., Mycobacterium marinum) or sporotrichosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because chronic nodular tenosynovitis and ascending lymphadenitis (sporotrichoid spread) classically follow traumatic cutaneous inoculation; excluded when culture from the aspirated fluid isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

Considered when chest CT revealed an ipsilateral pleural effusion accompanying right axillary lymphadenopathy; ruled out as direct pleural tuberculosis when diagnostic thoracentesis showed sterile exudate with negative AFB stains and negative mycobacterial cultures, representing a reactive sympathetic effusion.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining of the thumb abscess aspirate followed by mycobacterial culture confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis (with primary multidrug resistance inherited from the source patient), combined with hand MRI demonstrating flexor pollicis tenosynovitis, established primary inoculation cutaneous tuberculosis with flexor tenosynovitis.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute onset of palpitations and lightheadedness. She had a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a prior ischemic stroke, for which she took aspirin, irbesartan, metformin, and atorvastatin.

differentials.candidate: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with scar-related ventricular tachycardia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Top initial differential given multiple cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes mellitus, hypertension, previous stroke); ruled out by previous coronary angiography showing no obstructive atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.

differentials.candidate: Supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy or pre-excitation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a patient with a history of atrial flutter presenting with regular wide-complex tachycardia; excluded by electrocardiographic demonstration of atrioventricular dissociation with intermittent non-conducted P waves confirming monomorphic ventricular tachycardia.

differentials.candidate: Cardiac sarcoidosis or non-infectious inflammatory cardiomyopathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a non-ischemic etiology of basal conduction system disease, inflammatory myocarditis, and ventricular arrhythmias; distinguished by the pathognomonic inferolateral wall thinning/aneurysm, rural Mexican origin, and positive Trypanosoma cruzi serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Cardiac MRI demonstrating localized basal-to-mid inferolateral left ventricular wall thinning, dyskinesia/aneurysm, and transmural late gadolinium enhancement, combined with positive Trypanosoma cruzi IgG confirmed by CDC enzyme immunoassay and TESA-blot in a patient from rural Mexico, established chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (American trypanosomiasis).

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old Italian man presented with a 6-month history of multiple progressive nodules and ulcerations developing within pre-existing skin plaques. He had a 20-year history of plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma / iatrogenic lymphoproliferative disorder
differentials.rule_out_reason: High concern in a patient receiving chronic anti-TNF and methotrexate therapy presenting with ulcerating skin nodules showing dense dermal lymphoid infiltrates; ruled out by molecular gene rearrangement studies demonstrating polyclonal IgH and TCR gamma configurations without clonal malignant expansion.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune connective tissue disease / cutaneous lupus erythematosus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of interface dermatitis and dense pseudolymphomatous lymphoid infiltrate; excluded by negative direct immunofluorescence for immunoglobulins and C3, negative antinuclear and extractable nuclear antigen antibodies, and normal serum complement levels.

differentials.candidate: Secondary syphilis, cutaneous tuberculosis, or borreliosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because histopathology showed a rich plasma cell infiltrate in an immunosuppressed individual; ruled out by negative treponemal serology, negative Borrelia testing, and negative Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic evaluation of cutaneous biopsies with Giemsa, Feulgen, and hematoxylin-eosin staining revealing intracellular amastigotes bearing characteristic kinetoplasts within macrophages, confirmed by miniexon PCR and restriction fragment length polymorphism as Leishmania infantum, alongside positive anti-Leishmania serology (titer 1:1,600), established cutaneous pseudolymphoma secondary to Leishmania infantum infection.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old man in Sidama, Ethiopia, presented to a specialized internal medicine clinic with a 3-month worsening of crampy, intermittent abdominal pain. He reported a 3-year history of recurrent abdominal discomfort, episodic abdominal distension, and intermittent vomiting of ingested meals with occasional bilious content.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Raised due to ultrasound findings of asymmetric focal bowel wall thickening, luminal stenosis, proximal dilation, and regional mesenteric lymphadenopathy; ruled out by cross-sectional CT demonstrating multifocal concentric skip-like strictures and surgical pathology confirming granulomatous inflammation rather than adenocarcinoma.

Strongly considered given the 3-year indolent history, crampy postprandial pain, weight loss, multifocal small bowel strictures, and shouldering; excluded by the presence of centrally necrotic lymphadenopathy and histological confirmation of caseating necrosis, with failure of initial response to corticosteroids.

diagnostic_pivot: CT identification of multifocal small bowel constrictions alongside centrally hypoattenuating (necrotic) mesenteric lymph nodes, followed by surgical resection revealing concentric strictures and histopathology confirming epithelioid cell aggregates, Langhans giant cells, and central caseous necrosis, established intestinal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old woman from a rural area of Santander, Colombia, presented to the emergency unit with a 5-day history of high fever, chills, severe epigastric pain, intractable nausea, vomiting, non-bloody diarrhea, and a recent episode of hematemesis.

differentials.candidate: Septic shock secondary to bacterial gastrointestinal or intra-abdominal infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, diarrhea, acute abdomen, and refractory distributive shock requiring vasopressors; excluded by sterile blood, stool, and urine cultures, and the absence of localized bacterial collections on cross-sectional imaging.

differentials.candidate: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP / HUS) or Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Raised due to the paradoxical combination of severe consumptive thrombocytopenia and acute macrovascular portal vein thrombosis; excluded by the absence of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, absence of schistocytes on blood smear, normal ADAMTS13 activity, and negative antiphospholipid/thrombophilia panels.

differentials.candidate: Severe Leptospirosis, Malaria, or acute Viral Hepatitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Important considerations for acute tropical hemorrhagic fever presenting with profound transaminitis and multi-organ failure in Colombia; ruled out by negative blood smear examinations for parasites and negative serologic assays for Leptospira, hepatitis viruses (A, B, C), CMV, and HIV.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of positive anti-DENV-1 IgM by ELISA in the setting of hemorrhagic diathesis (petechiae, hematemesis), extreme plasma leakage (ascites, pleural effusions), profound thrombocytopenia (7,000/mm³), and ischemic hepatitis, accompanied by acute portal vein thrombosis, confirmed the diagnosis of severe dengue with thrombotic and coagulopathic complications.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old Malay woman presented to the otolaryngology clinic with a 1-month history of painless bilateral neck swelling that had progressively enlarged. Over this period, she experienced intermittent low-grade fevers without chills, night sweats, anorexia, or unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) with regional cervical lymph node metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: High suspicion in a 38-year-old woman in Southeast Asia presenting with an irregular nasopharyngeal lesion and bilateral necrotic cervical adenopathy; ruled out by nasoendoscopy showing normal fossae of Rosenmüller and subsequent histopathology confirming necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant epithelial cells.

Considered due to bilateral cervical nodal enlargement with central necrosis; excluded by lack of acute tenderness, erythema, or fluctuance, failure of response to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate, and absence of acute suppurative changes.

Considered because of painless, rubbery cervical lymphadenopathy and an upper aerodigestive tract mass in a young adult; excluded by biopsy demonstrating absence of monoclonal atypical lymphocytes and presence of classic caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis.

diagnostic_pivot: CECT demonstrating rim-enhancing hypodense (necrotic) cervical lymphadenopathy with a focal nasopharyngeal wall lesion, followed by excisional biopsy demonstrating necrotizing epithelioid cell granulomas with central necrosis and Langhans multinucleated giant cells, established primary nasopharyngeal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 14-month-old boy was brought for emergency evaluation due to persistent cough, wheezing, and hoarseness (trachyphonia) over several weeks, acutely complicated by progressive shortness of breath and high fever. The child had previously received sequential outpatient courses of oral and intravenous beta-lactams and macrolides, followed by systemic corticosteroids for presumptive acute laryngitis, with only fleeting symptom attenuation followed by rapid...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially treated with empirical amoxicillin-sulbactam, azithromycin, and subsequently intravenous ceftriaxone, but the child continued to deteriorate clinically with progressive necrotic lymphadenopathy.

Considered due to prominent trachyphonia, wheezing, and cough, and initially managed with systemic corticosteroids; however, fever recurred, respiratory distress worsened, and imaging demonstrated necrotizing mediastinal lymphadenopathy and dense consolidation incompatible with uncomplicated viral croup.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Talaromycosis (Talaromyces marneffei with Pneumocystis jirovecii Coinfection)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point occurred during repeat bronchoscopy revealing copious tracheal mucus, where BALF smear, fungal culture, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing identified Talaromyces marneffei alongside Pneumocystis jirovecii, which prompted targeted therapy with itraconazole and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and genetic uncovering of a de novo pathogenic STAT1 mutation.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old woman presented for evaluation of a 1-month history of a painful isolated mass on the medial aspect of the left calf, accompanied by bilateral numbness in her toes.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected due to an intensely hypermetabolic, deeply infiltrative intramuscular mass (SUVmax 15.9) in an older adult; however, biopsy revealed epithelioid granulomas with caseous necrosis without cytokeratin immunoreactivity and a very low Ki-67 proliferative index (10%).

Considered because of positive rheumatoid factor, elevated high-sensitivity CRP, positive ASO, and peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; but ESR, antinuclear antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were normal, and muscle histopathology did not show inflammatory vasculitis.

The definitive diagnosis was established by left gastrocnemius muscle biopsy demonstrating nodular epithelioid granulomas with central caseous necrosis, corroborated by positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex PCR specifically on frozen muscle sections, despite negative sputum, blood, urine, PPD, and IGRA testing.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male presented to the ophthalmology clinic complaining of progressive blurring of vision in his left eye and persistent headache for the past 15 days. He reported having experienced an acute, self-limited systemic febrile illness approximately three weeks (22 days) prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the segmental distribution of flame-shaped and dot-blot hemorrhages with macular edema along a branch vein; however, the patient was a young male without hypertension or hypercoagulability, and fundus examination showed concurrent arterial focal constriction, macular neurosensory detachment, and systemic thrombocytopenia following a febrile episode.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Acute Macular Neuroretinopathy (AMN) / Non-infectious Retinal Vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although OCT findings demonstrated neurosensory detachment and microvascular changes characteristic of AMN, non-infectious inflammatory vasculitis was ruled out as the primary etiology by the explicit temporal linkage to a recent systemic febrile illness accompanied by persistent systemic thrombocytopenia.

The diagnosis of dengue-associated maculopathy and retinopathy was established by the characteristic clinical constellation of branch vein vasculitis, neurosensory detachment, and thrombocytopenia occurring in the convalescent phase of a febrile illness, confirmed by positive Dengue virus IgM enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay serology.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old boy originating from a peri-urban area of South Sudan was brought to the hospital with a 1-month history of sudden-onset, progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness resulting in the complete inability to stand or walk without assistance.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered as the primary diagnosis given the focal expansile intramedullary conus lesion with perilesional edema causing rapid myelopathy in a young child; excluded upon histopathological analysis of the resected tissue, which demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cellular features.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Tuberculosis / Neurosarcoidosis / Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to granulomatous appearance and acute-onset myelitis; ruled out by normal serum ACE level, negative NMO and MOG autoantibodies, negative tissue acid-fast bacilli smear, negative tissue GeneXpert PCR, and sterile 48-hour tissue cultures.

Because non-invasive tests and stool/urine egg examinations were negative, the patient underwent laminoplasty and intramedullary conus biopsy, which definitively revealed chronic necrotizing granulomatous inflammation enclosing Schistosoma eggs, resulting in near-complete functional recovery after praziquantel and high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male residing in the metropolitan region of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, was referred to a specialty outpatient clinic on account of diffuse, progressive skin lesions across his body that had developed over the preceding 10 months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the chronic nodular cutaneous lesions in an endemic region of Brazil; however, the absence of classical ulcerations or mucosal involvement and the presence of a high bacillary load on slit-skin smear pointed away from Leishmania.

Considered for generalized papulonodular skin eruptions without primary neurological symptoms in a young adult, but ruled out by bacteriological identification of mycobacterial loads on slit-skin smear.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Multibacillary Leprosy (Borderline Lepromatous Form with Type 1 Neuritic Reaction)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of multibacillary borderline lepromatous disease was confirmed by positive slit-skin smear bacilloscopy demonstrating a high bacteriological index (5.25) and a positive Mitsuda test (5 mm), which was complicated 4 months into therapy by an acute type 1 reaction manifesting as severe ulnar neuritis.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female residing in the metropolitan region of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, presented to an outpatient specialty clinic with a 1-year history of persistent skin lesions and progressive neuropathic pain in both hands.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's long-standing insulin-dependent diabetes; however, the presence of discrete, well-defined hypochromic cutaneous plaques with localized intracutaneous sensory loss, alongside palpable supraepicondylar ulnar nerve thickening, is pathognomonic of an infectious/granulomatous etiology rather than metabolic polyneuropathy.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Cubital Tunnel Syndrome / Compressive Ulnar Neuropathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to neuropathic pain and weakness in the hypothenar muscles; ruled out by bilateral involvement, co-occurring anesthetic cutaneous macules, and absence of mechanical entrapment on ultrasound.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Borderline Tuberculoid Leprosy with Type 1 Reversal Reaction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although slit-skin bacilloscopy was negative (characteristic of paucibacillary infection), the diagnosis was confirmed by skin biopsy showing epithelioid granulomas in the dermis consistent with borderline tuberculoid leprosy undergoing a type 1 reversal reaction, and electrophysiology confirming bilateral ulnar myelin and secondary axonal neuropathy.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old Chinese female was transferred to a tertiary hospital presenting with an 8-month history of persistent, irregular high fevers (temperatures up to 39.4 C) and cough, accompanied by progressive thoracic chest and back pain of 3 months' duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered given chronic fever, lung consolidation, and destructive thoracic vertebral osteolysis; however, the patient failed a 6-month empirical trial of four-drug anti-tuberculosis therapy, and multiple PPD tests, interferon-gamma release assays, AFB smears, cultures, and tissue TB-qPCR assays were negative.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial Spondylodiscitis / Severe Community-Acquired Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked leukocytosis with 95.4% neutrophils, procalcitonin of 17.7 ng/mL, and vertebral destruction led to empiric intravenous piperacillin-sulbactam, levofloxacin, and meropenem; however, fevers persisted, blood cultures remained sterile, and she deteriorated into septic shock requiring vasopressors.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Talaromycosis with Anti-Interferon-Gamma Autoantibodies
differentials.rule_out_reason: Percutaneous lung biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with suspicious intracellular fungal elements on silver/PAS staining, followed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing detecting Talaromyces marneffei (confirmed by rDNA ITS PCR/sequencing) and detection of high-titer neutralizing anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies (1:2500), with rapid defervescence on amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male presented to a tertiary teaching hospital in the Southern Province of Rwanda complaining of a 3-year history of persistent hypogastric abdominal pain, excessive flatulence, and intermittent constipation.

differentials.candidate: Common Luminal Parasitic Infection (Giardiasis / Intestinal Helminthiasis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to gastrointestinal symptoms in an endemic region; however, symptoms failed to respond to mebendazole and tinidazole, and multiple microscopic stool examinations showed no evidence of protozoa, worms, or ova.

Suggested by the 3-year duration of intermittent constipation, bloating, and normal routine blood tests and endoscopy; ruled out by abdominal CT revealing enlarged pericecal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy and endoscopic detection of mucosal nodules.

Established by colonoscopy demonstrating multiple nodular mucosal lesions in the ascending colon and cecum, with biopsy revealing intramucosal Schistosoma mansoni eggs surrounded by chronic inflammatory cells and eosinophils, and ultrasound demonstrating characteristic periportal fibrosis, followed by complete symptom resolution within 24 hours of praziquantel administration.

clinical_summary: A male patient in his 50s presented to a tertiary hospital with a history of persistent cough, bloody sputum expectoration (hemoptysis), low-grade fever, and faintly visible cutaneous rashes localized to the thoracoabdominal junction, following an incidental pulmonary shadow identified on routine physical examination over six months earlier.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Highly suspected because of the patient's age in the 50s, 30-year smoking history, hemoptysis, and an obstructing right upper lobe mass with pleural effusion; however, repeated cytologic examinations of bronchoscopic fluid, pleural fluid, pulmonary mass tissue, and bone marrow biopsy showed no malignant cells.
Considered due to chronic hemoptysis, upper lobe mass lesion, and constitutional low-grade fever; ruled out by negative acid-fast staining despite an active suppurative inflammatory background.

The diagnosis was established when BALF fungal smear and culture demonstrated thermally dimorphic yeast colonies producing soluble red pigment at 28 C and typical penicillium-like conidiophores, confirmed by ITS rDNA PCR amplification and phylogenetic sequencing demonstrating 99.62% homology with Talaromyces marneffei.

clinical_summary: A patient was admitted to the hospital with a subacute respiratory infection of undetermined etiology, presenting with persistent cough, sputum expectoration, and recurrent fevers. Chest computed tomography (CT) performed during early admission demonstrated prominent pulmonary lesions characterized by patchy infiltration across bilateral lung fields.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated Invasive Mycosis (Invasive Aspergillosis / Candidiasis / Fungemia)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to persistent pulmonary infiltrates and lack of improvement on routine therapy; however, serum levels of 1,3-beta-D-glucan and galactomannan remained consistently within normal limits, and blood cultures showed no pathogen growth, ruling out typical disseminated mold infections and fungemia.

Treated empirically with broad-spectrum antibacterials in the early stage of hospitalization, but the patient continued to have recurrent fevers until targeted antifungal therapy was instituted following definitive microbial identification.

The diagnosis of Talaromyces marneffei was established by definitive etiological testing, prompting targeted voriconazole therapy which led to prominent radiological clearance of bilateral lung infiltrates and complete symptom recovery at 3 months.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male presented to the outpatient medical center complaining of an extensive, painless erythematous plaque involving his anterior neck and chest region that had been present for 9 years and had ulcerated 2 years prior to presentation.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Skin Infection / Chronic Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient was initially diagnosed with and treated for a routine bacterial cutaneous infection with systematic antibiotics and topical iodine, but failed to show any improvement and lesions steadily progressed over several years.

Active pulmonary involvement was considered given his history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis 12 years prior and bilateral fibrous foci on CT, but was excluded by the lack of pulmonary symptoms, stable fibrous lung changes, and negative sputum examinations.
Ulcerative chronic nodules and fistulae can indicate endemic or opportunistic fungal infections, but periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) fungal stains of the biopsied tissue were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by excisional biopsy of a cervical lymph node revealing classic caseating granulomatous inflammation, corroborated by highly elevated T-SPOT interferon-gamma release assay (1904.18 pg/mL) and a positive tuberculin skin test (15 mm induration), confirming scrofuloderma with subsequent complete resolution following four-drug anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old boy was brought to the pediatric emergency department of a tertiary teaching hospital in Senegal due to worsening epistaxis and bleeding gums that had been occurring sporadically over the preceding 3 months without formal medical follow-up.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The dramatic triad of massive hepatosplenomegaly, generalized macropolyadenopathy, and life-threatening cytopenias (hemoglobin 5.1 g/dL, platelets 3,000/mm³) raised high suspicion for leukemia, but the peripheral smear demonstrated only 7% blasts and 3% erythroblasts, which was inconsistent with an acute blast crisis.

differentials.candidate: Malaria, Retroviral Infection, Viral Hepatitis, or Sepsis with Underlying Cytopenia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the persistent high fever and systemic inflammatory picture, common infectious etiologies and underlying hematologic disorders (sickle cell disease, folate/cobalamin deficiency) were evaluated and systematically excluded.

diagnostic_pivot: Although an initial superficial lymph node biopsy was negative on microscopy, bone marrow aspiration followed by Giemsa staining definitively demonstrated intracellular amastigotes, and nested PCR of the bone marrow aspirate confirmed Leishmania infantum.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with 2 days of intermittent fevers (peak temperature 38.5°C), progressive respiratory distress, and dyspnea developing shortly after undergoing surgical incision and drainage of a perianal abscess at an outside hospital.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Sepsis and Bacterial Pneumonia with Septic Emboli
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden acute presentation following perianal abscess surgery with marked neutrophilic leukocytosis and critical hypoxia suggested severe bacterial sepsis; however, standard sputum smears and bacterial/fungal cultures of both sputum and blood were negative.

The development of a perianal abscess and fistula, subsequently accompanied by ileal and rectal ulcerations, raised strong suspicion for Crohn's disease, but histopathologic confirmation was precluded by active bleeding and the lesions resolved under modified anti-mycobacterial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive turning point occurred when cerebrospinal fluid next-generation sequencing detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis following a generalized seizure, and subsequent percutaneous needle aspiration of the fluctuant subcutaneous lumbar mass yielded purulent fluid that was positive on acid-fast bacilli smear, confirming disseminated tuberculosis involving the meninges, lungs, pleura, intestine, and soft tissues.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male presented to the orthopedics outpatient clinic complaining of persistent pain and a draining sinus tract over his left ankle that had been present for 1 year and was progressively worsening.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Pyogenic Osteomyelitis / Bacterial Septic Arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although chronic discharging sinus tracts often arise from pyogenic bone infections, the absence of trauma, protracted 1-year course, and drainage of caseous rather than purulent exudate were atypical for conventional bacterial pathogens.

Non-infectious inflammatory monoarthritides or synovial neoplasms can cause persistent joint swelling and pain, but they do not account for fistulization with cheesy caseous discharge or systemic evening fevers and weight loss.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point occurred when the patient underwent surgical debridement and curettage of the joint, where histopathologic analysis and culture and sensitivity testing of the caseous material confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male rural farmer with a 2-year history of hypertension and gout was admitted to the nephrology department for severe renal dysfunction characterized by a serum creatinine of 1221.75 µmol/L.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Because the high fever and rigors developed directly during hemodialysis, catheter sepsis was suspected, but empiric therapy with high-dose intravenous cefoperazone/sulbactam and vancomycin produced no clinical or antipyretic response.

Although the patient was a rural farmer at risk for vector exposures, typical signs of scrub typhus such as a characteristic cigarette-burn eschar or regional lymphadenopathy were completely absent on multiple physical examinations.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough was achieved via peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), which identified Orientia tsutsugamushi; switching antibiotics to oral doxycycline and moxifloxacin led to prompt defervescence within 5 days and uneventful recovery.

clinical_summary: A 76-year-old female with a medical history of essential hypertension presented to the hospital with a 1-week history of recurrent low-grade fever, malaise, and generalized aching in her limbs. Eleven days prior to presentation, she had sustained an untreated bite from an unknown insect while applying agricultural pesticides in an outdoor farmyard.

differentials.candidate: Severe Pyogenic Bacterial Pneumonia / Sepsis with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Because of bilateral pulmonary exudates, marked coagulopathy, and high inflammatory markers, empiric broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage with piperacillin/tazobactam and cefoperazone/sulbactam plus moxifloxacin was administered; however, the patient remained persistently febrile and inflammatory indices continued to rise.

Although the primary illness was rickettsial vasculitis, a secondary superinfection with Aspergillus fumigatus developed in the damaged airways and was identified via bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoscopy revealed severe mucosal erythema, erosion, and purulent secretions; metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchial rinse fluid definitively identified Orientia tsutsugamushi, confirming scrub typhus with acute pulmonary vasculitis and leading to targeted therapy with doxycycline.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female born in Guatemala presented to the emergency department complaining of severe diffuse headache, right-sided neck pain, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia that had started 3 days prior to arrival.
