differentials.rule_out_reason: Because of the rapid 3-day onset and mixed neutrophilic/lymphocytic pleocytosis, broad empirical antimicrobial therapy (vancomycin, ceftriaxone, ampicillin, acyclovir) was started, but was discontinued when multiplex CSF PCR for common bacterial and viral pathogens returned negative.

differentials.candidate: Fungal Meningoencephalitis (e.g., Cryptococcal or Dimorphic Mycoses)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Disseminated fungal infections can present with miliary parenchymal brain granulomas and basilar/dural enhancement, but cerebrospinal fluid fungal cultures remained negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite an initial negative serum IGRA and negative initial AFB smears, CSF cytopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation, and the initial CSF culture on hospital day 19 grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, confirming miliary tuberculous meningoencephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old male with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, and stable right hemiparesis secondary to a prior ischemic stroke presented to the hospital with swelling of his right ankle that had been progressively worsening over the preceding month.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Septic Arthritis / Gas-Forming Tenosynovitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The presence of soft-tissue gas on CT, fluctuant warm swelling, marked CRP elevation, and polynuclear leukocyte-rich exudate strongly suggested acute pyogenic or anaerobic bacterial infection; however, exhaustive aerobic and anaerobic cultures on blood agar, chocolate agar, and BHI broth remained sterile after 15 days.

differentials.candidate: Complicated Non-Infectious Diabetic / Neuropathic Arthropathy (Charcot Foot)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although peripheral neuropathy and diabetes predispose to destructive Charcot joint disease, the presence of an extensive purulent fluid collection with deep soft tissue and tendinous infiltration confirmed an active suppurative infectious process.

diagnostic_pivot: Because of non-improvement and persistent negative pyogenic cultures, repeated joint aspirate was examined for mycobacteria, demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, followed by positive cultures on Lowenstein-Jensen and MGIT media and real-time PCR (GeneXpert MTB/RIF) confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex without rifampicin resistance.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male who had resided in a rural area of São Paulo State for over 30 years presented to the medical center with a 3-month history of progressive dyspepsia and dysphagia, accompanied by an unintentional 17-kg weight loss and the emergence of multiple skin lesions over his face and head.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Cavitary upper lobe pulmonary consolidations, necrotic intra-abdominal adenopathy, bilateral adrenal enlargement, and multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions strongly raised suspicion for disseminated tuberculosis; however, sputum acid-fast bacilli smear, mycobacterial culture, and targeted PCR were all negative.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated / Metastatic Esophageal or Pulmonary Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: A friable, irregular esophageal ulcer in a chronic smoker with severe weight loss, massive necrotic lymphadenopathy, adrenal nodules, and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions raised high suspicion for advanced malignancy with systemic metastasis; however, histopathology of both the esophageal ulcer and subsequent lymph node biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with yeast structures rather than malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when submandibular lymph node biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with characteristic yeast forms on Grocott staining, concordant with esophageal biopsy findings and confirmed by specific serology titer of 1:128, establishing chronic multifocal disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old male presented to the medical emergency department with a 3-day history of fever, nausea, vomiting, headache, photophobia, anorexia, generalized abdominal pain, and bloody diarrhea. The patient, who works as a gardener, lives with his family in an informal settlement noted to be infested with rodents.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe abdominal tenderness, guarding, bloody diarrhea, and periappendiceal fluid on abdominal CT in a patient with septic shock initially suggested acute appendiceal perforation or peritonitis; however, urgent surgical consultation found the examination inconsistent with acute surgical appendicitis, with fluid representing reactive serosal ascites.

Given the acute febrile onset, travel background, profound jaundice, severe thrombocytopenia (38 × 10⁹/L), and acute renal failure, severe falciparum malaria was a prime diagnostic consideration; however, malaria rapid diagnostic antigen testing and multiple thin and thick peripheral blood smears were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The classic clinical triad of acute renal failure, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with disproportionately mild transaminitis, and prominent conjunctival suffusion in a gardener with documented rodent exposure strongly pointed to leptospirosis, which was definitively confirmed by positive Leptospira IgM serology alongside dramatic recovery on intravenous ceftriaxone.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old male presented to the emergency department via ambulance with acute chest tightness and dyspnea. He has a history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection managed with long-term oral antiretroviral therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pre-admission MRI and PET-CT showed large cystic-solid hepatic masses with tumor-like characteristics, prompting surgical resection; however, histopathologic examination of the resected tissue demonstrated no malignant cells.

In an HIV-infected patient with severe right pleural effusion, emaciation, and low-grade fevers, tuberculous pleurisy was strongly suspected; however, molecular PCR testing of the pleural fluid for Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA was negative.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or Fungal Liver and Pleural Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Elevated inflammatory markers, neutrophil leukocytosis, and large cystic liver/pleural fluid collections were consistent with bacterial or opportunistic fungal abscesses; however, routine aerobic/anaerobic bacterial and fungal cultures were negative.

Profound anemia, emaciation, massive lower gastrointestinal bleeding history, and hepatomegaly raised concern for an underlying hematologic or lymphoproliferative disorder, but bone marrow evaluation was normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous drainage of the hepatic mass yielded pathognomonic jam-like/anchovy-paste fluid, and mNGS of the aspirate identified Entamoeba trophozoites; retrospective review of the previously resected hepatic surgical specimen confirmed the presence of amoeba trophozoites, leading to complete clinical recovery upon metronidazole therapy.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old boy from a low socioeconomic background with no significant past medical or surgical history presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of intermittent to severe cramping abdominal pain rated 7 out of 10.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the clinical presentation and Alvarado score of 9 strongly suggested classic appendicitis, ultrasound did not show typical appendiceal dilatation, aperistalsis, or periappendiceal fluid, and exploration revealed co-occurrence with an intraluminal nematode infestation.
Considered due to right lower quadrant pain, low-grade fever, and leukocytosis, but surgical exploration revealed no bowel wall inflammation, perforation, or intrinsic ileal obstruction.

A common mimicker of acute appendicitis in pediatric patients presenting with fever, nausea, and right lower quadrant periumbilical pain; ruled out by operative confirmation of retrocecal appendicitis and parasite identification.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal ultrasonography identified an intraluminal tubular structure extending to the appendiceal base, and intraoperative exploration confirmed acute retrocecal appendicitis alongside a palpable worm 30 cm from the ileocecal valve; single-dose albendazole led to expulsion of the nematode in stool and histopathological confirmation of concurrent appendicitis and Ascaris lumbricoides infestation.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old woman with no significant past medical history was brought to the emergency department of a district hospital in Ghana following an acute episode of seizure activity. Her family witnessed repetitive nodding movements of the head accompanied by involuntary rhythmic jerking of the left upper limb lasting 1 to 2 minutes.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a new-onset focal motor seizure, but elderly onset without preceding aura or family history made idiopathic epilepsy unlikely, indicating an acquired structural intracranial lesion.

In an infectious-endemic setting, new-onset seizures and headaches could signify acute central nervous system infection; however, the patient was completely afebrile, alert, without neck stiffness or meningeal signs, and had normal hematologic indices.

Electrolyte abnormalities (hyponatremia, hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia) and acute glycemic swings are frequent triggers of new seizures in elderly patients; all metabolic and electrolyte panels were completely normal.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast-enhanced brain CT demonstrated pathognomonic subcortical cystic lesions with eccentric internal hyperdense foci (scolex) in the bilateral frontal lobes and left insular cortex without perilesional edema, confirming vesicular-stage parenchymal neurocysticercosis, which responded successfully to combined albendazole, praziquantel, dexamethasone, and anticonvulsant therapy.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man with no history of chronic medical illness presented to the emergency department following an acute seizure episode. While asleep, family members observed sudden generalized body stiffening followed rapidly by rhythmic clonic jerking of all four limbs lasting approximately 45 seconds, during which he was unresponsive.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to recurrent unprovoked generalized seizures occurring over a 12-month interval in a previously healthy adult, but adult-onset presentation without childhood history or family history of epilepsy suggested a secondary structural brain pathology.

differentials.candidate: Acute Meningoencephalitis / Central Nervous System Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute recurrent convulsions in an endemic environment could indicate infectious encephalitis or meningitis; however, the patient was completely afebrile, alert postictally, had a supple neck with negative Kernig's sign, and displayed normal white blood cell counts.

differentials.candidate: Toxic or Metabolic Seizure / Alcohol-Related Convulsion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Electrolyte disturbances, hypoglycemia, and alcohol withdrawal can precipitate acute generalized seizures in adults; excluded by normal random blood glucose, normal serum electrolytes and calcium/magnesium, and denial of chronic heavy drinking or substance abuse.

diagnostic_pivot: Contrast-enhanced head CT demonstrated pathognomonic rim-enhancing cystic lesions with eccentric internal hyperdense foci (scolex) in both frontal lobes without perilesional edema, accompanied by a calcified cortical nodule in the left parietal region, establishing vesicular and calcified parenchymal neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old woman originally from Nepal with no significant past medical history presented to the emergency department with a 2-week history of worsening fatigue, altered sensorium, dizziness, recurrent vomiting, fever, generalized holocranial headache, and photophobia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute-to-subacute febrile presentation with severe meningism, cranial neuropathy, and turbid CSF; however, CSF cytochemistry showed marked lymphocytic predominance (81%) rather than neutrophilia, and the patient failed to improve on empiric meningeal doses of vancomycin and ceftriaxone.

Lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis, altered consciousness, and normal initial head CT strongly suggested viral meningoencephalitis; however, marked hypoglycorrhachia, severe intracranial hypertension (opening pressure 36 cm H2O), progression despite acyclovir, and basilar leptomeningeal enhancement on MRI were incompatible.
Subacute basal meningitis presenting with cranial nerve palsy, intracranial hypertension, and lymphocytic pleocytosis can be caused by neurosyphilis; excluded by negative VDRL serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite initial negative CSF NAAT and normal chest CT, worsening intracranial hypertension (opening pressure 36 cm H2O), persistent lymphocytic hypoglycorrhachia, and cranial MRI demonstrating leptomeningeal enhancement with ventricular enlargement prompted empiric anti-tuberculosis therapy (HRZE) and dexamethasone, leading to dramatic clinical recovery, followed by definitive isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex from CSF culture on day 25.

clinical_summary: A 15-year-old student living in a rural agricultural setting with regular contact with domestic dogs presented to the emergency department with acute chest pain and worsening dyspnea. Her symptoms had evolved over the preceding month, characterized by cough productive of yellowish sputum, an episode of sudden expectoration of clear fluid contents, subjective fevers, night sweats, and marked deterioration in general...

differentials.candidate: Cavitary Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Secondary Pneumothorax
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute presentation with fever, night sweats, general decline, cavitary lesion with an air-fluid level, and prominent mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy strongly pointed to cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis; excluded by targeted serology and intraoperative extraction of an intact parasitic cyst.

Purulent sputum production, high inflammatory markers (CRP 165 mg/L), and an excavated cavity with hydropneumothorax suggested a ruptured bacterial lung abscess with empyema; however, thoracotomy revealed a well-organized parasitic cyst without suppurative bacterial liquefaction.

diagnostic_pivot: Epidemiological canine exposure, expectoration of cystic contents, hydropneumothorax communicating with a fluid cavity, positive hydatid serology (index 6.6), and emergency posterolateral thoracotomy demonstrating a primary pleural hydatid cyst with associated fibrin deposits confirmed ruptured thoracic echinococcosis, treated successfully by complete cyst resection and decortication.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old male residing in Bidar, Karnataka, India, presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of nonproductive cough and progressive grade III-IV dyspnea, preceded by fever and sore throat for 5 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a diabetic patient from India presenting with fever, cough, and diffuse bilateral nodular cavitary pulmonary lesions, tuberculosis was the prime infectious differential; ruled out by negative bronchoalveolar lavage acid-fast bacilli staining and negative GeneXpert MTB testing.

Multiple diffuse bilateral pulmonary nodules with central cavitation strongly mimicked hematogenous pulmonary metastases or cavitating neoplasia; ruled out by non-malignant findings on PET-CT evaluation.

Acute respiratory decompensation and hypoxemia prompted empiric initiation of doxycycline and metronidazole; however, empiric therapy was inadequate for severe nodular necrotizing sepsis, requiring identification of an intrinsically resistant environmental pathogen.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood cultures drawn on admission yielded Burkholderia pseudomallei within three days, confirming acute bacteremic thoracic melioidosis in a diabetic host; prompt transition to high-dose intravenous ceftazidime and meropenem followed by eradication therapy with co-trimoxazole and doxycycline led to full recovery.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of fever, general malaise, and hemoptysis. His medical history was notable for coronary artery disease and valvular heart disease, for which he had undergone coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve replacement seven years prior; he had recovered well post-operatively and was maintained on oral enteric-coated aspirin and...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Fulminant onset of fever, respiratory failure, high procalcitonin, and bilateral consolidations suggested severe bacterial pneumonia; however, the patient deteriorated despite broad-spectrum empiric coverage, and comprehensive conventional microbiologic stains, cultures, and serologies were completely negative.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pulmonary Thromboembolism / Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema
differentials.rule_out_reason: History of cardiac surgery, atrial fibrillation, elevated pro-BNP, reduced ejection fraction, and CT pulmonary angiography showing multiple pulmonary artery branch embolisms suggested acute thromboembolism and hydrostatic edema; however, lower extremity Doppler showed no deep vein thrombosis, and bronchoscopy subsequently revealed active diffuse bronchial mucosal hemorrhage rather than simple transudate.

diagnostic_pivot: Progression of bilateral pulmonary lesions prompted bedside bronchoscopy, revealing diffuse mucosal hemorrhage; metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid identified Leptospira interrogans and Aspergillus flavus, confirmed by BAL fungal culture. Cessation of empiric carbapenem/glycopeptide therapy and administration of targeted intravenous penicillin G combined with voriconazole led to prompt clinical and radiological resolution.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old female patient with a history of Down syndrome, residing in the province of Quillabamba within the department of Cusco, Peru—an Amazon jungle region—was referred and admitted to a tertiary pediatric institute due to progressive enlargement and widespread dissemination of cutaneous ulcerations.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a resident of the Amazon river basin with chronic ulcerative mucocutaneous granulomas and mucosal erosion, deep fungal infections were major considerations; ruled out by negative periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) fungal staining and absence of fungal structures on direct microscopy.

Extensive destructive cutaneous ulcers refractory to medical therapies in a young child with Down syndrome raised suspicion for Langerhans cell histiocytosis or a lymphoproliferative disorder; ruled out by negative CD1a immunohistochemical staining.

differentials.candidate: Primary Immunodeficiency with Unresponsive Cutaneous Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Refractory mucosal involvement and disseminated spread occurred in the context of Down syndrome-associated cellular immunodeficiency, verified by profound CD4 T-helper and B-cell lymphopenia on flow cytometry.

diagnostic_pivot: Skin punch biopsy revealed dense lymphohistiocytic dermal infiltration with abundant intracellular amastigotes, confirmed by direct microscopic smear examination, a positive Montenegro intradermal test (7 x 8 mm induration), an indirect immunofluorescence IgG titer of 1/160, and PCR-RFLP identifying Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis. Due to resistance to conventional deoxycholate formulations and antimonials, high-dose intravenous liposomal amphotericin B was initiated, leading to complete ulcer healing.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old, developmentally at par, right-handed Filipino male presented to our institution for evaluation of involuntary limb movements. Three weeks prior to presentation, he developed generalized headaches and intermittent, undocumented fevers, which subsequently became associated with involuntary dance-like flowing movements involving all four extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute-to-subacute chorea following febrile illness in a school-aged child prompted an initial diagnosis of rheumatic chorea and empiric parenteral penicillin; however, other major Jones criteria (carditis, polyarthritis, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules) were absent and the anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titer was normal (<200 IU/mL).

Considered at the outside hospital after penicillin failed to resolve the chorea, leading to administration of valproic acid; ruled out by normal mental status, absence of psychiatric disturbances or seizures, negative anti-NMDA receptor antibodies, and profound CSF hypoglycorrhachia incompatible with uncomplicated autoimmune encephalitis.

diagnostic_pivot: In a child residing in an endemic region with close household contact and subacute fever, lumbar puncture demonstrated profound hypoglycorrhachia (undetectable CSF glucose with blood glucose 82 mg/dL), marked hyperproteinorrachia (351 mg/dL), and lymphocytic pleocytosis (144 WBCs/mcL, 99% lymphocytes); despite negative acid-fast bacilli smear and PCR, tuberculous meningitis (BMRC Stage III) was clinically confirmed and supported on day 3 by contrast CT showing basal exudates, communicating hydrocephalus, and ischemic arteritic infarcts of the right caudate and internal capsule. Combination therapy with fixed-dose anti-TB medications and high-dose dexamethasone achieved prompt cessation of chorea.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a 3-month history of recurrent colicky lower abdominal pain that has acutely worsened over recent days. The pain initially was mild and intermittent, causing him to occasionally miss school, and was partially alleviated with nonnarcotic analgesics.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered due to prior medical history and CT findings of terminal ileal thickening with mesenteric lymphadenopathy, but excluded by sterile ascites with normal adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels and mucosal histopathology showing no granulomas or evidence of tuberculosis.

differentials.candidate: Adhesive or Post-inflammatory Small Bowel Obstruction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the history of previous intra-abdominal inflammation, but no surgical adhesions were identified; rather, mechanical luminal occlusion was caused by intraluminal helminth aggregations.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed small bowel encasement and intraluminal worm balls obstructing the proximal jejunum and ileum with ischemic necrosis of the distal ileum, establishing mechanical soil-transmitted helminthic obstruction.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old uncircumcised man presents to the clinic with painful ulcers located on the coronal groove of the penis that have persisted and progressed over the past eight months. The lesion began as small papules that gradually enlarged and broke down into tender, open ulcerations draining a yellowish exudate.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of painful, punched-out coronal groove ulcers in a sexually active adult, but refuted by negative treponemal and retroviral serological testing.
Considered due to the purulent yellowish discharge over the ulcer base, but ulcer swab Gram stain, Ziehl-Neelsen stain, and routine bacterial cultures yielded non-significant results.

differentials.candidate: Active Secondary Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Cutaneous Seeding
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when chest CT revealed patchy and nodular opacities, but bronchoalveolar lavage genomic sequencing was negative and lung lesions did not change after treatment, excluding active pulmonary infection.

diagnostic_pivot: A strongly positive Tuberculin Skin Test (30 x 20 mm induration), positive interferon-gamma release assay, and punch biopsy revealing granulomatous infiltrate with Langhans giant cells and caseous necrosis confirmed penile cutaneous tuberculosis, with complete ulcer healing under quadruple antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male of Indian origin is admitted to the emergency department in Szczecin, Poland, with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, fever, and severe right-sided chest and right subcostal pain that has worsened acutely over the past several days.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Liver Abscess and Empyema
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected due to profound inflammatory and sepsis parameters (procalcitonin 18 ng/mL, CRP 323.57 mg/L, lactate 7.94 mmol/L) and empirical ceftriaxone/metronidazole coverage was started, but all blood and urine cultures remained negative for bacterial pathogens.

Considered given the patient's immigration from an endemic area and subacute pulmonary-pleural presentation with fever and weight loss, but ruled out by negative sputum acid-fast bacilli staining and negative interferon-gamma release assay.

Considered because of remote diarrheal episodes in India, but stool antigen assay was negative, indicating that the patient had isolated invasive extraintestinal disease without concurrent shedding in feces.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency pleural decompression evacuated 3000 mL of brown 'anchovy-sauce' purulent fluid positive for Entamoeba histolytica antigen, accompanied by strongly positive serum amebic IgG antibodies (43.7 NTU), confirming transdiaphragmatic rupture of an amebic liver abscess.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male farmer from Jinghe County, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China, presents to the fever clinic with a 15-day history of persistent high-grade fevers and right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

differentials.candidate: Severe Pneumonia and Pyogenic Bacterial Sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed and treated with broad-spectrum fluoroquinolones without clinical improvement, and subsequently refuted by negative bacterial and fungal blood cultures.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis and Systemic Viral Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, marked transaminitis, cholestasis, and gallbladder wall thickening, but serological screens for viral etiologies were all non-reactive.
Traditional parasitological evaluation via light microscopy failed to detect intracellular organisms on peripheral blood smears or bone marrow aspirates.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified 20 species-specific sequence reads exclusively matching Leishmania donovani in the peripheral blood, subsequently corroborated by a positive rK39 dipstick assay and complete recovery following sodium antimony gluconate.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old man presents to the dermatology clinic in Bandung, Indonesia, with severe pruritus, blister formation, and worsening cutaneous edema overlying recurrent brownish-red lesions on his right lower leg, accompanied by fever and acute watery diarrhea that began five days ago.

differentials.candidate: Primary Idiopathic Wells' Syndrome (Eosinophilic Cellulitis) / Primary Hypereosinophilic Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the recurrent cutaneous plaques, profound peripheral eosinophilia (57%), and dermal eosinophilic infiltration displaying flame figures, but ruled out as an idiopathic primary disorder because the hypereosinophilia and reactive cutaneous eruption were driven by underlying parasitic infestation.

Considered due to acute inflammatory bullae and the presence of Gram-positive cocci on fluid examination, but the bacterial findings represented secondary bacterial impetiginization over an underlying eosinophilic dermatosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Isolation of Strongyloides stercoralis larvae on stool culture together with positive Toxocara IgG serology (index 2.04) confirmed soil-transmitted helminthiasis as the underlying etiology driving hypereosinophilia and reactive Wells' syndrome, which resolved upon treatment with albendazole.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presents to the emergency department with a 7-day history of high fever, productive cough, and rapidly progressive shortness of breath that began two days prior to returning from a two-week business trip to Thailand.

differentials.candidate: Typical Community-Acquired Pneumonia (Streptococcus pneumoniae / Legionella pneumophila)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected and treated empirically with piperacillin-tazobactam and azithromycin, but ruled out by negative urinary antigen assays and isolation of Gram-negative bacilli from blood and sputum.

Standard library MALDI-TOF initially identified Burkholderia thailandensis (score 1.81-1.88), but this represents a recognized misidentification by standard commercial databases for the virulent pathogen Burkholderia pseudomallei.
Considered given acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and bilateral pulmonary consolidations, but excluded by negative multiplex respiratory molecular tests.

diagnostic_pivot: Blood cultures flagging positive within 4 hours for Gram-negative bacilli with characteristic bipolar staining, definitively identified as Burkholderia pseudomallei with a 99.8% match by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, establishing the diagnosis of melioidosis.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 2-week history of cough producing scanty sputum and drenching night sweats. Over the preceding 3 months, he has experienced an unintentional 10-pound weight loss, though his general activity and sleep architecture have otherwise remained stable.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Fungal Infection (Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Endemic Mycosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered because the patient was immunosuppressed on a monoclonal antibody and presented with multifocal cavitary lung disease, but ruled out in favor of mycobacterial infection confirmed by a positive interferon-gamma release assay.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Cavitary Bacterial Pneumonia / Lung Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given cavitary opacities and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 61 mg/L), but the indolent 3-month course of constitutional wasting and night sweats pointed toward a chronic granulomatous process rather than acute pyogenic suppuration.

Considered due to subacute weight loss, night sweats, and cavitary masses with mediastinal lymph node enlargement, but the bilateral multifocal distribution was consistent with an active infectious disease, corroborated by antimycobacterial response.

diagnostic_pivot: A positive interferon-gamma release assay in conjunction with bilateral cavitary infiltrates on chest CT established active pulmonary tuberculosis occurring during anti-IL-17A biologic therapy, prompting quadruple antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old previously healthy man is brought to the emergency department after an acute onset of loss of consciousness. He has no known pre-existing medical conditions, and his past medical history is unremarkable.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected given the acute obtundation, high fever, marked CRP elevation (242.5 mg/L), and suppurative intraventricular fluid on MRI prompting empiric third-generation cephalosporin therapy, but ruled out when pus bacteriological analysis revealed acid-fast bacilli and positive GeneXpert for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

Considered due to an intraventricular rim-enhancing mass causing unilateral ventricular enlargement, but refuted by marked fever, acute elevation of inflammatory markers, diffusion restriction with fluid-fluid layering indicating purulent debris rather than tumor, and aspiration of frank pus.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency placement of an external ventricular drain yielded thick cloudy pus; Ziehl-Neelsen staining was positive for acid-fast bacteria and GeneXpert PCR confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing primary tuberculous pyogenic ventriculitis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old man residing in a rural area in northern Morocco presents to the hospital with progressive right hypochondriac pain associated with nausea and vomiting. He reports an indolent history of mild, intermittent right upper quadrant discomfort dating back twelve years, which has acutely intensified over recent weeks.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Polycystic Disease and Benign Mesenteric Cysts
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the extensive multifocal intrahepatic and extrahepatic peritoneal cystic involvement in a young adult, but disproven by characteristic hydatid cyst morphology (types CE1, CE2, and CE3a / Gharbi IV), strongly positive serology (>1280), and microscopic identification of parasitic hooks.

Considered due to widespread multilocular peritoneal seeding involving the iliac fossae, mesentery, and liver, but refuted by normal baseline laboratory parameters, absence of constitutional cachexia, and confirmation of non-viable parasitic scoleces and cuticles upon surgical exploration.

diagnostic_pivot: High-titer hydatid serology (IHA >1280, Novalisa IgG 30.30 NTU) followed by median laparotomy revealing extensive cyst dissemination and microscopic demonstration of Echinococcus granulosus cuticular hooks and invaginated/devaginated scoleces confirmed disseminated hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of intermittent hemoptysis. She reports expectorating small amounts of blood, with an estimated daily volume of less than 50 mL.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Heavily suspected due to chronic hemoptysis, a spiculated necrotic pulmonary mass on CT, and bronchial aspiration cytology showing anisokaryotic cells suggestive of malignancy, which prompted urgent oncologic lobectomy, but refuted by surgical histopathology revealing an intact parasitic cystic architecture without neoplastic transformation.

Considered given the necrotic cavitary appearance in an apical segment of the lower lobe and hemoptysis, but excluded by absent systemic symptoms, lack of caseating necrosis on CT-guided core biopsy, and absent granulomatous disease on resected histology.

diagnostic_pivot: Right lower lobectomy revealed an intraparenchymal thin-walled cystic mass whose histological evaluation revealed a pathognomonic acellular laminated membrane lined by an internal proligerous germinal membrane, establishing a pulmonary hydatid cyst despite negative preoperative serology and absence of canine exposure.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with a two-day history of fever, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, body aches, and profuse diaphoresis. On physical examination, he was noted to have high-grade fever, but the remainder of the examination was unremarkable with no localized abdominal peritonitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given prominent epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and unremarkable initial physical exam, but excluded by the severity of the temperature spikes (up to 40 °C), profound rigors, diffuse myalgias, and progressive deterioration unresponsive to simple supportive measures.

differentials.candidate: Acute Surgical Abdomen (e.g., Perforated Peptic Ulcer or Acute Pancreatitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the rapid progression from focal epigastric pain to severe diffuse abdominal pain with complete anorexia and persistent vomiting, but initial baseline laboratory workup was within normal limits without localized signs on initial presentation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred when specific diagnostic testing for tropical vector-borne pathogens returned simultaneously positive for both plasmodial infection and arboviral fever, confirming a severe concurrent co-infection responsible for the systemic hyperpyrexia, gastrointestinal crisis, and subsequent visceral risk.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old girl with no significant past medical history was referred from an outpatient clinic with a three-month history of generalized weakness, low-grade fevers, and marked hypoactivity. She had previously undergone multiple outpatient evaluations and courses of treatment for presumed upper respiratory tract infections without resolution.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered previously given fever, hypoactivity, and transient response to empirical intravenous antibiotics, but ruled out because the chronic 3-month timeline and neuroimaging showed a giant unilocular fluid-filled cyst with midline shift rather than diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement or thick ring-enhancing suppurative cerebritis.

differentials.candidate: Pediatric Cystic Intracranial Neoplasm (e.g., Pilocytic Astrocytoma or Cystic Ependymoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the large hemispheric mass with mass effect, morning headaches, and focal motor/cranial nerve deficits in a 5-year-old child, but definitively excluded when histopathologic examination of the en bloc excised lesion revealed parasitic cyst layers containing scolices rather than neoplastic glial architecture.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was achieved via neurosurgical craniotomy and intact microsurgical cyst excision, with definitive histopathological examination confirming a hydatid cyst containing multiple protoscolices.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old girl was admitted to a pediatric infectious disease department on Day 4 of an acute febrile illness with complaints of fever up to 40 °C, severe muscle aches, sore throat, rhinorrhea, dry cough, abdominal pain, loose stools, epistaxis, and a progressive cutaneous eruption on the extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given international tropical travel, high fever, abdominal tenderness, and loose watery stools, but excluded by negative dedicated blood film and stool pathogen screens, alongside the presence of leukothrombocytopenia, conjunctivitis, epistaxis, and a distinct centrifugal-to-centripetal maculopapular rash atypical for primary enteric infections or malaria.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Acute Respiratory Tract Infection / Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prominent cough, sore throat, nasal obstruction, CT evidence of maxillary sinusitis, and elevated CRP that prompted empirical intravenous ceftriaxone, but failed to account for the profound thrombocytopenia, spontaneous epistaxis, and characteristic 'isles of white in a sea of red' rash.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was achieved via whole blood nucleic acid amplification testing, which definitively isolated viral RNA corresponding to antigenic group B arbovirus (dengue virus), confirming acute dengue fever complicated by secondary/concomitant atypical respiratory mycoplasma infection.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old male with limited access to routine healthcare presented to an urgent care clinic with severe, progressive thoracic back pain and bilateral lower extremity weakness leading to impaired mobility.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic Malignancy (Primary Lung or Renal Carcinoma with Skeletal Metastases)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the spiculated pulmonary nodules, prominent 7.4 cm renal hilar mass, atrophic kidney, and destructive osteolytic spinal lesion causing cord compression, but ruled out because the diffuse miliary micronodular pattern, paraspinous fluid collection, and subsequent microbiological isolation proved a disseminated infectious etiology rather than carcinoma.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Spondylodiscitis with Secondary Pyogenic Mycotic Pseudoaneurysm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 4 cm thoracic spinal abscess with extensive lower thoracic vertebral osseous destruction and an adjacent expanding large vascular pseudoaneurysm, but ruled out when cultures showed no growth of common pyogenic bacteria (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus) and specifically confirmed acid-fast organisms.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic confirmation occurred when both sputum and urine microbiological smears and cultures demonstrated acid-fast bacilli (AFB), definitively proving disseminated tuberculosis manifesting simultaneously as miliary lung disease, tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott's disease), genitourinary tuberculosis, and a tuberculous pseudoaneurysm of the right renal artery.

clinical_summary: An 82-year-old woman originally from Ukraine presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of low-grade fever, non-productive cough, generalized weakness, and anorexia. She denied night sweats or notable weight loss and had no significant prior medical illnesses or chronic medications.

differentials.candidate: Community-Acquired Pneumonia with Reactive Paraneoplastic or Viral Pericarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed and treated with broad-spectrum oral antibiotics based on dry cough, basal reticular markings, and elevated CRP, but ruled out when her cardiac status deteriorated over four weeks into overt cardiac tamponade with large pulmonary nodules on CT.

Considered due to the patient's elderly age, anorexia, subacute course, multiple right lung parenchymal nodules up to 22 mm, and a massive exudative effusion with thickened pericardial leaflets, but excluded when pericardial fluid cytology, bronchoscopic evaluation, and tissue biopsy showed epithelioid granulomatous inflammation rather than malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive turning point occurred following pericardiocentesis yielding 1000 mL of exudative fluid (LDH 1599 U/L, protein ratio 9.6), where real-time polymerase chain reaction and mycological culture positively identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis, further corroborated by bronchoalveolar lavage PCR and endobronchial biopsy demonstrating caseating epithelioid granulomas.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old girl presented for outpatient evaluation of persistent right flank pain of seven months' duration. The pain was described as constant, non-radiating, and localized.

differentials.candidate: Complex Benign Renal Cyst / Bosniak Category IIF/III Cystic Mass
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the indolent presentation and presence of internal septations on sonography without constitutional symptoms, but ruled out because the subcapsular/perinephric location outside the parenchyma and specific fine internal echoes raised concern for an infectious etiology, later confirmed serologically and pathologically.

differentials.candidate: Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma / Retroperitoneal Cystic Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the persistent unilateral pain and atypical CT findings that did not show typical characteristics of a hydatid cyst, but ruled out following positive serology and surgical exploration which confirmed a benign parasitic capsule with daughter cysts rather than malignant cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established when specific hydatid IgG antibody serology returned positive at a titer of 1:160, followed by surgical extirpation with hypertonic saline scolicidal irrigation, which confirmed an intact subcapsular cyst containing characteristic daughter cysts on pathologic examination.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old man with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and a known left renal cortical cyst presented to the emergency department with a 15-day history of profound fatigue, anorexia, involuntary weight loss, and abdominal distension.

differentials.candidate: Cystic Renal Neoplasm (e.g., Multilocular Cystic Nephroma or Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suggested by abdominal CT imaging showing a 13 cm well-demarcated cystic lesion with parenchymal compression in an elderly diabetic male with B-symptoms, but ruled out when aspirated fluid analysis showed infectious purulent fluid with positive microbiological cultures rather than malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Acute Pyogenic Renal Abscess / Isolated Escherichia coli Pyonephrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, tachycardia, elevated inflammatory markers, and the eventual isolation of E. coli from the cystic fluid, but ruled out as the primary etiology because the patient had an indolent 15-day course, sterile initial urinalysis and urine cultures, and simultaneous recovery of acid-fast mycobacteria that had established the underlying cavitary renal lesion.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive turning point occurred when the patient underwent ultrasound-guided percutaneous puncture and drainage of the renal cystic lesion, with microbiological analysis of the aspirate successfully isolating Mycobacterium tuberculosis alongside co-infecting Escherichia coli, confirming renal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male manual laborer was brought to the emergency department by relatives in a bedridden, lethargic condition with a two-week history of worsening severe headache, fever, neck stiffness, and generalized weakness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis at emergency triage due to acute lethargy, fever, neck stiffness, and positive Brudzinski's sign, but excluded by the subacute 2-month constitutional prodrome, absence of classic pyogenic bacterial pathogens on CSF testing, and extensive concurrent pulmonary and spinal cord involvement.

differentials.candidate: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD) / Autoimmune Long-Segment Transverse Myelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the extensive longitudinal cervical cord hyperintensity and flaccid quadriparesis with spinal shock, but ruled out by negative serum ANA, NMOSD, and MOG antibodies, alongside systemic miliary pulmonary infiltrates and positive mycobacterial testing.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal confirmation was established when sputum Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) microscopy revealed numerous acid-fast bacilli (Grade-III growth) and a positive cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification test (CBNAAT) confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing disseminated tuberculosis with tubercular meningitis and longitudinal extensive cervical tuberculous myelitis.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old male agricultural worker presented to an emergency hospital facility following a sudden episode of massive hemoptysis, coughing up approximately 200 mL of fresh blood. Three days prior, while working in an agricultural field, he had sustained a minor knife laceration to his left lower leg that had resulted in brief bleeding and was left untreated.

differentials.candidate: Acute Necrotizing Bacterial Pneumonia / Bronchiectasis with Severe Hemoptysis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given sudden life-threatening hemoptysis, right middle lobe patchy consolidation, and prominent hypertrophic bronchial arteries, but ruled out because the diffuse bilateral miliary micronodular pattern and mediastinal lymphadenopathy strongly pointed toward a granulomatous process rather than standard pyogenic pneumonia.

Considered in a 72-year-old male with massive hemoptysis, localized parenchymal opacity, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, but excluded by the miliary distribution of lesions and definitive microbiological confirmation of mycobacteria rather than malignant cytology.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive turning point occurred when both the T-SPOT.TB interferon-gamma release assay and sputum mycobacterial polymerase chain reaction (TB-PCR) returned positive, confirming active pulmonary tuberculosis (which later provided the immunocompromised substrate for invasive fungal necrotizing fasciitis).

clinical_summary: A 4-month-old infant boy was brought to a regional hospital clinic by his mother because of an intensely pruritic, progressive cutaneous eruption that had persisted for one month. The infant was the only child in the household and resided with his parents in a rural village outside Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the family's suspicion of household bedbug presence, but ruled out because bedbug bites present as clustered or linear urticarial papules on exposed body parts rather than chronic pustular and scaly eruptions preferentially located in the palms, soles, and interdigital creases.

Considered given the prominent pustule-like lesions and marked irritability localized predominantly to the palms and soles of a 4-month-old infant, but excluded because acropustulosis is a non-infectious condition that does not explain the concurrent, contagious, nocturnal interdigital pruritic eruption present in the co-sleeping mother.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive turning point occurred during parasitological investigation, when dermatoscope examination revealed diagnostic burrows on the palm, and microscopic examination of skin scale scrapings at 100x magnification definitively identified female Sarcoptes scabiei mites and their eggs in both the infant and his mother.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old male with a medical history of type 2 diabetes presented with a 3-month history of persistent cough and severe back pain. The presentation was accompanied by prolonged fever and significant unintentional weight loss.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Sepsis and Disseminated Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute staphylococcal or enteric bacteremia causing septic arthritis and perianal abscesses typically presents with toxic signs and marked peripheral leukocytosis; the patient exhibited a prolonged 3-month course with completely normal white blood cell counts.

differentials.candidate: Pelvic Malignancy / Chordoma with Bone Metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although a destructive retrorectal and coccygeal mass in an older adult raises suspicion for chordoma or necrotic pelvic malignancy, the peripheral ring enhancement on MRI, concomitant apical pulmonary cavitation, and elbow synovitis pointed to a multifocal granulomatous infectious process.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when purulent fistula discharge, sputum, and left elbow joint aspirate demonstrated acid-fast bacilli and yielded positive molecular GeneXpert confirmation for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old previously healthy male manual laborer presented with an 18-month history of progressively worsening lower back pain and bilateral pain localized to the lumbar fossae. Eighteen months prior, he had developed mechanical low back pain without nocturnal awakenings or morning stiffness, worsened by physical labor.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Inflammatory back pain in a young male can suggest spondyloarthritis; however, the absence of bilateral sacroiliitis on pelvic imaging, lack of peripheral joint or enthesitic disease, and MRI demonstration of destructive discitis with bilateral psoas fluid collections excluded rheumatic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy.

While early mechanical symptoms and initial plain imaging suggested degenerative disc protrusions or primary bony neoplasms, the persistent worsening and decisive MRI findings confirmed an infectious spondylodiscitis with large bilateral muscular abscesses.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred following CT-guided percutaneous drainage of the psoas collections; aspirated purulent material was negative on routine aerobic/anaerobic cultures but showed acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, followed by positive Lowenstein-Jensen culture and GeneXpert MTB/RIF confirmation.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male diagnosed with HIV two months prior presented with numbness of the upper lip, dizziness, and headache. Over the preceding weeks, he had also experienced intermittent low-grade fevers, generalized fatigue, significant unintentional weight loss, and mild abdominal discomfort.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Toxoplasma gondii encephalitis is the most frequent cause of intracranial ring-enhancing target lesions in advanced HIV; however, the presence of long-segment intramedullary spinal cord hyperintensities and widespread retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy prompted broad consideration of disseminated opportunistic fungal or mycobacterial disease.

Cryptococcus neoformans commonly causes subacute meningitis and intracranial mass lesions in HIV patients, but classical target-like ring-enhancing brainstem lesions with restricted diffusion and diffuse retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy are atypical.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when metagenomic next-generation sequencing of the cerebrospinal fluid identified Talaromyces marneffei, confirming multisystem central nervous system talaromycosis with subsequent full clinical resolution on intravenous amphotericin B followed by oral itraconazole.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old male with known HIV infection presented to the hospital with a one-day history of acute abdominal pain and fever, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. He had been prescribed antiretroviral therapy with elvitegravir but had not attended regular follow-up and had previously discontinued an antifungal regimen after one month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute peritonitis with severe epigastric/periumbilical pain frequently raises concern for necrotizing pancreatitis or hollow viscus perforation; this was excluded by normal serum amylase and lipase levels and absence of focal pancreatic necrosis on CT.

Disseminated mycobacterial peritonitis is a major cause of subacute peritonitis and ascites in advanced HIV, but the interferon-gamma release assay was negative and serological markers strongly pointed toward an invasive fungal etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when pathogen-specific Talaromyces marneffei antigen testing returned positive in the setting of markedly elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan and galactomannan, confirming recurrent opportunistic peritonitis due to talaromycosis.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 1-year history of progressive erythema, swelling, and pain in her left breast, complicated by spontaneous ulceration with thin purulent drainage over the past month.

differentials.candidate: Invasive Breast Carcinoma / Inflammatory Breast Cancer
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient's advanced age, family history of breast cancer in two sisters, and a hard, fixed mass with poorly defined borders strongly suggested breast carcinoma; however, repeated cytological examinations demonstrated mixed inflammatory cells and abscess formation rather than neoplastic epithelial proliferation.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Granulomatous Mastitis / Pyogenic Breast Abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recurrent breast abscesses with sinus tracts frequently indicate idiopathic granulomatous mastitis or refractory bacterial abscess; however, the lack of response to antibiotics and intraoperative identification of extensive caseous necrosis and deep sinus tracts tracking to the pectoralis muscle pointed to a specific mycobacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during surgical excision, which revealed dark red necrotic and caseous material along deep pectoralis sinus tracts, confirmed on histopathology by multifocal caseous necrosis, granulomas, positive acid-fast staining, and positive TB-DNA molecular PCR testing.

clinical_summary: A 79-year-old female rural agricultural worker presented with a 3-month history of progressive upper abdominal discomfort, unintentional weight loss, and generalized weakness. Her past medical history was notable for hypertension, nephrolithiasis, and chronic gastritis treated with antihypertensives and proton pump inhibitors.

differentials.candidate: Aggressive Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma / Gastric Carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread polyserosal effusions and gastric wall thickening in an elderly patient suggested an aggressive metastatic malignancy or intravascular lymphoma; however, biopsy showed an indolent MALT lymphoma with reactive intravascular plasmablasts lacking light-chain restriction, which still could not explain the polyserosal effusions.

Although gastric biopsy and PCR confirmed monoclonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangements diagnostic of MALT lymphoma, indolent low-grade lymphoma fails to cause acute multisystem polyserositis with pericardial, pleural, and ascitic effusions.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred on retrospective pathological review of serial gastric biopsy specimens, which demonstrated conspicuous caseous necrosis, multinucleated Langhans giant cells, and acid-fast bacilli, confirming concurrent disseminated gastrointestinal and serosal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old woman (gravida 2, para 1, with one living child) at 7 weeks and 1 day of gestational age presented to the emergency department with acute lower abdominal pain initially concerning for acute appendicitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although referred for suspected acute appendicitis, the patient's amenorrhea, active cervical bleeding, positive pregnancy test, and pelvic ultrasound demonstrating a right adnexal mass confirmed an acute gynecologic/ectopic pathology rather than appendicitis.

While an ectopic rupture accounted for the acute hemoperitoneum, it did not explain the underlying tubal architectural damage; histological examination of the resected fallopian tube revealed that parasitic egg deposition was the causative driver of tubal inflammation.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred during histopathological examination of the salpingectomy specimen, which demonstrated calcified Schistosoma eggs embedded alongside chorionic villi within the fallopian tube, confirming female genital schistosomiasis as the underlying pathology.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old pregnant woman was referred to an outpatient dermatology clinic in Shiraz, Iran, with a 2-year history of a slowly growing, painless lesion on her nose. She reported no trauma, prior local injections, or constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats.

differentials.candidate: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) / Cutaneous B-cell Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: A painless, chronic, expanding tumoral plaque on the face of an adult raised high suspicion for cutaneous malignancy or lymphoma; however, biopsy did not show neoplastic keratinocytes or clonal lymphoid proliferation.

Chronic granulomatous diseases such as lupus vulgaris or sarcoidosis can cause infiltrative nasal plaques; however, histopathology revealed heavy dermal histiocytic infiltration containing intracellular protozoan organisms rather than tuberculoid or sarcoidal granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred upon microscopic examination of a nasal punch biopsy, which demonstrated abundant intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within dermal histiocytes, establishing the diagnosis of chronic tumoral cutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of progressive blackish discoloration of her toes bilaterally. She had no medical history of diabetes mellitus, systemic hypertension, or cardiovascular disease, and denied tobacco use.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Necrotizing Vasculitis (e.g., Polyarteritis Nodosa / ANCA-Associated Vasculitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Peripheral digital gangrene accompanied by an ESR over 100 mm/hr strongly suggested a systemic necrotizing vasculitis; however, ANCA was negative and the presence of cutaneous hypoaesthetic macules with thickened peripheral nerve trunks pointed toward a primary neuro-dermatological infectious etiology.

differentials.candidate: Peripheral Artery Disease / Thromboangiitis Obliterans (Buerger's Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe bilateral digital gangrene is commonly caused by occlusive arterial disease, but the patient lacked cardiovascular risk factors, all distal peripheral pulses were well palpated, and arterial Doppler ultrasonography showed no vascular occlusion.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when skin biopsy of the hypoaesthetic macules revealed borderline tuberculoid leprosy, corroborated by slit skin smears demonstrating a bacteriological index of 1+, with subsequent identification of IgM anti-cardiolipin antibodies explaining the thrombotic gangrene.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old female residing in the Mugu district of western Nepal presented to the outpatient department with a 2-year history of multiple, progressively enlarging, painless nodular lesions localized exclusively to her tongue.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic granulomatous tongue nodules in an endemic setting strongly suggest mycobacterial diseases such as tuberculosis or leprosy; however, slit-skin smears and special tissue stains were completely negative for acid-fast bacilli.

differentials.candidate: Lingual Amyloidosis / Mucosal Neuromas / Sarcoidosis / Mycosis Fungoides
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple smooth lingual nodules can mimic nodular amyloidosis, neuromas, or lymphoproliferative disorders, but Congo red staining was negative and histopathology showed chronic granulomatous inflammation without clonal lymphoid atypia.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when molecular testing by PCR targeting Leishmania donovani DNA was positive, alongside a positive rK-39 serological assay, establishing isolated lingual mucosal leishmaniasis (mucosal post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis variant).

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old man with a history of two renal transplantations (in 2006 and 2013) maintained on chronic immunosuppressive therapy with mycophenolate mofetil and tacrolimus presented to the hospital with a 5-day history of fever, asthenia, and myalgias.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially considered as the primary viral diagnostic hypothesis due to acute fever, altered mentation, and motor signs; however, CSF PCR for herpesviruses was negative, brain MRI lacked characteristic temporal lobe lesions, and CSF Gram stain and cultures showed no bacterial growth.
Ruled out based on absence of systemic signs of infection or sepsis, normal baseline laboratory investigations, absence of septic foci, and sterile CSF cultures.
Deemed improbable following extensive laboratory work demonstrating normal electrolytes, intact liver function, and no evidence of exogenous or immunosuppressant-related toxic agents.

Considered due to progressive rigidity, myoclonus, and focal seizures as an immune-mediated postinfectious process; however, it is predominantly a pediatric entity, brain MRI showed no white matter demyelination, and the patient improved spontaneously without immunomodulatory therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Because the NS1 antigen test loses diagnostic sensitivity after day 5 of illness, persistent neuro-inflammatory findings prompted serum IgM serology on symptom day 7 (2 days after negative NS1 testing), which returned positive and was confirmed 2 days later, establishing acute neuroinvasive arboviral disease in an endemic context.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old man with a 25-year history of relapsing and remitting brainstem neurologic deficits and mediastinal lymphadenopathy—previously treated with corticosteroids and maintenance methotrexate for histologically-proven non-caseating epithelioid granulomas—presented after developing a new mass on the anterior chest wall accompanied by an ipsilateral pleural effusion.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Thoracoscopic lymph node biopsy had demonstrated non-caseating epithelioid granulomas consistent with sarcoidosis with negative initial mycobacterial testing; however, following immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids and methotrexate, the emergence of a chest wall mass and empyema was proven to be active mycobacterial disease rather than sarcoid progression.

differentials.candidate: Relapsing inflammatory brainstem demyelination / Multiple sclerosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to episodic brainstem neurological deficits with pontine enhancement responsive to high-dose corticosteroids; however, CSF oligoclonal bands were negative, serum autoantibodies and inflammatory markers were normal, and the patient subsequently manifested non-neural thoracic granulomatous lesions and empyema.

diagnostic_pivot: In 2020, while maintained on methotrexate and corticosteroids, the patient developed a new chest wall mass and pleural effusion; GeneXpert molecular testing of the empyema fluid was positive for rifampin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing active pulmonary and pleural disease.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old male who immigrated to the United States from Guatemala 17 years prior presented to the emergency department after experiencing two witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizures on the day of presentation.

differentials.candidate: Intracranial neoplasm / Primary brain tumor or cerebral metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: New-onset adult seizures and intracranial space-occupying lesions initially raised suspicion for neoplastic pathology; however, brain CT and MRI revealed multiple punctate calcified and cystic lesions characteristic of involuting parasitic stages rather than mass lesions with surrounding infiltrative edema, and systemic oncologic staging was unrevealing.

Considered due to immigration from Guatemala and intracranial granulomatous-appearing lesions, but QuantiFERON-TB Gold testing was negative, chest imaging showed no tuberculosis, and imaging lacked basilar meningeal enhancement or caseating necrosis.

Considered in an immigrant from Central America recently prescribed systemic corticosteroids (prednisone); however, serum Strongyloides antibody testing was negative, and stool examination showed only commensal protozoa (Blastocystis hominis and Endolimax nana) without larvae.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative serum cysticercosis antibody testing (which frequently occurs in parenchymal calcified or low-burden disease), the combination of new-onset adult generalized seizures, immigration from endemic Guatemala, and cranial imaging showing multiple cystic and calcified lesions fulfilled the validated Del Brutto diagnostic criteria.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old man with refractory Crohn's disease maintained on chronic cumulative immunosuppressive therapy—including the oral Janus kinase inhibitor upadacitinib (30 mg daily) and maintenance low-dose systemic corticosteroids, following prior anti-TNF and IL-12/23 biologic agents—presented with a 6-month history of insidious clinical deterioration, characterized by progressive thoracic back pain and generalized fatigue.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic spinal malignancy or primary mediastinal neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Aggressive osteolytic vertebral destruction, paravertebral mass, and subcarinal lymphadenopathy strongly simulated advanced metastatic disease; however, an extensive panel of serum tumor markers was entirely normal, and mediastinal lymph node core biopsy cytology and immunohistochemistry showed no neoplastic cells.

Considered due to severe cumulative immunosuppression from a JAK inhibitor and corticosteroids; however, fungal blood/sputum cultures, serum galactomannan assay, and special fungal staining (PAS and Grocott-methenamine silver) on lymph node tissue were negative.

Autoimmune serologies including antinuclear antibodies and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative, and the lesion demonstrated destructive bone invasion and progressive cold abscess formation rather than enteropathic arthritis.

diagnostic_pivot: In this patient under cumulative immunosuppression with upadacitinib and corticosteroids, EBUS-guided transbronchial mediastinal lymph node core biopsy (EBUS-TDB) demonstrated Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA on Xpert MTB/RIF assay, establishing mediastinal tuberculous lymphadenitis with paravertebral cold abscess and Pott's disease.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old man with a history of untreated essential hypertension presented to the emergency department after acute onset of coma lasting 1 hour. On the day preceding presentation, he developed severe, progressive headache accompanied by more than five episodes of vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Subdural hematomas typically develop following blunt head trauma or falls; however, the patient's family explicitly corroborated the total absence of head injury or antecedent trauma, confirming spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage.

differentials.candidate: Hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage / Ruptured berry aneurysm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to a history of untreated hypertension and acute severe headache with vomiting; however, cranial CT showed an extensive extra-axial subdural hematoma along the cerebral convexity rather than basal ganglionic intraparenchymal or subarachnoid hemorrhage, and baseline coagulation parameters were normal.

diagnostic_pivot: The patient had been hospitalized 5 days prior with confirmed dengue hemorrhagic fever characterized by profound thrombocytopenia (30,000/μL) and positive serum anti-dengue IgM antibodies; persistent thrombocytopenia (74,000/μL) and disease-induced capillary fragility precipitated a fatal spontaneous subdural hematoma.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old previously healthy woman presented with a 21-month history of progressive left gluteal pain accompanied by mild radiation down the left lower limb and restricted mobility of the left hip.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chronic gluteal pain with radiating lower limb symptoms led to a prolonged misdiagnosis of lumbar disc displacement; however, conservative anti-inflammatory and neurotrophic therapies failed, and subsequent musculoskeletal ultrasound and pelvic MRI revealed communicating intramuscular infectious fluid collections rather than nerve root compression.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial abscess (e.g., Staphylococcal or Gram-negative pelvic abscess) / Brucellosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: An indolent 21-month clinical course without acute sepsis or leukocytosis (WBC 3.51 × 10⁹/L), sterile 72-hour routine blood cultures, negative Brucella cultures, and surgical drainage showing caseous necrotic debris rather than foul-smelling acute purulence excluded common pyogenic and brucellar etiologies.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration of the communicating iliac fossa and gluteus maximus lesions released 150 mL of caseous necrotic material with histological confirmation of caseating granulomatous inflammation, leading to prompt clinical resolution under quadruple antituberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old woman presented with a palpable right breast lump, chronic nonproductive cough, and dull chest pain. She had no significant past medical or family history.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic breast carcinoma (Stage IV metastatic disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and masses in a patient with biopsy-proven invasive ductal carcinoma and regional lymphadenopathy were initially suspected to represent hematogenous metastatic dissemination; however, 18F-FDG PET imaging revealed intense FDG uptake in the primary breast lesion and lymph nodes but complete photopenia/absence of uptake in the lung masses, indicating a benign non-malignant process.

differentials.candidate: Pulmonary tuberculosis or fungal granulomatous disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Granulomatous infections can present with bilateral pulmonary nodular opacities, but usually exhibit variable metabolic activity on FDG-PET; in this patient, complete absence of FDG uptake alongside positive echinococcal serology in an endemic resident favored parasitic cyst formation.

diagnostic_pivot: Geographic origin from the eastern region of the country where hydatid disease is endemic, non-avid lung lesions on FDG-PET scan, and a positive indirect hemagglutination serological test confirmed pulmonary echinococcosis coexisting with non-metastatic stage IIIC breast cancer.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old Hispanic woman who immigrated to the United States two years prior presented at 32 weeks of gestation in a twin pregnancy with preterm labor contractions. Her prenatal course had been uncomplicated except for an occasional mild nonproductive cough.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Tracheobronchial endoscopy showed irregular vegetations and a mass-like mediastinal lesion occluding the bronchial tree, raising strong concern for bronchogenic carcinoma; however, endobronchial biopsies demonstrated caseating granulomatous inflammation without atypical epithelial cells or malignancy.

Bronchoalveolar lavage culture isolated abundant Staphylococcus aureus, but transbronchial biopsy proved this to represent superficial bacterial colonization over chronically ulcerated caseating granulomas, with no clinical improvement on targeted anti-staphylococcal therapy.
Endobronchial fungal smears, fungal cultures, and fungal histopathological stains on bronchial biopsies were negative for yeasts or hyphae.

diagnostic_pivot: Endobronchial biopsy demonstrating classic caseating granulomatous inflammation, followed on hospital day 26 by positive DNA probe and culture isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from right lung tissue specimens, confirmed active pulmonary and endobronchial tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old woman (gravida 3, para 3) presented with a 4-month history of lower abdominal pain, anorexia, progressive severe constipation, and an unintentional weight loss of more than 10 kg.

differentials.candidate: Advanced gynecologic / pelvic malignancy (e.g., ovarian cystadenocarcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A massive 28-week-sized pelvic mass associated with severe anemia (Hb 7 g/dL) and rapid 10-kg weight loss strongly simulated ovarian or peritoneal malignancy; however, abdominal/chest CT and bone scintigraphy showed no metastasis, and surgical pathology demonstrated non-neoplastic parasitic cyst membranes.

differentials.candidate: Severe gastrointestinal malignancy or extrinsic colonic obstruction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe intractable constipation and profound weight loss suggested colonic obstruction from primary colorectal cancer; however, diagnostic colonoscopy demonstrated completely normal mucosa and lumen, confirming that bowel symptoms were due to extrinsic compression by pelvic cysts.

differentials.candidate: Pelvic endometriosis or benign ovarian cystadenoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Endometriomas or simple cystadenomas rarely present as massive, densely adherent multilocular cysts filling the broad ligament and adnexa with marked anemia and constitutional wasting, and histology revealed characteristic scolices rather than endometrial or serous/mucinous epithelium.

diagnostic_pivot: Exploratory laparotomy with excision of pelvic and adnexal cystic lesions demonstrated characteristic hydatid cysts, confirmed on microscopic examination by the presence of Echinococcus granulosus scolices and adjacent laminated cuticular membranes.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old patient living in an agricultural sheep-grazing rural region presented with a more than 1-year history of intermittent colicky abdominal pain accompanied by recurrent episodes of nausea and vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Intermittent colicky right upper quadrant pain associated with nausea and vomiting in a young non-alcoholic patient often suggests recurrent biliary colic from gallstones; however, cross-sectional radiological imaging identified cystic hepatic lesions rather than gallstone disease.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic liver abscess or Amoebic liver abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial or amoebic liver abscesses typically manifest with acute fever, chills, leukocytosis, and rapid progression; in this patient cohort, symptoms were mild, indolent, and chronic, persisting for over one year without acute septic toxicity.

diagnostic_pivot: Close zoonotic exposure to dogs and livestock in an agricultural sheep-grazing endemic zone, together with confirmatory serological testing and characteristic cystic hepatic features on radiological imaging, definitively established hepatic echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A patient presents for clinical evaluation and diagnostic workup of hepatobiliary disease. On physical examination, the patient is clinically stable without acute peritonitis.

differentials.candidate: Simple Hepatic Cyst / Congenital Biliary Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple hepatic cysts are benign developmental fluid collections that are typically non-parasitic and do not cause systemic inflammatory responses, eosinophilia, or elevated liver enzymes (AST, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin).

Infectious abscesses usually manifest with severe systemic toxicity, high fever, and peripheral neutrophilic leukocytosis, and on imaging they demonstrate thick peripheral rim enhancement rather than a well-defined non-enhancing hypodense cyst.

Biliary cystadenomas and cystic carcinomas generally feature thick fibrous capsules, enhancing internal septations, or mural nodules, rather than an unilocular, well-demarcated non-enhancing hypodense cystic lesion with eosinophilia.

The diagnostic turning point is the constellation of peripheral eosinophilia, a well-defined non-enhancing hypodense hepatic cyst exerting local vascular and gallbladder mass effect, and positive confirmatory echinococcal serological evaluation (ELISA and IHA).

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old man with a history of primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) diagnosed two years previously presents with a one-month history of intermittent fever. He reports no other associated systemic or localized symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Brucella infection frequently manifests as prolonged fever of unknown origin with hepatosplenic abscesses and adrenal granulomas in endemic areas, but was excluded by negative serologic assays, blood cultures, and bone-marrow cultures.

The co-occurrence of an enlarged adrenal gland with calcifications in an Addisonian patient alongside a focal hepatic hypodense lesion raised concern for adrenal carcinoma or metastatic malignancy, but hepatic cytology was negative for neoplastic cells.

Although purulent material obtained during laparotomy grew Streptococcus constellatus in pure culture, the presence of chronic adrenal calcifications and tissue granulomas pointed to an underlying chronic granulomatous etiology rather than simple monomicrobial pyogenic infection.

The definitive turning point was the demonstration of chronic granulomatous inflammation in adrenal and hepatic tissues combined with recovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from Lowenstein culture of the abscess material in a patient with a 12-mm Mantoux reaction.

clinical_summary: A 68-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with a two-month history of progressive general malaise, generalized arthralgia, myalgia, and low-grade fever. Ten days prior to admission, she developed dorsolumbar back pain radiating anteriorly to the right rib cage.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Brucellosis is a prevalent cause of subacute spondylitis with paravertebral inflammation and vertebral destruction in endemic Mediterranean regions, but was excluded by negative Brucella serology and sterile blood cultures.
