The presence of fever, a mobile intracardiac mass, mitral regurgitation, and splenic infarcts strongly suggested left-sided infective endocarditis; however, bronchoscopy excluded endobronchial lesions and GeneXpert of BAL confirmed active mycobacterial disease driving local vascular thrombosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis by GeneXpert in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in the setting of severe right lower lobe cavitary consolidation, establishing active pulmonary tuberculosis complicated by contiguous pulmonary venous thrombosis extending into the left atrium.

clinical_summary: A 74-year-old female retired home healthcare worker presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain and vomiting developing after a left inguinal hernia repair performed 7 days earlier. Her symptoms began 2 days post-procedure as severe, burning, non-radiating epigastric pain accompanied by low-grade fever, nausea, postprandial clear and mucoid vomiting, and obstipation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid profound unintentional weight loss (25 lbs), anorexia, altered stool caliber, and jejunal mural thickening raised high clinical suspicion for gastrointestinal carcinoma or lymphoma; however, CT showed no discrete mass or lymphadenopathy, and tumor markers were normal.

Obstipation, persistent vomiting, and small bowel distension occurring days after inguinal hernia repair suggested mechanical obstruction or incarcerated hernia; however, CT demonstrated generalized dilation up to 4.5 cm consistent with ileus without an identifiable mechanical transition point.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat upper endoscopy showing mucosal erythema and duodenal/gastric biopsies revealing numerous parasitic sections of Strongyloides stercoralis within glandular crypts, confirmed by stool ova and parasite examination demonstrating rhabditiform larvae.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a 5- to 6-day history of high fever associated with chills, abdominal pain, and vomiting. He denies any skin rash, arthralgias, cough, dyspnea, urinary symptoms, seizures, or bleeding diathesis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile illness accompanied by abdominal pain, vomiting, splenomegaly, and leukopenia in Delhi strongly suggested Salmonella enterica infection, but serological testing via the tube Widal test was negative.
Severe anemia, leukopenia, and massive splenomegaly (30 cm) in an Indian patient raised high suspicion for visceral leishmaniasis, but the rK-39 rapid immunochromatographic test was negative.
Vector-borne acute febrile illness presenting with cytopenias and systemic symptoms was evaluated for chikungunya, but specific serology was non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of concurrent dengue virus infection via reactive Dengue IgM ELISA alongside identification of mixed Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum malaria on peripheral smear and confirmatory 18S rRNA PCR.

clinical_summary: A 76-year-old man presents for outpatient evaluation of a severely pruritic cutaneous eruption that has persisted for 2 months. His past medical history is significant for an open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair 5 months prior, complicated by multiple vascular re-explorations, an infected retroperitoneal hematoma, and a right groin pseudoaneurysm managed with open debridements, a negative pressure wound therapy device, and...

differentials.rule_out_reason: The eruption began while receiving multiple broad-spectrum antibiotics, suggesting a drug exanthem; however, discontinuation of daptomycin and linezolid failed to resolve the pruritus, and the lesions progressed to tense bullae.

Tense bullae on an urticarial base in an elderly individual, with subepidermal splitting and linear IgG/C3 basement membrane deposition on direct immunofluorescence, mimicked bullous pemphigoid; however, it was a mimicker (scabies surrepticius) as proven by secondary transmission to cohabitants and microscopic identification of mites.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergence of pruritic papules in cohabiting household members (wife and son) and physical re-evaluation identifying classic interdigital finger burrows containing Sarcoptes scabiei mites, eggs, and scybala on mineral oil skin scraping.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old female at 29 weeks and 6 days of gestation presents with acute, severe right-sided abdominal pain radiating to the right lumbar region, accompanied by dyspnea, near-syncope, and reduced exercise tolerance over the preceding week.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute right lower quadrant peritonitis, fever, leukocytosis, and a subhepatic inflammatory collection strongly suggested perforated appendicitis in pregnancy; however, surgical exploration revealed a completely normal appendix.

Intraoperative identification of a firm, hard cecal mass with irregular contours in the setting of 20 kg unintentional weight loss raised suspicion for advanced colon cancer; however, histopathology demonstrated caseating mycobacterial infection rather than malignant cells.
Intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea were repeatedly treated as routine acute enteritis, but failed to explain severe weight loss, transmural bowel necrosis, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency exploratory laparotomy, right hemicolectomy, and definitive histopathological examination demonstrating primary caecal tuberculosis, in the setting of negative chest radiography, negative sputum AFB, and non-reactive Mantoux testing.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old female presents to an outpatient neurology clinic with a progressive gait disorder, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence. Her history began 19 years earlier with acute headache and fever treated with antimicrobial and corticosteroid therapy with symptomatic resolution.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The progressive development of gait disturbance, memory impairment, and urinary incontinence in an elderly female strongly suggested idiopathic NPH; however, CSF analysis demonstrated chronic active neuroinflammation with lymphocytic-eosinophilic pleocytosis, elevated proteins, and marked hypergammaglobulinemia, rather than normal CSF cellularity.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic / Chronic Neuroinfections (Toxoplasmosis, CMV, EBV, HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recurrent chronic meningeal inflammation and steroid dependency raised suspicion for chronic opportunistic viral or protozoal central nervous system infections, but specific serologies were non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive CSF antibody-enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (Ag-ELISA) alongside neuroimaging demonstrating communicating hydrocephalus and characteristic racemose multicystic lesions resembling a bunch of grapes lacking a scolex within the right Sylvian fissure.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old girl residing in a rural community in Kenitra province, Morocco, presents with a 2-week history of epigastric abdominal pain, accompanied by postprandial vomiting and diarrhea over the preceding 6 weeks.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An epigastric cystic mass adjacent to the gallbladder and duodenum accompanied by elevated pancreatic enzymes suggested a choledochal cyst; however, MRI and surgical exploration demonstrated normal caliber biliary ducts and showed the mass originated from the pancreatic head rather than the biliary tree.

An intimate anatomical relationship with the second portion of the duodenum in a 5-year-old child strongly raised suspicion for an enteric duplication cyst; however, surgical exploration proved that the mass arose from the pancreatic lodge and merely displaced the duodenum posteriorly without mucosal or muscular wall continuity.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive hydatid serology by ELISA followed by exploratory laparotomy demonstrating a pancreatic cyst containing pathognomonic "rock water" clear fluid and three proliferating hydatid germinative membranes.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old previously healthy male is brought to the emergency department with rapidly progressive tachypnea and dyspnea over the preceding 24 hours. His partner reports that he had been intermittently febrile for the past week, complaining of diffuse myalgias and headache.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An acute febrile illness with myalgia and headache in a returning traveler initially raised suspicion for influenza; however, progression to fulminant ARDS with negative viral panels and lack of improvement on supportive care prompted search for another etiology.

Severe pneumonia complicated by ARDS was suspected and treated with broad-spectrum antimicrobials, but blood, urine, and bronchoalveolar lavage cultures were sterile, and chest CT demonstrated diffuse edema rather than focal consolidation.

Returning travel from Costa Rica with fever, headache, myalgia, and pulmonary infiltrates prompted evaluation for malaria and dengue, but multiple blood smears and serologies were completely negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Re-evaluation of exposure history revealing freshwater swimming and ingestion in Costa Rica, prompt clinical recovery following penicillin therapy, and subsequent serological confirmation with positive Leptospira IgM and microscopic agglutination testing (MAT).

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male sushi chef who had never traveled outside Japan presented to the hospital with a 2-day history of high fever and severe muscle pain. Initial triage laboratory testing revealed a white blood cell count of 7,780/µL, platelet count of 89,000/µL, C-reactive protein of 36.4 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen of 47 mg/dL, serum creatinine of 2.41 mg/dL, and total...

differentials.candidate: Bacterial pneumonia and atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to acute respiratory failure, high-grade fever, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, and diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates, but the patient failed broad-spectrum antimicrobial coverage and specific non-invasive pathogen testing was negative.

Considered due to diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates accompanied by multi-organ failure and septic shock, but screening tests were negative and empiric antitubercular therapy produced no response.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was the recognition of severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome (SPHS) alongside the classic icteric triad of jaundice, acute renal failure, and severe thrombocytopenia in an individual with occupational wet-work/rodent contact exposure as a sushi chef, definitively established by the detection of pathogen DNA in urine via PCR and confirmed by a fourfold rise in paired convalescent microagglutination titers.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old Peruvian woman residing in Buenos Aires, Argentina, presented to the hospital and was admitted to the gastroenterology ward following multiple emergency department visits for intractable vomiting, chronic diarrhea, diffuse abdominal pain, fever, profound weight loss exceeding 16 kg, and decreased visual acuity in her right eye.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to diffuse small bowel wall thickening, severe jejunal and duodenal atrophy, and mucosal petechial lesions, but administration of high-dose corticosteroids led to catastrophic clinical deterioration and systemic sepsis rather than remission.

Considered given the patient's profound cachexia, chronic diarrhea, fever, and opportunistic ocular pathology (endophthalmitis), but specific viral and immunologic testing ruled out HIV infection and primary immune deficiencies.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when immunosuppression unmasked a fulminant hyperinfection syndrome featuring enteric bacteremia (E. coli, K. pneumoniae) and purpuric cutaneous lesions, leading to direct microscopic visualization of filariform larvae on enteral biopsies, skin lesions, and specialized stool sedimentation, subsequently confirmed to be driven by HTLV-1 co-infection.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old male surgeon working at a hospital in northern Togo presented with fever. He had documented prior vaccination against yellow fever.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially considered due to high endemicity and an initial positive blood smear, but the patient experienced progressive clinical deterioration without any therapeutic response to a full course of artemether/lumefantrine.

differentials.candidate: Acute surgical abdomen (perforated peptic ulcer or acute peritonitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to intractable, severe epigastric and diffuse abdominal pain in the setting of febrile systemic illness, prompting an emergency laparotomy which revealed no surgical perforation and caused catastrophic operative wound bleeding.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the confluence of acute sensorineural hearing impairment (hypoacusis), severe pharyngitis, profound leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, and lethal coagulopathy in a healthcare worker in rural West Africa, confirmed by molecular testing.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old male healthcare professional at a hospital in northern Togo presented on March 5, 2016, with acute fever, severe headache, chills, and generalized body aches, approximately three weeks after providing nursing care to a critically ill colleague who had suffered a fatal hemorrhagic illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the leading cause of acute febrile jaundice, cytopenias, and acute renal failure in West Africa, but empiric artemisinin combination therapy failed to provide any therapeutic benefit.
Considered given the classic presentation of acute viral hemorrhagic fever with fever, jaundice, and acute renal failure in Togo, but the patient had documented protective vaccination.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the epidemiologic clustering of severe febrile illness and hemorrhagic manifestations among healthcare workers in the same hospital ward, combined with marked AST-predominant transaminitis and profound thrombocytopenia, confirmed by molecular detection of viral RNA.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old woman was admitted to a hospital in London, United Kingdom, after collapsing in the street. She reported an indolent 14-month history of night sweats and steady loss of energy, but was otherwise asymptomatic and reported no fevers.

differentials.candidate: Hematologic malignancy (lymphoma, leukemia, or myelodysplastic syndrome)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The leading clinical suspicion based on 14 months of constitutional night sweats, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and cytopenias without fever, leading directly to bone marrow evaluation.

differentials.candidate: Chronic viral hepatitis and parasitic coinfection (HBV, HCV, Strongyloides, HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as plausible infectious explanations for chronic hepatomegaly and cytopenias in an international traveler, but specific serologic panels were non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the unexpected cytological identification of intracellular amastigotes on bone marrow aspirate, followed by internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) gene amplification and sequencing confirming an atypical non-donovani visceralizing parasite, explaining the negative rK39 serologic screen.

clinical_summary: A 63-year-old woman residing in central Texas presented to a regional emergency department because of persistent fatigue, recurrent fevers, and chills lasting three weeks. Her past medical history was notable for Crohn's disease treated with mercaptopurine and mesalamine, hypertension, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease with microhematuria, obesity, and depression.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected because of residence in an endemic Texas region and a weakly positive anti-WNV IgM, but specific molecular testing by reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction failed to detect WNV nucleic acid.
Considered during early outpatient evaluation due to persistent fever, headache, and cytopenias in Texas, prompting empiric doxycycline, but specific rickettsial serology was negative.
Considered due to acute jaundice, scleral icterus, and significant transaminitis, but serologic markers for acute viral hepatitis were non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the histological confirmation of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) on bone marrow biopsy (macrophages phagocytosing erythrocytes) driven by severe systemic flavivirus infection, followed by bone marrow RT-PCR and sequencing confirming locally acquired dengue virus type 3.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female was referred and admitted to the hospital with a 7-day history of abdominal pain and tenderness. She had no history of chronic medical conditions, no alcohol consumption, no family history of malignancy, and took no prescribed or herbal medications.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary clinical concern given the combination of a complex septated ovarian cyst, multiple peritoneal nodular implants, exudative ascites, and elevated CA-125 (107.5 U/mL), but serial peritoneal fluid cytologies revealed only lymphocytes with no malignant cells.

Considered due to acute abdominal tenderness and inflammatory markers, but excluded by the absence of leukocytosis, absence of systemic signs of sepsis, and lymphocytic rather than neutrophilic exudate.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the demonstration of an ascites adenosine deaminase (ADA) level of 62 U/L (more than double the upper limit of normal), followed by a trucut core needle biopsy of the peritoneal nodules confirming granulomatous inflammation with histiocytic cells.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male law enforcement officer with a history of type II diabetes mellitus presented to the outpatient department with a 3-week history of progressive right facial swelling and painful, mobile upper right posterior teeth.

differentials.candidate: Odontogenic buccal and canine space abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial provisional diagnosis based on severe periodontitis, tooth mobility, and buccal fluctuation, but surgical incision and drainage yielded only scanty purulent fluid and bacterial cultures were completely sterile after 72 hours with persistent facial swelling.

Suspected when advanced imaging demonstrated aggressive osteolytic destruction of the anterior/posterior maxillary walls, hard palate, and orbital extension, but histopathology revealed caseating granulomas rather than neoplastic cells.
Considered in a patient with uncontrolled diabetes presenting with destructive paranasal sinus polyposis and bone erosion, but special histological stains for fungal hyphae were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was transnasal endoscopic visualization of a granular maxillary mass and biopsy revealing epithelioid histiocytic granulomas with Langhans giant cells and caseation necrosis, confirmed by positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining and a positive Mantoux test without pulmonary involvement.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old man was admitted to the surgery department complaining of diffuse abdominal pain, dyspnea, generalized fatigue, and progressive weakness. His past medical history was notable for hospitalization at another medical center two months earlier for an episode of acute pancreatitis.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The leading presumptive diagnosis given the preceding history of acute pancreatitis and a thick-walled retrogastric fluid collection, but intraoperative exploration and needle aspiration revealed crystal-clear fluid rather than turbid pancreatic fluid, and evacuation yielded distinct daughter cysts and endocyst membranes.

Considered due to the thick-walled retroperitoneal collection, surrounding fat stranding, elevated C-reactive protein, and persistent abdominal pain, but excluded by the absence of systemic sepsis and the non-purulent, clear nature of the aspirated cyst contents.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic pivot occurred intraoperatively during puncture of the retroperitoneal pancreatic mass, which yielded pathognomonic crystal-clear fluid followed by open fenestration and evacuation of multiple daughter cysts and laminated endocyst membrane.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old female was referred to an allergy and clinical immunology unit for evaluation of severe, refractory atopic dermatitis. Since early infancy, she had suffered from perennial eczematous skin lesions accompanied by asthma, both experiencing seasonal exacerbations in the spring and autumn.

differentials.candidate: Refractory atopic dermatitis with aeroallergen (dust mite) sensitization
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary cause of her perennial dermatitis flares since early childhood, but strict environmental remediation that successfully resolved her asthma produced no improvement in her dermatitis, which worsened despite topical and oral corticosteroid therapies.

Considered given positive skin prick tests to hen's egg, cow's milk, and tomato in infancy, but complete elimination of these dietary triggers from her diet failed to induce remission of her cutaneous lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the discovery of unexplained peripheral eosinophilia (14.4%) prompting serologic investigation for parasitic helminthiasis, revealing markedly elevated parasite-specific IgE (32.50 kU/L), followed by complete resolution of eczema and marked reduction in eosinophilia and specific IgE after anthelmintic therapy with mebendazole.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male resident of Brasília, Federal District, Brazil, presented to the clinic with an erythematous plaque on his nose. The lesion had developed approximately one month prior, following a recreational fishing trip in the state of Amazonas, Brazil.

differentials.candidate: HIV-Associated Opportunistic Cutaneous Infection / Kaposi Sarcoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the atypical, non-healing facial plaque and concern for underlying cellular immunodeficiency leading to anergic cutaneous presentations; ruled out by non-reactive serologic testing.

differentials.candidate: Deep Fungal Granulomatous Infection (e.g., Paracoccidioidomycosis or Sporotrichosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Endemic Amazonian exposure and chronic facial plaques strongly mimic deep fungal granulomas; excluded by microscopic biopsy demonstrating vacuolated histiocytes filled with characteristic protozoan amastigotes rather than fungal spores or yeasts.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was established by positive skin biopsy smears, culture isolation on McNeal, Novy & Nicolle medium, and molecular ITS1 PCR-RFLP identifying Leishmania amazonensis.

clinical_summary: A 78-year-old woman with advanced gastric cancer and multiple lymph node metastases, receiving second-line weekly paclitaxel monotherapy, presented with high fever and altered sensorium. Four days prior, she had presented to the outpatient department with a temperature of 38.0°C; at that time, physical examination, complete blood count, serum chemistries, urinalysis, and blood cultures showed no significant findings, and she was...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary cause of fever on admission given the new right upper lobe pulmonary infiltrate on chest CT, prompting empiric piperacillin/tazobactam therapy; however, despite transient fever reduction, progressive delirium, drowsiness, and communicative hydrocephalus supervened.

In the setting of advanced metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis was suspected when ventricular enlargement, periventricular edema, and mononuclear pleocytosis appeared; ruled out by serial negative cerebrospinal fluid cytologies and lack of response to dexamethasone.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was reached when progressive hydrocephalus, mixed pleocytosis, and profound hypoglycorrhachia led to molecular confirmation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis by positive PCR in both cerebrospinal fluid and sputum.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old child from a rural area of southeast Rajasthan presented with a progressive history of headache, occasional vomiting, decreased visual acuity, and right-sided hemiparesis. The family reported domestic contact with pet dogs.

differentials.candidate: Intracranial Cystic Neoplasm (e.g., Low-Grade Cystic Astrocytoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect given the focal neurological deficit, hemiparesis, papilledema, and intracranial space-occupying lesion in a child; parasitic cysts constitute only a tiny fraction of operated cerebral mass lesions.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated Visceral Hydatidosis with Brain Metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cerebral hydatid involvement usually occurs secondary to primary filter organ infestation in the liver or lungs; excluded by normal systemic screening examinations.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis of intracranial hydatid disease was established upon complete neurosurgical extirpation of the intact parasitic cyst using rupture-preventing techniques, followed by prolonged adjuvant albendazole therapy.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old female of Marshallese origin who emigrated to the United States five years prior and resided in crowded living conditions presented to the emergency department with nausea, persistent nonbloody nonbilious vomiting, and abdominal pain.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially presumed to be post-viral gastroparesis with mild pancreatitis; ruled out by rapid recurrence of severe vomiting, worsening renal failure, and subsequent surgical demonstration of mesenteroaxial gastric volvulus.

Strongly suspected due to chronic cough, weight loss, pulmonary infiltrates, and acid-fast bacilli observed in sputum and initial culture; ruled out when species-specific PCR testing of sputum and skin was negative for M. tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when skin biopsies demonstrated abundant acid-fast bacilli within histiocytes consistent with lepromatous leprosy, confirmed definitively by positive M. leprae PCR at the National Hansen's Disease Center.

clinical_summary: A 5-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented with a right groin mass present for two months and progressive abdominal distension for 15 days, accompanied by occasional periumbilical pain, vomiting, and diarrhea.

differentials.candidate: Pancreatic / Peritoneal Malignancy (e.g., Pancreatoblastoma or Peritoneal Carcinomatosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Raised as the foremost concern due to the combination of a pancreatic mass lesion, ductal dilatation, massive ascites, cachexia, and a markedly elevated CA-125 level (484.5 U/mL); excluded by diagnostic paracentesis and surgical exploration which demonstrated inflammatory exudate without malignant cells.

Massive peritoneal fluid collection accompanied by bowel wall thickening and elevated inflammatory markers suggested secondary bacterial peritonitis complicating pancreatitis; excluded by sterile ascites cultures.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative non-invasive immunological testing (serum anti-TB antibody, tuberculin skin test, and interferon-gamma release assay), laparoscopic biopsy of the abdominal mass yielded tissue that was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA by polymerase chain reaction.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old female resident of Sri Lanka presented with persistent fever, chills, and rigors of two weeks' duration, accompanied by generalized malaise and anorexia. She had a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus managed on oral hypoglycemic agents, with good glycemic control (fasting blood glucose 112 mg/dL, HbA1c 5.7%).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered during initial evaluation given two weeks of high unremitting fevers with chills and rigors in a diabetic patient; excluded by the absence of murmurs, absence of peripheral vascular or immunologic stigmata, and lack of typical endocardial organisms.

When deep musculoskeletal pain, sacroiliitis, and a massive iliopsoas collection developed, chronic zoonotic and mycobacterial infections endemic to the region were considered; ruled out by negative tuberculin skin testing, normal chest radiography, negative Brucella antibodies, and lack of mycobacterial growth in drained abscess fluid.

Initial automated blood culture bottle flagged positive for B. cepacia on day three, but colony morphology, bipolar Gram staining, intrinsic aminoglycoside resistance, and molecular testing overturned this initial identification.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis was confirmed when the bloodstream isolate demonstrated bipolar staining slender Gram-negative rods with resistance to gentamicin and susceptibility to ceftazidime/meropenem, accompanied by an IgM antibody titer of 1:640 and positive Burkholderia pseudomallei PCR.

clinical_summary: A 73-year-old male born in Tanzania, who immigrated to Canada in the 1970s without prior BCG vaccination and had traveled extensively, presented for evaluation of chronic lower extremity skin lesions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the working diagnosis given 16 years of negative exhaustive evaluations and apparent therapeutic failure following a 9-month course of single-agent isoniazid; however, single-agent monotherapy is inadequate for erythema induratum, and robust immunological reactivity to specific mycobacterial antigens was later demonstrated.

Considered because chronic lower extremity edema and nodularity in an older individual can represent stasis microangiopathy, supported by an initial superficial punch biopsy; however, prior deeper histological examination demonstrated true subcutaneous granulomatous lobular panniculitis.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic pivot occurred when interferon-gamma release assay (QuantiFERON-TB Gold) returned strongly positive (>10 IU/mL), establishing Mycobacterium tuberculosis sensitization and leading to curative quadruple anti-tubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented with a seven-month history of a painful, progressive swelling of her left foot. Physical examination revealed an indurated tumefaction involving the soft tissues of the left foot with multiple cutaneous fistulous tracts discharging purulent exudate containing macroscopic granular material.

differentials.candidate: Chronic Bacterial Osteomyelitis with Cutaneous Fistulization
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the chronic suppurative presentation with purulent drainage and fistulous tracts in the foot; ruled out by plain radiographs demonstrating completely normal bone architecture without sequestrum or cortical destruction.

Mycetoma is etiologically classified into actinomycotic (bacterial, caused by aerobic actinomycetes) and eumycotic (fungal) forms; actinomycotic infection was excluded by direct microscopy of the extruded grains, which showed thick fungal structures rather than thin bacterial branching filaments.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic pivot was achieved by combining the pathognomonic clinical triad (tumefaction, sinuses, and granules) with direct microscopic demonstration of fungal hyphae within the black grains, confirming eumycetoma (Madura foot) successfully managed with surgical debridement and prolonged ketoconazole.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old man presented to the surgical emergency department with acute obstipation, diffuse abdominal pain, progressive abdominal distension, and vomiting. One year prior while residing in Egypt, he had received antiparasitic treatment for an endemic intestinal helminthic infection, but no confirmatory post-treatment follow-up investigations had been performed to verify cure.

differentials.candidate: Mechanical Intestinal Obstruction (e.g., Adhesive Bands, Internal Hernia, or Volvulus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary admitting diagnosis given absolute constipation, persistent vomiting, severe distension, absent bowel sounds, collapsed rectum, and dilated bowel loops on CT; however, exploratory laparotomy showed adynamic paralytic ileus rather than a mechanical intraluminal or extrinsic mechanical block.

Gangrenous appendicitis with localized peritonitis was identified at surgery, but typical obstructive appendicolith was absent, and mucosal ulceration with transmural gangrene was caused by dense intramural parasite egg embolization.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnosis of appendiceal schistosomiasis causing gangrenous appendicitis was established on histopathological examination of the resected appendix, which revealed transmural necrosis containing multiple viable Schistosoma ova, despite negative postoperative stool microscopy.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old gravida 3 para 1 woman with a medical history of cervical insufficiency, polycystic ovarian syndrome, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, and type 2 diabetes mellitus conceived via frozen embryo transfer in Massachusetts.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Cytomegalovirus and other TORCH pathogens represent the most common infectious etiologies of congenital microcephaly and intracranial vasculopathy; excluded by documented maternal rubella immunity, negative TORCH maternal panels, and negative neonatal CMV testing.

differentials.candidate: In Vitro Fertilization / Cryopreserved Embryo Viral Contamination
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a potential vector for transmission during assisted reproduction; however, epidemiologic investigation confirmed that the embryo had been cryopreserved in 2013, two years prior to the regional epidemic outbreak.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative neonatal serum and urine RT-PCR and IgM testing, the diagnosis of congenital Zika syndrome was definitively confirmed when reference testing at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention detected viral RNA across all submitted placental specimens, pointing to sexual transmission from the traveling spouse.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presented to a referral hospital in Uganda with a 2-week history of headache with fevers and a 1-day history of confusion.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In an HIV-infected patient presenting with subacute headache, fevers, and meningismus, cryptococcal meningitis is a primary opportunistic etiology, but was definitively excluded by a negative lateral flow cryptococcal antigen assay.

Acute confusion, tachypnea, rigors, and meningismus prompted initial empiric coverage with high-dose ceftriaxone, but was ruled out following CSF analysis and molecular confirmation of mycobacterial infection, leading to cessation of antibacterial therapy.

Rigors, fever, and confusion in an endemic area suggested cerebral malaria, but an initial antigen-based rapid diagnostic test was negative, and CSF parameters demonstrated marked pleocytosis and hyperproteinorachia indicative of intracranial inflammation rather than isolated parasitic sequestration.

diagnostic_pivot: The patient had dual central nervous system and systemic parasitic co-infection: lumbar puncture demonstrated elevated opening pressure (33 cm CSF), pleocytosis (590 WBC/µL), and elevated protein (419 mg/dL), with Mycobacterium tuberculosis confirmed on CSF Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra; persistent spiking fevers (39.6°C) and tachycardia prompted blood microscopy that revealed Plasmodium falciparum trophozoites, confirming severe malaria co-infection.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old woman with no prior psychiatric history presented to the emergency department with an acute onset of psychotic symptoms, including paranoid delusions, psychomotor agitation, and initial insomnia. She harbored persecutory beliefs that her sister had practiced witchcraft against her and that her boyfriend was unfaithful.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute agitation and persecutory delusions in a young adult frequently stem from illicit drug ingestion or toxin exposure, but the patient had no drug use history and urine toxicology was completely negative.

differentials.candidate: Organic intracranial lesion or intracranial tuberculoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: New-onset psychiatric symptoms can be heralded by space-occupying intracranial lesions, encephalitis, or secondary central nervous system complications of pleural infection, but unenhanced head CT showed no structural abnormality.

differentials.candidate: Primary psychotic disorder (schizophreniform or brief psychotic disorder)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A first-break psychiatric illness was considered, but the acute onset temporally linked to new antimicrobial therapy, absence of prior psychiatric history, and rapid complete remission following drug discontinuation argued against a primary psychotic disorder.

diagnostic_pivot: Drug-induced psychosis secondary to isoniazid neurotoxicity during treatment for pleural tuberculosis was confirmed by the acute onset four days after drug initiation, rapid remission within seven days of discontinuing isoniazid, and uneventful sequential re-introduction of rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol while permanently omitting isoniazid.

clinical_summary: A patient presented for evaluation following the recent development of symptomatic cholelithiasis. Physical examination was unremarkable, with no localized abdominal tenderness or jaundice.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple developmental cysts of the liver are typically non-calcified with imperceptible walls, whereas this lesion had well-defined borders with minimal peripheral calcifications.
The patient experienced symptoms attributed to gallstones, but ultrasound and clinical exam showed no wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, or signs of acute inflammation.

diagnostic_pivot: Cross-sectional imaging identified a well-defined 5 x 4.5 cm hepatic segment VI cystic mass with peripheral calcifications classified as Gharbi stage II, confirming hepatic echinococcosis (hydatid cyst) coexisting with cholelithiasis, which was directly confirmed on laparoscopic visualization.

clinical_summary: A patient presented for laparoscopic surgical management of a cystic lesion located on the diaphragmatic surface of the liver and concurrent planned gallbladder intervention. During initial laparoscopy, the cystic structure on the hepatic surface was identified and prepared for operative intervention, with placement of hypertonic saline-soaked protective gauze across the diaphragmatic surface to guard against fluid extravasation prior to needle...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple cysts do not contain internal germinative layers, daughter vesicles, or parasitic debris, whereas endocyst inspection confirmed internal cystic elements requiring partial pericystectomy.
Neoplastic mucinous lesions require complete oncologic capsule resection rather than scolicidal decompression and partial pericystectomy.

diagnostic_pivot: Intraoperative needle aspiration of cystic fluid followed by direct laparoscopic exploration of the cavity identified characteristic intracystic elements confirming hepatic hydatid disease (echinococcosis), managed definitively via 10% hypertonic saline instillation, partial pericystectomy, and concurrent cholecystectomy.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female worker from south-central China presented with a 1-year history of recurrent cutaneous nodules distributed over almost her entire body. The illness began as a single dark-red nodule on the left shoulder that progressed to painful ulceration and weeping, followed by widespread erythema, nodules, erosions, recurrent fevers with temperatures reaching 41°C, and polyarthralgia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to painful ulcerating subcutaneous nodules, atrophic scarring, fevers, arthralgias, and positive anticardiolipin antibodies, but ruled out by hypesthesia on the lower extremities, lateral eyebrow alopecia, and heavily bacillary slit-skin smears.

Thought to explain the tender, relapsing lobular-appearing inflammatory skin nodules, but does not account for peripheral sensory deficits, madarosis, or occlusive vasculopathy secondary to mycobacterial invasion.

diagnostic_pivot: The demonstration of a 4+ bacteriological index on slit-skin smears, and biopsy showing necrotizing thrombotic vasculopathy with intracellular acid-fast bacilli exhibiting 100% 16S rRNA gene sequence homology to Mycobacterium leprae established diffuse multibacillary leprosy with Lucio's phenomenon.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old previously healthy girl presented to a pediatric hospital in Houston, Texas, in the spring of 2017 with acute febrile illness. Four days later (day 5), her twin brother presented with an identical febrile illness.

differentials.candidate: Arboviral infection (e.g., West Nile virus, Dengue)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Recent mosquito exposure in Houston, Texas, raised concern for locally acquired mosquito-borne viral infections, but symptoms followed a relapse timeline months after travel and were confirmed by intraerythrocytic parasite detection.

differentials.candidate: Locally acquired / autochthonous Plasmodium falciparum malaria
differentials.rule_out_reason: Emergence of febrile illnesses in multiple family members in Texas raised suspicion of local vector transmission, but origin from northern Afghanistan and delayed presentation 6 to 10.5 months post-resettlement reflected delayed relapses of dormant hypnozoites rather than local transmission.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of peripheral blood smears confirmed intraerythrocytic parasites consistent with Plasmodium vivax malaria across all six related family members, successfully treated initially with atovaquone/proguanil followed by primaquine hypnozoite eradication.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old woman with a history of diabetes mellitus, who had been non-compliant with insulin therapy for six months, presented to the emergency department with a 1-week history of fever with rigors, vomiting, headache, bilateral leg pain, and myalgias, as well as urinary incontinence for the preceding three days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to right costovertebral angle fullness and tenderness, fever, vomiting, and urinary incontinence in an uncontrolled diabetic, but urine microscopy showed no pyuria, blood and urine cultures were sterile, and fevers failed to respond to broad-spectrum beta-lactams or carbapenems.
Acute fever with rigors, prostration, and myalgias in a tropical region suggested malaria, but peripheral blood smears were repeatedly negative.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical constellation of persistent high fever, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and elevated transaminases prompted suspicion of rickettsial infection; initiation of doxycycline produced prompt defervescence, and serology returned strongly positive on Scrub Typhus Detect IgM (OD 1.732, cut-off <0.500).

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old previously healthy male was admitted to a tertiary hospital with a 1-month history of progressive dyspnea, cough, and fever. His symptoms began with low-grade fever, dry cough, and night sweats.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High-virulence bacteria causing cavitary pneumonia were suspected, but the patient failed an initial 10-day antibiotic regimen as well as four days of inpatient meropenem, ciprofloxacin, and vancomycin.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune systemic vasculitis / collagen vascular disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute cavitating pulmonary consolidation with night sweats and elevated CRP raised consideration of autoimmune pulmonary disease, but antinuclear antibody testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: While initial bronchoalveolar lavage at an outside hospital was negative, persistence of cavitary necrosis, temporary steroid responsiveness, and recurrence of fevers prompted a repeat bronchoscopy that demonstrated acid-fast bacilli on smear and positive PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, leading to complete recovery on antituberculous therapy.

clinical_summary: An 87-year-old man of Chinese descent with a past medical history of diabetes mellitus and ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with a 1-week history of productive cough with green sputum and dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially diagnosed based on positive pneumococcal urinary antigen, but the patient progressively deteriorated with somnolence and hypoxemia despite escalating ceftriaxone and adding vancomycin.

differentials.candidate: Acute decompensated heart failure / cardiogenic pulmonary edema
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given his history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and worsening bilateral pulmonary opacities, cardiogenic pulmonary edema was considered, but aggressive diuresis did not improve his oxygenation or clinical trajectory.

diagnostic_pivot: Apical consolidations and a calcified granuloma in an immigrant from an endemic region represented unrecognized active tuberculosis coinfection; following acute decompensation, bronchoalveolar lavage demonstrated acid-fast bacilli that speciated as Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old male farmer presented to an infectious diseases outpatient clinic in Ceará State, Northeastern Brazil, complaining of a chronic, painful oral lesion that had been progressing over the preceding three years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A leading cause of chronic destructive mucosal ulceration in rural South America, but ruled out by direct cytological examination of palatal imprints which showed yeast structures and no Leishmania amastigotes.

A chronic destructive, infiltrative hard palate mass in an elderly male with a 40 pack-year smoking history strongly suggested malignant neoplasm, but biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation and fungal yeasts rather than neoplastic epithelial dysplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Cytological and histopathological evaluation of the hard palate lesion demonstrated multi-sized yeast forms, and panfungal PCR (ITS1/ITS4) with sequencing confirmed 98.8% homology to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, accompanied by positive double radial immunodiffusion, confirming autochthonous paracoccidioidomycosis in an emerging geographic zone.

clinical_summary: A 70-year-old male presents for evaluation of painful, eruptive cutaneous lesions on his upper extremities, accompanied by fever and marked constitutional decline. One month prior to admission, he had initiated a multi-agent antimicrobial regimen for a microbiologically documented chronic lower respiratory tract infection, but he halted the therapy upon the emergence of the skin eruptions.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Direct microscopic examination of the eruptive skin lesions was negative for acid-fast organisms.

differentials.candidate: HIV-Associated Opportunistic Vascular Proliferation / Epidemic Kaposi's Sarcoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Retroviral and viral hepatitis serologies were negative, establishing an immunocompetent classic disease presentation.

diagnostic_pivot: Cutaneous punch biopsy revealed spindle and vascular cell proliferation with extravasated erythrocytes, confirming Kaposi's sarcoma developing concomitantly with pulmonary tuberculosis, which responded favorably to resumption of antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old male presents to a dental clinic complaining of painful, progressive oral lesions of two months' duration. He describes marked constitutional symptoms, including significant unintentional weight loss and asthenia over the preceding three months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Specific polyclonal immunohistochemical reactivity against Paracoccidioides brasiliensis was negative in the biopsied granulomatous tissue.
Immunohistochemical evaluation with polyclonal antibodies directed against Leishmania spp. was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Initial sputum smear positivity confirmed underlying pulmonary tuberculosis, and subsequent incisional oral biopsy with special fungal staining (PAS and GMS) confirmed concurrent opportunistic oral histoplasmosis.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old non-smoking female presents with a two-week history of new-onset cough and sputum production. Four months earlier, she was admitted to a community hospital with polypnea, cough, sputum, and intermittent fevers, where chest CT demonstrated a right pleural effusion and pleural thickening.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Serum tumor markers were normal and CT-guided percutaneous biopsy demonstrated benign inflammatory cellular infiltration rather than malignant neoplasia.
Serum fungal biomarker assays, including galactomannan (GM-test) and (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (G-test), were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Initial resolution of tuberculous pleuritis coupled with positive immune reactivity assays and biopsy demonstrating epithelioid-lymphocytic infiltration established a paradoxical reaction resolving on continued antitubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old female presents for scheduled pulmonary follow-up. Six months earlier, during a routine physical examination at a local hospital, asymptomatic pulmonary infiltrates were discovered, and she was started on a standard four-drug oral antimicrobial regimen.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pulmonary Neoplasm / Solitary Nodule Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Serum tumor markers were normal and histopathologic examination of the biopsied nodule demonstrated granulomatous inflammation without malignancy.
Fungal antigen assays, including galactomannan (GM-test) and (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (G-test), were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive cell-mediated immune assays and CT-guided lung core biopsy demonstrating a tuberculous granuloma confirmed a paradoxical reaction, which regressed under continued anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old male construction worker residing in northeastern Iran presents to a cardiology clinic complaining of palpitations for two weeks, accompanied by intermittent atypical chest pain that is neither positional nor exertional.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a discrete, thick-walled intramyocardial cystic lesion embedded in the interventricular septum rather than isolated diffuse myocarditis.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated Visceral Hydatid Disease with Secondary Cardiac Involvement
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cross-sectional computed tomography of the chest and abdomen confirmed isolated cardiac involvement without hepatic or pulmonary lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical resection of the interventricular septal cyst via cardiopulmonary bypass and histological examination revealing protoscolices and classic three-layered cyst architecture confirmed cardiac hydatidosis.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male expatriate who lived his entire life in Malawi and relocated to Johannesburg one year ago presents with a four-month history of progressive, non-tender nodules on his face and trunk that have caused him significant social distress.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Physical examination demonstrated bilateral peripheral nerve thickening, and histological evaluation showed spindle cells packed with acid-fast bacilli rather than benign fibrohistiocytic proliferation.
The patient presented de novo with no prior diagnosis, personal contact with infected individuals, or prior treatment.

diagnostic_pivot: Bilateral earlobe slit skin smears demonstrated a high bacterial index, and nodule biopsy revealed intertwining spindle cells teeming with acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, confirming de novo histoid leprosy.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old male with a 35-year history of heavy tobacco and alcohol use presents to the emergency department complaining of dry cough and progressive dyspnea. He has worked for most of his life in rural agricultural activities in Brazil and regularly chewed on raw vegetation while working in the fields.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Microscopic examination for acid-fast bacilli was negative across three consecutive sputum specimens.

differentials.candidate: Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Pulmonary Metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Hard palate mucosal biopsy demonstrated granulomatous infectious inflammation rather than malignant epithelial cells.

diagnostic_pivot: The clinical presence of moriform palatal lesions in a rural laborer coupled with characteristic perihilar pulmonary infiltrates and histopathologic confirmation of typical yeast forms established paracoccidioidomycosis.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old female presents to a hospital in Jakarta, Indonesia with a seven-month history of progressive quadriparesis. Her symptoms began insidiously with mild, dull neck pain, followed by ascending paresthesias and progressive weakness affecting all four extremities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic infections produce rapid acute disc destruction and septic collapse, whereas this patient showed an indolent 7-month subligamentous osteolytic process across 14 contiguous vertebral segments.

Radiographic and cross-sectional imaging showed anterior vertebral body destruction with massive contiguous paravertebral cold abscesses rather than isolated pedicular osteolysis or neoplastic marrow infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: The classic neuroimaging constellation of extensive contiguous anterior vertebral destruction with bilateral paravertebral abscesses was highly typical of spinal tuberculosis, which achieved neurological recovery and bony bridging under targeted antitubercular chemotherapy and surgical decompression.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old female presents to an outpatient department in rural India complaining of the acute onset of severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain. She has no significant past medical history and denies chronic fever, cough, night sweats, or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: While acute appendicitis was the initial pre-operative clinical diagnosis, histological examination of the resected appendix revealed caseating epithelioid granulomas rather than pyogenic phlegmonous inflammation.
Granulomas in Crohn's disease are non-caseating, whereas microscopic examination revealed caseous necrosis that achieved curative remission on antitubercular therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Appendectomy followed by histopathological examination revealing poorly formed epithelioid cell granulomas with caseous necrosis in the serosa confirmed tubercular appendicitis, which responded well to a 9-month antitubercular regimen.

clinical_summary: A 78-year-old male, originally from China and residing in the United States for several years without recent international travel, presents with acute confusion, urinary incontinence, poor oral intake, and profound weakness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Emergency non-contrast head CT excluded acute cerebral infarction or hemorrhage, confirming that the neurological decline represented recrudescence of prior deficits induced by systemic sepsis.

Although Klebsiella pneumoniae was isolated from blood and abscess fluid, serum serological testing demonstrated positive antibodies confirming an underlying amoebic cavity with superimposed bacterial infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Detection of serum Entamoeba histolytica antibodies via ELISA in a patient with a cystic liver lesion complicated by secondary bacterial bacteremia established bacterial superinfection of an amoebic liver abscess, successfully treated with dual therapy.

clinical_summary: A 51-year-old Vietnamese female, who migrated to the United States at age 25, presented to the clinic with new indurated, tender skin lesions, worsening extremity pain, and bilateral lower extremity edema.

differentials.candidate: Persistent or Relapsing Active Mycobacterial Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the eruption of new indurated tender skin lesions, fever, and 30-lb weight loss after defaulting from follow-up; ruled out by histopathologic comparison with her prior biopsy, which demonstrated diminished inflammatory infiltrates and degenerating bacilli indicative of response to therapy rather than active mycobacterial multiplication.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Bacterial or Fungal Panniculitis / Soft-Tissue Superinfection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the tender erythematous subcutaneous nodules, fever, and neutrophilic leukocytosis in a patient previously on immunosuppressive therapy; excluded by sterile fungal and bacterial tissue cultures.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Type 2 Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum) in Lepromatous Leprosy
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 4-mm punch biopsy revealed dermal foamy macrophages with an intense neutrophilic infiltrate extending into subcutaneous fat, perivascular mixed inflammation with fibrinoid necrosis, and degenerating beaded acid-fast bacilli in histiocytes and cutaneous nerve twigs, confirming a Type 2 immunological reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum), which responded promptly to thalidomide.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old female originally from Ethiopia presented to the emergency department with progressive dyspnea on exertion and right-sided chest pain over the preceding several weeks. Her medical history was significant for unexplained end-stage renal disease diagnosed several months earlier, managed with maintenance hemodialysis in Ethiopia, India, and subsequently the United States.

differentials.candidate: Malignant Lymphoma / Paraneoplastic Humoral Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered due to subcarinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, exudative pleural effusion, and markedly elevated serum PTHrP; ruled out by absence of malignant cells on pleural fluid cytology, normal peripheral blood flow cytometry, and negative serum leukemia/lymphoma panel.
Considered in an ESRD patient presenting with acute-on-chronic dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain; definitively excluded by repeated negative chest CT angiography.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis with Hypercalcemia and Elevated PTHrP
differentials.rule_out_reason: Mediastinoscopy with excisional lymph node biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomas, and pleural biopsy culture yielded Mycobacterium tuberculosis; initiating weight-based anti-tubercular therapy normalized PTHrP to 35 pg/mL, resolved serum hypercalcemia, and achieved clinical recovery.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old male farmer residing in Chennai, South India, presented with severe pain in his left elbow followed by bilateral knee and right ankle pain for the past 3 months, accompanied by intermittent fevers over the preceding 10 days.

differentials.candidate: Primary Staphylococcus aureus Septic Arthritis and Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the purulent presentation and initial operative pus culture from the left elbow growing S. aureus; ruled out as the primary driving etiology because the patient experienced clinical failure and recurrence of multifocal symptoms despite two weeks of intravenous cefoperazone-sulbactam therapy.
Considered due to fever, bacteremia concern, and multifocal osteoarticular seeding in a diabetic patient; ruled out by normal transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Melioidosis Causing Multifocal Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: In the setting of occupational soil exposure and uncontrolled diabetes, non-improvement prompted bilateral knee and ankle arthrotomies, where intra-articular pus collections yielded positive PCR for Burkholderia pseudomallei and serial blood cultures grew Gram-negative bacilli with characteristic bipolar staining, confirming melioidosis; high-dose intravenous ceftazidime followed by 6 months of oral co-trimoxazole achieved full clinical cure.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old woman (gravida 3, para 2, abortus 1) at 39 weeks of gestation was admitted in active labor to the department of gynecology of a field hospital deployed in South Sudan.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the acute onset of high fever, rigors, and chills occurring within 24 hours of vaginal delivery; ruled out by normal maternal C-reactive protein (5.2 mg/L) and sterile blood and urine cultures.

Considered in light of maternal fever during delivery and isolated neonatal thrombocytopenia (platelets 72,000/µL); ruled out by the newborn's vigorous clinical state, normal physical examination, and normal CRP (<5 mg/L).

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Maternal and Congenital Falciparum Malaria
differentials.rule_out_reason: Maternal peripheral blood smear demonstrated Plasmodium falciparum ring forms with 4% parasitemia; subsequent surveillance thick and thin blood films in the infant at day 3 confirmed congenital transmission with P. falciparum trophozoites at 1.5% parasitemia, leading to parasitological clearance following artemether-lumefantrine and chloroquine therapy.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male, who worked as a recycler and had a history of heavy smoking and alcohol consumption without known medical comorbidities, was referred to the neurosurgery division following a single epileptic seizure 1 week prior to admission, followed by progressive right-sided weakness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis due to severe dental neglect and solitary rim-enhancing brain mass with edema; ruled out by lesion progression despite 40 days of empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy (ceftazidime, metronidazole, and vancomycin) and histological absence of pyogenic bacterial suppuration.

Considered given an aggressive, expanding solitary intra-axial hemispheric mass with mass effect and subfalcine herniation in a chronic smoker; ruled out by histopathological evaluation of the resected mass demonstrating chronic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and fungal organisms rather than neoplastic glial proliferation.

Complete micro-surgical resection of the recurrent 3-cm lesion and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) staining revealed characteristic yeast cells displaying peripheral budding resembling a 'ship's wheel' and 'Mickey Mouse ears', confirming Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infection in the absence of systemic lesions; the patient achieved substantial neurological recovery following discontinuation of antibiotics and initiation of oral itraconazole.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old previously healthy boy presented with high fever, headache, generalized body aches, and retro-orbital pain for 5 days. On day 3 of fever, an outpatient complete blood count had revealed a white blood cell count of 5.7 x 10^3/µL and a platelet count of 170 x 10^3/µL.

differentials.candidate: Primary Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP) / Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when profound thrombocytopenia persisted for over 12 months with cutaneous purpura; ruled out as primary autoimmune disease by negative antinuclear antibodies, negative anti-double-stranded DNA, negative antiphospholipid antibodies, and normal complement and immunoglobulin profiles, confirming secondary post-infectious pathogenesis.

Considered due to severe persistent refractory thrombocytopenia requiring long-term evaluation; ruled out by normal peripheral blood cell morphology and a normal bone marrow examination with preserved megakaryopoiesis and absence of dysplasia or blast cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever with Post-Infectious Chronic ITP
differentials.rule_out_reason: The acute presentation of retro-orbital pain, hemoconcentration, polyserositis (pleural effusion, gallbladder thickening), and severe thrombocytopenia was confirmed by positive NS1 antigen and seroconversion with positive IgM and IgG on day 7; cross-reactive post-infectious immune destruction led to chronic immune thrombocytopenic purpura successfully managed with corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old female presented with progressively worsening bilateral headaches over the preceding year, accompanied by vertigo and intermittent nausea. The headaches were characteristically worse at night and upon awakening in the morning, gradually improving throughout the day.

differentials.candidate: Intraventricular Brain Neoplasm (Ependymoma / Colloid Cyst / Subependymoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary etiology for fourth ventricular obstruction causing non-communicating hydrocephalus in a young adult; ruled out by magnetic resonance imaging demonstrating a cystic structure containing an internal linear enhancement/parasitic larva, and operative pathology confirming non-neoplastic parasitic larval tissue.
Considered given the patient's immigration background and chronic hydrocephalic presentation; ruled out by negative testing for tuberculosis infection.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Intraventricular Neurocysticercosis with Obstructive Hydrocephalus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Neuroimaging visualized a lobulated fourth ventricular cyst containing a visible larva, and surgical suboccipital craniotomy with en bloc resection demonstrated a mature Taenia solium plerocercoid larva measuring 1.2 x 0.5 x 0.2 cm encased within a gelatinous cystic membrane; endoscopic third ventriculostomy combined with albendazole and praziquantel led to full symptomatic cure.

clinical_summary: A 30-year-old female presented to the emergency department with approximately ten episodes of profuse watery diarrhea and four episodes of vomiting over the preceding 24 hours. She had consumed fried seafood one day before the onset of symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to seafood consumption, yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies on TCBS agar, and marked gas production in carbohydrate fermentation and triple sugar iron agar; definitively ruled out by species-specific PCR which was negative for V. furnissii and 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrating 99% sequence identity to V. cholerae.

differentials.candidate: Invasive Enteric Bacterial Infection (Shigellosis / Salmonellosis / Campylobacteriosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given marked leukocytosis (WBC 15,400 cells/cumm) and rapid dehydration with prerenal azotemia; ruled out by absence of abdominal cramps, absence of fever, non-purulent macroscopic stool characteristics, and negative blood cultures.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Novel Gas-Producing Vibrio cholerae Gastroenteritis with Acute Kidney Injury
differentials.rule_out_reason: Microscopic examination by hanging drop demonstrated darting motility, and although carbohydrate fermentation showed atypical gas production, 16S rRNA sequencing, species-specific PCR, and slide agglutination confirmed Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1, biovar El Tor, serotype Ogawa; rehydration and ciprofloxacin led to full clinical recovery and normalization of renal function within 3 days.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male farmer presented to the neurology outpatient department in northern India with progressive weakness involving all four extremities over the preceding 15 days. Approximately 1 week prior to the onset of weakness, he had experienced an episode of fever with flu-like symptoms that subsided with antipyretic therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial provisional diagnosis due to acute post-febrile weakness affecting all four limbs preceded 1 week earlier by flu-like illness; ruled out by the presence of chronic hypopigmented anesthetic skin patches and demonstration of mycobacterial dermatoneuropathy on slit-skin sampling rather than acute autoimmune demyelinating polyradiculopathy.

Considered because the patient had been taking dapsone for 6 months as part of multi-agent therapy; ruled out as the primary etiology for the patient's acute presentations given the persistence of viable acid-fast bacilli on cutaneous smears and coincidental nocturnal filarial parasitemia.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Leprosy Complicated by Asymptomatic Lymphatic Filariasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Six-site slit-skin sampling confirmed short acid-fast bacilli under oil immersion (100x) confirming active leprosy, along with the unexpected incidental demonstration of sheathed microfilariae on earlobe slit smears and nocturnal blood films confirming Wuchereria bancrofti co-infection; the patient was initiated on diethylcarbamazine alongside continued multi-agent leprosy therapy.

clinical_summary: A Filipino male in his 30s presented to an outpatient dermatology clinic in Singapore with a persistent, non-tender, non-pruritic erythematous plaque over his right upper back that had been present for several years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the annular, ring-like configuration of the long-standing plaque on the trunk; ruled out by failure to respond to topical antifungal therapy and physical examination demonstrating an infiltrated plaque completely devoid of epidermal scale.

Considered due to the annular infiltrated non-scaly appearance and generalized monomorphic papules without systemic signs; ruled out by histopathological evaluation demonstrating diffuse superficial dermal histiocytic infiltration without well-formed sarcoidal granulomas or Langhans giant cells.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Borderline Lepromatous Leprosy (Hansen's Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Punch biopsy of the skin lesions revealed Fite-positive acid-fast bacilli within dermal histiocytic infiltrates, and line-probe molecular assay (GenoType LepraeDR) confirmed Mycobacterium leprae DNA without resistance mutations in rpoB, gyrA, or folP1, establishing leprosy in a non-endemic clinical practice setting.

clinical_summary: A male operating theatre assistant in Singapore presents for evaluation of a persistent skin lesion. He originally migrated from a rural region with rice paddy fields to the city for employment.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient exhibited bilateral peripheral ulnar nerve thickening and multiple lesions characteristic of the lepromatous spectrum, classic polar lepromatous leprosy was ruled out by the absence of infiltration and coarsening of facial skin.

differentials.candidate: Known Direct Contact Transmission / Household Exposure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Direct recent contact transmission from a recognized index case was ruled out by detailed epidemiological history, which is common given the prolonged incubation period.

diagnostic_pivot: The cardinal clinical combination of an annular indurated plaque with central sensory impairment and bilateral peripheral nerve thickening established borderline lepromatous leprosy, which demonstrated marked clinical resolution following multi-drug therapy.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old boy from a rural area in Nepal presents with a 1-year history of progressive fullness and pain over the upper abdomen. He reports no fever, jaundice, vomiting, or altered bowel habits.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Ruled out by the chronic one-year duration and total absence of fever, jaundice, systemic toxicity, leukocytosis, or bowel symptoms.
Considered given the initial negative serological screening, but seronegativity is known to occur in intact or thick-walled hydatid cysts, prompting subsequent operative confirmation.

diagnostic_pivot: CT confirmed features favoring hydatid etiology, and definitive confirmation was established during laparotomy by cytological identification of free hooklets in cyst aspirate and histopathology demonstrating a laminated cuticular layer with protoscolices.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital for investigation of progressive abdominal distension associated with non-specific abdominal pain and fever of 2 months' duration that has evolved without clinical improvement.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the multifocal lytic bone lesion and chronic granulomatous inflammation, but ruled out by negative specialized fungal histochemical stains.

differentials.candidate: Primary Calvarial Malignancy / Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the midline frontal lytic lesion with cortical breakthrough and soft tissue component, but skull biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells rather than neoplastic infiltration.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative special stains on the calvarial biopsy, left ankle synovium biopsy was performed and molecular testing by Xpert MTB/RIF definitively detected the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male with moderately controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with exertional breathlessness, cough, right-sided shoulder pain, and unintentional weight loss of 1 month's duration. He reports no anorexia, fevers, or sputum expectoration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Ruled out by detailed occupational history revealing no exposure to avian antigens, poultry, or industrial dusts and chemicals.

Considered in light of miliary nodularity and normal ACE levels, but excluded as the sole diagnosis due to strong tuberculin positivity and necrotizing granulomatous features, confirming dual pathology with tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Transbronchial lung biopsy showed granulomas with Langhans' giant cells and fibrinoid necrosis leading to a diagnosis of miliary tuberculosis, while subsequent paradoxical clinical worsening, development of uveitis, and complete resolution with steroids and methotrexate established concurrent miliary tuberculosis and sarcoidosis.

clinical_summary: A 66-year-old German woman presents to a university hospital otorhinolaryngology clinic with progressive nasal obstruction. Her past medical history is notable for hypothyroidism and rheumatoid arthritis, for which she received continuous immunosuppressive therapy including methotrexate and an anti-TNF-blocker (adalimumab) initiated several years ago.

differentials.candidate: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA) / Autoimmune Midline Destructive Lesion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a primary differential given the patient's known severe autoimmune history (rheumatoid arthritis) and destructive septal ulceration under biologic therapy, but ruled out by histopathology demonstrating intracellular parasites rather than vasculitis.

Distinguished from simple cutaneous recurrence because the patient had previously received definitive treatment for her elbow lesion and now presented with aggressive endonasal mucosal tissue destruction.

diagnostic_pivot: Biopsy of the nasal septal lesion revealed chronic inflammation, necrosis, and intracellular amastigotes, with molecular PCR confirming Leishmania infantum DNA, establishing mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old female presents with a 1-month history of severe left eye pain accompanied by headaches and a 2-week history of progressive reduction of vision in the left eye. Her past history is significant for unexplained weight loss over the past 2 years, remitting and relapsing suppurative cervical masses, anorexia, and postprandial nausea and vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Neuroretinitis with macular star is most commonly caused by Bartonella henselae, but this was excluded by the patient's complete lack of feline contact and negative workup.

differentials.candidate: Ocular Syphilis, Lyme Disease, or Sarcoidosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: These classic infectious and granulomatous causes of neuroretinitis were ruled out by negative FTA-ABS, negative Lyme serology, and normal ACE levels.

diagnostic_pivot: The TB-QuantiFERON Gold assay returned positive while all alternative infectious tests were non-revealing; initiation of quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy produced dramatic systemic healing of suppurative scrofuloderma, weight gain, and complete resolution of optic nerve and retinal swelling.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old male farmer living in a rural area presents for specialist evaluation of a chronic, progressive lesion on his left foot of 3 years' duration. He has a known history of type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with insulin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially considered due to the vesicular presentation, but excluded after failure of topical corticosteroids and progressive evolution into deep chronic fistulas.
Considered due to the patient's underlying insulin-dependent diabetes and disturbed glycemic assessments, but ruled out after complete failure of systemic antibiotic therapy and local wound care.

diagnostic_pivot: Due to the atypical appearance of the chronic fistulizing lesion, dermatological referral was made and deep biopsy histopathology confirmed the presence of Madurella mycetomi grains with severe underlying bony destruction.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old woman presents with deep abdominal pain and epigastric discomfort of nearly 1 month's duration, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She previously completed an empiric course of anti-infective therapy without resolution of symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on cross-sectional CT and MRI showing a peripancreatic mass anterior to the inferior vena cava, but ruled out by completely normal duodenoscopy, negative CA19-9 and other tumor markers, and absence of vascular invasion.
High FDG avidity (SUVmax 9.4 increasing to 12.0) raised suspicion for malignant adenopathy, but the mass showed internal punctate high-density calcific shadows and lacked vascular encasement.

diagnostic_pivot: The benign vascular profile and punctate calcifications on PET-CT combined with a strongly positive tuberculin test established tuberculosis of celiac lymph nodes, which achieved marked shrinkage and symptom resolution following antituberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old Kazakh male presents to the hospital with a 2-month history of right-sided lower back pain and progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness without antecedent trauma. The pain is aggravated by physical activity and partially relieved by rest, with a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain score of 7 out of 10.

differentials.candidate: Spinal Schwannoma / Nerve Sheath Dumbbell Tumor
differentials.rule_out_reason: Dumbbell-shaped extradural masses traversing and enlarging an intervertebral foramen typically represent benign nerve sheath tumors, but surgical exploration revealed a tense, cystic lesion containing a pearly white parasitic endocyst.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Spinal Hydatidosis from Visceral Seeding
differentials.rule_out_reason: Spinal hydatid cysts typically arise secondary to hematogenous dissemination from primary liver or lung echinococcosis, but thorough systemic imaging confirmed isolated primary spinal disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Total operative removal of the pearly translucent endocyst followed by histopathological examination revealing inflammatory granulation tissue, multinucleated giant cells, and the hydatid endocyst germinal layer established primary spinal hydatid cyst disease.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male is referred to an outpatient dermatology clinic with an extensive verrucous plaque and malodorous purulent discharge involving his buttocks, left thigh, and scrotum. The cutaneous condition began two years ago as small, mildly pruritic plaques confined to the buttocks.
