differentials.rule_out_reason: Verrucous plaques following soil contact in tropical plantation workers strongly suggest subcutaneous/deep mycoses, but direct fungal microscopic examination and specialized biopsy stains were negative.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pyogenic Bacterial Infection / Pyoderma Vegetans
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pus culture yielded gram-negative bacteria, but this reflected secondary superficial colonizing flora rather than the primary etiologic pathogen, consistent with past antibiotic failure and presence of caseating granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Sputum GeneXpert molecular testing detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, while cutaneous biopsy demonstrated pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and caseating epithelioid granulomatous inflammation, confirming tuberculosis verrucosa cutis with active pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 26-year-old male farmer with no significant past medical or family history was found dead at home and referred by authorities for forensic evaluation. Family members reported that he had owned and actively managed a large agricultural farm for the preceding 5 years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in unwitnessed sudden death in a young individual, but excluded by comprehensive postmortem toxicological analysis.

differentials.candidate: Atherosclerotic Coronary Artery Disease / Myocardial Infarction
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prodromal history of chest pain and syncope, but ruled out by pristine coronary vasculature and normal left ventricular myocardium.
Considered given the right ventricular intracavitary cystic lesion with potential for outflow tract obstruction or embolization, but refuted by patent pulmonary arteries without luminal occlusion.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the cardiac cystic wall demonstrated the definitive three-layered architecture of a hydatid cyst—fibrous pericyst, laminated acellular ectocyst, and germinative endocyst—confirming cardiac echinococcosis as the cause of fatal arrhythmia.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old Ghanaian woman presented for dermatologic consultation with a 2-year history of an extensive, excruciatingly pruritic papulosquamous eruption. The cutaneous lesions initially began as small papules and vesicles within the web spaces of her fingers and progressively disseminated across her trunk and extremities to involve the entire body.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially managed as contact dermatitis, but ruled out by complete therapeutic failure with topical corticosteroid regimens, worsening hyperkeratotic progression, and transmission of pruritic lesions to household family members.

diagnostic_pivot: Potassium hydroxide preparation and light microscopy of epidermal skin scrapings confirmed crusted (Norwegian) scabies by demonstrating intense mite hyperinfestation with abundant Sarcoptes scabiei mites and viable ova.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old man presented to the hospital with a 4-month history of progressive cough and a 2-month history of exertional polypnea. He was a former smoker with a 60 pack-year history (consuming 30 cigarettes per day for 40 years).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis given the heavy smoking history, elevated CYFRA 21-1, and invasive hilar mass lacking calcification or cavitation; confirmed as coexisting malignancy by peripheral biopsy but excluded as the sole pathology once transbronchial biopsy revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with mycobacterial DNA.

diagnostic_pivot: Transbronchial lung biopsy (TBLB) of the right hilar mass demonstrated chronic necrotizing inflammation, and molecular testing identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA directly within the lesion, establishing active pulmonary tuberculosis coexisting with lung cancer.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old previously healthy man living in Paris presented to the emergency department with the sudden onset of acute psychiatric symptoms—including paranoid delusions, auditory hallucinations, and severe anxiety—accompanied by fever, dry cough, and profound asthenia.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Pulmonary Infection (Pneumocystis jirovecii / Pulmonary Tuberculosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to fever, cough, pulmonary micronodules, and severe CD4 lymphopenia, but excluded by negative microbiological cultures and staining of sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Acute Primary HIV-Induced Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary cause of persistent fever, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, and macrophage activation, but refractory to high-dose intravenous immunoglobulins and antiretroviral therapy, prompting further search for an occult trigger.

differentials.candidate: Viral and Protozoal Co-infections (Viral Hepatitis, Toxoplasmosis, Syphilis, CMV, EBV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as potential etiologies for hepatosplenomegaly and persistent cytopenias in an immunocompromised host, but systematically ruled out by non-reactive serologies and undetectable viral loads.

diagnostic_pivot: Bone marrow trephine biopsy demonstrated definitive hemophagocytosis and revealed intracellular Leishmania spp. amastigotes, further confirmed by positive Leishmania infantum enzyme-linked and Western blot serologies, establishing visceral leishmaniasis as the inciting driver of secondary HLH.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old male originally from Bangladesh presented with a 2-month history of dry cough, intermittent high-grade fevers, and an unintentional weight loss of 17 kg over the same period. His medical history was notable for poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus of 1 year's duration, treated with oral hypoglycemic agents and insulin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to prolonged fever, systemic inflammation, septic monoarthritis, and pulmonary infiltrates consistent with septic emboli, but excluded by normal two-dimensional echocardiography showing no valvular vegetations.

Considered due to the 2-month triad of cough, fever, 17-kg weight loss, and lower lobe pulmonary opacities in a diabetic patient, but superseded by microbiological culture identification of an acute bacterial pathogen.

diagnostic_pivot: Diagnostic ultrasound-guided arthrocentesis of the right knee and simultaneous blood cultures yielded Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming disseminated melioidosis with septic monoarthritis, with whole-body FDG PET/CT further demonstrating multiorgan hypermetabolic involvement.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man residing in Jakarta presented with progressive jaundice preceded by 7 days of nausea, vomiting, and epigastric discomfort. He initially developed an acute flu-like prodrome consisting of fever, chills, severe headache, myalgias, and arthralgias.

differentials.candidate: Isolated Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Hepatitis B
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial working diagnosis based on known HBsAg carriage and positive IgM anti-HBc; however, the disproportionate degree of indirect hyperbilirubinemia (29.06 mg/dL indirect vs 7.0 mg/dL direct), severe thrombocytopenia, and sudden anuric renal failure were atypical for an uncomplicated viral flare alone.
Considered as potential precipitants of acute hepatic decompensation and acute kidney injury, but excluded by non-reactive viral serologies and negative RT-PCR testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Subsequent collateral history revealed travel to an endemic region (Serui, Papua) 4 days prior to symptom onset; rapid diagnostic testing was positive, and peripheral blood smear demonstrated intraerythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum with 12.6% parasitemia, confirming severe falciparum malaria with acute tubular necrosis and hemolytic jaundice.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a 2-month history of right cervical lymph node enlargement and recurrent fevers persisting for over 1 month, accompanied by an erythematous cutaneous rash, lower extremity edema, and painful subcutaneous nodules over both lower legs.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given subacute febrile illness with pulmonary and lymph node involvement in a young adult, but ruled out by negative serum cryptococcal capsular antigen testing.

Considered due to the combination of subacute fevers, cervical lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, and upper-lobe infiltrates with mediastinal adenopathy; however, indeterminate T-SPOT, repeatedly negative conventional cultures, and lack of clinical response to empirical quadruple antituberculous therapy ruled it out as the primary standalone cause.

Considered in a young patient with B symptoms, persistent generalized lymphadenopathy, and high inflammatory markers, but excluded by bone marrow biopsy demonstrating reactive infectious changes without clonal malignant proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Refractory symptoms despite multiple antibacterial and antituberculous courses prompted consideration of endemic dimorphic fungal infection given the prior rodent exposure; targeted qPCR confirmed Talaromyces marneffei (1,798 copies/μL), establishing disseminated talaromycosis with prompt clinical response to liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 31-year-old woman presented to the hospital on postpartum day 6 following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by intrauterine fetal demise (with a nuchal cord). She reported a 5-day history of severe epigastric pain, persistent hiccups, hematemesis of ingested material, right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort, and severe fatigue.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial leading clinical diagnosis given acute right upper quadrant pain, fever history, and cholestatic jaundice; ruled out when abdominal ultrasound demonstrated a normal extrahepatic biliary system and an absence of common bile duct calculi.
Considered due to acute jaundice and postpartum hepatic dysfunction, but excluded by non-reactive viral hepatitis panels.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of stool identified Entamoeba trophozoites, and subsequent abdominal ultrasound demonstrated multiple hypoechoic lesions in the right hepatic lobe consistent with amebic liver abscesses, which completely resolved following targeted metronidazole therapy.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old Indonesian girl presented with a 3-year history of persistent, progressively worsening headaches. Her surgical history was notable for gross total resection of a craniopharyngioma 8 years earlier, complicated by postoperative hydrocephalus requiring placement of a flat-bottom medium-pressure ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt at the right Kocher point.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary preoperative diagnosis supported by surgical history, direct adherence to the shunt catheter tract, elevated relative cerebral blood volume on DSC perfusion MRI, and elevated choline peaks on MRS; definitively ruled out when surgical histopathology demonstrated granulomatous tissue without neoplastic epithelium.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Shunt Infection / Bacterial Brain Abscess / Meningoencephalitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of indwelling ventriculoperitoneal hardware, but excluded by the indolent 3-year afebrile course, absence of nuchal rigidity or neurological signs, normal systemic inflammatory markers, and absence of leptomeningeal inflammation on neuroimaging.

diagnostic_pivot: Right frontotemporal craniotomy and resection of the calcified hardware-associated mass revealed extensive caseating granulomas with epithelioid cells, surrounding lymphocytes, central necrosis with calcification, and Langhans giant cells, establishing an intracranial tuberculoma.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy presented to the pediatric emergency department with a 3-month history of a painless limp in the left lower extremity without fever or trauma. He had no significant past medical history, but epidemiological history revealed regular contact with domestic dogs and sheep in his rural village (Douar) in the Kalaa Sraghna region of Morocco.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a child with a large psoas cystic collection and elevated inflammatory markers, but ruled out by the indolent 3-month clinical course, absence of fever or constitutional symptoms, completely painless hip mobility, and lack of systemic sepsis.

differentials.candidate: Secondary Muscular Seeding from Hepatic Hydatid Cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Muscular hydatid cysts typically arise secondary to rupture or hematogenous dissemination from primary liver cysts, but ultrasound confirmed isolated psoas involvement with completely normal liver parenchyma.

diagnostic_pivot: Pelvic MRI revealed a Gharbi type II cystic lesion with hypointense T1/T2 signal containing a pathognomonic central floating membrane (water-lily sign), and surgical excision confirmed the diagnosis through extraction of the germinative proliferous membrane during pericystectomy.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old overweight female presented to the outpatient dermatology clinic with slightly tender lumps and hyperpigmented depressed scars on both lower legs. Her skin lesions first developed ten years prior as erythematous macules and nodules; some of these lesions subsequently ulcerated and healed leaving firm, hyperpigmented, atrophic scars.

differentials.candidate: Connective Tissue Panniculitis (Morphea Profunda / Lupus Panniculitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 10-year chronicity, prominent subcutaneous fat atrophy causing lower limb asymmetry, and violaceous plaques, but excluded by histopathology lacking collagen sclerosis or mucin deposition and negative direct immunofluorescence.
Considered in a young female with chronic lobular panniculitis and lower extremity ulcers, but ruled out by the absence of vasculitis and the presence of caseating granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Erythema Induratum of Bazin (Tuberculid Panniculitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by granulomatous lobular panniculitis with caseous necrosis, strongly positive tuberculin skin test (20 mm induration), detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA on skin biopsy by GeneXpert MTB/RIF, and positive 99mTc-ethambutol scintigraphy, with complete clinical remission following fixed-dose combination anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 3-month-old boy was brought to a tertiary pediatric clinic with severe malnutrition, failure to thrive, and persistent jaundice. He had previously been diagnosed with neonatal cholestatic jaundice attributed to a congenital viral infection.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Infection with Active Hepatitis / Retinitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to neonatal cholestasis, elevated transaminases, hearing impairment, and positive CMV IgM, but active systemic viral disease was ruled out by negative plasma viral PCR and normal fundoscopy.
Considered given severe failure to thrive, opportunistic pulmonary infection, and depressed CD4 percentage (19%), but ruled out by negative maternal exposure history and non-reactive serology.

Suspected due to positive tuberculin skin test, right upper-middle infiltrates on chest radiography, household exposure to a non-compliant father with drug-resistant disease, and rapid GeneXpert MTB/RIF positivity on gastric aspirate showing rifampicin resistance; confirmed by positive mycobacterial culture and line-probe assays demonstrating resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and second-line injectable agents, with preserved susceptibility to fluoroquinolones.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old girl presented to the pediatric clinic with profound weight loss, fever for one month, and hemoptysis for two days. Family contacts, including both parents, underwent initial screening for chronic respiratory infections and were negative.

differentials.candidate: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection with Opportunistic Pulmonary Cavitary Disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the adolescent presentation with severe wasting/malnutrition, prolonged fever, and apical pulmonary infiltrates with hemoptysis, but excluded by negative HIV screening.
Considered given household risk dynamics, but excluded by comprehensive negative screening of both parents, pinpointing casual/community contact with an infected neighbor.

Confirmed by GeneXpert MTB/RIF showing rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, followed by positive mycobacterial culture and line-probe assays demonstrating resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and second-line injectables, with preserved susceptibility to fluoroquinolones. Subsequent treatment required substituting bedaquiline with linezolid after marked QTc prolongation developed.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old married female, resident of Uttar Pradesh, India, was brought to the emergency department presenting with acute manic symptoms including incessant talking, elated and inappropriate affect, grandiose delusions that she was a goddess, persecutory ideas regarding family members, decreased need for sleep, marked psychomotor agitation, and muttering to herself.

differentials.candidate: Primary Psychiatric Disorder (Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the alternating polarity of a prior perinatal depressive episode followed by florid mania (grandiosity, pressured speech, insomnia), but excluded by new-onset seizures, leukocytosis, and objective psychological testing indicating an organic brain etiology.
Considered as a classic infectious mimic causing mania, psychotic symptoms, cognitive deficits, and seizures, but ruled out by non-reactive serology.

Considered given high endemicity in India, recurrent seizures, and systemic leukocytosis, but ruled out by brain MRI demonstrating cystic lesions with eccentric scolex in the colloidal vesicular and calcified stages rather than thick-walled nodular tuberculomas or neoplasia.

Confirmed by brain MRI displaying multiple bi-hemispheric cerebral and cerebellar cystic lesions with surrounding FLAIR edema, eccentric nodules (scolex) in the colloidal vesicular stage, and subsequent CT showing scattered calcified lesions in the calcified nodular stage, with symptom resolution following anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, steroids, and albendazole.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus presented with a 4-month history of daily, persistent, and progressively worsening pulsulsatile bitemporal headaches accompanied by photophobia, without nausea, vomiting, or phonophobia.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial Subdural Empyema with Calvarial Osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in an immunosuppressed lupus patient presenting with an extra-axial fluid collection and adjacent skull erosion, but ruled out intraoperatively by the absence of frank purulence and sterile bacterial cultures.

Considered given active SLE with malar rash presenting with chronic headache, focal motor deficit, and leptomeningeal enhancement, but excluded by surgical biopsy demonstrating granulomatous fungal infection rather than immune complex pachymeningitis.

Confirmed during craniotomy and dural resection by histopathological demonstration of noncaseating granulomas containing multinucleated giant cells, asteroid bodies, and silver-stain-positive rounded birefringent yeast forms characteristic of Paracoccidioides, leading to complete clinical and radiological recovery on 12 months of oral itraconazole.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old woman, originally from Cape Verde, was referred to the emergency department with a protracted, progressive clinical syndrome characterized by severe headaches that were acutely triggered by movements of the head, accompanied by episodic vomiting and gait ataxia.

differentials.candidate: Fourth Ventricle Ependymoma / Posterior Fossa Neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute presentation of obstructive hydrocephalus, episodic positional headaches (Bruns' syndrome), and gait ataxia in an adult, but excluded by neuroimaging demonstrating a mobile, non-infiltrating cystic lesion rather than a solid invasive mass.

Considered given a well-circumscribed intraventricular cystic lesion obstructing cerebrospinal fluid outflow, but ruled out by the demonstration of an enhancing eccentric mural nodule (scolex) and postoperative histopathological confirmation.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Fourth Ventricular Neurocysticercosis with Obstructive Hydrocephalus (Bruns' Syndrome)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Identified by brain MRI revealing a 2.6 x 1.8 cm mobile cystic lesion within the fourth ventricle with an eccentric mural scolex acting as a ball-valve mechanism to obstruct the fourth ventricular outflow, successfully treated with telovelar craniotomy, en bloc cyst resection, and histopathological confirmation.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old previously healthy male was transferred to the emergency department of a tertiary referral center in South Korea during the summer season due to a 10-day history of recurrent high fever.

differentials.candidate: Acute Coronary Syndrome (Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to chest symptoms, ischemic ST depressions in lateral leads (V5-V6), progressive troponin elevation (rising to 9.383 ng/mL), and regional wall motion abnormalities, but ruled out by urgent coronary angiography demonstrating widely patent coronary arteries.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral or Autoimmune Fulminant Myocarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered following rapid deterioration into refractory cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest requiring VA-ECMO, and endomyocardial biopsy demonstrating lymphocytic myocarditis, but comprehensive testing for common cardiotropic viruses and autoimmune antibodies was negative.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Scrub Typhus with Fulminant Myocarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Clinically suspected based on the pathognomonic scrotal eschar, maculopapular rash, and lawn exposure despite the unseasonal summer presentation; confirmed by whole-blood nested PCR detecting the 56-kDa gene of Orientia tsutsugamushi (Ikeda strain), endomyocardial biopsy confirming CD3+/CD5+ T-lymphocytic infiltration, and dramatic hemodynamic and functional recovery supported by VA-ECMO, azithromycin, and doxycycline.

clinical_summary: A resident of the municipality of Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil, was admitted to a public hospital in July 2018 with an acute febrile syndrome characterized by fever, diffuse myalgias, and headache.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Sepsis / Occult Bacterial Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered due to the dramatic leukocytosis (20,900/mm^3) and severe elevation of C-reactive protein (240.59 mg/dL), but ruled out by sterile bacterial cultures.

differentials.candidate: Acute Viral Hepatitis (Hepatitis B or C) / Acute Retroviral Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the acute febrile syndrome with hepatocellular injury (elevated AST, ALT, GGT, and direct bilirubin), but ruled out by non-reactive viral serologies.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Dengue (DENV-2 Serotype Coinfection with Yellow Fever Virus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although initial rapid diagnostic tests for dengue (IgM, IgG, NS1) were negative and yellow fever IgM was inconclusive, multiplex quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) decisively detected genetic material from both dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2) and yellow fever virus (YFV).

clinical_summary: A 49-year-old male who had undergone orthotopic liver transplantation approximately nine months earlier was admitted to the hospital with a one-week history of recurrent episodes of abnormal temperature regulation and hypothermia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, leukocytosis, and subsequent rise of inflammatory markers (CRP 61.8 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.85 ng/mL, IL-6 48 pg/mL) in an immunosuppressed liver transplant recipient, but ruled out by complete lack of response to broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic coverage.

differentials.candidate: Acute Allograft Rejection / Drug-Induced Hypereosinophilic Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to profound peripheral blood hypereosinophilia (60.90%) in an allograft recipient on immunosuppressive therapy, but ruled out by direct pathogen identification and mechanical parasite recovery rather than immunological rejection.

Prompted by profound peripheral hypereosinophilia (60.9%) and refractory fevers despite antibiotics; confirmed by plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identifying 60 Clonorchis sinensis sequence reads, subsequent CDC trematode IgG positivity, and macroscopic visualization of numerous adult flukes flushed from the biliary tree during biliary drainage, leading to full clinical and hematologic normalization following oral praziquantel.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male presented to the outpatient medical center in Hawassa, Ethiopia, with a one-month history of a persistent non-productive cough and a three-month history of profound, unquantified weight loss and anorexia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to profound cachexia, diffuse peripheral lymphadenopathy (cervical and submental), and marked hepatosplenomegaly, but ruled out by ultrasound showing centrally necrotic intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy and fine needle aspiration demonstrating tuberculous abscess.

Considered in an East African adult presenting with chronic wasting, marked hepatosplenomegaly, and generalized lymphadenopathy, but excluded by lymph node aspiration revealing tuberculous necrotizing inflammation rather than Leishmania donovani amastigotes.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Tuberculosis in Advanced HIV Infection (Urine LAM Positive)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although all standard sputum diagnostic tests were negative due to non-productive cough and severe immunosuppression (confirmed HIV coinfection with CD4 count of 14 cells/mm^3), the diagnosis of disseminated tuberculosis was definitively confirmed by a positive lateral-flow urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assay and lymph node FNAC, leading to full clinical recovery and weight gain following anti-tuberculosis therapy and antiretroviral therapy.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic for baseline clinical evaluation. He was diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection 3 months ago during voluntary serostatus screening after his wife tested positive at a nearby clinic.

differentials.candidate: Asymptomatic HIV Infection without Opportunistic Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the complete lack of constitutional or localized symptoms and normal physical exam, uncomplicated HIV was initial impression; however, profound CD4 depletion (<100 cells/mm³) mandates active screening for subclinical disseminated opportunistic disease.

Active pulmonary tuberculosis was an immediate consideration given high endemicity and severe immunosuppression, but the patient produced no sputum spontaneously and initial conventional molecular sputum testing was unrevealing.

diagnostic_pivot: In severely immunocompromised HIV patients with CD4 <100 cells/mm³, subclinical disseminated tuberculosis frequently escapes pulmonary detection; lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM) antigen assay provided the decisive rapid point-of-care confirmation of active infection.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old man presents with a 2-month history of sore throat, nasal congestion, dysphagia, and low-grade fever with temperatures up to 37.6°C. He has no prior history of chronic organ disease, including diabetes, renal dysfunction, or liver disease, and denies immunosuppressive medication use, corticosteroid therapy, or known personal or family history of chronic respiratory infections.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A 2-month history of progressive cervical lymphadenopathy, dysphagia, and nasopharyngeal mucosal thickening with indistinct margins strongly suggested nasopharyngeal malignancy; however, endoscopic biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid cells and multinucleated giant cells rather than neoplastic architecture.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial or Invasive Fungal Nasopharyngitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Thick purulent exudate in the nasopharynx suggested acute-on-chronic bacterial or fungal infection; routine bacterial culture grew no pathogenic bacteria, fungal culture grew pseudomycetes (representing non-invasive commensal colonization), and definitive histology revealed granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on sputum examination and positive T-cell testing, coupled with rigid endoscopic nasopharyngeal biopsy revealing epithelioid reaction and multinucleated giant cells characteristic of tuberculous granuloma, definitively confirmed the diagnosis.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old Asian Indian man with no significant past medical history presents to an emergency department in the Midwestern United States with fever and diffuse body aches. He arrived from India 4 days prior to presentation.

differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, severe musculoskeletal pain, elevated transaminases, high LDH, and marked thrombocytopenia in a traveler returning from India strongly suggested acute malaria; however, microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear was negative for intraerythrocytic parasites.

Fever, diffuse myalgias, and presentation to a Midwestern hospital raised concern for tick-borne illness; however, specific serological testing was negative and the short incubation post-travel favored an imported tropical arbovirus.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of acute travel from India, a familial contact with confirmed arboviral infection, precipitous drop of platelets to a nadir of 10 K/μL with delayed development of lower extremity petechiae, followed by spontaneous recovery and confirmatory convalescent serology.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old South African woman is admitted to a district hospital with progressive, painless bilateral vision loss and mild intermittent headaches responsive to simple analgesics. She has a history of HIV infection diagnosed in 2006, previously complicated by treatment default and virological failure (CD4 nadir 39 cells/μL), currently stabilized on second-line antiretroviral therapy with an HIV viral load of 136...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Rural farm residence, exposure to meat, intraocular mass effect with retinal traction, and peripheral eosinophilia raised suspicion for cysticercosis; however, specific cysticercosis enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was negative.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic Retinal Infections (CMV Retinitis, Ocular Toxoplasmosis, Syphilitic Uveitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Profound prior CD4 nadir in an HIV patient presenting with panuveitis, retinal vasculitis, and visual loss typically points to opportunistic viral, treponemal, or protozoal retinitis; all corresponding serological assays were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Advanced retinal imaging demonstrating tractional bands and a characteristic 'double-walled sign' representing an echinococcal cystic cavity in the posterior segment, corroborated by positive specific Echinococcus ELISA serology.

clinical_summary: A 57-year-old male furniture manufacturing worker is admitted with a 5-week history of abdominal distension, anorexia, and constipation, 1 week of left-sided chest pain following a workplace contusion from a wrench, and 1 day of high fever with chills.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral cavitary/nodular lung lesions in the setting of proteinuria and renal pathology prompted an initial outside diagnosis of autoimmune vasculitis; however, worsening during high-dose steroid therapy and subsequent microbial identification proved opportunistic infection rather than primary autoimmunity.

Profound immunosuppression, oral candidiasis, cavitary pulmonary lesions, and significantly elevated (1,3)-beta-D-glucan (745 ng/L) strongly suggested invasive mold infection, with Aspergillus fumigatus cultured from lavage; however, antifungal therapy failed to control disease progression due to unrecognized concurrent mycobacterial and bacterial co-infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing yielded positive results for M. tuberculosis gene probes (A, B, C, and E), and subsequent metagenomic next-generation sequencing confirmed a complex polymicrobial opportunistic infection consisting of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Nocardia nova, Aspergillus fumigatus, and cytomegalovirus.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for a long-standing, refractory cavitary pulmonary infection that has progressed despite years of multiple empirical and guided antimicrobial regimens. She has no personal history of chronic hepatitis, diabetes mellitus, or pre-existing chronic structural lung disease.

differentials.candidate: Primary or Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (HIV / Common Variable Immunodeficiency)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Refractory cavitary pulmonary destruction persisting across years of therapy in a young adult raised high suspicion for underlying host immunosuppression; workup demonstrated intact immune parameters.

Sequential therapeutic failure was initially presumed to represent progressive acquisition of resistance within a single bacterial clone; however, serial phenotypical tests demonstrated paradoxical reversals from resistance back to sensitivity, incompatible with a single evolving isolate.

diagnostic_pivot: Whole-genome sequencing of longitudinal sputum isolates revealed mixed polyclonal infection by two distinct genomic clusters of lineage 2.3 Mycobacterium tuberculosis differing by up to 196 SNPs, whose simultaneous presence and divergent resistance mutations explained the prolonged treatment failure and structural lung destruction.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female residing in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra presents to a rural hospital following two episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures. She reports a 1-year history of persistent left-sided headaches.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A ring-enhancing cystic intracranial lesion with extensive perilesional edema, 9 mm midline shift, and high lipid-lactate peak on MRS raised immediate concern for an encapsulated cerebral abscess; however, the patient was completely afebrile, systemic exam was unremarkable, inflammatory markers and visceral scans were clear, and the internal architecture revealed multivesicular daughter cysts rather than purulent fluid.

A 5 cm mass producing chronic headache, new-onset seizures, ventricular effacement, and subfalcine herniation in a teenager strongly mimics a primary cystic neoplasm; however, classic daughter cyst architecture within a large unilocular mother cyst on neuroimaging was characteristic of parasitic hydatid disease.

diagnostic_pivot: Left frontotemporal craniotomy with surgical identification and excision of the multivesicular cyst, followed by definitive histopathological examination confirming a hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 47-year-old Japanese male university lecturer presents with a 2-week history of dry cough, a 1-week history of progressive dyspnea, and profound unintentional weight loss of 17 kg over several months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Profound CD4 depletion (<20/μL), subacute hypoxemic respiratory failure, elevated (1,3)-beta-D-glucan, and diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT strongly pointed to PJP; however, sputum PCR for P. jirovecii was negative and blood cultures grew filamentous fungal elements.

Presence of filamentous fungi in blood cultures with elevated beta-D-glucan raised suspicion for angioinvasive molds such as Aspergillus or Fusarium; however, serum galactomannan was negative and the organism exhibited dimorphic broom-like structures distinct from Aspergillus.

diagnostic_pivot: Aerobic blood culture yielded a dimorphic mold with characteristic broom-like penicillus bodies on lactophenol cotton blue staining, definitively identified by whole-genome and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing as Talaromyces marneffei, contracted during prior residence in Guangzhou, China.

clinical_summary: A 46-year-old man presents with a 7-month history of episodic left knee joint pain and swelling, nocturnal fevers, productive cough, anorexia, and recurrent painful erythematous nodules over his limbs. His medical history is notable for untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, cigarette smoking, and heavy alcohol intake.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy combined with erythema nodosum, peripheral arthritis, and elevated inflammatory markers strongly resembled sarcoidosis; however, high-resolution CT demonstrated cavitary destructive changes and subsequent microbiological analysis confirmed an infectious etiology.

differentials.candidate: Primary Autoimmune Disease / Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with Antiphospholipid Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: Erythema nodosum, multi-station adenopathy, inflammatory arthritis, and isolated APTT prolongation with positive antiphospholipid antibodies suggested primary autoimmune disease; however, anti-dsDNA and rheumatoid factor were negative, and pulmonary cavitary disease progressed as active infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat chest computed tomography demonstrating a cavity with a classic tree-in-bud appearance and right hilar adenopathy, accompanied by positive acid-fast bacilli on serial sputum examination (fourth and fifth specimens), confirming active cavitary pulmonary infection underlying secondary acquired factor VIII inhibitor autoantibodies.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder since age 20 and unspecified neonatal hepatomegaly presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of throbbing headache, arthralgias, severe myalgias, and documented fever up to 40.4°C that responded only partially to ibuprofen and failed to respond to acetaminophen.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant accompanied by elevated lipase, amylase, and hepatic enzymes initially suggested biliary tract obstruction; however, ultrasonography revealed a normal gallbladder without stones and nondilated bile ducts.

Longstanding alcohol use disorder history raised suspicion for toxic-metabolic pancreatitis; however, serum triglycerides were only mildly elevated (267 mg/dl, well below the >1,000 mg/dl threshold for pancreatitis), serum calcium was normal, and widespread petechiae with severe thrombocytopenia pointed to an acute infectious arboviral etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Clinical presentation in an endemic region characterized by high fever, severe thrombocytopenia (23,000/μL), hemoconcentration, and third-spacing (ascites, pleural effusion) leading to acute pancreatic inflammation, confirmed by positive IgM and IgG viral antibodies.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old man residing in a rural countryside region presented for evaluation of chronic facial lesions. Five months prior to presentation, he developed progressive erythema and swelling over the right forehead that failed to improve after multiple courses of topical antibiotic ointments.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the initial presumptive diagnosis given periorbital edema and hyperemia, but ruled out due to the lack of heat or tenderness, five-month indolent duration, and failure to respond to intravenous ampicillin-sulbactam and piperacillin-tazobactam.
Considered in the differential diagnosis of periorbital crusted erythematous lesions, but excluded due to the chronic five-month course and absence of characteristic painful grouped vesicles.
Considered due to the crusted facial plaques, but ruled out by refractoriness to multiple courses of topical antibiotics and systemic beta-lactams.
Considered empirically by infectious diseases after antibacterial failure, but ruled out due to persistent lack of clinical regression during intravenous amphotericin-B therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred following failure of broad-spectrum antibacterial and antifungal therapy when a full-thickness skin biopsy was obtained, demonstrating diagnostic histopathological findings of cutaneous protozoan infection.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old Caucasian female from Colombia with a recent diagnosis of high-risk early T-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia was admitted for scheduled induction chemotherapy. She had no prior significant personal or family medical history.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially strongly suspected due to febrile neutropenia with ground-glass pulmonary nodules in a patient undergoing leukemia chemotherapy, but excluded by negative serum galactomannan, negative bronchoalveolar lavage galactomannan and fungal cultures, and lack of response to voriconazole and isavuconazole.

Considered when hepatic injury and persistent pulmonary nodules developed, and later when lymphadenopathy appeared, but excluded by liver biopsy showing no hematologic malignancy and subsequent lymph node histology demonstrating granulomatous inflammation rather than lymphoblasts.

Considered during evaluation of persistent lung nodules and prominent cervical lymphadenopathy, but excluded by negative molecular assays from bronchoalveolar lavage and negative Ziehl-Neelsen staining and PCR on lymph node tissue.

diagnostic_pivot: Following persistent fever, pulmonary nodules unresponsive to azoles, and the appearance of prominent cervical lymphadenopathy, an excisional lymph node biopsy was performed, which definitively demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation containing diagnostic yeasts.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old previously healthy male student from France was brought by emergency rescue services to the health center and subsequently transferred to the regional hospital after collapsing while hiking in a remote rainforest area in French Guiana.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prominent presenting symptoms of fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea, but ruled out as the primary etiology by negative stool cultures and parasitological examinations, as well as multisystem hematologic and renal derangements.
Considered given the patient's collapse, prostration, marked thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury, but physical examination showed no signs of septic shock or circulatory collapse.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic discovery occurred with blood smear microscopy and rapid antigen testing, which revealed intraerythrocytic protozoal parasitemia and severe acute renal failure confirming severe imported infection.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old woman residing in Jiuzhaigou, Sichuan Province, China, was admitted to a tertiary hospital for evaluation of prolonged fever of unknown origin and worsening pancytopenia. Six days prior to transfer, she developed acute-onset high fever peaking at 39.6°C, accompanied by chills, shivering, cough, sputum production, fatigue, and dyspnea.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to progressive pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, and dysplastic erythroid morphology (>10%) on marrow aspirate, but excluded by normal bone marrow chromosome karyotyping and negative myeloid gene mutation panels.

Considered initially given high fever, chills, cough, and sputum production, but excluded by lack of pulmonary infiltrates on chest CT and failure of fevers to remit on empiric ceftriaxone, clindamycin, piperacillin/tazobactam, and moxifloxacin.
Considered during admission and empirically treated with oseltamivir, but fever persisted without improvement.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of cell-free DNA and RNA detected thousands of genus-specific reads, which was subsequently corroborated by a positive rK39 serological dipstick and direct identification of protozoa on repeat bone marrow smear review.

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old man presented to the hospital with a one-month history of recurrent, debilitating high-grade fevers associated with rigors and shaking chills. The fevers were refractory to outpatient management, with temperatures spiking up to 41.0°C.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's prior medical history and elevated amylase and lipase levels, but ruled out as the primary etiology by complete lack of response to broad-spectrum intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam and the absence of bacterial isolates on routine cultures.

differentials.candidate: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-driven lymphoproliferative disorder / Primary EBV infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the positive EBV finding alongside fever, cytopenias, and hepatosplenomegaly, but an initial bone marrow evaluation showed no pathogenic microorganisms or atypical lymphoproliferation, and the underlying protozoal trigger was subsequently uncovered.

Considered when active hemophagocytosis was identified on marrow aspiration, but excluded by molecular genetic testing showing no pathogenic mutations associated with familial hemophagocytic syndromes.

diagnostic_pivot: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free DNA detected specific sequences of Leishmania donovani, prompting targeted review of the bone marrow aspirate which revealed protozoal amastigotes, confirmed by positive rK39 serology.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old woman with no prior chronic medical history presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of episodic upper abdominal pain. The pain was described as dull, non-radiating, exacerbated by movements and positional changes, and refractory to oral antacids and analgesics.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute epigastric pain, anorexia, and nausea, but ruled out given complete lack of relief with antacids and analgesics, along with ultrasound showing significant common bile duct dilation and intraductal tubular filling defects.

Considered given dilated common bile duct and biliary colic symptoms, but ruled out by ultrasound and cholangiography which demonstrated linear tubular structures rather than acoustic shadowing biliary calculi.

diagnostic_pivot: Urgent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) revealed adult macroscopic roundworms within the stomach, duodenum, and biliary tree, with extraction from the left hepatic duct confirming biliary infestation by soil-transmitted nematodes.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old female presented for evaluation of a persistent, painful mass in her left breast. She reported a history of breastfeeding that had ceased one year prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the large 10-cm palpable breast mass, axillary lymphadenopathy, and BI-RADS IVa MRI classification, but ruled out by core needle biopsy demonstrating benign granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

Considered due to acute inflammatory signs, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, and elevated CRP, but ruled out by complete lack of response to successive courses of amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, third-generation cephalosporins, and metronidazole.
Considered as a potential granulomatous etiology of chronic mastitis and lymphadenitis, but excluded by negative Brucella serology.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative direct stains, cultures, and IGRA testing, clinical presentation with necrotic nodal involvement and complete therapeutic resolution upon initiation of standard anti-tuberculosis therapy definitively confirmed primary tuberculous mastitis.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old patient living in Brazil presented to the clinical service for scheduled post-treatment longitudinal surveillance. The patient had previously received and completed a full therapeutic course of liposomal amphotericin B for a severe systemic protozoal infection with initial clinical resolution.

differentials.candidate: Secondary intercurrent bacterial or opportunistic infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a post-treatment elderly patient with recurrent systemic symptoms, but ruled out as longitudinal molecular tracking demonstrated direct resurgence of the primary protozoal pathogen load rather than a secondary process.

Considered when symptoms returned, but differentiated from primary failure because initial clinical remission had been achieved following liposomal amphotericin B, with relapse occurring late at month six.

diagnostic_pivot: Longitudinal surveillance utilizing quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) detecting parasite kinetoplast DNA (kDNA) revealed a 2-log increase in circulating parasite load months before overt symptom onset, definitively establishing clinical relapse.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old boy was referred to a specialized pediatric clinic for comprehensive diagnostic evaluation of recurrent, severe multi-station lymphadenopathy and chronic systemic symptoms. At 6 months of age, he initially developed prolonged fever and prominent left axillary lymphadenitis that failed to improve after multiple courses of oral and intravenous antibacterial therapy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered during initial presentations in infancy, but ruled out by complete lack of response to both oral and intravenous broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens, followed by identification of caseating granulomas on histopathology.

Considered given recurrent generalized multi-station lymphadenopathy, fever, and progressive weight loss in a young child, but ruled out by fine-needle aspiration cytology and biopsy demonstrating caseating granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic lymphoproliferation.

Considered due to recurrent febrile episodes with mesenteric lymphadenitis and positive serology, but ruled out as the cause of chronic pulmonary and peripheral nodal disease, which responded to multi-drug antimycobacterial regimens.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological demonstration of caseating granulomatous inflammation across multiple nodal stations and confirmation of widespread pulmonary and mesenteric disease established the diagnosis of disseminated mycobacterial disease in a child with primary immunodeficiency.

clinical_summary: A 7-year-old boy was referred to the Pediatric Tropical and Infectious Diseases unit for evaluation of a six-week illness characterized by prolonged high-grade fever, severe abdominal pain, and progressive weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's history of recurrent febrile illness with severe abdominal pain and elevated Widal titers, but ruled out as the cause of the current presentation given the prominent bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and productive pulmonary symptoms.

Considered given prolonged nocturnal fevers, drenching night sweats, marked weight loss, and widespread hilar and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, but excluded by molecular identification of a specific infectious pathogen.

Considered in the differential diagnosis of an inherited immunodeficiency presenting with recurrent granulomatous lymphadenitis and deep visceral infections, but ruled out by a normal dihydrorhodamine reduction (DHR) flow cytometry assay.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis of disseminated mycobacterial infection was conclusively established by specific molecular PCR assays detecting IS6110 and mtp40 target sequences in blood and sputum, in the setting of homozygous IL12RB1 loss-of-function mutation.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old nonsmoking man with no known medical comorbidities presents with a 2-month history of dull aching pain in the left hemithorax, accompanied by 7 days of dry cough and progressive shortness of breath.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the subacute 2-month presentation of chest pain and exudative hydropneumothorax in an agrarian endemic region, but pleural fluid adenosine deaminase (ADA) was low (23 U/L, well below the usual >40 U/L cutoff for tuberculosis) with marked pleural eosinophilia rather than lymphocytic predominance.

differentials.candidate: Complicated bacterial empyema / Ruptured bacterial lung abscess
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of cough, dyspnea, leukocytosis, and an air-fluid level on radiography, but ruled out by clear serous and eosinophilic fluid rather than purulent exudate, absence of high fevers, and subsequent visualization of an intra-cavitary crumpled membrane.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst (Echinococcosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Established following tube thoracostomy when follow-up radiography and computed tomography revealed a cavitary lesion in the left lower lobe containing a wavy collapsed endocyst floating on fluid (pathognomonic water-lily/camolette sign), corroborated by positive IgG ELISA against antigen B.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old man weighing 65 kg presents for evaluation of a localized skin lesion on his left ear that has been present for 2 months. He has a history of diabetes mellitus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the scaly, crusting auricular lesion in an immunocompromised diabetic host, but ruled out by direct microscopic examination of lesion scales with potassium hydroxide showing no fungal elements.

differentials.candidate: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma / Non-melanoma skin cancer
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's age and a chronic, painless, scabrous, non-healing ulcerated plaque on a sun-exposed auricle, but ruled out when tissue smears revealed intracellular amastigotes rather than malignant epithelial cells.

Confirmed when Giemsa-stained microscopic smears of marginal scrapings revealed numerous intracellular amastigotes, and species-specific kDNA PCR demonstrated a 760-bp amplicon diagnostic of Leishmania tropica.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old previously healthy adolescent male residing in the urban area of São Paulo state, Brazil, is admitted to the hospital with a 3-week history of generalized lymphadenopathy. His history includes tobacco use (5-6 cigarettes daily), recreational marijuana and cocaine use, and frequent gardening.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected given the acute B-symptoms (fever, drenching sweats, 10-kg weight loss), diffuse generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and massive chylous ascites in an adolescent, but excluded by lymph node histopathology demonstrating granulomatous fungal inflammation with multiple exosporulations rather than malignant lymphoid proliferation.

Considered due to the reticuloendothelial involvement, fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and South American geographic origin, but ruled out by specific serologic counterimmunoelectrophoresis showing only a 1:1 titer against Histoplasma capsulatum compared to a diagnostic 1:512 titer against Paracoccidioides, as well as distinct fungal morphology.

Confirmed by excisional inguinal lymph node biopsy revealing epithelioid granulomas with multinucleated giant cells and characteristic fungal yeast structures with multiple exosporulations (mariner's wheel appearance) consistent with Paracoccidioides spp., supported by counterimmunoelectrophoresis titers of 1:512.

clinical_summary: A 7-month-old male infant in Kenya presents with persistent fevers, cough, and rapid breathing that have been ongoing for 5 weeks. He is the only child of non-consanguineous parents.

differentials.candidate: Refractory pyogenic bacterial or opportunistic fungal pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to protracted 5-week respiratory failure, persistent fever, oral thrush, and failure of multiple broad-spectrum antibiotics, but bronchoalveolar lavage bacterial and fungal cultures were negative and periodic acid-Schiff stain on tissue was negative for fungi.

Considered because axillary lymphadenitis occurred ipsilaterally to the BCG vaccination scar in an infant with suspected underlying inborn immunodeficiency, but molecular line probe assay confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex sensitive to isoniazid and rifampicin.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Pulmonary and Lymphatic Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Confirmed when left axillary lymph node biopsy demonstrated caseous granulomatous lymphadenitis, the tuberculin skin test was strongly positive (26 mm induration at 72 hours), and Genotype MTBDRplus VER 2.0 molecular testing of lymph node tissue detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 71-year-old man presents with persistent foul-smelling perianal discharge. He has no significant chronic medical illnesses and reports no use of tobacco, alcohol, or illicit substances.

differentials.candidate: Recurrent cryptoglandular anal fistula / Complex fistulizing perianal Crohn's disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the multi-decade history of anal fistula surgery, recurrent suppuration across multiple pelviperineal compartments, and persistent foul-smelling discharge, but ruled out when histological assessment revealed invasive adenocarcinoma and caseating granulomas rather than non-specific or non-caseating inflammation.

differentials.candidate: Primary anal canal squamous cell carcinoma / Metastatic pelvic neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 1x2 cm ulcerative growth and complex tissue infiltration, but systemic imaging showed no metastases, and histopathology confirmed mucinous adenocarcinoma synchronously accompanied by necrotizing epithelioid granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Synchronous Anal Tuberculosis and Anal Mucinous Adenocarcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by biopsy examination of the ulcerative lesion demonstrating an anal mucinous adenocarcinoma coexisting with epithelioid granulomas and caseous necrosis diagnostic of anal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old male residing in São Paulo, Brazil, presents with recurrent episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia (SVT) requiring hospital admission. He has a longstanding history of chronic cardiomyopathy and underwent implantation of a dual-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) seven years earlier.

differentials.candidate: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with post-infarction ventricular scar
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to dense inferolateral left ventricular scarring and monomorphic ventricular tachycardia in an older adult, but ruled out by coronary imaging integrated with electroanatomic data revealing non-ischemic substrate rather than coronary atherosclerotic disease.

Considered in a patient with severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias, but electroanatomic mapping demonstrated the prototypical endo-epicardial scar localized to the inferolateral-basal segment of the left ventricle pathognomonic of chronic Chagasic heart disease.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Chronic Chagas Heart Disease (American Trypanosomiasis / Trypanosoma cruzi)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Confirmed as the foundational cause of the patient's endo-epicardial scar-mediated ventricular tachycardia storm and dilated cardiomyopathy, which had proven refractory to antiarrhythmic drugs and catheter ablations, successfully managed with stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT).

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old Indian male presents to the emergency department following an alleged road traffic accident. On primary survey and initial neurological examination, the patient is unresponsive, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 9 (eye opening 2, verbal response 3, motor response 4).

differentials.candidate: Cerebral metastases / Multiple necrotic brain metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of multiple spherical cortical and subcortical lesions in a middle-aged adult with sudden neurological collapse, but contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated thin-walled cysts with eccentric enhancing protoscolices and no surrounding tumor edema or primary neoplasm.

A frequent differential diagnosis in endemic India for multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions, but tuberculomas are solid or rim-enhancing granulomas without an internal fluid cyst and scolex, and the lesions in this patient were in the classic non-inflamed vesicular stage.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Neurocysticercosis with concomitant subretinal ocular cysticerci
differentials.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by pathognomonic contrast-enhanced brain MRI demonstrating multiple cysts with enhancing protoscolices meeting absolute criteria for neurocysticercosis, complemented by ophthalmologic fundoscopy, SD-OCT, and B-scan ultrasonography demonstrating concomitant subretinal cysts with hyperechoic scolices.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old Asian Indian gentleman is admitted to the hospital with a 1-week history of severe postural giddiness and persistent vomiting. He has a history of prolonged self-administration of oral corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.5 to 1 mg daily) for nearly one year to treat a chronic rash in his inguinal area.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The initial presumed diagnosis supported by chronic dexamethasone overuse, hypotension, vomiting, and suppressed morning cortisol, but although blood pressure responded to intravenous stress hydrocortisone, intractable vomiting persisted after 48 hours and the patient suffered rapid multiorgan failure, pointing to an underlying infectious process.

differentials.candidate: Septic shock from occult pyogenic bacteremia / Bacterial sepsis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's acute decompensation into fatal multiorgan failure in an immunosuppressed state, but extensive sepsis workup including blood cultures was negative.

Confirmed when upper gastrointestinal endoscopy performed for refractory vomiting revealed yellowish-white pseudomembranous lesions throughout the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum, with histopathologic section of gastric biopsy demonstrating larval and adult forms of Strongyloides stercoralis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 1, is referred to the emergency department with a 1-week history of lower abdominal pain localized to the hypogastric region. She reports subjective fevers at home, although she is afebrile on arrival.

differentials.candidate: Advanced ovarian adenocarcinoma with peritoneal carcinomatosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The leading clinical and radiologic diagnosis based on the 56x48 mm adnexal mass, ascites, markedly elevated CA 125 (198 U/ml), and peritoneal nodularity on CT scan, but disproven intraoperatively when the ovaries were found to be intact without a primary ovarian tumor.

Considered due to the diffuse small bowel and peritoneal deposits with mesenteric lymphadenopathy found on exploration, but anatomopathological analysis confirmed benign granulomatous disease and excluded neoplastic or malignant cells.

Confirmed when histopathological examination of multiple peritoneal and epiploic nodule biopsies demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation diagnostic of peritoneal tuberculosis without any malignant cells.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old male with no significant prior medical history presents with a 1-month history of progressive headaches, decreased visual acuity, and visual field disturbance. On physical examination, he is alert and oriented, but mildly feverish.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The most common consideration for a sellar-suprasellar mass causing chiasmatic compression with temporal hemianopia in an adolescent, but argued against by normal endocrine hormonal panels, low-grade fevers, and the presence of satellite lesions in the posterior fossa and hypothalamus.

Considered due to the basilar and hypothalamic-sellar granulomatous distribution in a young immunocompetent patient, but serological screens and HIV testing were negative, while specific mycobacterial assays were positive.

differentials.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis (Sellar-Suprasellar Tuberculoma and Tuberculous Meningitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Established by lumbar puncture revealing lymphocytic pleocytosis, hypoglycorrhachia, and elevated protein, with positive CSF PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and confirmed by positive Mantoux and Interferon-Gamma Release Assays.

clinical_summary: An 81-year-old retired lawyer was found unresponsive at his residence in São Paulo state, Southern Brazil, and was submitted to the local coroner's office for post-mortem evaluation. He lived alone and was married; no antecedent history of dysentery, chronic illnesses, prescription medications, or recent travel could be retrieved from available records.

differentials.candidate: Ischemic colitis / Mesenteric ischemia with bowel necrosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Ischemic colitis is common in the elderly and can cause colonic gangrene and perforation, but it typically affects vascular watershed areas and spares the rectum, whereas this patient presented with pancolonic necrotizing ulcerations extending from cecum to rectum with flask-shaped morphology.

differentials.candidate: Inflammatory bowel disease (Fulminant Ulcerative Colitis or Crohn's Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe inflammatory bowel disease can lead to toxic megacolon, pancolitis, and perforation, but histopathological evaluation of the ulcer beds revealed deep undermining margins composed of necrotic debris with a striking paucity of inflammatory cells, unlike the dense cryptolytic or transmural lymphoid inflammatory infiltrates characteristic of IBD.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the colonic ulcer margins demonstrated necrotic undermining ulcers containing trophozoites with foamy cytoplasm and eccentric nuclei showing ingested erythrocytes positive on Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) staining, establishing fulminant necrotizing colitis caused by Entamoeba histolytica.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old Filipino female presented to the emergency department after sustaining a fall following focal myoclonus of the left lower extremity of undetermined duration and transient loss of consciousness. She reported an acute left-sided headache and experienced two episodes of emesis upon arrival.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given solitary intra-axial mass in the frontal lobe with surrounding edema, focal motor seizures, and progressive hemiparesis in an afebrile adult, but ruled out when histological analysis demonstrated parasitic egg deposition with perivascular gliosis rather than high-grade neoplastic glial proliferation.

Considered because of intracranial space-occupying lesion with acute intracranial hypertension (headache, vomiting) and focal neurological deficits; ruled out by absence of fever, lack of leukocytosis or systemic inflammatory symptoms, and surgical biopsy demonstrating non-bacterial parasitic granulomas without purulent necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of multiple surgical biopsies obtained during right frontal craniotomy revealed scattered perivascular aggregates of parasitic ova accompanied by prominent reactive gliosis, confirming central nervous system involvement by Schistosoma.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old female with no prior history of childhood vaccinations presented to the pediatric department at a tertiary care center in Karachi, Pakistan, with a 6-month history of low-grade intermittent fever and progressive weight loss, accompanied by abdominal pain and generalized edema for the preceding 14 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suspected due to acute fever spike to 102°F, peritonitis, leukocytosis with neutrophilia, elevated CRP, and a ruptured right lobe hepatic collection; ruled out by lack of clinical response to broad-spectrum intravenous cefotaxime and metronidazole, the protracted 6-month wasting prodrome, subsequent emergence of intracranial ring-enhancing lesions, and positive mycobacterial testing.

Considered highly likely in an endemic South Asian pediatric population presenting with a solitary right hepatic lobe abscess and localized rupture; ruled out by negative serum amoebic serology, negative stool ova/parasite evaluation, and lack of improvement on intravenous metronidazole.

diagnostic_pivot: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of gastric secretions tested positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and tuberculin skin testing demonstrated 12 mm induration, confirming disseminated tuberculosis manifesting with ruptured hepatic tuberculoma, inferior vena cava thrombosis, and intracranial tuberculomas.

clinical_summary: A 59-year-old male presented to the orthopedics outpatient department with a 1-year history of progressive low back pain aggravated by physical activity, accompanied by intermittent low-grade fever, night sweats, and persistent fatigue.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute-to-chronic lumbar discitis, vertebral osteolysis, and paravertebral fluid collection in an immunocompromised HIV-infected patient; ruled out by the indolent 1-year progression, presence of multiple bony sequestra and cold paravertebral abscesses rather than acute suppurative pyogenic necrosis, and subsequent microbiological isolation of resistant mycobacteria.

Considered in an older adult with constitutional symptoms, weight loss, elevated ESR, and vertebral osteolytic destruction; ruled out by classic involvement and collapse of the L2–L3 intervertebral disc space with extensive paravertebral/psoas abscess collections, as hematogenous neoplasms characteristically spare the disc space.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical debridement and subsequent abscess drainage of postoperative sinus formation confirmed persistent caseating spinal infection, with definitive drug susceptibility testing demonstrating secondary multidrug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to isoniazid and rifampin.

clinical_summary: A 39-year-old woman residing in Cali, Colombia, presented with a 6-month history of pruritic macules on her limbs that had progressively evolved into reddish-brown papules and nodules, some demonstrating mild scaling and superficial ulceration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered primary diagnosis given disseminated reddish-brown nodular eruptions and positive treponemal screening; ruled out by complete lack of clinical improvement after completing three weekly cycles of intramuscular benzathine penicillin G, negative tissue PCR for Treponema pallidum DNA, and histopathologic confirmation of acid-fast bacilli.

Prevalent in Colombia causing chronic papulonodular and ulcerated cutaneous lesions on exposed limbs; ruled out by histopathology lacking intracellular amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) and instead revealing lipid-laden histiocytic granulomas filled with acid-fast bacilli.

diagnostic_pivot: Excisional biopsy of two cutaneous nodules demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation containing globi of acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining, confirming multibacillary lepromatous leprosy in a patient with madarosis.

clinical_summary: A 67-year-old Sri Lankan male with a 5-year history of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis well-controlled on methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine presented with a 2-month history of a progressively enlarging, painless swelling of the left wrist accompanied by paresthesias and numbness involving the radial aspect of the left hand.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the most probable initial diagnosis given the patient's longstanding history of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis presenting with florid flexor synovial hypertrophy causing secondary carpal tunnel syndrome; ruled out when surgical excision revealed caseating granulomas and mycobacterial growth rather than sterile inflammatory pannus.

differentials.candidate: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor / Pigmented villonodular synovitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the indolent, slowly progressive, mass-like lobulated synovial expansion tracking along the tendon sheaths through the carpal canal without bony erosion on plain radiographs; ruled out by histopathology demonstrating necrotizing caseous granulomas and positive microbial cultures.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the excised synovial mass revealed caseating granulomatous necrosis with Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells, and synovial tissue culture on Lowenstein-Jensen medium with immunochromatographic MPT64 assay definitively confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of persistent headaches, low-grade fever, and recurrent episodes of vomiting. On physical examination, she was alert and oriented with stable vital signs.

differentials.candidate: Central nervous system tuberculosis / Tuberculous meningitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on the endemic background and a 2-month insidious history of fever, headache, vomiting, and hydrocephalus; ruled out by normal CSF protein, glucose, and lactate levels, negative GeneXpert molecular testing, and absence of pachymeningeal enhancement.

Considered due to fluid-signal extra-axial cystic lesion expanding the basal cistern and displacing the midbrain without surrounding parenchymal vasogenic edema; ruled out because high-resolution imaging revealed multiple internal undulating thin septations rather than a simple unilocular epithelial cyst or diffusion-restricting epidermoid.

diagnostic_pivot: High-resolution Fast Imaging Employing Steady-state Acquisition (FIESTA) MRI clearly delineated multiple thin septations within the fluid-filled prepontine cistern lesion without scolex or post-contrast enhancement, establishing the diagnosis of racemose neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old male presented to the neurology service with a 5-year history of recurrent seizures, progressive gait impairment, ataxia, urinary incontinence, and insidious memory loss and forgetfulness. Based on the presence of hydrocephalus identified on prior neuroimaging, he had previously been evaluated at an outside center and treated empirically for chronic infectious meningitis with hydrocephalus, completing a 3-month course of...

differentials.candidate: Central nervous system tuberculosis / Chronic tuberculous meningitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected elsewhere as the cause of chronic hydrocephalus and progressive neurological deficits; ruled out by complete lack of clinical improvement following 3 months of compliant targeted medical therapy, absence of basal meningeal exudates, and demonstration of non-enhancing cisternal cysts.

Considered due to the 5-year insidious clinical triad of gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and progressive cognitive decline accompanied by marked ventriculomegaly; ruled out by the co-occurrence of seizures and the demonstration of focal cyst-like cisternal expansion causing structural pontine indentation.

diagnostic_pivot: High-resolution FIESTA sequence MRI demonstrated pathognomonic thin internal septations within the dilated ambient cistern and Sylvian fissures exerting mass effect upon the pons, confirming the diagnosis of racemose neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 61-year-old male presented to the outpatient department with a 3-day history of headaches and a 2-day history of fever. His past medical history was notable for an ischemic stroke in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) distribution three years prior (January 2020).

differentials.candidate: Recurrent ischemic stroke / Post-infarction cystic encephalomalacia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's prior right MCA ischemic stroke presenting with acute headache, fever, and bulbar symptoms; ruled out by MRI showing an active, expansile multilobulated cystic mass with distinct peripheral enhancement and internal structural architecture, rather than non-enhancing gliotic cystic encephalomalacia.

Considered because of acute fever, headache, and a ring-enhancing lesion in the Sylvian fissure; ruled out by absence of toxic leukocytosis or surrounding mass effect with prominent vasogenic edema, and the specific demonstration of a calcified mural scolex on susceptibility imaging without purulent necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) identified an eccentric blooming focus representing the characteristic larval scolex within the right Sylvian fissure cyst, while FIESTA imaging demonstrated multiple thin communicating septations throughout the fissure, establishing racemose neurocysticercosis.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old Persian female presented with a 6-month history of an asymmetric, painless swelling in the right periumbilical region without cutaneous drainage or secretion. She reported an unintentional weight loss of 8 kilograms over the preceding three months despite an unchanged diet.

differentials.candidate: Abdominal wall soft-tissue neoplasm (e.g., Desmoid tumor / sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to an enlarging palpable abdominal wall mass accompanied by substantial constitutional weight loss (8 kg) in a young adult; ruled out by contrast CT demonstrating a non-enhancing cystic lesion with peripheral fat stranding rather than a solid enhancing invasive spindle-cell mass, and histopathology confirming caseating granulomatous inflammation.

differentials.candidate: Benign abdominal wall cyst (e.g., epidermal inclusion cyst / hematoma / seroma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the mobile, well-bordered, non-tender, cystic characteristics in the anterior abdominal wall in a young afebrile patient; ruled out by histologic findings of lymphoid follicles with germinal centers, caseous necrosis, and Langhans multinucleated giant cells with confirmed positive mycobacterial PCR.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the surgically resected cyst wall demonstrated chronic fibroconnective tissue with lymphoid follicle formation, germinal centers, and caseous granulomatous inflammation rimmed by Langhans multinucleated giant cells, confirmed by positive real-time PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension, metastatic colon adenocarcinoma at the hepatic flexure with hepatic metastases, and hepatic flexure stricture status post colonic stenting presented with a 5-day history of right-sided abdominal pain, constipation, nausea, and non-bloody, non-bilious emesis.

differentials.candidate: Malignant Large Bowel Obstruction / Stent Occlusion
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had documented transverse colon obstruction secondary to metastatic adenocarcinoma, mechanical obstruction alone did not explain the inflammatory colitis changes on CT or the presence of an infectious enteric co-pathology delaying surgical intervention.
Common bacterial enteropathogens were considered given radiographic colitis, but conventional stool cultures returned completely negative and the patient lacked typical diarrheal symptoms.
