differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in a patient returning from Guinea and Sierra Leone with severe prostration, jaundice, DIC, and hemorrhagic manifestations, but specific testing identified dengue virus serotype 3 rather than other hemorrhagic viruses.

Dengue hemorrhagic fever accounted for thrombocytopenia, hemorrhagic manifestations, and plasma leakage, but could not be considered in isolation because blood smears demonstrated active, life-threatening malaria parasitemia.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of 3% Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia on thick and thin blood films in combination with positive dengue IgM/IgG seroconversion and RT-PCR confirmation of dengue 3 viral RNA, establishing concurrent co-infection.

clinical_summary: A 4-month-old male infant residing in a rural district in southwest Iran is brought to the emergency department due to refusal of feeds, vomiting, episodes of retching, and altered stool consistency.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Viral gastroenteritis is the leading cause of vomiting and loose stools in young infants, but it typically presents with watery non-bloody stools and does not feature peripheral eosinophilia or protozoan forms on fecal examination.

differentials.candidate: Invasive bacterial enterocolitis (e.g., Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial enterocolitis usually causes marked pyrexia, toxicity, and neutrophilic leukocytosis, rather than a normal leukocyte count of 7,800/μL with eosinophilia.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic examination of fresh stool using Lugol's iodine and concentration technique demonstrating Entamoeba histolytica cysts and trophozoites with ingested erythrocytes and leukocytes, resolving completely with oral metronidazole.

clinical_summary: A 3-year-old male child residing in Gorakhpur, India, is admitted with high-grade fever for 12 days, generalized tonic-clonic convulsions for 6 days, and altered sensorium for 1 day. On examination, the child is febrile with temperature of 103 °F, pulse 158/min (feeble), respiratory rate 54/min, blood pressure 56/32 mm Hg, and a Glasgow coma score of 4.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial meningitis was suspected given septic shock and profound coma, but lumbar puncture showed only a mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (72% lymphocytes, 68 cells/mm3) with normal CSF sugar, and blood cultures were sterile.
Typhoid encephalopathy was considered in the setting of prolonged remittent fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and altered sensorium, but serological and microbiological tests were negative.

While JEV is endemic in Gorakhpur and causes acute encephalitis syndrome with lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis, monoinfection did not account for the high level of hemoparasitemia that required prompt antimalarial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid diagnostic test and peripheral blood thick and thin smears demonstrating dual Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia (6% parasitemia), together with positive CSF JE IgM antibodies confirming concurrent JEV encephalitis.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old woman presents to the hospital with a 3-month history of an enlarging, painful mass on the left lateral side of her neck. She reports no fever or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the painful, fluctuant mass with erythematous, inflammatory overlying skin and elevated ESR, but ruled out because the lesion was an organized multicystic structure rather than a suppurative bacterial collection.

Considered given the chronic 3-month progressive course of a fluctuant supraclavicular mass with elevated ESR, but excluded as the lesion was not originating from lymph nodes and surgical pathology lacked caseating granulomas.

differentials.candidate: Cystic hygroma or Branchial cleft cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital cystic lateral neck masses typically manifest earlier in life and present as painless, non-inflammatory fluid collections without multiple internal daughter cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Perioperative visualization of the hydatid cyst wall and multiple daughter cysts containing scoleces following excision, confirmed on histopathological examination.

clinical_summary: A 34-year-old nomadic male presents to the hospital with chronic swelling of his anteromedial left leg accompanied by multiple sinuses discharging yellowish granules, which have developed progressively over the past 4 years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial osteomyelitis causes chronic discharging sinuses, but plain radiographs typically show prominent periosteal reaction, sequestrum, and involucrum, which were absent here, and the purulent drainage lacks characteristic fungal/actinomycotic grains.

Tuberculosis cutis can produce chronic subcutaneous nodules and sinuses in pastoralists with weight loss, but discharges caseous necrotic debris rather than discrete grains, and tissue biopsy revealed fungal and actinomycotic microabscesses.

differentials.candidate: Soft tissue sarcoma (e.g., synovial sarcoma or fibrosarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Mesenchymal malignancies can cause chronic lower-extremity soft-tissue mass with cortical bone erosion, but do not present with multiple grain-discharging sinus tracts and are ruled out by histopathology showing suppurative granulomas containing grains.

diagnostic_pivot: Incisional biopsy histopathology demonstrating abscesses containing both actinomycetoma and eumycetoma grains, definitively establishing the diagnosis of mixed mycetoma.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of persistent hiccups and progressive dyspnea. The patient was otherwise healthy, but reports regular domestic exposure to dogs and sheep.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to complete unilateral hemithoracic opacification, dullness to percussion, and absent breath sounds, but thoracic imaging revealed a giant encapsulated intrapulmonary cystic fluid lesion rather than free pleural fluid collection.

differentials.candidate: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation or Bronchogenic cyst
differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital bronchopulmonary foregut cysts can be cystic and large, but they rarely present de novo as a 29 cm mass in an 18-year-old with internal daughter vesicles and close contact with dogs and sheep.

differentials.candidate: Intrathoracic malignancy (e.g., Pleuropulmonary blastoma, synovial sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Primary thoracic malignancies can produce massive unilateral thoracic opacification with mediastinal shift, but imaging and intraoperative examination demonstrated a non-invasive fluid cyst with viable daughter cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Computed tomography demonstrating a giant 29 x 17 cm cystic lesion occupying the left lung and pushing the mediastinum, followed by intraoperative confirmation and conservative excision of the giant viable hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old male presents with continuous high-grade fever without chills or rigors for one week, accompanied by vomiting, altered sensorium, delirium, and unresponsiveness of one-day duration. On physical examination, the patient is unconscious with pulse 82/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and blood pressure 110/60 mm Hg.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial sepsis with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe bacterial sepsis and meningococcemia can present with high fever, delirium, shock, and DIC, but patient blood samples and transfused component cultures were completely sterile.

differentials.candidate: Fulminant acute viral hepatitis with hepatic encephalopathy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Right upper quadrant tenderness, jaundice (bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL), coagulopathy, and coma raised concern for acute hepatic failure, but the coma was accompanied by heavy parasitic red blood cell infestation rather than primary hepatocyte necrosis.

TTP can present with fever, profound thrombocytopenia, altered sensorium, and markedly elevated LDH, but the coagulopathy was marked by severe DIC with hypofibrinogenemia and blood films revealed direct parasitic invasion.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of peripheral blood revealing intra-erythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum ring forms (1 per 1000 RBC) in the setting of deep unarousable coma and multi-organ dysfunction, confirming severe cerebral malaria.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male businessman residing in Srinagar presents to the hospital with acute fever, chills, diffuse myalgias, and severe headache. Two days prior to symptom onset, he had returned from a one-week trip to Delhi in October; he took no prophylactic medications before or during travel.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial viral serology confirmed acute dengue infection matching the regional Delhi outbreak, but persistence of marked fever spikes and chills despite supportive therapy prompted further investigation that revealed an active concurrent parasite infection.

Malaria was strongly considered due to travel to an endemic area without prophylaxis, chills, and thrombocytopenia, but isolated malaria could not account for the independently verified positive dengue IgM ELISA serology.

A common cause of acute high fever and headache in travelers returning from urban India, but ruled out by normal liver enzymes, normal abdominal ultrasound, and positive specific tests for viral and parasitic agents.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive IgM ELISA for dengue virus combined with Malaria Ag (pLDH/HRP2) card test positive for both Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum and blood smears showing intra-erythrocytic ring forms of P. falciparum, confirming concurrent dual infection.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old male residing in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, presents to the hospital with painful, warm nodules of various sizes across his body, in addition to gummatous subcutaneous lesions that developed over the previous two months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Empiric intravenous therapy against Staphylococcus with oxacillin and subsequently vancomycin was administered, but no bacterial growth was recovered and the patient experienced neither clinical improvement nor defervescence.

Considered because the patient was receiving methotrexate and prednisone and had nodular subcutaneous necrosis, but sterile non-infectious panniculitis was ruled out by identification of viable acid-fast bacilli and mycobacterial growth.

differentials.candidate: Polymyositis flare with reactive cutaneous vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's underlying history of polymyositis with proximal muscle weakness and elevated CPK (282 IU/L), but CPK rapidly normalized during hospitalization while cutaneous gummas and fever persisted, pointing away from an autoimmune flare.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of numerous acid-fast bacilli (+++) on repeated aspirated secretion from the gummatous lesions followed by culture growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with rapid clinical cure following quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old multiparous woman at 36 weeks of gestation with no significant past medical history presented to the emergency department with an 8-day history of malaise, chills, myalgias, jaundice, abdominal pain, and asthenia.

differentials.candidate: Viral hepatitis (HAV, HBV, HCV, CMV) and HIV
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of acute deep conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and transaminitis in a febrile patient, but eliminated by negative specific viral serologies.
Considered due to high fever, leukocytosis, elevated CRP, and multiorgan failure, but ruled out by sterile blood/urine cultures and normal biliary imaging on ultrasound.

differentials.candidate: HELLP syndrome / Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the third-trimester onset of microangiopathic-like features with thrombocytopenia, renal failure, and elevated transaminases, but rendered improbable by stable normotensive pressures, high fever, and severe myalgias.

diagnostic_pivot: Epidemiologic history of public bath exposure and positive specific IgM antibody titers established the diagnosis of severe leptospirosis complicated by multivisceral organ failure and acute respiratory distress syndrome.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old woman presented to the surgical outpatient department with a 6-month history of swelling in the right calf region associated with pain that was aggravated on walking. The swelling had been gradually increasing in size.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Suggested by ultrasound, but clinically excluded because the swelling failed to reduce on knee flexion, and intraoperative dissection revealed an intramuscular lesion rather than a popliteal synovial communication.
Considered for a fluctuant lower-extremity mass, but ruled out by completely normal vascular flow without Doppler signal abnormalities.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration of the gastrocnemius muscle cavity revealed multiple characteristic daughter cysts, confirmed as muscular hydatidosis on histopathological examination.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old previously healthy woman presented to the hospital with a 24-day history of persistent fever and headache. She had no history of overseas travel for several years and no known history of pulmonary disease.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected and treated with intravenous acyclovir, but ruled out due to lack of therapeutic response, escalating intracranial pressure, worsening CSF pleocytosis, and profound hypoglycorrhachia.
Inconsistent with the 24-day subacute duration, absence of marked nuchal rigidity on admission, and near-pure lymphocytic predominance (98% lymphocytes) rather than neutrophilia in the CSF.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeated lumbar puncture in the face of refractory intracranial hypertension demonstrated definitive microbiological evidence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis via direct microscopy and nucleic acid amplification.

clinical_summary: A 36-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of progressive nodular, ulcerative, and crusted impetiginous skin lesions involving the trunk, upper extremities, and thighs. The eruption began as small, tender nodular lesions over the trunk that gradually disseminated to the upper and lower limbs.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of vesicles, pustules, and honey-colored impetiginous crusts, but excluded by negative bacterial culture from lesion exudate.

Considered because of acute, tender polymorphic erythematous lesions accompanied by systemic fever and polyarthralgias, but ruled out on biopsy by histiocytic foamy infiltration rather than leukocytoclastic vasculitis or sterile neutrophilia.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination demonstrated a subepidermal Grenz zone with dense sheets of foamy histiocytes, and Fite acid-fast staining demonstrated numerous globi and bacilli characteristic of multibacillary lepromatous disease.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old man with a 2-year history of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), who had not received medical follow-up or antiretroviral therapy, presented to the emergency department with persistent abdominal pain for 3 weeks, accompanied by diarrhea, poor appetite, and vomiting.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial intra-abdominal abscess / perforated appendicitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected and treated empirically with intravenous antibiotics, but ruled out by complete lack of clinical improvement and persistent fevers.

Considered due to the large hypovascular lower abdominal mass and extensive para-aortic lymphadenopathy in an untreated AIDS patient, but histopathology of the resected surgical specimen revealed infectious colitis without malignant neoplasia.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency laparotomy and bowel resection revealed invasive protozoan enterocolitis with transmural gangrenous necrosis and perforation directly involving adjacent retroperitoneal structures.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male tractor driver from Pará, Brazil, with a history of rural activities, presented with a 5-month history of chronic left knee monoarthritis and polymorphic skin lesions. He had known HIV infection diagnosed two years previously without prior clinical follow-up; he had initiated zidovudine, lamivudine, and lopinavir/ritonavir 3 weeks earlier as his first antiretroviral regimen.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the ulcerated tegumentary lesions in an endemic region of Brazil, but ruled out by negative specific screening testing.
Considered due to the polymorphic papulonecrotic skin eruption and chronic destructive osteoarticular involvement in an HIV-positive host, but excluded by non-reactive nontreponemal serology.
Considered given chronic granulomatous-like monoarthritis and osteolysis in advanced immunosuppression, but blood cultures for mycobacteria and sputum molecular tests were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Biopsy of both the skin and the synovial membrane revealed characteristic round, birefringent yeast cells exhibiting multiple peripheral budding, confirmed by positive tissue culture.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of progressive painless jaundice, pruritus, acholic (clay-colored) stools, anorexia, and weight loss. On physical examination, she had marked icterus and a palpable, non-tender, cystic gallbladder (Courvoisier sign).

differentials.candidate: Metastatic ampullary adenocarcinoma (distant M1 mediastinal metastasis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected based on the high standardized uptake value (SUV max 14.7) in enlarged subcarinal nodes, but ruled out when EUS-guided nodal aspirate showed non-neoplastic granulomatous inflammation.
Inconsistent with the PET-CT imaging pattern, which revealed isolated subcarinal mediastinal nodal enlargement without any positive peripancreatic or retroperitoneal lymph nodes.

diagnostic_pivot: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) of the subcarinal node demonstrated granulomatous inflammation and positive polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus presented with a 4-month history of painless, progressive visual loss in both eyes, with the right eye affected more severely than the left.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary working diagnosis preoperatively due to brilliant contrast enhancement and extension onto the planum sphenoidale, but ruled out when intraoperative biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation rather than a dural neoplasm.
Considered as a potential granulomatous cause, but initial non-invasive screening with chest radiography and Mantoux skin testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Following resection of the mass, automated radiometric culture of the orbital tissue confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis coexisting with invasive Aspergillus fungal elements.

clinical_summary: A 41-year-old woman presented to her primary care physician with a history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain that had been present intermittently for several years but had worsened considerably over the preceding year.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Raised as the primary concern on abdominal CT due to the large multiloculated pancreatic head mass and peripancreatic adenopathy, but ruled out when tumor markers were normal and EUS-FNA cytology showed granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial intra-abdominal abscess / bacterial infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Inconsistent with the prolonged, multi-year course, absence of leukocytosis, and sterile blood cultures.

diagnostic_pivot: EUS-guided fine needle aspiration revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with negative malignancy, and subsequent AFB culture from the cell block grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male painter from São Paulo, Brazil, with no significant past medical history, presented with a 20-day history of fever, myalgia, muscle weakness, cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, epigastric pain, and lower limb edema.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary suspect due to severe acute kidney injury, profound myalgia, and elevated transaminases in Brazil, but ruled out by negative serological testing.
Considered because of oliguric renal failure, proteinuria, and active urinary sediment, but excluded by normal complement levels and negative autoantibodies.

diagnostic_pivot: A positive dengue virus IgM ELISA confirmed acute infection, and percutaneous renal biopsy confirmed acute tubular necrosis with intratubular myoglobin deposition secondary to rhabdomyolysis.

clinical_summary: A 90-year-old woman presented to the emergency department complaining of right upper quadrant abdominal pain that began approximately one month prior. She was in good physical condition, without a history of chronic medical disease, tobacco use, or alcohol abuse.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Hepatocellular carcinoma typically presents as a solid, invasive vascular mass in patients with chronic liver injury, rather than a well-demarcated spherical fluid collection with dense peripheral ring calcification and normal hematology.

Hepatic abscesses typically cause acute systemic illness, fever, and marked leukocytosis with irregular inflammatory cavity walls, which is inconsistent with this patient's chronic indolent course, normal blood counts, and calcified rim.

differentials.candidate: Polycystic liver disease and simple hepatic cysts
differentials.rule_out_reason: Simple and polycystic liver lesions are congenital thin-walled epithelial cysts lacking heavy circumferential calcification and typical hydatid architecture.

diagnostic_pivot: Prompted by the serendipitous chest radiograph finding in a rural farmer, abdominal computed tomography and ultrasonography were performed, confirming the classical features of an 8.5 x 9.5 cm hydatid cyst localized to the right hepatic lobe.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old boy with no prior medical history presented with progressive headache, vomiting, and right-sided weakness developing over the preceding 3 months. There was no reported history of fever or seizures.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The large size, calcification, irregular enhancement, prominent perilesional edema, and severe mass effect initially raised high suspicion for a malignant neuroepithelial tumor, but intraoperative findings showed a firm, avascular mass with granulomatous histology.

differentials.candidate: HIV-associated intracranial opportunistic lesion or CNS lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Focal mass lesions with marked surrounding vasogenic edema in endemic areas require ruling out immunosuppression-associated infections or lymphoma, but serologic screening was non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid neurologic deterioration dictated urgent craniotomy, where complete excision of a firm, yellowish, avascular intra-axial lesion demonstrated histopathologic features diagnostic of an intracranial tuberculoma in a child from an endemic area.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old boy presented with a 4-month history of persistent fever, diaphoresis, and anorexia. He had a history of travel 4 months earlier to a province located in northern Iran.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The combination of prolonged fever, cytopenias, massive organomegaly, and deep retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy strongly mimicked a malignant lymphoproliferative process or primary HPS, but the hyperinflammatory syndrome was secondary to an occult protozoan infection.
Bacterial bloodstream infection was suspected as a trigger for prolonged fever and severe systemic inflammation, but microbiological cultures remained sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite three initial negative bone marrow aspirates causing a substantial diagnostic dilemma, persistence of clinical suspicion led to a fourth bone marrow aspiration, which definitively revealed intracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies within marrow macrophages.

clinical_summary: An 8-year-old boy from Tehran presented with a 2-month history of prolonged fever, abdominal pain, and jaundice. He had a travel history to a province located in northern Iran 4 months prior to presentation.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral hepatitis (HAV, HBV, HCV, HDV) and systemic viral infections (CMV, EBV, HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Marked jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, transaminitis, and systemic toxicity prompted extensive evaluation for viral hepatitis and acute mononucleosis-like viruses, but targeted serological assays were completely negative.

Hemolytic jaundice, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and fever in a returning traveler raised suspicion for endemic blood protozoa or spirochetes, but peripheral smear and serologic testing were negative.
Severe toxicity, leukopenia, and pleural effusion suggested occult severe bacterial infection, but blood and urine cultures were sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Although three consecutive bone marrow aspirates from the patient were negative, the patient presented with full features of secondary hemophagocytic syndrome, and his co-traveling older brother had an identical clinical presentation with a bone marrow aspirate definitively demonstrating Leishman-Donovan bodies and hemophagocytosis.

clinical_summary: A 64-year-old woman with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus presented to the dermatology department with a 20-month history of nonpruritic, erythematous, ulcerated lesions on both lower legs. She reported no history of local trauma or insect bites, and denied fever or constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a diabetic patient, chronic atrophic violaceous pretibial plaques with indurated borders are classic for necrobiosis lipoidica; however, histopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation containing intracellular amastigotes rather than interstitial collagen degeneration.
Crusted, necrotic ulcerations on the lower limbs in diabetes frequently stem from bacterial infections, but bacteriological investigations showed no pathogenic bacterial growth.

diagnostic_pivot: A skin biopsy showed a dense dermal lymphocytic and granulomatous infiltrate with multinucleated giant cells, and Giemsa staining identified pathognomonic intracellular basophilic structures corresponding to Leishmania amastigotes.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old woman presented with a 1-year history of a painless, slowly enlarging lump in her left breast. She had no family history of breast malignancy, no prior use of oral contraceptives or estrogen therapy, and no history of nipple discharge.

differentials.candidate: Isolated metastatic ductal carcinoma (without concurrent infectious lymphadenitis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The breast mass and palpable axillary lymphadenopathy were clinically and cytologically diagnosed as carcinoma metastatic to axillary lymph nodes; however, final histopathology demonstrated that nodal enlargement was overwhelmingly due to coexistent granulomatous inflammation.

Tender axillary lymphadenopathy adjacent to a breast neoplasm could represent reactive hyperplasia, but histopathology revealed necrotizing caseating granulomas rather than benign reactive proliferation alone.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of 14 excised axillary lymph nodes revealed that 13 nodes harbored tuberculous lymphadenitis with caseating granulomas and Langhans' giant cells, confirmed by a positive Ziehl-Neelsen stain for acid-fast bacilli coexisting with carcinomatous deposits.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old Gabonese woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with glibenclamide presented with a 7-day history of high fever, weakness, headache, vomiting, and a painful right knee.

differentials.candidate: Pseudomonas aeruginosa / Pseudomonas spp. bacteremia and septic arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Isolates from blood, abscess, and synovial fluid were initially classified phenotypically as Pseudomonas species, but melioidosis is inherently resistant to cephalosporins like ceftriaxone, and genomic typing later refuted this classification.

differentials.candidate: Staphylococcal or Streptococcal pyogenic abscess and septic arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Cutaneous wound abscesses and septic monoarthritis in diabetic agriculturalists are commonly caused by gram-positive pyogenic cocci, but no typical gram-positive pathogens were recovered.

diagnostic_pivot: Subsequent multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and whole-genome sequencing reclassified the gram-negative bacillus as Burkholderia pseudomallei (strain Gb100), confirming fatal septicemic melioidosis.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old woman presented with recurrent upper abdominal pain of 3 years' duration, which had notably increased in frequency over the preceding year. She had no significant co-morbidities.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The periampullary mass on MRCP and elevated CA 19-9 pointed to primary periampullary malignancy as the sole cause of ductal dilation and symptoms, but endoscopic imaging revealed an intraluminal parasite inside the pancreatic duct.
Recurrent biliary-pancreatic colic with elevated canalicular enzymes suggested ductal calculi, but imaging showed an elongated non-shadowing tubular structure rather than calcified shadowing stones.

diagnostic_pivot: Endoscopic ultrasound revealed characteristic long, linear, non-shadowing echogenic strips within the dilated main pancreatic duct representing an adult Ascaris lumbricoides worm, which was subsequently extracted via ERCP prior to oncologic resection.

clinical_summary: A 48-year-old woman presented with a 20-day history of non-radiating right upper quadrant and epigastric pain associated with nausea and dyspeptic bloating. She had no previous history of chronic respiratory illness or contact with chronically ill individuals.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A subcapsular cystic liver mass in an adult typically indicates bacterial pyogenic abscess, but aspiration fluid cultures showed no bacterial or fungal growth and the lesion persisted despite 14 days of parenteral metronidazole and ciprofloxacin.

Amebic abscess is a prominent cause of solitary subcapsular hepatic collections, but stool microscopy showed no cysts or ova, amebic serology was negative, and the lesion failed to regress on metronidazole therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Repeat CT-guided aspiration yielded cloudy cream-colored pus that was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis by PCR, and subsequent laparoscopic peritoneal biopsy demonstrated granulomatous peritonitis with caseating necrosis.

clinical_summary: A 38-year-old male Guatemalan soldier presented to a military medical center with recurrent fever and fatigue. Three months earlier, he had returned from a 9-month military deployment in Africa (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and Kenya), where he slept under an untreated bed net and took weekly mefloquine chemoprophylaxis with intermittent missed doses.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute fever, thrombocytopenia, coastal travel in Guatemala, and a positive rapid dengue diagnostic assay suggested dengue, but the patient's recurrent cyclical fevers and persistent intraerythrocytic parasites confirmed a protozoan etiology.

differentials.candidate: Autochthonous Plasmodium vivax / Plasmodium falciparum malaria
differentials.rule_out_reason: Endemic Central American malaria species were presumed by regional microscopy, but the hospital microbiologist recognized atypical morphological features, and molecular assays ruled out vivax and falciparum.

diagnostic_pivot: Plasmodium genus-specific nested PCR and real-time PCR performed on whole blood established a P. ovale mono-infection, and BLAST sequence analysis confirmed the classic subtype P. ovale curtisi, verified by the CDC Malaria Branch.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old male with no significant past medical or social history presented with high-grade fever and right hypochondrial pain of two weeks' duration. On physical examination, the patient was febrile, visibly jaundiced, and had tender hepatomegaly palpable just below the right costal margin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical triad of fever, jaundice, and right hypochondrial pain with severe cholestatic jaundice suggested choledocholithiasis complicated by ascending cholangitis, but biliary ductal obstruction was caused by laminated parasitic membranes and cystic debris rather than gallstones.

High-grade fever, tender hepatomegaly, and right upper quadrant pain raised concern for a pyogenic bacterial liver abscess, but imaging and serology demonstrated a defined intraparenchymal cyst communicating directly with the biliary tree rather than a suppurative bacterial cavity.

diagnostic_pivot: Serologic testing was positive and abdominal CT demonstrated an intraparenchymal hepatic cyst opening into the common bile duct with intraluminal hydatid membranes, confirmed by surgical evacuation.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old man residing in Eastern France presented with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and a profound inflammatory syndrome. One month previously, he had been hospitalized in the intensive care unit for acute calculous cholecystitis associated with severe sepsis, which resolved without hepatic collection at that time.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Recent hospitalization for acute calculous cholecystitis and severe sepsis with marked procalcitonin elevation strongly favored a secondary bacterial pyogenic liver abscess, but diagnostic aspiration was sterile on bacteriological culture.
Residence in Eastern France and partitioned hepatic cystic collections raised concern for Echinococcus multilocularis or E. granulosus, but serologic screening for both larval cestodes was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: High-titer positivity on ELISA and latex agglutination serologies, followed by specific Entamoeba histolytica DNA PCR amplification from the hepatic aspirate, confirmed amebic liver abscess despite a 22-year latency period.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old European male with HIV infection diagnosed in 1985 presented with a history of drenching sweats, increasing abdominal distension, and severe lethargy. He had traveled to Spain in 1992.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Visceral Kaposi's sarcoma is a well-recognized complication of advanced HIV immunodeficiency presenting with organomegaly and skin lesions, prompting chemotherapeutic consideration, but histology lacked spindle cell neoplastic changes.

Drenching sweats, hepatosplenomegaly, and worsening pancytopenia in an HIV-positive patient with low CD4 count strongly suggested lymphoma or disseminated mycobacterial infection, but bone marrow analysis demonstrated parasitic amastigotes.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic demonstration of intracellular amastigotes in bone marrow aspirates and tissue biopsies confirmed visceral leishmaniasis, subsequently corroborated by urine antigen detection.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old asthmatic male presented with right cervical lymphadenopathy and fever. His past medical history was notable for carcinoma of the tongue treated 10 years earlier with left hemiglossectomy and suprahyoidal neck dissection.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Prior history of tongue carcinoma made locoregional metastatic recurrence the leading initial suspicion, but whole-body imaging showed diffuse multi-station nodal involvement (cervical, mediastinal, abdominal, pelvic, femoral) atypical for head and neck metastasis.

Widespread supradiaphragmatic and infradiaphragmatic lymphadenopathy with intense FDG avidity raised strong suspicion of lymphoma, but fine-needle aspiration demonstrated acid-fast bacilli rather than neoplastic lymphoid proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Cervical lymph node fine-needle aspiration cytology demonstrating strong positivity for acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, together with a strongly positive tuberculin skin test (15 mm induration), established extrapulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 13-year-old male was admitted with a one-week history of fever and asthenia. He had end-stage renal failure attributed to vesicoureteral reflux and had undergone a second deceased-donor renal transplantation three months previously.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute febrile respiratory illness with pulmonary consolidation and elevated inflammatory markers in an immunosuppressed host suggested typical or atypical bacterial pneumonia, but cavitary progression and persistent fevers prompted invasive evaluation.

Invasive fungal infection is a leading cause of cavitary lung lesions in solid organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive therapy, but bronchoscopic microbiological workup revealed mycobacteria rather than fungal pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite a negative tuberculin skin test (secondary to immunosuppressive anergy) and negative gastric aspirates, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrated Mycobacterium tuberculosis, fully susceptible to first-line agents.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old male residing in Apucarana, Paraná, Brazil, presented for evaluation of an atypical cutaneous lesion on the right side of his back that had been present for approximately one month.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The prominent plaque architecture, desquamation, and marked lichenification clinically mimicked chronic inflammatory or papulosquamous dermatoses, but ulcerated margins, refractoriness to conservative topical measures, and parasite demonstration excluded them.
Endemic South American subcutaneous fungal infections frequently manifest as large, verrucous, or ulcerated plaques, but mycological examinations were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct examination of lesion scrapings stained with Giemsa identified Leishmania amastigotes, supported by culture in blood base agar, a positive Montenegro skin test (10 mm induration), and positive indirect immunofluorescence.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old previously healthy male from southern Saudi Arabia presented with a 3-month history of acute-onset, progressive severe lower back pain, followed by progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness, urinary incontinence, and loss of sensation below the umbilicus, leaving him wheelchair-bound.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive myelopathy with longitudinally extensive cord edema initially responded transiently to pulse corticosteroids, mimicking autoimmune myelitis, but the patient suffered prompt clinical relapse and autoimmune workup was negative.
An extensive T6–T9 mass-like lesion raised suspicion for viral myelopathy (HIV, CMV, EBV) or paraneoplastic/neoplastic disease, but CSF cytology and viral serologies were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: A high Schistosoma antibody titer (1:64) combined with definitive spinal cord biopsy confirmed schistosomal granulomatous myelopathy.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old previously healthy Saudi male presented with a 2-month history of progressive bilateral lower limb weakness and urinary incontinence, accompanied by pain in the right thigh. He denied fever, upper extremity symptoms, headache, trauma, or constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Progressive paraparesis, conus hyperintensity, and positive CSF oligoclonal bands raised high suspicion for demyelinating disease, but brain MRI was normal and Schistosoma serology was massively elevated.
Endemic granulomatous spinal infections in the Arabian Peninsula were considered given CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis, but serologic screening for brucellosis and other pathogens was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Markedly elevated Schistosoma antibody titers on two occasions (1:512 and 1:4096) in a patient with conus medullaris myelopathy and travel to Egypt confirmed spinal schistosomiasis, even with negative ova on rectal biopsy and stool/urine exams.

clinical_summary: A 69-year-old female with an unremarkable past medical history presented for evaluation of persistent dyspepsia. She denied weight loss, anorexia, asthenia, or vomiting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A smooth subepithelial bulge along the lesser curvature and posterior gastric wall initially suggested a primary gastric mesenchymal neoplasm, but endosonography demonstrated that the lesion originated from the adjacent left hepatic lobe.

An anechoic left hepatic fluid collection could represent a benign simple liver cyst or mucinous cystic neoplasm, but endosonography revealed an internal undulating membrane, and pathology confirmed a laminated parasitic wall.

diagnostic_pivot: Endoscopic ultrasound demonstrating a predominantly anechoic hepatic lesion containing a characteristic floating membrane (type 3 cyst), confirmed by histopathology showing an acellular lamellar wall with vestigial protoscolex.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old male from a rural coastal village in Esmeraldas province, Ecuador, presented for evaluation of chronic, widespread skin eruptions. At age 16, papules had first appeared on his left knee and right cheek, which progressively increased in size and number over eight years.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Widespread infiltrated papules and nodules involving the face and earlobes closely mimicked lepromatous leprosy—leading to prior empiric multidrug therapy—but absence of peripheral nerve hypertrophy, preserved cutaneous sensation, and absence of acid-fast bacilli excluded it.

differentials.candidate: Disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis (DCL) vs. localized cutaneous leishmaniasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The extensive non-ulcerating cutaneous dissemination was distinguished from localized or disseminated disease by the presence of specific cellular anergy against parasite antigen with intact response to other skin antigens.

diagnostic_pivot: Slit-skin smears and histopathology demonstrating foamy histiocytes packed with innumerable Leishmania amastigotes without acid-fast bacilli, confirmed as Leishmania mexicana by PCR analysis.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old woman from Balao Chico, Guayas province, Ecuador—a rural mountainous area located at an altitude of 200 meters above sea level—was transferred to a specialized hospital for evaluation of a generalized, non-healing skin eruption.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the rapid eruptive appearance of hundreds of generalized vesiculopustular, crusting cutaneous lesions. However, the patient's lesions followed an indolent, weeks-long chronic trajectory without typical systemic toxicity or spontaneous crisis, and showed zero clinical improvement across two separate hospitalizations.

Considered initially as a presumptive diagnosis of generalized cutaneous fungal granulomatosis endemic to South America, but direct microscopic examination of ulcer material showed no characteristic yeast forms.

Considered because the excavated ulcers were covered with thick crusts and draining purulent fluid; however, microscopic evaluation and culture of ulcer exudate failed to detect Staphylococcus aureus, revealing secondary beta-hemolytic streptococcus instead.

Suspected early in the clinical course because of intense right lumbar pain and localized vesicular eruption; ruled out by widespread non-dermatomal dissemination into 308 ulcerative lesions spanning the entire body.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of multiple skin lesion smear samples confirmed scanty intracellular amastigotes, subsequently identified by species-specific monoclonal antibody serodeme analysis as Leishmania (Viannia) panamensis, alongside stool microscopy demonstrating concurrent triple intestinal infection with Trichuris trichiura, Ascaris lumbricoides, and Ancylostoma duodenale.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old man from a small rural community in Chimborazo province, Ecuador—a subtropical mountainous area situated at the base of the Andean slopes at an altitude of 500 meters above sea level—presented for evaluation of chronic, widespread cutaneous lesions with mucosal involvement.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the extensive, confluent papulonodular lesions covering the trunk and extremities. Ruled out by the presence of superficial mucosal involvement of the nose and lip (which does not occur in diffuse CL), intact delayed-type hypersensitivity on skin testing (17-mm induration), responsiveness to antimonials, and molecular identification of Leishmania (Viannia) guyanensis rather than an anergic Leishmania mexicana complex species.

Considered early during the single insect-bite-like papular stage on the forearm; excluded by the subsequent two-year multi-anatomic dissemination across the lower extremities, thorax, abdomen, ears, nose, and mucosal surfaces.

diagnostic_pivot: Detection of scanty intracellular amastigotes on smear examination of active lesions, accompanied by a robust 17-mm positive Montenegro delayed-type hypersensitivity skin reaction and definitive PCR identification of Leishmania (Viannia) guyanensis from biopsy and FTA card specimens, confirming disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old male farmer from the Philippines with a history of diabetes mellitus presented for further evaluation of persistent fever and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. He had no history of international travel.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the two-week history of high-grade fever, right upper abdominal pain, and geographic endemicity in the Philippines. Ruled out by the lack of clinical response to four days of intravenous ampicillin-sulbactam and cross-sectional imaging demonstrating a discrete, localized segment 8 hepatic abscess.

differentials.candidate: Typical pyogenic liver abscess (Enterobacteriaceae / Klebsiella pneumoniae)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered given the segment 8 liver abscess in a patient with diabetes mellitus. However, the infection failed to respond to initial broad-spectrum beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor coverage and needle aspiration cultures specifically yielded Burkholderia pseudomallei.

diagnostic_pivot: Percutaneous laparoscopic ultrasound-guided aspiration of the segment 8 hepatic lesion yielded purulent exudate whose culture demonstrated moderate growth of Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming hepatic melioidosis and prompting prompt transition to intravenous meropenem.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old girl presented to a pediatric clinic for evaluation of persistent neck swelling, low back pain, and progressive hip pain. She lived with a crowded family in Turkey in a low socioeconomic setting.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the insidious onset of hip and low back pain, marked gait disorder, elevated ESR/CRP, and reactive thrombocytosis in an adolescent. Ruled out by thoracic and pelvic advanced cross-sectional imaging revealing a pulmonary Ghon complex, T8-T10 Pott's disease with paraspinal abscess, and tuberculous hip arthritis with intramuscular cystic cold abscesses.

Considered because of Turkey's endemicity and the combination of musculoskeletal spinal and hip involvement with constitutional symptoms and high inflammatory markers. Excluded by a negative Brucella agglutination test.
Considered initially as a simple localized adenitis, but ruled out because the enlarged cervical lymph node showed no response or reduction in size following a course of broad-spectrum antibiotics.

diagnostic_pivot: Cross-sectional thoracic and pelvic imaging demonstrating coexistent classic pulmonary Ghon complex on CT, T8-T10 Pott's abscess on spine MRI, and tuberculous hip arthritis on pelvic MRI, in conjunction with a 16-mm PPD induration and household contact history.

clinical_summary: An 11-year-old boy presented with a 5-day history of drooping of both eyelids, accompanied by headache and unsteady walking for the past 2 days. He had no history of fever, seizures, or visual loss.

differentials.candidate: Ocular myasthenia gravis / neuromuscular junction disorder
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of subacute bilateral symmetrical ptosis in a pediatric patient with normal pupillary reactions. Excluded by the rapid development of headache, ipsilateral cerebellar signs (dysdiadochokinesia and ataxia), and brain imaging demonstrating an intracranial focal mass.

Considered given the solitary ring-enhancing dorsal midbrain lesion with extensive surrounding edema causing cerebellar and brainstem signs in a child. Excluded by proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrating a massive lipid peak characteristic of central caseous necrosis rather than high malignant choline proliferation, together with complete resolution on medical antitubercular therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: Brain MRI revealing a dorsal midbrain ring-enhancing lesion with extensive vasogenic edema, coupled with MR spectroscopy demonstrating an elevated lipid resonance and decreased NAA characteristic of a CNS tuberculoma, in a child with known epidemiologic exposure who achieved full clinical recovery with 4-drug ATT and corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old man presented to a tertiary neurosurgical center following an acute neurological deterioration during an acute systemic febrile illness. The patient had an acute onset of high-grade fever lasting for 7 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because 7 days of high-grade fever followed by sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness, and sinus bradycardia raised immediate suspicion of central nervous system infection with severe intracranial hypertension. Ruled out by urgent cranial CT showing acute ventriculomegaly caused by an obstructive hemorrhagic sellar and suprasellar mass at the foramen of Monro rather than diffuse encephalitis.

Considered due to the sudden hemorrhage into a pituitary neoplasm. However, isolated spontaneous apoplexy does not explain the week-long high-grade fever, systemic capillary leakage, and profound thrombocytopenia (platelet count 27,000/mm3), which were directly precipitated by acute severe dengue infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological confirmation of acute dengue infection (positive NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies) with severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count 27,000/mm3) that triggered catastrophic intratumoral hemorrhage into an occult ACTH-positive pituitary adenoma, causing acute obstructive hydrocephalus at the foramen of Monro.

clinical_summary: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of progressive abdominal fullness, accompanied by poor appetite, general malaise, and an involuntary weight loss of approximately 6 kg over the same period.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis based on subacute weight loss, prominent ovaries, dilated fallopian tubes, multiloculated ascites, omental stranding, and a significantly elevated CA-125 level of 188.6 U/mL. Excluded when surgical biopsies demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, Langhans giant cells, and acid-fast bacilli without malignant cells.

Considered due to peritoneal thickening, mesenteric nodules, omental infiltration, and retroperitoneal adenopathy. Excluded by the absence of an ileocecal or other luminal digestive tract tumor on CT, and definitive biopsy findings demonstrating necrotizing caseating granulomatous infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic evaluation of operative biopsies obtained from the peritoneum, ovary, and fallopian tube demonstrating chronic granulomatous inflammation with central caseous necrosis, epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and positive acid-fast staining for mycobacterial bacilli.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old boy presented with a 6-month history of persistent pain and progressive swelling over the medial aspect of his left foot of unclear etiology. The pain had progressively worsened to the point where he was unable to bear weight on the affected limb.

differentials.candidate: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis / chronic inflammatory monoarthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the chronic 6-month course of joint pain, swelling, and antalgic gait in a child lacking systemic fever. Ruled out by plain radiographs demonstrating focal marginal erosions of the talonavicular joint and histological confirmation of caseating necrotic granulomas with subsequent culture growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial septic arthritis / acute osteomyelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the erosive destructive changes of the midtarsal bones and inability to bear weight. Ruled out by the indolent 6-month chronicity, absence of fever or constitutional toxicity, normal white blood cell count, and synovial aspirate yielding caseating granulomas rather than acute neutrophilic suppurative infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Image intensifier-guided needle biopsy of the talonavicular joint yielding thick grayish-white purulent fluid that revealed epithelioid granulomas with caseating necrosis on histopathology and grew Koch's bacillus (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) on mycobacterial culture.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old woman from Chitwan District, Nepal, presented to a tertiary hospital with a 9-day history of persistent high-grade fever. She reported frequent visits to the jungle to gather firewood and graze cattle.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the acute onset of high fever, jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, acute thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and occupational jungle exposure in Nepal. Excluded by negative serological antibody testing for Leptospira IgM and IgG.

Considered because of prolonged high-grade remittent fever, hepatosplenomegaly, vomiting, and headache in an endemic tropical region. Ruled out by a negative Widal agglutination test and the clinical identification of dual necrotic cigarette-burn cutaneous eschars.

Considered due to high intermittent fever accompanied by chills, rigors, sweating, jaundice, and splenomegaly. Ruled out by repeated negative peripheral blood smear examinations for plasmodial parasites.

diagnostic_pivot: Physical examination identification of dual necrotic cigarette-burn cutaneous eschars on the right deltoid and waist in an exposed forest worker with pleural effusion, confirmed by positive rapid immunochromatography for Dengue IgM/IgG and positive ELISA serology for Scrub Typhus, verifying dual acute coinfection.

clinical_summary: A 54-year-old Thai agricultural worker residing in Nakhon Si Thammarat presented to the emergency department with a 1-month history of persistent fever and right upper abdominal pain. He had no known past medical or surgical history, and had no prior diagnosis of diabetes or immune compromise.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of a 1-month history of fever, right upper quadrant pain, and hepatomegaly in a tropical endemic area. Ruled out because amebiasis typically presents as large solitary or confluent cavity lesions rather than multiple scattered microabscesses complicated by portal vein thrombosis, and blood cultures yielded Burkholderia pseudomallei.

differentials.candidate: Typical enteric pyogenic liver abscess / pylephlebitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of suppurative pylephlebitis with portal vein thrombosis and jaundice in a patient with severe uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. Excluded by the lack of an identifiable gastrointestinal luminal source (e.g., appendicitis or diverticulitis) and microbiological isolation of Burkholderia pseudomallei.

Considered given the 1-month subacute duration, marked alkaline phosphatase elevation, and chronic-appearing portal vein obstruction with cavernous transformation. Excluded by the acute septic clinical presentation, lack of a focal neoplastic parenchyma lesion, complete recanalization following targeted antimicrobial and anticoagulant therapy, and blood cultures positive for Burkholderia pseudomallei.

diagnostic_pivot: Isolation of Burkholderia pseudomallei in blood culture from a newly diagnosed diabetic farmer in Thailand presenting with multiple small hepatic microabscesses and left portal vein thrombosis with cavernous transformation, establishing the diagnosis of systemic melioidosis complicated by septic pylephlebitis.

clinical_summary: A 17-year-old female was admitted to the emergency department at 2:50 AM with refractory generalized tonic-clonic seizures. She had a remote past medical history of childhood seizures diagnosed at eight years of age, for which she received diphenylhydantoin for two years; the anticonvulsant was successfully discontinued at age ten with no subsequent seizure activity.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteroviruses are frequent pathogens responsible for acute outbreaks of pediatric meningoencephalitis presenting with status epilepticus; however, molecular testing in the cerebrospinal fluid was negative.

differentials.candidate: Breakthrough status epilepticus secondary to remote childhood epilepsy
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient had a remote history of seizures treated in childhood, but simple seizure recurrence does not account for the rapid onset of devastating cerebral edema and severe ventricular collapse leading directly to brain death.

diagnostic_pivot: The demonstration of positive dengue nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) antigen by enzyme-linked immunoassay confirmed acute dengue infection presenting as fatal neurotropic dengue encephalopathy with status epilepticus.

clinical_summary: A 14-year-old female presented to the emergency department at 2:20 AM with acute high-grade fever, progressive headache, and new-onset generalized seizures. Her symptoms began approximately 12 hours after her elder sibling experienced an acute, catastrophic neurological illness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteroviruses are recognized causes of clustered viral central nervous system infections leading to agitation, status epilepticus, and severe cerebral edema in children and teenagers, but CSF PCR was negative.

differentials.candidate: Acute toxic ingestion / common household poisoning
differentials.rule_out_reason: The rapid occurrence of severe seizures and encephalopathy in two siblings within a 12-hour window strongly raised suspicion for an environmental or household toxin, but high sustained fever (39 °C) and absence of toxicological findings argued for an infectious etiology.

diagnostic_pivot: Serum serology was positive for nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) antigen by ELISA, establishing severe neurotropic dengue virus infection complicated by malignant intracranial hypertension, cerebral edema, and uncal herniation.

clinical_summary: A 6-year-old female resident of Axochiapan, Morelos, was evaluated at a local community health center for acute onset of fever. Her symptoms began on June 3, coinciding with the acute onset of severe febrile and neurological illnesses in two older siblings within the same household.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Because multiple children in the same home presented with acute symptoms within days of one another, toxic ingestion was investigated; however, detailed maternal questioning and anti-doping screens revealed no evidence of toxic exposure, and this child exhibited no toxidromic signs.

The patient presented with mild, isolated fever responding well to paracetamol, which resembled an ordinary childhood viral upper respiratory infection, but epidemiologic link to severe household sibling cases prompted specific arboviral testing.

diagnostic_pivot: Due to the severe neurological complications observed in her siblings, serum serology for dengue NS1 antigen was performed via ELISA and returned positive, confirming mild acute dengue virus infection.

clinical_summary: A 36-month-old child of low socioeconomic status was brought to the clinic with an eight-month history of persistent pain and progressive swelling over the dorsum of the right hand, complicated by the development of a discharging sinus over the preceding two months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial osteomyelitis typically responds to standard broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy and yields positive bacterial cultures, whereas this patient experienced treatment failure with amoxicillin-clavulanate and showed sterile purulent drainage.

An expansile, cystic, and lytic bone lesion with cortical erosion on plain radiography strongly suggested a benign or malignant bone neoplasm; however, the presence of a draining sinus and histopathologic findings of caseating granulomas excluded malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive tuberculin skin testing followed by intra-osseous biopsy of the metacarpal lesion demonstrating classic caseous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid and Langhans giant cells established the diagnosis of isolated tuberculous dactylitis.

clinical_summary: A 40-year-old male traveler arriving from Monrovia, Liberia, via transit stops in Accra, Ghana, and Lomé, Togo, collapsed acutely at the international airport terminal in Lagos, Nigeria, on July 20, 2014.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Malaria is the leading cause of acute febrile collapse in travelers arriving in West Africa, but the patient exhibited persistent high fever and multi-system clinical deterioration despite empiric antimalarial treatment.

differentials.candidate: Typhoid fever (enteric fever / Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Enteric fever frequently causes sustained high fevers, sore throat, and gastrointestinal symptoms in this region, but failed to improve with antibacterial therapy and progressed to hemorrhagic manifestations.
Lassa virus and dengue virus are endemic causes of viral hemorrhagic fever in West Africa, but singleplex RT-PCR of blood and urine specimens yielded no amplification products.

diagnostic_pivot: Reverse transcriptase PCR targeting the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L) gene on patient blood and urine samples successfully amplified the diagnostic 300-bp filovirus amplicon, subsequently sequenced and matched to Zaire ebolavirus.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old female presented for rheumatologic evaluation due to severe pain radiating from the right inguinal region and right hip down to the right knee. She had a long-standing history of intermittent low back pain, but over the preceding week, she developed constant right hip and groin pain radiating to the knee that worsened with rest.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to inflammatory back pain, asymmetric peripheral arthritis, and sacroiliac bone marrow edema on MRI, but the patient was 53 years of age, lacked a family history, and tested negative for HLA-B27.

differentials.candidate: Tuberculous arthritis or bacterial septic arthritis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of unilateral knee synovitis with significant joint effusion; however, arthrocentesis yielded non-purulent fluid with 8,000 leukocytes/µL, negative Gram stain, and negative mycobacterial PCR and cultures.
Brucellosis is a prominent endemic cause of peripheral arthritis accompanied by sacroiliitis, but specific serological tests were completely negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal CT demonstrating the classic 'water-lily sign' combined with a strongly positive indirect hemagglutination titer (1/320) confirmed hydatid cyst disease (echinococcosis) as the underlying antigenic driver of reactive arthritis and sacroiliitis.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old male with a one-year history of histologically confirmed idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (polymyositis) was admitted for evaluation of an indolent soft tissue swelling. For management of his underlying muscle disease, he had been maintained on high-dose systemic corticosteroid therapy (initially 1 mg/kg daily, subsequently tapered over ten weeks to 1 mg/kg on alternate days) and weekly oral methotrexate titrated...

differentials.candidate: Acute pyogenic bacterial abscess (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial pyogenic abscesses are typically characterized by cardinal inflammatory signs including acute pain, erythema, and local heat; in contrast, this patient presented with an indolent 'cold' lesion, and histology showed non-specific necrosis without typical pyogenic bacterial isolates.

Prolonged methotrexate immunosuppression predisposes to opportunistic lymphoproliferative malignancies presenting with painless lymphadenopathy; however, lymph node biopsy and abscess aspiration demonstrated abundant mycobacterial growth rather than malignant lymphoid proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Culture confirmation from aspirated abscess fluid and axillary lymph node biopsy demonstrating niacin and nitrate reduction, corroborated by devR gene RFLP and rapid bacteriophage assay, established the diagnosis of extrapulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old man from a middle-class socioeconomic background was admitted to a tertiary care hospital with a one-month history of persistent fever, vague abdominal pain, and progressive abdominal distention. He reported no history of hematemesis, melena, cough, breathlessness, chest pain, joint pain, or changes in bowel habits, and had no prior personal or familial history of liver disease.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prominent constitutional symptoms, profound leukocytosis, extreme thrombocytosis, and exudative ascites; however, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy, and CEA level (1.97 ng/mL) were normal, and ascitic cytology was negative for malignant cells.

Cirrhosis was considered in the setting of ascites and jaundice; however, the patient lacked clinical stigmata of chronic liver disease, prothrombin time was normal, and ascitic fluid revealed an exudate with 95% lymphocytes and sterile cultures.

Prolonged fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and hyperbilirubinemia in an endemic area suggested visceral leishmaniasis, but the rK39 rapid antigen test was negative, and the peripheral blood showed marked leukocytosis rather than pancytopenia.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative tuberculin skin testing and negative sputum smears, analysis of ascitic fluid demonstrating a lymphocytic-predominant (95%) exudate (protein 38 g/L) with elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA 22.6 U/L) in a patient with a leukemoid reaction prompted empiric antituberculous therapy, resulting in complete resolution of fever and ascites.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old male was transferred by emergency ambulance to a tertiary hospital due to high fever, progressive fatigue, and acute cognitive alteration. The patient had returned to Japan two weeks prior following a six-month business trip to Nigeria.

differentials.candidate: Viral upper respiratory tract infection ('common cold')
differentials.rule_out_reason: Repeatedly diagnosed in outpatient clinics; however, an uncomplicated upper respiratory tract viral illness does not account for altered consciousness, severe thrombocytopenia (17,000/µL), and marked hyperbilirubinemia (5.1 mg/dL).

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial sepsis with disseminated intravascular coagulation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to high fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, severe thrombocytopenia, and elevated CRP (23.14 mg/dL), but the patient had deteriorated despite oral cephalosporin therapy (cefaclor) and showed prominent hemolysis without septic shock.

diagnostic_pivot: Emergency microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear revealed erythrocytes parasitized by Plasmodium falciparum ring forms with a parasitemia index of 5.4%, confirmed by a positive rapid immunochromatographic antigen test and PCR.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old female presented with progressive weakness and heaviness in both lower extremities that had steadily worsened over the preceding two months, severely impairing her ability to walk. Her past medical history was notable for having undergone four surgical procedures over the preceding six years for recurrent multi-organ visceral cystic lesions affecting the lungs and liver.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Arachnoid cysts can present as benign T2-hyperintense dorsal epidural fluid collections causing spinal cord compression; however, they typically present as single unilocular collections without bony involvement or thick inflammatory epidural reactive tissue.

Primary spinal cord nerve sheath tumors can undergo cystic degeneration causing progressive paraparesis, but typically demonstrate solid nodular contrast enhancement and do not span six vertebral segments as multiple daughter cysts.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration via T7 laminectomy revealed multiple extradural and bony cysts with whitish laminated membranes and debris, which on parasitologic and histopathologic examination confirmed Echinococcus granulosus (hydatid disease) in a patient with a history of recurrent pulmonary and hepatic cysts.

clinical_summary: A 75-year-old male from rural West Virginia was transferred to the intensive care unit for progressive respiratory failure and septic shock. His medical history was notable for rheumatoid arthritis treated with infliximab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate, a recent gout flare treated with a prednisolone taper, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, stage III chronic kidney disease, deep vein thrombosis complicated by gastrointestinal...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and hyponatremia were initially attributed to diabetic gastropathy and dehydration, but the patient rapidly progressed to refractory septic shock and respiratory failure unresponsive to prokinetic therapy and fluid resuscitation.

New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate alongside bilateral pulmonary infiltrates raised suspicion for acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema, but BNP was normal (51 pg/mL) and aggressive diuresis produced no clinical or radiographic improvement.
Bilateral multifocal airspace disease in a critically ill patient suggested hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia or secondary ARDS, but repeated blood and respiratory cultures remained sterile.

diagnostic_pivot: Bronchoscopy performed for refractory infiltrates demonstrated diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid revealed Strongyloides stercoralis larvae, confirming Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome triggered by anti-TNF biologic therapy and corticosteroids in an Appalachian resident.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department following a first-time generalized tonic-clonic seizure. Over the preceding six months, he had noted anorexia and an unintentional weight loss of 8 kg, without fever, night sweats, or other constitutional symptoms.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions accompanied by massive mesenteric infiltration, lymphadenopathy, and progressive 8 kg weight loss strongly suggested disseminated metastatic disease, but extensive radiographic and subsequent histological evaluation found no neoplastic primary.

Multiple ring-enhancing intracerebral lesions with prominent vasogenic edema favored pyogenic abscesses on neuroimaging, but the patient had no fever, focal neurological signs, or elevated inflammatory focus, and all blood and CSF cultures were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Histological examination of the mesenteric lesions revealed multiple noncaseating perivascular granulomas, and tissue PCR was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming disseminated central nervous system and peritoneal tuberculosis in an immunocompetent patient.

clinical_summary: A 28-year-old male presented to the hospital during a seasonal epidemic period with acute onset of fever, asthenia, generalized myalgia, and arthralgia. He had a past medical history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura diagnosed six years prior, for which he had discontinued therapy approximately five years ago.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient with a known history of ITP, severe isolated-appearing thrombocytopenia was initially managed as an ITP relapse; however, the subsequent sudden emergence of fever, hemolytic anemia, and acute focal neurologic deficits indicated a systemic microangiopathic process rather than isolated platelet destruction.

The sudden development of severe headache, vomiting, mental confusion, motor aphasia, and right hemiplegia raised high suspicion for an acute intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral infarction in the setting of severe thrombocytopenia, but emergency brain MRI was completely normal.
Secondary thrombotic microangiopathy in a young patient can be precipitated by an underlying autoimmune connective tissue disease, but antinuclear antibody (ANA) testing was negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Peripheral blood smear examination demonstrated innumerable schistocytes confirming thrombotic microangiopathy / TTP, and serologic testing returned positive IgM antibodies for dengue virus (with chikungunya virus coinfection), establishing dengue-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old female retail manager presented to an emergency department in South Carolina for evaluation of syncope. Thirteen days earlier, she had returned from a 10-day trip to Lagos, Nigeria, where she visited family.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Prominent nausea, diarrhea, fever, and dehydration leading to syncope strongly suggested acute travel-associated infectious gastroenteritis, but a comprehensive multiplex stool molecular panel was negative for all viral, bacterial, and protozoan gastrointestinal pathogens.

High daily fevers with headache, gastrointestinal symptoms, and relative bradycardia or syncope after travel to West Africa raised concern for enteric fever, but the patient had received the oral typhoid vaccine and blood culture identification subsequently established nontyphoidal Salmonella bacteremia rather than Salmonella Typhi.

diagnostic_pivot: Giemsa-stained thick and thin blood smears demonstrated microcytic normochromic anemia, numerous intraerythrocytic trophozoite rings, and classic crescentic gametocytes confirming Plasmodium falciparum malaria (3.5% parasitemia), corroborated by positive rapid antigen testing, which predisposed the host to concurrent nontyphoidal Salmonella bacteremia.

clinical_summary: A 10-year-old boy presented to the medical center for evaluation of fever and suspected central nervous system infection. On initial presentation, non-contrast computed tomography (CT) of the brain was obtained, demonstrating calcific densities within the parietal lobe of the cerebral cortex.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A child presenting with fever, marked CSF protein elevation (248 mg/dL), and low CSF glucose (36.8 mg/dL) raises immediate concern for pyogenic bacterial meningitis; however, bacterial meningitis typically produces severe neutrophilic pleocytosis, whereas the patient's CSF showed a predominantly lymphocytic response (91% lymphocytes) in a subacute presentation.

Aseptic viral meningitis frequently manifests with lymphocytic pleocytosis, but CSF glucose typically remains normal rather than depressed to 36.8 mg/dL, CSF protein is only modestly elevated, and viral infection does not account for intracerebral calcific lesions or persistent meningeal enhancement.

Intracranial calcific densities in the parietal lobe of a pediatric patient could represent calcified granulomas of parenchymal neurocysticercosis, but inactive calcified cysts do not explain high CSF protein (248 mg/dL), severe hypoglycorrhachia, or persistent meningeal enhancement.

diagnostic_pivot: The constellation of marked CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (91%), profound hypoglycorrhachia, strikingly elevated protein (248 mg/dL), and progressive neuroimaging revealing multiple ring-enhancing tuberculomas with persistent meningeal enhancement established tuberculous meningitis with intracranial tuberculomas.

clinical_summary: A 22-year-old male presented to the cardiology clinic with progressive exertional angina. His past medical history was notable for a pulmonary cystic lesion treated surgically via cystectomy and capitonnage followed by a 12-week course of oral anthelmintic therapy five years prior.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Exertional angina with exercise-induced ST depression and angiographic coronary occlusions suggests severe coronary atherosclerosis, but this is exceptionally rare in a 22-year-old without metabolic risk factors and fails to account for the well-defined left ventricular cystic mass.

differentials.candidate: Primary Cardiac Neoplasm (Cardiac Myxoma or Fibroma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A well-circumscribed anterior left ventricular mass detected on echocardiography can represent a primary benign cardiac tumor, but primary cardiac neoplasms are usually solid, do not typically infiltrate between the left main and coronary branches, and do not present with clear fluid content.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical excision revealed a calcified 2x2 cm cyst infiltrating the coronary arteries containing crystal-clear fluid ('eau de roche'), with pathological examination and positive echinococcal IgG-ELISA confirming an intracoronary hydatid cyst (Echinococcosis).

clinical_summary: An 84-year-old Japanese woman presented to the hospital with a history of fever and progressive dyspnea. Her past medical history was notable for diabetes mellitus, myelodysplastic syndrome (refractory anemia with excess blasts in transformation) diagnosed five months prior treated with cyclosporine (100 mg/day) and packed red blood cell transfusions, and humeral and pelvic fractures sustained five and four months prior,...

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial presentation of fever, dyspnea, and prominent leukocyturia led to a working diagnosis of urinary tract infection, but the patient had persistent high fevers despite completing seven days of intravenous cefmetazole (2 g/day).

differentials.candidate: Leukemic Progression / Malignant Infiltration of MDS
differentials.rule_out_reason: In a patient with known RAEB-t receiving immunosuppressive therapy, new pulmonary symptoms and multiple hepatic nodules up to 15 mm raised suspicion for disease progression or secondary malignancy, but thoracic CT and microbiological evaluation identified an infectious granulomatous process.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracic computed tomography demonstrated bilateral pleural effusions and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and sputum polymerase chain reaction (PCR) returned positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming disseminated/miliary tuberculosis in an immunosuppressed host.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old woman with a history of iron deficiency anemia on oral iron supplementation presented with an isolated swelling in the right parotid region that had been slowly enlarging over the preceding five months.

differentials.candidate: Primary Parotid Malignancy with Regional Lymph Node Metastases
differentials.rule_out_reason: A solitary parotid mass associated with multiple hard, fixed homolateral jugulodigastric lymph nodes and contrast enhancement on MRI strongly indicated salivary gland carcinoma with regional nodal metastases, prompting oncologic surgical planning.

A well-limited, mobile pretragal mass evolving over months is typical of a benign mixed tumor, but the presence of multiple hard, fixed cervical lymphadenopathies is inconsistent with an uncomplicated benign adenoma.
