diagnostic_pivot: Partial exofacial parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation was performed to obtain tissue, and anatomopathological examination revealed caseating granulomatous inflammation, establishing primary parotid and cervical lymph node tuberculosis in the absence of pulmonary disease.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old woman with no notable past medical history presented with a left sub-angulo-mandibular mass that had been evolving for approximately four months. The swelling was accompanied by localized pain, mild erythema, and low-grade fever reaching 38.0°C, without weight loss, chewing discomfort, trismus, or salivary purulence.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A cystic deep parotid lesion with peripheral rim enhancement, restricted diffusion, local tenderness, erythema, and low-grade fever strongly suggested an acute or subacute bacterial abscess, but the indolent 4-month progression without purulent discharge from Stensen's duct or systemic leukocytosis was atypical for common pyogenic parotitis.

differentials.candidate: Cystic Salivary Gland Neoplasm (Warthin Tumor / Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 4 cm well-defined mass of mixed echostructure with central fluid predominance in the parotid gland can mimic a cystic salivary neoplasm, but localized inflammatory signs, fever, and diffusion restriction favored an infectious or inflammatory granulomatous process.

diagnostic_pivot: Conservative parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation revealed epithelial-gigantocellular granulomas with caseous necrosis on histopathology, and culture of aspirated fluid on Lowenstein-Jensen medium yielded acid-fast bacilli, confirming primary tuberculosis of the parotid gland.

clinical_summary: A 58-year-old man presented to the hepatogastroenterology clinic with a one-month history of persistent right hypochondrium pain and vomiting. The pain was dull and aching in character, mild in intensity, gradual in onset, progressive over time, non-radiating, and unrelated to food intake.

differentials.candidate: Gallbladder Carcinoma with Direct Liver Invasion and Regional Nodal Metastasis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Irregular thickening of the gallbladder fundus with an ill-defined hypodense mass invading directly into the adjacent liver parenchyma, porta hepatis lymphadenopathy, and progressive weight loss strongly suggested advanced gallbladder cancer, prompting surgical oncologic planning for extended cholecystectomy.

Infiltrative biliary-hepatic masses with portal lymphadenopathy often represent cholangiocarcinoma or metastatic gastrointestinal malignancy, but normal serum CA 19-9 (18.9 U/mL) and negative chest CT and bone scintigraphy argued against widespread malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Pre-resection diagnostic laparoscopy revealed perihepatic adhesions with multiple small whitish granulomatous spots on the liver surface, and frozen section histopathological biopsy demonstrated numerous caseating epithelioid granulomas containing Langhans giant cells, establishing primary hepatobiliary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric emergency department with vomiting and severe abdominal pain. On physical examination, tenderness is elicited in the right lower quadrant.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Right lower quadrant tenderness, fever, and leukocytosis in a child strongly suggested complicated acute appendicitis with an inflammatory phlegmon or plastron, but surgical exploration revealed a well-encapsulated, discrete 10-cm retrovesical cystic mass separate from the concurrently inflamed appendix.

A retrovesical hematoma was considered preoperatively given the complex cystic collection on ultrasound, but operative exploration demonstrated an intact 10-cm cystic mass lacking hemorrhagic debris or coagulated blood.

diagnostic_pivot: Total surgical excision of the retrovesical cyst and appendectomy, followed by histopathological examination, definitively demonstrated the pathognomonic diagnostic features of a hydatid cyst coexisting with acute appendicitis, despite a negative indirect hemagglutination serology.

clinical_summary: A 4-year-old Maasai boy presents to the hospital accompanied by his brother with a 1-year progressive history of dry cough and worsening difficulty in breathing that has compromised his daily physical activity, accompanied by intermittent fever.

differentials.candidate: Bacterial pneumonia / complicated parapneumonic effusion / empyema
differentials.rule_out_reason: Subacute-to-chronic respiratory distress and massive unilateral thoracic opacification raised suspicion for unresolved bacterial pneumonia with parapneumonic effusion, but the condition was refractory to multiple courses of antibiotics and imaging identified an encapsulated fluid-filled cyst rather than consolidative or pleural exudative disease.

A 1-year history of cough, progressive respiratory compromise, and intermittent fever in an endemic pastoral setting raised high suspicion for childhood tuberculosis, but there was no history of tuberculosis contact and cross-sectional imaging revealed a massive unilocular fluid-filled cyst without parenchymal cavitation or lymphadenopathy.

diagnostic_pivot: Chest computed tomography demonstrated a massive 11.7 x 8.6 x 11.0 cm thick-walled unilocular cystic lesion causing complete right middle and lower lobe collapse and contralateral mediastinal shift, which was surgically resected via thoracotomy as an intact 20-cm hydatid cyst.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old female with a history of HIV diagnosed at age 15 and poor adherence to combination antiretroviral therapy (intermittent tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz) presents to the emergency room with a 10-day history of intermittent lower abdominal pain, nausea, bilious vomiting, and asthenia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given profound HIV immunosuppression, CMV was initially considered the most probable opportunistic cause of bowel ulceration and spontaneous perforation, prompting empiric ganciclovir; however, resected tissue histology demonstrated prominent chronic granulomas without cytomegalic viral inclusion bodies.

Malignant neoplasms and Kaposi sarcoma represent recognized causes of spontaneous intestinal perforation in advanced retroviral disease, but surgical pathology confirmed chronic granulomatous inflammation and mucosal ulcerations without evidence of malignant cellular proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the resected ileocecal specimen demonstrated chronic bowel inflammation, multiple mucosal ulcers, and characteristic epithelioid granulomas within the mucosa and mesenteric lymph nodes, confirming intestinal tuberculosis as the underlying etiology of perforation in the setting of severe immunosuppression (CD4 count 94 cells/mm³).

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a 7-day history of dull, aching left upper quadrant abdominal pain accompanied by intermittent fever, rigors, drenching night sweats, anorexia, and generalized malaise.

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial sepsis / septic shock with intra-abdominal peritonitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: High fever, altered mental status, localized abdominal guarding, and hemodynamic collapse prompted blood culture collection and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic administration for septic shock, but blood cultures were negative and systemic decompensation was driven by severe parasitic hemolysis and internal hemorrhage.

differentials.candidate: Traumatic or hematologic splenic rupture / hematologic malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Hemoperitoneum with perisplenic hematoma raised suspicion for occult traumatic rupture or atraumatic rupture secondary to hematologic malignancy, but the patient denied trauma, displayed normal coagulation and leukocyte counts, and CT showed no underlying lymphoproliferative neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Peripheral blood microscopy demonstrated numerous intraerythrocytic ring stages with a high parasitemia index exceeding 5%, confirming severe malaria complicated by circulatory shock and a contrast-enhanced CT-verified grade II spontaneous subcapsular splenic rupture.

clinical_summary: A 72-year-old postmenopausal woman is referred to the outpatient gynecology clinic for evaluation of suspected uterine prolapse. Her medical history includes three uncomplicated vaginal deliveries, menopause at age 52, and chronic essential hypertension managed with valsartan; she does not smoke and has no history of jaundice, hepatic disease, or prior abdominal surgeries.

differentials.candidate: Malignant ovarian neoplasm / epithelial ovarian carcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 9-cm multilocular adnexal mass containing solid components in a 72-year-old postmenopausal woman strongly suggested primary ovarian carcinoma, but CA-125 and CEA were normal, the IOTA ADNEX calculated risk was low (1.4%), and intraoperative frozen section formally ruled out malignancy.

A benign mucinous or serous cystadenoma was considered due to the multicystic appearance with internal septations, but surgical histopathology demonstrated characteristic parasitic cuticular and germinal membranes of a hydatid cyst rather than an epithelial neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive histopathologic examination of the resected adnexal specimen revealed an isolated ovarian hydatid cyst, with postoperative abdominal CT confirming complete absence of hepatic or pulmonary involvement and establishing primary ovarian echinococcosis.

clinical_summary: A 77-year-old man is admitted to the internal medicine ward with a 5-day history of progressive left preauricular swelling. The swelling was painless and insidious in onset, progressively increasing in size.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapid parotid enlargement with marked neutrophilic leukocytosis and CRP 330 mg/L strongly suggested pyogenic bacterial infection, but the patient failed outpatient oral ciprofloxacin and inpatient intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole, blood cultures were negative, and imaging lacked a drainable purulent abscess.

Unilateral salivary gland enlargement and cervical lymphadenopathy prompted evaluation for granulomatous or autoimmune sialadenitis, but antinuclear antibodies, anti-SSA/SSB serologies, and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme were all negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Fine-needle aspiration cytology of the parotid compartment revealed neutrophils, lymphocytes, and necrotic debris, with smear examination demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, a positive PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and subsequent confirmatory mycobacterial culture.

clinical_summary: A 76-year-old male with JAK2V617F mutation-positive polycythemia vera, maintained on ruxolitinib 20 mg daily since March 2018, presents to the hospital in September 2018 with a several-week history of pyrexia, fatigue, and progressive abdominal distension.

differentials.candidate: Peritoneal carcinomatosis / metastatic recurrence of colon adenocarcinoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Diffuse peritoneal thickening and massive ascites in a patient with recently resected colon adenocarcinoma raised primary concern for metastatic peritoneal carcinomatosis, but diagnostic paracentesis revealed an exudative mononuclear effusion with total absence of neoplastic cells.

In the setting of targeted immunosuppression from the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib, opportunistic non-tuberculous mycobacterial peritonitis was evaluated, but specific atypical mycobacterial PCR was negative and culture exclusively isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Ascitic fluid analysis revealed a markedly elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA) level of 57.5 U/L (normal threshold ≤36.0 U/L), which alongside prior surgical findings of necrotic epithelioid granulomas prompted anti-tuberculous therapy, definitively confirmed after 50 days by positive mycobacterial ascites culture.

clinical_summary: A 33-year-old pregnant woman, originally from Pakistan and residing in the United Kingdom since 2014, presents to the emergency department at 40 weeks of gestation with intractable lower back pain, left L5 sciatica, and a newly developed left foot drop.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis / bacterial osteomyelitis (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pyogenic spinal infection typically presents with acute febrile toxicity, rapid bony erosion, and prominent destruction of the intervertebral disc spaces; in contrast, imaging demonstrated preserved disc spaces ('good discs') despite extensive sacral osteolysis, indolent progression, and sterile extended bacterial cultures.

differentials.candidate: Primary pelvic bone neoplasm or metastatic sacral malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extensive sacral osteolysis and bilateral suprasacral masses accompanied by chronic weight loss raised suspicion for a primary sacral malignancy (such as chordoma or giant cell tumor) or metastasis, but cross-sectional MRI confirmed multiseptated, thick-walled fluid-filled cold abscesses tracking across fascial planes.

diagnostic_pivot: Although bone aspirate AFB microscopy, molecular PCR, and 42-day mycobacterial cultures were negative, histological examination of the placenta delivered post-partum identified characteristic chronic granulomata within chorionic villi, confirming extrapulmonary tuberculosis as the cause of spinopelvic destruction.

clinical_summary: A 20-year-old male trout farm worker presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of malaise, fevers, diarrhea, vomiting, and jaundice, acutely complicated by hemoptysis, severe headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia.

differentials.candidate: Systemic autoimmune vasculitis / Pulmonary-renal syndrome (ANCA vasculitis or anti-GBM disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Concomitant diffuse pulmonary hemorrhage, severe acute kidney injury, and extreme systemic inflammation strongly suggested a vasculitic pulmonary-renal syndrome, prompting empiric intravenous methylprednisolone; however, comprehensive vasculitis and autoimmune serologies were completely negative.

differentials.candidate: Severe atypical or fungal pneumonia with multiorgan failure
differentials.rule_out_reason: Four-quadrant airspace consolidation and acute respiratory failure raised suspicion for opportunistic fungal infection or atypical pathogens, but blood beta-D-glucan, galactomannan, BAL viral screens, mycoplasma PCR, and cultures were all negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Reference laboratory testing confirmed positive serum Leptospira Panbio IgM ELISA and dual-target real-time 16SrRNA/Lipl32 PCR, establishing severe leptospirosis (Weil disease with pulmonary hemorrhage syndrome) successfully supported with venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO).

clinical_summary: A 55-year-old patient living in a rural endemic area is referred for hospital evaluation of dull left hypochondrial pain evolving over the preceding 6 months, without associated nausea, vomiting, or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: A large retroperitoneal mass closely associated with the adrenal gland prompted evaluation for a catecholamine-producing pheochromocytoma, but arterial blood pressure was normal and 24-hour urinary vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) and metanephrines were entirely within normal limits.

A 12-cm adrenal mass in an adult raises strong suspicion for primary adrenocortical carcinoma or sarcoma, but cross-sectional CT revealed a sharply circumscribed, multicystic architecture with scattered calcifications and complete absence of perirenal fat infiltration or vascular invasion.

diagnostic_pivot: Laparotomy revealed a 12-cm pearly-white multivesicular cyst in the left adrenal gland whose puncture yielded clear hydatid fluid, with subsequent histopathological examination establishing a primary adrenal hydatid cyst despite negative preoperative serology.

clinical_summary: A 35-year-old male originally from Russia presented to a specialized dermatology service in Mexico City evaluation of two persistent ulcerative skin lesions with active borders. The patient reported extensive travel between May and June to several countries in the Middle East (Israel, Turkey), the Balkan region (Armenia, Georgia), and Russia.

differentials.candidate: New World Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (Leishmania mexicana / Leishmania braziliensis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient sought initial medical care in Chiapas, Mexico, an endemic focus of L. mexicana, species-specific molecular amplification and phylogenetic analysis established Old World L. tropica acquired during travel in the Middle East or Balkans rather than local New World transmission.

differentials.candidate: Benign Cutaneous Lesion / Non-specific Inflammatory Dermatosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The initial assumption of a benign or non-infectious inflammatory process treated empirically with cryotherapy was disproven by the rapid recurrence with active, indurated ulcerative borders.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct visualization of intracellular amastigotes within macrophages on Giemsa-stained smears coupled with multilocus PCR and sequencing confirmed Leishmania tropica, which resolved completely following intralesional meglumine antimoniate (glucantime).

clinical_summary: A 65-year-old immunocompetent man presented to a respiratory outpatient clinic with a 2-year history of recurrent productive cough and progressive weight loss. He denied fevers, night sweats, hemoptysis, dysuria, hematuria, or known sick contacts.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The unexpected unilateral hydroureter and hydronephrosis in the lower moiety of a duplex kidney raised high suspicion for calculus or urothelial malignancy, but dedicated multiphasic renal CT showed no mass, calculi, or compressive lymphadenopathy.

differentials.candidate: Inactive Fibrocalcific Pulmonary Scarring / Non-infectious Bronchiolitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial negative sputum examinations and chronic apical scarring suggested inactive remote insult, but the coexistence of tree-in-bud micronodules and constitutional wasting indicated an active paucibacillary infectious process.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis was established when specialized urine culture yielded Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, revealing extrapulmonary genitourinary involvement coexisting with active pulmonary disease, followed by clinical weight gain and radiographic clearance on quadruple therapy.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old previously healthy man presented to the clinic with a 3-week history of swelling and dull discomfort over the left sternoclavicular joint region. He reported no fever, night sweats, anorexia, or weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The CT demonstration of cortical joint destruction and loculated fluid suggested pyogenic septic arthritis, prompting initial intravenous ceftriaxone; however, the absence of fever, lack of leukocytosis, lack of warmth/tenderness (cold abscess), and negative routine bacterial cultures ruled out pyogenic bacteria.

differentials.candidate: Primary Osseous Malignancy (e.g., Osteosarcoma or Chondrosarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Aggressive osteolysis of the clavicular and sternal heads can mimic malignant neoplasms, but the presence of frank purulent fluid communicating with the joint space pointed towards a chronic infectious granulomatous process.

diagnostic_pivot: Open biopsy revealed frank caseous pus growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with histological confirmation of multiple granulomatous lesions with prominent caseous necrosis.

clinical_summary: A 16-year-old female from the Terai region presented to the emergency department with a 5-day history of high-grade fever that had not responded to empirical parenteral antibiotics. A dermatology consultation was requested for concurrent asymptomatic, skin-colored cutaneous lesions over her extremities that had developed insidiously over the preceding 6 months, beginning on the left lower leg and subsequently involving the...

differentials.candidate: Primary or Autoimmune Anetoderma (e.g., associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The flaccid, wrinkling plaques with loss of dermal elastic recoil strongly suggested anetoderma; however, antinuclear antibody testing was negative, and classical anetoderma does not feature peripheral nerve enlargement or sensory deficits.
Disseminated cutaneous plaques accompanied by acute constitutional symptoms and edema can mimic treponemal disease, but nontreponemal serologic screening was non-reactive.

diagnostic_pivot: The combination of cutaneous hypoesthesia, tender peripheral neuropathy, facial and peripheral edema representing an acute Type 1 reversal reaction, confirmed by slit skin smear demonstrating acid-fast bacilli (BI 3+) and neurotropic granulomatous histology.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old previously healthy man presented to an ophthalmology clinic with sudden-onset, painless, profound diminution of vision in both eyes that had persisted for 10 days. One week prior to the development of visual impairment, he experienced an acute febrile syndrome characterized by high fevers, severe generalized myalgias, and marked prostration.

differentials.candidate: Systemic Autoimmune Retinal Vasculitis (e.g., Lupus, Behçet's Disease)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bilateral occlusive retinal vasculitis and cotton wool spots can represent manifestations of collagen vascular disease; however, targeted autoimmune panels were negative, and the ocular findings were preceded by an acute tropical febrile illness with transient thrombocytopenia.

Acute macular arteriole occlusion and retinal ischemia can arise from embolic stroke or carotid plaques, but vascular and cardiac Doppler evaluations showed completely normal anatomy without embolic origins.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation of acute arboviral infection via positive NS1 antigen and IgM serology established the diagnosis of post-febrile immune-mediated bilateral retinal vasculitis with macular infarction.

clinical_summary: A 3-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department with a 3-day history of progressive abdominal distension, complete failure to pass stools or flatus, and intractable bilious vomiting. His birth history was notable for an un-booked pregnancy and delivery to a mother with a history of substance abuse who was diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) postpartum.

differentials.candidate: Idiopathic Pediatric Mechanical Bowel Obstruction (Intussusception / Volvulus)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute bilious vomiting, distension, and absent rectal gas in a toddler strongly suggest intussusception or volvulus; however, surgical exploration revealed extensive necrotic mesenteric and retroperitoneal adenopathy with multiple small bowel perforations and caseous plaques rather than an anatomical loop twist or lead-point intussusception.

differentials.candidate: Primary Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Reactive Ileus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Severe pediatric mycobacterial dissemination typically stems from obvious pulmonary parenchymal destruction; however, chest radiography demonstrated no findings of pulmonary involvement.

diagnostic_pivot: Rapid sputum molecular testing (GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra) and culture confirmed rifampicin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, while exploratory laparotomy confirmed extensive necrotizing granulomatous inflammation of mesenteric lymph nodes and caseous ileal perforation.

clinical_summary: A 23-year-old pregnant female presented for clinical evaluation during the third trimester of gestation with an acute onset of fever, generalized arthralgia, a diffuse erythematous cutaneous exanthema, and prominent pruritus.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Dengue co-circulates in the same geographical regions and shares overlapping acute symptoms of fever, rash, and arthralgia in pregnancy; however, rapid diagnostic antigen screening was negative.

Acute exanthematous febrile illness in pregnancy requires ruling out primary maternal CMV or rubella, but serological evaluation demonstrated chronic preexisting IgG immunity rather than primary acute infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis of acute maternal infection was established by positive quantitative RT-PCR in both serum and urine, corroborated by reactive IgM and plaque reduction neutralization testing (PRNT90%).

clinical_summary: A 21-year-old pregnant woman presented for clinical evaluation during the second trimester of gestation after developing an acute episode of fever. She had no documented antecedent medical problems, and her antenatal course up to that point had been uneventful.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Dengue and chikungunya frequently cause acute febrile illness in pregnant women in the same geographic areas, but specific IgM serologies for both viruses were non-reactive.

differentials.candidate: Congenital TORCH Pathogens / Treponemal / Retroviral Infection
differentials.rule_out_reason: Maternal fever during pregnancy warrants exclusion of classic teratogenic infections; however, IgM assays and serological tests for toxoplasmosis, cytomegalovirus, rubella, syphilis, and HIV were non-reactive, with IgG positivity merely reflecting preexisting distant immunity to rubella and CMV.

diagnostic_pivot: Specific IgM serology was reactive for ZIKV and confirmed by high-specificity 90% plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT90%) demonstrating neutralizing antibodies.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old pregnant female presented to an antenatal clinic during the second trimester of gestation reporting the acute onset of a generalized cutaneous exanthema accompanied by generalized arthralgias. She had no previous medical conditions or complications during her current pregnancy.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Chikungunya frequently co-circulates and presents with acute exanthema and arthralgia, but it typically produces severe, immobilizing polyarthritis, and specific molecular evaluation confirmed flaviviral rather than alphaviral etiology.

Dengue virus is a prominent differential diagnosis for acute rash in endemic tropical regions, but it typically features biphasic high fevers, retro-orbital pain, and hemorrhagic diathesis, which were absent here.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation of acute maternal infection was established by positive quantitative RT-PCR in serum (690 copies/mL) alongside positive 90% plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT90%) neutralizing antibodies.

clinical_summary: A 29-year-old pregnant woman presented to the outpatient obstetric clinic during the second trimester of gestation reporting the acute onset of a generalized pruritic cutaneous eruption. She reported no prior medical conditions, drug exposures, or obstetric complications.

differentials.candidate: Polymorphic Eruption of Pregnancy (PUPPP) / Gestational Pruritus
differentials.rule_out_reason: Pruritic rash in pregnancy is frequently attributed to benign non-infectious dermatoses; however, PUPPP typically arises in late pregnancy (third trimester) and lacks the characteristic infectious serological markers and teratogenic risk of viral exanthems.

Dengue and chikungunya are common differentials for acute tropical exanthems but are not classically associated with congenital microcephaly, and confirmatory testing established high titers of neutralizing antibodies specific to Zika virus.

diagnostic_pivot: Confirmation was established by positive maternal Zika-specific IgM serology and high-specificity PRNT90% neutralizing antibodies, with maternal-fetal transmission evidenced by severe fetal microcephaly (head circumference 30 cm) at delivery.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 25-year-old pregnant woman presents during the third trimester of gestation for clinical evaluation reporting the acute onset of an exanthematous skin rash accompanied by generalized pruritus. Routine prenatal monitoring is underway to assess maternal health and monitor fetal growth.

differentials.rule_out_reason: In arbovirus-endemic regions, gestational fever, rash, and pruritus frequently raise suspicion for dengue; however, dengue does not cause congenital microcephaly and cross-reactive flavivirus antibodies are distinguished by plaque reduction neutralization testing demonstrating specific neutralizing antibodies.

Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy frequently occur in the third trimester, but represent a non-infectious, self-limiting disorder without viral seroconversion or fetal developmental abnormalities.

diagnostic_pivot: Acute positive IgM serology confirmed by high-specificity plaque reduction neutralization testing (PRNT90%) confirming neutralizing antibodies, resulting in congenital fetal microcephaly (head circumference of 27 cm at 37 weeks gestation).

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 28-year-old pregnant woman presents for clinical evaluation during the third trimester of pregnancy after experiencing an acute episode of fever. Gestational monitoring is initiated to evaluate maternal and fetal health.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as a leading cause of acute fever during pregnancy in endemic areas; ruled out by non-reactive specific IgM serology.
Considered as a common cause of febrile illness in pregnant women; excluded by non-reactive IgM serology.

differentials.candidate: Congenital TORCH Infections (Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, Cytomegalovirus, Syphilis, HIV)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the maternal fever and high risk of congenital fetal central nervous system and musculoskeletal malformations; ruled out as acute causative infections by non-reactive IgM serologies for all five agents.

diagnostic_pivot: Demonstration of positive IgM serology for the target flavivirus, corroborated by delivery of an infant at 38 weeks with congenital microcephaly (head circumference 28 cm) and arthrogryposis of upper and lower limbs, and confirmed by placental tissue detection of viral NS1 protein and negative-strand viral RNA indicating active replication.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A female patient with multiple sclerosis, previously treated with alemtuzumab complicated by recurrent bilateral acute iridocyclitis, presents two weeks following her second cycle of alemtuzumab with a dyspeptic syndrome persisting for several days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Alemtuzumab therapy frequently induces secondary autoimmune complications (such as the patient's earlier iridocyclitis); however, imaging demonstrated discrete fluid-filled cystic lesions compressing the IVC rather than solid lymphadenopathy or autoimmune infiltration.

differentials.candidate: Simple / Non-parasitic Hepatic or Retroperitoneal Cysts
differentials.rule_out_reason: Congenital or simple solitary cysts are benign epithelial structures that do not trigger profound systemic immune activation or extreme IgE elevation (>=1000 kU/L).

diagnostic_pivot: Serological demonstration of elevated antibodies against Echinococcus multilocularis in combination with cystic inferior vena cava compression and profound hyper-IgE, leading to initiation of albendazole antiparasitic therapy.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A patient presents with intermittent fever spikes exceeding 38°C, shivering, and abdominal pain occurring predominantly in the evenings. Broad-spectrum empiric intravenous antimicrobial therapy with piperacillin/tazobactam is initiated for suspected acute intra-abdominal infection.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial Intra-abdominal Sepsis / Suppurative Thrombophlebitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: High-grade fever spikes, chills, and abdominal pain strongly suggested acute bacterial infection warranting empiric piperacillin/tazobactam; however, no bacterial infection was proven and systemic microbiological cultures remained sterile.
Considered due to the combination of rigors, spiking fevers, and extensive caval thrombosis; ruled out by negative blood cultures and normal echocardiography.

diagnostic_pivot: Advanced cross-sectional abdominal imaging (ultrasonography, CT, and MRI) revealing massive reactivation of echinococcosis in the right retroperitoneum and suprarenal IVC, almost complete obturation of the IVC and common iliac veins by non-enhancing cystic material, and enlargement of a hepatic hydatid cyst to 39 mm.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A patient with extensive vascular occlusion of the inferior vena cava (IVC) and common iliac veins bilaterally presents for multidisciplinary surgical consultation following the clinical resolution of an acute febrile illness.

differentials.candidate: Acute / Subacute Deep Venous Thrombosis Requiring Surgical Thrombectomy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extensive occlusion of the IVC and common iliac veins typically prompts surgical thrombectomy; however, surgical intervention was declined because well-developed collaterals made the thrombosis functionally chronic and asymptomatic, and open intervention carried prohibitive peri-operative risks.

Bacterial infection of thrombosed veins was considered during the preceding febrile episode; however, symptoms resolved rapidly upon combined therapy, indicating that the acute reaction was driven by parasitic reactivation rather than an uncontrolled bacterial process.

diagnostic_pivot: Recognition that the chronic caval and iliac venous occlusion was caused by reactivation and vascular dissemination of chronic cystic echinococcosis, successfully managed medically while avoiding high-risk surgical resection.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 25-year-old patient with no significant prior medical history presents with a two-month history of rapidly progressive dysphagia and bilateral hearing loss, accompanied by persistent fever, drenching night sweats, profound asthenia, and an unintentional 8 kg weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapidly progressive bilateral hearing loss, cavum tissue mass, cervical lymphadenopathy, and marked constitutional weight loss initially raised strong suspicion for cavum malignancy; ruled out by biopsy revealing non-neoplastic epithelioid granulomatosis.

differentials.candidate: HIV Infection with Opportunistic Pharyngitis / Malignant Lymphoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Profound constitutional decline, severe weight loss, and diffuse purulent pharyngeal lesions suggested advanced retroviral immunosuppression or lymphoproliferative disease; ruled out by negative HIV serology and normal overall immunological assessment.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological demonstration of epithelioid granulomatosis on cavum and pharyngeal biopsies, cervico-thoracic CT showing cavitary lung lesions, and positive sputum smear for Koch bacillus, confirming multifocal acute miliary tuberculous pharyngitis (Isambert disease) and pulmonary tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 16-month-old female infant is admitted to the hospital with a 3-day history of fever, fatigue, and poor appetite. On physical examination, she is cachectic and lethargic.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe life-threatening hypercalcemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis; ruled out by profound parathyroid hormone suppression.

differentials.candidate: Exogenous Vitamin D Intoxication / Thiazide Consumption
differentials.rule_out_reason: High serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and calcitriol levels suggested exogenous toxic vitamin D ingestion; ruled out by the absence of excessive dietary calcium, vitamin D supplements, or thiazide diuretics.

diagnostic_pivot: Chest CT revealing widespread pulmonary consolidations, calcified lymphadenopathy, and cavitary mass lesions, in an infant not immunized with BCG whose mother failed to complete gestational anti-tuberculosis therapy, definitively confirmed by detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA by PCR in serum.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A young male with a history of untreated human immunodeficiency virus infection presents for clinical evaluation with a sudden onset of progressive blurring of vision in both eyes. Over the preceding year, he had been self-administering intravenous dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, and vitamin C, as well as high-dose oral multivitamins and minerals.

differentials.candidate: Other Systemic Opportunistic Infections (e.g., Syphilis, Cryptococcosis, Toxoplasmosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: In an untreated immunocompromised patient presenting with retinitis, focal neurologic deficits, and cutaneous lesions, systemic infections such as ocular syphilis, cryptococcal disease, or toxoplasmosis were considered; ruled out by comprehensive negative systemic diagnostic investigations.

Cutaneous eruption in a patient injecting illicit intramuscular/intravenous steroids and high-dose vitamins could represent a hypersensitivity drug reaction or severe seborrheic dermatitis; ruled out by physical diagnostic confirmation of widespread ectoparasitic infestation.

diagnostic_pivot: Clinical examination identifying generalized scabies along with bilateral necrotizing retinitis, prompting directed topical treatment with permethrin cream alongside systemic and intravitreal ganciclovir therapy.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> An 11-month-old male infant presents to a regional hospital with acute fever, upper abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. Initial laboratory testing reveals mild anemia with a hemoglobin level of 10.9 g/dL and hepatic impairment with an aspartate aminotransferase (AST) of 44 U/L and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) of 134 U/L.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute congestive heart failure and cardiomegaly in an infant frequently stem from viral myocarditis; ruled out by microscopic identification of circulating flagellated parasites and positive protozoal serology.

Endemic tropical causes of fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and anemia in infants; ruled out by thick smear microscopy demonstrating specific Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes rather than Plasmodium or intracellular Leishmania donovani amastigotes.

diagnostic_pivot: Direct microscopic identification of Trypanosoma cruzi on thick blood smear examination, corroborated by positive Chagas immunofluorescent IgG titers of 1/160, cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio 62%) on chest radiograph, and right atrial and ventricular overload on electrocardiogram, confirming acute Chagas disease with cardiac involvement.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 49-year-old male farmer living in Guangxi, with a two-month history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) treated with oral prednisone (30 mg/day), is referred for further evaluation due to recurrent fever, cough, and fatigue refractory to a three-week course of intravenous meropenem.

differentials.candidate: Severe Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Lupus Pneumonitis / Lupus Nephritis Flare)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The constellation of eyelid erythema, oral ulceration, high-grade proteinuria, hypocomplementemia, and high ESR suggested active lupus with pulmonary involvement; however, immunosuppression with intravenous methylprednisolone failed to resolve pulmonary disease and nine days later chest CT demonstrated progressive infiltration and pleural effusion with subsequent hemoptysis.

differentials.candidate: Refractory Bacterial Sepsis / Severe Nosocomial Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Prior isolation of Gram-negative bacteria from blood cultures raised concern for persistent bacterial septicemia; ruled out by complete lack of response to an extensive three-week course of intravenous meropenem.

diagnostic_pivot: Microbiological isolation of thermal dimorphic fungus Talaromyces marneffei from sputum and bone marrow cultures in a severely immunosuppressed HIV-negative farmer from an endemic region, leading to definitive treatment with amphotericin B and voriconazole.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old female factory worker born and residing in Guangxi, China, presents with recurrent right thigh swelling, severe pain, fevers, and cutaneous ulceration. She has a 4-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus managed with maintenance oral prednisone (30 mg daily).

differentials.candidate: Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus flare / Lupus vasculitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had long-standing SLE with high-titer ANA and prior skin histology interpreted as vasculitis, normal complement levels and normal anti-dsDNA titers along with progressive suppurative ulceration despite steroid therapy ruled out an isolated autoimmune flare.

While coagulase-negative staphylococci were isolated from initial blood and ulcer cultures, standard antibacterial therapy failed to induce permanent resolution, and the recurrent ulceration was sustained by an underlying invasive dimorphic fungus.

diagnostic_pivot: In an immunosuppressed patient from an endemic region with fever, profound anemia, and refractory cutaneous ulceration, microbiological cultures of blood and ulcer secretions isolated the dimorphic fungal pathogen Talaromyces marneffei, with complete clinical resolution upon antifungal therapy.

clinical_summary: A 43-year-old woman with no underlying medical comorbidities presents to an academic hospital with recurrent respiratory symptoms. She previously resided in a rural area of South Africa.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An interventricular septal mass effacing the right ventricle was provisionally interpreted as a ventricular thrombus, but the patient had normal ECG, normal cardiac biomarkers, no regional wall motion abnormality, and advanced imaging demonstrated an infiltrating multi-cystic mass with calcified components rather than an organized clot.

differentials.candidate: Primary cardiac neoplasm (e.g., cardiac myxoma, fibroma, or sarcoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Solid intracardiac tumors can arise in the interventricular septum and cause chamber effacement, but 3D transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated an infiltrating cystic lesion with calcifications and fluid content communicating across cardiac structures rather than a solid vascular neoplasm.

diagnostic_pivot: Serological testing demonstrated an Echinococcus indirect haemagglutination titer of 1:500, and thoracic CT/3D TOE confirmed extensive bilateral pulmonary hydatid cysts with an interventricular septal hydatid cyst protruding into the right atrium.

clinical_summary: A 25-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and chronic viral hepatitis C presents with progressive lower extremity weakness and loss of bowel and bladder sphincter control evolving over the past 2 months.

differentials.candidate: HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy / Viral opportunistic myelitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: While the patient has poorly controlled HIV with irregular antiretroviral adherence, vacuolar myelopathy typically presents with symmetrical, painless spastic ataxia without a discrete sensory level, whereas this patient presented with an acute-on-chronic focal T8 sensory-motor spinal cord compression.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic spinal epidural abscess / Bacterial spondylodiscitis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Bacterial spinal epidural abscess usually presents with rapid progression, severe focal back tenderness, and acute systemic sepsis, whereas this patient developed insidious progression over 2 months while already on broad antimicrobial therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The focal compressive T8 myelopathy in a patient undergoing treatment for disseminated disease represents an intradural extramedullary thoracic tuberculoma, arising either as a paradoxical inflammatory response or as clinical treatment failure in an immunocompromised host.

clinical_summary: A 62-year-old woman, postmenopausal for 12 years and multiparous (G7P5A2) with hypertension and no prior history of abdominal surgery, presents with chronic pelvic pain persisting for 8 months. On physical examination, the abdomen is soft and non-tender without palpable masses.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Both pelvic ultrasound and MRI initially diagnosed the 4-cm fundal uterine mass as a typical subserous leiomyoma due to its well-demarcated appearance and frank T2 hyposignal, but surgical exploration revealed a cystic lesion and histology confirmed parasitic hydatid membranes.

Given the patient's postmenopausal age, chronic pelvic pain, and large concurrent pelvic masses, malignant pelvic neoplasia was strongly suspected intraoperatively, but pathology confirmed benign ovarian serous cystadenomas and a calcified uterine parasitic cyst without malignant cellular proliferation.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the resected surgical specimen confirmed a primary subserous calcified hydatid cyst of the uterine fundus occurring in association with ovarian serous cystadenomas, with postoperative chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound confirming absence of other hydatid localizations.

clinical_summary: A 69-year-old overweight woman (BMI 27 kg/m²), menopausal for 16 years and multiparous (G6P4A2) with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presents with chronic pelvic pain of 3 months duration.

differentials.candidate: Uterine leiomyoma (cystic or degenerating uterine fibroid)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A 5-cm uterine fundal mass in a 69-year-old woman is typically regarded as a benign fibroid, and the patient underwent surgery under the preoperative presumption of a benign cyst/leiomyoma, but histopathologic evaluation confirmed a parasitic hydatid cyst.

The development of a symptomatic 5-cm pelvic mass in a woman 16 years post-menopause raised concern for neoplastic disease, but complete imaging revealed no invasive features or metastatic deposits, and histopathology confirmed a hydatid cyst.

diagnostic_pivot: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) demonstrated strongly positive hydatid serology at a titer of 1/320, and conservative surgical dome resection confirmed a solitary primary hydatid cyst of the uterus.

clinical_summary: An adult patient with confirmed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection presents to a clinical referral center in Uganda for evaluation of chronic respiratory symptoms, persistent productive cough, and constitutional decline.

differentials.candidate: Opportunistic bacterial or fungal pneumonia (e.g., Pneumocystis jirovecii or Streptococcus pneumoniae)
differentials.rule_out_reason: In HIV-infected individuals, opportunistic bacterial or fungal pathogens frequently cause acute-on-chronic respiratory symptoms, but ongoing microbiological evaluation confirmed persistent positive sputum smears indicating an acid-fast mycobacterial etiology.

Standard first-line therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol [RHZE]) typically results in rapid clinical and microbiological conversion in susceptible disease, but the patient exhibited persistent positive smears and documented resistance to first-line agents.

diagnostic_pivot: Comprehensive mycobacterial drug susceptibility testing identified drug-resistant strains—including multidrug resistance (MDR-TB resistant to rifampicin and isoniazid) and poly-drug resistance (resistant to isoniazid, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide)—necessitating second-line regimens.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old pregnant woman at approximately 33 to 34 weeks of gestation, residing in the riverside community of Marimarituba, Santarém municipality (Pará State), Brazil, is admitted to the hospital with a 1-week history of daily fevers, severe diffuse myalgias, and 2 days of acute diarrhea accompanied by new-onset peripheral edema.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Acute fever, severe myalgia, diarrhea, peripheral edema, and thrombocytopenia in the Amazon basin strongly suggested dengue or another epidemic arbovirus, but the patient's symptoms were driven by a protozoan parasite with high persistent parasitemia and potential for congenital transmission.

Malaria is highly endemic in riverside Amazonian communities and causes acute febrile paroxysms with cytopenias, but peripheral blood microscopy revealed extracellular flagellated trypomastigotes rather than intracellular Plasmodium trophozoites.

diagnostic_pivot: Microscopic examination of the peripheral blood smear identified motile trypomastigotes, serological testing demonstrated positive indirect immunofluorescence (IgG 1/320, IgM 1/160) and indirect hemagglutination, and qPCR revealed 53.51 parasites Eq/mL, confirming acute orally acquired Chagas disease with subsequent vertical transmission to her infant.

clinical_summary: A 26-year-old pregnant woman at 15 weeks of gestation is admitted to the medical intensive care unit (MICU) with an 11-day history of cough, progressive fatigue, and night sweats, complicated by 6 days of high fever up to 39.3°C and 2 days of acute dyspnea, worsening fever reaching 40.1°C, and altered sensorium.

differentials.candidate: Acute viral or atypical bacterial pneumonia with ARDS
differentials.rule_out_reason: Rapidly progressive respiratory failure with diffuse bilateral infiltrates in an immunosuppressed pregnant patient strongly suggested severe influenza, RSV, or atypical bacterial infection, but extensive serological and multiplex microbiological assays were entirely negative.

differentials.candidate: Exacerbation / Relapse of Evans syndrome or Autoimmune disease
differentials.rule_out_reason: Given her past history of Evans syndrome and worsening thrombocytopenia in pregnancy, an autoimmune hematologic relapse was considered, but direct Coombs testing and broad autoantibody screens (ANA, ENA, ANCA) were negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Positive sputum nested PCR and acid-fast bacilli staining, confirmed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of BALF and blood, demonstrated disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which triggered reactive hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) evidenced by bone marrow hemophagocytosis, hyperferritinemia (6649 ng/mL), and elevated soluble CD25.

clinical_summary: An 18-year-old female patient with no notable past medical history presents with chronic pain in the right iliac fossa evolving in a context of anorexia and an unintentional weight loss of 10 kg over the past 4 months.

differentials.candidate: Ovarian cystadenoma / Pelvic cystic teratoma (Adnexal neoplasm)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A large, well-demarcated pelvic fluid collection with mural nodules in a young female with marked weight loss strongly suggested an ovarian cystic neoplasm, but exploratory laparotomy revealed completely normal ovaries and appendix, with the mass originating within the mesentery.

A cystic, hypervascular mesenteric lesion with thick walls and mural nodules can represent a mesenteric duplication cyst or stromal neoplasm, but histopathology revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than a true epithelial lining or neoplastic stromal cells.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathological examination of the resected specimen demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis, and molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming isolated abdominopelvic tuberculous lymphadenitis.

clinical_summary: A 60-year-old female with no significant past medical history presents with a 1-month history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, progressive jaundice, clay-colored stools, and generalized itching, acutely accompanied by high fevers and shaking chills for the past 3 days.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The clinical presentation of Charcot's triad (pain, fever, and jaundice) in the setting of multiple gallbladder stones initially led to a diagnosis of calculous cholangitis, but ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging revealed that the biliary obstruction was secondary to a communicating hepatic cystic mass fistulizing into the gallbladder.

differentials.candidate: Pyogenic or amoebic liver abscess with biliary communication
differentials.rule_out_reason: A hepatic cystic mass communicating with the biliary tree in a septic patient can represent a ruptured bacterial or amoebic abscess, but surgical exploration revealed parasitic daughter cysts within the gallbladder and an intact hydatid cyst wall rather than purulent abscess cavity necrosis.

diagnostic_pivot: Abdominal CT scan and surgical laparotomy confirmed a segment IV hepatic hydatid cyst that had spontaneously ruptured and fistulized into the gallbladder, discharging daughter cysts into the biliary tree and precipitating obstructive cholangitis.

clinical_summary: An 82-year-old female presented with a painful and progressive swelling over her right thigh region that had been evolving for 5 years. She had no prior medical history, fever, or history of trauma.

differentials.candidate: Soft tissue sarcoma / Malignant cystic mesenchymal neoplasm
differentials.rule_out_reason: A giant, 5-year progressive, firm thigh and gluteal mass in an elderly patient strongly raises concern for a soft tissue sarcoma; however, MRI demonstrated characteristic cystic morphology with thin T2-hypointense enhancing walls and multiloculated, septated fluid content without invasive solid nodular or osteolytic components.

Elevated CRP (82 mg/L) and deep muscular involvement can suggest a chronic bacterial abscess; however, the absence of fever, trauma, or local skin inflammation, preserved joint mobility, and indolent 5-year evolution make acute or subacute pyogenic infection unlikely.

diagnostic_pivot: Definitive diagnosis of primary musculoskeletal hydatid disease was established by positive serology, absence of lesions on thoraco-abdomino-pelvic and cerebral CT scans, and confirmed by operative resection with hypertonic saline irrigation and histopathological examination.

clinical_summary: A 3-year-old boy, the dizygotic twin brother of a known patient with bilateral retinoblastoma born following in-vitro fertilization, was undergoing annual surveillance screening for retinoblastoma. There was no other family history of retinoblastoma, and surveillance during his first two years of life showed no ocular pathology.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The child's twin brother had bilateral retinoblastoma, raising high clinical suspicion for familial retinoblastoma; however, initial annual screenings over the first two years were completely negative, and fundus examination showed discrete, tiny yellowish-white retino-choroidal granulomas without retinal detachment or intraocular endophytic/exophytic calcified masses.

Multiple enhancing brain lesions in a child with headaches can represent neurocysticercosis or parasitic granulomas; however, concurrent bilateral retino-choroidal lesions and subsequent immunodiagnostic testing directed the diagnosis toward mycobacterial disease.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point was investigation for tuberculosis prompted by the characteristic retino-choroidal and brain lesions, resulting in a strongly positive tuberculin skin test (20 mm) and positive QuantiFERON TB gold test, with complete resolution of all ocular and CNS lesions following anti-tubercular therapy.

clinical_summary: A 14-month-old female infant was admitted to the hospital with fever, marked hepatosplenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypoxemia, and significantly elevated serum ferritin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: The infant met classic diagnostic criteria for HLH based on fever, hepatosplenomegaly, bicytopenia, and severe hyperferritinemia; however, bone marrow examination revealed intracellular protozoal amastigotes, proving that the hemophagocytosis was reactive and secondary to an infectious parasitic trigger rather than an inherited genetic disorder.

differentials.candidate: Primary Gram-negative bacterial sepsis / Septic shock
differentials.rule_out_reason: The patient developed septic complications with skin lesions and blood cultures grew Klebsiella spp., requiring broad-spectrum coverage with cefepime and vancomycin; however, this bacteremia was a secondary opportunistic infection arising in the background of parasite-induced reticuloendothelial disease and liver failure.

diagnostic_pivot: The definitive diagnostic breakthrough occurred on bone marrow examination (myelogram), which revealed Leishmania spp. along with hemophagocytosis, prompting initiation of liposomal amphotericin B and corticosteroids with clinical cure.

clinical_summary: A 7-month-old male infant presented with fever for 10 days associated with hepatosplenomegaly, bicytopenia, pallor, anasarca, and markedly elevated serum ferritin.

differentials.rule_out_reason: An infant presenting with prolonged fever, hepatosplenomegaly, bicytopenia, and severe hyperferritinemia fulfills diagnostic criteria for HLH; however, the hyperinflammatory syndrome was determined to be secondary to an infectious protozoan etiology rather than a primary genetic immune defect.

differentials.candidate: Severe bacterial sepsis with capillary leak / Febrile neutropenia
differentials.rule_out_reason: The presence of anasarca, fever, and neutropenia raised immediate concern for severe bacterial infection and capillary leak, necessitating broad-spectrum antibiotics (cefepime) and supportive transfusions of platelets, packed red blood cells, and albumin; however, the illness was caused by a protozoan parasite.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnosis was confirmed by a positive rK39 immunochromatographic rapid test and detection of amastigotes alongside hemophagocytosis on bone marrow myelogram, leading to full recovery following liposomal amphotericin B and corticosteroids.

clinical_summary: Two pediatric patients presented with severe febrile illness and organomegaly: Patient 1: A one-year-old male child was admitted with a 3-month history of continuous fever, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, hypertriglyceridemia, increased ferritin, and hemodynamic instability requiring blood transfusion.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Both patients fulfilled diagnostic criteria for HLH (fever, organomegaly, severe cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, and hypertriglyceridemia); however, the disorder was determined to be secondary to visceral leishmaniasis rather than primary familial HLH or leukemia, as evidenced by bone marrow findings.

differentials.candidate: Acute Bacterial Enteric Sepsis / Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome
differentials.rule_out_reason: In the second patient, acute onset of fever, hematochezia, oliguria, generalized edema, and pancytopenia strongly suggested acute severe bacterial sepsis or hemolytic uremic syndrome, prompting immediate empiric cefepime; however, blood cultures were negative and bone marrow revealed parasitic amastigotes.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic turning point in both patients was the demonstration of Leishmania spp. with hemophagocytosis on bone marrow myelogram, corroborated by positive rK39 rapid testing, with clinical cure achieved using liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A 9-year-old male child with a history of autoimmune hepatitis treated with maintenance prednisone, azathioprine, and vitamin D was admitted with fever and headache of 12 days' duration associated with polyarthralgia.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Because the patient had pre-existing autoimmune hepatitis on immunosuppressants, new jaundice and hepatosplenomegaly were initially suspected to represent an autoimmune relapse or drug toxicity; however, the presence of persistent fever, polyarthralgia, and markers of secondary hemophagocytic syndrome (hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia) indicated an infectious driver.

Febrile neutropenia in a chronically immunosuppressed child prompted empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage with cefepime; however, the primary infectious pathogen was a protozoan parasite, and the patient improved definitively once antileishmanial treatment was administered.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred on day 2 when an immunochromatographic rapid test with rK39 antigen returned positive for visceral leishmaniasis with hemophagocytic syndrome, successfully treated with liposomal amphotericin B.

clinical_summary: A patient of Mexican origin presented with severe diffuse cutaneous infiltration complicated by widespread necrotizing skin reactions (diffuse infiltrative involvement and reactional ulcerations), which ran a rapidly progressive, fatal clinical course.

differentials.rule_out_reason: M. haemophilum was considered because it can cause cutaneous ulcerating granulomatous lesions and demonstrated significant sequence homology with the isolated acid-fast bacilli; however, comparative 16S rRNA alignment demonstrated a higher match to lepromatous species (97.9% vs. 97.3%) and a distinct insertion sequence absent in M. haemophilum.

While clinically presenting with diffuse lepromatous disease, genetic analysis revealed that strain FJ924 possessed a unique 19-bp AT-rich insertion in its 16S rRNA gene distinct from the 16-bp insertion of M. leprae, proving it was a genetically divergent novel species rather than standard M. leprae.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot was the discovery and genetic characterization of Mycobacterium lepromatosis via 16S rRNA PCR sequencing of autopsy and archived biopsy specimens as a second causal agent of diffuse lepromatous leprosy and Lucio's phenomenon.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old woman with no underlying medical comorbidities presented with progressively worsening left-sided pelvic pain, especially when walking, which had become severe enough to impede her ability to weight-bear. She reported that an initial left pelvic mass known for several years had grown substantially, and she had newly noted a second enlarging mass over the left posterior gluteal area.

differentials.candidate: Primary pelvic bone malignancy / Chondrosarcoma / Osteosarcoma
differentials.rule_out_reason: Extensive osteolytic destruction of the iliac wing, sacroiliac joint involvement, and large firm pelvic/gluteal masses in a middle-aged adult strongly suggested a primary malignant bone neoplasm; however, CT imaging showed a multiloculated thick-walled cystic structure rather than a malignant osteoid or chondroid tumor matrix.

Given her chronic pelvic pain and referral from gynecology for a pelvic mass, an ovarian cystic tumor was considered; however, CA125 was normal and cross-sectional imaging confirmed extraperitoneal musculoskeletal and osseous origin rather than an adnexal mass.

diagnostic_pivot: Surgical exploration of the extraperitoneal lesion revealed pathognomonic thick hydatid sand and multiple daughter cysts, and histopathological analysis confirmed hydatid disease of the left pelvic bone and soft tissue, managed successfully with scolicidal irrigation and albendazole.

clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with sudden-onset right-sided weakness and aphasia that occurred 3 hours prior to presentation. Over the preceding month, he had experienced headaches manifested by paroxysmal pain in both temples and the base of the neck, alongside a history of fever and chills and an episode of vomiting 3 days ago.

differentials.candidate: Primary atherothrombotic / thromboembolic acute ischemic stroke
differentials.rule_out_reason: The sudden focal deficit within 3 hours and non-contrast CT hypodensity led to initial thrombolysis with rt-PA; however, persistent fever, refractory hyponatremia, and subsequent MRI revealed that the CT hypodensity was perilesional vasogenic edema around a tuberculoma rather than primary ischemic infarction.

differentials.candidate: Cardioembolic stroke secondary to infective endocarditis
differentials.rule_out_reason: The combination of fever, chills, leukocytosis, and acute stroke syndrome suggested septic embolization from infective endocarditis; however, transthoracic echocardiography ruled out intracardiac vegetations or neoplasms.

diagnostic_pivot: Lumbar puncture performed for persistent fever and refractory hyponatremia revealed elevated opening pressure (>40 cmH2O) and lymphocytic pleocytosis, with high-throughput CSF sequencing detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and contrast MRI demonstrating pontine cistern nodular enhancement confirming tuberculous meningitis complicated by vasculitic cerebral infarctions.

clinical_summary: A 52-year-old male painter presented to the outpatient department of a tertiary care hospital with recurrent episodes of fever with chills throughout the past month. He also complained of dull, aching, continuous, non-migratory pain in bilateral feet, the right knee, the right shoulder joint, and the neck for the preceding 20 days, accompanied by swelling of bilateral upper and lower...

differentials.candidate: Lower limb necrotizing fasciitis with deep vein thrombosis
differentials.rule_out_reason: Working diagnosis on admission based on extreme limb pain, swelling, profound leukocytosis with thrombocytopenia, and saphenofemoral vein thrombosis; however, skin inspection lacked erythema or necrosis, standard empiric regimens (piperacillin/tazobactam, vancomycin, clindamycin) failed, and blood cultures identified the true environmental pathogen.

Acute severe tenderness of the right knee and shoulder joints with marked immobility raised strong suspicion for septic arthritis; however, comprehensive CT imaging revealed disseminated multiorgan infection with deep abscesses in the lungs, spleen, prostate, and shoulder musculature.

diagnostic_pivot: The diagnostic pivot occurred when blood cultures flagged positive within 48 hours for bipolarly stained Gram-negative bacilli exhibiting characteristic colonial morphology and intrinsic aminoglycoside/polymyxin resistance, confirmed as Burkholderia pseudomallei by VITEK-II, alongside CT imaging revealing occult visceral abscesses.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 44-year-old female with a history of incompletely treated latent infection was diagnosed approximately one month earlier with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). She was treated with arsenic trioxide plus all-trans retinoic acid.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the development of respiratory compromise and fever during induction therapy with arsenic trioxide and all-trans retinoic acid; however, fevers and systemic inflammatory signs persisted despite dexamethasone therapy and were ultimately explained by disseminated infection.

Considered given right upper quadrant abdominal signs and hepatotoxicity during neutropenia and intensive chemotherapy; however, percutaneous cholecystectomy tube drainage and subsequent removal failed to resolve fevers or hepatic dysfunction, which were driven by disseminated hepatic and marrow granulomas.

Considered when initial phenotypic drug susceptibility testing from a reference laboratory reported resistance to isoniazid and ethambutol, prompting an expanded second-line regimen; however, whole-genome sequencing and public health confirmatory testing demonstrated that the isolate was fully pan-susceptible lineage 4 with zero resistance-conferring mutations.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was the growth of acid-fast bacilli from blood cultures drawn during neutropenic fever workup, positive follow-up respiratory cultures, and bone marrow biopsy revealing multiple granulomas, confirming disseminated disease.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 38-year-old female presents to the physician at a medical center in an endemic tropical country 2 days after receiving a viral vector COVID-19 vaccine. She reports the acute onset of myalgia, high fever, and a widespread skin rash.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the acute onset of fever, myalgia, rash, and thrombocytopenia coincided temporally with vaccination 2 days prior; however, the coagulation profile showed no abnormalities or consumptive coagulopathy, and the patient resided in a tropical region with high endemicity for vector-borne infections.

Considered because viral hemorrhagic fevers are prevalent in this tropical region; targeted viral diagnostics specifically identified the culprit virus rather than other regional hemorrhagic pathogens.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was laboratory confirmation of acute arboviral infection via non-structural protein 1 antigen detection (NS1Ag positive), confirming acute disease.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 43-year-old female (height 160 cm, weight 46 kg, BMI 18.0) is admitted to the hospital with a 2-month history of repeated fever and space-occupying lesions in the liver.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the 2-month history of remittent nocturnal fevers, weight loss, respiratory complaints, and hepatic space-occupying lesions; excluded by negative chest imaging, negative tuberculin skin testing, negative tuberculosis IgG/IgM serology, and a negative T-Spot interferon-gamma release assay.

Considered given the multiple space-occupying liver lesions on abdominal CT; ruled out by negative serum tumor markers across multiple oncologic panels and percutaneous liver biopsy demonstrating inflammatory eosinophilic necrosis without malignant cells.

Suspected based on regional endemicity in Chongqing and liver lesions with hypereosinophilia; ruled out by negative ELISA serology for liver flukes and lack of clinical or radiographic resolution after praziquantel therapy.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) performed on liver biopsy tissue and peripheral blood, which conclusively identified species-specific reads of Fasciola hepatica, establishing the diagnosis of foodborne trematodiasis.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 37-year-old female immigrant from El Salvador presents to the emergency department with a headache, strange behavior, auditory hallucinations, and paranoid delusions. She describes feeling depressed, with decreased appetite, sleep deprivation, and forgetfulness.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered upon presentation because of acute behavioral disturbance, forgetfulness, and perceptual abnormalities; ruled out by preserved level of consciousness, intact orientation and memory, and an MMSE score of 27.

Considered given prominent persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, constricted affect, and lack of focal deficits on neurological exam; ruled out as a primary functional psychiatric illness once diagnostic neuroimaging revealed underlying organic structural frontoparietal lesions.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was cranial CT and MRI showing right frontoparietal hypodensities, encephalomalacia, and abnormal irregular calcifications corresponding to past parasitic CNS infection in a patient who never took prescribed albendazole.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 31-year-old right-hand-dominant male originally from Afghanistan who moved to the United States 7 years prior presents to the emergency department with persistent, worsening right wrist pain of greater than 3 months' duration and new-onset fluctuance at the volar wrist.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Diagnosed initially after acute pain following lifting trauma; ruled out by failure of conservative management, progressive joint pain lasting over three months, soft-tissue fluctuance, and radiographic evidence of severe osseous destruction.

Diagnosed at a subsequent emergency visit; ruled out because degenerative osteoarthritis is atypical in a young 31-year-old man and cannot account for rapidly destructive carpal osteopenia, cystic erosions, or purulent volar fluctuance.

differentials.candidate: Neuropathic (Charcot) Joint secondary to Cervical Syrinx
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because the patient demonstrated marked upper extremity hyperreflexia in the setting of severe articular degeneration; ruled out by cervical spine MRI which demonstrated no syrinx.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was surgical debridement revealing purulent synovitis and severe bone erosion, positive interferon-gamma release assay, histologic identification of caseating granulomas, and synovial aspirate cultures growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 31-year-old female office worker presents for comprehensive diagnostic evaluation of persistent and worsening hypereosinophilia, initially detected on routine antenatal screening (eosinophil count 0.34 x 10^9/L, 6.3%) and escalating postpartum.

differentials.candidate: Clonal Hypereosinophilic Syndrome / Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the massive peripheral eosinophilia (72%) and hypercellular bone marrow (35% eosinophils); excluded by the lack of clonal proliferation of eosinophil precursors and a negative FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene assay.

Initially diagnosed based on positive anti-T. spiralis IgG serology and undercooked pork consumption; ruled out as an isolated process because anthelmintic treatment failed to lower eosinophil counts, IgE surged above 2,500 IU/mL, and an extending necrotizing hepatic lesion emerged adjacent to the biliary tract.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was percutaneous liver biopsy histopathology revealing eosinophilic abscess formation, with metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identifying 1,299 species-specific reads of Fasciola hepatica, confirmed by PCR, establishing a coinfection.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 41-year-old pregnant woman at 35 weeks gestation by early dates presents to an infectious disease clinic with a 7-month history of progressively worsening left flank fullness, left shoulder pain, and marked abdominal distention.

differentials.candidate: Non-Parasitic Splenic Cysts (Congenital Epidermoid / Splenic Pseudocyst)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered for benign cystic splenomegaly in an adult; however, non-parasitic cysts are typically solitary and unilocular, whereas ultrasound demonstrated extensive multicystic involvement replacing more than 90% of splenic tissue in a patient with rural pastoral environmental risk.

Considered in an HIV-positive patient with a past history of tuberculous arthritis; ruled out by sustained virologic suppression with a CD4 count of 500 cells/uL, absence of constitutional B-symptoms, and cystic imaging morphology rather than solid necrotic microabscesses.

diagnostic_pivot: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was characteristic multivesicular cystic appearance on ultrasound replacing the splenic parenchyma combined with a strongly positive indirect hemagglutination assay (IHA) titer of 1:1024, confirming hydatid disease.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 10-year-old male child presents to the surgical clinic with a 10-month history of frequent, colicky, postprandial abdominal pain and vomiting. The pain is generalized, aggravated by food intake, and accompanied by anorexia, chronic constipation, and significant weight loss.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of the large 10 x 3 cm obstructing intraluminal mass, circumferential colonic thickening, weight loss, and regional lymphadenopathy; ruled out following surgical resection, which demonstrated granulomatous parasitic inflammation rather than malignant neoplasia.

Strongly suspected given the patient's family history of lymphoma in his brother, combined with extensive abdominal, parahepatic, and pulmonary lymphadenopathy; excluded by histopathology revealing non-caseating granulomas formed around trematode ova rather than clonal lymphoid proliferation.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 47-year-old male who works as an international exhibition organizer presents with acute neurologic deterioration. His medical history is notable for recurrent otitis with purulent otorrhea and fevers following a tympanoplasty and radical cavity revision on the left ear 6 months earlier.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Provisionally diagnosed due to weakly positive anti-Zic4 antibodies in the CSF; however, intensive immunosuppressive therapy with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy and therapeutic plasma separation produced no clinical improvement, and cultures subsequently confirmed bacterial neuroinfection.

clinical_summary: <case_prompt> A 3-year-old girl presents for medical evaluation due to growth retardation. On physical examination, her vital signs are stable, and she demonstrates poor physical growth parameters for age without other focal physical abnormalities.

differentials.candidate: Pediatric Neoplasm with Metastatic Disease (e.g., Hepatoblastoma / Neuroblastoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because a toddler presenting with growth failure and concurrent multi-organ (thoracic and abdominal) space-occupying lesions raises concern for primary pediatric malignancy with metastases; ruled out by smooth, encapsulated cystic radiopacities lacking invasive solid features.

differentials.candidate: Congenital Bronchogenic and Hepatic Epithelial Cysts
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as benign non-parasitic cysts of early childhood; however, congenital cystic malformations are usually solitary and isolated to a single organ, whereas simultaneous multi-organ pulmonary and hepatic involvement is classic for larval cestode cysts.
