clinical_summary: A 68-year-old male with no known history of chronic medical illness or prior trauma presents with complaints of progressive headache, dizziness, and involuntary weight loss that have persisted for six months.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions with surrounding edema in an older patient with chronic weight loss and concurrent lung and liver nodules strongly suggested metastatic cancer, but histopathological evaluation revealed parasitic germinative membranes without neoplastic cells.

Cystic echinococcosis classically manifests as unilocular, well-defined fluid cysts with clear margins, whereas this patient presented with infiltrative, multivesicular lesions with irregular contours and calcifications mimicking a malignant tumor.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of the biopsied liver lesions definitively established the diagnosis by identifying the characteristic germinative membranes of Echinococcus multilocularis.

clinical_summary: A previously healthy 20-year-old female presents for outpatient evaluation after experiencing a generalized tonic-clonic seizure while sleep-deprived. She reports localized hip pain, but denies recent fever, chills, cough, loss of appetite, weight loss, night sweats, or symptoms of upper respiratory, gastrointestinal, or urinary tract infection.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Multiple ring-enhancing intracranial lesions presenting with seizures in a young adult led to an initial diagnosis of neurocysticercosis and empirical antiparasitic therapy; however, the patient developed new fevers, repeat neuroimaging after 4 weeks showed no interval improvement, and subsequent lymph node histology confirmed mycobacterial disease.

Bacterial brain abscesses typically produce ring enhancement and mass effect, but the patient presented afebrily with normal initial hematology, lacked an extracranial suppurative nidus, and subsequent biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis rather than acute bacterial suppuration.

diagnostic_pivot: Development of a new anterior cervical lymph node prompted excisional biopsy, which revealed necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis with Langhans-type giant cells alongside a positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold test, confirming tuberculosis with subsequent resolution on anti-tuberculosis therapy.

clinical_summary: A 53-year-old man from Hubei Province, China, who has resided in Guangdong Province for a long period, is admitted with a one-month history of intermittent high fevers (reaching >39°C), generalized abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, fatigue, anorexia, involuntary weight loss, and mild cough.

differentials.rule_out_reason: CMV colitis frequently produces discrete mucosal ulcers in advanced AIDS with CD4 < 50 cells/μL, and low-level CMV-DNA was detected; however, immunohistochemical staining of colonic tissue was negative for CMV and revealed fungal yeast cells.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a prominent cause of ileocecal ulceration, lymphadenopathy, and systemic wasting in advanced HIV, but tuberculosis T-SPOT testing was negative and colonic histology revealed septate fungal spores rather than caseating granulomas.

diagnostic_pivot: Histopathologic examination of colonic mucosal biopsies with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains revealed intracellular short fusiform and sausage-shaped yeast cells with characteristic central transverse septa aggregated within CD68+ histiocytes, establishing intestinal talaromycosis.

clinical_summary: A 45-year-old male presents with recurrent high fevers and cough of two weeks' duration, accompanied by progressive weakness, anorexia, and an involuntary 10-kg weight loss. He has no prior medical, surgical, or family history of hematologic or histiocytic disorders.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Both Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus viremias were present in this host with advanced AIDS, which can precipitate secondary HLH; however, blood culture isolation confirmed that disseminated fungal infection was the primary underlying trigger.

The left upper lung occupancy and profound pancytopenia raised concern for primary lung carcinoma with bone marrow involvement, but the mass regressed with medical therapy and lacked malignant features on repeat imaging.

diagnostic_pivot: On hospital day 4, blood cultures grew Talaromyces marneffei, confirming disseminated fungal sepsis driving secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

clinical_summary: A 24-year-old female with a five-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) maintained on long-term oral prednisone (10 mg daily) and hydroxychloroquine is transferred for evaluation of persistent abdominal pain, intractable watery diarrhea, and recurring fevers up to 40°C of three months' duration.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Intestinal vasculitis was initially considered given the history of SLE and low complements, and treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy (500 mg/day for 3 days twice); however, diarrhea did not improve and clinical SLE disease activity was low (SLEDAI score of 3).

Colonoscopy demonstrated multiple ulcers throughout the large intestine and biopsy revealed chronic inflammation with granulation tissue hyperplasia mimicking Crohn's disease; however, the clinical picture in an immunosuppressed patient with calcified thoracic/abdominal lymphadenopathy pointed toward a chronic granulomatous infection.

diagnostic_pivot: Following verification of a vesicorectal fistula by cystography and fecal creatinine analysis, colonic mucosal biopsies tested positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis by PCR on two occasions and showed acid-fast bacilli on direct staining, establishing intestinal tuberculosis.

clinical_summary: A 44-year-old male residing in Shanxi Province, China, with a five-year history of antisynthetase antibody syndrome managed with cyclosporine A, presents for acute evaluation due to relapse of high fevers and profound functional decline.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's underlying antisynthetase syndrome on immunosuppressive therapy, an autoimmune flare driving secondary HLH was the primary suspicion and initially treated with chemo-immunotherapy; however, rapid relapse during steroid taper indicated an unresolved underlying infectious trigger.
Common viral triggers of HLH in immunosuppressed patients were considered, but molecular viral loads and serologies returned negative.

diagnostic_pivot: Recognition of the patient's residence in an endemic area of Shanxi Province led to bone marrow aspiration showing Leishman-Donovan bodies and positive Leishmania infantum DNA, confirming visceral leishmaniasis as the underlying etiology.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old woman with no significant prior medical history is transferred to the hospital for evaluation of rapidly progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness. Three weeks prior, she developed lower thoracic and lumbar back pain, which was initially managed as muscular strain following normal lumbar spine radiographs.

differentials.candidate: Autoimmune Demyelinating Myelopathy (Transverse Myelitis vs. Multiple Sclerosis)
differentials.rule_out_reason: A solitary ring-enhancing intramedullary cord lesion with surrounding edema and rapid onset paraparesis in a young woman without brain lesions suggested acute transverse myelitis, and steroids produced temporary clinical improvement, but intraoperative exploration revealed an encapsulated parasitic cyst.

A solitary enhancing intramedullary spinal mass with progressive paraparesis and cord expansion frequently represents an astrocytoma or ependymoma, but surgical resection demonstrated a cystic cavity containing purulent fluid and a parasite capsule rather than neoplastic tissue.

diagnostic_pivot: Thoracic laminectomy and midline durotomy with excision of the intramedullary T8 lesion yielded gross cystic material and cyst capsule, with pathology confirming neurocysticercosis despite negative preoperative serum antibody testing.

clinical_summary: A 32-year-old woman residing in Guangdong Province, China, presents with acute-onset dyspnea and chest pain of four days' duration, accompanied by cough productive of small amounts of sputum and occasional low-grade fever.

differentials.candidate: Malignant Mediastinal Neoplasm (Lymphoma vs. Thymic Carcinoma)
differentials.rule_out_reason: The acute middle mediastinal mass causing severe tracheal stenosis and superior vena cava compression in a young adult strongly raised suspicion of lymphoma or thymic neoplasm, but multiple biopsies demonstrated inflammatory changes without tumor cells.

T-SPOT testing was positive, which raised suspicion of tuberculous lymphadenitis in an endemic setting; however, acid-fast stains of lung tissue and needle aspirates were negative, and fungal cultures confirmed a dimorphic mold.

diagnostic_pivot: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) yielded specimens that grew characteristic red-pigmented fungal colonies on Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25°C, with histopathology revealing yeast cells with characteristic transverse septa on PAS and GMS staining.

clinical_summary: A 5-month-old female infant is admitted due to recurring fever and productive cough of two weeks' duration unresponsive to outpatient cephalosporin and penicillin regimens. She was born full-term with a birth weight of 2.7 kg.

differentials.candidate: Refractory Bacterial or Viral Community-Acquired Pneumonia
differentials.rule_out_reason: Initial presentation of fever and productive cough was managed as common infant pneumonia, but sequential administration of broad-spectrum antibacterial agents produced no clinical improvement, prompting evaluation for opportunistic infections in the setting of thymic hypoplasia.

While P. jirovecii was detected as a coinfection on molecular sequencing, isolated PJP does not cause prominent bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy following BCG vaccination or acid-fast bacilli in gastric aspirates.

diagnostic_pivot: Concentrated smears of sputum and gastric aspirates revealed acid-fast bacilli and blood next-generation sequencing mapped Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex sequences in an infant with axillary lymphadenopathy following BCG vaccination, establishing disseminated BCG tuberculosis disease in the setting of SCID.

clinical_summary: A 42-year-old previously healthy male residing in the countryside of Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, presents with progressive facial and mucosal ulcerations, profound weight loss, and generalized lymphadenopathy. He has a three-year history of chronic diarrhea and abdominal pain.

clinical_summary: A 37-year-old male presents with intermittent fever (up to 102°F) for four days and generalized weakness in both the upper and lower extremities. On examination, he is alert, conscious, and oriented.

clinical_summary: A patient presents for neurological evaluation with progressive unsteadiness and gait difficulty. On admission, the Glasgow Coma Scale score is 15 (E4V5M6).

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the combination of subacute cerebellar ataxia and positive serum anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies (125 IU/mL), but excluded by normal thyroid function tests and a negative serum anti-NAE antibody test.

differentials.candidate: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration / Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered because of subacute progressive cerebellar ataxia and low BMI, but ruled out by negative serum paraneoplastic neuronal antibodies (EUROLINE 12 Ag) and exhaustive endoscopic and cross-sectional imaging demonstrating no occult malignancy.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite normal head CT and brain MRI scans, contrast-enhanced CT showed dilated bronchioles with apical lesions, FDG-PET demonstrated intense uptake in hilar lymph nodes and the left lung, and subsequent bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis by smear and culture, establishing central nervous system tuberculosis manifested as cerebellar ataxia.

clinical_summary: A patient presents for neurological evaluation with significant gait disturbance and posture changes. Physical examination reveals an abnormal gait, slight camptocormia, and decreased spontaneous movements of the right upper limb.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered in light of slight camptocormia and unilateral reduction in upper extremity spontaneous movement, but excluded by the complete lack of cardinal parkinsonian signs (tremor, rigidity, immobility, postural instability) and long-term resolution without dopaminergic therapy.

clinical_summary: An 86-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer in remission following radiotherapy, arterial hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents for his routine annual health checkup. clinical_summary: A 31-year-old male residing in Hainan, China presents with low back pain and intermittent diarrhea of more than one month's duration. Six months earlier, he underwent renal transplantation for uremia and has since been maintained on immunosuppressive triple therapy comprising tacrolimus, mycophenolate enteric-coated tablets, and methylprednisolone.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient developed severe hemorrhagic lower gastrointestinal bleeding while maintained on corticosteroid therapy, but excluded when colonoscopy revealed multiple colonic ulcers with active bleeding at the ileocecal junction directly related to invasive fungal infection.

clinical_summary: A female patient presents with a subacute-to-chronic breast mass with overlying scrofulous skin changes, an active draining cutaneous fistula, and severe keloid scarring. She reports persistent fevers and night sweats, alongside worsening enlargement of the affected breast.

differentials.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected based on the breast mass and localized inflammation, prompting empirical intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam; however, the atypical scrofulous cutaneous appearance, persistent drainage, and lack of acute pyogenic response ruled against an ordinary pyogenic process.

diagnostic_pivot: Despite negative acid-fast staining and negative cartridge-based PCR on fluid aspirate, and core biopsy histology showing only necrotic fibroadipose tissue without typical granulomas, automated and solid core biopsy cultures grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming primary breast tuberculosis with full drug susceptibility.

clinical_summary: A 27-year-old male presents for clinical evaluation one year after undergoing liver transplantation for an extensive, unresectable infiltrative hepatic lesion. He is maintained on chronic post-transplant immunosuppressive therapy.

differentials.candidate: Metastatic liver cancer / De novo malignancy
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as the primary differential diagnosis for new-onset simultaneous multiorgan parenchymal masses in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, but excluded when histopathological biopsy confirmed parasitic metacestode proliferative tissue rather than malignant neoplasia.

differentials.candidate: Pre-existing extrahepatic metastasis prior to transplantation
differentials.rule_out_reason: Considered as an explanation for multi-organ involvement, but excluded by comprehensive pre-transplant clinical examination and whole-body imaging confirming no lesions outside the liver.

diagnostic_pivot: Follow-up computed tomography of the brain and thorax 1 year post-transplant demonstrated multiple parenchymal lesions, which upon tissue biopsy were confirmed as metastatic alveolar echinococcal recurrences exacerbated by post-transplantation immunosuppressive therapy.
